148N-6
《字林西报》，1936年6月7日，星期日

“迪克”王在克勒费尔审判中被判挪用公款罪名成立

塞莱特证词支持指控：美亚银行买办挪用资金；律师与法官发生争执

在昨天江苏高等法院第二分院审理前美亚银行经理朱利叶斯·克勒费尔上诉案期间，美国前地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士提供了进一步证词，指向已停业的美亚银行公司买办“迪克”王（"Dick" Wong）涉嫌挪用和侵吞公款。

克勒费尔因与中国籍人士亨利·杨（Henry Young）先生所有的20,000美元和俄籍人士M. M. 埃波特（M. M. Epport）先生所有的12,000美元失踪案中的违反信托责任行为，被判处六个月监禁。这两笔款项均交由银行保管。

称王有罪

塞莱特博士在作证时的要点如下：
1. 他作为律师和清算人深信，市检察官办公室拥有足够的信息，足以让任何理性的人相信王在杨的交易中犯有刑事罪行，并且他侵吞了属于银行的100,000美元。
2. 他获悉，市检察官R. T. 布莱恩（R. T. Bryan）先生及其助手鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生已向负责银行信托部的职员徐玉松（Tsu Yu-soong，音译）保证，不会对他提起刑事诉讼。这一信息是徐在塞莱特博士办公室的一次谈话中提供的。
3. 他从埃波特和杨的账目中无法得知显示克勒费尔在这些案件中有刑事犯罪行为的迹象。

昨天的聆讯特点是助理市检察官T. S. 李（T. S. Lea）与辩护律师之间反复发生激烈的口头冲突。

在聆讯的一个阶段，当三名辩护律师都开始起哄，指责助理市检察官李打断塞莱特博士的证词时，庭审暂时中断。

当陈定赛（Chen Ding-sai，音译）博士指出布莱恩先生和鲁先生据称向负责银行信托部的职员徐玉松承诺，如果他在证词中牵连克勒费尔，就不会对他提起刑事诉讼时，暂时的僵局开始了。

律师争吵

宗法官（Judge Tsoong）传召塞莱特博士回到证人席，并就这一点向他提问。李先生跳起来想说些什么。他被辩护律师陈博士打断，随后格罗斯曼（A. Grossmann）博士和费舍尔（O. Fischer）博士这两位辩护方律师也加入了进来。

格罗斯曼博士和费舍尔博士挥舞着双手，大声嚷嚷说李先生试图打断证人。与此同时，有人建议塞莱特博士继续，他便继续作证。此时法庭变成了

“迪克”王先生被传召出庭，讲述了亨利·杨先生如何拿着20,000美元现钞找到他，并要求他将这笔钱兑换成银元，以便在信托部保管。王称他去找克勒费尔，克勒费尔告诉他建议杨将钱存入活期存款，因为银行状况不佳。

当杨拒绝这样做时，王说他再次去找克勒费尔，克勒费尔批准接收这笔钱进行保管。他否认在银行关闭前知道这笔钱从保管账户转为活期存款的情况。

职员从未见过钱

接下来传召负责银行保管部的职员徐玉宗（Tsu Yu-tsoong，音译）作证。他告诉法庭，他被要求签署收据，但实际上他从未见过这笔钱。

当法官询问这种程序是否违法时，徐说银行里做了许多违法的事情。

他告诉法庭，他将杨的交易转交给沃尔特·拉夫（Walter Rave）先生，后者批准了这一程序。关于埃波特的交易，徐说他询问了克勒费尔，克勒费尔指示他遵循与杨案相同的方法。

正是在这一点上，辩方律师陈先生希望法官询问徐，他是否与布莱恩先生和鲁先生达成谅解，即如果他牵连克勒费尔，就不会对他提起刑事诉讼。

在早些时候的聆讯中，塞莱特博士的证词多次被宗法官驳回，后者认为所有牵连“迪克”王的要点均不相关。

辩护律师对此提出异议，声称王的证词在克勒费尔的审判中对定罪起到了重要作用。他们主张，任何能证明王不可信的证据，以及任何能针对他的确凿证据，都与本案有关。

辩方律师陈先生告诉法庭，指向王有罪的证据已提交给市检察官办公室。这番话使助理市检察官T. S. 李先生站了起来。他说，警方曾多次向塞莱特博士索取证据，但这位前地区检察官总是说他很忙。

正是在反驳李先生陈述的这一时刻，塞莱特博士断言，警方手中已有足够的证据可以对王提起诉讼。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, May 23, 1936

Sellett On Stand
In Kleffel Case

AOBC Compradore Loan
Cash And Used Funds
For Own Factory

Dr. George Sellett, prominent American lawyer who prosecuted the case against Frank Raven and J. Warner Brown after the collapse of the American-Oriental Bank last year, appeared in the 2nd Kiangsu High Court this morning as a witness in the appeal case brought by Mr. Julius Kleffel, German, former manager of the A.O.B.C., against the decision of the First Special District Court sentencing him to six months' imprisonment for breach of confidence.

During the testimony of Dr. Sellett, who was concerned mostly with giving details of the transactions involved in the deposits of Mr. Henry Young and Mr. Eppert, it was brought out that the compradore of the bank had arranged to raise money and to borrow money in order that the native banks might show a credit balance. It was also brought out that the compradore of the A.O.B.C had loaned money to employees and had used $50,000 for a lock factory which was the compradore's own property.

German Official Sits In
A great deal of interest was created in the courtroom when Dr. Kempe, vice-consul and chief of the legal department of the German Consulate, came to listen to the case.

Dr. Sellett began his testimony with details of the Henry Young account. He said that on April 8, 1935, Mr. Young had deposited $20,000 in notes in the bank for safe keeping. If the ordinary procedure had been followed, this amount would have been converted by the compradore into silver and put into the safe keeping vault. A receipt was given to Young signed by Tsu and Raven. The

compradore, however, did not convert the deposit into silver, but obtained the $20,000 and booked it as a gold deposit, thereby increasing the account.

Not Signed By Raven
In the safe-keeping vault the gold deposit receipt was placed under the name of Henry Young, this receipt was signed by Tsu and Feingold, but not by Raven.

Concerning the Eppert transaction, the witness said that the same procedure had been followed, except that no actual money had been paid into the bank, but a check drawn on the bank, and instructions given to convert the $12,000 into silver and the amount put into safekeeping stock.

If the proper procedure had been followed, the compradore would have to use from the amount "cash due from compradore" $12,000, decreasing the balance of the account thereby. This was not done, but the same procedure as in the Young transaction was followed.

Questions Put
At the conclusion of Dr. Sellett's testimony, the judge asked Kleffel if he had any questions to ask the witness. Kleffel replied that his lawyers had several questions to ask the witness.

Dr. A Grossman started to question Dr. Sellett. The judge advised counsel to ask only those question which were necessary.

Four or five questions which Dr. Grossman asked were not allowed to be answered. The tendency of all these questions was to show that Dr. Sellett had filed complaint with the Municipal Advocate against the compradore of the bank concerning the nature of the account "cash due from compradore." The judge considered that these questions were immaterial.

Motion Overruled
A motion by Dr. Grossman that the correspondence between Dr. Sellett and the Municipal Advocate be disclosed was overruled.

Dr. Ficher, lawyer for defence, questioned the witness whether he had had conversations with the compradore concerning indebtedness. Dr. Sellett disclosed that the compradore had admitted in the presence of Mr. Gill, Dr. Sellett and his secretary, and the counsel of the compradore, that on December 31, 1934, the date on which the "cash due from compradore" was audited for the last time, he had arranged to raise some money and to borrow money in order to have native banks show credit balances in conformity with the books of the A.O.B.C. This practice was always followed on the date of audit.

Police Accused
Dr. Sellett also disclosed that the compradore confessed to having used bank funds to give several loans to employees of the bank and the different Raven companies. He also confessed to having used $50,-000 for a lock factory which is the compradore's own property.

At this point, Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru jumped to his feet and said the testimony was irrelevant. Strong exceptions were made by counsel for the defence. It was alleged that these facts were very important to the defense and it was stated that the "police have not done their duty."

The hearing was then adjourned sine die.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月23日，星期六

塞莱特出庭作证
在克莱费尔案中

美亚银行买办借款
挪用现金及资金
用于自家工厂

乔治·塞莱特博士（Dr. George Sellett），这位在去年美亚银行（American-Oriental Bank）倒闭后起诉弗兰克·拉文（Frank Raven）和J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）的著名美国律师，今天上午作为证人出现在江苏高等法院第二分院，出席由德籍人士、前美亚银行经理朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）先生提起的上诉案。克莱费尔不服第一特区地方法院以背信罪判处其六个月监禁的判决。

在塞莱特博士作证期间，其证词主要涉及亨利·杨（Henry Young）先生和埃珀特（Eppert）先生存款所涉交易的细节。庭上披露，该银行买办曾安排筹款和借款，以便钱庄显示出贷方余额。庭上还披露，美亚银行买办曾向员工放贷，并将5万美元用于一家锁厂，该锁厂为买办自有财产。

德国官员旁听
当德国领事馆副领事兼法律部主任肯佩博士（Dr. Kempe）前来旁听案件时，法庭内引起了极大关注。

塞莱特博士首先就亨利·杨账户的细节开始作证。他说，1935年4月8日，杨先生将2万美元现钞存入银行保管。如果按照常规程序办理，这笔款项本应由买办兑换成银元并放入保管库。杨先生收到了一张由徐（Tsu）和拉文签名的收据。

然而，买办并未将该笔存款兑换成银元，而是取得了这2万美元，并将其记为黄金存款，从而增加了账户金额。

拉文未签名
在保管库中，黄金存款收据被归在亨利·杨名下，该收据由徐和芬戈尔德（Feingold）签名，但拉文未签名。

关于埃珀特的交易，证人表示遵循了相同的程序，只不过没有实际资金存入银行，而是开具了一张以该银行为付款行的支票，并指示将1.2万美元兑换成银元，并将该金额放入保管库存。

如果遵循适当程序，买办必须从“买办欠款”科目中支取1.2万美元，从而减少账户余额。但这并未做到，而是采取了与杨先生交易中相同的做法。

提出质询
在塞莱特博士作证结束时，法官询问克莱费尔是否有问题要问证人。克莱费尔回答说，他的律师有几个问题要问证人。

A·格罗斯曼博士（Dr. A Grossman）开始向塞莱特博士提问。法官建议辩护律师只询问必要的问题。

格罗斯曼博士提出的四五个问题被禁止回答。所有这些问题的倾向性都在于表明，塞莱特博士曾就“买办欠款”账户的性质向工部局公诉人投诉该银行买办。法官认为这些问题与案件无关。

动议被驳回
格罗斯曼博士要求披露塞莱特博士与工部局公诉人之间通信往来的动议被驳回。

被告律师菲舍尔博士（Dr. Ficher）询问证人是否曾就债务问题与买办进行过谈话。塞莱特博士披露，买办曾在吉尔先生（Mr. Gill）、塞莱特博士及其秘书以及买办的法律顾问面前承认，在1934年12月31日——即最后一次审计“买办欠款”之日——他已安排筹集和借入一些资金，以便使钱庄的贷方余额与美亚银行的账簿相符。在审计日总是遵循这一做法。

指控警方
塞莱特博士还披露，买办承认曾动用银行资金向银行员工及不同的拉文公司提供多笔贷款。他还承认曾动用5万美元用于一家属于买办自有财产的锁厂。

此时，工部局公诉人保罗·Y·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）起身表示该证词与案件无关。辩护律师提出强烈异议。据称这些事实对辩护方非常重要，并指出“警方未尽职责”。

随后听证会无限期休庭。

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MAY 17, 1936

Fresh Request
For Sellett As
Witness Made

Attorneys For Kleffel
At Appeal Hearing
Ask Appearance

A fresh request to call Dr. George
Sellett, liquidator of the defunct
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration, to appear as witness for
the defense was made in the 2nd
Kiangsu High Court yesterday at the
second hearing of the appeal case
brought by Mr. Julius Kleffel,
former Manager of the Bank,
against his conviction on a charge
of breach of confidence rendered in
the First Special District Court early
in March.

The same request was made at
the first appeal hearing held one
week ago but Dr. Sellett was not
summoned. Attorneys for Mr.
Kleffel pressed the matter yesterday,
maintaining that the liquidator
could give evidence that might help
to free Mr. Kleffel, who is now
facing a six-month jail sentence.

Mr. Kleffel was originally tried on
charges of fraud, misappropriation
and breach of confidence in connec-
tion with the disappearance of
$20,000 belonging to Mr. Henry
Young, Chinese, and $12,000, the
property of Mr. M. M. Eppert, Rus-
sian, from the safe-keeping vaults
of the bank. He was acquitted of
fraud and misappropriation.

Walter Raven Testifies

Yesterday's session, which lasted
throughout the morning, was featur-
ed by testimony given by Mr. Walter
Raven, former Assistant Manager of
the Bank, and a verbal battle be-
tween the prosecution and defense
lawyers, with Dr. A. Grossman, as
Kleffel attorney, playing a leading
role.

Asked who gave the order trans-
ferring Mr. Young's safe-keeping
account to call deposit, Mr. Raven
declared that "it looks as if Mr.
Tsu did so. I did not know that the
money had been transferred to call-
deposit until I was told so in Mr
Bryan's office." The Mr. Tsu referred
to is Mr. Tsu U-soong, former A.-
O.B.C. clerk.

Mr. Raven continued that he
could only surmise as to what Tsu
had to gain by making such a
transfer. "Mr. Kleffel, just before
the bank closed, kept asking Wong
(the bank comprador) to withdraw
the money of the A.-O.B.C. from
the native banks," the witness de-
clared. "If Tsu owed Wong money,
he might give the order for transfer,
and then the pressure from Kleffel
on Wong would be reduced. With
cash on hand, the pressure would be
less and less."

The witness then recalled that
Wong had made the statement in
both Mr. Kleffel's and his presence
that the Young matter had been
taken care of. This was before the
bank closed. Continuing, he began
to point out alleged mistakes in the
transcriptions of his testimony made
during the Kleffel trial in the lower
court. He was interrupted by the
court. The latter pointed out that

the matter was irrelevant and had
no bearing on the case.

Attorneys Blacker

At this juncture, the defense
lawyers rose to their feet and pro-
tested. Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant
Municipal Advocate, also arose and
advised the attorneys to sit down.
There was considerable loud legal
by-play and after order returned, the
court asked Mr. Raven how much
money he owed the A.-O.B.C. He
stated that he owed U.S.$600 and
$30,000 in Shanghai currency. He
further testified that he had not
signed Mr. Young's safe-keeping de-
posit slip. He added that he had
never examined the account since
there were more than 2,000 ac-
counts in the bank and that he, nor
no other one man, could possibly
examine them all.

Mr. L. Feingold, former cashier
of the bank, who gave testimony
regarding the routine of the con-
cern in the lower court, repeated
this same testimony before the
High Court yesterday. At the con-
clusion of the session, the hearing
was adjourned until May 23.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年5月17日，星期日

再次请求
传唤塞莱特
作为证人

克莱费尔律师
在上诉听证会上
要求出庭作证

昨天，在江苏高等法院第二分院举行的朱利叶斯·克莱费尔先生（前银行经理）上诉案第二次听证会上，再次提出请求，传唤已停业的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）清算人乔治·塞莱特博士作为辩方证人出庭。克莱费尔不服今年3月初第一特区地方法院以背信罪对其作出的定罪判决。

在一周前的第一次上诉听证会上也曾提出同样的请求，但未传唤塞莱特博士。克莱费尔的律师昨天坚持此事，主张清算人可以提供可能有助于免除克莱费尔先生罪责的证据，克莱费尔目前正面临六个月的监禁刑期。

克莱费尔最初因与华人亨利·杨先生的2万美元及俄国人M·M·埃珀特先生的1.2万美元从银行保管库失踪有关的欺诈、挪用和背信指控受审。他被宣告欺诈和挪用罪名不成立。

沃尔特·拉文作证

昨天的庭审持续了整个上午，主要特点是前银行副经理沃尔特·拉文先生（Mr. Walter Raven）提供的证词，以及控辩双方律师之间的口头交锋，其中担任克莱费尔律师的A·格罗斯曼博士发挥了主要作用。

当被问及是谁下令将杨先生的保管账户转为活期存款时，拉文先生宣称：“看起来是徐先生这么做的。直到我在布莱恩先生（Mr. Bryan）的办公室被告知此事时，我才知道这笔钱已被转为活期存款。”这里提到的徐先生是指前美亚银行职员徐玉松（Tsu U-soong，音译）。

拉文先生继续说，他只能推测徐通过这种转移能获得什么利益。“就在银行关闭前，克莱费尔先生一直要求黄（Wong，银行买办）从钱庄提取美亚银行的资金，”证人宣称。“如果徐欠黄的钱，他可能会下达转移指令，这样克莱费尔对黄的压力就会减轻。手头有现金，压力就会越来越小。”

证人随后回忆说，黄曾在克莱费尔先生和他本人在场的情况下声明，杨先生的事情已经处理妥当。这是在银行关闭之前。接着，他开始指出在下级法院审理克莱费尔案期间，其证词转录中所谓的错误。他被法庭打断。法庭指出该事项与案件无关，对本案没有影响。

律师发生冲突

此时，辩护律师起立抗议。助理工部局公诉人保罗·Y·鲁先生也起立，建议律师们坐下。现场出现了相当大声的法律程序插曲，待秩序恢复后，法庭询问拉文先生欠美亚银行多少钱。他表示欠600美元和3万上海两（Shanghai currency）。他进一步作证说，他没有签署杨先生的保管存款单。他补充说，他从未查核过该账户，因为银行有2000多个账户，他或其他任何一个人都不可能全部查核。

前银行出纳员L·芬戈尔德先生（Mr. L. Feingold）曾在下级法院就该公司的日常业务提供证词，昨天他在高等法院重复了同样的证词。庭审结束时，听证会休庭至5月23日。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, May 2, 1936.

Deadline In Raven
Appeal Passes, No
Word From America

With the deadline for perfecting
his appeal passed today, and no
word received from America, it is
believed in Shanghai that Mr. Frank
Jay Raven, convicted by the United
States Court for China in connec-
tion with collapse of the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation and
allied interests, has not carried his
case to a higher tribunal.

At the office of the U.S. District
Attorney here no news had come in
by noon, and it is thought that Mr.
Raven has given up his original
intention of making an appeal to
the Court at San Francisco, as he
said he would at the conclusion of
his dramatic trial here during the
month of January.

Mr. John Warner Brown, con-
victed on similar charges of fraud,
theft and embezzlement also filed
an appeal, but withdrew it before
the two men were deported the
latter part of February to the peni-
tentiary on McNeill's Island, in the
State of Washington. Mr. Brown's
term was for two years.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月2日，星期六

拉文上诉
期限已过，
美国方面杳无音信

随着完善其上诉手续的截止日期今天过去，且未收到来自美国的任何消息，上海方面认为，因美亚银行公司及相关利益方倒闭案被美国在华法院定罪的弗兰克·杰伊·拉文（Frank Jay Raven）先生，并未将其案件提交至更高一级的法庭。

截至中午，此地美国地区检察官办公室尚未收到任何消息，人们认为拉文先生已放弃他最初向旧金山法院上诉的打算，正如他在一月份此处戏剧性的审判结束时所说的那样。

约翰·华纳·布朗（John Warner Brown）先生也因类似的欺诈、盗窃和挪用公款罪名被定罪，他也提出了上诉，但在两人于2月下旬被驱逐至华盛顿州麦克尼尔岛（McNeill's Island）监狱之前撤回了上诉。布朗先生的刑期为两年。

page_data.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MAY 2, 1936
REG.
D.

A.-O. Bank
To Pay 10%
On June 15

Dr. George Sellett Is
Named Liquidator
Of Raven Group

IS ALSO TRUSTEE
OF ASIA REALTY

To Post Bonds Total-
ing U.S.$110,000
With Court

"We have continued to collect moneys owing to American-Oriental Banking Corporation and will pay a 10 per cent dividend to the depositors and other creditors of the bank about June 15, 1936." Dr. George Sellett, newly appointed liquidator of the defunct Raven financial institutions and trustee of the Asia Realty Company, told newspapermen yesterday afternoon.

Dr. Sellett was named liquidator to succeed the late Mr. Frank Hough by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China yesterday morning. He will be required to post a bond of U.S.$60,000 for the faithful performance of his duties in connection with the task of liquidator and a bond of U.S.$50,000 as trustee of the Asia Realty Company.

Four orders were issued by Judge Helmick, three making Dr. Sellett liquidator of the American-Oriental Bank, the Raven Trust Company and the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the fourth made him the ARCO trustee. The three orders were exactly alike in phraseology. They stated: "It appearing to the Court that owing to the lamentable death of Frank L. Hough there is no liquidator herein, wherefore, it is ordered, adjudged and decreed that George Sellett be and he hereby is appointed Liquidator."

The Asia Realty order stated that he "shall in his discretion continue to manage and operate the business" in the same manner as it has heretofore been conducted by the officers and directors.

Dr. Sellett's statement, issued after his appointment, follows in full:

"Mr. Hough's task of liquidating these companies was most difficult. The ability and the exemplary courage and impartiality with which he dealt with the numerous complicated problems of the liquidation have in a very large measure simplified the work of completing the liquidation of the companies. We have continued to collect moneys owing to the Bank and will pay a 10 per cent dividend to the depositors and other creditors of the Bank about June 15, 1936.

"We are unable at this time to announce a date for payment of a dividend to creditors of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation but hope to be able to make an announcement within the reasonably near future. Upon the suspension of business of the Raven Trust Company the assets of the Trust Company were of almost no value.

"Very little money has been collected for the Trust Company and it is probable that there will be nothing available for distribution among the general creditors of the Trust Company. Our efforts are being directed toward effecting the collection of all collectable moneys owing to the Bank, the Finance Company and the Trust Company before the end of the year 1936, for payment of further dividends and with a view to finally winding up the companies early in 1937.

"Asia Realty Company has been very economically managed under the trusteeship and we believe that the secured and other creditors of the Realty Company are better protected than they were immediately before the Realty Company went into trusteeship. The value of the interests of unsecured creditors in the Realty Company will depend upon Shanghai real estate values. Whether the Realty Company will be reorganized is at the moment undetermined."

赫尔米克法官发布了四项命令，其中三项任命塞莱特博士分别为美亚银行、雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）和美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的清算人，第四项任命他为ARCO（即亚洲地产公司）受托人。这三项命令的措辞完全相同。命令指出：“鉴于弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）不幸逝世，本案目前无清算人，兹命令、裁定并宣告：乔治·塞莱特获任并特此被任命为清算人。”

“霍夫先生清算这些公司的任务极为艰巨。他在处理清算过程中众多复杂问题时所展现的能力、堪称典范的勇气以及公正态度，在很大程度上简化了完成公司清算的工作。我们一直在催收欠付银行的款项，并将于1936年6月15日左右向银行储户及其他债权人支付10%的股息。

“我们目前无法宣布向美亚金融公司债权人支付股息的日期，但希望能在不久的将来予以公布。雷文信托公司停业时，其资产几乎毫无价值。

“为该信托公司收得的款项极少，很可能没有任何资金可供分配给信托公司的普通债权人。我们的努力方向是在1936年底前，追回所有可追回的欠付银行、金融公司和信托公司的款项，以便支付进一步的红利，并旨在于1937年初最终结束这些公司的业务。

“亚洲地产公司在受托管理期间一直非常节俭地运营，我们相信，该地产公司的有担保债权人及其他债权人的权益保护状况，优于该公司进入受托管理之前的即刻状态。无担保债权人在该地产公司的权益价值将取决于上海的房地产价值。该地产公司是否会重组，目前尚未确定。”

这位银行清算人离开上海时，原计划在费城接受专家两个月的治疗。

抵达费城后，他入院观察，有一段时间他的情况似乎相当良好。约十天后病情恶化，又过了一周，外科医生决定进行扁桃体切除术。

霍夫先生去世的消息于周二清晨传至上海。这一消息令人震惊，因为这位清算人在许多圈子里都广为人知且深受喜爱。他自1933年起担任中国 RCA-Victor 公司的董事总经理。他于去年6月3日由美国驻华法院任命为雷文相关机构的清算人。

据悉，霍夫先生的葬礼将在其故乡费城举行。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 29, 1936

Taken By Death

Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, Managing Director of the R.C.A.-Victor Company of China and prominent American resident of Shanghai, who died at a hospital in Philadelphia Monday. News of his death was received here at 2 a.m. yesterday.

Dr. Sellett To Carry On At Bank Position

News Of Hough Death In Philadelphia Shocks City

Until the appointment of another liquidator to succeed the late Mr Frank L. Hough, who died early yesterday in Philadelphia, Dr George Sellett, prominent American attorney, will continue to remain in charge of the affairs of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation and allied institutions of the Raven Group.

In the meantime, Shanghai mourns the passing of one of the city's most prominent American business men. News of Mr. Hough's death came as a decided shock to all his many friends and business associates.

Mr. Hough died at 10.55 a.m. Monday following the removal of his tonsils at the University of Pennsylvania Hospital, where he had been a patient for several weeks. He left here on March 8 on the Empress of Japan and had expected to be back in Shanghai early in May.

One week after his arrival in Philadelphia, his native city, he entered the hospital for observation only. Shortly before leaving Shanghai, he had undergone a physical examination and discovered that his blood pressure was high. Later, he started suffering from eye trouble and it was primarily to have his eyes treated by Philadelphia specialists that prompted him to make the trip to the United States.

Cabled Nothing Serious

Upon entering the hospital, he cabled Mrs. Hough who remained in Shanghai, residing at their new home at 432 Avenue Haig, that nothing really serious had been discovered by the doctors, but added that he intended remaining at the hospital 10 or 12 days for observation. Another cable received a few days later was to the effect that physicians were of the opinion that there was no necessity for an operation.

Three days ago, a cable was received stating that physicians had decided to remove his tonsils in an effort to relieve his blood pressure. A few hours later another cable arrived stating that the operation had been performed but that Mr. Hough was in a serious condition. Late Monday afternoon, another message from the hospital at Philadelphia announced that he was not expected to live through the night. The cable announcing his death was received at the R.C.A.-Victor Offices, of which Mr. Hough was the Managing-Director, yesterday morning.

Both the R.C.A.-Victor and the offices of the liquidator of the Raven concerns were closed immediately on receipt of the tragic news, while the United States Court for China, which also was in session at the time, was adjourned for the day. One short case had been heard when Dr. Sellett, who had entered the courtroom, arose and informed the court of Mr. Hough's death. After paying brief tribute to the memory of the deceased, he suggested that court be adjourned.

"A Splendid Citizen"

Judge Milton J. Helmick granted the adjournment, stating: "The suggestion is well taken. Mr. Hough was an exemplary public servant, a splendid citizen and a faithful officer of this Court."

It is understood that a liquidator to succeed Mr. Hough may be appointed by Judge Helmick before the end of the current week.

Mr. Hough was born in Philadelphia in 1885 and would have been 51 years old next Monday. His father was a well-known newspaperman, having been Editor of the Philadelphia Bulletin for many years. He also owned a half-interest in the famous Philadelphia Athletics, world baseball champions at various times in the history of major league baseball.

Completing his education in Philadelphia, he became interested in the motion picture and electrical industries and joined the Thomas A. Edison Company in 1908. After spending a number of years in the factories and laboratories of the concern, Mr. Hough went on the road as a traveling representative for the Edison products. He spent three years traveling throughout the Northwestern United States, introducing light bulbs, phonographs and other products of the Edison concern to the then unmodernized districts of the American prairies. Thus Mr. Hough was an important factor in leaving the mark of the great Edison in the still wild hinterlands of the cattle and wheat country of the United States.

Installed Power Plants

One of his jobs while traveling through the Northwest was to assist and supervise the installation of power plants in the small towns and cities of the Dakotas, Wyoming, Montana and Western Nebraska. Many of these plants still remain in operation.

Possessing a thorough knowledge of the electrical industry and the electrical goods business, Mr. Hough soon became one of the crack men with the Edison concern and in 1918, came to Shanghai as a representative of the Edison-Electric Company. He remained in China until 1920 when he went to Java for the company, living there until 1922.

Upon his return to the United States, Mr. Hough joined the old Victor Talking Machine Company, and was sent to the Argentine to manage the company there. For the next 10 years, Mr. Hough made his headquarters at Buenos Aires. He returned to Camden in 1932 and came to Shanghai the following year as Managing-Director of the R.C.A.-Victor Company of China. He was named liquidator of the defunct Raven financial concerns and trustee of the Asia Realty Company by Judge Milton J. Helmick on June 3 of last year, about 10 days after the collapse of the American-Oriental Bank.

Mr. Hough took over the handling of the affairs of the concerns immediately. When the court seals on the bank were broken and he formally took over his office, there was only $7,000 in the vaults and some seven or eight millions outstanding. By dint of hard work against innumerable obstacles, Mr. Hough collected sufficient funds within a few weeks to pay off back salaries of the employees.

Efficient Liquidator

Within four months, he announced a payment of all depositors with accounts less than $50 in the bank. Some $60,000 was disbursed. By Christmas, he had collected more than $800,000 and had made a 7½ per cent payment to all depositors.

From the time he took over the liquidation of the Raven concerns until shortly before his departure, Mr. Hough spent many long hours in the office of the bank as well as the offices of R.C.A.-Victor. He fell ill last November but after remaining at home for a few days, returned to his offices and went back to work. He made one short trip to North China, and upon his return, announced that he was not feeling well.

No noticeable improvement in his condition was made and after the Raven and Brown trial, he was confined to his bed at home for some time. Upon his return to his office, eye trouble developed and it was then that he decided to consult specialists in America.

Mr. Hough was an ardent baseball fan and possessed expert knowledge of the game; knowledge attained during his early association with the Athletics. During the summer months of last year when he was literally buried with work, about the only recreation that he was able to find time to enjoy was an occasional motion picture and the Sunday and Saturday afternoon baseball games.

《字林西报》，1936年4月29日，星期三

溘然长逝

美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）清算人、中国 RCA-胜利公司（R.C.A.-Victor Company of China）董事总经理、上海知名美侨弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生，于周一在费城一家医院逝世。其死讯于昨日凌晨2时传抵此处。

塞莱特博士将继续担任银行职务

费城霍夫死讯震惊全市

在任命另一位清算人接替已于昨日清晨在费城逝世的弗兰克·L·霍夫先生之前，著名美国律师乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士将继续负责已停业的美亚银行公司及雷文集团（Raven Group）相关机构的事务。

与此同时，上海为一位本市最杰出的美国商界人士的离世而哀悼。霍夫先生的死讯令其众多好友及商业伙伴深感震惊。

霍夫先生于周一上午10时55分在宾夕法尼亚大学医院去世，此前他因切除扁桃体在该院接受治疗，并已住院数周。他于3月8日乘“日本皇后号”（Empress of Japan）离开上海，原预计五月初返回上海。

抵达故乡费城一周后，他入院仅做观察。在离开上海前不久，他曾接受体检，发现血压偏高。随后，他开始遭受眼疾困扰，正是为了请费城的专家治疗眼疾，才促使他前往美国。

致电称并无大碍

入院后，他向仍留在上海、居住在海格路432号新居的霍夫夫人发电报称，医生并未发现真正严重的问题，但补充说他打算在医院留观10至12天。几天后收到的另一封电报大意是，医生认为无需进行手术。

三天前，收到一封电报称，医生决定切除其扁桃体，以试图缓解其高血压。几小时后，又收到一封电报称手术已完成，但霍夫先生情况危急。周一下午晚些时候，费城医院发来的另一则消息宣布，预计他无法熬过当晚。宣布其死讯的电报于昨日上午送达霍夫先生担任董事总经理的 RCA-胜利公司办公室。

获悉这一悲剧消息后，RCA-胜利公司及雷文企业清算人办公室立即关闭，当时正在开庭的美国在华法院也休庭一天。刚审理完一个简短案件后，进入法庭的塞莱特博士起身向法庭通报了霍夫先生的死讯。在对死者致以简短的敬意后，他建议休庭。

“一位优秀的公民”

米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官批准了休庭申请，并表示：“该建议甚妥。霍夫先生是一位模范的公仆，一位优秀的公民，也是本法庭忠实的官员。”

据悉，赫尔米克法官可能会在本周末前任命一位清算人来接替霍夫先生。

霍夫先生于1885年出生于费城，下周一他将年满51岁。其父是一位著名的报人，曾多年担任《费城公报》（Philadelphia Bulletin）编辑。他还拥有著名的费城运动家队（Philadelphia Athletics）的一半股权，该队在职业棒球大联盟历史上曾多次获得世界棒球冠军。

在费城完成学业后，他对电影和电气行业产生兴趣，并于1908年加入托马斯·A·爱迪生公司（Thomas A. Edison Company）。在该公司的工厂和实验室工作数年后，霍夫先生作为爱迪生产品的旅行代表外出奔波。他花了三年时间在美国西北部各地旅行，向当时尚未现代化的美国大草原地区推广灯泡、留声机及其他爱迪生公司的产品。因此，霍夫先生是在美国尚属荒野的畜牧和小麦产区留下伟大爱迪生印记的重要因素。

安装发电厂

他在西北部旅行期间的工作之一，是协助和监督在南达科他州、怀俄明州、蒙大拿州和内布拉斯加州西部的小城镇安装发电厂。其中许多电厂至今仍在运行。

凭借对电气行业和电器商品业务的透彻了解，霍夫先生很快成为爱迪生公司中的佼佼者，并于1918年作为爱迪生电气公司（Edison-Electric Company）的代表来到上海。他留在中国直至1920年，随后为公司前往爪哇，在那里居住至1922年。

回到美国后，霍夫先生加入了老维克多留声机公司（Victor Talking Machine Company），并被派往阿根廷管理那里的公司。在接下来的10年里，霍夫先生以布宜诺斯艾利斯为总部。他于1932年返回卡姆登（Camden），并于次年以中国 RCA-胜利公司董事总经理的身份来到上海。去年6月3日，即在美亚银行倒闭约10天后，他被米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官任命为已停业的雷文金融企业的清算人及亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）的受托人。

霍夫先生立即接手处理这些企业的事务。当银行上的法院封条被揭开，他正式就职时，金库中仅有7,000美元，而外债高达七八百万美元。凭借不畏无数障碍的辛勤工作，霍夫先生在几周内筹集到足够的资金，支付了员工的欠薪。

高效的清算人

四个月内，他宣布向银行存款不足50美元的所有储户进行赔付。共发放了约60,000美元。到圣诞节时，他已筹集超过800,000美元，并向所有储户支付了7.5%的款项。

从接手雷文企业的清算工作直到离境前不久，霍夫先生在银行办公室以及 RCA-胜利公司办公室度过了许多漫长的时光。他于去年11月生病，在家休息几天后，便返回办公室继续工作。他曾短暂前往华北旅行，回来后表示身体不适。

他的病情未见明显好转，在雷文与布朗案（Raven and Brown trial）审判结束后，他在家中卧床休养了一段时间。重返办公室后，眼疾发作，于是决定赴美咨询专家。

霍夫先生是一位狂热的棒球迷，并对这项运动拥有专业的知识；这些知识源于他早期与运动家队的关联。在去年夏季那些他几乎被工作埋没的日子里，他唯一能抽出时间享受的娱乐活动，不过是偶尔看场电影，以及观看周六和周日下午的棒球比赛。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 29, 1936
A.-O. Bank
Failure Hits
City Hospital
St. Luke's 1935 Report
Reveals No New Build-
ing Planned Now
FUNDS SAVED FOR
20 YEARS LOST
Interior Floods Bring
Influx Of Poor
Patients

Listing the failure of the Ameri-
can-Oriental Banking Corporation
as a great blow to its finances, the
1935 report of the St. Luke's Hos-
pital issued yesterday disclosed that
the proposed new hospital, labora-
tory and nurses training school
building will be postponed inde-
finitely.
The hospital also ended the year
with a $6,000 deficit, due to the
general depression in Shanghai and
the influx of destitute patients from
flood areas.
On the money lost due to the
bank failure: the report said:
"Practically the whole of our new
building fund was deposited in the
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration, the Raven Trust Com-
pany or loaned to the Asia Realty
Company. In round figures we had
in these institutions approximately
$727,000. It seems that the best we
can hope for is to recover about
60 per cent and most of this from
what was in the Asia Realty Com-
pany.
"These funds," the hospital Super-
intendent continued, "represented
20 years' of accumulation from
many donors, so that the prospects
for our new plant are not very
bright. However, the sick and the
injured in Shanghai must be cared
for, so we are preparing to fix up
our old building as much as pos-
sible and carry on."
Floods Bring Patients
During the year, floods in many
parts of China brought an increase
of patients to the St. Luke's. On
financing the hospitalization of
these people, the report said, "These
patients, of course, are unable to
pay any part of their expenses and
we had trouble getting rid of them
after they were healed.
"When we offered them fare to
go back home they simply said that
there was no use of going back as
the country was covered with water.
The only thing that could be done
was to give them small amounts
from our Social Service Fund to
help them start anew in Shanghai,"
the report continued.
"There were several pathetic
cases of children who had lost their
homes and in one case at least, a
whole family had been drowned ex-
cept a 12-year-old boy who was
brought to the St. Luke's by a rick-
sha coolie who found him lying in
an alleyway. He had stolen rides
on river boats to get to Shanghai
and became ill while begging on the
streets. We were happy to be able
to find a home for him with the
National Child Welfare Associa-
tion," the report revealed.

Drain On Resources
All these free patients, the St.
Luke's Superintendent pointed out,
were a drain on the hospital's re-
sources. Also, the depression in
Shanghai forced many people who
would otherwise go to private rooms
to enter wards where the fee was
not enough to cover their care.
At present, the hospital, forced
to remain in its old quarters, is in
need of money to retile the kit-
chen. This will cost about $1,400.
Also, the medical building of the
hospital, now insufficiently heated
with stoves and grates, is needing
a new furnace. Some $6,400 is
expected from donors for this
purpose.
During 1935, St. Luke's received
a total of $16,355.30 in contributions
and $29,698.60 in subsidies from
the Shanghai Municipal Council
and the American Church Mission
appropriation.
A total of 113,383 cases were
treated during the year by the hos-
pital's out-patient department.
Some 3,012 persons used the wards,
totaling 49,784 days in hospital
service.

《字林西报》，1936年4月29日，星期三

美亚银行
倒闭冲击
市立医院
圣路加医院1935年报告
揭示目前无新建计划
二十年积蓄付诸东流
内部水患引来贫困患者激增

圣路加医院（St. Luke's Hospital）昨日发布的1935年度报告将美亚银行公司的倒闭列为对其财务的重大打击，并披露拟议中的新医院、实验室及护士培训学校大楼将无限期推迟。

由于上海普遍的经济萧条以及来自洪水灾区的贫困患者涌入，该医院年底还出现了6,000美元的赤字。

关于因银行倒闭造成的资金损失，报告称：
“我们几乎全部的新楼基金都存入美亚银行公司、雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company），或贷给了亚洲地产公司。粗略计算，我们在这些机构的存款约为727,000美元。看来我们最多只能指望收回约60%，且大部分来自亚洲地产公司的存款。”

医院院长继续说道：“这些资金代表了众多捐赠者二十年的积累，因此我们新设施的前景并不乐观。然而，必须照顾上海的病患和伤者，所以我们正准备尽可能修缮旧大楼，并维持运营。”

洪水带来患者

这一年，中国许多地区的洪水导致圣路加医院的患者增加。关于资助这些人的住院治疗费用，报告称：“这些患者当然无力支付任何费用，而且他们在痊愈后，我们也难以让他们离开。
当我们提供路费让他们回家时，他们只是说回去没用，因为家乡遍地是水。唯一能做的，就是从我们的社会服务基金中给他们少量资助，帮助他们在上海重新开始，”报告继续写道。
“有几个失去家园的儿童案例令人唏嘘，其中至少有一个案例，全家溺亡，只剩下一名12岁男孩，由一名在巷子里发现他的黄包车夫带到圣路加医院。他是搭便船来到上海的，在街头乞讨时病倒。我们很高兴能为他在全国儿童福利协会（National Child Welfare Association）找到一个归宿，”报告透露。

资源消耗

圣路加医院院长指出，所有这些免费患者都在消耗医院的资源。此外，上海的经济萧条迫使许多原本会住私人病房的人转入普通病房，而其支付的费用不足以覆盖护理成本。

目前，医院被迫留在旧址，急需资金重新铺设厨房瓷砖。这将花费约1,400美元。此外，医院的医疗大楼目前仅靠火炉和炉栅供暖，不足以满足需求，需要更换新的锅炉。预计将从捐赠者那里为此目的筹集约6,400美元。

1935年间，圣路加医院共收到捐款16,355.30美元，以及来自上海工部局和美国教会使命拨款（American Church Mission appropriation）的补贴29,698.60美元。

全年医院门诊部共诊治病例113,383例。约有3,012人使用病房服务，累计住院天数为49,784天。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 2, 1936 D. 3

KLEFFEL APPEAL SET
FOR APRIL 18

Ex-Bank Manager And
S.M.P. Seek Reversal
Of Court Decision

The hearing of the appeal in
the case of Julius Kleffel, German,
former general manager and vice-
president of the now defunct
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration, who was recently con-
victed on a charge of breach of
confidence, will be heard before
the Second Branch of the Kiang-
su High Court on Saturday morn-
ing, April 18.

Mr. Kleffel is appealing against
the decision of Judge Dzien, hand-
ed down in the First Special Dis-
trict Court last month, in finding
him guilty of breach of confidence
and sentencing him to six months'
imprisonment and a fine of $1,000,
as well as ordering him to pay
back $20,000 to Mr. Henry Young,
Chinese, one of the complaining
witnesses.

The Shanghai Municipal Police
has also appealed the decision
of Judge Dzien. The legal repre-
sentatives of the Police seek the
reversal of the lower court's deci-
sion in acquitting Mr. Kleffel on
charges of fraud and misappro-
priation.

Action against Mr. Kleffel was
commenced early in February of
this year, shortly after the close
of the now famous Raven and
Brown trial in the United States
Court for China. Messrs. Frank J.
Raven and J. Warner Brown were
sentenced to five and two years'
imprisonment, respectively, in the
U.S. Penitentiary at McNeill's
Island, for fraud and misappro-
priation in connection with the
affairs of the now defunct Ameri-
can-Oriental Finance Corporation.

Mr. Kleffel upon being summon-
ed before the Chinese tribunal to
answer to charges of fraud, mis-
appropriation and breach of con-
fidence, in connection with the
disappearance of $32,000 from
safe-keeping vaults of the bank,
denied all knowledge of same. He
placed the blame on the shoulders
of Mr. Dick Huang, the bank's
compradore and a Chinese em-
ployee.

Following numerous hearings he
was acquitted of charges of fraud
and misappropriation, but convict-
ed for breach of confidence. Dur-
ing the trial he was allowed to
remain on bail of $20,000 and
during the period of appeal the
same bail is being allowed.

《字林西报》，1936年4月2日，星期四 D. 3

克莱费尔上诉案定于
4月18日审理

前银行经理与
上海公共租界工部局警务处寻求推翻
法院判决

德国人朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）系已倒闭的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前总经理兼副总裁，近期因违反信托罪被定罪。其上诉听证会将于4月18日（星期六）上午在江苏高等法院第二分院进行。

克莱费尔先生正在对迪岑（Dzien）法官上月在第一特区地方法院作出的判决提出上诉。该判决认定其犯有违反信托罪，判处六个月监禁及罚款1,000美元，并责令其向投诉证人之一、华人杨亨利（Henry Young）先生退还20,000美元。

上海公共租界工部局警务处亦对迪岑法官的判决提出上诉。警方的法律代表寻求推翻下级法院就欺诈和挪用公款指控宣告克莱费尔先生无罪的判决。

针对克莱费尔先生的诉讼始于今年2月初，即中美联合法庭著名的雷文与布朗案（Raven and Brown trial）结案后不久。弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生因涉及已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）事务中的欺诈和挪用公款行为，分别被判处五年和两年监禁，服刑于麦克尼尔岛（McNeill's Island）美国联邦监狱。

克莱费尔先生被传唤至中国法庭，就银行保管库中32,000美元失踪一事所涉及的欺诈、挪用公款和违反信托指控进行答辩，他否认对此有任何知情。他将责任归咎于该银行买办黄迪克（Dick Huang）先生及一名华籍雇员。

经过多次聆讯，他被宣告欺诈和挪用公款罪名不成立，但违反信托罪成立。在审判期间，他获准以20,000美元保释金保外候审，在上诉期间仍维持同等保释条件。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MARCH 29, 1936

Kleffel Fails
To Appear
At Appeal

Case Is Adjourned Sine
Die At Request Of
Attorney

Mr. Julius Kleffel, former Manager of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, failed to appear in 2nd Kiangsu High Court yesterday morning for the first hearing of his appeal against the decision of the First Special District Court, sentencing him to six months imprisonment and to pay a fine of $1,000 for breach of confidence in connection with two safe-keeping transactions handled by the bank before it closed last May.

Police representatives and Messrs. R. T. Bryan, Jr., Municipal Advocate, and Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, appeared in court, ready to proceed with the case. Mr. Kleffel was represented by his attorneys, Dr. A. Grossman, and associates. Counsel for Mr. Kleffel asked for an adjournment and the case was remanded sine die. The proceedings were conducted in chambers. No indication was given as to when the appeal proceedings might get under way.

While, Mr. Kleffel has appealed against the decision of the lower court convicting him of breach of confidence; the Shanghai Municipal Police have filed appeal against the action of the First Special District Court in acquitting the former banker of fraud and misappropriation. This latter step, it has been pointed out, was taken as a counter-move against the Kleffel appeal.

Mr. Kleffel was tried for fraud, misappropriation and breach of confidence in connection with two safe-keeping transactions, involving $32,000. The money was placed in the bank, $20,000 by Mr. Henry Young, Chinese, and Mr. M. M. Epport, Russian, during April, 1935, a month before the bank closed. The two depositors were given safe-keeping receipts but later, the money was diverted to call account and when the bank closed, it was not in the safe-keeping vault.

Mr. Kleffel denied that he had anything to do with the diversion of the $32,000 to call account, nor did he know about the transactions until after the bank had closed. He placed the blame for the irregularity on the shoulders of the Chinese comprador and a Chinese clerk in charge of safe-keeping.

（手写签名：R. A. Grossman）
（手写签名：Julius Kleffel）

《大美晚报》，1936年3月29日，星期日

克莱费尔未
出席上诉
庭审

应律师请求
案件无限期休庭

美亚银行公司（已倒闭）前经理朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）先生昨日上午未出现在江苏高等法院第二分院，参加针对第一特区地方法院判决的首次上诉听证。原判因其在该行去年5月关闭前处理的两笔保管业务中违反信托，判处其六个月监禁并罚款1,000美元。

警方代表、市政检察官小R·T·布莱恩（R. T. Bryan, Jr.）先生及助理市政检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生出庭，准备推进案件审理。克莱费尔先生由其律师A·格罗斯曼（A. Grossman）博士及其同事代理。克莱费尔的辩护律师请求休庭，案件被无限期推迟（sine die）。诉讼程序在内庭进行。目前尚未表明上诉程序何时可能启动。

虽然克莱费尔先生已就下级法院判定其违反信托罪的判决提出上诉；但上海公共租界工部局警务处已就第一特区地方法院宣告这位前银行家欺诈和挪用公款无罪的决定提起上诉。据指出，后一步骤是作为对克莱费尔上诉的反制措施而采取的。

克莱费尔先生因涉及两笔总额32,000美元的保管交易，受审欺诈、挪用公款和违反信托罪。这笔钱由华人杨亨利（Henry Young）先生和俄国人M·M·埃波特（M. M. Epport）先生于1935年4月存入该行，即银行关闭前一个月。两名存款人获得了保管收据，但后来这笔钱被转入活期账户，当银行关闭时，款项已不在保管库中。

克莱费尔先生否认自己参与将32,000美元转入活期账户的行为，并称直到银行关闭后才知晓这些交易。他将这一违规行为的责任归咎于华籍买办和负责保管的一名华籍职员。

（手写签名：R. A. Grossman）
（手写签名：Julius Kleffel）

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, MARCH 27, 1936
138.5d
Appeal Filed
By S.M.P. In
Kleffel Case
Seek Reversal Of Ac-
quittal On Two
Charges
EX-BANKER ALSO
APPEALS DECISION
Police Action Reported
To Be Counter-
Move
The Shanghai Municipal Police
have appealed against the decision
of Judge Dzien, of the First
Special District Court, in handing
down an acquittal against Mr. Julius
Kleffel, former Manager of the de-
funct American-Oriental Banking
Corporation, on charges of fraud and
misappropriation, a CHINA PRESS
reporter learned yesterday.
In the meantime, Mr. Kleffel has
filed appeal against the decision of
Judge Dzien in finding him guilty
on a charge of breach of confidence,
under which the accused was
sentenced to five months' imprison-
ment and ordered to pay a fine of
$1,000, as well as to pay $20,000 to
Mr. Henry Young, Chinese, one of
the complaining witnesses. First
hearing of the appeal will be held
in 2nd Kiangsu High Court at 10
o'clock tomorrow morning.
Action of the police in filing
appeal against the lower court's
decision was made as a counter-
move, it was reported.
The Kleffel case had its beginning
shortly after the close of the now
famous Raven and Brown trial in
the United States Court for China,
in which Messrs. Frank J. Raven
and John Warner Brown were
sentenced to five and two-year
terms at the U. S. Federal Prison,
McNeill's Island for fraud and mis-
appropriation in connection with the
affairs of the defunct American-
Oriental Finance Corporation.
Mr. Kleffel, a German, was sum-
moned before the First Special Dis-
trict Court to answer charges of
fraud, misappropriation and breach
of confidence in connection with two
safe-keeping transactions in the
A.O.B.C. The chief complaining
witness was Mr. Young, who test-
ified that he had placed $20,000 in
cash in safe-keeping with the bank
early in April, 1935, shortly before
the bank closed its doors. It was
further brought out that Mr. M. M.
Epport, Russian, had placed $12,000
in safe-keeping the latter part of
April the same year. When the safe-
keeping vault was opened after the
bank had closed, it was discovered
that these two sums had not been
placed in safe-keeping although re-
ceipts for that purpose had been
given to the customers. The money
had been diverted to call account.
Mr. Kleffel flatly denied that he
knew anything about the trans-
action and a good bit of the blame
was placed on the shoulders of the
compradore, Mr. "Dick" Wang, and
a Chinese clerk in charge of safe-
keeping. Mr. Kleffel was acquitted
of fraud and misappropriation
charges but was convicted of breach
of confidence. He was also ordered
to pay back the $20,000 lost in the
bank by Mr. Young.
Mr. Kleffel was under $20,000 cash
bond during the course of the trial
and this bond was held in force
during the period of appeal.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
在克莱费尔案中
提起上诉
寻求推翻两项
指控的无罪判决
前银行家亦
对判决提出上诉
据报道警方行动为
反制措施
据《大美晚报》记者昨日获悉，上海公共租界工部局警务处已就第一特区地方法院迪岑（Dzien）法官对已倒闭的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前经理朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）先生在欺诈和挪用公款指控上作出无罪判决的决定提出上诉。

与此同时，克莱费尔先生已就迪岑法官判定其违反信托罪成立的判决提出上诉，据此被告被判处五个月监禁，罚款1,000美元，并责令向投诉证人之一、华人杨亨利（Henry Young）先生支付20,000美元。上诉首次听证将于明日上午10时在江苏高等法院第二分院举行。

据报道，警方就下级法院判决提起上诉的行动是作为一种反制措施。

克莱费尔案始于中美联合法庭著名的雷文与布朗案结案后不久，该案中弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和约翰·沃纳·布朗（John Warner Brown）先生因涉及已倒闭的美亚金融公司事务中的欺诈和挪用公款行为，在麦克尼尔岛（McNeill's Island）美国联邦监狱分别被判处五年和两年刑期。

德国人克莱费尔先生被传唤至第一特区地方法院，就美亚银行公司两笔保管交易中涉及的欺诈、挪用公款和违反信托指控进行答辩。主要投诉证人是杨先生，他作证称于1935年4月初，即银行关闭前不久，将20,000美元现金交由该行保管。进一步查明的事实显示，俄国人M·M·埃波特（M. M. Epport）先生于同年4月下旬将12,000美元交由保管。银行关闭后打开保管库时，发现这两笔款项并未存入保管库，尽管已向客户开具了相应的收据。这笔钱已被转入活期账户。

克莱费尔先生断然否认对该交易有任何了解，并将大部分责任归咎于买办“迪克”王（"Dick" Wang）先生和负责保管的一名华籍职员。克莱费尔先生被宣告欺诈和挪用公款罪名不成立，但违反信托罪成立。他还被责令偿还杨先生在该行损失的20,000美元。

克莱费尔先生在审判期间以20,000美元现金保释，该保释在上诉期间继续有效。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 11, 1936

Kleffel Given Six Months'
Term And $1,000 Fine

Former A.-O.B.C. Manager Found Guilty Of Breach
Of Confidence, Ordered To Pay $20,000; To
Retain Liberty During Appeal

Mr. Julius Kleffel, German, former General Manager and Vice-President of the now defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, was sentenced to six months' imprisonment and fined $1,000 by Judge Dzien in the First Special District Court yesterday morning upon being found guilty on the charge of breach of confidence in connection with the disappearance from the safe-keeping vaults of the bank of $32,000 at the time of its closure on May 24, last.

Judge Dzien, in passing sentence, acquitted Mr. Kleffel on charges of misappropriation and fraud, which were also framed against him by the prosecution. In dealing with the civil claim of $20,000 filed against Mr. Kleffel by Mr. Henry Young in connection with the criminal action, the jurist ordered the former General Manager of the bank to pay back the money together with interest at five per cent. per annum.

Mr. Kleffel was not present in court at the time that sentence was pronounced by Judge Dzien, but was waiting in his motor car parked on Tsepoo Road, just outside the court compound, to hear his fate. In passing sentence Judge Dzien ruled that Mr. Kleffel would have to be taken into custody and confined to Ward Road Gaol immediately, but upon application of the defence counsel, Dr. A. Grossman, he allowed the accused to remain on his original cash bail of $20,000 during the period of appeal. Dr. Grossman stated yesterday morning that an appeal would be filed immediately with the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court.

Third Officer Sentenced

Mr. Kleffel is the third officer of the defunct Raven organizations to be tried and sentenced. The first two, Mr. Frank Jay Raven, President of the Bank and the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and Mr. J. Warner Brown, Vice-President and Manager of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, were sentenced to five and two years' imprisonment, respectively, by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China on February 3, of this year. The two American officers were found guilty on seven charges of embezzlement and fraudulent false pretences following a trial lasting a month.

Immediately upon conviction both Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown were confined in the Ward Road Gaol and later they were sent in custody of the captain of the President McKinley to the United States to serve their sentences in the McNeil's Island Penitentiary. Mr. Brown had waived his right of appeal, while Mr. Raven has filed an appeal, his attorney, Mr. Richard T. Evans of Tientsin, having sailed for the United States a fortnight ago, to represent him there.

Prosecution A Surprise

The prosecution of Mr. Julius Kleffel, commenced more than eight months after the failure of the bank, came as a big surprise, especially after the defence introduced into evidence a testimonial given to Mr. Kleffel by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the Raven companies, on November 24, last. In this testimonial, Mr. Hough stated that Mr. Kleffel had carried out his duties as bank manager properly and that he was in no way indebted to the bank. During the trial Mr. Robert T. Bryan, Municipal Advocate, called Mr. Kleffel a "crooked banker" and attacked Mr. Hough for allegedly shielding Mr. Kleffel.

The complaint against Mr. Kleffel was signed by Mr. Henry Young, a Chinese who claimed to have lost $20,000 and Mr. M. M. Eppert, a Russian who alleged the loss of $12,000. Mr. Hough's signature was also on the complaint. He stated that he had signed it upon the request of the U.S. District Attorney, Mr. Felthan Watson, and Mr. Bryan, the Municipal Advocate, being told that they wished to thoroughly investigate the affairs of the bank.

Mr. Kleffel was charged under Article 336, 339 and 342 of the Chinese Criminal Code with misappropriation, fraud and breach of confidence. It was alleged by the prosecution that under his instructions the two deposits amounting to $32,000 were taken from the safekeeping account and placed in deposit on call account. The two chief witnesses for the prosecution, Mr. Dick Huang, the comprador of the defunct bank, and Mr. S. E. Tsu, the head of the safekeeping department, alleged that Mr. Kleffel knew about the two transactions. The accused denied this, maintaining that it was impossible for him to keep track of hundreds of transactions that had passed through the bank daily. He placed the blame for the diversion of the two accounts from safekeeping to deposit on call account on the comprador and the head of the safekeeping department.

Mr. Walter Francis Raven, former assistant manager and office manager of the bank, testified that Mr. Kleffel knew nothing regarding the Young transaction, while the Eppert transaction he had brought to the attention of Mr. Kleffel, but was told to use his own judgment about it. Mr. Raven maintained that he signed the two safekeeping receipts on the understanding that Mr. Tsu as head of the safekeeping department had received the cash and placed it in the vaults. Mr. Tsu's signature also appeared on the receipts.

《字林西报》，1936年3月11日，星期三

克莱费尔（Kleffel）被判六个月监禁
及罚款1,000美元

前美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）经理被裁定违反信托罪成立，责令支付20,000美元；上诉期间保释在外

德国人朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）先生，系已停业的美亚银行前总经理兼副总裁，昨日上午在第一特区地方法院由迪岑（Dzien）法官审理，因被裁定在该行去年5月24日关闭时涉及保险库内32,000美元失踪一案中犯有违反信托罪，判处其监禁六个月并罚款1,000美元。

迪岑法官在宣判时，宣告克莱费尔先生无罪，免除了检方对其提出的挪用公款和欺诈指控。在处理亨利·杨（Henry Young）先生就刑事诉讼向克莱费尔先生提起的20,000美元民事索赔时，这位法官命令该银行前总经理偿还这笔款项，并按年利率百分之五支付利息。

迪岑法官宣判时，克莱费尔先生并未出庭，而是在法院大院外停在芝罘路（Tsepoo Road）的汽车里等候判决结果。迪岑法官在宣判时裁定，克莱费尔先生必须立即被收押并关入华德路监狱（Ward Road Gaol），但经辩护律师格罗斯曼（A. Grossman）博士申请，他允许被告在上诉期间维持原有的20,000美元现金保释。格罗斯曼博士昨日上午表示，将立即向江苏高等法院第二分院提出上诉。

第三名高管被判刑

克莱费尔先生是已倒闭的雷文（Raven）集团中被审判和判刑的第三名高管。前两名高管，即银行及美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）总裁弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）先生，以及美亚金融公司副总裁兼经理J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生，于今年2月3日由美国在华法院的米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官分别判处五年和两年监禁。这两名美国高管在为期一个月的审判后，被裁定七项挪用公款和欺诈性虚假陈述罪名成立。

定罪后，雷文先生和布朗先生立即被关入华德路监狱，随后他们在“麦金莱总统号”（President McKinley）船长的监管下被送往美国，在麦克尼尔岛监狱（McNeil's Island Penitentiary）服刑。布朗先生放弃了上诉权，而雷文先生已提出上诉，其代理人、天津的理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）律师已于两周前乘船前往美国，在那里代表他进行诉讼。

起诉令人意外

对朱利叶斯·克莱费尔先生的起诉是在银行倒闭八个多月后才开始的，这引起了巨大的意外，尤其是在辩方于去年11月24日向法庭提交了一份由雷文公司清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生写给克莱费尔先生的推荐信作为证据之后。在这封推荐信中，霍夫先生表示，克莱费尔先生恰当地履行了银行经理的职责，且不欠银行任何债务。在审判期间，市公廨检察官罗伯特·T·布莱恩（Robert T. Bryan）先生称克莱费尔为“奸诈银行家”，并攻击霍夫先生涉嫌包庇克莱费尔先生。

对克莱费尔先生的控告由声称损失20,000美元的华人亨利·杨先生和声称损失12,000美元的俄国人M·M·埃珀特（M. M. Eppert）先生签署。霍夫先生的签名也在控告书上。他表示，他是应美国地区检察官费尔森·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生和市公廨检察官布莱恩先生的要求签署的，因为他们被告知希望彻底调查该银行的事务。

克莱费尔先生被依据《中华民国刑法》第336、339和342条指控犯有挪用公款、欺诈和违反信托罪。检方指控称，在他的指示下，两笔共计32,000美元的存款从保管账户中被取出，并存入活期存款账户。检方的两名主要证人，即已倒闭银行的买办黄迪克（Dick Huang，音译）先生和保管部主管徐S. E.（S. E. Tsu，音译）先生，指称克莱费尔先生知晓这两笔交易。被告否认了这一说法，坚称他不可能跟踪每天经过银行的数百笔交易。他将这两笔账户从保管账户转为活期存款账户的责任归咎于买办和保管部主管。

银行前助理经理兼办公室主任沃尔特·弗朗西斯·雷文（Walter Francis Raven）先生作证说，克莱费尔先生对杨先生的交易一无所知，而对于埃珀特先生的交易，他曾提请克莱费尔先生注意，但被告知自行斟酌处理。雷文先生坚持认为，他签署两张保管收据是基于这样的理解：即作为保管部主管的徐先生已收到现金并将其放入保险库。徐先生的签名也出现在收据上。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MARCH 1, 1936

Kleffel Is Accused As
A “Crooked Banker” By
The Municipal Advocate

Mr. Bryan Makes Ringing Indictment Of Accused In
Closing Speech For The Prosecution; Says Every
Possible Irregularity Was Committed

LIQUIDATOR OF A.-O.B.C. SUBJECTED TO
CAUSTIC CRITICISM FOR HIS STAND

“I submit that the evidence in this case has disclosed a nefarious story of criminality, embezzlement, fraud, negligence, mismanagement, breach of confidence, deception, falsehood and prevarication,” said Mr. Robert T. Bryan, Jnr., Municipal Advocate, in the First Special District Court yesterday morning in summing up the case for the prosecution against Mr. Julius Kleffel, former General Manager and Vice-President of the now defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation.

Mr. Kleffel is charged with misappropriation, fraud and breach of confidence under Articles 336, 339 and 342 of the Chinese Criminal Code in connection with the disappearance of $32,000 from the safekeeping vault of the A.-O.B.C.

Complainants in the case are Mr. Young, a Chinese, who deposited $20,000, and Mr. M. M. Eppert, who deposited $12,000 with the Bank for safekeeping in April, 1935, shortly before the institution crashed, together with the other Raven concerns.

The accused, who has pleaded not guilty, declaring that he knew nothing of the two accounts on which the charges are based, is represented by Dr. Grossman and Dr. D. S. Chen. Dr. Chen addressed the Court after the conclusion of the Municipal Advocate’s speech and an adjournment was then ordered to Tuesday morning at 10 o’clock, when it is expected that Dr. Grossman will sum up for his client.

Answering the contention of the defence that Mr. Dick Huang, who was the comprador of the Bank, was responsible for the mishandling of safekeeping deposits, Mr. Bryan, early in his speech, which occupied a full hour, declared that no such suggestion could be seriously entertained.

Roles Of The Parties

“Compradore Huang was only a marionette. Kleffel was the master mind who pulled the strings. Had Huang not done what Kleffel wanted him to do, Huang would have been discharged. Now we have the spectacle of Kleffel, who operated behind the scenes as the master mind, wanting to blame everything on the comprador. It must be admitted that, according to the evidence, Huang was not exactly what one could call a scrupulously honest man, but that fact does not exonerate Kleffel, who held the responsible positions of General Manager and Vice-President.

After severely criticizing the evidence given by Walter F. Raven, Mr. Bryan went on to contend that the evidence showed Kleffel to have committed about every irregularity and every malpractice a banker could commit.

“Article 34 of the Chinese Banking Law prohibits a bank from granting any loan which is in excess of 10 per cent. of its capital. Yet we have it in evidence that Kleffel, as manager of the A.-O.B.C., granted one loan which amounted to $2,500,000, equal to almost the entire capital of the Bank.

“This sum was loaned to Harking Motors, in which two officers of the Bank were directors. The Liquidator of the Bank has been able to recover only $400,000 of this sum.

Real Estate Loans

“The Chinese Banking Law prohibits loans on real estate, except in special circumstances which do not appear in this case. Yet Kleffel lent $1,300,000 to the Asia Realty Company. And this money was lent, if you please, not on a first mortgage, but on a second mortgage. The Liquidator of the Bank has been unable to collect a cent.”

Mr. Bryan then went on to state that Kleffel had granted loans to officers, directors and employees of the Bank, and to his own relatives, without any proper security. He even persuaded the comprador of the Bank to go into business with his (Kleffel’s) brother and advanced them the Bank’s money for the purpose.

“And on top of all this he permitted the Raven family to use the Bank as a pocket book,” counsel declaimed. “Even more, he speculated in gold bars with the Bank’s credit. Now he tells us that he owes the Bank nothing, that he owes the comprador nothing. But the fact remains that at one time he did owe the Bank money and that he did use the Bank’s credit for his speculations. The only difference between Kleffel, on the one hand, and Raven and Brown, on the other, is that the former was more lucky than the latter. Raven and Brown lost on their speculations and Kleffel won and made money.

“Kleffel says he lost money when the Bank closed down. If this is true, he could well afford to lose it, for he made plenty by speculating with the Bank’s credit.”

Knew It Was Wrong

Coming to the charges themselves, Mr. Bryan said Kleffel knew it was wrong to transfer customers’ safekeeping deposits from safekeeping to call deposit. This was precisely why he put nothing in writing regarding the $20,000 and $12,000.

“We have to consider the defendant’s culpability in the light of his general practices as manager of the Bank. On a previous occasion he pledged $82,000 worth of debentures, the property of the Shanghai American School, and later he had to redeem them with money taken from his own pocket in order to avoid getting into trouble.

“The most conclusive evidence of the defendant’s guilt, however, is the action of Dr. Grossman, his counsel, in approaching the comprador with a view to settling this case out of Court. This Court is entitled to assume that Dr. Grossman acted on Kleffel’s instructions, because Kleffel did not want to go to Court. This is virtually an admission of guilt on the part of the defendant Kleffel.”

Criticism Of Hough

Mr. Bryan then passed on to a criticism of the role played by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the Raven concerns, in regard to Mr. Kleffel, saying that he did so with great regret. “I regret it,” he said, “but I have my duty to perform.”

“It was Mr. Hough’s business to collect debts owing to the A.-O.B.C. and distribute them among the creditors—not to go around whitewashing crooked bank managers, as he did in the testimony he gave to Kleffel and in the evidence which he tendered in this Court......

“He had the temerity to come into this Court and express the opinion that Kleffel is not guilty, despite the evidence that Kleffel committed every possible irregularity.”

Concluding his speech, M. Bryan said that many people had been pauperized by the failure of the A.-O.B.C. A verdict of guilty would not restore what had been lost, nor yet bring back to life the man who committed suicide when he lost all he had in the crash.

“But it will show that this Court is not prepared to tolerate dishonest bankers.”

Defence Opens

Dr. D. S. Chen then spoke for the defence in Chinese and in the course of his remarks asserted that the proposal made by Dr. Grossman to the comprador for a settlement of the case out of court did not refer to the criminal action but to the civil claims for $20,000 and $12,000 which were at the foundation of the charges.

Dr. Chen went on to say that the recent sensational Raven-Brown trial in the United States Court for China had had the effect of casting suspicion on everyone who had held office in any of the Raven companies. Because of this, without previous careful investigation, an innocent man, whose family had lived in China for over 50 years, and who had always held an honourable position in the foreign community of Shanghai, had become involved in a prosecution which was not based on previous careful investigation.

The case against Mr. Kleffel, counsel proceeded, rested entirely on the evidence of the comprador and Mr. Tsu, the latter being head of the safekeeping department of the Bank. The safe custody receipts had been signed, both in the case of the $20,000 and the

R. (Bryan)
Information
J.H.B. 2 MAR. 1936

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1936年3月1日

工部局检察官指控克莱费尔为
“奸诈银行家”

布莱恩先生在控方结案陈词中对被告提出严厉指控；称其犯下了一切可能的违规行为

美亚银行清算人因其立场受到尖锐批评

“本人认为，本案证据揭示了一桩涉及犯罪、挪用公款、欺诈、疏忽、管理不善、违背信任、欺骗、虚假陈述及推诿塞责的邪恶故事，”工部局检察官小罗伯特·T·布莱恩（Robert T. Bryan, Jnr.）先生昨日上午在第一特区法院对已倒闭的美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation，简称A.-O.B.C.）前总经理兼副总裁朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）先生一案进行控方总结陈词时说道。

克莱费尔先生被控违反《中华民国刑法》第336条、第339条和第342条，涉嫌挪用公款、欺诈及违背信任，罪名与美亚银行保管库中失踪的32,000美元有关。

本案原告为一名姓杨（Young，音译）的华人，其存入20,000美元，以及M. M. 埃珀特（M. M. Eppert）先生，其存入12,000美元。两人于1935年4月将款项存入该行保管，不久后该行便随其他雷文（Raven）系公司一同崩溃。

被告 pleaded not guilty（认罪不成立/ plea 为无罪），声称对作为指控依据的两个账户一无所知，由格罗斯曼博士（Dr. Grossman）和陈D.S.博士（Dr. D. S. Chen）代表出庭。在工部局检察官发言结束后，陈博士向法庭发表了讲话，随后法庭宣布休庭至周二上午10时，预计届时格罗斯曼博士将为其当事人作总结陈词。

针对辩方关于该行买办黄迪克（Dick Huang，音译）先生应对保管存款处理不当负责的主张，布莱恩先生在其长达一小时的发言伊始便声明，此类说法不足为信。

各方角色

“黄买办不过是个傀儡。克莱费尔才是幕后操纵的智囊。如果黄没有按照克莱费尔的意愿行事，他早就被解雇了。现在我们看到克莱费尔这出戏码，他作为幕后智囊运作，却想把所有责任推给买办。必须承认，根据证据，黄确实称不上是一个一丝不苟的诚实之人，但这一事实并不能免除身兼总经理和副总裁要职的克莱费尔的责任。

在严厉批评了沃尔特·F·雷文（Walter F. Raven）提供的证词后，布莱恩先生继续主张，证据显示克莱费尔犯下了银行家所能犯下的几乎每一种违规和舞弊行为。

“《中国银行法》第34条禁止银行发放超过其资本10%的任何贷款。然而我们有证据表明，克莱费尔作为美亚银行经理，发放了一笔高达2,500,000美元的贷款，这几乎相当于该行的全部资本。

“这笔钱贷给了哈金汽车公司（Harking Motors，音译），该行两名高管在其中担任董事。银行清算人仅能追回其中的400,000美元。

房地产贷款

“《中国银行法》禁止以房地产为抵押发放贷款，除非存在本案并未出现的特殊情况。然而克莱费尔向亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）出借了1,300,000美元。而且请注意，这笔钱并非基于一押，而是基于二押发放的。银行清算人未能收回分文。”

布莱恩先生接着指出，克莱费尔在没有任何适当担保的情况下，向银行的高管、董事和员工以及他自己的亲属发放贷款。他甚至说服银行买办与其（克莱费尔的）兄弟合伙做生意，并为此垫付了银行的资金。

“除此之外，他还允许雷文家族将银行当作私人钱包使用，”这位律师慷慨陈词道。“更有甚者，他利用银行信用投机黄金条块。现在他告诉我们，他不欠银行任何东西，也不欠买办任何东西。但事实是，他曾经确实欠银行钱，并且确实利用银行信用进行投机。克莱费尔一方面，与雷文和布朗（Brown）另一方面，唯一的区别在于前者比后者更幸运。雷文和布朗在投机中亏损，而克莱费尔获胜并赚了钱。

“克莱费尔说银行倒闭时他亏了钱。如果这是真的，他也完全亏得起，因为他利用银行信用投机赚了不少钱。”

明知故犯

谈到指控本身时，布莱恩先生说，克莱费尔知道将客户的保管存款从保管账户转为活期存款是错误的。这正是他对那20,000美元和12,000美元不留任何书面记录的原因。

“我们必须结合被告作为银行经理的一贯做法来考量其罪责。在此之前，他曾将价值82,000美元的上海美国学校（Shanghai American School）的债券作为抵押，后来为了避免惹上麻烦，他不得不自掏腰包赎回这些债券。

“然而，证明被告有罪的最确凿证据，是他的辩护人格罗斯曼博士接触买办试图庭外和解的行为。本庭有权假定格罗斯曼博士是奉克莱费尔之命行事，因为克莱费尔不想对簿公堂。这实际上构成了被告克莱费尔对罪行的承认。”

对霍夫的批评

布莱恩先生随后转而批评雷文系公司清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生在克莱费尔一案中所扮演的角色，并表示他对此深感遗憾。“我感到遗憾，”他说，“但我有责任履行。”

“霍夫先生的职责是追讨欠美亚银行的债务并将其分配给债权人——而不是像他在给克莱费尔的证词以及在本案中向本庭提交的证据中所做的那样，四处为奸诈的银行经理洗白......

“他竟敢来到本庭，发表意见称克莱费尔无罪，尽管证据显示克莱费尔犯下了一切可能的违规行为。”

布莱恩先生在结束发言时说，美亚银行的倒闭使许多人陷入贫困。有罪判决无法挽回损失，也无法让那位在崩盘中失去一切而自杀的人死而复生。

“但这将表明，本庭绝不容忍不诚实的银行家。”

辩方开场

随后，陈D.S.博士用中文为辩方发言，他在发言中断言，格罗斯曼博士向买办提出的庭外和解提议，并非针对刑事诉讼，而是针对作为指控基础的20,000美元和12,000美元的民事索赔。

陈博士接着说，最近在美国在华法院审理的轰动一时的雷文-布朗案，导致人们对曾在任何雷文公司任职的人都产生了怀疑。因此，在没有事先进行仔细调查的情况下，一个无辜的人——其家族在中国生活了50多年，且在上海外侨社区中一直享有崇高地位——卷入了一场并非基于事先仔细调查的起诉。

 counsel（律师）继续说道，针对克莱费尔先生的案件完全依赖于买办和徐先生（Mr. Tsu，音译）的证词，后者是该行保管部主任。无论是20,000美元还是

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, MARCH 14, 1936

Full Text Of J. Kleffel's
Judgment Is Issued

In Holding Kleffel Guilty Of Confidence Breach,
Judge Dzien Dealt Leniently With Accused, As
He Held There Was No Selfish Motives

A rough translation of the full text of the judgment of six months' imprisonment and a fine of $1,000 imposed upon Julius Kleffel, German, former General Manager and Vice-President of the now defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, for successive breach of confidence, imposed by Judge Dzien Hoong-nien on March 10, was issued yesterday by the office of the Municipal Advocate.

Judge Dzien held Kleffel guilty of successive breach of confidence for having juggled with depositor's securities. However, he held that there was no selfish motive behind the acts of the accused and, therefore, imposed a comparatively short term of imprisonment, and, in addition, the Judge imposed a much bigger fine, as he pointed out, "in order to be just."

Judge Dzien acquitted Kleffel on charges of misappropriation and fraud, holding that there was not sufficient evidence against him.

Notice Of Appeal Filed

Dr. A. Grossman, attorney for the defence, had filed notice of appeal. Kleffel being allowed to remain on the $20,000 cash security during the period of appeal.

The Judgment

Following is the rough translation of the judgment handed down by Judge Dzien in the Shanghai First Special Area District Court last Tuesday:

"The accused was charged with Misappropriation, Fraud and Breach of Confidence by the Central Police Station. This Court has tried the case and hereby decides as follows:

"Six months' imprisonment and fined $1,000 for successive breach of confidence. Commutation to labour shall be in the proportion of three dollars to one day, but not more than six months labour. Not guilty on other charges.

Facts

"Kleffel was the General Manager of the American Oriental Banking Corporation at 29, Nanking road. On April 8, 1935, Yang Sin-ching alias Henry Yang gave Wong Yih-zai, the Bank's Compradore, $20,000 in bank notes, and asked him to exchange same for silver dollars which were to be deposited in the Bank for safe-keeping. Kleffel first instructed Wong Yih-zai to request Yang Sih-ching to deposit the money on call deposit. Yang Sin-ching did not consent. Kleffel then ordered Wong Yih-zai to accept the money for safe-keeping. A receipt was accordingly signed by W. F. Raven and Tsu Yue-soong, the officers in charge of the Safe-keeping Department, and given to Yang Sih-ching. Actually, they entered this deposit into the Call Deposit Account and they put a call deposit receipt for this amount of money in the safe-keeping vaults in lieu of the $20,-000 silver. As a rule, the Bank cannot use money deposited for safe-keeping, but it can use money on call deposit. At that time, the

Bank was in need of funds, so the officers of the Bank took the money to supply the need. On the 30th of the same month, M. M. Epport, a Russian, gave to W. F. Raven and Tsu Yue-soong a check on that Bank for $12,000 and requested them to withdraw the sum and exchange it for silver dollars to be kept by them as money in safe-keeping. They then consulted with Kleffel and with his consent, they did the business according to the precedent made in the Yang Sih-ching matter. On May 24 of the same year, the Bank closed. Yang Sih-ching and Epport were unable to take back from the safekeeping vault their money entrusted to the Bank for safe-keeping, because the money had been unlawfully used by the Bank for other purposes. Consequently, each of them suffered a loss. The Police accordingly instituted a prosecution against Kleffel.

Reasons

On April 8, 1935, Yang Sih-ching gave to Wong Yih-zai, Compradore of the Bank, $20,000 in bank notes, asking him to exchange them for silver dollars and to keep same in the Bank for safe-keeping. A safe-keeping receipt was signed by W. F. Raven and Tsu Yue-soong, responsible officers of the Safe-keeping Department, and given to Yang Sih-ching. In fact, they entered this deposit into the Call Deposit Account and placed the call deposit receipt in the safekeeping vault, in lieu of the $20,000 silver. On the 30th of the same month, M.M. Epport gave to Raven and Tsu Yue-soong a check on that Bank for $12,000, and requested them to withdraw the sum, and change it into silver dollars to be kept by them as money in safe-keeping. A safe-keeping receipt was accordingly signed and issued to Epport by them. Actually, they acted according to the precedent of Yang Sin-ching. These are the salient facts of the case.

What this Court has to examine and decide is whether the statements made by Wong Yih-zai and Tsu Yue-soong to the effect that they acted in accordance with the instructions of Kleffel are credible or not. Both the accused and his lawyers contended:

The books, accounts and receipts concerning the two transactions did not bear the accused's signature, so it can be seen that the accused had no knowledge. Up to April 8 of last year, only $103,-000 appeared in the Compradore's account books. However, on the 8th of the same month, the amount was increased to more than $120,-000. This sufficiently proves that the person who directly by unlawful acts enjoyed the use of the money was the compradore, Wong Yih-zai. Tsu Yue-soong had close relations with Wong Yih-zai, his statements which were favourable to Wong Yih-zai, are clearly incredible.

Testimonial Utilized

They further utilized a testimonial given to Kleffel by Frank L. Houghn, Liquidator of the Raven Companies, on November 24, 1936 to the effect that Kleffel had carried out his duties as bank manager properly and that he was in no way indebted to the bank and a statement made by the liquidator that the accused should not be held criminally responsible as a means of proving that the accused is not guilty. He further relied on the following statement of Haven as another way of proving his innocence.

I signed the receipts according to what Tsu Yue-soong told me. On the day of the closure of the Bank, accused told me that somebody had committed irregularities with regard to the money kept in the Safe-keeping Department and that the officer placed the call deposit receipt in the safe-keeping vault in lieu of cash. I then had knowledge of it.

On April 8 of last year, the compradore's office sent the $20,-000 in bank notes received from Yang Sin-ching, together with other bank notes totalling $71,-000 to the Bank of China and deposited same in the current account of the American Oriental Banking Corporation. Detective Sub-inspector Wiligoss was sent to the Bank of China to investigate. He found this true and a copy of the entries in the books of the Bank have been made and submitted to this Court. The deposit could be withdrawn only upon the production of written evidence signed by the responsible officers of the American Oriental Banking Corporation, therefore the compradore could not have withdrawn it. This has been stated very clearly by the liquidator, Mr. Houghn and the Cashier of the American Oriental Banking Corporation Mr. Fiengold.

Compradore's Statement

Furthermore, Wong Yih-zai said in his statement:

With reference to the money received daily by the American Oriental Banking Corporation, besides paying the various kinds of deposits on that day, there were still three ways of handling money; (1) to place same in the vaults as cash reserve; (2) to deposit same with local banks as a reserve which could be drawn upon at any time. At the time of withdrawal, two responsible officers of the bank must sign as written evidence. The compradore had no power to withdraw the money; (3) to charge same to the compradore's account, as a reserve for paying the Bank's accounts. What remained unpaid was treated as the compradore's overdraft upon which he was required to pay interest. There was a fixed procedure in the receiving and paying money between the Bank and the compradore's office. Furthermore, it must be on written evidence.

（批：Jilo D. 6748 / 16 3 36）
（印：16 MAR 1936）

《字林西报》，1936年3月14日，星期六

朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（J. Kleffel）判决书全文发布

在裁定克莱费尔犯有背信罪时，迪恩法官对被告从宽处理，因其认定并无自私动机

市公署检察官办公室昨日发布了由迪恩洪年（Dzien Hoong-nien）法官于3月10日作出的判决书的粗略译文。该判决判处德籍人士、已倒闭的美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前总经理兼副总经理朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）因连续背信罪监禁六个月并罚款1,000美元。

迪恩法官认定克莱费尔因操纵储户证券而犯有连续背信罪。然而，他认为被告的行为背后没有自私动机，因此判处相对较短的刑期；此外，法官还处以高额罚款，正如他指出，“为了体现公正”。

迪恩法官宣判克莱费尔在挪用公款和欺诈指控上无罪，理由是证据不足。

提交上诉通知

辩护律师A. 格罗斯曼博士（Dr. A. Grossman）已提交上诉通知。在上诉期间，允许克莱费尔继续以20,000美元现金保释。

判决书

以下是迪恩法官上周二在上海第一特区地方法院下达的判决书的粗略译文：

“被告被中央捕房指控犯有挪用公款、欺诈和背信罪。本庭已审理此案，现判决如下：

“因连续背信罪，判处监禁六个月，并罚款1,000美元。易科劳役的比例为三元抵一日，但劳役期限不超过六个月。其他罪名无罪。

事实

“克莱费尔曾任南京路29号美亚银行总经理。1935年4月8日，杨新庆（Yang Sin-ching，又名Henry Yang）交给该行买办王义哉（Wong Yih-zai）纸币20,000元，要求将其兑换成银元，并存入银行保管。克莱费尔起初指示王义哉要求杨新庆将这笔钱作为活期存款存入。杨新庆不同意。随后，克莱费尔命令王义哉接受这笔钱进行保管。据此，保管部主管官员W. F. 雷文（W. F. Raven）和徐岳松（Tsu Yue-soong）签署了一张收据，并交给杨新庆。实际上，他们将这笔存款记入活期存款账户，并将相应金额的活期存款收据放入保管库，以代替那20,000银元。通常，银行不得使用保管存款，但可以使用活期存款资金。当时，

银行急需资金，因此银行官员动用这笔资金以满足需求。同月30日，俄国人M. M. 埃波特（M. M. Epport）交给W. F. 雷文和徐岳松一张该行支票，金额12,000美元，要求他们提取该款项并兑换成银元，由他们作为保管款存放。他们随后与克莱费尔商议，并在其同意下，依照杨新庆一案的先例办理了此项业务。同年5月24日，银行停业。杨新庆和埃波特无法从保管库中取回委托银行保管的钱款，因为该笔钱款已被银行非法挪作他用。因此，两人均遭受损失。警方遂对克莱费尔提起公诉。

理由

1935年4月8日，杨新庆交给该行买办王义哉纸币20,000元，要求将其兑换成银元并存放在银行保管。保管部负责官员W. F. 雷文和徐岳松签署了一张保管收据，并交给杨新庆。事实上，他们将这笔存款记入活期存款账户，并将活期存款收据放入保管库，以代替那20,000银元。同月30日，M. M. 埃波特交给雷文和徐岳松一张该行支票，金额12,000美元，要求他们提取该款项，并兑换成银元，由他们作为保管款存放。据此，他们签署并向埃波特出具了保管收据。实际上，他们是依照杨新庆一案的先例行事的。以上是本案的主要事实。

本庭需要审查和裁决的是，王义哉和徐岳松关于他们是按照克莱费尔的指示行事的陈述是否可信。被告及其律师辩称：

涉及这两笔交易的账簿、账目和收据上没有被告的签名，由此可见被告并不知情。截至去年4月8日，买办账簿上仅显示103,000美元。然而，在同月8日，金额增加至120,000美元以上。这充分证明，直接通过非法行为享受资金使用利益的人是买办王义哉。徐岳松与王义哉关系密切，他作出的有利于王义哉的陈述显然不可信。

采用的证词

他们进一步利用了一份由雷文公司（Raven Companies）清算人弗兰克·L. 霍恩（Frank L. Houghn）于1936年11月24日向克莱费尔出具的证明，内容大致为克莱费尔妥善履行了银行经理的职责，且他对银行没有任何债务；清算人还声明不应追究被告的刑事责任，以此作为证明被告无罪的依据。他还依赖哈芬（Haven）的以下陈述作为证明其清白的另一种方式。

我是根据徐岳松告诉我的话签署收据的。在银行停业当天，被告告诉我，有人在保管部的钱款方面存在违规行为，该官员将活期存款收据放入保管库以代替现金。我于是得知了此事。

去年4月8日，买办办事处将从杨新庆处收到的20,000元纸币，连同其他总计71,000元的纸币，送往中国银行，并存入美亚银行的往来账户。警探副督察威利戈斯（Wiligoss）被派往中国银行进行调查。他发现情况属实，并已制作银行账目记录的副本提交本庭。该存款只有在出示由美亚银行负责官员签署的书面凭证后方可提取，因此买办不可能提取该款项。这一点已由清算人霍恩先生和美亚银行出纳员芬戈尔德（Fiengold）先生非常清楚地说明。

买办的陈述

此外，王义哉在其陈述中说：

关于美亚银行每日收到的款项，除了支付当天的各类存款外，还有三种处理方式：(1) 作为现金储备放入金库；(2) 作为可随时提取的准备金存入本地银行。提取时，必须由两名银行负责官员签署书面凭证。买办无权提取该款项；(3) 记入买办账户，作为支付银行账目的准备金。未支付的部分视为买办的透支，他需为此支付利息。银行与买办办事处之间的收款和付款有固定的程序。此外，必须凭书面凭证办理。

（批注：Jilo D. 6748 / 16 3 36）
（印章：1936年3月16日）

This corresponded with the
testimony of Messrs. Hough and
Fiengold. In April of last year,
the American Oriental Banking
Corporation was badly in need of
money. This is again not denied
by the accused. Further supported
by the accused's own statement
that the comprador told him about
the Yang Sin-ching's safe-keeping
transaction and that Kaven had
come to see him about the safe-
keeping transaction of the Russ-
ian, Mr. M. M. Epport; also by
Kaven's statement that he had
consulted with the accused con-
cerning the safe-keeping of the
money belonging to the Russian
and that daily returns of the total
amount of deposits were prepared
and that the General Manager was
informed; also, by Tsu Yue-soong's
statement that when Simson came
to audit the accounts, he found
these two accounts were not in
order and that it was only after
he had asked the General Manag-
er, that he signed his name; also,
by the fact that Mr. Hough, and
Yang Sin-ching, signed the Police
Department's First Information
Report stating that the accused
was being summoned; also, by the
letter of thanks to Wong Yin-zai,
on April 30 of last year, in which
it was stated:
We do not know how to express
our gratitude towards you for your
excellent work done for our Bank
in these difficult days. My husband
has repeatedly told me that had
you not helped him in the difficul-
ties encountered by him, he would
be in a desperate condition;
also, by the letter of recommenda-
tion written by the accused for
Tsu Yue-soong, on the 30th of last
year, in which it is stated:
Mr. Tsu Yue-soong has been en-
trusted by us with the safe-keeping
of all our securities and valuables.
We have the utmost confidence in
him.
It is evident that the person
who used Yang Sih-ching and
Epport's money entrusted to the
Bank by them for safe-keeping,
there obtained an unlawful
benefit, is the American Oriental
Banking Corporation and not the
compradore Wong Yih-zai. The
evidence given by Messrs. Hough
and Kaven, in which they endeav-
oured to exonerate the accused is
not credible. . . . .
The accused admitted himself
that Wong Yih-zai made use of
these bonds placed in safe-keep-
ing more than once. Since Wong
Yih-zai repeated the same acts
over and over again, why did the
accused not make an investigation
into the matter before the subse-
quent acts were committed. On the
other hand, after the Bank was
closed, he redeemed the securities
even with his wife's title deed. It
sufficiently proves that the con-
tentions offered by the accused to
the effect that since he had no
knowledge beforehand, had not
signed his name, and was not re-
sponsible for these acts are pre-
varications.

Short Term
By comparing the accused's
statement with Wong Yih-zai and
Tsu Yue-soong's statements to the
effect that the money placed by
Yang Sih-ching and Epport for
safe-keeping was changed to a
deposit on call upon instructions
received from the accused, it
becomes more clear that the latter
statements are worthy of belief.
Since the money placed by Yang
Sih-ching and Epport with the
Bank for safe-keeping was trans-
ferred into a deposit on call by
the accused, and because the
money was unlawfully used by the
Bank, same could not be returned
from the vault. As a consequence,
each of them suffered a loss. The
evidence is very clear that the ac-
cused should be found guilty of
successive breach of confidence.

By considering the object the com-
mitting the offence by the accused,
there is yet no selfish motives. So
a comparatively short term of im-
prisonment shall be imposed, and
in addition to which, a much
bigger fine is imposed in order to
be just.

Other Charges
With reference to the other
charges that when he was the
General Manager of the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation, he
asked Wong Yin-zai to buy and
sell gold bars; that when a loss
was incurred, he ordered the com-
pradore to advance him the money
belonging to the Bank as if it were
owned by the compradore to the
Bank and that in case of gain, he
immediately withdrew all what he
had gained and that he granted
large loans with insufficient secu-
rities, it was found that the ac-
cused was not indebted to the
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration. All what he owed to
Wong Yih-zai has been returned
to him. This is proved by the cer-
tificate issued by Mr. Hough and
the receipt signed by Wong Yin-
zai. Wong Yih-zai paid interest
on the money loaned to him by
the Bank. This is also proved by
the passbook in which the interest
paid by the compradore to the
Bank is recorded. Before a loan
is granted, it must be passed by
the Board of Directors. The ac-
cused has no power to arbitrarily
act alone. This point has been
clearly stated by Mr. Hough.
Whether or not the accused is
guilty of these charges, there is
not sufficient evidence to prove
them. The accused should there-
fore be pronounced not guilty of
these charges in order to avoid
injustice.
This judgment is hereby render-
ed as per text above in accordance
with Article 342, Section 1, the
first part of Article 56, and Article
42, Sections 2 and 3 of the
Criminal Code and Article 298
Section 1 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure.
Dated: March 10, 1936.
Signed: DIZEN HOONG NIEH, Judge.

这与霍夫（Hough）先生和菲恩戈尔德（Fiengold）先生的证词相符。去年四月，美亚银行（American Oriental Banking Corporation）急需资金。这一点被告亦未否认。此外，还有以下证据佐证：被告自称买办曾告知其杨信卿（Yang Sin-ching）的保管业务，且凯文（Kaven）曾就俄国人 M. M. Epport 先生的保管业务前来与其商谈；凯文亦陈述称，他曾就该俄国人的款项保管事宜与被告商议，并编制了存款总额的日报表呈报总经理；徐岳松（Tsu Yue-soong）陈述称，辛森（Simson）前来审计账目时，发现这两笔账目不符，直至其询问总经理后，方才签字；霍夫先生和杨信卿在警方首份报案书（First Information Report）上签字，声明传唤被告；以及去年四月三十日致黄寅斋（Wong Yin-zai）的感谢信，信中写道：
“对于您在这些艰难时期为本行所做的出色工作，我们不知如何表达感激之情。我丈夫多次告诉我，若非您在困难之际施以援手，他早已陷入绝境；”
此外，还有被告于去年三十日（注：原文如此，疑为三十日或某月三十日）为徐岳松出具的推荐信，其中写道：
“徐岳松先生受我方委托，保管我方所有证券及贵重物品。我们对他抱有极大的信心。”
显而易见，挪用杨信卿和埃波特（Epport）委托银行保管的款项并从中获取非法利益的是美亚银行，而非买办黄义斋（Wong Yih-zai）。霍夫先生和凯文先生所作的旨在为被告开脱的证词不可信……

被告承认，黄义斋不止一次动用这些处于保管状态的债券。既然黄义斋反复实施相同行为，被告为何未在后续行为发生前对此事进行调查？另一方面，在银行停业后，他甚至用其妻子的地契赎回证券。这充分证明，被告所谓其事先不知情、未签字且不对这些行为负责的辩解纯属托辞。

短期刑期
通过将被告的陈述与黄义斋和徐岳松的陈述进行对比，后者称杨信卿和埃波特用于保管的款项是接到被告指示后转为活期存款的，由此可以更清楚地看出，后者的陈述更值得采信。由于杨信卿和埃波特存放于银行保管的款项被被告转为活期存款，且该款项被银行非法使用，导致无法从金库中归还。因此，他们各自遭受了损失。证据非常明确，被告应被判犯有连续背信罪。

考虑到被告犯罪的目的，其并无自私动机。因此，判处相对较短的刑期，并额外处以高额罚款，以示公正。

其他指控
关于其他指控，即其在担任美亚银行总经理期间，要求黄寅斋买卖金条；当出现亏损时，命令买办垫付属于银行的资金，仿佛该资金为买办所有并存入银行；而在获利时，则立即提取全部收益；以及在担保不足的情况下发放巨额贷款。经查，被告并不欠美亚银行债务。其欠黄义斋的所有款项均已归还。这一点由霍夫先生出具的证明书和黄寅斋签署的收据所证实。黄义斋为其向银行借入的款项支付利息。这一点也由记录买办向银行支付利息的存折所证实。发放贷款前，必须经董事会批准。被告无权擅自单独行动。霍夫先生已清楚说明了这一点。无论被告是否对这些指控有罪，均无充分证据予以证明。因此，为避免不公，应宣告被告对这些指控无罪。
本判决依据《刑法》第342条、第56条第一部分、第42条第2款和第3款，以及《刑事诉讼法》第298条第1款作出。
日期：1936年3月10日。
签署：洪念祖（DIZEN HOONG NIEH），法官。

《字林西报》，1936年3月11日，星期三

雷文、布朗被收监
已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）总裁弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和副总裁 J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生，于上月早些时候在此因挪用公款和欺诈罪名被定罪，据美国驻华法警爱德华·L·福佩尔（Edward L. Faupel）先生收到的电报消息，两人已乘坐“麦金莱总统号”轮船抵达美国，并被关押在麦克尼尔岛（McNeill's Island）的监狱中。
