THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, FEBRUARY 14, 1936

Impassioned Address Is
Made By The Defence
At Julius Kleffel's Trial

Mr. W. F. Raven, Assistant Manager Of American-
Oriental Banking Corporation, Undergoes A
Gruelling Cross-Examination At Hearing

TESTIMONIAL SIGNED BY MR. HOUGH IN
EVIDENCE—"ABOVE REPROACH"

The second session of the trial of Mr. J. Kleffel, German,
former General Manager and Vice-President of the defunct
American-Oriental Banking Corporation, in the First Special
District Court yesterday afternoon on charges of misappro-
priation, fraud and breach of confidence, was opened with
an impassioned address by the defence, pleading for fairness
and begging the Court not to be influenced by the recent
proceedings and judgment in the trial of F. J. Raven and
J. Warner Brown in the United States Court for China.

The highlight of the session
before Judge Dzien, which occupied
over two-and-a-half hours, was the
gruelling cross-examination of Mr.
Walter Francis Raven, former
Assistant Manager and Office
Manager of the American-Oriental
Banking Corporation, by Mr.
Robert T. Bryan, Jr., Municipal
Advocate. The prosecution is be-
ing conducted by Mr. Paul Y. Ru,
Assistant Municipal Advocate,
with Mr. Bryan having been
watching the proceedings since the
start. Yesterday, however, Mr.
Bryan took an active part in the
proceedings and, with the permis-
sion of the Court, questioned Mr.
Raven trying to elicit the reason
why, if the two transactions,
owing to which Mr. Kleffel is now
facing criminal charges, were ir-
regular, they had not been referred
to Mr. Kleffel for signature. These
questions were put after Mr.
Raven, a witness called by the
defence, had told the Court that
any transactions not in the regular
routine of the bank had always
been referred to Mr. Kleffel for
signature.

Mr. Kleffel, when arraigned be-
fore the Court last Tuesday, plead-
ed not guilty to the charges
framed against him and stated
that, up to the time the bank
closed on the morning of May 24
last, he had no knowledge of the
two accounts forming the basis of
the charges. Yesterday, however,
Mr. Huang Yeh-zai, the compra-
dore of the defunct bank, stated
on the witness stand that upon
accepting a deposit of $20,000 from
a Mr. Henry Young on April 8
last, to be put in the safe-keeping
account, he made out a deposit
slip and took it to Mr. Kleffel. Mr.
Tsu Yu-soong, chief of the safe-
keeping department also testified
yesterday that he received the
same receipt from Mr. Kleffel.

Another highlight of yesterday's
proceedings was the introduction
of an important and rather a
surprising exhibit in view of the
prosecution having been instituted
by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator
of the bank, in addition to the two
other complainants, who had lost
their money, due to the alleged
misappropriation, fraud and breach
of confidence. The exhibit put in
was a testimonial signed by Mr.
Hough on November 26 last, in his
capacity as liquidator of the Bank,
in which he stated that Mr.
Kleffel's "personal position was
above reproach and that he owed
no monies nor was he obligated to
the Bank in any way."

The charge against Mr. Kleffel
is: "For that he, whilst performing
his duty as General Manager of
the American-Oriental Banking
Corporation, did, on April 8, 1935,
and April 10, 1935, embezzle or
otherwise misappropriate sums of
money that were deposited with the
Bank under safe-keeping, to wit,
$20,000 from Henry Young and
$12,000 from Mr. M. M. Eppert."

Defence Address

At the opening of the trial, Mr.
Walter Francis Raven, who had
been waiting outside the court-
room, was called in, but before he
went on the witness stand, Dr. D.
S. Chen, who is appearing for the
defence together with Dr. Gross-
man, made an impassioned address
to the Court. The address follows:
"In this case our client is
charged with misappropriation
under Article 336, paragraph 2,
and the prosecution alleges that
there is sufficient evidence to
prove that in both cases the
alleged crimes were committed on
instructions of the accused,
allegedly given to the witness,
Tsu, and that the said accused
had guilty knowledge of the fact
that such crimes were committed.
"I shall refrain myself to com-
ment on the charge at the present
time. I shall do so during my
final arguments and I reserve for
myself to make at that time all
the legal and moral comments
which may seem fit.
"At the present time I want,
however, to outline the defence
as this prosecution is instituted
in a heated atmosphere, after a
rather sensational trial in another
court, and it seems to me that
the influence of this heated
atmosphere as aforesaid must be
certainly dispelled during this
trial, if we have to look forth and
to find out whether the defendant
is guilty or not. I have to point
out also that I have entire con-
fidence in the wisdom of your
Honour, that your Honour will
find the right way and the right
decision in this case.

Testimony Worthless

"The defence will show that the
testimony of Tsu and Huang is
worthless as on the face of the
documents which the prosecution
produced it is rather obvious that
the responsibility of the first one
is at the stake, and that the
second one was and is heavily in-
debted to the Bank, and if some-
body had some advantage from
these transactions, that was
Huang.
"The evidence will show, fur-
thermore, that these two trans-
actions are to be considered as
quite unusual in the line of the
defunct A.O.B.C., and that it was
therefore necessary for the staff
to ask for written instructions
from the Defendant if the re-
sponsibility of the Defendant could
be involved. No written instruc-
tions were asked for and Mr. Tsu,
who is now the main witness of
the prosecution, did not even find
it worthwhile to have the respec-
tive slips and tickets okayed by
his superior, whom he is now ac-
cusing of having given him in-
structions to handle these two
cases wrongly.
"The evidence will show that
this defendant was not even in
the physical condition to have
knowledge or even guilty knowl-
edge of the fact that such irre-
gularities have been committed,
and that if such irregularities
were found after the closure of
the A.O.B.C., they have been done
without any intention on the part
of the Defendant.

"Above Reproach"

"We will show that after the
affairs of the Bank have been
closely examined by the Liquidator,
Mr. Frank L. Hough, and his
legal Adviser, Dr. George Selleit,
nothing has been found which will
incriminate this Defendant and
that according to the statements
of the said Liquidator, the con-
duct of the Defendant, while being
in this office and after in assisting
the Liquidator, was always 'above
reproach.'
"The evidence will show that
the said Liquidator, even after
this Defendant left his service,
asked him to join him again and
offered him, shortly before this
prosecution was started (in De-
cember 1935), a position connect-
ed with considerable responsibil-
ity, as handling cash, etc.
"The evidence will show that
this Defendant was not only never
indebted to the Bank or to the
Affiliated Companies, but he is one
of the biggest losers of the de-
funct Raven group, as he and his
immediate family had about
$27,000 worth of deposits in this
Bank, which have not been with-
drawn from the Bank, and that
he entirely lost about $200,000
by his holdings of stock in the
Companies of the Raven Group.
"For all the above we offer the
testimony of Walter Raven, a citi-
zen of the United States of Amer-
ica, 433 Avenue Haig, Frank L.
Hough, Liquidator of the A.O.B.C.,
citizen of the United States of
America, Robert Dollar Building,
51 Canton Road, and L. Feingold,
Cashier of the A.O.B.C., a Russian
citizen, 15 Route Paul Henry, and
we respectfully pray that these
witness should be summoned by
this Honourable Court to appear
at the next hearing and to give
testimony for the above.
"The evidence will show that
the cash position of the Bank from
April 6, 1935, up to the closure of
the Bank was always such that
$20,000—or even $32,000—never
affected same seriously, and the
possibility existed for the Bank,
during the whole time, to clear
this matter out if the Manager
had knowledge of same."

Testimonial Letter

Following is the letter signed by
Mr. Hough, given to Mr. Kleffel
as a testimonial. It was written
on A.O.B.C. letter head:
Nov. 26, 1935.
To whom it may concern:
Mr. Julius Kleffel, the holder
of this letter and whose signature

《字林西报》，1936年2月14日，星期五

辩护方在朱利叶斯·克莱费尔（Julius Kleffel）受审时发表激昂陈词

美亚银行协理 W. F. 雷文先生在听证会上经受严厉盘问

霍夫先生签署的证明书作为证据——“无可指责”

昨日下午，在第一特区法院审理已倒闭的美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前总经理兼副总裁、德籍人士 J. 克莱费尔先生被控挪用公款、欺诈及违背信任罪一案的第二次庭审中，辩护方以一番激昂的陈词开场，恳求公正，并乞请法庭不要受到近期在华美国法院对 F. J. 雷文和 J. 沃纳·布朗审判中的诉讼程序及判决的影响。

昨日庭审由迪恩法官（Judge Dzien）主持，历时两个半小时以上，其高潮部分是市政检察官小罗伯特·T. 布莱恩先生对美亚银行前协理兼办公厅主任沃尔特·弗朗西斯·雷文先生进行的严厉盘问。本案公诉由助理市政检察官徐义（Paul Y. Ru，音译）先生负责，布莱恩先生自始至终旁听了诉讼过程。然而，昨日布莱恩先生积极参与了诉讼程序，并在获得法庭许可后，向雷文先生提问，试图探明：如果导致克莱费尔先生目前面临刑事指控的两笔交易确属违规，为何未呈交克莱费尔先生签字。这些问题是在作为辩方证人出庭的雷文先生告诉法庭“凡是不属于银行常规业务的交易，历来均呈交克莱费尔先生签字”之后提出的。

克莱费尔先生于上周二在法庭受审时，对所列指控表示不认罪，并声明直至去年5月24日上午银行停业为止，他对构成指控基础的两个账户毫不知情。然而，昨日该已倒闭银行的买办黄业哉（Huang Yeh-zai，音译）先生在证人席上陈述，去年4月8日，他在接受一位亨利·杨（Henry Young）先生存入保管账户的20,000美元存款时，开具了一张存款单，并将其拿给克莱费尔先生。保管部主任朱玉松（Tsu Yu-soong，音译）先生昨日也作证称，他从克莱费尔先生那里收到了同样的收据。

昨日诉讼的另一亮点是引入了一份重要且相当令人惊讶的物证，鉴于本案是由银行清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生以及另外两名因所谓挪用、欺诈和违背信任而遭受金钱损失的投诉人共同提起的公诉。提交的物证是一份由霍夫先生于去年11月26日以银行清算人身份签署的证明书，其中他声明克莱费尔先生的“个人地位无可指责，他不欠银行任何款项，也不以任何方式对银行负有义务。”

对克莱费尔先生的指控是：“他在担任美亚银行总经理履行职责期间，于1935年4月8日和1935年4月10日，侵吞或以其他方式挪用了存入银行保管账户的款项，即来自亨利·杨的20,000美元和来自 M. M. 埃珀特（M. M. Eppert）先生的12,000美元。”

辩护方陈词

庭审开始时，一直在法庭外等候的沃尔特·弗朗西斯·雷文先生被传唤入内，但在他登上证人席之前，与格罗斯曼博士（Dr. Grossman）一同代表辩护方的陈博士（Dr. D. S. Chen）向法庭发表了激昂的陈词。陈词如下：

“在本案中，我们的当事人被控违反第336条第2款之挪用公款罪，公诉方声称有充分证据证明，在这两起案件中，所谓犯罪是根据被告向证人朱某发出的指示实施的，且该被告明知这些犯罪发生而具有犯罪故意。

“我此刻暂不对指控发表评论。我将在最后辩论阶段这样做，并保留在那时作出所有看似合适的法律和道德评论的权利。

“然而，目前我想概述一下辩护立场，因为本次公诉是在一种热烈的氛围中提起的，此前另一家法院进行了一场相当轰动的审判，在我看来，如果我们必须展望并查明被告是否有罪，就必须在此次审判中消除上述热烈氛围的影响。我还必须指出，我对阁下的智慧充满信心，相信阁下会在本案中找到正确的途径并作出正确的裁决。

证词毫无价值

“辩护方将表明，朱某和黄某的证词毫无价值，因为从公诉方出示的文件表面来看，显然第一个人的责任岌岌可危，而第二个人过去和现在都严重欠银行债务，如果有人从这些交易中获益，那个人就是黄某。

“证据还将表明，这两笔交易在已倒闭的美亚银行业务范围内被视为极不寻常，因此，如果涉及被告的责任，职员有必要向被告寻求书面指示。但他们并未寻求书面指示，而作为公诉方主要证人的朱先生，甚至认为不值得让其上级批准相应的单据和票证，而他现在却指控其上级曾指示他错误地处理这两起案件。

“证据将表明，被告当时的身体状况甚至无法知晓，更不可能明知此类违规行为已经发生，而且如果在美亚银行停业后发现此类违规行为，那也是在没有被告任何意图的情况下发生的。

‘无可指责’

“我们将表明，在清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生及其法律顾问乔治·塞莱特（George Selleit，音译）博士仔细审查银行事务后，未发现任何能归罪于被告的事项，并且根据该清算人的陈述，被告在任职期间以及随后协助清算人期间，其行为始终‘无可指责’。

“证据将表明，即使在该被告离职后，所述清算人仍邀请他重新加入，并在本次公诉开始前不久（1935年12月），向他提供了一个涉及重大责任的职位，如管理现金等。

“证据将表明，该被告不仅从未欠银行或关联公司任何债务，而且他是已倒闭的雷文集团最大的损失者之一，因为他及其直系亲属在该银行存有约27,000美元的存款，这些存款尚未从银行取出，而且他因持有雷文集团各公司的股票而损失了约200,000美元。

“基于上述所有理由，我们提供以下人士的证词：美国公民、海格路433号（Avenue Haig）的沃尔特·雷文；美亚银行清算人、美国公民、广东路51号罗伯特·美元大楼（Robert Dollar Building）的弗兰克·L. 霍夫；以及俄罗斯公民、保罗·亨利路15号（Route Paul Henry）的美亚银行出纳 L. 芬戈尔德（L. Feingold）。我们恭敬地请求本庭传唤这些证人出席下一次听证会，并就上述事项作证。

“证据将表明，从1935年4月6日起至银行停业止，银行的现金状况始终未因20,000美元——甚至32,000美元——而受到严重影响，如果经理知情，银行在整个期间都有可能清理此事。”

证明信

以下是霍夫先生签署并作为证明书交给克莱费尔先生的信件。该信写在美亚银行信笺上：

1935年11月26日。

致有关人士：

本函持有人朱利叶斯·克莱费尔先生，其签名

appears below, has been connected for some years with the American-Oriental Banking Corporation as Vice-President and General Manager. On May 24, 1935, the officers sought relief in the United States Court by asking for the appointment of a Liquidator.

Upon my appointment, Mr. Kleffel offered me his services to assist me, which I accepted. I found Mr. Kleffel of great assistance to me in every department, and the wholehearted manner in which he gave me his services is indeed appreciated.

Upon investigation of the affairs of the Bank, I found that Mr. Kleffel's personal position was above reproach and that he owed no monies nor was he obligated to the Bank in any way.

Mr. Kleffel was compelled to leave me due to ill-health induced by the strain and worry of the closure of the Bank.

Yours Very Truly,
(Signed) Frank L. Hough,
Liquidator,
American-Oriental Banking
Corporation.
Signature of J. Kleffel.

Raven Takes Stand

Following the address of the defence, Mr. Ru made a short speech in which he pointed out that if the accused himself had not profited by the illegal transactions, a third person had benefited to the detriment of the two complainants. Referring to the testimonial letter put in as evidence by the defence, Mr. Ru contended that, in a way, it constituted a forgery, as the various details in it were supplied by members of his own staff.

Mr. Walter Francis Raven then took the stand. He stated he was an American citizen, 29 years old and residing at 433 Avenue Haig. He stated that he was assistant manager and office manager of the defunct A.C.B.C. In answer to questions put by Judge Drien, he said that anything out of the ordinary and regular routine of the Bank had to be initialled by Mr. Kleffel.

Giving examples, Mr. Raven stated that if Mr. Kleffel approved an overdraft, he would send a chit to the cashier; all letters which in any way related to the policy of the Bank had to be initialled by Mr. Kleffel, cheques above the overdraft amount were also always initialled by Mr. Kleffel, as well as all cash payments in connection with the bank expenses.

Asked whether Mr. Kleffel initialled all payments made by the Bank in the course of a day, Mr. Raven pointed out that same was impossible as hundreds and hundreds of cheques were cashed daily, however, Mr. Kleffel was always given a statement of the Bank's cash position at the end of each day. Mr. Raven stated that same was for Mr. Kleffel's reference only and that he did not believe that 'Mr. Kleffel initialled the report.

According to Mr. Raven, the comprador and the safe deposit department of the Bank were separate departments. Mr. Raven told the Court that he was in charge of the safe-keeping department, with a department head under him.

Signed Receipt

Mr. Raven told the Judge that he had signed the safe-deposit receipt in the name of Mr. Henry Young for $20,000. This is one of the amounts which forms the basis of the charges against Mr. Kleffel. The amount was placed in a "Call-Deposit" account instead of the "Safe-Keeping Deposit" account as the receipt specified. Going over the usual procedure which was adopted when safe-keeping deposits were received, Mr. Raven stated that Mr. Tsu, head of the safe-keeping deposit department, would make all the arrangements with the customer and then come to him, with a receipt, which he (Mr. Raven) signed.

In reply to the Judge, Mr. Raven admitted that he never saw any cash or valuables which were taken into safe-keeping.

On what grounds, then, did you sign the the deposit receipt?—questioned the Judge.

Mr. Tsu was a responsible officer of the Bank and had been with the Bank for 15 years. He was a bonded man—was the quick rejoinder.

On April 8, Mr. Young brought $20,000 in silver dollars to the Bank for safe-keeping, Mr. Tsu had obtained permission from Mr. Kleffel regarding accepting it, and then you signed the receipt?—Decidedly untrue.

"Mr. Tsu came to me with the request to accept for safe-keeping the silver dollars," stated Mr. Raven, "We had not been keeping any specie in safe-keeping, and I told Mr. Tsu how I felt about it and that other banks also did not accept such deposits of silver dollars. Mr. Tsu, however, mentioned that it was a special request of Mr. Dick Huang, the comprador, so I signed it, and that is all I know about it."

Signed As Should Have

Upon being asked why he had signed a safe-keeping deposit receipt when the money actually went into call-deposit, Mr. Raven stated that he signed as he should have done, as the money was supposed to go into the safe-keeping vault.

Upon being questioned whether he spoke with Mr. Kleffel regarding the matter, the witness replied that he had not, and added that Mr. Tsu and asked him to sign it and accept the deposit because the comprador had requested it. Giving his reasons for not wanting to accept the deposit in silver dollars, Mr. Raven pointed out that the Bank's vault was small.

Judge—You must have known that no actual cash went into the vault, but a receipt for a deposit on call?—How could I know? I never examined Tsu's vaults.

Judge—I do not believe that you are telling the truth, because if Mr. Tsu was trusted as much as you say he was he would not have had to explain to you to have the deposit accepted,—I was against specie deposits.

Judge—In the case of the deposit of Mr. Epport, why did you sign the receipt?—Mr. Epport was an old customer of the Bank and he was frightened about the currency situation in China, and I wanted to help him.

Describing the procedure adopted in the Epport case, Mr. Raven said that Mr. Epport drew a cheque for $12,000 and gave it to Mr. Tsu, who should have taken silver from the vaults and put it in the safe-keeping vault. Asked why he had not seen to it that same was carried out properly, Mr. Raven replied that he could not supervise everything himself and had to trust heads of departments.

Mistake Discovered

It was then put to Mr. Raven by the Judge that some time after Mr. Epport had transferred $12,-000 to safe-keeping, he called on Mr. Raven and asked if everything was all right Mr. Raven could not recall the visits.

Judge—You told him that everything was all right. To do so, you must have known that the money was in the safe-keeping vault?—I presumed that Mr. Tsu had carried out his duty and put the money in the safe-keeping vault. I did not actually see him put the $20,000 there.

Judge—When did you hear that no cash was in the safe-keeping vault?—The Bank closed at 7 a.m. on May 24 last. At noon that day, Mr. Kleffel came to me in a state of great excitement and said, "My God, Walter! Do you know what those fools in the office have done?" I said "No." He then said, "They have changed the safe-keeping deposit to call deposit," and that was the first time I knew about it.

Mr. Raven then branded Mr. Tsu's evidence as an absolute lie. He pointed out that if a deposit went through the comprador, an officer of the Bank had to know about it. Tsu had to know, as he signed both the call and safe-keeping deposit receipts.

Judge—If the comprador wanted to embezzle the money, he could not do it alone; someone from the bank had to be involved?—Yes.

Tsu Suspected

At this stage, Mr. Ru took up the cross-examination of the witness.

Mr. Ru—Mr. Tsu has been with the Bank for about 15 years; he has a good record. Is he now under suspicion?—I certainly think that he must be the one who had done something wrong in the Bank. I might think that he made a mistake in the first place.

Upon being shown a stub of the deposit receipt issued to Mr. Young, Mr. Raven identified that the "C" deposit, meaning Call-Deposit, was written in Mr. Tsu's writing.

Dr. Grossman, counsel for the defence, than put in a question, "What kind of advantage would the comprador have in connection with this irregularity?

Raven—Huang was pressed by Mr. Kleffel in April and in May to draw balances from Chinese banks. Huang, however, was against it, saying that the Bank would lose face. When the Bank closed, it was discovered that the comprador had no balances in Chinese banks. Huang would have, therefore, benefitted by the irregularity of having additional cash on hand when Mr. Kleffel called for it.

Bryan Cross-Examines

Mr. Raven was just getting off the stand when Mr. Bryan, putting on a lawyer's cloak over his overcoat, commenced his gruelling cross-examination.

Mr. Bryan—You said "C" Deposit was an unusual transaction?—I said transfer was an unusual transaction.

Mr. Bryan—You said when Mr. Tsu came to you that you did not want to accept the 20,000 silver dollars and that other banks did not do it?—Yes, very true.

Mr. Bryan—Then you did say it was unusual?—Wait a minute, Mr. Bryan, don't confuse my words; combining the two made an unusual transaction.

Mr. Bryan—Although it was an unusual transaction, you did not see fit to consult the General Manager?—I was deciding the policy on that point. I might add that in the case of the Young deposit, I did it at the special request of Mr. Huang, the comprador, and in the Epport case, I did go in to consult Mr. Kleffel.

Mr. Bryan—In the other case, you did consult the General Manager; why not in the first case?—It was only unusual because it was rare; as safe-keeping, it was all right.

Mr. Bryan—But you had never taken in silver dollars before?—No, but it was only an article put in safe-keeping.

Mr. Bryan—In the Epport case, you did consult Mr. Kleffel; why didn't you do so in the Young case?—I did it at the express request of the comprador, who had equal authority with Mr. Kleffel. He handled all Chinese business himself.

如下所示，他多年来一直担任美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）的副总裁兼总经理。1935年5月24日，该行高管向美国法院寻求救济，申请任命一名清算人。

在我获任后，克莱费尔先生（Mr. Kleffel）主动提出为我提供协助，我接受了他的提议。我发现克莱费尔先生在各个部门都给予了我极大的帮助，他全心全意地为我服务，对此我深表感激。

在对银行事务进行调查后，我发现克莱费尔先生的个人操守无可指责，他不欠任何款项，也不以任何方式对银行负有义务。

由于银行关闭带来的压力和忧虑导致健康恶化，克莱费尔先生被迫离我而去。

此致，
敬礼
（签名）弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough），
清算人，
美亚银行公司。
J. 克莱费尔签名。

雷文出庭作证

在辩护方陈述之后，鲁先生（Mr. Ru）发表了简短讲话，他指出，即使被告本人并未从非法交易中获利，也有第三方受益，而两名原告则因此受损。谈到辩护方作为证据提交的那封推荐信时，鲁先生辩称，从某种意义上说，这构成了伪造，因为信中的各种细节是由他自己的职员提供的。

随后，沃尔特·弗朗西斯·雷文（Walter Francis Raven）先生出庭作证。他声明自己是美国公民，29岁，居住在海格路（Avenue Haig）433号。他声明自己是已倒闭的美亚银行公司（A.C.B.C.）的助理经理兼办公室经理。在回答德里恩法官（Judge Drien）提出的问题时，他说，凡是不属于银行日常常规事务的事项，都必须由克莱费尔先生简签。

举例来说，雷文先生指出，如果克莱费尔先生批准透支，他会向出纳员发送一张便条；所有与银行政策有关的信件都必须由克莱费尔先生简签，超过透支金额的支票也总是由克莱费尔先生简签，以及与银行费用有关的所有现金支付也是如此。

当被问及克莱费尔先生是否简签了银行一天内做出的所有付款时，雷文先生指出这是不可能的，因为每天有成百上千张支票被兑现，然而，克莱费尔先生每天结束时都会收到一份银行现金头寸报表。雷文先生表示，该报表仅供克莱费尔先生参考，他不相信克莱费尔先生会在该报告上简签。

据雷文先生称，银行的买办部和保管箱部是独立的部门。雷文先生告诉法庭，他负责保管部，手下有一名部门主管。

签署收据

雷文先生告诉法官，他以亨利·杨（Henry Young）先生的名义签署了一张金额为20,000美元的保管箱收据。这是构成对克莱费尔先生指控基础的金额之一。这笔钱被存入“活期存款”账户，而不是收据上指定的“保管存款”账户。在回顾接收保管存款时采用的通常程序时，雷文先生表示，保管存款部主管徐先生（Mr. Tsu）会与客户做好所有安排，然后拿着收据来找他，由他（雷文先生）签署。

在回答法官提问时，雷文先生承认，他从未见过任何被存入保管的现金或贵重物品。

那么，你是基于什么理由签署存款收据的呢？——法官问道。

徐先生是银行的一名负责官员，已在银行工作了15年。他是有担保的职员——这是迅速的回应。

4月8日，杨先生将20,000银元带到银行进行保管，徐先生就接受此事获得了克莱费尔先生的许可，然后你签署了收据？——绝对不实。

“徐先生来找我，请求接受银元进行保管，”雷文先生说道，“我们一直没有保管任何铸币，我告诉徐先生我对这件事的看法，并且其他银行也不接受此类银元存款。然而，徐先生提到这是买办黄迪克先生（Mr. Dick Huang）的特殊要求，所以我签了字，这就是我所知道的全部。”

按理应如此签署

当被问及为什么在资金实际进入活期存款的情况下却签署了保管存款收据时，雷文先生表示，他是按理应做到的那样签署的，因为这笔钱本应进入保管库。

当被问及是否就此事与克莱费尔先生交谈过时，证人回答说没有，并补充说，徐先生让他签署并接受存款，因为买办提出了请求。在解释不想接受银元存款的原因时，雷文先生指出，银行的保险库很小。

法官——你肯定知道没有实际现金进入保险库，而是一张活期存款的收据？——我怎么会知道？我从未检查过徐先生的保险库。

法官——我不相信你在说实话，因为如果徐先生像你所说的那样值得信任，他就不必向你解释以让存款被接受，——我是反对铸币存款的。

法官——在埃波特先生（Mr. Epport）的存款案中，你为什么签署收据？——埃波特先生是银行的老客户，他对中国的货币局势感到恐慌，我想帮助他。

描述埃波特案中采用的程序时，雷文先生说，埃波特先生开了一张12,000美元的支票交给徐先生，徐先生本应从保险库中取出银元并放入保管库。当被问及为何没有确保此事得到妥善执行时，雷文先生回答说，他无法亲自监督所有事情，必须信任各部门主管。

发现错误

随后，法官向雷文先生指出，在埃波特先生将12,000美元转入保管后的一段时间，他拜访了雷文先生并询问一切是否正常，雷文先生记不起这些访问。

法官——你告诉他一切正常。要做到这一点，你必须知道钱在保管库里？——我推测徐先生履行了他的职责，把钱放进了保管库。我并没有亲眼看到他把那20,000美元放进去。

法官——你什么时候听说保管库里没有现金的？——去年5月24日上午7点银行关闭。当天中午，克莱费尔先生非常激动地来找我，说：“天哪，沃尔特！你知道办公室里那些蠢货做了什么吗？”我说“不知道”。然后他说，“他们把保管存款改成了活期存款”，那是我第一次知道这件事。

随后，雷文先生称徐先生的证词完全是谎言。他指出，如果一笔存款经过买办，银行的一名官员必须知情。徐先生必须知情，因为他同时签署了活期和保管存款收据。

法官——如果买办想侵吞这笔钱，他不可能单独做到；必须有银行内部的人参与？——是的。

怀疑徐先生

在此阶段，鲁先生开始对证人进行交叉质询。

鲁先生——徐先生在银行工作了大约15年；他的记录良好。他现在受到怀疑了吗？——我当然认为他一定是那个在银行做了错事的人。我也许会认为他起初是犯了一个错误。

在向雷文先生出示发给杨先生的存款收据存根后，雷文先生确认，“C”存款，即活期存款（Call-Deposit），是徐先生的笔迹。

随后，辩护律师格罗斯曼博士（Dr. Grossman）提出了一个问题，“买办在这种违规行为中会有什么好处？”

雷文——克莱费尔先生在四月和五月催促黄先生从中国银行提取余额。然而，黄先生反对这样做，称银行会丢面子。当银行关闭时，发现买办在中国银行没有余额。因此，当克莱费尔先生要求提款时，黄先生会因手头有额外现金这一违规行为而受益。

布莱恩进行交叉质询

雷文先生正要离开证人席时，布莱恩先生（Mr. Bryan）在大衣外披上律师袍，开始了严厉的交叉质询。

布莱恩先生——你说“C”存款是一笔不寻常的交易？——我说的是转账是一笔不寻常的交易。

布莱恩先生——你说当徐先生来找你时，你不想接受那20,000银元，而且其他银行也不这样做？——是的，非常真实。

布莱恩先生——那么你确实说过这不寻常？——等一下，布莱恩先生，不要混淆我的话；将两者结合才构成了一笔不寻常的交易。

布莱恩先生——虽然这是一笔不寻常的交易，但你认为没有必要咨询总经理？——我在决定这方面的政策。我可以补充说，在杨先生存款案中，我是应买办黄先生的特别要求做的，而在埃波特案中，我确实去咨询了克莱费尔先生。

布莱恩先生——在另一个案件中，你咨询了总经理；为什么在第一个案件中没有？——这只是因为罕见才显得不寻常；作为保管，这是可以的。

布莱恩先生——但你以前从未接收过银元？——没有，但这只是作为保管物品放入而已。

布莱恩先生——在埃波特案中，你咨询了克莱费尔先生；为什么在杨先生案中没有这样做？——我是应买办的明确要求这样做的，他的权力与克莱费尔先生相等。他亲自处理所有中国业务。

Mr. Bryan—So the compradore
had equal authority with Mr.
Kleffel?—I took Huang's word as
much as Mr. Kleffel's in the line
of Chinese business.
Chinese Business
Mr. Bryan—The reason why you
did not consult Mr. Kleffel in the
Young case was because it was
Chinese business?—Yes.
Mr. Bryan—Is there any differ-
ence in the responsibility of the
Bank in Chinese business and
Russian business? (Laughter)—
No.
Mr. Bryan—Any other reason
why you did not consult Mr.
Kleffel in the Young case other
than that it was Chinese business?
—Absolutely not.
Mr. Bryan—Mr. Tsu has been
with the Bank for about 15 years;
he has always been faithful and
honest, as far as you know?—Yes.
Mr. Bryan—So far as you know,
he has never been guilty of un-
truthfulness, and yet in this case
you make allegations which, to say
the least, are irregular?—Well, on
the face of it. His name appears
on both the "C" deposit receipts.
Mr. Bryan—Why had you not
checked the silver in the vaults?—
Physical impossibility. The sum
of $20,000 silver is not a small
matter.
Mr. Bryan—You did not think
it worth investigating?—Every
day there are $20,000 deposits or
more, and I did not check them.
Mr. Bryan—Wasn't it unusual
that you did not see fit to report
to the General Manager?—Un-
usual in the sense of rare, yes.
Unusual in the form that the
Bank never handled before, no.
Verbal Instructions
Mr. Tsu was then called into
the Court for questioning.
Judge—Who gave you the re-
ceipt for safe-keeping?—Mr. Tai
Feng.
Judge—To whom did you give
the receipt afterwards and under
what department?—To Mr. Chen.
There was no clear division of
departments.
Mr. Tsu was then asked to iden-
tify the signatures appearing on
the receipt in connection with the
Young deposit. He identified the
upper signature as that of Mr.
Huang, and the lower one as his
own, adding that he had signed
the receipt after consulting the
General Manager.
Judge—Why did you not ask
the General Manager to initial
the receipt?—I am too small an
officer of the Bank to insist on
same.
Judge—Who checked the ac-
count of the Young deposit?—A
German officer, who is now in
Germany.
Mr. Kleffel was called up for
questioning at this stage. He
stated that the German referred
to was a young man of 17 or 18
years of age, just out of school
and put into the Bank as an
apprentice to learn the business.
Mr. Kleffel denied that he had
sent anyone to check the safe de-
posit vaults in May of last year.
Referring to the duties of the
young German, Mr. Kleffel men-
tioned that the young man had
to see that anything that came in
for safe-keeping was to go into
the vaults, and when he found it
to be correct, he was to initial the
ledger. He had initialled the en-
try opposite the Young account
that a "C" deposit slip had gone
into the vaults.

"Absolute Lie"
Mr. Kleffel pointed out that in
the 12 months that the young
German had worked in the Bank,
he had only spoken to him twice.
Judge—Tsu said when the
young German saw the entry in
the Young account, he refused to
initial it, but went to see you.—
That is an absolute lie.
Upon being questioned about
the Eppert account, Mr. Kleffel
stated that if Mr. Raven had come
to see him about it, which he
could not recollect, he came to see
him about the specie question and
not about transferring the amount
from sake-keeping account to call
deposit.
Questioned as to what he con-
sidered should be referred to him,
Mr. Kleffel replied that anything
that any member of the staff
thought was above his authority
was brought for his signature.
Especially, pointed out Mr. Kleffel,
Mr. Tsu, as he now says, if he
saw something was irregular, he
should have brought it to me for
signature.
Compradore Testifies
Mr. Dick Huang, the compra-
dore of the Bank, was then called
to testify. He stated that Mr.
Young had deposited $20,000 with
the Bank on April 8, last and
that the money was put in call
deposit, but he took it and gave
it to the Bank of China. He was
asked a number of questions on
that point.
Mr. Huang then said that he
had put up $105,000 as bond to
Bank and added that he owed
over $110,000 to the Bank. He
then admitted that he had signed
the Young deposit receipt, but
later gave it to the General
Manager.
Mr. Huang then stated that
usually about $110,000 was under
his care. He received the money
during the day and handed it to
the Bank at night.
Judge—I suppose when you re-
ceived the $20,000 Young deposit,
you must have paid the money
out?—Yes, part of it to my native
bank under my name. Should the
native bank have closed, I would
have been responsible for the
money.
Mr. Kleffel then was questioned
on the point of the compradore's
guarantee and pointed out that
same was in U.S.$40,000 par
value American-Oriental Banking
Corporation shares. At the
closure of the Bank, the compra-
dore owed the Bank over $100,000.
Judge—That about equals his
guarantee?
Mr. Kleffel—The shares have
no value now, with the Bank
closed. Then there is a difference.
One was security and the other
was a trust fund.
Judge—Mr. Raven said that at
the end of April and in May, the
Bank was badly in need of money?
Mr. Kleffel—We were pressed.
At this stage, Judge Dzlen ad-
journed the hearing until 2 p.m.
next Thursday. Mr. Kleffel was
allowed to remain on $20,000
cash bail.

布莱恩先生——那么，买办与克莱费尔先生拥有同等权力？——在处理华务方面，我对黄先生的信任程度不亚于对克莱费尔先生。

华务
布莱恩先生——你在杨氏案中未咨询克莱费尔先生，是因为该案属于华务？——是的。
布莱恩先生——银行在处理华务与俄务时的责任有何不同？（笑声）——没有。
布莱恩先生——除了因为是华务之外，你在杨氏案中未咨询克莱费尔先生还有其他原因吗？——绝对没有。
布莱恩先生——据你所知，朱先生在银行任职约15年，一直忠诚诚实？——是的。
布莱恩先生——据你所知，他从未有过不诚实的行为，然而在此案中你却提出了至少可以说是不合常规的指控？——嗯，从表面上看是这样。他的名字出现在两张“C”类存款收据上。
布莱恩先生——你为何没有检查金库中的银元？——实际上不可能。两万银元并非小数目。
布莱恩先生——你认为不值得调查？——每天都有两万或更多的存款，我并未逐一检查。
布莱恩先生——你觉得不向总经理汇报并不反常吗？——就罕见程度而言，是的，这很反常。但就银行此前从未处理过的形式而言，并不反常。

口头指示
随后传唤朱先生到庭受询。
法官——谁给了你保管收据？——戴丰先生。
法官——后来你将收据交给了谁，归属哪个部门？——交给了陈先生。当时部门划分并不明确。
随后要求朱先生辨认与杨氏存款相关的收据上的签名。他指认上方的签名为黄先生所签，下方的签名为他自己所签，并补充说他在咨询总经理后签署了该收据。
法官——你为何不要求总经理在收据上简签？——我在银行职位太低，无法坚持这样做。
法官——谁核对了杨氏存款的账目？——一名德国职员，现已在德国。
此时传唤克莱费尔先生受询。他表示，前述德国人是一名十七八岁的年轻人，刚毕业进入银行当学徒以学习业务。
克莱费尔否认他曾派人在去年五月检查保险箱金库。谈及这名年轻德国人的职责时，克莱费尔提到，该年轻人的任务是确保所有存入保管的物品进入金库，并在确认无误后在分类账上简签。他曾在杨氏账户对应的条目旁简签，表明一张“C”类存款单已存入金库。

“彻头彻尾的谎言”
克莱费尔指出，在这名年轻德国人在银行工作的12个月里，他只与他交谈过两次。
法官——朱先生说，当这名年轻德国人看到杨氏账户中的条目时，他拒绝简签，而是去见你。——那是彻头彻尾的谎言。
在被问及埃珀特账户时，克莱费尔表示，如果雷文先生曾就此事宜见过他（他已记不清），那么雷文是来讨论硬币问题，而不是关于将金额从保管账户转移至活期存款账户的事宜。
当被问及他认为哪些事项应呈报给他时，克莱费尔回答说，任何职员认为超出其权限的事项都会送来请他签字。克莱费尔特别指出，正如朱先生现在所说，如果他发现某事不合常规，本应将其送来请我签字。

买办作证
随后传唤银行买办黄迪克先生作证。他表示，杨先生于去年4月8日向银行存入20,000美元，这笔钱被作为活期存款处理，但他取出后交给了中国银行。他就这一点接受了多项提问。
黄先生随后表示，他已向银行缴纳了105,000美元作为保证金，并补充说他欠银行超过110,000美元。他随后承认自己签署了杨氏存款收据，但后来将其交给了总经理。
黄先生接着表示，通常由他保管的资金约为110,000美元。他在白天接收款项，并在夜间交给银行。
法官——我想当你收到杨氏的20,000美元存款时，你一定已将这笔钱支付出去了？——是的，部分以我的名义支付给了我名下的钱庄。如果该钱庄倒闭，我将对这笔资金负责。
随后就买办担保一事询问克莱费尔，他指出担保品为面值40,000美元的美亚银行股票。在银行关闭时，买办欠银行超过100,000美元。
法官——这大致相当于他的担保额？
克莱费尔先生——随着银行关闭，这些股票现已毫无价值。此外还有区别。一个是担保品，另一个是信托基金。
法官——雷文先生说，四月底和五月初，银行严重缺乏资金？
克莱费尔先生——我们确实资金紧张。
此时，德伦法官宣布休庭，直至下周四下午2点继续审理。允许克莱费尔以20,000美元现金保释候审。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 13, 1936

Haley, Prosecution Witness
May Take Raven, Brown To Jail

Auditor Being Considered For Job As Deputy-
Marshal To Look After Two Bankers On
Journey To McNeill's Island

That Mr Cletus J. Haley, United States Government auditor, and perhaps the most important prosecution witness in the recent Raven trial, is being considered as the man to take custody of Frank I. Raven and J. Warner Brown, former American-Oriental Finance Corporation officials, during their trip across the Pacific to the Federal Prison at McNeill's Island, was learned by a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday afternoon.

Both Raven and Brown are now in Ward Road Jail, awaiting transportation back to the United States and McNeill's Island where they will enter the Federal Prison to serve five and two year sentences respectively, having been convicted by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China 10 days ago on seven counts of embezzlement and fraud.

It is not yet definite as to whether Mr. Haley will be sworn in as Deputy U. S. Marshal and given custody of the two men. U. S. Marshal Edward Faupel stated yesterday that he discussed the matter with Mr. Haley and the latter had expressed his willingness to take the job. The Marshal stated that he was yet undecided as to what to do about the matter but would have a definite statement to make in a day or two.

Mr. Haley had ordinarily expected to leave Shanghai for San Francisco on Saturday, February 15. The two prisoners are to sail for the United States on the President McKinley leaving this port on February 18. Inasmuch as Mr. Haley is a United States Government official, and is returning to America anyway, it is felt that it might be a wise move to place the prisoners in his charge rather than to hand them over into the custody of the Captain of the ship. Under Mr. Haley's care, it is felt that the prisoners would have more freedom of movement on board ship and that it will not be necessary to keep them locked in their staterooms. It also will be possible under such arrangement to provide them with good staterooms.

Mr. Haley came to Shanghai last November for the express purpose of testifying for the prosecution against Messrs. Raven and Brown. He was a former employee of the A.O.F.C. and testified that he had made a report, giving copies to both Raven and Brown to the effect that shares purchased by customers for safe-keeping should be placed in safe-keeping. The report also pointed out that in case something should happen to the concern, officials would be "wide open to legal action." His report was one of the strong points produced in evidence.

He testified, however, that he bore no ill-will toward either Raven or Brown and that his associations with them had been friendly.

《字林西报》，1936年2月13日，星期四

海利，控方证人
可能押送雷文、布朗入狱

审计员正被考虑担任副法警职务，以便在两名银行家前往麦克尼尔岛途中看管他们

《字林西报》记者昨日下午获悉，美国政府审计员克莱图斯·J·海利先生，或许是近期雷文审判中最重要的控方证人，正被考虑作为人选，在美亚金融公司前官员弗兰克·I·雷文和J·沃纳·布朗横渡太平洋前往麦克尼尔岛联邦监狱的途中负责看管他们。

雷文和布朗目前均关押在华德路监狱，等待被遣返美国并送往麦克尼尔岛，他们将在那里进入联邦监狱服刑，刑期分别为五年和两年。十天前，他们在中国美国法庭被米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官裁定犯有七项挪用公款和欺诈罪。

海利先生是否会被宣誓就职为美国副法警并负责看管这两人，目前尚未确定。美国法警爱德华·福佩尔昨日表示，他已与海利先生讨论此事，后者表示愿意接受这项工作。法警称他对此事尚未做出决定，但将在这一两天内发表明确声明。

海利先生原计划于2月15日星期六离开上海前往旧金山。两名囚犯将于2月18日乘坐“麦金莱总统号”轮船离开本港驶往美国。鉴于海利先生是美国政府官员，且无论如何都要返回美国，人们认为将囚犯交给他看管，而非移交给船长看管，可能是明智之举。在海利先生的照看下，囚犯在船上的行动自由会更大，无需将他们锁在客舱内。在这种安排下，还可以为他们提供较好的客舱。

海利先生于去年11月来到上海，专门目的是在针对雷文和布朗先生的诉讼中为控方作证。他曾是美亚金融公司的前雇员，他作证说，他曾提交一份报告，并将副本交给雷文和布朗，指出为客户购买并用于保管的股票应放入保管库。报告还指出，万一公司发生变故，官员们将“完全面临法律诉讼的风险”。他的报告是呈堂证据中的有力要点之一。

然而，他作证说，他对雷文或布朗均无怨恨，他与他们的交往一直是友好的。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 12, 1936.2

Raven Likely
To Sail With
Brown To U. S.

Former A.O.F.C. Head
Not Expected To
Drop Appeal

Mr. Frank J. Raven, former President of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, now in liquidation, sentenced to five years' imprisonment for embezzlement and fraud, will, in all probability, sail for the United States and the Federal prison at McNeill's Island, Puget Sound, on the Dollar liner President McKinley.

This information was obtained yesterday afternoon after it was learned that Mr. Raven had not withdrawn his notice of appeal, and probably would not do so. It was stated that inasmuch as bail had been denied by Judge Milton J. Helmick of the United States Court for China, he would most likely sail on the same boat that is to take his former associate, Mr. John Warner Brown, to America and the same penitentiary. Mr. Brown was tried in the United States Court for China on the same charges and sentenced to two years' imprisonment.

Notices of appeal were filed by Mr. C. Franklin, attorney for the two men, a week ago. At the same time, motion for bail also was filed. The motion was denied and

last Saturday, Mr. Brown withdrew his appeal.

The United States Court for China is scheduled to leave for Canton on the President Hoover this morning. Departure was delayed one day owing to the late arrival of the Hoover in this city. The court is expected to return to Shanghai in about two weeks and will shortly thereafter leave for Tientsin for the trial of Dr. John Colbert, accused of having attempted to murder his wife by administering poison to her over a long period.

The two principal cases to be heard in Canton are the Banque de l'Indo-Chine vs. Paget and the National City Bank of New York vs. Hashim. The first involves the complicated estate of the late Mr. Charles Souders Paget, who died on July 26, 1933. He left no will and his widow applied for administration of the estate on behalf of herself and her three children. There are two mortgages against real estate left by Mr. Paget, one of which is claimed by the Banque de l'Indo-Chine. The second case concerns foreclosure of mortgage.

《字林西报》，1936年2月12日，星期三.2

雷文可能
与布朗一同
乘船赴美

前美亚金融公司负责人
预计不会撤回上诉

美亚金融公司（现已清算）前总裁弗兰克·J·雷文先生，因挪用公款和欺诈罪被判处五年监禁，极有可能乘坐美元轮船公司的“麦金莱总统号” liner 前往美国及位于普吉特湾麦克尼尔岛的联邦监狱。

这一消息是昨日下午得知的，当时获悉雷文先生并未撤回其上诉通知，且可能不会这样做。据悉，由于中国美国法庭的米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官拒绝保释，他很可能将与他的前同事约翰·沃纳·布朗先生乘坐同一艘船前往美国及同一所监狱。布朗先生在中国美国法庭因相同指控受审，并被判处两年监禁。

两人的律师C·富兰克林先生于一周前提出了上诉通知。同时，也提交了保释申请。该申请被驳回，且

上周六，布朗先生撤回了他的上诉。

中国美国法庭定于今天上午乘坐“胡佛总统号”前往广州。由于“胡佛总统号”抵达本市较晚，行程推迟了一天。预计法庭将在约两周后返回上海，随后不久将前往天津，审理约翰·科尔伯特博士一案，他被指控在长时期内通过投毒企图谋杀其妻子。

将在广州审理的两起主要案件是印度支那银行诉佩吉特案，以及纽约花旗银行诉哈希姆案。第一起案件涉及已故查尔斯·苏德斯·佩吉特先生复杂的遗产，他于1933年7月26日去世。他未留遗嘱，其遗孀代表自己及三个子女申请管理遗产。佩吉特先生留下的房地产上有两项抵押贷款，其中一项由印度支那银行主张。第二起案件涉及抵押品赎回权的取消。

（批：归档

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 9, 1936

APPEAL WITHDRAWN
BY J. W. BROWN

Likely to Leave for U.S. on
February 18

John Warner Brown, who a week ago was sentenced to two years imprisonment on McNeill's Island by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the U.S. Court for China on seven counts of embezzlement and false pretences in connection with the transactions of the defunct American Oriental Finance Corporation, yesterday withdrew his appeal to the Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco.

His move followed close on the decision of Judge Helmick on Friday denying bail to him and his co-defendant, F. J. Raven, who was sentenced to five years.

American Court officials said yesterday that probably Brown would be sent to America on February 18 in the ss. President McKinley, which goes to Seattle, where the Federal penitentiary is located. He is not as yet certain as to who will be deputed to make the trip with Brown to America.

Mr. Raven made no announcement yesterday as regards his appeal.

（批：File 9/2 17 FEB. 1936）

《北华捷报》，1936年2月9日，星期日

J. W. 布朗
撤回上诉

可能于2月18日启程赴美

约翰·沃纳·布朗在一周前由中国美国法庭的米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官就其与已倒闭的美亚金融公司交易相关的七项挪用公款和虚假陈述罪名判处在麦克尼尔岛监禁两年，昨日他撤回了向旧金山巡回上诉法院提出的上诉。

他的这一举动紧随赫尔米克法官周五拒绝他和同案被告F. J. 雷文（被判处五年徒刑）保释的决定之后。

美国法院官员昨日表示，布朗可能会于2月18日乘坐前往西雅图的“麦金莱总统号”轮船被送往美国，联邦监狱即位于那里。目前尚不确定谁将被委派陪同布朗前往美国。

雷文先生昨日未就其上诉事宜发表任何声明。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 9, 1936

Kleffel Cited To Tell Court
Of $20,000 In A.O.B.C. Boxes

German Bank Manager
Called To Chinese
Tribunal Tuesday

Mr. J. Kleffel, former Vice-President and General Manager of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, now in process of liquidation, has been summoned to appear before the First Special District Court on Tuesday, February 11, for hearing in connection with certain money alleged to have been missing from the bank at the time it was taken over by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator, last June.

This information was obtained by a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday morning after summons had been served by an official of the Shanghai Municipal Police. The summons was issued under the Chinese Criminal Code in accordance with provisions in which an involved person can be summoned to appear before the court rather than brought before the tribunal on a writ of detention. The present case involves a sum of approximately $20,000, alleged to have been placed in the bank for safe-keeping purposes.

Except for the fact that Mr. Frank L. Hough signed the complaint, no further details of the case could be obtained. Serving of summons and the date set for hearing, however, were definitely confirmed. Mr. Kleffel, being of German nationality, is subject to the jurisdiction of the First Special District Court.

Mr. Kleffel was manager of the American-Oriental Bank for several years and is well-known in practically all foreign communities of Shanghai. He was with the bank for more than a decade, starting in

J. Kleffel

a minor capacity and later working up to the post of Vice-President and General Manager. It is stated that he lost heavily of his own funds when the bank closed its doors.

He has resided in the Far East for many years, coming here from Japan at the conclusion of the World War where he had been interned in a Japanese prison camp.

During his years in the banking business in Shanghai, Mr. Kleffel was known as a brilliant exchange man and was in charge of the exchange transactions of the American-Oriental Bank.

After the bank closed its doors on May 23, and a liquidator was appointed, Mr. Kleffel assisted the liquidator for several months. He is married and resides in Columbia Circle.

9 FEB. 1938

《字林西报》，1936年2月9日，星期日

克莱费尔被传唤出庭
就美亚银行箱内两万美元一事作证

德籍银行经理
将于周二受审于
中国法庭

已停业并正处于清算过程中的美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前副总裁兼总经理J. 克莱费尔（J. Kleffel）先生，已被传唤于2月11日星期二出席第一特区法院，就据称在去年六月由清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生接管该银行时从银行失踪的某些款项进行聆讯。

此消息是《字林西报》记者于昨日上午在工部局警务处官员送达传票后获悉的。该传票依据《中华民国刑法》相关规定签发，根据这些规定，涉案人员可被传唤出庭，而非通过拘留令拘提至法庭。本案涉及金额约两万美元，据称这笔钱是存入银行以求保管的。

除了弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生签署了控告书这一事实外，无法获得该案的其他细节。然而，传票的送达和确定的聆讯日期已得到确切证实。克莱费尔先生具有德国国籍，受第一特区法院管辖。

克莱费尔先生担任美亚银行经理多年，在上海几乎所有的外侨社区中都广为人知。他在该银行工作超过十年，起初担任

J. Kleffel

低级职务，后来逐步晋升至副总裁兼总经理一职。据说，在该银行关门时，他个人的资金遭受了重大损失。

他在远东居住多年，是在世界大战结束时从日本来到这里的，此前他曾被关押在日本的战俘营中。

在上海从事银行业期间，克莱费尔先生以精通外汇业务而闻名，并负责美亚银行的外汇交易。

在该银行于5月23日关门并任命清算人后，克莱费尔先生协助清算人工作了数月。他已婚，居住在哥伦比亚圈（Columbia Circle）。

1938年2月9日

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 8, 1936
73 3/5.

Judge Helmick Denies Bail
For Raven And Brown

Considered Opinion Filed In Which The View Is
Expressed That The Grounds Of Appeal Will Be
Found Unsubstantial By Higher Court

An order denying bail to Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, former heads of the now-defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, convicted of embezzlement and fraudulent false pretences and sentenced to imprisonment for five and two years, respectively, in the McNeill's Island Penitentiary, was entered yesterday afternoon by Judge Milton J. Helmick of the United States Court for China, who was the trial judge in the case.
A considered opinion accompanied the decision, which was conveyed to the convicted men by Mr. C. S. Franklin, one of the defence attorneys, soon after it was filed. Both men are confined in the Ward Road Gaol, awaiting transfer to the United States to commence serving their sentences.

Seven Grounds Of Appeal
The convicted men asked for bail pending the hearing of an appeal against their conviction by the San Francisco Circuit Court of Appeals. They set forth seven grounds for their appeal, but Judge Helmick, executing what he terms an "embarrassing and inconsistent assignment" in ruling on the bail application, records the view that all the grounds will be viewed by the Court of Appeals as "unsubstantial."
The trial of Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown lasted exactly one month, from January 2 to February 3, and ended with a finding that the accused had embezzled fully-paid securities belonging to clients of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation by pledging them in a margin account with E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco, instead of holding them in safekeeping.

Full Text Of Opinion
The full text of Judge Helmick's opinion regarding the bail application is as follows:—
"This is an application by defendants to be admitted to bail pending appeal from their conviction and sentence in this Court. The right of bail is governed by No. VI of Rules promulgated by the Supreme Court of the United States, effective September 1, 1934, which reads as follows:
Bail. The defendant shall not be admitted to bail pending an appeal from a judgment of conviction save as follows: Bail may be granted by the trial judge or by the appellate court, or, where the appellate court is not in session, by any judge thereof or by the circuit justice. Bail shall not be allowed pending appeal unless it appears that the appeal involves a substantial question which should be determined by the appellate court.
"Rule VI is so new that it has received only meagre discussion and construction by the United States Courts, and so far as this Court can discover there are only two reported cases dealing with it. The first is Kittrell v. U.S.A. (C.C.A. 10), 76 Fed. II, 333, which affords no assistance because the Appellate Court virtually decided the merits of the appeal in denying bail. The second case is United States v. Delaney, 8 Fed. Suppl. 224, which is a scholarly and entertaining opinion by a U.S. District Judge of New Jersey, dealing in rather philosophical and non-legalistic fashion with the policy of denying appeal bail after conviction.

An Embarrassing Assignment
"Rule VI visits upon the trial Judge the embarrassing and inconsistent assignment of attempting with neutral detachment to weigh his own acts in the trial and predict with what degree of gravity the Appellate Court will look upon the grounds of appeal. In the case of United States v. Delaney, supra, detachment in making the decision was sought by calling in a different District Judge to pass upon the right of bail. The case recites: 'We have thought it wise in this District to lend perspective by prescribing the assistance of a Judge other than the one who presided at the trial.' Unfortunately there is no other in this jurisdiction to summon to the task.
"The application of Rule VI manifestly depends upon what is a substantial question which should be determined by the Appellate Court, or rather, what the trial Court believes the Appellate Court will believe is 'a substantial question which should be determined by the Appellate Court.' We have no judicial definition of the term 'substantial question' as used in Rule VI, but perhaps it is used to describe a ground of appeal which is likely to insure the success of the appeal and the reversal of the conviction. But whatever the right definition may be, the element of prophecy is inevitably involved, and as was said in United States v. Delaney, supra, 'we cannot surely predict the reaction of the judicial mind, appellate or otherwise, to the application of a legal question.' If likelihood of success on appeal is the correct test, this Court is of the opinion there is no 'substantial question' involved in the appeal of these defendants, although it demands great temerity on the part of this Court to prejudge the merits of the appeal and to assume the Appellate Court will certainly agree.

Grounds Set Forth
"The grounds of defendants' appeal are as follows:
1.—That appellants were denied a trial by jury.
2.—That appellants' request for special findings of fact and conclusions of law were refused.
3.—That the acts with which the appellants stand charged were not committed within the jurisdiction of the trial court and therefore the trial court had no jurisdiction to try appellants.
4.—That the trial court committed error in various rulings made during the course of the trial with respect to the admission and exclusion of evidence.
5.—That the motion of appellants to dismiss the charges made at the conclusion of the case for the prosecution was denied.
6.—That the motion in arrest of judgment was denied.
7.—That the verdict or findings of the trial court that appellants were guilty of the offences charged in counts 2, 4, 5, 7, 10, 13 and 15 was contrary to the evidence and the weight of evidence.

"The 2nd, 5th, 6th, and 7th are purely formal. The 4th is without substance because only a few rulings of a trivial nature were made on objections to evidence during the trial, and these were not unfavourable to the defendants. The 3rd ground surely has no merit, and in any event could not apply to all of the counts of the Information on which defendants were convicted. The bald statement of the first ground on paper doubtless appears 'substantial' to the uninformed, but those familiar with this jurisdiction know that during 90 years of American exercise of extraterritorial rights in China, including the last 30 years during which this Court has been in existence, no person accused of crime has ever been accorded a jury trial.

A Settled Policy
"This settled policy, confirmed by the decision of the Supreme Court of the United States in the case of In re. Ross, in 1891, has come to be taken so much for granted that the demand of defendants for a jury trial struck everyone as an extraordinary novelty. A number of convictions of this Court have been reviewed on appeal by the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals without comment by that Court on the lack of a jury. It is possible that this question, which appears so unsubstantial to us in China who are so familiar with the uniqueness of this jurisdiction, may appear substantial to the Appellate Court at home, but this Court ventures to forecast, not merely to guess, that the Appellate Court will not overturn the long-sanctioned and hitherto unchallenged procedure of this jurisdiction. If this prediction turns out a mistake it will be a very bad mistake indeed, but the risk must be taken unless the Court abdicates the duty imposed upon it by the letter and the spirit of Rule VI.
"Bail will be denied and it is so ordered."

（批：File）
（签名）
（印：8 FEB. 1936）

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年2月8日，星期六
73 3/5.

赫尔米克法官拒绝
雷文和布朗的保释申请

提交了一份经过深思熟虑的意见书，其中表示
上诉理由将被上级法院认定为缺乏实质依据

美国在华法院法官米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）于昨日下午下达命令，拒绝给予弗兰克·J. 雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J. 沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生保释。这两人是现已停业的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的前负责人，因犯有挪用公款和欺诈性虚假陈述罪，分别被判处在麦克尼尔岛（McNeill's Island）监狱服刑五年和两年。赫尔米克法官是该案的初审法官。

随判决一同提交的还有一份经过深思熟虑的意见书，该意见书在归档后不久即由辩护律师之一C. S. 富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生传达给两名被判刑者。两人目前均被关押在华德路监狱，等待被引渡至美国开始服刑。

七项上诉理由

两名被判刑者请求在旧金山巡回上诉法院审理其针对定罪的上诉期间予以保释。他们列出了七项上诉理由，但赫尔米克法官在裁定保释申请时，执行了他所称的“令人尴尬且不一致的任务”，并记录了他的观点，即所有理由都将被上诉法院视为“缺乏实质依据”。

雷文先生和布朗先生的审判历时整整一个月，从1月2日至2月3日，最终认定被告将属于美亚金融公司客户的已缴清证券，不是作为保管持有，而是作为保证金账户抵押给了旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company），从而挪用了这些证券。

意见书全文

赫尔米克法官关于保释申请的意见书全文如下：—

“这是被告申请在其对本法院的定罪和量刑提出上诉期间获准保释。保释权受美国最高法院颁布的、于1934年9月1日生效的规则第六条管辖，该条规定如下：

保释。除以下情况外，被告在对定罪判决提出上诉期间不得获准保释：保释可由初审法官或上诉法院授予，或者，如果上诉法院未开庭，可由其任何法官或巡回大法官授予。除非看来上诉涉及应由上诉法院裁定的实质性问题，否则在上诉期间不得允许保释。

“规则第六条如此新近，以至于美国法院对其讨论和解释寥寥无几，据本法院所知，只有两个已报道的案例涉及该规则。第一个是基特雷尔诉美国案（Kittrell v. U.S.A. (C.C.A. 10), 76 Fed. II, 333），该案未提供助益，因为上诉法院在拒绝保释时实际上已经对上诉的是非曲直作出了裁决。第二个案例是美国诉德莱尼案（United States v. Delaney, 8 Fed. Suppl. 224），这是一份由新泽西州一位美国地区法官撰写的富有学识且有趣的意见书，以相当哲学化且非法律主义的方式探讨了定罪后拒绝上诉保释的政策。

一项令人尴尬的任务

“规则第六条给初审法官带来了一项令人尴尬且不一致的任务，即试图以中立超然的态度权衡自己在审判中的行为，并预测上诉法院将以何种严肃程度看待上诉理由。在上述美国诉德莱尼案中，为了在作出决定时保持超然，曾邀请另一位地区法官来裁定保释权。该案陈述道：‘我们认为，在本区通过规定由非主持审判的法官协助，有助于提供视角。’不幸的是，在本司法管辖区内没有其他法官可以召来承担此项任务。

“规则第六条的适用显然取决于什么是‘应由上诉法院裁定的实质性问题’，或者更确切地说，取决于初审法院认为上诉法院会相信什么是‘应由上诉法院裁定的实质性问题’。对于规则第六条中使用的‘实质性问题’一词，我们没有司法定义，但也许它用来描述一种可能确保上诉成功并推翻定罪的上诉理由。但无论正确的定义是什么，预言的因素都不可避免地包含在内，正如在美国诉德莱尼案中所说，‘我们无法确切预测司法思维，无论是上诉法院还是其他法院，对法律问题的应用会作何反应。’如果上诉成功的可能性是正确的检验标准，本法院认为，这些被告的上诉中不涉及任何‘实质性问题’，尽管本法院预先判断上诉的是非曲直并假设上诉法院肯定会同意，这需要极大的鲁莽。

所列理由

“被告的上诉理由如下：
1.—上诉人被剥夺了由陪审团审判的权利。
2.—上诉人要求特别认定事实和法律结论的请求被拒绝。
3.—指控上诉人的行为并非在初审法院的管辖范围内实施，因此初审法院无权审判上诉人。
4.—初审法院在审判过程中关于证据采纳和排除的各项裁决中存在错误。
5.—上诉人在控方结案时提出的驳回指控的动议被拒绝。
6.—停止判决的动议被拒绝。
7.—初审法院认定上诉人在第2、4、5、7、10、13和15项罪名中有罪的裁决或认定事实与证据及证据的分量相悖。

“第2、5、6和7项纯属形式问题。第4项缺乏实质内容，因为在审判期间针对证据异议仅作出了一些微不足道的裁决，且这些裁决对被告并非不利。第3项理由肯定没有价值，而且无论如何不能适用于被告被定罪的所有起诉书罪名。第一项理由在纸面上的直白陈述无疑会让不知情者显得‘具有实质性’，但熟悉本司法管辖区的人都知道，在美国在华行使治外法权的90年中，包括本法院存在的最后30年里，从未有任何被指控犯罪的人获得过陪审团审判。

既定政策

“这一既定政策在1891年美国最高法院在罗斯案（In re. Ross）的判决中得到确认，如今已被视为理所当然，以至于被告要求陪审团审判让每个人都感到这是一种非凡的新奇事物。本法院的多项定罪曾在第九巡回上诉法院的上诉审查中得到审议，而该法院对缺乏陪审团一事未置一词。有可能这个问题，在我们这些如此熟悉本司法管辖区独特性的在华人士看来如此缺乏实质性，但在国内的上诉法院看来可能具有实质性，但本法院大胆预测，不仅仅是猜测，上诉法院不会推翻本司法管辖区长期认可且迄今未受挑战的程序。如果这一预测结果是错误的，那确实是一个非常严重的错误，但除非本法院放弃规则第六条文字和精神所赋予的职责，否则必须承担这一风险。

“保释将被拒绝，特此命令。”

（批：归档）
（签名）
（印：1936年2月8日）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 1936

NO DECISION YET ON
RAVEN-BROWN BAIL

U.S. Court Leaving For
Canton Next Week;
Tientsin Later

No decision has yet been made
by Judge Milton J. Helmick on the
motion for bail, pending appeal,
which was submitted to the Unit-
ed States Court for China by Mr.
Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner
Brown, who were sentenced on
Monday to five and two years' im-
prisonment, respectively, following
their conviction on charges of em-
bezzlement and fraudulent false
pretences. Judge Helmick was ex-
pected to deal with the motion yes-
terday, but no action had been
taken by the time the Court offi-
ces closed down for the day.

Having disposed of the Raven-
Brown trial, Judge Helmick plans
to leave for Canton early next
week to conduct a session of the
U.S. Court for China in that city,
where one or two civil cases await
hearing.

Judge Helmick will sail on the
s.s. President Hoover, which is
due to leave next Tuesday. He will
be accompanied by Mr. William T.
Collins, Clerk of the Court, Miss
Helen Wiley, Court Reporter, Mr.
Zee Yang-ling, Court Interpreter,
and Mrs. Helmick.

Tientsin After Canton

The Court session in Canton is
expected to last only a few days
and when the Judge and officials
return to Shanghai they are ex-
pected to proceed, within a few
days, to Tientsin, for the trial of
Dr. John Colbert, the well-known
medical man who is charged with
attempting to murder his wife by
giving her poison.

On the way back to Shanghai
from Tientsin, the Court may stop
at Hankow for a session, in order
to dispose of the case of Eugene
Brinson and Carl J. Lemcke,
charged by the U.S. District At-
torney, on the complaint of the
Chinese authorities, with attempt-
ing to liberate Joseph Walden,
otherwise Mr. "X," from his pri-
son cell in Wuchang, where he is
serving a 15-year sentence for
military and political espionage.

Dr. Colbert and Messrs. Brinson
and Lemcke are at liberty, on bail.

S. 6701f 17

《字林西报》，1936年2月6日，星期四

雷文-布朗保释案尚未裁决

美国法院下周启程前往广州；随后前往天津

米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官尚未对弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生向美国驻华法院提交的待上诉期间保释动议作出裁决。二人于周一因挪用公款及欺诈性虚假陈述罪名成立，分别被判处五年和两年监禁。赫尔米克法官原预计昨日处理该动议，但直至法院办公室当日下班时，仍未采取任何行动。

在处理完雷文-布朗案的审判后，赫尔米克法官计划于下周初启程前往广州，在该市主持美国驻华法院的庭审，届时将有一至两起民事案件等待审理。

赫尔米克法官将乘坐“胡佛总统号”（s.s. President Hoover）轮船启程，该船定于下周二离港。随行人员包括法院书记员威廉·T·柯林斯（William T. Collins）先生、法庭速记员海伦·威利（Helen Wiley）小姐、法庭翻译杨泽龄（Zee Yang-ling，音译）先生以及赫尔米克夫人。

广州之后前往天津

预计在广州的庭审仅持续数日，当法官及法院官员返回上海后，预计将在数日内前往天津，审理约翰·科尔伯特（John Colbert）博士一案。科尔伯特博士是知名医生，被控企图通过投毒杀害其妻子。

在从天津返回上海的途中，法院可能会在汉口停留并开庭，以处理尤金·布林森（Eugene Brinson）和卡尔·J·莱姆克（Carl J. Lemcke）的案件。二人受美国地区检察官指控，系应中国当局投诉，被控企图将约瑟夫·瓦尔登（Joseph Walden，即“X”先生）从武昌的牢房中解救出来。瓦尔登目前正因军事和政治间谍罪服十五年徒刑。

科尔伯特博士以及布林森和莱姆克先生目前均获准保释在外。

Raven, Brown File Notices
Of Appeal, Ask For Bail

Convicted Men Set Forth Seven Grounds For The
Reversal Of Judgment; Verdict Declared To
Be Against The Weight Of Evidence

A motion for the release on bail
of Frank J. Raven and J. Warner
Brown, now locked up in Ward
Road Gaol following their convic-
tion and sentence on charges of
embezzlement and fraudulent false
pretences, was submitted to the
United States Court for China yes-
terday by Mr. Richard T. Evans
and Mr. C. S. Franklin, legal re-
presentatives of the convicted men,
and will be decided this morning
in Chambers by Judge Milton J.
Helmick.

At the same time, notice of ap-
peal against their conviction and
sentence was given by the defend-
ants through their attorneys. Bail
is being sought pending the hear-
ing of the appeal by the Circuit
Court of Appeals in San Francisco,
"on the ground that it appears
that the appeal involves substan-
tial questions which should be de-
termined by the appellate court as
set forth in the notice of appeal."

Mr. Raven was sentenced to five
years' imprisonment in the Mc-
Neill's Island Penitentiary, while
Mr. Brown was given two years
in the same institution. The con-
victed men set forth the following
grounds for the setting aside of
their conviction and sentence:

Grounds Of Appeal

1.—That they were denied a trial
by jury.
2.—That their request for special
findings of fact and conclusions of
law was refused.

3.—That the acts with which
they were charged were not com-
mitted within the jurisdiction of
the trial court and therefore the
trial court had no jurisdiction to
try them.
4.—That the trial court commit-
ted error in various rulings made
during the course of the trial with
respect to the admission and ex-
clusion of evidence.
5.—That the motion to dismiss
the charges, made at the conclusion
of the case for the prosecution,
was denied.
6.—That the motion in arrest of
judgment was denied.
7.—That the verdict or findings
of the trial court were contrary
to the evidence and the weight of
the evidence.

If the motion for bail pending
appeal is denied by the Court, the
convicted men still have recourse
to the appellate court. Should the
bail application finally fail, how-
ever, it is expected that they will
be sent from here on the first Am-
erican vessel bound for Seattle, to
commence serving their sentences.

L. G. (Crime)
Information.

雷文、布朗提交上诉通知，申请保释

定罪者列出七项推翻判决的理由；称裁决违背证据权重

理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生和C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生作为两名定罪者的法律代表，昨日向美国驻华法院提交了一项动议，要求对弗兰克·J·雷文和J·沃纳·布朗进行保释释放。二人此前因挪用公款及欺诈性虚假陈述罪名成立并被判刑，现关押在提篮桥监狱（Ward Road Gaol）。该动议将由米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官于今日上午在法官内室（Chambers）作出裁决。

与此同时，被告通过其律师提交了针对其定罪和量刑的上诉通知。鉴于“上诉似乎涉及上诉通知中所述应由上诉法院裁定的实质性问题”，被告方正在寻求在旧金山巡回上诉法院审理上诉期间的保释。

雷文先生被判处在麦克尼尔岛联邦惩教所（McNeill's Island Penitentiary）服刑五年，布朗先生在同一机构服刑两年。定罪者列出了以下撤销其定罪和量刑的理由：

上诉理由

1. 他们被剥夺了由陪审团审判的权利。
2. 他们要求作出特别事实认定和法律结论的请求被拒绝。

3. 被指控的行为并非发生在审判法院的管辖范围内，因此审判法院无权对他们进行审判。
4. 审判法院在审判过程中就证据的采纳和排除作出的各项裁定存在错误。
5. 在控方案件陈述结束时提出的驳回指控动议被拒绝。
6.  arrest of judgment（停止执行判决/逮捕判决）动议被拒绝。
7. 审判法院的裁决或认定事实与证据及证据权重相悖。

如果法院驳回了待上诉期间的保释动议，定罪者仍可向上诉法院寻求救济。然而，如果保释申请最终失败，预计他们将搭乘首班驶往西雅图的美国船只从这里被遣送，开始服刑。

L. G. （犯罪科）
情报。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 4, 1936
1/32 81

Raven, Brown Sentenced
To Prison Terms In A
Federal Penitentiary

U.S. Court Gives Raven Five Years And Brown Two,
To Be Served On McNeil's Island, Seattle;
Motion For Arrest Of Judgment Denied

CONVICTED MEN LIKELY TO APPEAL; BUT
REMOVAL TO U.S. EXPECTED SOON

Sentences of five years' imprisonment in the case of Mr. Frank J. Raven and two years in the case of Mr. J. Warner Brown, were passed by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China yesterday morning, following their conviction last Saturday on seven counts of embezzlement and fraudulent false pretences, of which they were found guilty in their capacities as President, and Vice-President and Manager, respectively, of the now-defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, which closed its doors on May 23 last year when all the Raven enterprises crashed.

The convicted men spent the week-end in cells at the Ward Road Gaol and were brought to Court yesterday morning to hear their sentences. Thereafter, they were returned to the gaol and it is expected that they will be sent from here to McNeil's Island Penitentiary to serve their sentences about the middle of this month.

Arrest Motion Denied

A motion for arrest of judgment as regards both Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown was submitted to the Court by defence counsel and denied by Judge Helmick before passing of sentence, the defence thereafter noting an exception to this ruling. Grounds submitted for the motion were as follows:

1.—That the Court denied the defendants a trial by jury.
2.—That the Court refused the request of the defendants to make special findings of fact and conclusions of law.
3.—That it appears from the record and transcript of evidence in the case that the acts with which the defendants were charged were not committed within the jurisdiction of the United States Court for China and that therefore the Court had no jurisdiction to try the defendants or either of them.

A Cause Celebre

With the passing of sentence yesterday morning, "finis" was written to a trial which had long since become a cause celebre. The substance of the charges on which the two men were convicted was that they took clients' fully-paid securities, which should have been held in safekeeping, and pledged them to E. A. Pierce and Company of San Francisco as margin for the trading activities of the A.-O.F.C.

Although the last act in this protracted legal drama had been robbed of much of its sensationalism because of the fact that convictions had already been recorded, thus making sentence inevitable, a crowd even larger than previous days gathered to witness the last proceedings. Long before 10 o'clock, when the session was due to commence, the courtroom was filled and the entrance jammed with between 30 and 40 people.

Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown were brought to Court under escort of two uniformed members of the Shanghai Municipal Police and took their customary places in the courtroom a few minutes before the Judge entered.

Convicted Men Nervous

Mr. Brown was the first to enter. He came alone and sat down, the cynosure of all eyes, until Mr. Raven entered a moment or two later. Both men were obviously wrought up and nervous.

Having left for Tientsin on Saturday, Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, was conspicuous by his absence. Mr. C. S. Franklin, attorney for Mr. Brown, was, however, present.

Judge Helmick entered at 10 a.m., took his seat on the Bench, and after denying the motion for arrest of judgment, addressed himself to Mr. Raven: "Frank J. Raven, do you have anything to say why the sentence of this Court should not be passed upon you?"

Visibly trembling, his hands clutching two sheets of paper, one pencilled, the other typewritten, Mr. Raven, who had risen to his feet at the Judge's command, commenced to read a statement.

Raven Makes Statement

"Your Honour," he began, "I was advised by my attorney, because of the precarious state of my health, not to take the witness-stand. I wish to make a statement. With your permission, I will read it. It will only take a few minutes."

Pausing momentarily from time to time to make out his handwriting, Mr. Raven said:

"I have been convicted on the testimony of Mr. Rosse and Mr. Brown and on the evidence contained in the Haley report and the Cocquelet report.

"Mr. Rosse had been discharged by me for incompetency when his highly paid services were no longer useful to the company (American-Oriental Finance Corporation). It was done in the best interests of the company and the shareholders, but Mr. Rosse has borne malice towards me ever since. He never mentioned to me once in any conversation the subject of paid-up shares in the margin account. Mr. Rosse's conversations with me were always confined to Mr. Rosse and his relation to the company. I am positive and know full well he never mentioned to me paid-up shares in the margin account—not once.

Criticizes Brown Testimony

"In Mr. Brown's testimony, during the first four days, he was inclined to be truthful. He said he thought he had conversations with me on paid-up shares, but he couldn't remember a single time or place or conversation, for the very simple reason that there weren't any. He maintained that attitude through four days of cruel, gruelling cross-examination by the prosecution. On the last day, he broke down completely, so dazed and muddled he didn't know what he was saying, and he agreed to anything and everything the prosecution said, regardless of fact or truth.

"After working with Mr. Brown for over 12 years, I say he is a man of average ability, fundamentally and basically honest. You couldn't hire him or pay him to do a deed he considered dishonest. He has made many mistakes.

"If Mr. Brown will tell you the truth this morning before you pronounce sentence, he will say that under cruel cross-examination last Friday he made mis-statements. He will say that he never showed me the Cocquelet report. It was never shown me by anyone. I have never seen it. He will tell you he can't remember discussing the Haley report with me, for he never did.

"The Haley report was made at a time when I was slowly recovering from an almost fatal illness. I didn't read it. I initialled it and filed it for future reference. Haley admitted under oath that he never discussed the report with me. Brown never did either, and I hope he will have the courage to tell the truth to-day. All I ask is the truth.

Declares Innocence

"If you convict me on the two reports I never read and the evidence of these two witnesses, which I know and they know to be untrue, you will be sending me, an innocent man, to the penitentiary.

"Your Honour, I have nothing further to say except that I have never knowingly or intentionally committed any of the breaches of the law of which I have been accused. This is the whole truth."

When the statement had been read, Judge Helmick pronounced sentences on Mr. Raven of five years each on Counts 2, 7, 10, 13 and 15, and three years each on Counts 4 and 5, the sentences to run concurrently and to be served in the United States Federal Penitentiary on McNeil's Island in Puget Sound, near Seattle, Washington, or any other penitentiary which may be designated by the United States District Attorney.

Brown Sentenced

The Judge then commanded Mr. Brown to rise and asked whether he had anything to say why sentence should not be passed upon him.

Facing the Judge calmly, with head erect, Mr. Brown replied firmly: "I have nothing to say."

The convicted man was then given sentences of two years on each of the seven counts on which he and Mr. Raven were found guilty, the sentences to run concurrently and to be served also on McNeil's Island.

After this, the Court adjourned and Messrs. Raven and Brown were escorted back to gaol. Mr. C. S. Franklin indicated to press reporters that an appeal would certainly be made against Mr. Raven's conviction, but was non-committal in regard to Mr. Brown.

（批：4 FEB. 1936）

《字林西报》，1936年2月4日，星期二
1/32 81

雷文、布朗被判
联邦监狱监禁刑期

美国法院判处雷文五年、布朗两年，
在西雅图麦克尼尔岛服刑；
驳回停止判决动议

定罪者可能上诉；但
预计不久将被引渡至美国

昨天上午，米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官在美国驻华法院对弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生判处五年监禁，对J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生判处两年监禁。此前，两人于上周六被裁定七项挪用公款及欺诈性虚假陈述罪名成立。他们在已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）分别担任总裁，以及副总裁兼经理职务时犯下上述罪行。去年5月23日，随着雷文旗下所有企业崩溃，该公司关门停业。

两名定罪者在华德路监狱的牢房中度过了周末，并于昨天上午被提至法庭听候宣判。随后，他们被押回监狱。预计他们将于本月中旬左右从这里被送往麦克尼尔岛监狱（McNeil's Island Penitentiary）服刑。

驳回停止判决动议

辩护律师向法庭提交了针对雷文先生和布朗先生的停止判决（arrest of judgment）动议，但赫尔米克法官在宣判前予以驳回，辩护方随后对该裁决提出异议。提出该动议的理由如下：

1. 法院剥夺了被告接受陪审团审判的权利。
2. 法院拒绝了被告要求作出特别事实认定和法律结论的请求。
3. 从案件记录和证据誊本来看，被告被指控的行为并非发生在美国驻华法院的管辖范围内，因此法院无权审判被告中的任何一人或两人。

一桩轰动一时的案件

随着昨天上午的宣判，这场早已成为轰动一时之案的审判画上了句号。两人被定罪的主要指控内容是：他们拿走了客户本应妥善保管的全额付款证券，并将其抵押给旧金山的E. A. Pierce and Company，作为美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）交易活动的保证金。

尽管由于定罪已成定局，判刑不可避免，使得这场漫长法律戏剧的最后一幕少了许多耸人听闻的色彩，但前来见证最后程序的民众甚至比前几天更多。在上午10点庭审预定开始之前很久，法庭内已座无虚席，入口处也挤满了三四十人。

雷文先生和布朗先生在两名身穿制服的上海公共租界工部局警务处警员的押解下进入法庭，并在法官入庭前几分钟坐到了他们在法庭上的惯常位置。

定罪者神情紧张

布朗先生首先进入法庭。他独自进来并坐下，成为众人目光的焦点，直到一两分钟后雷文先生进入。两人都明显显得激动不安和紧张。

雷文先生的辩护律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生已于周六前往天津，因此他的缺席引人注目。然而，布朗先生的代理律师C. S. 富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生在场。

赫尔米克法官于上午10时入庭，在法官席就座，在驳回停止判决动议后，他对雷文先生说道：“弗兰克·J·雷文，你有什么理由说明本庭不应对你进行宣判吗？”

雷文先生遵照法官命令起立，双手紧握着两张纸，一张是铅笔手写的，另一张是打字机打印的， visibly trembling（明显颤抖着），开始宣读一份声明。

雷文发表声明

“法官阁下，”他开始说道，“我的律师因我健康状况不佳，建议我不要出庭作证。我想作一份声明。经您允许，我将宣读它。这只需要几分钟。”

雷文先生不时停顿片刻以辨认自己的笔迹，说道：

“我是基于罗斯先生（Mr. Rosse）和布朗先生的证词，以及海利报告（Haley report）和科克莱特报告（Cocquelet report）中所载的证据而被定罪的。

“罗斯先生曾因无能被我解雇，当时他高薪服务对公司已不再有用。这是为了公司和股东的最大利益，但罗斯先生从此对我怀恨在心。他在与我的任何谈话中从未提及过一次保证金账户中已缴足股份的问题。罗斯先生与我的谈话总是局限于罗斯先生本人及其与公司的关系。我确信并完全清楚，他从未向我提及保证金账户中的已缴足股份——一次也没有。

批评布朗的证词

“在布朗先生的证词中，在前四天里，他倾向于如实陈述。他说他认为曾与我谈论过已缴足股份的事，但他记不起任何一次时间、地点或谈话内容，原因很简单，因为根本不存在这样的谈话。在检方长达四天的残酷、严酷的交叉盘问中，他一直保持着这种态度。在最后一天，他彻底崩溃了，神志恍惚、混乱不堪，不知道自己在说什么，并且不顾事实或真相，同意了检方所说的一切。

“在与布朗先生共事超过12年后，我说他是一个能力平平的人，本质上和基本面上是诚实的。你无法雇佣他或收买他去做出他认为不诚实的行为。他犯过许多错误。

“如果布朗先生今天在您宣判前说出真相，他会说在上周五残酷的交叉盘问下，他作了不实陈述。他会说他从未向我展示过科克莱特报告。没有任何人向我展示过这份报告。我从未见过它。他会告诉您，他不记得与我讨论过海利报告，因为他确实没有这样做。

“海利报告是在我从一场几乎致命的疾病中缓慢康复期间制作的。我没有阅读它。我只是在文件上签了首字母缩写并将其归档以备将来参考。海利在宣誓下承认他从未与我讨论过该报告。布朗先生也没有，我希望他今天有勇气说出真相。我所要求的只是真相。

宣称无罪

“如果您依据两份我从未阅读过的报告以及这两名证人的证词给我定罪，而我和他们都知道这些证词是不真实的，那么您就是将我，一个无辜的人，送进监狱。

“法官阁下，我没有什么要说的了，除了我从未明知故犯地实施过任何我被指控的违法行为。这就是全部真相。”

声明宣读完毕后，赫尔米克法官宣布对雷文先生的判决：第2、7、10、13和15项罪名各判处五年监禁，第4和5项罪名各判处三年监禁，刑期同时执行，在华盛顿州西雅图附近普吉特湾的麦克尼尔岛美国联邦监狱，或由美国地区检察官指定的任何其他监狱服刑。

布朗获刑

法官随即命令布朗先生起立，询问他是否有理由说明不应对他进行宣判。

布朗先生昂首挺胸，平静地面对法官，坚定地回答：“我无话可说。”

随后，该定罪男子在其与雷文先生被裁定有罪的七项罪名上各被判处两年监禁，刑期同时执行，同样在麦克尼尔岛服刑。

此后，法庭休庭，雷文先生和布朗先生被押回监狱。C. S. 富兰克林先生向记者表示，肯定会对雷文先生的定罪提出上诉，但对于布朗先生的情况则未置可否。

（批注：1936年2月4日）

Question Of Bail
Noting of appeal paves the way
for a bail application, which, it
was learned, would be dealt with,
if and when made, in the Judge's
Chambers. Consideration of
applications for bail will be made
under a United States Supreme
Court rule of March 8, 1934,
which provides that "a defendant
shall not be admitted to bail pend-
ing appeal from conviction save
as follows: bail may be granted
by the trial judge or by the appel-
late court, but bail shall not be
allowed pending appeal unless it
appears that the appeal involves
a substantial question which should
be determined by the appellate
court."
Mr. C. C. Curtis of the San
Francisco office of E. A. Pierce
and Company, and Mr. C. J.
Haley, A.-C.F.C. official, who were
brought here by the prosecution
last November 18 to testify against
the two defendants, will return
to the United States by the s.s.
President Taft on February 15,
it was learned yesterday.
It is considered possible that
Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown, unless
meanwhile admitted to bail, will
be shipped off to McNeil's Island
on the same vessel.

保释问题
提起上诉为申请保释铺平了道路，据悉，如果提出申请，将在法官办公室处理。保释申请的审议将依据1934年3月8日美国最高法院的一项规则进行，该规则规定：“除以下情况外，被告在针对定罪的上诉待决期间不得获准保释：初审法官或上诉法院可以准予保释，但在上诉涉及应由上诉法院裁定的实质性问题之前，不得在上诉待决期间准予保释。”
据悉，旧金山E. A. Pierce and Company办事处的C. C. 柯蒂斯（C. C. Curtis）先生和美亚金融公司（A.-C.F.C.）官员C. J. 海利（C. J. Haley）先生将于2月15日乘坐“塔夫脱总统号”轮船返回美国。他们二人是去年11月18日由检方带至此地对两名被告作不利证词的。
据认为，雷文先生和布朗先生除非在此期间获准保释，否则可能会搭乘同一艘船被送往麦克尼尔岛。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, FEBRUARY 2, 1936

U.S. Court Finds Raven
And Brown Both Guilty
Of Embezzlement, Fraud

Tense And Crowded Courtroom Listens To Verdict
By Judge Helmick: Women Break Into Tears
As Defendants Are Escorted To Prison

SENTENCE TO BE PASSED ON FORMER HEAD
OF THE A.-O.F.C. TO-MORROW MORNING

“The Government, with meticulous, painstaking and thorough completeness, has presented both evidence and law in support of the Information. From all the evidence, the Court is convinced beyond a reasonable doubt of the guilt of these defendants. The Court finds the defendants Frank Jay Raven and John Warner Brown guilty in the manner and form as charged in counts 2, 4, 5, 7, 10, 13 and 15 of the Information.”

These words, pronounced by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China yesterday morning, convicted Messrs. Raven and Brown, President and Vice-President, respectively, of the now defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, on charges of embezzlement and fraudulent false pretences and brought to a conclusion the most long-drawn-out and in all respects most notable trial in the Court’s history.

Immediately they had been uttered, the Judge ordered the defendants to be handed over to the custody of the United States Marshal. They are now lodged in the Ward Road Gaol and will be brought before the Court for sentence at 10 o’clock to-morrow morning.

Courtroom Scene

Public interest in the trial having been keyed to a high pitch ever since proceedings commenced on January 3, it was a keenly expectant courtroom audience which gathered yesterday morning to hear the verdict. Spectators began arriving as early as 9 a.m. although the Court was not due to open until 10. By 9.45, every available seat was taken and late-comers were obliged to hold tenaciously to standing-room places just outside the courtroom door.

Many prominent local business men were present and a number of fashionably-dressed women. Some of these were former business associates or friends of the defendants.

In contrast to proceedings on previous days, when the courtroom buzzed with conversation before sessions commenced, there was an almost audible hush which reflected the gravity of the occasion.

As the hands of the clock moved relentlessly towards the hour of 10, Mr. Warner Brown entered alone and took his seat silently behind the table reserved for the defence attorneys. His face eloquently betrayed the nervous tension to which the trial had subjected him, but he managed to convey a flickering smile to friends and acquaintances present.

No Greeting Exchanged

Mr. Raven strode in shortly afterwards and took a seat beside Mr. Brown, but no greeting of any kind was exchanged between the two men whose fate was hanging
(Continued on Page 5, Col. 3.)

in the balance. The former czar of the Raven enterprises looked neither to right nor left, but gazed straight ahead at the vacant Judge’s bench. He was evidently straining to maintain the composure which he managed to display throughout the trial, but nervously clasped and unclasped his hands.

With but two minutes to go before 10 o’clock, Dr. George Sellett, Special Assistant District Attorney, who conducted the case for the Government, entered and took his seat. He was closely followed by his assistant, Dr. Harold Nelson, by Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, and Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for Mr. Brown.

At the Press table, in addition to local newspaper reporters, there were present representatives of two of the big press associations, on hand to hear the verdict and flash it to all corners of the earth where the outcome of the trial is of interest.

Promptly at 10 o’clock the door connecting the courtroom with the Judge’s Chambers was opened by the usher. Judge Helmick entered with judicial solemnity and took his seat on the Bench as the Assistant U. S. Marshal proclaimed the familiar words: “Hear ye, hear ye, hear ye, the Honourable United States Court for China is now in session!”

Intense Silence For Verdict

An intense silence preceded the Judge’s first words. Eyes moved restlessly from Judge to defendants and back again. Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown visibly tensed themselves in their seats. Everyone leaned forward to catch what was said.

“The Court has decided that it will make no filing of special findings of fact or conclusion of law.” These were the Judge’s first words, answering an application made by defence counsel the day previously.

Then came the verdict, to which Judge Helmick added that the defendants would be handed over immediately to the custody of the United States Marshal and brought up for sentence on Monday morning.

Judgment Arrest Sought

Mr. Evans was instantly on his feet to ask for an arrest of judgment in the case of Mr. Raven, on the ground that the Court had failed to make special findings of fact or conclusions of law. To this, Judge Helmick countered with the statement that any such application would have to be submitted to the Court in writing. Mr. Evans concurred, declaring that he had made the verbal application first because such applications were required to be made immediately after judgment.

Again the Assistant Marshal’s voice rang out. Judge Helmick left the Bench and retired to his Chambers and the courtroom instantly became intensely alive with excitement. The whole of the proceedings had occupied less than five minutes.

As the crowded audience began streaming from the courtroom, Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown were shepherded through the throng to the office of the United States Marshal, where an order for their committal to Ward Road Gaol was made out.

Women In Tears

Several women broke down in tears as the defendants passed along the corridors, faces blanched but grimly set. Several advanced and gave Mr. Raven a warm hand-clasp. Mr. Brown, however, appeared to enjoy fewer friendships and walked forlornly to the Marshal’s office.

Their bail of U.S. $10,000 each having been automatically suspended by the verdict, the question of release on bond will not be raised again until sentence is passed and an appeal, if any, noted, it was learned in the office of the U.S. Marshal. Accordingly, a warrant of committal to Ward Road Gaol was made out and the convicted were taken thither via Central Police Station on Foochow Road, where further records had to be completed.

Mr. Raven was heard to request that he be allowed to see his brother, Mr. Charles Raven, before lodgment in gaol, but it is not known whether he was given this opportunity.

Raven To Appeal

Approached on the question of appeal, Mr. Richard T. Evans, Mr. Raven’s attorney, said definitely that his client would appeal against the decision of the Court, but no definite statement could be obtained from Mr. C. S. Franklin as to whether his client, Mr. Warner Brown, would appeal.

The defendants were convicted on seven of the 15 counts listed in the Information filed against them by the District Attorney. The

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1936年2月2日

美国法院裁定雷文
与布朗均犯有
挪用公款及欺诈罪

法庭气氛紧张且座无虚席，聆听赫尔米克法官宣判：被告被押往监狱时，女性旁听者不禁落泪

前美亚金融公司总裁将于明晨受审判刑

“政府以细致、刻苦且彻底完备的方式，提出了支持起诉书的证据和法律依据。根据所有证据，本庭确信这些被告的罪行已超出合理怀疑的范围。本庭裁定被告弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）和约翰·沃纳·布朗（John Warner Brown）在起诉书第2、4、5、7、10、13和15项指控中所述的方式和形式下罪名成立。”

这些话是米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官昨天上午在美国驻华法院宣读的，据此判定现已解散的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）总裁雷文先生和副总裁布朗先生犯有挪用公款和欺诈性虚假陈述罪，从而结束了该法院历史上历时最长且在各方面最为引人注目的审判。

话音刚落，法官即命令将被告移交美国法警羁押。他们目前被关押在华德路监狱，并将于明天上午10点被提堂听候判刑。

法庭情景

自1月3日开庭以来，公众对此次审判的关注度一直居高不下，昨天上午聚集在法庭聆听判决的观众充满了急切的期待。尽管法院预定10点才开庭，但 spectators 早在上午9点就开始抵达。到了9点45分，所有可用座位均已坐满，迟到者不得不紧紧占据法庭门外仅存的站立位置。

许多当地知名商界人士出席，还有不少衣着时尚的女性。其中一些人是被告的前商业伙伴或朋友。

与此前几天开庭前法庭内人声鼎沸的景象形成鲜明对比的是，现场几乎是一片可闻的寂静，反映出这一时刻的严肃性。

当时针无情地指向10点时，沃纳·布朗先生独自进入法庭，默默地在为辩护律师预留的桌子后面坐下。他的面部表情生动地流露出审判给他带来的神经紧张，但他仍努力向在场的朋友和熟人挤出一丝微笑。

未作任何问候

雷文先生随后大步走进来，坐在布朗先生旁边，但这两名命运悬而未决的人之间没有进行任何形式的问候。
（续第5页，第3栏。）

这位曾经主宰雷文企业帝国的“沙皇”既不左顾也不右盼，而是直视前方空荡荡的法官席。他显然在竭力保持他在整个审判过程中设法展现出的镇定，但双手却紧张地反复握紧又松开。

距离10点仅剩两分钟时，代表政府主控此案的特别助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士进入法庭并就座。紧随其后的是他的助手哈罗德·纳尔逊（Harold Nelson）博士、雷文先生的律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生，以及布朗先生的律师C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生。

在记者席上，除了本地报纸记者外，还有两家大型通讯社的代表在场，准备聆听判决并将其迅速传送到全球各地关注审判结果的地方。

10点整，法警打开了连接法庭与法官办公室的门。赫尔米克法官带着司法庄严的神情步入法庭，并在法官席就座，此时美国副法警宣读出那句熟悉的话语：“肃静，肃静，肃静，尊敬的美国驻华法院现在开庭！”

宣判前的极度寂静

法官开口前是一片极度的寂静。目光不安地在法官和被告之间来回移动。雷文先生和布朗先生在座位上明显变得紧张起来。每个人都向前探身，以便听清所说的话。

“本庭决定不提交特别事实认定或法律结论。”这是法官的第一句话，回应了辩护律师前一天提出的申请。

随后便是判决，赫尔米克法官补充说，被告将立即被移交给美国法警羁押，并于周一上午提堂听候判刑。

寻求中止判决

埃文斯先生立即起身，以法院未能作出特别事实认定或法律结论为由，要求中止对雷文先生案件的判决。对此，赫尔米克法官反驳称，任何此类申请必须以书面形式提交法院。埃文斯先生表示同意，声明他之所以先提出口头申请，是因为此类申请需要在判决后立即提出。

副法警的声音再次响起。赫尔米克法官离开法官席，退回到他的办公室，法庭内瞬间因激动而变得喧闹起来。整个诉讼过程耗时不到五分钟。

当拥挤的观众开始涌出法庭时，雷文先生和布朗先生被引导穿过人群，来到美国法警办公室，在那里签署了将他们收押至华德路监狱的命令。

女性落泪

当被告沿着走廊走过时，几名女性忍不住落泪，她们面色苍白但神情严峻。几人走上前去，热情地与雷文先生握手。然而，布朗先生似乎朋友较少，孤零零地走向法警办公室。

据从美国法警办公室获悉，由于判决已自动暂停了他们每人1万美元的保释金，在判刑以及是否提出上诉（如有）之前，不会再讨论保释释放问题。因此，签发了将其收押至华德路监狱的令状，罪犯经由福州路中央巡捕房被带往那里，因为需要在那里完成进一步的记录手续。

有人听到雷文先生请求在入狱前允许见他的兄弟查尔斯·雷文（Charles Raven）先生，但尚不清楚他是否获得了这个机会。

雷文将上诉

当被问及上诉问题时，雷文先生的律师理查德·T·埃文斯先生明确表示，他的客户将对法院的判决提出上诉，但从C·S·富兰克林先生那里无法获得关于其客户沃纳·布朗先生是否会上诉的明确声明。

被告在地区检察官对他们提起的起诉书中列出的15项指控中的7项上被判有罪。这
