first of these convicting counts
(count No. 2) charged the defend-
ants with the embezzlement of
U.S. $11,553 from Mr. Lucien
Claude Marie Basset, a local ex-
change broker. This sum re-
presented the proceeds of a draft
which Mr. Basset gave to the A.-
O.F.C. for the purchase of 100
shares of American Telephone and
Telegraph Company stock on
December 18, 1933.

The second count (No. 4)
charged that they "feloniously
and with intent to defraud" Mr.
Basset, falsely represented to him
that they had, on December 16,
1933, purchased this stock for him,
whereas in fact they had not done
so.

Basset Defrauded
In the third count (count No. 5)
the defendants were charged with
defrauding Mr. Basset by re-
presenting to him that they had
purchased and sold certain stocks
for him, thereby inducing him, in
consequence, to remit U.S. $10,000
to E. A. Pierce and Company, San
Francisco agents of the A.-O.F.C.,
which sum was to be used to estab-
lish for Mr. Basset additional
credit with the A.-O.F.C. for stock
purchase transactions.

The fourth count (count No. 7)
charged the defendants with em-
bezzling U.S. $507.60 paid to the
A.-O.F.C. by Mr. Edward P. How-
ard for the purchase of 50 shares
of Douglas Aircraft stock.

The fifth count (count No. 10)
charged the embezzlement of Sh.
$1,225.57, paid to the A.-O.F.C. by
Mr. Gordon Yates for the purchase
of certain shares.

The sixth count (count No. 13)
charged the embezzlement from
Mr. C. R. Jones of Sh. $549.18. Mr.
Jones, it was set out, paid this
sum to the A.-O.F.C. for the pur-
chase of Electric Bond And Share
stock.

Last Convicting Count
The final convicting count (count
No. 15) charged - the em-
bezzlement of divers shares de-
livered by Stanley G. Kirkland to
the A.-O.F.C.

In the Information as filed, 18
counts were set out, but for
technical legal reasons there were
two or three counts on each trans-
actions referred to in the Informa-
tion, except in cases where false
pretenses were charged. In several
of the transactions, for example,
there were counts of embezzlement
of a negotiable instrument (the
cheque or draft handed by custom-
ers to the A.-O.F.C. for stock pur-
chases), theft of this negotiable in-
strument, and embezzlement of its
proceeds. Legally, however, con-
viction was possible on only one
count for each transaction.

There was thus conviction on one
count for each transaction set out
in the Information. The seven
counts on which conviction was ob-
tained were those especially stress-
ed by Dr. George Sellett in his
argument before the Court at the
conclusion of the trial.

Government's Case
As regards all the embezzlement
charges concerning cheques and
drafts, the Government contended
that clients of the A.-O.F.C. hand-
ed their money to that concern to
buy outright certain specified
shares and that these shares were
not bought (save in part, on mar-
gin), while the proceeds of the
clients' cheques were placed in the
general bank accounts of the cor-
poration.

In the Kirkland transaction, the
client was alleged to have entrust-
ed certain shares of stock to the
A.-O.F.C. for safekeeping, but em-
bezzlement was committed by pledg-
ing these shares in the A.-O.F.C.'s
margin account with Pierce and
Company, thereby pledging them
for the corporation's own indebted-
ness.

The two counts of false pretences
(fraud) alleged that the A.-O.F.C.
obtained money from Mr. Basset
by misrepresenting to him that
shares which he had previously
ordered had been purchased and
paid for in full and placed in safe-
keeping for him, whereas in fact
they had not been paid for in full
and were in the margin account
with Pierce and Company.

The indictment of Mr. Raven
and Mr. Brown arose from the col-
lapse of the Raven enterprises on
May 23 last year and followed an
investigation of the affairs of these
enterprises by Mr. Frank L.
Hough, the Liquidator.

巴塞特受骗
在第三项指控（第5项）中，
被告被指控通过向巴塞特先生

在为巴塞特先生在美亚金融公
司建立额外的股票交易信用额
度。

第四项指控（第7项）指
控被告挪用了爱德华·P·霍华
德（Edward P. Howard）先生支付

第五项指控（第10项）指
控挪用了戈登·耶茨（Gordon Yates）
先生支付给美亚金融公司用于

第六项指控（第13项）指
控从C·R·琼斯（C. R. Jones）先生
处挪用549.18上海两。据陈述，
琼斯先生将这笔钱支付给美亚
金融公司，用于购买电力债券与
股票公司（Electric Bond And Share）的股
票。

最后一项定罪指控
最后的定罪指控（第
15项）指控挪用了斯坦利·G·
柯克兰（Stanley G. Kirkland）交付
给美亚金融公司的各种股份。

在提交的起诉书中，列出了18
项指控，但由于技术性的法律原
因，除涉及虚假陈述的情况外，
起诉书中提到的每笔交易都有两
到三项指控。例如，在几笔交易
中，既有挪用可转让票据（客户
交给美亚金融公司用于购买股票
的支票或汇票）的指控，也有盗
窃该可转让票据及其收益的指控。
然而，在法律上，每笔交易只能
就一项指控定罪。

因此，针对起诉书中列出的每
笔交易，均有一项指控成立。获
得定罪的七项指控正是乔治·塞
莱特博士在审判结束时向法庭陈
述中特别强调的那些。

政府方的案情
关于所有涉及支票和汇票的
挪用公款指控，政府方主张，美
亚金融公司的客户将钱交给该公
司以直接购买某些指定股份，而
这些股份并未被购买（部分保证金
交易除外），同时客户支票的收益
被存入该公司的普通银行账户。

在柯克兰的交易中，据称客户
将某些股票委托给美亚金融公司
保管，但该公司将这些股票质押
在皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）的美亚
金融公司保证金账户中，从而为
公司自身的债务进行质押，构成
了挪用公款。

两项虚假陈述（欺诈）指控指
称，美亚金融公司通过向巴塞特
先生虚假陈述称他此前订购的股
份已全额购买并付款，并为他妥
善保管，而实际上这些股份并未
全额付款，而是存在于皮尔斯公
司的保证金账户中，从而从巴塞
特先生处获取资金。

对雷文先生和布朗先生的起
诉源于去年5月23日雷文企业的
崩溃，并紧随清算人弗兰克·L·
霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生对这些
企业事务的调查之后。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 1, 1936 132 J P

Judge Helmick To Give
Verdict In Raven Case
At 10 O'Clock To-day

Trial Closed Yesterday Afternoon After Delivery
Of Speeches By Dr. Sellett And The Defence;
District Attorney's Scathing Remarks

FRANKLIN DESCRIBES HIS CLIENT AS THE
WORLD'S MOST HOPELESS WITNESS

A verdict is expected to be delivered this morning in the case of Mr. Frank Jay Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, charged in the U.S. Court for China with embezzlement, theft and fraud in connection with shares held for clients in the now defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

Argument concluded late yesterday afternoon after a day devoted to summing-up by Dr. George Sellett, Assistant U.S. District Attorney, and Messrs. Richard T. Evans and Cornell S. Franklin for the defence. While defence attorneys pleaded the lack of intent on the part of their clients to embezzle funds belonging to clients, the prosecution lashed both men as "adopting every conceivable dishonest and disreputable practice imaginable" in the operation of their business.

What was probably the outstanding highlight of the day's proceedings was provided by Mr. C. S. Franklin, representing Mr. J. Warner Brown, who, at the very opening of his speech, took the remarkable course of describing his own client as "the world's poorest, most feeble and most hopeless witness."

With crowds jamming the corridors so densely that court attendants had literally to fight their way into the courtroom, the last sessions of the dramatic case opened at 10 a.m. with excitement at its height. Mr. Raven walked in, his customary erect self, and sat down. Mr. Brown followed. There was no exchange of greeting between them and they did not speak once during the long and biting address by the Assistant District Attorney.

On behalf of both counsel for the defence, Mr. C. S. Franklin handed to the court a petition asking for special findings of fact and conclusions of law, upon which Judge Helmick said he would rule later.

Dr. Sellett was immediately on his feet, fingering a pencil as he opened his deliberate and carefully enunciated address.

"When these proceedings opened four weeks ago to-day," he said, "the Government promised that it would prove certain facts as to criminality in this case. It would be impossible for us to outline even in brief form the evidence which has been presented in court, but I desire to review it in a very general way and then to talk about the law applicable to the case at Bar.

The information, Dr. Sellett continued, contained 16 counts of embezzlement, larceny and fraud. Not all of these could be sustained, he admitted, but that of these at least seven were counts on which both defendants were guilty.

There were five charges in the Basset case; embezzlement of the cheque, embezzlement of the proceeds of the cheque, larceny of the proceeds of the cheque, and two counts of obtaining money under false pretences, for U.S. $28,000 and U.S. $10,000. On the first and latter two charges, the Government held the defendants were guilty.

Out of the charges in the Kirkland case, embezzlement of shares and larceny of shares, the Government held the defendants were guilty of the first charge.

In the Howard case of three counts, the defendants were guilty of embezzlement of the proceeds.

In the Jones and Yates cases, each of three counts, the defendants were both guilty of embezzlement of the proceeds of the cheques.

Raven's Position

Turning to a sharp outline of the position of both defendants with regard to the defunct company, Dr. Sellett continued:

"The evidence shows that Raven was president of the A.-O.F.C. at all times material to this action. Brown was a director and manager from as early as 1930. Then and at all times these men had powers of attorney to act and deal with all business of the corporation as they saw fit.

赫尔米克法官将于今日上午十时
就雷文案作出判决

塞莱特博士与辩方发表演说后，审判于昨日下午结束；
地区检察官言辞严厉

富兰克林称其委托人为“世上最无可救药的证人”

预计今天上午将对弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）先生和J. 华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生一案作出判决。二人被控在美国驻华法院犯有挪用公款、盗窃和欺诈罪，罪名涉及为已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）客户持有的股票。

经过一整天由美国助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士以及辩护律师理查德·T. 埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生和康奈尔·S. 富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）先生进行的总结陈词，辩论于昨日下午晚些时候结束。虽然辩护律师辩称其委托人并无挪用客户资金的意图，但检方猛烈抨击这两人在经营业务过程中“采取了所有可以想象到的不诚实和不光彩的手段”。

当天庭审中最引人注目的亮点，大概是由代表J. 华纳·布朗先生的C. S. 富兰克林先生提供的，他在发言伊始便采取了一种非同寻常的做法，形容自己的委托人是“世上最糟糕、最软弱且最无可救药的证人”。

由于走廊里挤满了人群，法警简直不得不杀出一条路才能进入法庭，这起戏剧性案件的最后几次庭审于上午10时开始，现场气氛紧张到了极点。雷文先生以他惯常的挺拔姿态走进来并坐下。布朗先生紧随其后。两人之间没有互相问候，在助理地区检察官漫长而尖锐的发言期间，他们也没有说过一句话。

代表两位辩护律师，C. S. 富兰克林先生向法庭提交了一份请愿书，请求作出特别事实认定和法律结论，赫尔米克法官表示他将在稍后对此作出裁决。

塞莱特博士随即起身，一边摆弄着一支铅笔，一边开始了他那从容不迫、吐字清晰的发言。

他说：“就在四周前的今天，当本案诉讼程序开始时，政府承诺将证明本案中有关犯罪行为的某些事实。我们不可能即使以简要的形式勾勒出已在法庭上出示的证据，但我希望非常概括地回顾这些证据，然后谈谈适用于本案的法律。”

塞莱特博士继续说道，起诉书包含16项关于挪用公款、盗窃和欺诈的指控。他承认，并非所有这些指控都能成立，但在这些指控中，至少有七项是两名被告均有罪的。

巴塞特（Basset）案中有五项指控：挪用支票、挪用支票所得款项、盗窃支票所得款项，以及两项以虚假借口骗取钱财的指控，金额分别为28,000美元和10,000美元。对于第一项和后两项指控，政府认为被告有罪。

在柯克兰（Kirkland）案的指控中，涉及挪用股票和盗窃股票，政府认为被告在第一项指控上有罪。

在霍华德（Howard）案的三项指控中，被告犯有挪用所得款项罪。

在琼斯（Jones）和耶茨（Yates）案中，各有三项指控，两名被告均犯有挪用支票所得款项罪。

雷文的立场

接着，塞莱特博士简要而尖锐地概述了两名被告相对于这家已倒闭公司的立场，他继续说道：

“证据表明，在与本诉讼相关的所有重要时期，雷文一直是美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）的总裁。布朗自1930年起就担任董事和经理。当时及此后所有时间里，这两人都拥有授权书，可以按照他们认为合适的方式处理公司的所有业务。

“我们可以预见，辩方会辩称雷文不知道所发生的事情，所有这些行为都是在未经他知情和同意的情况下发生的。至于布朗，证据的性质使得他利用这一辩解无济于事。虽然他的许多证词必须

be disbelieved, the commonsense view compels belief in some of his admissions, that he had full knowledge of what was going on.

"There is no evidence in the record whatsoever," Dr. Sellett declared, his voice rising as he gestured forcibly, "not in the whole of this voluminous record, that Raven did not have a complete knowledge of what was going on. He was president of the corporation (here Dr. Sellett produced the bye-laws of the corporation to read out the powers of the president), the chief executive. He was empowered to conduct the general active business, to execute all agreements; he was in general supervision and direction of the other officers and it was his duty to see that their work was being carried out properly.

"Not One Scintilla"

"There is not in the whole of the record one scintilla of evidence that Raven was not cognizant of the entire situation of the company. There are only innuendoes in the form of questions asked in cross-examination by the defence counsel of witnesses.

"In 1929 he personally went to America and arranged with E. A. Pierce and Company for the beginning of his stock brokerage business. On March 7, 1930, the first transaction took place. Mr. Brown then goes to the United States—it had already been planned that he would manage the company—and after he had been there two weeks attending the office of Pierce and Company he writes a letter, May 13, 1930, to Mr. Raven dealing with the matter of fully-paid shares as 'highly important and involving considerable legal liability.' This letter is initialled by Raven and it is inescapable that he did not know in June, 1930, that the matter of fully-paid shares was something important and that the legal liability was considerable.

"On November 18, 1932, Mr. Cocquelet makes a report to Mr. Brown. Mr. Brown asked for it, saying he wanted to show it to Raven. It sets forth that there were then 50 clients whose shares were fully paid for to an amount of U.S. $68,000. The report sets out that there would be a loss of U.S. $235,000 sustained by the A.-O.F.C. if the accounts should be sold out then.

Pledging Clients' Money

"At that time in the R. T. Co. 101-1-1 account (Raven's) there was a loss of U.S. $84,000 and a U.S. $4,000 loss on another Raven account. Let us picture that Raven indebtedness to the corporation of U.S. $88,000 and at the same time that U.S. $68,000 has been pledged to finance the company, and he, the president, has lost heavily.

"On September 12, 1933, the companies set up an 'Executive Council' which ran the business of the company, in fact all of the Raven group. The boards of directors were not running the companies; they were picked for their standing in Shanghai, as window-dressing. They were to have as little information as possible. The inference is plain.

"This was also the policy with regard to the auditors. They were not to be shown the minute books of the Executive Council and boards of directors. If there was any information that they must have it was to be given them through extracts from the minutes."

Then, turning to a brief resume of the Benjamin shares trans-

necessary, to show that there was no criminal intent. The record is replete with evidence that these defendants were both guilty of every conceivable, dishonest and disreputable practise in managing the affairs of the company.

"Idiotic, Stupid Defence"

"The defence is going to be the high cable costs, the fact that legal advice was obtained, that the company was able to pay back the shares out of the margin account and that if you take people's money who are going to speculate it is all right to embezzle their property right away.

"The first is a silly, stupid, idiotic defence, in keeping with all the other things he (Mr. Brown) did and said on the witness stand. The fact that clients were intending to speculate is no defence, or that the company was at all times able to make good the property they had converted. As to the last, I don't know, I hardly think that counsel for the defence will suggest that this evidence should be believed."

The Defence

Long before 2 p.m., when the court was due to reassemble, the courtroom was packed to capacity, while a large number of people crowded the entrance and stood throughout the entire afternoon listening to the proceedings as best they might.

Argument for the defence was about equally divided between Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, and Mr. C. S. Franklin, who represents Mr. Brown. Mr. Franklin devoted himself to a general outline of the defence positions, while Mr. Evans dealt with the legal authorities.

Opening the counter-attack against the case for the prosecution, Mr. Franklin started his speech, which lasted one hour, with a warm tribute to Dr. Sellett and an apologia for Mr. Brown, who for several days this week was subjected to the withering fire of the prosecuting attorney's cross-examination.

"Feeble Witness"

"We listened this morning," Mr. Franklin declared, "to a very able presentation of the Government's case by a brilliant prosecuting attorney. During the latter part of the trial itself, we listened to the masterly cross-examination of the world's poorest, most feeble and most hopeless witness—Mr. Warner Brown, one of the defendants in this case.

"Now despite the obvious fact that Mr. Brown was thoroughly frightened on the witness-stand, to such an extent that his brain almost ceased to function, it was apparent throughout that he was really trying to tell the truth and at the same time avoid being tripped up and entangled by an exceptionally clever and well-conducted prosecution.

"Regardless of all the contradictory statements which he made, I submit that the fundamentals of his testimony remained unshaken. I propose to go over the fundamentals briefly. An analysis of the evidence will show a surprising lack of any real contradictions. Such contradictions as there have been, flowed from questions which were inferences and deductions drawn from the basic testimony."

Mr. Franklin then launched on a brief review of Mr. Brown's career with the A.-O.F.C., going back to the early part of 1930, when the A.-O.F.C. first decided seriously to go into the brokerage business.

Describing Mr. Brown's visit to San Francisco, where according to the testimony he studied the brokerage business in the offices of E. A. Pierce and Company, counsel declared that Mr. Brown had studied it to the extent that

misgivings about these fully-paid shares as I had when I was in San Francisco." Now Mr. Haley handed his report to Mr. Brown in Hongkong, but, according to the evidence, Mr. Haley did not raise this question of fully-paid shares with Mr. Brown after they were both back in Shanghai.

"From early 1932 there were three lawyers in the A.-O.F.C. offices, Mr. Price, Mr. Driscoll and Mr. Elder. It can reasonably be supposed that Mr. Raven thought, and had reason to think, that if anything was wrong with the procedure in handling fully paid shares, one or other of these lawyers would have pointed it out and seen that it was changed.

"Mr. Brown thought, and was entitled to think, the same as Mr. Raven in this matter.

"By 1933," Mr. Franklin proceeded, "the practice of handling fully-paid shares as they were handled had acquired the dignity of long-established precedent. It was automatically extended to the handling of the Basset shares. There is every indication that Basset's account was intended as a trading account. There was nothing to indicate to the defendants that it might not become an active trading account at any time."

Counsel then proceeded to deal with the other fully-paid share transactions involving the several complaining witnesses in the case, pointing out that these witnesses had indicated that their intention of trading with their shares at some time, thus justifying the A.-O.F.C. in treating their accounts as trading accounts.

Accounts Treated As One

Coming to the Benjamin shares, which were turned over by the Raven Trust Company to the A.-O.F.C. and pledged by the latter to Pierce and Company, counsel drew the court's attention to the fact that the testimony showed that the A.-O.F.C. had always treated the Raven Trust Company accounts as one, and when Mr. Driscoll had asked the A.-O.F.C. to transfer these shares to safekeeping Mr. Brown rightly refused to do so, since the Trust Company accounts with the A.-O.F.C. were already undermargined and would, if the transfer were made, be undermargined that much more.

"Mr. Brown," counsel stressed,

portion owed U.S. $31,000 against holdings amounting to U.S. $780,-000; Tls. 80,000 against holdings amounting to Tls. 1,000,000; Sh. $207,000 against holdings amounting to Sh. $2,700,000. The holdings, consisting largely of shares in the other Raven companies, were not worthless as the prosecution contended, since they were quoted on the stock exchange and had a loan value, even if they could not be sold because of the tightness of the money market.

Concluding his address, Mr. Franklin said that had Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown had guilty knowledge that they were doing wrong in regard to the handling of fully-paid shares, it would have been a simple matter for them to have instructed Pierce and Company to draw on the letters of credit which they held in the A.-O.F.C. account and transfer the fully-paid shares to safekeeping. They could have done that and still had a surplus on the letters of credit, counsel contended.

"It is my submission," he ended, "that the evidence does not show that the defendants are guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Unless that reasonable doubt is overcome, they should be acquitted."

Mr. Evans' Address

Mr. Evans then rose to address the court and began by disclaiming a suggestion made by Dr. Sellett in the morning that the medical evidence called in regard to Mr. Raven's condition was for any other purpose than purely the merits of the case. "I want it understood," he said, "that there was no plea for mercy implied in that step.

"The conduct of the defendants," he went on to contend, "was perfectly open at all times. They did not pretend to any of the complaining witnesses that their shares were held in safekeeping. Had this not been the case, and the defendants had guilty knowledge of wrong-doing, it would have been very easy for them to have destroyed the records of that wrong-doing."

Coming to the letter which Mr. Brown had written to Mr. Raven from San Francisco regarding the handling of fully-paid shares by Pierce and Company, Mr. Evans said that the words: "We will introduce something similar when I return to Shanghai," were construed merely as meaning that Mr. Brown and his colleagues would take care of the matter. Mr. Raven did not consider it necessary to act.

Brown's Evidence Discounted

Turning to the Cocquelet report, counsel contended that the only evidence that this report came into Mr. Raven's hands was given by Mr. Brown and that this testimony, in view of all the circumstances, must be discounted. The next time that the question of fully-paid shares occurred, as far as Raven was concerned, was when the "voluble Mr. Rosse" testified to having raised the question. "But this witness showed so much animus," counsel said, "that his evidence, also, should be strongly discounted."

With regard to the Haley report, Mr. Evans pointed out that Mr. Raven had just come through a serious illness when it was submitted. True, the first page was initialled by Mr. Raven and the report contained a section regarding the handling of fully-paid shares. But this section was buried in the report and occupied only one page. The only testimony showing that Mr. Raven had really studied the report came from Mr. Raven's secretary who testified that his initials on the document indicated that it had received his attention. Mr. Brown testified that Mr. Raven had seen the report, but this testimony required strong corroboration

“卷宗中没有任何证据，”塞莱特博士宣称，他的声音随着有力的手势而提高，“在这部头庞大的卷宗中，完全没有证据表明雷文对正在发生的事情缺乏全面了解。他是该公司的总裁（此处塞莱特博士出示了公司章程以宣读总裁的职权），是首席执行官。他有权开展一般的主动业务，执行所有协议；他对其他职员进行总体监督和指导，其职责是确保他们的工作得到妥善执行。

“毫无蛛丝马迹”

“在整个卷宗中，连一丝一毫的证据都没有表明雷文不了解公司的全部情况。只有辩护律师在交叉询问证人时以提问形式提出的暗示。

“1929年，他亲自前往美国，并与E. A. Pierce and Company（皮尔斯公司）安排开始他的股票经纪业务。1930年3月7日，第一笔交易发生。随后布朗先生前往美国——此前已计划由他管理公司——他在皮尔斯公司办公室待了两周后，于1930年5月13日给雷文先生写了一封信，谈及全额缴付股份事宜，称其‘极为重要且涉及相当大的法律责任’。这封信上有雷文的简签，因此无可逃避的是，他在1930年6月不可能不知道全额缴付股份事宜是一件重要的事情，且法律责任相当重大。

“1932年11月18日，科克莱特先生向布朗先生提交了一份报告。布朗先生要求这份报告，称他想把它给雷文看。报告指出，当时有50名客户的全额缴付股份金额达68,000美元。报告还指出，如果当时将账户平仓出售，A.-O.F.C.公司将遭受235,000美元的损失。

抵押客户资金

“当时在R. T. Co. 101-1-1账户（雷文的）中有84,000美元的亏损，而在另一个雷文账户中有4,000美元的亏损。让我们设想一下，雷文欠公司88,000美元，同时又有68,000美元被抵押用于为公司融资，而他作为总裁却遭受了巨额亏损。

“1933年9月12日，各公司成立了一个‘执行委员会’来经营公司业务，实际上是整个雷文集团的业务。董事会并不经营这些公司；挑选他们是因为他们在上海的地位，作为装点门面之用。他们获得的信息应尽可能少。推论显而易见。

“这也是对待审计员的政策。不向他们展示执行委员会和董事会的会议记录簿。如果有任何他们必须知道的信息，则通过会议记录的摘录提供给他们。”

必要的，以表明没有犯罪意图。卷宗中充满了证据，表明这两名被告在管理公司事务时犯下了各种可以想象的、不诚实和不光彩的行为。

“愚蠢、笨拙的辩护”

“辩方将提出的理由是高昂的电报费用、获得了法律建议、公司能够从保证金账户中偿还股份，以及如果你拿走打算投机的人的钱，立即挪用他们的财产是可以接受的。

下午2点法庭预定重新开庭之前很久，法庭内就已座无虚席，而大量人群挤在入口处，并在整个下午站立着，尽其所能地聆听诉讼程序。

辩方的辩论大致平均分配给代表雷文先生的理查德·T·埃文斯律师和代表布朗先生的C. S·富兰克林先生。富兰克林先生致力于概述辩方立场，而埃文斯先生则处理法律依据问题。

在对检方案件展开反击时，富兰克林先生开始了他的演讲，持续了一个小时，他首先向塞莱特博士致以热情的敬意，并为布朗先生作了辩解，布朗先生在本周几天里遭受了公诉人交叉询问的猛烈抨击。

“软弱的证人”

“今天上午，”富兰克林先生宣称，“我们听取了一位才华横溢的公诉人对政府案件的非常有力的陈述。在审判本身的后半段，我们听取了针对世界上最糟糕、最软弱和最无望的证人——本案被告之一华纳·布朗先生——的高超交叉询问。

“现在，尽管布朗先生在证人席上显然受到极度惊吓，以至于他的大脑几乎停止运转，但 throughout 整个过程很明显，他确实试图讲述真相，同时避免被异常精明且操作得当的检方绊倒和纠缠。

“不管他做出了多少相互矛盾的陈述，我认为他证词的基本要素仍然未被动摇。我打算简要回顾这些基本要素。对证据的分析将显示出真正矛盾之处的惊人缺乏。存在的任何矛盾都源于从基本证词中得出的推断和演绎的问题。”

随后，富兰克林先生简要回顾了布朗先生在A.-O.F.C.公司的职业生涯，追溯到1930年初，当时A.-O.F.C.首次认真决定进入经纪业务。

描述布朗先生访问旧金山的情况，根据证词，他在E. A. Pierce and Company（皮尔斯公司）的办公室研究了经纪业务，辩护律师宣称布朗先生对此进行了研究，程度达到了

反对法律的规定

<!-- Image (603, 54, 775, 266) -->

联邦地区法官梅里尔·E·奥蒂斯在堪萨斯城作出裁决，宣布《瓦格纳劳资纠纷法》（Wagner Labour Disputes Act）整体违宪，这是一项新政法律，赋予员工在不受到雇主干扰的情况下组织和谈判的权利。[美联社。]

我在旧金山时对这些全额缴付股份所持有的疑虑一样。”现在黑利先生在香港将他的报告交给了布朗先生，但是，根据证据，黑利先生在他们两人回到上海后并没有向布朗先生提出这个关于全额缴付股份的问题。

“从1932年初起，A.-O.F.C.办公室里有三位律师，普赖斯先生、德里斯科尔先生和埃尔德先生。可以合理地推测，雷文先生认为，并且有理由认为，如果处理全额缴付股份的程序有任何错误，这些律师中的一位或多位会指出并确保其得到更改。

“布朗先生在此事上的想法与雷文先生相同，并且有权这样想。

“到了1933年，”富兰克林先生继续说道，“按照当时方式处理全额缴付股份的做法已经获得了长期既定先例的尊严。这种做法自动延伸到了巴塞特股份的处理上。有种种迹象表明，巴塞特的账户意在作为交易账户。没有任何迹象向被告表明它可能不会在任何时候成为活跃的交易账户。”

辩护律师接着处理案件中涉及几位投诉证人的其他全额缴付股份交易，指出这些证人曾表示他们打算在某个时间用他们的股份进行交易，从而证明A.-O.F.C.将他们的账户视为交易账户是正当的。

账户被视为一体

谈到本杰明股份，这些股份由雷文信托公司移交给A.-O.F.C.，后者将其抵押给皮尔斯公司，辩护律师提请法庭注意，证词显示A.-O.F.C.一直将雷文信托公司的账户视为一个整体，当德里斯科尔先生要求A.-O.F.C.将这些股份转移至保管库时，布朗先生正确地拒绝了这样做，因为信托公司在A.-O.F.C.的账户已经保证金不足，如果进行转移，保证金不足的情况将更加严重。

“布朗先生，”辩护律师强调，

欠款31,000美元，对应持有价值780,000美元的资产；欠款80,000两，对应持有价值1,000,000两的资产；欠款207,000元，对应持有价值2,700,000元的资产。这些持有资产主要由其他雷文公司的股份组成，并不像检方声称的那样毫无价值，因为它们在证券交易所挂牌，具有贷款价值，即使由于银根紧缩而无法出售。

在结束发言时，富兰克林先生说，如果雷文先生和布朗先生明知在处理全额缴付股份方面做错事，那么指示皮尔斯公司提取他们在A.-O.F.C.账户中持有的信用证款项，并将全额缴付股份转移至保管库，将是简单的事情。辩护律师辩称，他们本可以这样做，并且在信用证上仍有盈余。

“我的主张是，”他总结道，“证据并未显示被告的罪行超出了合理怀疑的范围。除非消除这种合理怀疑，否则他们应被宣告无罪。”

埃文斯先生的发言

随后埃文斯先生起身向法庭发言，他首先否认了塞莱特博士上午提出的暗示，即关于雷文先生状况的医学证据除了纯粹为了案件本身的优劣之外还有其他目的。“我要让大家明白，”他说，“这一步骤并不意味着请求宽恕。

“被告的行为，”他继续辩称，“始终是完全公开的。他们没有向任何投诉证人假装他们的股份被妥善保管。如果不是这种情况，且被告对不当行为有罪知，那么销毁这些不当行为的记录对他们来说将非常容易。”

谈到布朗先生从旧金山写给雷文先生关于皮尔斯公司处理全额缴付股份的信，埃文斯先生说，“当我回到上海时，我们将引入类似的做法”这句话仅仅被解释为意味着布朗先生和他的同事会处理此事。雷文先生认为没有必要采取行动。

布朗的证词被打折扣

谈到科克莱特报告，辩护律师辩称，证明该报告到达雷文先生手中的唯一证据是由布朗先生提供的，鉴于所有情况，该证词必须被打折扣。就雷文而言，下一次出现全额缴付股份问题时，是“健谈的罗斯先生”作证说提出了这个问题。“但是这位证人表现出如此多的恶意，”辩护律师说，“他的证词也应被大幅打折扣。”

关于黑利报告，埃文斯先生指出，提交该报告时，雷文先生刚刚经历了一场重病。诚然，第一页有雷文先生的简签，且报告包含关于处理全额缴付股份的部分。但这一部分深埋在报告中，仅占一页。显示雷文先生确实研读了该报告的唯一证词来自雷文先生的秘书，他作证说他在文件上的简签表明该文件已引起他的注意。布朗先生作证说雷文先生看过该报告，但这一证词需要强有力的佐证

内阁获得更多支持
即将到来的选举对政府的影响
一名工人的
东京最“干净”的选举

东京，1月30日电。——随着日本大选竞选活动进入高潮，投票日定于2月20日，普通市民仍在疑惑这一切究竟是为了什么。

民众对选举缺乏兴趣，原因很简单，因为没有任何一个政党或政党联盟被认为能够赢得多数席位。如果我们看到一种政策，其事实情况完全不同，那么关于公平和诚实的说法或许还有些道理，但本案的情况并非如此。

塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）在总结陈词中指出，他从未见过证据如此确凿的案件。在他的反驳发言中，历时40分钟并结束了他的辩论，塞莱特博士宣称：

“被告并非因一般性的道德败坏而受审，而是针对具体的行为。必须予以证明。不能通过参照其他行为来证明参与情况。除非雷文（Raven）知道从客户那里收到的钱款被用于他们确实参与的行为，否则不能认定他有罪。”

处理雷文先生作为A.-O.F.C.总裁的法律地位问题，辩方律师引用了相关案例。他指出，除非能证明公司负责人对雇员的行为给予了授权或同意，否则公司在民事或刑事上均不对雇员的行为负责。这种授权或同意不能推定。必须予以证明。

关于巴斯塞特（Basset）的交易，辩方声称，A.-O.F.C.发送给巴斯塞特的报表并未显示被告与巴斯塞特之间存在主仆关系。因为在所谓的“卖空”交易中，并没有证明存在虚假借口。富兰克林先生（Mr. Franklin）指出，纽约证券交易所关于报告的规定并不适用于这些交易，因为它们并非以该术语的本意进行报告，尽管富兰克林先生宣称这些交易“在各方面都是卖空”，但实际上根本不是真正的卖空。

试图回应塞莱特博士关于这些销售完全未经雷文先生知情而进行的论点，富兰克林先生说，证据已确凿地表明，这些销售是通过密码账户106-L 7（A.-O.F.C.的账户）、101-I. 1（雷文先生的账户）等在1935年5月至4月期间进行的，涉及出售大量属于A.-O.F.C.客户的证券，其中包括许多已缴足股款的股票，其效果是……

接下来谈到所谓的保管问题。富兰克林先生宣称：“当客户在经纪公司开立账户时，必须推定，当他购买或存入股票时，除非他明确说明这些股票是用于交易目的，否则应将其置于保管状态。”

随后，富兰克林先生发表了在其整个发言中被普遍认为是最重要的一段陈述。

布朗先生（Mr. Brown）回到上海，并咨询了詹姆斯·普赖斯先生（Mr. James Price）。我们可以想象普赖斯对布朗说：“当然，处理客户已缴足股款证券的问题非常重要。”皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）是纽约证券交易所的成员，必须遵守其规则，而其业务的延续对此至关重要。他们有一条从旧金山到纽约的私人专线，以促进业务扩展。他们不受纽约证券交易所关于股份转入转出规则的约束，只要我们能按要求交付已缴足股款的证券。但是，正如普赖斯先生向布朗先生解释的那样，“只要我们能随时交付已缴足股款的证券，我们系统中的这种不规范做法是可以接受的。”

这一点从布朗先生1930年从旧金山写给雷文先生的一封信中得到证实，信中指出皮尔斯公司有一种处理客户已缴足股款证券的系统，并且“当我们回到上海时，我们将引入一些类似的做法”。辩方律师引用了这封信，以及德里斯科尔先生（Mr. Driscoll）给布朗先生的信，信中称股票应放入保管库，如果当时转移“不方便”，则采取另一种方式。

然而，当海利报告（Haley report）提交时，此事再次被提起，显示在15万美元已缴足股款证券中，仅有5万美元处于保管状态。罗斯（Rosse）在1933年10月就此事寻求建议， presumably（大概）对另一位律师给出的解释感到满意。

接着，他指出，一名具备良好资格的人士给出的解释让布朗先生和雷文先生都对A.-O.F.C.的处理系统感到满意。

塞莱特博士宣称：“显然，当A.-O.F.C.拿到这些股票时，他们将其dumped（抛售/投入）到自己的保证金账户中，以协助他们自己的交易。他（本杰明）不欠他们一分钱；他甚至没有从他们那里购买这些股票。他们的行为就像有人拿着一包珠宝和钱说‘帮我保管’，然后他们却拿出来进行抵押和质押一样公然且犯罪。”

“有人暗示在这个行业中存在不同的道德准则。也许有人会辩称，因为这些人打算投机，所以拿走他们的财产并进行质押是合适的。世界上没有任何理由，常识中也没有任何理由说明这个行业不应受与其他诚实行业相同的规则约束。经纪人在此案中的责任与其他代理人相同。”

“也许辩方会认为这还不够。好吧，我们还有更多。我们有海利报告。他是从美国被请来的，因为他懂得如何经营业务，他在1931年1月向雷文先生提交了一份报告。”

“他的报告说：‘情况危险。我们有属于客户的15万美元已缴足股款股票，而我们保管的只有5万美元。这些股票不是我们的，而是我们为客户信托持有的。我们应该尽快将这些股票取出，因为如果发生任何意外，我们将不得不在公开市场上重新建立客户的头寸。此外，我们也完全暴露在法律诉讼的风险之下。’海利先生在这里使用的语言几乎与布朗先生本人在1930年使用的相同。”

“我想辩方仍然会说，其他人最终影响了雷文，甚至到了崩溃的边缘……”

“辩方将要求你们发挥想象力，去相信雷文不知道发生了什么。但我怀疑，如果有丝毫证据支持雷文不知情的说法，辩方律师就不会省略它。请记住，没有任何一点证据会让任何人重视这种说法。”

“我预料会有另一种为雷文辩护的理由，即他病得很重，以至于在很长一段时间内无法胜任工作，他不知道自己在做什么。我怀疑医疗证据的目的是什么……”

雷文是主要的投机者；他以各种可能的方式开始；他是一个投机者；他放弃了两个R. T. Co.的账户，转而通过稳定、持续的密码账户损失了11.6万美元。这种交易在各方面都是不诚实和不光彩的。如果公众知道这些账户是如何运作以及为谁运作的，他们还会与这家金融公司做生意吗？上海人会赌博吗？为什么要设立他的密码代码？是为了不让员工知道这种情况的存在吗？当然，有两三个人知道，但大多数人不知道。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JANUARY 31, 1936

Last Act But One In Raven,
Brown Trial Due To-day

Legal Argument Starts At 10 a.m., With Equal Time
Allotted To Prosecution And Defence; Remand
For Judgment Expected At Conclusion

The penultimate act in the vigorous legal drama which has been played across the stage of the United States Court for China during the past four weeks will open at 10 o'clock this morning when Judge Milton J. Helmick takes the bench to hear arguments of counsel for the prosecution and the defence in closure of the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, who are indicted on 16 charges of theft, embezzlement and fraud in connection with the collapse last May of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, of which the defendants were President and Vice-President, respectively.
Trial of the case, which has been the most long-drawn-out, and in some respects the most dramatic in the history of the American Court in Shanghai, commenced on January 3. Through numerous sessions, the Court has collected 337 exhibits in the case and a record running into several thousand pages. The cost of the trial to the United States Government is believed to run into several tens of thousands of U.S. dollars.

Allotment Of Time
Five hours have been allotted to counsel for argument, it was learned yesterday. The prosecution, which is being conducted by Dr. George Sellett as Special Assistant U.S. District Attorney, will have the first two-and-a-half hours in which to present its case, and the remaining two-and-a-half will be given to Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, and Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for Mr. Brown.
The charges against the two defendants relate to the alleged practice of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation in taking the fully-paid shares of their clients and hypothecating them to E. A. Pierce and Company, who were the San Francisco brokers of the A.-O.F.C., as margin for the A.-O.F.C.'s own market transactions.
Voluminous evidence was led by the prosecution on this point and two witnesses were specially brought here from the United States to testify to the practices of the A.-O.F.C. The first of these was Mr. C. C. Curtis, an employee of E. A. Pierce and Company, and the second Mr. C. J. Haley, a former officer of the A.-O.F.C.

Remand Expected
It is not expected that Judge Helmick will deliver judgment immediately on the conclusion of the legal argument to-day, but that the defendants will be remanded for judgment to some later date.
Mr. Raven is on a bail bond of U.S. $10,000, while Mr. Brown has bail in a similar sum. It is expected, in the event of a conviction, that both defendants will appeal to the United States Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco.

《字林西报》，1936年1月31日，星期五

雷文、布朗案倒数第二幕，
今日开庭审理

法律辩论于上午10时开始，控辩双方时间均等；预计辩论结束后将休庭以待判决

过去四周在美国驻沪法院上演的激烈法律戏剧的倒数第二幕，将于今天上午10时拉开帷幕，届时米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官将出庭，听取控方和辩方律师在弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生审判结案时的陈词。这两名被告分别担任去年5月倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的总裁和副总裁，被指控犯有16项盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈罪。
该案的审理始于1月3日，是上海美国法院历史上历时最长、且在某些方面最具戏剧性的案件。经过多次庭审，法院已收集了337件证物，庭审记录长达数千页。据信，此次审判给美国政府带来的费用高达数万美元。

时间分配

据悉，昨天已为律师辩论分配了五个小时的时间。由特别助理美国地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士负责的控方，将拥有前两个半小时来陈述其案情，剩下的两个半小时将留给雷文先生的辩护律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生和布朗先生的辩护律师C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生。
对两名被告的指控涉及美亚金融公司涉嫌将其客户的全额付款股票抵押给E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company），作为该公司自身市场交易的保证金，而E. A. 皮尔斯公司是美亚金融公司在旧金山的经纪商。
控方就这一点提供了大量证据，并专门从美国带来两名证人作证，以证实美亚金融公司的操作惯例。第一位是E. A. 皮尔斯公司的雇员C·C·柯蒂斯（C. C. Curtis）先生，第二位是美亚金融公司的前高管C·J·哈利（C. J. Haley）先生。

预计休庭待判

预计赫尔米克法官不会在今天法律辩论结束后立即宣判，而是会将被告还押，择日宣判。
雷文先生以1万美元美金保释，布朗先生的保释金数额相同。预计如果被判有罪，两名被告都将向位于旧金山的美国巡回上诉法院提出上诉。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JANUARY 30, 1936

Sensational Happenings
In Court As Raven Case
Evidence Is Concluded

UNPRECEDENTED SITUATION OCCURS AS
PROSECUTION AND DEFENCE ATTACK
CREDIBILITY OF MR. BROWN

NEWSPAPER REPORTER IS CAUSE OF THE
TRIAL'S DRAMATIC DEVELOPMENT

Brown Testifies To Heated Meeting With Raven In
Chocolate Shop Yesterday; Tells Raven That
He "Will Not Take Whole Brunt"

Dramatic and sensational developments flowed one after the other in rapid succession in the United States Court for China yesterday afternoon at the final session of the Raven-Brown trial, which concluded at 5.15 p.m. with the announcement that argument by counsel would commence on Friday morning at 10 o'clock, thus allowing a day's rest to both the prosecution and the defence after the arduous labours through which they have passed.

The defendants, Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, president and vice-president, respectively, of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, are charged on 16 counts with theft, embezzlement and fraud in connection with the handling of customers' fully-paid securities. The prosecution is in the hands of Dr. George Sellett, Assistant U.S. District Attorney. Mr. Raven is being defended by Attorney Richard T. Evans of Tientsin, while Mr. Brown is represented by Mr. C. S. Franklin of the local law firm of Franklin and Harrington.

During the course of the session, an amazing and almost unprecedented situation arose in which the credibility of Mr. J. Warner Brown, called by the defence as a witness, was being attacked almost simultaneously by both counsel for the prosecution and the defence as the result of remarks made to a local newspaper reporter by Mr. Brown during the lunch hour recess and a luncheon conversation between Mr. Brown and Mr. Raven which took place a few minutes later in the Chocolate Shop on Nanking Road.

Both exhibits, Mr. Franklin stated, were furnished to the defence by the Government on request. They were received without any opposition being offered.

Event Of Importance

With this formal proceeding over, the first indication of possible sensational developments was afforded to the courtroom, crowded as never before since the trial opened on January 3, when Mr. Evans rose and informed the Court that an event had occurred of such importance that it was necessary to seek the advice of the Court as to how to proceed. Addressing himself to the Judge, Mr. Evans said: "Both counsel for the defence and the prosecution would like to consult Your Honour in Chambers and we would ask that you adjourn the Court so that this may be done."

Judge Helmick concurred and the Court rose. The consultation in Chambers lasted about 15 minutes, from 2.30 to 2.45 p.m. Ladies in the courtroom took up their knitting, while most members of the large audience joined

Everyone Tired Out

At the conclusion of the session, Mr. Brown had been on the witness-stand for some 20 hours all told. Judge Helmick, the court officials and counsel for the contending sides appeared worn and jaded, and the Court readily acceded to Mr. Evans' request that, the defence having rested its case, the Court adjourn to Friday morning, since the argument was likely to be a protracted one and it was desirable that both counsel and the Court tackle the next phase of the trial in a fresher condition.

When the trial was resumed at 2 p.m. after a brief but lively morning session, the Court received in evidence defendants' exhibits 336 and 337 which were tendered by Mr. C. S. Franklin. The first of these exhibits was a statement of the A.-O.F.C.'s financial position with banks and foreign agents at various times material to the case, while the second was a statement of securities held by the A.-O.F.C. in Shanghai in their investment and trading securities portfolios on dates pertinent to the issues involved.

《字林西报》，1936年1月30日，星期四

雷文案证据终结，
法庭内发生轰动性事件

出现前所未有之局面：
控辩双方同时攻击
布朗先生的可信度

报纸记者引发
审判的戏剧性发展

布朗作证称昨日在巧克力店与雷文发生激烈会面；告诉雷文他“不会独自承担全部冲击”

昨天下午，在雷文-布朗案的最后一次庭审中，戏剧性和轰动性的发展接连迅速出现。庭审于下午5点15分结束，宣布律师辩论将于周五上午10时开始，从而使控辩双方在经历了艰苦的工作后得以休息一天。

被告弗兰克·J·雷文先生和J·沃纳·布朗先生分别是已倒闭的美亚金融公司的总裁和副总裁，他们因处理客户全额付款证券而被控16项盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈罪。检方由助理美国地区检察官乔治·塞莱特博士负责。雷文先生由天津律师理查德·T·埃文斯辩护，布朗先生则由本地富兰克林和哈林顿律师事务所（Franklin and Harrington）的C·S·富兰克林先生代理。

在庭审过程中，出现了一种令人惊讶且几乎前所未有的情况：由于布朗先生在午餐休息时间对当地一名报社记者发表的言论，以及几分钟后布朗先生与雷文先生在南京路巧克力店（Chocolate Shop）进行的午餐谈话，作为辩方证人出庭的J·沃纳·布朗先生的可信度同时受到控方和辩方律师的攻击。

富兰克林先生表示，这两份证物均是应辩方要求由政府提供的。接收这些证物时未遇到任何反对。

重要事件

随着这一正式程序的结束，自1月3日开庭以来从未如此拥挤的法庭迎来了可能发生轰动性发展的第一个迹象。当时埃文斯先生起身告知法庭，发生了一件极其重要的事件，有必要寻求法庭关于如何继续进行的建议。埃文斯先生对法官说：“辩方和控方律师都希望在内室（Chambers）向阁下请教，我们请求休庭以便进行此事。”

赫尔米克法官表示同意，法庭休庭。内室磋商持续了约15分钟，从下午2点30分到2点45分。法庭内的女士们拿起针织活计，而大多数旁听席上的观众也加入了……

众人疲惫不堪

庭审结束时，布朗先生已在证人席上总共坐了约20个小时。赫尔米克法官、法庭官员以及双方律师都显得疲惫不堪，法庭轻易地同意了埃文斯先生的请求，鉴于辩方已结束举证，且辩论可能会很漫长，法庭休庭至周五上午，以便双方律师和法庭以更饱满的精神状态应对审判的下一阶段。

在短暂但活跃的上午庭审后，审判于下午2点恢复，法庭接受了由C·S·富兰克林先生提交的被告方第336号和337号证物。第一份证物是美亚金融公司在与案件有关的不同时间与银行及外国代理商的财务状况说明，第二份证物是美亚金融公司在上海持有的投资和交易证券组合中，在与所涉问题相关的日期持有的证券说明。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 29, 1936

Difficulty With Raven
Auditors Brought Out
By Brown Examination

Fourth Day Of Penetrating Cross-Questioning Of
Defendant Brings Different Version Of
"Short Sales" In Raven Account

SPECULATION CAUSED BY HINT OF
MEDICAL WITNESS TO-DAY

Testimony showing that the American-Oriental Finance Corporation had experienced considerable difficulty in the spring of last year in getting its auditors to certify its balance sheet, as it had been prepared in the Corporation's offices, and that a change of auditors had consequently taken place, was among the highlights brought out by Mr. J. Warner Brown in the United States Court for China yesterday afternoon in the continued trial of Mr. Brown and Mr. Frank J. Raven on 16 counts of theft, embezzlement and fraud. Throughout the entire day, Dr. George Sellett, Assistant District Attorney, continued his gruelling cross-examination of Mr. Brown and at the close of the afternoon session the witness had occupied the stand for about 17 hours.
The cross-examination of Mr. Brown is expected to end this morning. At close of Court yesterday, it was announced that the trial would resume at 9.30 this morning in order to meet the convenience of a "medical witness" whom the defence proposes to call. This started considerable speculation as to what type of evidence this witness would tender and an even more crowded courtroom than yesterday is expected.

With the resumption of the trial yesterday afternoon at 2 o'clock, Dr. Sellett continued questioning Mr. Brown on the subject of "short sales" put through Mr. Raven's account with the A.-O.F.C. shortly before the crash of the Raven concerns in May of last year. Cross-examination regarding these "short sales" occupied much of the morning session, the prosecution endeavouring to show that the A.-O.F.C. was desperately trying to lay its hands on ready cash to pour into the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, upon which all the Raven companies were pyramided, and which was then in a precarious situation.

Didn't Tell Raven
Dr. Sellett: Before putting through those so-called short sales, did you inform Mr. Driscoll?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: And you did not inform Mr. Raven, either at the time, or subsequently?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Why did you refrain from taking the matter up with Mr. Raven?
Mr. Brown: I don't know why. At the time, I was busy handing over affairs to my successor in view of my forthcoming departure for Manila.
Dr. Sellett: Did you have Mr. Raven's authority to place buying and selling orders through that account of his R. T. Co. 101-I. 1?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Did you operate on that account during the summer of 1933, when Mr. Raven was absent in the United States?
Mr. Brown: Not alone.
Dr. Sellett: Before Mr. Raven's departure, did you have any conversation with him regarding the operation of that account?
Mr. Brown: Perhaps.
Dr. Sellett: You wouldn't operate on another man's account without his authority?
Mr. Brown: In this case, not without Mr. Raven's authority.
Prosecuting counsel then drew the witness's attention to the fact that in direct examination he had stated that the short sales referred to had been put through Mr. Raven's account by mistake, that they should have gone through the account R. T. Co. 106-17, which was the A.-O.F.C.'s account with itself. Mr. Brown had testified that the wrong cipher number had been entered on the ticket made out in respect of the sales.
Dr. Sellett: Why did you wait until now to tell us the truth—that these sales were quite deliberately put through the account of Mr. Raven? Don't you think your previous testimony was apt to mislead the Court?

Good Intentions
Mr. Brown: I didn't intend to be misleading.
Witness went on to say that on May 7, 1935, when he departed for Manila, he believed it would have been possible to have taken all fully-paid shares out of the A.-O.F.C.'s margin account with Pierce and Company and transfer them to safekeeping.
Dr. Sellett: You think this could have been done—without difficulty?
Mr. Brown: I believe it could have been done, but not without difficulty.
Dr. Sellett: Suppose only the American-Oriental Banking Corporation had closed down. Would it have been possible, under those circumstances, for the A.-O.F.C. to continue in business?
Mr. Brown: The reason for the closure of the A.-O.F.C. was the bank crash.
Dr. Sellett: But you could have delivered to customers their fully-paid shares?
Mr. Brown: I think so.
Dr. Sellett: How?
Mr. Brown: By calling in a loan to the Raven Trust Company and selling our seats on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dr. Sellett: What was the value of those seats in May, 1935?
Mr. Brown: About U. S. $125,000.

Held Only Equity
Dr. Sellett: Was not the value of those seats going down then?
Mr. Brown: No, I think the value was going up.
Dr. Sellett: But the A.-O.F.C. had borrowed against the value of those seats. What was the actual equity which the A.-O.F.C. had in those seats?
Mr. Brown: About U. S. $70,000.
Dr. Sellett: Then even if you had realized that sum you would still have required about U.S. $50,000 in order to take fully-paid shares out of the margin account with Pierce and Company?
Mr. Brown: No, I think we would have required about U. S. $10,000 more.
Dr. Sellett: Was the question of selling the seats in order to place customers' fully-paid securities in safekeeping ever discussed?
Mr. Brown: In 1933 we discussed it, but not in connection with the question of putting fully-paid shares in safekeeping.
Prosecuting counsel then reverted once more to the "short sales" made in the spring of 1935 and suggested to the witness that the money which the A.-O.F.C. was getting thereby was used to bolster up the American-Oriental Banking Corporation. Mr. Brown said that it was used by the A.-O.F.C. for its own purposes and to assist the Asia Realty Company.
Dr. Sellett: But when the A.-O.F.C. was diverting funds received from Pierce and Company as a result of the so-called short sales to the A.-O.B.C. you knew that the A.-O.B.C. was in a precarious position?
Mr. Brown: No, I really didn't.

Didn't Know Losses
Dr. Sellett: Were you not aware that one month before the closure deposits to the value of about Sh.$1,000,000 had been withdrawn from the A.-O.B.C. and that the A.-O.B.C. had lost, in addition, another million on exchange transactions?
Mr. Brown: I did not know that deposits had shrunk to that extent, nor that so much had been lost on exchange. It was explained to me that people had withdrawn their money and were remitting it home on account of the favourable exchange situation.
Dr. Sellett then switched to the subject of the A.-O.F.C.'s balance sheet. "In the spring of 1935," he queried Mr. Brown, "you had considerable difficulty in getting the auditors to certify your balance sheet—is that not so?" Mr. Brown admitted that there had been some difficulty.
Dr. Sellett: And on Sunday morning you and Mr. Raven met Mr. Sturrock (of the auditing firm of Turner, Sturrock and Brown) at the French Club with a view to inducing him to certify the balance sheet as it had been drawn up in your offices—is that so?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Your attempt was unsuccessful was it not?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: So then you resolved to sell your seats on the New York Stock Exchange to the Raven Trust Company for U.S.$130,000. This sum the Raven Trust Company paid to you by a cheque drawn on the A.-O.B.C. It included interest at 6 per cent.—is that so?
Mr. Brown: That is so.
Dr. Sellett: And then you got the balance sheet signed?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: And then the A.-O.F.C. returned the U.S. $130,000 to the Raven Trust Company, plus the interest—a week later?
Mr. Brown: Yes.

《字林西报》，1936年1月29日，星期三

雷文案出现困难
布朗受审带出审计师问题

被告接受深入盘问的第四天
就雷文账户中的“卖空”交易提出不同说法

今日因暗示将传唤医学证人而引发猜测

昨日下午，在中国美国法院继续审理布朗先生和弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生被控盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈等16项罪名的过程中，J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生提出的证词成为焦点之一。证词显示，美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）在去年春季曾面临巨大困难，无法让其审计师认证由该公司办公室编制的资产负债表，因此不得不更换审计师。在整个一天中，助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士继续对布朗先生进行严酷的交叉盘问，至下午庭审结束时，该证人已在证人席上度过了约17个小时。

预计对布朗先生的交叉盘问将于今天上午结束。昨日休庭时宣布，为了配合辩方拟传唤的一位“医学证人”的时间，庭审将于今天上午9时30分恢复。这一消息引发了人们对该证人将提供何种证据的大量猜测，预计法庭内的拥挤程度将超过昨日。

随着昨日下午2时庭审恢复，塞莱特博士继续就去年5月雷文旗下企业崩溃前不久，通过雷文在美亚金融公司的账户进行的“卖空”交易一事向布朗先生提问。关于这些“卖空”交易的交叉盘问占据了上午庭审的大部分时间，检方试图证明，美亚金融公司当时正拼命设法获取现金，以注入美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation），所有雷文旗下的公司都建立在该银行之上，而该银行当时处境岌岌可危。

未告知雷文

塞莱特博士：在进行那些所谓的卖空交易之前，你是否通知了德里斯科尔（Driscoll）先生？
布朗先生：没有。
塞莱特博士：你当时或事后也没有通知雷文先生吗？
布朗先生：没有。
塞莱特博士：你为何不与雷文先生商议此事？
布朗先生：我不知道为什么。当时，鉴于我即将前往马尼拉，我正忙于向我的继任者移交事务。
塞莱特博士：你是否有权通过雷文先生名下的R. T. Co. 101-I. 1账户下达买卖指令？
布朗先生：没有。
塞莱特博士：在1933年夏季雷文先生不在美国期间，你是否操作过该账户？
布朗先生：并非独自操作。
塞莱特博士：在雷文先生离开之前，你是否与他讨论过该账户的操作事宜？
布朗先生：也许有。
塞莱特博士：未经他人授权，你不会操作其账户吧？
布朗先生：在此案中，若无雷文先生授权，我不会操作。

随后，公诉律师提请证人注意，他在直接询问中曾陈述，所述的卖空交易是误入雷文账户的，本应进入R. T. Co. 106-17账户，即美亚金融公司与其自身的往来账户。布朗先生曾作证称，在开具有关这些销售的单据时，填错了密码编号。

塞莱特博士：你为何等到现在才告诉我们真相——即这些交易是故意通过雷文先生账户进行的？你不认为你之前的证词容易误导法庭吗？

出于好意

布朗先生：我无意误导。
证人接着说，1935年5月7日他启程前往马尼拉时，他认为有可能将美亚金融公司在皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）保证金账户中的所有全额付款股票取出，并转移至安全保管。

塞莱特博士：你认为这可以毫无困难地完成吗？
布朗先生：我相信可以做到，但并非没有困难。
塞莱特博士：假设只有美亚银行倒闭。在这种情况下，美亚金融公司是否可能继续经营？
布朗先生：美亚金融公司关闭的原因是银行崩盘。
塞莱特博士：但你本可以将客户的全额付款股票交付给他们？
布朗先生：我想是的。
塞莱特博士：如何做到？
布朗先生：通过收回借给雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的贷款，并出售我们在纽约证券交易所的席位。
塞莱特博士：1935年5月，这些席位的价值是多少？
布朗先生：大约12.5万美元。

仅持有权益

塞莱特博士：当时这些席位的价值不是在下跌吗？
布朗先生：不，我认为价值在上涨。
塞莱特博士：但美亚金融公司已以这些席位的价值为抵押进行了借款。美亚金融公司在这些席位中实际拥有的权益是多少？
布朗先生：大约7万美元。
塞莱特博士：那么，即使你变现了这笔金额，你仍然需要大约5万美元才能从皮尔斯公司的保证金账户中取出全额付款股票？
布朗先生：不，我想我们还需要大约1万美元。
塞莱特博士：是否曾讨论过出售席位以便将客户的全额付款证券置于安全保管之下？
布朗先生：我们在1933年讨论过，但与将全额付款股票置于安全保管的问题无关。

公诉律师随后再次回到1935年春季进行的“卖空”交易话题，并向证人暗示，美亚金融公司由此获得的资金被用于支撑美亚银行。布朗先生表示，这笔资金被美亚金融公司用于自身目的以及协助亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）。

塞莱特博士：但是，当美亚金融公司将因所谓卖空交易而从皮尔斯公司收到的资金转拨给美亚银行时，你知道美亚银行处境岌岌可危吗？
布朗先生：不，我真的不知道。

不知晓亏损

塞莱特博士：你难道不知道，在关闭前一个月，约有价值100万上海两的存款从美亚银行被提取，且美亚银行在外汇交易中还另外损失了100万吗？
布朗先生：我不知道存款减少到那种程度，也不知道在外汇上损失了这么多。有人向我解释称，人们提取资金是因为汇率形势有利，正将钱汇回家乡。

随后，塞莱特博士转而讨论美亚金融公司的资产负债表问题。“在1935年春季，”他询问布朗先生，“你在让审计师认证你的资产负债表方面遇到了很大困难——是吗？”布朗先生承认确实存在一些困难。

塞莱特博士：而在某个周日早晨，你和雷文先生在法国总会会见了斯托罗克（Sturrock）先生（来自特纳、斯托罗克和布朗审计事务所），目的是诱使他认证由你们办公室编制的资产负债表——是吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：你们的尝试失败了，不是吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：于是你们决定以13万美元的价格将你们在纽约证券交易所的席位出售给雷文信托公司。这笔款项由雷文信托公司通过一张以美亚银行为付款行的支票支付给你们。其中包括6%的利息——是吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：然后你们就让资产负债表签了字？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：然后在一周后，美亚金融公司将13万美元连同利息退还给了雷文信托公司？
布朗先生：是的。

Changed Auditors
Prosecuting counsel then asked whether it was not a fact that Turner, Sturrock and Brown had been replaced as auditors of the A.-O.F.C. by Messrs. Thompson and Company and that this was done by a resolution of the Executive Council of the Raven enterprises passed on December 31, 1934. Witness replied in the affirmative.
Dr. Sellett: The minutes of that meeting include a resolution that minutes be not placed at the disposal of the corporation's auditors and that they be furnished with certified copies of only such minutes as are "considered necessary" for the auditors—is that so?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Now if you had, in your balance sheet for 1934, given proper information, your balance sheet would not have shown the profit it did?
Mr. Brown: We gave the auditors all the information they wanted.
Dr. Sellett: Did you expect the auditors to divine that the account R. T. Co. 106-L.7 was the A.-O.F.C.'s own account?
Mr. Brown: They didn't ask whose account it was.
Dr. Sellett: As a matter of fact they did inquire about that account and about all the other cipher accounts and they were told that these were accounts of clients of the A.-O.F.C.—formally a correct statement, but actually entirely misleading and therefore dishonest.

Clients Furnished "Margin"
Prosecuting counsel then led the witness to admit that at the time the Raven concerns crashed, fully-paid securities belonging to customers of the A.-O.F.C. were actually financing half of the total margin requirements of the A.-O.F.C. in its account with Pierce and Company.
After this admission, Mr. Brown was asked whether the knowledge of this position didn't bring home to him the significance and importance of determining just what were the rights and duties of the A.-O.F.C. in the handling of customers' fully-paid securities.
In reply, Mr. Brown said he did not realize that the figures involved were so big.
Dr. Sellett: But what about the report by Mr. Haley (which showed that the A.-O.F.C. was holding U.S. $150,000 of customers' fully-paid securities, of which only U.S. $50,000 were in safekeeping)?
No answer being given, Dr. Sellett fired his next question at the witness: "So then you admit that you used these fully-paid securities to finance the A.-O.F.C.'s own business?"
Mr. Brown: Yes.

Unprotected Accounts
Dr. Sellett: This at a time when Mr. Raven had the huge unprotected balance of U.S. $116,000 outstanding against him on the books of the A.-O.F.C.: when there was your own unprotected account, the account of Mr. James Price, the legal genius of the company, and the accounts of other officers of the A.-O.F.C. and their associates?
Mr. Brown: Yes, but the accounts were not entirely unprotected.
Dr. Sellett: With that situation before you, did it not occur to you that it was improper to use fully-paid shares of customers in the way that you did?
Mr. Brown: We were able to make delivery at any time.
Dr. Sellett: But only by action which would have resulted in the closure of the A.-O.F.C.—is that not so?

Mr. Brown: No, we possessed borrowing ability and could have sold out our seats on the New York Stock Exchange.
Further questions by Dr. Sellett elicited the information that margin cards of the cipher accounts were always kept on Mr. Brown's desk in the office and not in the file with the other cards. "Was this because you wanted to have them constantly under attention to see that the accounts were properly margined, or because you wanted the position of these accounts concealed from others in the office?" Dr. Sellett asked.
Mr. Brown: Because I wanted to have them under my constant attention in regard to margining.
Dr. Sellett then switched to the transactions with Mr. Lucien Claude Basset, one of the complaining witnesses in the case. Mr. Brown had testified earlier that had he known that Mr. Basset had not signed a hypothecation consent form he would have instructed that this client's account be closed.
Dr. Sellett: Have you thought over the testimony you gave on this point yesterday? Is there anything you would like to change.

Veracity Questioned
Mr. Brown's reply was in the negative and Mr. Franklin, counsel for Mr. Brown, objected to the line of questioning.
Dr. Sellett: I only wanted to try and save the time which will be consumed in calling a witness for rebuttal. It can easily be proved that the witness told an untruth in this matter.
To Mr. Brown: Did you not tell Miss Woolley that it was not necessary for Mr. Basset to sign a hypothecation consent?
Mr. Brown: I don't remember, but I do know that I always insisted that all clients sign these consents.
Dr. Sellett: Was Mr. Raven kept informed at all times as to the amount of fully-paid shares in the margin account with Pierce and Company?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
As the afternoon session drew to a close, Dr. Sellett proceeded to question Mr. Brown in respect to the charges set forth in the indictment, dealing with the last charge first.
Dr. Sellett: When you wrote a letter to Pierce and Company on May 16, 1933 forwarding Mr. Kirkland's shares, did you intend that those shares be placed in the margin account, or did you just make a mistake?
Mr. Brown hesitated for a long time. Prosecuting counsel followed up: "Did you, knowingly and intentionally, in transmitting those shares to Pierce and Company, intend that they be placed in the margin account?
Judge Helmick: The answer can be just "yes" or "no."
Mr. Brown: Yes, but knowing quite well that we owed them to Mr. Kirkland.
Dr. Sellett: Did you not know that in the margin account these shares of Mr. Kirkland would be used by Pierce and Company as security for the A.-O.F.C.'s debit balances, just as all other shares were similarly used?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Now, regarding the cheque for Sh.$549.18 which you received from Mr. C. R. Jones on March 18, 1935, for the purchase of 50 Electric Bond and Share stocks. You deposited that cheque in the A.-O.F.C.'s dollar account with the A.-O.B.C. Did you intend the proceeds of that cheque to be mingled with all the other funds of the A.-O.F.C. with the bank, and used as if it were the A.-O.F.C.'s own money?

Mr. Brown: That was the way we handled all receipts. We didn't keep the various items separate.
Dr. Sellett: So you intended that the cheque be used for the A.-O.F.C.'s general purposes?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: In other words, you did not intend using the proceeds of the cheque to purchase the 50 Electric Bond and Share stocks ordered by Mr. Jones?
Mr. Brown equivocated and replied that part of the proceeds went to purchase the 50 shares, but not all at one time.
Dr. Sellett: But were those shares fully paid for at any time?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Now we come to the Yates transaction.
Mr. Brown: This was the same as in the Jones case.
Dr. Sellett: You intended the same things as in the Jones case?
Mr. Brown: Yes, that's the way we handled it.
Dr. Sellett: And the Curtis-Wright shares which Yates ordered and paid for with his cheque for Sh. $1,225.97—were they always left in the margin account with Pierce?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Now the Howard transaction. Mr. Howard gave you a draft for U. S. $507.60 on July 7, 1934. When happened to it?
Mr. Brown: It was deposited in the account of the A.-O.F.C. with the A.-O.B.C.—the U. S. dollar account—as with other similar transactions.
Dr. Sellett: And it was not used to buy and pay in full for the 30 Douglas Aircraft shares which Mr. Howard ordered?
At this stage the Court adjourned until 9.30 a.m. to-day.

Morning Proceedings
Most of the morning session was devoted by Dr. Sellett to cross-examination of Mr. Brown on the subject of the so-called short sales made on Mr. Raven's account, R. T. Co. 101-I.1. shortly before the crash of the Raven enterprises last year.
Mr. Brown said that Mr. Raven had not been consulted about the sales on his account, which took place on May 2, 1935, five days before Mr. Brown sailed for Manila. Mr. Raven was in Shanghai at the time and could easily have been reached, Dr. Sellett brought out.
"Did it not occur to you," he asked Mr. Brown, "that in involving Mr. Raven in a transaction amounting to U. S. $104,000 you might have consulted Mr. Raven?
Mr. Brown: As I recall, it was after 5 o'clock and Mr. Raven had left the office.
Dr. Sellett: 'Could you not have reached him by 'phone?
Mr. Brown: Well, yes.
Dr. Sellett: Did you make any effort to get in touch with him?

Big Deal Alone
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Must we understand that in a transaction involving U. S. $104,000 you acted without his authority?
Mr. Brown: That's the actual fact.

更换审计师

公诉律师随后询问，特纳（Turner）、斯塔罗克（Sturrock）和布朗（Brown）是否确实已被汤普森公司（Messrs. Thompson and Company）取代，不再担任 A.-O.F.C. 的审计师，且这一变动是依据雷文企业（Raven enterprises）执行委员会于 1934 年 12 月 31 日通过的一项决议进行的。证人给予了肯定答复。

塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）：那次会议的纪要中包含一项决议，规定会议纪要不向公司审计师公开，仅向他们提供那些被认为对审计师“有必要”的会议纪要的核证副本——是这样吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：那么，如果你在 1934 年的资产负债表中提供了适当的信息，你的资产负债表就不会显示出那样的利润，是吗？

布朗先生：我们向审计师提供了他们想要的所有信息。

塞莱特博士：你是否指望审计师能猜出账户 R. T. Co. 106-L.7 实际上是 A.-O.F.C. 自己的账户？

布朗先生：他们没有问这是谁的账户。

塞莱特博士：事实上，他们确实查询过该账户以及所有其他密码账户，并被告知这些是 A.-O.F.C. 客户的账户——这在形式上是正确的陈述，但实际上完全具有误导性，因此是不诚实的。

客户提供“保证金”

公诉律师随后引导证人承认，在雷文相关企业崩溃时，属于 A.-O.F.C. 客户的全额付款证券实际上为 A.-O.F.C. 在皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）账户中总保证金要求的一半提供了资金。

在这一承认之后，有人问布朗先生，了解这一情况是否使他意识到确定 A.-O.F.C. 在处理客户全额付款证券方面的权利和义务的意义和重要性。

作为回应，布朗先生表示他没有意识到涉及的金额如此之大。

塞莱特博士：但是海利先生（Mr. Haley）的报告呢（该报告显示 A.-O.F.C. 持有价值 150,000 美元的客户全额付款证券，其中只有 50,000 美元处于保管状态）？

由于没有给出回答，塞莱特博士向证人提出了下一个问题：“那么你承认你使用了这些全额付款证券来为 A.-O.F.C. 自身的业务提供资金？”

布朗先生：是的。

无保护账户

塞莱特博士：当时雷文先生（Mr. Raven）在 A.-O.F.C. 的账簿上有着巨大的无保护余额，高达 116,000 美元；当时还有你自己的无保护账户、该公司法律天才詹姆斯·普赖斯先生（Mr. James Price）的账户，以及 A.-O.F.C. 其他高管及其关联方的账户？

布朗先生：是的，但这些账户并非完全没有保护。

塞莱特博士：面对这种情况，你没有想到以你所使用的方式动用客户的全额付款股票是不当的吗？

布朗先生：我们随时能够进行交割。

塞莱特博士：但这只有通过会导致 A.-O.F.C. 关闭的行动才能实现——难道不是这样吗？

布朗先生：不，我们拥有借贷能力，并且可以出售我们在纽约证券交易所的席位。

塞莱特博士的进一步提问引出了以下信息：密码账户的保证金卡片总是放在布朗先生办公室的办公桌上，而不是与其他卡片一起归档。“这是因为你想让它们时刻受到关注，以确保账户保证金充足，还是因为你想向办公室里的其他人隐瞒这些账户的状况？”塞莱特博士问道。

布朗先生：因为我想让它们在我的持续关注之下，以便处理保证金事宜。

随后，塞莱特博士转向与吕西安·克劳德·巴塞特先生（Mr. Lucien Claude Basset）的交易，他是本案的投诉证人之一。布朗先生此前作证说，如果他早知道巴塞特先生没有签署抵押同意书，他会指示关闭该客户的账户。

塞莱特博士：你是否反思过你昨天就此点所作的证词？有什么你想更改的吗？

真实性受到质疑

布朗先生的回答是否定的，布朗先生的律师富兰克林先生（Mr. Franklin）反对这种提问方式。

塞莱特博士：我只是想节省传唤反驳证人所耗费的时间。很容易证明证人在此事上说了谎。

问布朗先生：你没有告诉伍利小姐（Miss Woolley）巴塞特先生没有必要签署抵押同意书吗？

布朗先生：我不记得了，但我确实知道我一直坚持要求所有客户签署这些同意书。

塞莱特博士：雷文先生是否随时知晓在皮尔斯公司的保证金账户中全额付款股票的数量？

布朗先生：是的。

随着下午庭审接近尾声，塞莱特博士开始就起诉书中列出的指控讯问布朗先生，首先处理最后一项指控。

塞莱特博士：当你于 1933 年 5 月 16 日致信皮尔斯公司并转交柯克兰先生（Mr. Kirkland）的股票时，你是打算将这些股票放入保证金账户，还是仅仅犯了一个错误？

布朗先生犹豫了很长时间。公诉律师追问：“在将这些股票转交给皮尔斯公司时，你是否明知且故意地打算将它们放入保证金账户？

赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）：回答可以是简单的“是”或“否”。

布朗先生：是的，但我非常清楚我们欠柯克兰先生这些股票。

塞莱特博士：你难道不知道在保证金账户中，柯克兰先生的这些股票会被皮尔斯公司用作 A.-O.F.C. 借方余额的担保，就像所有其他股票一样被使用吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：现在，关于你于 1935 年 3 月 18 日从 C. R. 琼斯先生（Mr. C. R. Jones）那里收到的用于购买 50 股电力债券与股票公司（Electric Bond and Share）股票的 549.18 上海两支票。你将那张支票存入了 A.-O.F.C. 在 A.-O.B.C. 的美元账户。你是否打算将该支票的收益与 A.-O.F.C. 在银行的所有其他资金混合，并像使用 A.-O.F.C. 自有资金一样使用它？

布朗先生：这就是我们处理所有收款的方式。我们没有将各项款项分开存放。

塞莱特博士：所以你打算将该支票用于 A.-O.F.C. 的一般用途？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：换句话说，你并不打算使用该支票的收益来购买琼斯先生订购的 50 股电力债券与股票公司股票？

布朗先生闪烁其词，回答说部分收益用于购买这 50 股股票，但并非一次性全部购买。

塞莱特博士：但这些股票在任何时候都付清全款了吗？

布朗先生：没有。

塞莱特博士：现在我们来看耶茨（Yates）的交易。

布朗先生：这与琼斯案的情况相同。

塞莱特博士：你的意图与琼斯案中的意图相同？

布朗先生：是的，我们就那样处理的。

塞莱特博士：耶茨订购并用其 1,225.97 上海两支票支付的柯蒂斯-莱特（Curtis-Wright）股票——它们是否一直留在皮尔斯公司的保证金账户中？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：现在是霍华德（Howard）的交易。霍华德先生于 1934 年 7 月 7 日给了你一张 507.60 美元的汇票。后来发生了什么？

布朗先生：它被存入了 A.-O.F.C. 在 A.-O.B.C. 的账户——即美元账户——与其他类似交易一样。

塞莱特博士：而且它并没有用于购买并全额支付霍华德先生订购的 30 股道格拉斯飞机公司（Douglas Aircraft）股票？

此时，法庭休庭，直至今天上午 9:30 继续开庭。

上午庭审

上午庭审的大部分时间都用于塞莱特博士就所谓在去年雷文企业崩溃前不久以雷文先生账户 R. T. Co. 101-I.1 进行的卖空交易对布朗先生进行交叉质询。

布朗先生说，雷文先生并未就以其账户进行的销售事宜进行过咨询，这些销售发生在 1935 年 5 月 2 日，即布朗先生乘船前往马尼拉的前五天。塞莱特博士指出，雷文先生当时在上海，很容易联系到。

“你没有想到，”他问布朗先生，“在让雷文先生参与一笔金额为 104,000 美元的交易时，你可能应该咨询一下雷文先生吗？

布朗先生：据我回忆，当时已经过了 5 点，雷文先生已经离开了办公室。

塞莱特博士：你不能通过电话找到他吗？

布朗先生：嗯，可以。

塞莱特博士：你有没有努力尝试与他取得联系？

独自达成大笔交易

布朗先生：没有。

塞莱特博士：我们是否必须理解为，在一笔涉及 104,000 美元的交易中，你在未经他授权的情况下采取了行动？

布朗先生：那是事实。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JANUARY 28, 1936

Price Blamed For Deals
With Fully-Paid Shares
And Code Number Account

Exhaustive Questioning Of Brown Persists During
Third Day; Prosecutor Breaks Down Argument
Of Cable Costs Against Safekeeping

RAVEN TOOK “CONSERVATIVE ATTITUDE,”
DID NOT DISCUSS PROPRIETY

Ending his third day of examination and cross-examination on charges of larceny, fraud and embezzlement which are being brought against him and Mr. Frank Jay Raven as officers of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Company, Mr. J. Warner Brown held again yesterday to his denial that he had dealt illegally with clients’ fully-paid shares which were put into the A.-O.F.C. “margin” account and hypothecated to Messrs. E. A. Pierce and Company. During another day of gruelling questioning on the mass of documented evidence piled up by the prosecution, he maintained that the policy of the firm had been correct “so long as the company was strong and able to deliver shares to clients when wanted.”

Dr. George Sellett, prosecuting for the Government in the U.S. Court for China, was unable to draw from witness any statement regarding Mr. Raven’s part in the policy of the company, other than a statement that he had taken a “conservative attitude.”

Sitting and standing room was again at a premium when court opened in the morning. A bevy of housewives had come with their needles and knitting wrapped up in towels, to settle down for the morning. Mr. M. Spelman and a number of financial men were in time to get front row seats, while a well-known cabaret owner was comfortably ensconced in the rear.

J. Warner Brown carried his bulky brief-case to the witness-stand and as Dr. Sellett prepared to resume questioning him, he said: “I would like to correct a statement I made on Saturday regarding bucketing. I was misled by Dr. Sellett. All of our orders were put through E. A. Pierce as actual sales. My statements were that we did nothing illegal in the A.-O.F.C. in the way of bucketing.”

Matching Sales

Dr. Sellett: What do you mean —that every purchase was a sale through E. A. Pierce? Did you ever match sales?

Brown: Yes, occasionally. Every time you had a buyer and a seller for the same stock it was the policy of the company to match sales?—Yes, generally. Out of a barrage of questions arising from this lead, witness contradicted his first statements and said that he did not approve of “matching” and that very few such transactions had taken place.

Dr. Sellett: You did nothing to prevent that practice?—I didn’t approve of it. Well, if you didn’t approve of it, who did approve of it?—The cable department. Weren’t you the manager?—Yes. I put it to you that you knew it was the policy of the company and that it was carried out continually—No.

“Name One Person”

Seeming to be greatly interested in witness’ statement that he had not approved of this policy, Dr. Sellett asked: “Name one person in the company whom you told not to match orders—just one person.”

A long silence ensued, after which Brown said he could not remember, but that he had not approved from the very beginning.

Then he said he thought he had issued instructions.

Dr. Sellett: What happened?—I told them not to do it again. That was all that happened?—I don’t remember one such transaction a year. Now, what are we to believe? —I didn’t approve of it. It wasn’t the policy of the company.

Charged Cables, Taxes

A period of relentless questioning on another tack ensued in which Dr. Sellett wrung from witness a qualified admission that although no cable expenses were incurred when “matching orders” occurred, clients were nevertheless charged with cable costs. Witness said he thought this was usual banking practice, in exchange transactions, etc.

Dr. Sellett: Do you know that any other bank than the American-Oriental Bank followed this practice. Any reputable bank?—I heard that it was. You charged each client with the stock exchange tax?—I don’t know. I didn’t see how the orders were made up. You, as manager of the A.-O.F.C. for five years, didn’t know that clients were charged this tax?—No.

The prosecutor’s manner grew gentle again as he asked witness about his statements made on Friday, in which he justified the practice of keeping fully-paid stocks of clients in the A.-O.F.C. margin account. He asked him to recapitulate them. Witness said that they were: the prohibitive cable costs which clients would not absorb; the fact that the company was strong and able to deliver shares whenever wanted by the clients; the fact that clients might want to use fully-paid shares as margin for trading or in connection with exchange transactions.

A Complainer

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever find a client who complained about the prohibitive cost of cables?—Yes, Mr. Crowe, of the Ford Motor Exports.

Dr. Sellett: I submit that is an example. His shares were being delivered to a bank in New York, were they not?—Yes. Was Mr. Crowe told his shares were being kept in the margin account?—I don’t think so. Was there ever a client during your five years’ experience who didn’t want his stocks put in safekeeping because of prohibitive cable charges?—Witness did not answer.

Dr. Sellett then tried, unsuccessfully, to get a definite statement on the attitude of Mr. Raven towards the propriety of keeping fully-paid shares in the margin account. Mr. Brown would only say that the attitude of Mr. Raven had been one concern for clients’ protection and that he had taken a “conservative attitude.”

What Mr. Raven Wanted

Then we may believe that he wanted the fully-paid shares kept in safekeeping?—Witness replied in the affirmative, but qualified his answer in several different ways. I want to know whether you did or did not discuss it?—I think that we discussed it and that he took the conservative view that something should be done about it. What were you going to do about it?—We didn’t discuss that. I am very much interested to know on just what side Mr. Raven was, when the decision was made to deal in the way you did for five years?—He was on the conservative side.

Returning to the matter of “prohibitive cable costs,” Dr. Sellett drew from witness an estimate that it would cost U.S.$5 to instruct E. A. Pierce to buy and put shares in safekeeping. Then he admitted that a code word for “buy and put in safekeeping” would cost no more than the word “buy.” For putting them in and out of safekeeping it would cost about U.S.$1.50.

Why Prohibitive

Is that prohibitive?—I don’t think that your example is average. We would have to include a statement of the balance of shares in safekeeping. Why? You never did it by letter, did you? Why should you adopt Pierce and Company procedure just because you are using a more expeditious way of sending messages?—I think we would have to do it. These practices of the A.-O.F.C. were fully known to you and Mr. Raven?—It was known to me. Did you ever discuss with Mr. Raven in the last three or four years the matter of fully-paid shares? — I think I remember mentioning Mr. Haley’s report.

Dr. Sellett was unable again to get any definite answer regarding conversations with Mr. Raven. Exasperated, he asked: Is this one subject upon which your memory is very, very dim or are you now in the sorry predicament of being manager of this company for five years and yet not being able to recall what view your superior took regarding fully-paid shares?

The “Conservative Attitude”

Mr. Brown said he took the “conservative attitude,” but would not elucidate further.

Dr. Sellett: Then we have it this way—that the A.-O.F.C., for four-and-a-half years while you were its manager, consistently hypothecated fully-paid securities and the responsibility for doing so was shouldered entirely by you?—Largely.
