《上海泰晤士报》，1936年1月28日，星期二

价格被归咎于涉及全额付款股份和代码号账户的交易

第三天持续对布朗进行详尽讯问；检察官驳斥了关于保管费用的论点

雷文采取“保守态度”，未讨论适当性

J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生在针对他和弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）先生作为已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Company）高管所面临的盗窃、欺诈和挪用公款指控的审讯和交叉质询的第三天结束时，昨天再次否认他非法处置了存入美亚金融公司“保证金”账户并抵押给E·A·皮尔斯公司（Messrs. E. A. Pierce and Company）的客户全额付款股份。在公诉方堆积如山的大量书面证据面前，经过又一天的严酷质询，他坚称公司的政策是正确的，“只要公司实力雄厚，能够在客户需要时交付股份。”

代表美国政府在中国美国法院起诉的乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士未能从证人那里引出任何关于雷文先生在公司政策中所扮演角色的陈述，除了他说雷文采取了“保守态度”。

上午开庭时，坐席和站立空间再次紧缺。一群家庭主妇带着用毛巾包裹的针线和编织物前来，准备安顿下来度过上午。M·斯佩尔曼（M. Spelman）先生和许多金融界人士及时赶到，获得了前排座位，而一位著名的歌舞厅老板则舒适地安坐在后排。

J·华纳·布朗带着他笨重的公文包走向证人席，当塞莱特博士准备恢复对他进行讯问时，他说：“我想纠正我周六关于‘对敲’（bucketing）所作的一项陈述。我被塞莱特博士误导了。我们所有的订单都是通过E·A·皮尔斯公司作为实际销售执行的。我的陈述是，我们在美亚金融公司没有进行任何非法的‘对敲’行为。”

匹配销售

塞莱特博士：你是什么意思——每一笔购买都是通过E·A·皮尔斯公司进行的销售？你是否曾经进行过销售匹配？
布朗：是的，偶尔会有。每当同一只股票既有买家又有卖家时，公司的政策就是进行销售匹配？——是的，通常是这样。在这一线索引发的一连串问题中，证人推翻了他最初的陈述，说他并不赞成“匹配”，而且此类交易很少发生。

塞莱特博士：你没有采取任何措施阻止这种做法？——我不赞成它。好吧，如果你不赞成，谁赞成了？——电报部。你不是经理吗？——是的。我向你指出，你知道这是公司的政策，并且一直在执行——不。

“说出一个人”

塞莱特博士似乎对证人声称他不赞成这一政策的陈述非常感兴趣，问道：“说出公司里你告诉过不要匹配订单的一个人——就一个人。”
随后是一段长长的沉默，之后布朗说他不记得了，但他从一开始就不赞成。
然后他说他认为他发出过指示。
塞莱特博士：发生了什么？——我告诉他们不要再这样做。就发生了这些？——我不记得一年中有过这样一笔交易。现在，我们要相信什么？——我不赞成。这不是公司的政策。

指控电报费、税款

随后是一段沿着另一条思路进行的无情质询，塞莱特博士迫使证人做出有条件的承认，即虽然在“匹配订单”发生时没有产生电报费用，但客户仍被收取了电报成本。证人表示他认为这在银行实务、外汇交易等中是惯例。
塞莱特博士：你知道除美亚银行外还有其他银行遵循这种做法吗？任何信誉良好的银行？——我听说有。你向每位客户收取了证券交易所税吗？——我不知道。我没看过订单是如何组成的。你作为美亚金融公司五年的经理，不知道客户被收取了这项税款？——不知道。

检察官的语气再次变得温和，他询问证人周五所作的陈述，他在其中辩解了将客户全额付款股票保留在美亚金融公司保证金账户中的做法。他要求证人重述这些理由。证人说是：客户不愿承担的高昂电报成本；公司实力雄厚，能够在客户需要时随时交付股份；客户可能希望使用全额付款股份作为交易保证金或与外汇交易相关用途。

一名抱怨者

塞莱特博士：你是否发现过有客户抱怨高昂的电报成本？——是的，福特汽车出口公司（Ford Motor Exports）的克罗（Crowe）先生。
塞莱特博士：我认为这是一个例子。他的股份正被交付给纽约的一家银行，不是吗？——是的。克罗先生是否被告知他的股份正被保留在保证金账户中？——我想没有。在你五年的经历中，是否有客户因为高昂的电报收费而不希望将股票存入保管库？——证人未作回答。

随后，塞莱特博士试图就雷文先生对将全额付款股份保留在保证金账户中的适当性的态度获得明确的陈述，但未成功。布朗先生只说雷文先生的态度是关心客户保护，并且他采取了“保守态度”。

雷文先生想要什么

那么我们可以相信他希望将全额付款股份保存在保管库中？——证人给予肯定回答，但以几种不同的方式对其回答进行了限定。我想知道你们是否讨论过此事？——我想我们讨论过，他采取了保守的观点，认为应该对此采取一些措施。你打算对此做什么？——我们没有讨论那个。我很想知道，在决定以你们过去五年的方式进行交易的决策中，雷文先生究竟站在哪一边？——他站在保守的一边。

回到“高昂电报成本”的问题上，塞莱特博士从证人那里引出一个估算，即指示E·A·皮尔斯公司购买并将股份存入保管库的费用为5美元。然后他承认，用于“购买并存入保管库”的代码字费用不会超过“购买”一词的费用。将它们存入和取出保管库的费用约为1.50美元。

为何高昂

那算高昂吗？——我认为你的例子不具有代表性。我们必须包括一份保管库中股份余额的对账单。为什么？你从未通过信件这样做过，是吗？仅仅因为你们使用更快捷的信息发送方式，为什么要采用皮尔斯公司的程序？——我认为我们必须这样做。美亚金融公司的这些做法为你和雷文先生所 fully 知晓？——为我所知。在过去三四年里，你是否与雷文先生讨论过全额付款股份的问题？——我想我记得提到过哈利（Haley）先生的报告。

塞莱特博士再次无法就与雷文先生的谈话获得任何明确答复。他恼怒地问道：这是你记忆非常模糊的一个话题，还是说你如今处于可悲的境地，担任这家公司经理五年，却无法回忆起你的上级对全额付款股份持何种观点？

“保守态度”

布朗先生说他是采取“保守态度”，但不愿进一步阐明。
塞莱特博士：那么情况就是这样——在美亚金融公司，在你担任经理的四年半时间里，一直抵押全额付款证券，而这样做的责任完全由你承担？——很大程度上是的。

page_data.en:
fully-paid shares in this way?—
Not single-handed.
Who else?—I discussed it with
various people and they agreed
for the reasons mentioned that
it was legal.
Dr. Sellett: Did Mr. Raven
agree or did he not agree with
your method of handling custom-
ers' fully-paid shares?
Mr. Brown: He generally
agreed with proposals I put up to
him.

Yes Or No?
Dr. Sellett: Did he or did he
not agree with the practice in
handling fully-paid shares—did
you ever discuss the matter with
him?
Mr. Brown: No, I did not
bring the matter up with him.
Dr. Sellett: During the several
years that you were with the A.-
O.F.C. did you not mention the
matter of handling fully-paid
shares even in casual conversa-
tions with Mr. Raven?
Mr. Brown: Yes, casually.
Dr. Sellett: Did Mr. Raven
take an interest in the affairs of
the A.-O.F.C.?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Where was his
office in relation to yours?
Mr. Brown: Before he moved
his office to the building of the
Asia Realty Company it was next
door to mine in the building at
29 Nanking Road.

A Connecting Door
Dr. Sellett: Was there a con-
necting door between your two
offices?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Was it used by
both of you in passing to and
from each other's offices?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: How long did you
have these connecting offices?
Witness replied that he and Mr.
Raven had these connecting offices
during the latter part of 1930,
the greater part of 1931 and also
during the early part of 1932. He
discussed A.-O.F.C. affairs with
Mr. Raven almost daily during
those periods.
Dr. Sellett: Was Mr. Raven
available to the managers of all
his corporations in about the same
degree?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: What salary did
Mr. Raven draw from the
A.-O.F.C.?

Drew An Allowance
Mr. Brown replied that he drew
an allowance and not a salary.
Dr. Sellett: What is the differ-
ence between an allowance and a
salary?
At this point Mr. Evans objected
on the ground that the Court had
previously ruled that the question
of the salaries drawn by Mr.
Brown and Mr. Raven was im-
material. "I don't object to the
question as such," counsel said,
"but it seems to me a waste of
time to seek information which
is immaterial."
Dr. Sellett: Very well, we'll wait
until Mr. Raven takes the witness-
stand—that is, if he does take the
witness-stand.

An Improper Remark
Mr. Evans protested that this
was an improper remark, as
counsel for the prosecution had
no right to suggest that Mr.
Raven would not take the witness-
stand. Judge Helmick ordered that
Dr. Sellett's remark be stricken
from the record.
Dr. Sellett: Now, Mr. Brown,
what salary were you getting from
the A.-O.F.C.?
Mr. Brown: The highest salary
I received was Sh. $2,200 per
month. At one time it was Sh.
$1,760.

Dr. Sellett: So the highest
salary you received was Sh. $2,200
and the lowest Sh. $1,760—is that
so?
Mr. Brown: Yes. But I paid in
five per cent. of my salary to a
superannuation fund. To this five
per cent. the A.-O.F.C. added five
per cent.
Further questions to the wit-
ness by Dr. Sellett elicited the
information that Mr. Brown had
been absent from Shanghai on
several occasions during his
employment with the A.-O.F.C.
He took two weeks' vacation in
1932, another two-three weeks in
September, 1933. During February-
March, 1934 he was on a trip to
Hongkong, Canton and Manila.
In June, 1934, he went to the
U.S.A. via Siberia, returning to
Shanghai in October of that year.
In January-February, 1935 he
spent about one month in Manila.
Finally, on May 7, 1935 he again
proceeded to Manila and was still
there when the Raven concerns
crashed.
Dr. Sellett: So, except for the
periods mentioned, you were con-
tinuously in Shanghai while in the
employ of the A.-O.F.C.?
Mr. Brown: Yes, apart from
visits to Nanking for a day or
two.

Mr. Brown's Duties
Witness said that he performed
the duties of Vice-President,
Manager and Director of the
A.-O.F.C.
Dr. Sellett then switched his
cross-examination to the question
of the fully-paid shares of Mr.
Maurice Benjamin, whose name
was mentioned in the course of
evidence tendered for the prosecu-
tion as a customer whose shares
had been transferred to safekeep-
ing 'little by little' at Mr.
Driscoll's insistence.
Answering Dr. Sellett's ques-
tions, Mr. Brown said that the
question of transferring these
shares to safekeeping was discuss-
ed by the Executive Council of
the Raven enterprises in Septem-
ber, 1933, after the matter had
been talked over by Mr. Brown
and Mr. Driscoll.
Dr. Sellett: Did Mr. Driscoll ask
you to transfer these shares to
safekeeping?

Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: And what was your
reply?
Mr. Brown: I told Mr. Driscoll
that the R. T. Co. cipher accounts
would have to be properly margin-
ed before anything could be done.
Dr. Sellett: Did you suggest to
him that it would be inconvenient
to transfer Mr. Benjamin's shares
to safekeeping?
Mr. Brown: No, I was concerned
to get these cipher accounts pro-
perly margined.

Huge Debit Balances
Dr. Sellett: One of these
accounts, R. T. Co. 101-I.1, which
was the account of Mr. Raven—
this account had a debit balance
of U.S. $100,000 or more through-
out the summer of 1933? When
all the securities in it were sold
out after the crash, there remain-
ed a debit balance of U.S. $116,000
—is that correct?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Did you know that
this account was heavily under-
margined in 1933?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: What efforts did
you make to get Mr. Raven's
account properly margined?
Mr. Brown: I took the matter
up with Mr. Driscoll.

Why Not Directly
Dr. Sellett: Were your relations
with Mr. Raven not such that you
could have taken such an import-
ant matter up with him directly?
Mr. Brown: This and the other
cipher accounts were Raven Trust
Company accounts. I looked to the
Raven Trust Company and, there-
fore, spoke to Mr. Driscoll.
Dr. Sellett: Did you not mention
it to Mr. Raven, even in a small
way?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: What did Mr. Raven
say?
Mr. Brown: He told me he
would take the matter up with
Mr. Driscoll.

Afternoon Session
Seemingly untired after the
grilling morning session, Dr.
Sellett continued in the afternoon
with a presentation of various
documents concerned with the put-
ting of shares in safekeeping.
Producing a letter from Mr.
Driscoll referring to the shares
of Mr. Maurice Benjamin, which
said in part: "if it should be in-
convenient for you to transfer
these shares at this time," he
asked whether any reason occurred
to witness why this expression
should have been used. He replied
that he could think of none.
Dr. Sellett: Perhaps I can
suggest one. You would have had
to put up cash amounting to three-
quarters of the value of the
securities to get them out of
margin. Don't you think that is
the reason why he used that ex-
pression?—No.
Wasn't it a consideration of any
importance?—We could have done
it.

Considered A.-O.F.C.
Questioned on the record of
minutes at which it was "decided
to set aside the shares little by
little so that most of them would
be transferred by the time Mr.
Benjamin returned to Shanghai,"
Mr. Brown said he refused to
release them because the R. T.
Co. accounts were undermargined
and he kept insisting upon more
security. He denied knowing of
any reason for the reference in
the minutes to the return of Mr.
Benjamin, but finally said he might
have differed from the view of
others on the Executive Council.
He was looking after the interests
of the A.-O.F.C.
They were influenced by the
fact that the shares belonged to
Mr. Benjamin, that they didn't
belong to the Finance Company,
while you were thinking of the
A.-O.F.C.?—They took the other
position.
That the property belonging to
Mr. Benjamin should be put in
safekeeping?—Yes.
Taking up the matter of the
R. T. Co. accounts. Isn't it a fact
that there was a general increase
in the debit balances in these
accounts from the opening until
the close of the company?—Wit-
ness admitted that there was.
Looking at the minutes of that
meeting, the letter to E. A. Pierce
transferring the Benjamin shares,
the letter from Driscoll on that
matter—do you still insist that
you were using it simply as a
lever to get more margin?—Yes.
You have no explanation for the
words "inconvenience," no explana-
tion for the mention of Mr.
Benjamin's return to Shanghai?
—No.
How about your own account?
page_data.zh:
以这种方式处理全额缴付股份？——
并非我一人所为。
还有谁？——我与 various people（各类人士）讨论过，他们出于前述原因同意这是合法的。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生是否同意你处理客户全额缴付股份的方式？
布朗先生：他通常同意我向他提出的建议。

是或否？
塞莱特博士：他究竟是否同意处理全额缴付股份的这种做法——你是否曾与他讨论过此事？
布朗先生：不，我没有向他提起此事。
塞莱特博士：在你任职于 A.-O.F.C. 的几年间，你难道从未在与雷文先生的随意交谈中提及处理全额缴付股份的事宜吗？
布朗先生：有，非正式地提过。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生对 A.-O.F.C. 的事务感兴趣吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：他的办公室与你的办公室位置关系如何？
布朗先生：在他将办公室迁至亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）大楼之前，他的办公室就在南京路 29 号大楼内我的办公室隔壁。

一扇连通门
塞莱特博士：你们两间办公室之间有一扇连通门吗？
布朗先生：有。
塞莱特博士：你们双方往返彼此办公室时都使用这扇门吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：你们拥有这些连通办公室有多久？
证人回答说，他与雷文先生在 1930 年下半年、1931 年大部分时间以及 1932 年初期间拥有这些连通办公室。在这些时期，他几乎每天都与雷文先生讨论 A.-O.F.C. 的事务。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生对其所有公司的经理们提供的接见程度大致相同吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生从 A.-O.F.C. 领取多少薪水？

领取津贴
布朗先生回答说，他领取的是津贴而非薪水。
塞莱特博士：津贴和薪水有什么区别？
此时，埃文斯先生提出异议，理由是法庭此前已裁定布朗先生和雷文先生所领薪水的问题无关紧要。“我并非针对问题本身提出异议，”该律师说，“但在我看来，去寻求无关紧要的信息是浪费时间。”
塞莱特博士：很好，那我们就等到雷文先生出庭作证时再说——假如他真的出庭作证的话。

不当言论
埃文斯先生抗议称这是一句不当言论，因为控方律师无权暗示雷文先生不会出庭作证。赫尔米克法官命令将塞莱特博士的这句话从记录中删除。
塞莱特博士：那么，布朗先生，你从 A.-O.F.C. 领取多少薪水？
布朗先生：我收到的最高薪水是每月上海银元 2,200 元。有一段时间是上海银元 1,760 元。

塞莱特博士：所以你收到的最高薪水是上海银元 2,200 元，最低是上海银元 1,760 元——是这样吗？
布朗先生：是的。但我将薪水的百分之五存入养老基金。A.-O.F.C. 也为这百分之五配套存入百分之五。
塞莱特博士向证人提出的进一步问题揭示出，布朗先生在受雇于 A.-O.F.C. 期间曾多次离开上海。他在 1932 年休假两周，1933 年 9 月又休假两到三周。1934 年 2 月至 3 月，他前往香港、广州和马尼拉旅行。1934 年 6 月，他经西伯利亚前往美国，并于同年 10 月返回上海。1935 年 1 月至 2 月，他在马尼拉度过了约一个月。最后，在 1935 年 5 月 7 日，他再次前往马尼拉，并在雷文相关企业崩溃时仍在那里。
塞莱特博士：所以，除了上述时期外，你在受雇于 A.-O.F.C. 期间一直连续留在上海？
布朗先生：是的，除了去南京逗留一两天之外。

布朗先生的职责
证人说，他履行了 A.-O.F.C. 副总裁、经理和董事的职责。
随后，塞莱特博士将交叉询问转向莫里斯·本杰明（Maurice Benjamin）先生的全额缴付股份问题，检方在举证过程中提到了他的名字，称其为客户，其股份是在德里斯科尔（Driscoll）先生的坚持下“一点一点”转移至保管状态的。
回答塞莱特博士的问题时，布朗先生说，将这批股份转移至保管状态的问题是由雷文企业的执行委员会在 1933 年 9 月讨论的，此前布朗先生和德里斯科尔先生已就此事项进行过商谈。
塞莱特博士：德里斯科尔先生要求你将这些股份转移至保管状态吗？

布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：你是怎么回答的？
布朗先生：我告诉德里斯科尔先生，R. T. Co. 的密码账户必须先补足适当的保证金，然后才能采取任何行动。
塞莱特博士：你是否向他暗示，将本杰明先生的股份转移至保管状态会造成不便？
布朗先生：没有，我关心的是让这些密码账户补足适当的保证金。

巨额借方余额
塞莱特博士：其中一个账户，R. T. Co. 101-I.1，即雷文先生的账户——在 1933 年整个夏季，该账户的借方余额是否达到或超过 100,000 美元？当崩盘后其中所有证券被售出时，仍剩下 116,000 美元的借方余额——这正确吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：你知道该账户在 1933 年严重保证金不足吗？
布朗先生：知道。
塞莱特博士：你做了哪些努力以使雷文先生的账户保证金充足？
布朗先生：我与德里斯科尔先生讨论了此事。

为何不直接沟通
塞莱特博士：你与雷文先生的关系难道不足以让你直接将如此重要的事项向他提出吗？
布朗先生：这个账户以及其他密码账户都是雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的账户。我找的是雷文信托公司，因此是与德里斯科尔先生交谈。
塞莱特博士：你难道没有以任何方式向雷文先生提及此事吗？
布朗先生：提过。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生怎么说？
布朗先生：他说他会与德里斯科尔先生讨论此事。

下午庭审
似乎并未因上午严厉的质询 session（环节）而疲惫，塞莱特博士在下午继续出示各种与股份存入保管状态有关的文件。
他出示了一封来自德里斯科尔先生的信，信中提及莫里斯·本杰明先生的股份，部分内容为：“如果此时转移这些股份对你而言不便，”他询问证人是否想到使用这种表述的任何原因。证人回答说他想不出任何原因。
塞莱特博士：也许我可以提示一个原因。你需要支付相当于证券价值四分之三的现金，才能将其从保证金账户中取出。你不认为这就是他使用这种表述的原因吗？——不认为。
这难道不是一个重要的考量因素吗？——我们可以做到。

考虑 A.-O.F.C.
就会议记录中被“决定一点一点留出股份，以便在本杰明先生返回上海时大部分股份已被转移”这一条目进行质询时，布朗先生说，他拒绝放行这些股份，因为 R. T. Co. 账户保证金不足，他坚持要求提供更多担保。他否认知道会议记录中提及本杰明先生返回有任何理由，但最后表示他可能与执行委员会其他成员的观点不同。他是在维护 A.-O.F.C. 的利益。
他们是受到股份属于本杰明先生、而不属于金融公司这一事实的影响，而你当时考虑的是 A.-O.F.C.？——他们持相反立场。
即属于本杰明先生的财产应放入保管状态？——是的。
谈到 R. T. Co. 账户的事项。在公司开业至关闭期间，这些账户的借方余额普遍增加，这难道不是事实吗？——证人承认确有此事。
查看那次会议的记录、将本杰明股份转让给 E. A. Pierce 的信函、以及德里斯科尔关于此事的信函——你仍然坚持说你只是以此作为杠杆来获取更多保证金吗？——是的。
你对“不便”一词没有任何解释，对本杰明先生返回上海的提及也没有任何解释？——没有。
那你自己的账户呢？

page_data.en:
In the summer of 1933 until January, 1934. Was there an improvement in the general condition?—I don't recall.

Brown's Losses
Dr. Sellett then produced records which showed that the account of witness had gone from a debit balance of U.S. $21,000 in June, 1933, to a debit balance of U.S. $70,000 in January, 1934.
And that was the period during which you were objecting to the transfer of the Benjamin shares into safekeeping. Do you still want us to understand that you are giving a full and frank statement? —Yes.
And it was easy to fulfill the margin requirements of E. A. Pierce?—Most of the time.
And you actually had more than the amount of your paid-up capital invested in shares of the Raven Group?—I don't think so.
Dr. Sellett then referred to a letter written by Mr. Brown to Mr. Price in New York in which he said, in part, that "we have borrowed to the limit with local banks and Kleffel refuses to grant more loans. We are carrying the Raven accounts for over a million dollars."
Transferring his interest then to the account called 106-1.-7. which he called a "queer creature" which was consistently dealt with as though the debit balance it showed was an asset of the A-O.F.C., Dr. Sellett asked why it came into being. Witness said it was the trading account and the error account.
Why didn't you carry it just as the A.-O.F.C. trading account?— It was one of Mr. Price's ideas. He suggested that we do it.

Manipulation Seen
And if it had been incorporated in the balance sheet as it should have, it would have showed, instead of an asset of U. S. $117,-000, a debit of U. S. $204,000 when the value of the securities had been allowed for?—Yes.
And the balance sheet would have showed a loss instead of a profit?—Unless we took it out of reserves.
In order to show a profit you had to write your reserves down? —We wrote them down because of investments.
Yes, your investments were depreciating. It would have been written out of reserves rather than to show a loss. That was the policy of the company, wasn't it?—Witness did not answer.
Wasn't the matter of public confidence an important thing when you made up the balance sheet?—We wanted to show as good a sheet as we could.
Out of an admission that the code account was of no assistance to the A.-O.F.C. in dealing, Dr. Settlett proceeded to ask whether or not the auditor might not have been thus induced to believe that the account was a bona-fide client's trust account. Witness said he didn't think so, that they could have asked him.
Did they in fact ever ask you about the R. T. Co. accounts?— No.
Suppose they had asked what R. T. Co. 106-1-7 was in the spring of 1935?—I would have told them.
Do you think the auditor would have permitted it to be set up as an asset of the Finance Company? —I don't know.
Do you think that any auditor worthy of confidence would have permitted it?—There was no answer from witness.
Don't you recall the auditors asking about the accounts and being told they were clients of the Raven Trust?—No.
If I recall your testimony correctly you said that your account had been transferred to Mrs. Brown's name because the auditors objected to a director having an account. What did the auditors say to you on this occasion?— They wanted me to pay it off or to make some other disposal of it.

Put In Wife's Name
And you transferred it to her name in early 1935 prior to the certifying of the balance sheet for 1934?—Yes.
Did you discuss this with Mr. Raven?—I think so. I discussed with him the matter of a loan from the bank to pay it off. I made a loan of $20,000. I may have talked the other matter over with him, but I can't remember.
As manager of the A.-O.F.C. you transferred an account of U. S. $48,000 without the knowledge, approval or consent of Mr. Raven?—Did you inform him of this at any time?—I think I did.
Did you remain responsible for the account?—I think I signed the signature card.
Was the $20,000 from the A.-O.B.C. ever actually paid into the account?—I made the loan with Mr. Walter Raven and later it was recalled.
Why?—Because I could not supply the security I thought I could get.
Turning to the Haley account, in which mention was made of the "dangerous position" with regard to fully-paid shares kept in the margin account, which stated "we are wide open to legal procedure if such a position should come about," Dr. Sellett asked witness whom he had discussed this report with. He said he might have talked it over with Mr. Rosse, but he did not remember that he took any particular stand on the matter.
Did you discuss it with anyone else?—I don't recall any direct conversation with anyone.
Didn't it occur to you to take it up with Mr. Driscoll in the same way you did previously with Mr. Price?—I may have mentioned it to him.
Cross-examination of Mr. Brown is expected to continue as court resumes to-day and it is probable that Mr. Raven will take the stand in the afternoon.

从1933年夏季直到1934年1月。总体状况是否有改善？——我不记得了。

布朗的损失
塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）随后出示了记录，显示证人的账户从1933年6月的借方余额21,000美元，变为1934年1月的借方余额70,000美元。
而那段时期正是你反对将本杰明（Benjamin）的股份转入保管的时期。你是否仍希望我们要理解为你正在作出全面且坦率的陈述？——是的。
那么，满足E. A. Pierce公司的保证金要求很容易吗？——大多数时候是这样。
而且你实际投入雷文集团（Raven Group）股份的资金超过了你的实缴资本额？——我不这么认为。
塞莱特博士随后引用了布朗先生写给纽约普赖斯先生（Mr. Price）的一封信，信中部分内容为：“我们已向本地银行借款至极限，而克莱费尔（Kleffel）拒绝提供更多贷款。我们持有的雷文账户金额超过一百万美元。”
随后将其权益转入名为106-1.-7的账户，他称该账户为“怪胎”，并且一直将其显示的借方余额当作A-O.F.C.（亚细亚-东方金融公司）的资产来处理，塞莱特博士询问该账户产生的原因。证人称这是交易账户和差错账户。
你为什么不直接将其作为A.-O.F.C.的交易账户处理？——这是普赖斯先生的主意之一。是他建议我们这样做的。

可见的操纵
如果它像应当做的那样被纳入资产负债表，在计入证券价值后，它将显示为204,000美元的借方余额，而不是117,000美元的资产，对吗？——是的。
那么资产负债表将显示亏损而不是盈利？——除非我们从准备金中扣除。
为了显示盈利，你们必须调减准备金？——我们因投资原因调减了准备金。
是的，你们的投资在贬值。这会被从准备金中注销，而不是显示亏损。这是公司的政策，不是吗？——证人未作回答。
在编制资产负债表时，公众信心难道不是重要因素吗？——我们希望尽可能展示一份好看的报表。
鉴于承认代码账户对A.-O.F.C.的交易毫无帮助，塞莱特博士接着询问，审计师是否因此可能被诱导相信该账户是真实的客户信托账户。证人表示他不这么认为，因为他们本可以问他。
他们实际上曾问过你关于R. T. Co.（音译）账户的事吗？——没有。
假设他们在1935年春季询问R. T. Co. 106-1-7是什么，你会怎么做？——我会告诉他们。
你认为审计师会允许其作为金融公司的资产列示吗？——我不知道。
你认为任何值得信赖的审计师会允许这样做吗？——证人没有回答。
你不记得审计师曾询问这些账户，并被告知它们是雷文信托（Raven Trust）的客户吗？——不记得。
如果我没记错你的证词，你曾说你的账户已转入布朗夫人名下，因为审计师反对董事持有账户。当时审计师对你说了什么？——他们希望我清偿该账户，或对其作其他处置。

转入妻子名下
那么在1934年资产负债表认证之前，你在1935年初将其转到了她名下？——是的。
你与雷文先生讨论过此事吗？——我想是的。我与他讨论了从银行贷款以清偿该账户的事宜。我贷了一笔20,000美元的款项。我可能也与他商量过另一件事，但我记不清了。
作为A.-O.F.C.的经理，你在雷文先生不知情、未批准或未同意的情况下，转移了一个48,000美元的账户？——你曾在任何时候通知过他吗？——我想我通知过。
你仍对该账户负责吗？——我想我在签名卡上签了字。
来自A.-O.B.C.（音译）的20,000美元是否实际存入该账户？——我与沃尔特·雷文先生（Mr. Walter Raven）办理了这笔贷款，后来又被收回。
为什么？——因为我无法提供我认为能获得的担保。
转向海利（Haley）账户，其中提到了关于全额付款股份保留在保证金账户中的“危险处境”，并称“如果出现这种情况，我们将完全面临法律诉讼”，塞莱特博士询问证人与谁讨论过这份报告。他说他可能已与罗斯先生（Mr. Rosse）商讨过，但他不记得自己在此事上采取了任何特定立场。
你还与其他人讨论过吗？——我不记得与任何人有过直接交谈。
你难道没想到像之前对待普赖斯先生那样，向德里斯科尔先生（Mr. Driscoll）提出此事吗？——我可能向他提过。
预计对布朗先生的交叉讯问将在今天法庭复庭后继续，雷文先生很可能在下午出庭作证。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JANUARY 26, 1936 13198

Mr. Brown Admits That
Raven Company Engaged
In "Bucketing" Deals

Dr. Sellett Relentlessly Questions Defendant On
A.-O.F.C. Practice Of Dealing In Fully-Paid
Shares Belonging To Customers Of Concern

EVIDENCE FOR DEFENCE STARTS AFTER U.S.
COURT DENIES MOTION TO DISMISS CASE

An admission that the American-Oriental Finance Corporation had been engaged in "bucketing" operations in connection with the handling of customers' fully-paid securities was made by Mr. J. Warner Brown in the United States Court for China yesterday morning under cross-examination by Dr. George Sellett, U. S. District Attorney, who is conducting the prosecution of Mr. Brown and Mr. Frank J. Raven on 16 counts of theft, embezzlement and fraud in connection with the collapse of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and kindred enterprises in May of last year.

The cross-examination of Mr. Brown was continued from Friday, when the defendant first took the witness-stand in his own defence and was confined to the methods of the A.-O.F.C. in the handling of customers' securities which had been paid for in full.

Pursuing his questioning with relentlessness and rapidity, the Assistant District Attorney started off yesterday morning by reference to the transactions which the A.-O.F.C. had with Mr. Lucien Claude Basset, one of the complaining witnesses in the case, who previously testified to the loss of his full-paid securities, amounting in value to about U.S. $50,000.

Those Signature Cards

Dr. Sellett pointed out that Mr. Basset's signature card was blank on the side provided for hypothecation consent. To which Mr. Brown replied that salesmen had instructions to get both sides of the cards signed.

Dr. Sellett: But some clients paid in full for their shares?

Mr. Brown: Every account was regarded as a trading account. I did not know Mr. Basset's card was not signed on both sides. I insisted that all clients sign the hypothecation consent. That was the rule of the corporation.

Dr. Sellett: Suppose Mr. Basset had refused to sign this consent—would you have told him to take his account out?

Mr. Brown: Likely.

Dr. Sellett: There were some 25 to 50 signature cards with the hypothecation consent not signed —were you aware of that?

Mr. Brown: I was not. I hadn't reviewed them for a year or more.

Prosecuting counsel then asked if E. A. Pierce and Company also demanded that clients who bought fully-paid shares sign a hypothecation consent. Mr. Brown said that they did.

Would Terminate Account

Dr. Sellett: Would you have terminated the Basset account if you had found out that the hypothecation consent was unsigned?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: You would have taken all his shares out of the margin account with Pierce and Company, paying three-fourths of their value to get them out, and turned them over to him, besides paying him his credit balance of U.S. $5,000?

Mr. Brown said he would.

In the case of the transaction with Major Howard, another of the complaining witnesses who paid for his shares in full and did not sign a hypothecation consent, Mr. Brown said that the fact that Major Howard had given a draft in payment was "all the more reason" why the consent should have been signed.

Dr. Sellett: That draft was drawn by the Shanghai branch of the National City Bank of New York on the New York office of that bank, in favour of the A.-O.F.C. Were you afraid the bank would fold up before the draft could be cashed?

Mr. Brown: It represented an outstanding obligation for 30 days.

Same In Other Cases

In further testimony, Mr. Brown told the Court that he would have told the other complaining witnesses in the case, Messrs. Kirkland, Yates and Brown, to take out their accounts if he had known that they had not signed hypothecation consents. Where these consents had been crossed out on signature cards, it was done without his knowledge or authority. He did not know it had been done until he came to court.

In turning again to the Basset transactions, witness told Dr. Sellett that there was good reason for demanding a hypothecation consent in this case because the client gave no money with his first order.

Dr. Sellett: But what greater protection was there for the A.-O.F.C. if he had signed it—your risk was the same in either case?

Brokerage House Procedure

Mr. Brown: It was brokerage house procedure.

Dr. Sellett: I am aware of that, but a lot of brokerage house procedure was unfortunately not inherited by the A.-O.F.C. And you don't in any case appear to be familiar with that procedure.

On objection by the defence, the last part of Dr. Sellett's statement was ordered stricken from the record.

Prosecuting counsel then selected from the Government exhibits in the case a series of advices and statements sent to Mr. Basset advising this client that the A.-O.F.C. had "on hand" for him 300 A. T. & T. shares and 100 Western Union shares. These were handed to Mr. Brown.

Dr. Sellett: What did you intend Mr. Basset to understand by these statements?

Mr. Evans objected, but Dr. Sellett said his purpose was to show criminal intent, and the objection was overruled. Mr. Brown answered the question by saying that it was intended to convey to Mr. Basset that he was "long" on the shares.

Dr. Sellett: Did you not intend to convey to him that the shares were fully paid for?

Mr. Brown: I don't think so.

Would Not Mislead

Dr. Sellett: Then do you not think that he might have been misled by these statements?

Mr. Brown (after a lengthy pause): The statements only showed that these shares were available for him.

Dr. Sellett: Had he no right to infer that the shares were held for him, free and unencumbered?

Mr. Brown: The statements don't say so. The shares were available to him when he wanted them.

Dr. Sellett: If the A.-O.F.C. had no A. T. & T. or Western Union shares, were the statements still correct?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

"Bucketing" Operations

Dr. Sellett then turned to practices which he described as "bucketing" operations, and drew from the witness admissions that it was the A.-O.F.C.'s practice, to sell out a "long" client in order to effect a short sale.

Prosecuting counsel then posed a hypothetical case. "Suppose," he said, "Client A buys 100 shares of General Motors, paying for them in full. The A.-O.F.C. places the shares in the margin account with Pierce and Company. Later, Client B comes in and places an order for the short sale of 100 General Motors. Would you sell out Client A in order to fill the order of Client B?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: Suppose Client A comes in and asks for his shares?

Mr. Brown: Then we have to go out and buy them.

Dr. Sellett: Do you tell Client A that that is what you would have to do?

Balance Each Other

Mr. Brown finally answered by saying that the two transactions, Client A and Client B; "balanced each other."

Continuing with his hypothetical example, Dr. Sellett said: "Let us suppose that you bought Client A's 100 General Motors at 25. The market rises. When you have to deliver the shares to Client A, the price is no longer 25, but 50. That will mean that the A.-O.F.C. has lost $2,500. Are my mathematics correct?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: So that result is that the A.-O.F.C. has speculated and lost $2,500, less any commissions which it may have made on the Client A and B transactions?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

Knows About "Bucketing"

Dr. Sellett: Do you know what "bucketing" is? Ever heard of it?

Mr. Brown: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: The transaction we have just described—do you know that that is "bucketing?"

《上海星期时报》，1936年1月26日 13198

布朗先生承认
雷文公司从事
“对赌”交易

塞莱特博士就美亚金融公司处理客户全额付清股份的做法
 relentlessly（毫不留情地）讯问被告

在美国法院驳回撤销案件动议后，辩方开始举证

昨天上午，在中国美国法院，J. 华纳·布朗先生在美方地区检察官乔治·塞莱特博士的交叉讯问下承认，美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）在处理客户已全额付清的证券时曾从事“对赌”（bucketing）操作。塞莱特博士正在就去年五月美亚金融公司及相关企业倒闭一事，以16项盗窃、挪用和欺诈罪名起诉布朗先生和弗兰克·J. 雷文先生。

对布朗先生的交叉讯问自周五继续进行，当时被告首次出庭为自己辩护，讯问内容局限于美亚金融公司处理客户已全额付清证券的方法。

助理地区检察官昨天上午以毫不留情且迅速的方式继续提问，他首先提及美亚金融公司与吕西安·克劳德·巴塞特先生（Lucien Claude Basset）进行的交易。巴塞特先生是本案的控方证人之一，此前曾作证称其损失了价值约5万美元的全额付清证券。

那些签名卡

塞莱特博士指出，巴塞特先生的签名卡在用于抵押同意的一侧是空白的。对此，布朗先生回答说，销售人员接到的指示是让客户签署卡片的两面。

塞莱特博士：但有些客户是全额支付他们的股份的？

布朗先生：每个账户都被视为交易账户。我不知道巴塞特先生的卡片两面都没有签字。我坚持要求所有客户签署抵押同意书。这是公司的规定。

塞莱特博士：假设巴塞特先生拒绝签署这份同意书——你会让他销户吗？

布朗先生：很可能。

塞莱特博士：大约有25到50张签名卡上的抵押同意书未签署——你知道这件事吗？

布朗先生：我不知道。我已经有一年多没有审查它们了。

随后，公诉律师询问E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company）是否也要求购买全额付清股份的客户签署抵押同意书。布朗先生说他们确实如此。

将终止账户

塞莱特博士：如果你发现抵押同意书未签署，你会终止巴塞特的账户吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：你会把他所有的股份从皮尔斯公司的保证金账户中取出，支付其价值的四分之三以将其取出，并交还给他，此外还支付他5,000美元的贷方余额吗？

布朗先生表示他会这样做。

在涉及另一位控方证人霍华德少校（Major Howard）的交易案例中，霍华德少校全额支付了股份款项且未签署抵押同意书，布朗先生表示，霍华德少校开具汇票付款这一事实更是“理应”签署同意书的理由。

塞莱特博士：那张汇票是由纽约花旗银行（National City Bank of New York）上海分行开给该银行纽约办事处的，收款人为美亚金融公司。你是担心在汇票兑现之前银行会倒闭吗？

布朗先生：它代表了一笔为期30天的未偿债务。

其他案件亦然

在进一步的证词中，布朗先生告诉法庭，如果他早知道其他控方证人柯克兰先生、耶茨先生和布朗先生未签署抵押同意书，他也会让他们销户。至于签名卡上被划掉的同意书，是在他不知情或未经授权的情况下进行的。直到出庭受审，他才知道此事。

当再次回到巴塞特的交易时，证人告诉塞莱特博士，在此案中要求签署抵押同意书是有充分理由的，因为该客户在下第一笔订单时并未支付任何资金。

塞莱特博士：但如果他签署了同意书，对美亚金融公司有什么更大的保护呢？——在这两种情况下，你的风险是一样的？

经纪行程序

布朗先生：这是经纪行的惯例。

塞莱特博士：我知道这一点，但不幸的是，美亚金融公司并没有继承许多经纪行的惯例。而且无论如何，你似乎并不熟悉那套程序。

经辩方反对，法官命令将塞莱特博士陈述的最后一部分从记录中删除。

随后，公诉律师从本案的政府证物中挑选了一系列发送给巴塞特先生的通知和对账单，告知该客户美亚金融公司为他“持有”300股美国电话电报公司（A. T. & T.）股票和100股西联汇款公司（Western Union）股票。这些文件被递交给布朗先生。

塞莱特博士：你打算让巴塞特先生通过这些对账单理解什么？

埃文斯先生提出反对，但塞莱特博士表示其目的是展示犯罪意图，反对被驳回。布朗先生回答问题时说，其意图是让巴塞特先生明白他在这些股票上是“做多”（long）的。

塞莱特博士：你难道不打算让他明白这些股票是全额付清的吗？

布朗先生：我不这么认为。

不会误导

塞莱特博士：那么你不认为他可能会被这些对账单误导吗？

布朗先生（停顿良久）：这些对账单只显示这些股票可供他使用。

塞莱特博士：他难道没有权利推断这些股票是为他持有的，且无留置权和无负担吗？

布朗先生：对账单上没有这么说。当他需要时，这些股票可供他使用。

塞莱特博士：如果美亚金融公司根本没有美国电话电报公司或西联汇款公司的股票，这些对账单仍然正确吗？

布朗先生：是的。

“对赌”操作

随后，塞莱特博士转向他称为“对赌”（bucketing）操作的做法，并从证人处引出供认，即美亚金融公司的做法是，为了进行卖空交易而平仓一位“做多”的客户。

公诉律师随后提出了一个假设案例。“假设，”他说，“客户A购买100股通用汽车公司股票，并全额付款。美亚金融公司将这些股票放入皮尔斯公司的保证金账户。后来，客户B进来下达卖空100股通用汽车股票的订单。你会平仓客户A以履行客户B的订单吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：假设客户A进来要求提取他的股票？

布朗先生：那我们就得出去买入它们。

塞莱特博士：你会告诉客户A你必须这样做吗？

相互抵消

布朗先生最后回答说，这两笔交易，即客户A和客户B的交易，“相互抵消”。

塞莱特博士继续他的假设例子说：“让我们假设你以25美元的价格买入了客户A的100股通用汽车股票。市场上涨。当你必须向客户A交付股票时，价格不再是25美元，而是50美元。这意味着美亚金融公司损失了2,500美元。我的计算正确吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：所以结果是，美亚金融公司进行了投机并损失了2,500美元，减去其在客户A和B交易中可能获得的任何佣金？

布朗先生：是的。

知晓“对赌”

塞莱特博士：你知道什么是“对赌”吗？听说过吗？

布朗先生：是的。

塞莱特博士：我们刚才描述的那笔交易——你知道那就是“对赌”吗？

Mr. Brown: Not when it is through Pierce and Company—through a brokerage house.
Dr. Sellett: If the A.-O.F.C. had handled these transactions as they should have done, they could not have made or lost anything by fluctuations in the market as far as customers' fully-paid securities were concerned. These would have been in safekeeping. But the A.-O.F.C. took a position against its clients and stood to win or lose by fluctuations in the value of the securities. Is that not the case?
Mr. Brown (after a long pause): Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Of course! It's as simple as A.B.C. And that is the way the so-called "short sales" were made.
Mr. Brown: We had very few short sales.
Dr. Sellett: Yes, but such as you had were handled in that way.

What Basset Believed
Reverting again to the Basset shares, Dr. Sellett asked Mr. Brown whether Mr. Basset, after receiving several statements from the A.-O.F.C. showing that his shares were "on hand," was not entitled, as a reasonably intelligent man with business experience, to believe that the A.-O.F.C. actually had the stated number of shares "on hand" for him. "He might be mistaken, but he would logically believe that?" counsel queried.
Mr. Brown: They were available to him if he wanted to get them.
Dr. Sellett: Would he not believe that they were actually in New York, in the hands of Pierce and Company, who supposedly held them for him through the A.-O.F.C.?
Mr. Brown: I don't know what he believed." (Laughter among the audience).
Dr. Sellett: What would you have believed in his position?
Judge Helmick then intervened. "Do you care what he would have believed?" he asked. The Court then adjourned to Monday at 10 a.m.

Friday's Proceedings.
In view of the protracted nature of the case, which has already entered its fourth week, and the desire of both the prosecution and the defence to hurry it on as much as possible, the Court took the unprecedented step of sitting on Friday, the opening day of the Chinese New Year. The entire day was devoted to the testimony of Mr. J. Warner Brown, who took the witness-stand in his own defence, and his cross-examination by Dr. George Sellett, Assistant District Attorney.
Shortly after the opening of the session, and after stipulations of formal evidence regarding the liquidation of the Raven concerns had been entered in the record, Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Warner Brown, submitted a motion for the dismissal of the case against both of the defendants, advancing four grounds in favour thereof.

Motion To Dismiss
First of all, counsel submitted, there was no evidence submitted by the Government which showed larceny. Secondly, the evidence led, after making every fair inference in favour of the government, did not show that either money or goods had been obtained by the defendants by false pretences. Thirdly, the evidence, allowing every fair inference in favour of the Government, did not show that there had been any conversion by the defendants either of money or shares which would sustain the charge of embezzlement. Fourthly and finally, there was no evidence of felonious or criminal intent.

Replying briefly, Dr. Sellett read correspondence which had passed between the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and a Mr. M. S. Chen, who had testified for the prosecution as to certain supposed safekeeping share transactions which he had with the corporation. He then proceeded to analyze some of the evidence for the prosecution and to quote authoritative cases in rebuttal of the contentions of the defence.
Each defendant was not guilty of every count in the indictment, Dr. Sellett said. "But," he continued, "when there is intent from the very beginning to appropriate property, then it becomes larceny. What happened to the property after the defendants laid their hands upon it is just exactly what they intended to happen to it. This is larceny by trick.

Words Unnecessary
"No words, written or spoken, are needed to lay the basis for false pretence. The defendants did not have to tell Mr. Basset, for example, that his shares were safe. Does anyone suppose that Mr. Basset would have parted with his money if he had known what was happening. The evidence is overwhelming of continued embezzlement in the Basset transactions.
"With regard to the Howard case, the Government is aware that the defendants were not in Shanghai. But from at least May 13, 1930, both defendants knew that all business with these complaining witnesses would be carried on as it was in fact carried on. It does not matter whether they were in the United States or Timbuctoo; they knew their subordinates would carry on according to design.

Evidence Said Conclusive
"I submit," Dr. Sellett concluded, "that the Court has no alternative but to overrule the motion. The evidence is conclusive and overwhelming."
Judge Helmick: In face of the Chen testimony, the motion to dismiss is overruled. The defence may now present their case.

Mr. John Warner Brown, co-defendant of Mr. Frank J. Raven, then took the witness-stand.
Replying to his counsel, Mr. C. S. Franklin, he said that he was an American citizen, 46 years of age, and had considerable experience in American banking institutions. He came to China in the latter part of 1918 to audit the books of the Presbyterian Mission in South China. He continued with the Mission until 1923 and then joined the American - Oriental Banking Corporation. He was married in 1914 and had three children. His wife was now in California.

Requested By Raven
It was at the request of Mr. Raven that he joined the A.-O.F.C., his first post being that of assistant manager. In 1926, he became manager of the Tientsin branch of the bank. He went on home leave in 1930 and upon his return in September of that year joined the A.-O.F.C. at Mr. Raven's request.

Mr. Brown said he never been an officer or director of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the Raven Trust Company or the Asia Realty Company..
When he joined the A.-O.F.C. in 1930, he became a director and vice-president. At that time he had had no experience of finance company work, nor experience of trading in New York securities or commodities. While on home leave in 1930, however, he spent two weeks in the offices of E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco, studying these classes of business in relation to share dealings, both "margin" and fully-paid. He went through the various departments under the guidance of Mr. Wood and Mr. Curtis, officials of E. A. Pierce and Company.

Mr. Price Advises
"In 1930," witness continued, "Mr. Price was secretary and legal advisor to the A.-O.F.C. with Mr. Frank J. Hill as his assistant. Mr. Price passed on all forms, including signature cards, from a legal standpoint. I discussed with him procedure in regard to fully-paid shares. I also talked to Mr. Hill and Mr. Raven on the same subject. Mr. Price told me it was quite legal for us to carry fully-paid shares in our margin account with Pierce and Company as we were not subject to the rules of the New York Stock Exchange, and provided we kept our financial position so that we could meet any demand made on us for delivery of shares."
Mr. Franklin: Did Mr. Price give any reasons for that procedure?
Mr. Brown: Yes, he said it was a different matter with Pierce and Company, because they were members of the New York Stock Exchange while the A.-O.F.C. was not. The A.-O.F.C. was therefore not bound by the same procedure. He also referred to the cost of transferring shares in and out of safekeeping daily, which he said would be prohibitive on account of cables.
Mr. Franklin: Did you consider the possibility of placing securities in safe-keeping by means of letters to Pierce and Company, instead of by cabling?

Safekeeping Unnecessary
Mr. Brown: Yes, I discussed that with Mr. Price. He said it would not be necessary so long as we maintained a cash position and were able to deliver shares on demand.
Mr. Franklin then asked the witness whether he also had an account with the A.-O.F.C. Witness said that he did, under his own name.
"Why did you transfer that account into your wife's name?" counsel queried.
Mr. Brown: Because the auditor said he didn't want a director of the corporation to have an account on the books.
Questioned regarding the extensive "short" sales in April and May, 1935, just before the Raven concerns crashed, and which were the subject of considerable testimony by witnesses for the prosecution, Mr. Brown said the question of making these sales through the cipher accounts 160-L7 and 101-I1, the first of which was the A.-O.F.C.'s account with itself and the second the account of Mr. Raven, came up for discussion in April. Several officials felt that the market was well down and favoured making short sales. He (Mr. Brown) was opposed because he thought the market was due for a rise, which was what actually happened in May.

布朗先生：如果是通过皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）——即通过一家经纪行办理，那就不是这样。
塞莱特博士：如果美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）按照应有的方式处理这些交易，就客户的全额付款证券而言，他们本不会因市场波动而获利或受损。这些证券本应处于保管状态。但是，美亚金融公司采取了与其客户对立的头寸，并因证券价值的波动而面临盈亏。难道事实并非如此吗？
布朗先生（长时间停顿后）：是的。
塞莱特博士：当然！这就像ABC一样简单。所谓的“卖空”就是这样进行的。
布朗先生：我们的卖空交易很少。
塞莱特博士：是的，但你们所做的那些就是按这种方式处理的。

巴塞特相信什么
再次回到巴塞特股票的问题上，塞莱特博士询问布朗先生，巴塞特先生在收到美亚金融公司发出的几份对账单、显示其股票“在手”之后，作为一个具备商业经验的理智之人，难道无权相信美亚金融公司确实为他“持有”所述数量的股票吗？“他可能会弄错，但从逻辑上讲他会相信这一点，是吗？”辩护律师问道。
布朗先生：如果他想提取，这些股票是可以提供给他的。
塞莱特博士：他难道不会相信这些股票实际上在纽约，由皮尔斯公司持有，而皮尔斯公司据称是通过美亚金融公司代他持有的吗？
布朗先生：我不知道他相信什么。”（听众中传来笑声）。
塞莱特博士：处在他的位置，你会相信什么？
赫尔米克法官随即介入。“你在乎他会相信什么吗？”他问道。法庭随后休庭，至周一上午10时继续开庭。

周五的庭审程序。
鉴于本案历时漫长，已进入第四周，且控辩双方均希望尽可能加快审理进度，法庭采取了前所未有的举措，在中国农历新年的第一天（周五）开庭。全天时间均用于听取J·华纳·布朗先生的证词，他作为被告之一出庭为自己辩护，并接受助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特博士的交叉质询。
庭审开始后不久，在将有关雷文（Raven）相关企业清算的形式证据录入记录之后，华纳·布朗先生的代理律师理查德·T·埃文斯先生提出动议，要求驳回针对两名被告的案件，并提出了四项支持理由。

驳回动议
首先，辩护律师提出，政府方未提交任何显示存在盗窃行为的证据。其次，即使作出所有有利于政府的合理推断，现有证据也未显示被告通过虚假借口获取了任何金钱或货物。第三，即使作出所有有利于政府的合理推断，现有证据也未显示被告对任何金钱或股票进行了挪用，从而足以支持侵占罪的指控。第四也是最后一点，没有任何证据证明存在重罪意图或犯罪意图。

塞莱特博士简要回应，宣读了美亚金融公司与M·S·陈先生之间的往来信函，陈先生曾作为控方证人作证，提及他与该公司进行的某些所谓保管股票交易。随后，他开始分析控方的一些证据，并引用权威案例以反驳辩护方的主张。
塞莱特博士说，每名被告并非对起诉书中的每一项罪名都有罪。“但是，”他继续说道，“如果从一开始就有占有财产的意图，那就构成了盗窃。被告得手后财产遭遇的情况，恰恰就是他们意图让其发生的情况。这是通过欺诈手段实施的盗窃。

无需言语
“无需书面或口头的言辞即可奠定虚假借口的基础。例如，被告不必告诉巴塞特先生他的股票是安全的。如果有人认为，假如巴塞特先生知道实情还会交出他的钱，那才是荒谬的。在巴塞特交易中，持续存在侵占行为的证据是压倒性的。
“关于霍华德一案，政府方面知晓被告当时不在上海。但至少从1930年5月13日起，两名被告都知道，与这些投诉证人的所有业务都将按照实际进行的方式开展。无论他们是在美国还是在廷巴克图（Timbuctoo），都无关紧要；他们知道其下属会按照既定计划行事。

证据据称确凿无疑
“我提请法庭注意，”塞莱特博士总结道，“法庭别无选择，只能驳回该动议。证据确凿且具压倒性。”
赫尔米克法官：鉴于陈先生的证词，驳回动议被驳回。辩护方现在可以陈述其案情。

弗兰克·J·雷文先生的共同被告约翰·华纳·布朗先生随后出庭作证。
在回答其辩护律师C·S·富兰克林先生的提问时，他表示自己是美国公民，现年46岁，在美国银行机构拥有丰富经验。他于1918年末来到中国，审计华南长老会传教团的账目。他在该传教团工作至1923年，随后加入美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）。他于1914年结婚，育有三名子女。其妻子目前居住在加利福尼亚州。

应雷文之邀
他是应雷文先生的邀请加入美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）的，最初担任副经理一职。1926年，他成为该银行天津分行的经理。1930年他回国休假，同年9月返回后，应雷文先生之邀加入美亚金融公司。

布朗先生表示，他从未担任过美亚银行公司、雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）或亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）的高级职员或董事。
当他于1930年加入美亚金融公司时，他成为了董事兼副总裁。当时，他没有金融公司工作的经验，也没有在纽约进行证券或商品交易的经验。然而，在1930年回国休假期间，他在旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company）办公室度过了两周时间，研究与股票交易相关的此类业务，包括“保证金”交易和全额付款交易。他在E. A. 皮尔斯公司官员伍德先生和柯蒂斯先生的指导下，参观了各个部门。

普莱斯先生的建议
证人继续说道：“1930年，普莱斯先生担任美亚金融公司的秘书兼法律顾问，弗兰克·J·希尔先生是他的助手。普莱斯先生从法律角度审批所有表格，包括签名卡。我曾与他讨论过关于全额付款股票的操作程序。我也就同一主题与希尔先生和雷文先生进行过交谈。普莱斯先生告诉我，我们将全额付款股票存放在我们在皮尔斯公司的保证金账户中是完全合法的，因为我们不受纽约证券交易所规则的约束，前提是我们保持财务状况，能够满足任何要求交付股票的需求。”
富兰克林先生：普莱斯先生是否给出了采取该程序的理由？
布朗先生：是的，他说对于皮尔斯公司而言情况不同，因为他们是纽约证券交易所的成员，而美亚金融公司不是。因此，美亚金融公司不受相同程序的约束。他还提到了每天将股票转入和转出保管状态的成本，他说由于电报费用，这一成本将是高得令人望而却步的。
富兰克林先生：你是否考虑过通过致函皮尔斯公司而非发电报的方式来存放证券进行保管？

无需保管
布朗先生：是的，我与普莱斯先生讨论过此事。他说，只要我们保持现金头寸并能够按需交付股票，就没有必要这样做。
富兰克林先生随后询问证人是否在美亚金融公司也有账户。证人表示他有，是以他自己的名义开设的。
“你为什么将该账户转入你妻子的名下？”辩护律师问道。
布朗先生：因为审计师表示他不希望公司董事在账簿上拥有账户。
当被问及1935年4月和5月，即在雷文相关企业崩溃前夕进行的大规模“卖空”交易（控方证人对此提供了大量证词）时，布朗先生表示，关于通过密码账户160-L7和101-I1进行这些销售的问题曾在4月份进行过讨论，其中第一个账户是美亚金融公司与其自身的账户，第二个是雷文先生的账户。几位官员认为市场已大幅下跌，倾向于进行卖空交易。他（布朗先生）持反对意见，因为他认为市场即将反弹，而实际情况也确实如他在5月份所预料的那样发生了。

No Cash Needed
Mr. Franklin: Did you consider at that time that the A.-O.F.C. was in need of cash?
Witness: I did not.
Mr. Brown added that neither, in his opinion, did the American-Oriental Banking Corporation need cash. He knew that money was "tight," but not more so than during the preceding six months.
Replying to further questions, Mr. Brown told the Court that he left Shanghai for Manila on May 7, 1935, and had no idea at that time that the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was in a precarious condition.
"When I was told by Mr. Cook in the Manila office that a wire had been received from Mr. C. V. Starr, stating that the Raven concerns had closed down, my first words were that it was not true.

Sellett Cross-Examines
Dr. Sellett then rose to cross-examine the witness and questioned him closely about the knowledge which he had gained regarding the handling of fully-paid shares when he had been for two weeks in the Pierce offices in San Francisco. Counsel for the prosecution then turned to the practice of the A.-O.F.C. in the handling of customers' fully-paid shares.
Dr. Sellett: Assuming I was a client of the A.-C.F.C., and had had no conversation whatsoever with you, or anyone else, as to the manner in which the A.-O.F.C. was going to handle my fully-paid shares, and I came to you and placed an order for 100 A.T. and T., and when you notified me that my order had been executed I gave you my draft in full payment of the amount of the purchase—regulations or no regulations of the New York Stock Exchange—would not you, as a business man, know that it was your duty to me to make me the owner of those shares and to keep them free and unencumbered?
Mr. Brown: It would depend upon whether you had any outstanding orders.

Dictates Of Conscience
Dr. Sellett (with vigour): I have no outstanding orders and the facts are just as I have related them to you! I have paid you every cent on those shares. Suppose you had never seen Jim Price and never had his expert legal advice—what would your own conscience tell you was the proper thing to do with that property?
Mr. Brown: Hold it for your account.
Dr. Sellett: Would your conscience permit you to take that property and hypothecate it for the account of the A..O.F.C.?
Mr. Brown: As long as I could make delivery on demand I should think it would be all right.
Dr. Sellett: You think that under the circumstances described, after I had paid in full for the shares, you would be within your rights in taking them to your bankers and saying: "Here are some shares. Lend me $5,000 on them." Do you feel you would have a right to do that?

Brown Hesitates
Mr. Brown (after long hesitation): As long as I could repay you at any time—yes.
Dr. Sellett: Suppose you are in the banking business. I come to you and say: "Here are 100 shares of A.T. and T. I wish you to keep them for me. I may want to use them one of these days, to borrow on them from your bank." Would you feel that, under those circumstances, you could take my 100 shares over to the Bank of China and borrow money on them?
Mr. Brown: I don't think that is an equitable question. I think you would have to say whether they were for safekeeping or not.
Dr. Sellett: I don't even say anything about safekeeping. I don't know that word; it is not in my vocabulary. I say: Here are my shares. Some day I might want to borrow money on them." Can you, the next day, take them to the Bank of China and borrow on them for your own bank's use?

Sees No Comparison
Mr. Brown (after a long pause): I don't think there is a comparison with this business, considering the distance from New York.
Dr. Sellett: In your business as a banker over a period of some 13 to 15 years, you had occasion to receive from time to time, from bank clients, certain property, other than money — stocks, property or bonds, etc.?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: Did you ever feel at liberty, in any of those cases, to take that property and hypothecate it for the bank's purposes?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Do you think that a different code of ethics, or morals, or whatever you want to call it, would be applicable in a brokerage concern?

Defendant Silent
Mr. Brown did not reply.
Dr. Sellett: Let us go back to San Francisco. You wrote a letter from there to Mr. Raven on May 13, 1930, stating: "I took up with Mr. Curtis the question of securities in the margin account that had been fully paid for. When that happens with Pierce, they take them out of margin and place them in safekeeping. We will arrange to do this, as the liability in this respect is considerable in case we should have such shares in our margin account and borrowed against them." Were you surprised that Pierce and Company should handle fully-paid shares in that way?
Mr. Brown: No.
Dr. Sellett: Of course not! You would know that the broker has no business hypothecating or encumbering property which belongs to clients? You would understand it in that way, even if you had never heard of the rules of the stock exchange—wouldn't you?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: So, when you learned how Pierce and Company were handling safekeeping shares, you didn't think that the only reason they set them aside was because there was some rule of the stock exchange? Your common sense told you that they had to be kept free and unencumbered?
Mr. Brown: You treat them in such a way that when delivery is called for you are able to make it.

His Mental Attitude
Dr. Sellett: Before your return to China, I submit that your mental attitude was that fully-paid shares should be kept free and unencumbered—is that not so?
Mr. Brown: Yes, that is why I wrote that letter to Mr. Raven on May 13, 1930.
Dr. Sellett: And in that letter you say not one word about the regulations of the New York Stock Exchange?
Mr. Brown: No, that is right.
Dr. Settlelt: Did you subsequently change your mind on the question of setting aside, in safekeeping, customers' fully-paid shares?
Mr. Brown: Yes, in the course of the next year. I was chiefly influenced by Mr. Price's counsel. I discussed the matter with Mr. Raven. The thing that impressed me was that the A.-O.F.C. was tremendously sound at the time and that we could make delivery of shares at any time whenever anyone came in and asked for them.

Using Others' Property
Dr. Sellett: Still, you were conscious of the fact that it was someone else's property you were dealing in?
Mr. Brown: Yes.
Answering questions concerning the shares bought and fully paid for by Mr. Lucien Claude Basset, one of the complaining witnesses in the case, Mr. Brown said he did not know that Mr. Basset's shares had been fully paid for, since only short-margined accounts were referred to him.
Dr. Sellett: Would not a proper understanding of your financial position with Pierce and Company and your obligations to your clients necessitate your having full information as to all fully-paid shares? I put this to you as a business man of long experience?
Mr. Brown: Yes.

无需现金
富兰克林先生：您当时是否认为美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）需要现金？
证人：我不这样认为。
布朗先生补充说，在他看来，美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）也不需要现金。他知道资金“紧张”，但并不比前六个月更甚。
在回答进一步的问题时，布朗先生告诉法庭，他于1935年5月7日离开上海前往马尼拉，当时他并不知道美亚银行公司处于危急状态。
“当库克先生在马尼拉办事处告诉我，收到C. V. 斯塔尔先生发来的电报，称雷文（Raven）旗下的公司已停业时，我第一句话就是那不是真的。

塞莱特进行交叉质询
塞莱特博士随后起身对证人进行交叉质询，就证人在旧金山皮尔斯（Pierce）办事处两周期间所获得的关于处理已缴清股份的知识，对他进行了严密盘问。随后，控方律师转而询问美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）在处理客户已缴清股份方面的做法。
塞莱特博士：假设我是美亚金融公司（此处原文误作 A.-C.F.C.，应指 A.-O.F.C.）的客户，此前从未与您或任何其他人就美亚金融公司将如何处理我已缴清股份的方式进行过任何交谈，我找到您并下达了购买100股美国电话电报公司（A.T. and T.）股票的订单，当您通知我订单已执行时，我向您交付了全额支付购买款项的汇票——无论纽约证券交易所是否有相关规定——作为一名商人，您难道不知道您对我的责任是使我成为这些股票的所有人，并保持其自由且无负担吗？
布朗先生：这取决于您是否有任何未结订单。

良心的指令
塞莱特博士（有力地）：我没有任何未结订单，事实正如我向您陈述的那样！我已经为您支付了这些股票的全部款项。假设您从未见过吉姆·普赖斯（Jim Price），也从未得到过他的专业法律建议——您自己的良心会告诉您，处置这笔财产的正确做法是什么？
布朗先生：为您账户持有。
塞莱特博士：您的良心会允许您拿走这笔财产并为美亚金融公司（A..O.F.C.，原文如此）的利益而抵押吗？
布朗先生：只要我能按需交付，我认为这没问题。
塞莱特博士：您认为在上述情况下，在我全额支付股票款项后，您有权拿着它们去找您的银行家说：“这里有一些股票。凭此借给我5,000美元。”您觉得您有权这样做吗？

布朗犹豫不决
布朗先生（长时间犹豫后）：只要我能随时偿还您——是的。
塞莱特博士：假设您从事银行业。我找到您说：“这里有100股美国电话电报公司股票。我希望您为我保管。将来某一天，我可能会想用它们向您的银行借款。”在这种情况下，您会觉得您可以拿着我的100股去中国银行并以此借款吗？
布朗先生：我认为这不是一个公平的问题。我认为您必须说明这些股票是否用于保管。
塞莱特博士：我甚至没提保管的事。我不知道这个词；它不在我的词汇表中。我说：这是我的股票。将来某一天我可能想凭此借款。”第二天，您能否拿着它们去中国银行，为您自己银行的用途而借款？

认为无可比性
布朗先生（停顿良久）：考虑到与纽约的距离，我认为这与本行业务没有可比性。
塞莱特博士：在您担任银行家的13到15年间，您是否有机会不时从银行客户那里接收某些非金钱财产——股票、地产或债券等？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：在任何这些情况下，您是否曾觉得可以自由支配这些财产并将其为银行的目的而抵押？
布朗先生：没有。
塞莱特博士：您是否认为在经纪行中适用不同的道德准则、伦理规范，或者无论您怎么称呼它？

被告沉默
布朗先生没有回答。
塞莱特博士：让我们回到旧金山。您于1930年5月13日从那里给雷文先生写了一封信， stating: “我与柯蒂斯先生讨论了保证金账户中已全额付清的证券问题。当皮尔斯公司遇到这种情况时，他们会将这些证券从保证金账户中取出并放入保管库。我们将安排这样做，因为如果我们的保证金账户中有此类股票并以此借款，这方面的责任相当重大。”您对皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）以这种方式处理已缴清股份感到惊讶吗？
布朗先生：不。
塞莱特博士：当然不会！您会知道经纪人无权抵押或设押属于客户的财产？即使您从未听说过证券交易所的规则，您也会这样理解，不是吗？
布朗先生：是的。
塞莱特博士：所以，当您得知皮尔斯公司如何处理保管中的股份时，您并不认为他们将其单独存放的唯一原因是因为证券交易所的某些规定？您的常识告诉您，这些股份必须保持自由且无负担？
布朗先生：您以这样一种方式对待它们，以便在要求交付时能够进行交付。

他的心态
塞莱特博士：在您返回中国之前，我认为您的心态是已缴清股份应保持自由且无负担——难道不是这样吗？
布朗先生：是的，这就是我于1930年5月13日给雷文先生写那封信的原因。
塞莱特博士：在那封信中，您只字未提纽约证券交易所的规定？
布朗先生：不，没错。
塞莱特博士（原文拼写错误 Settlelt）：您后来是否改变了关于将客户已缴清股份单独存放以备保管的看法？
布朗先生：是的，在接下来的一年里。我主要受到普赖斯先生建议的影响。我与雷文先生讨论了此事。令我印象深刻的是，美亚金融公司当时非常稳健，我们可以随时向任何前来索取的人交付股份。

使用他人财产
塞莱特博士：尽管如此，您还是意识到您正在处理的是他人的财产？
布朗先生：是的。
在回答有关本案申诉证人之一吕西安·克劳德·巴塞特（Lucien Claude Basset）先生购买并全额付清的股份的问题时，布朗先生说，他不知道巴塞特先生的股份已全额付清，因为只有短期保证金账户才转交给他处理。
塞莱特博士：作为一名经验丰富的商人，难道对您与皮尔斯公司的财务状况以及您对客户的义务的正确理解，不需要您掌握所有已缴清股份的完整信息吗？我将此问题提交给您。
布朗先生：是的。

SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JANUARY 24, 1936

A.-O.F.C. Had Account With
Itself, Listed As Asset

Witness Tells Of Strange Item In Firm's Balance
Sheet As Prosecution's Case In Raven Trial
Closes; Raven's Salary Said Immaterial

Contrary to expectation, the session of the United States Court for China yesterday morning, at which the Assistant District Attorney, Dr. George Sellett, concluded his presentation of the case for the prosecution in the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown on 16 counts of theft, embezzlement and fraud, provided one rather sensational highlight when Mr. Thomas Waung, former chief accountant of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the last Government witness in the case, testified as to certain items which appeared in the balance sheet of the A.-O.F.C. when it was still a going concern.

Mr. Waung testified that the A.-O.F.C.'s trading account with itself in New York stocks and commodities had been listed in the balance sheet at the end of 1934 as a collectable asset. This account, the witness said, showed a debit balance of U.S. $117,914, which amount was secured to the extent of only U. S. $30,000.

Should Be Written Off

In the course of further testimony, Mr. Waung told the Court that it had been his opinion that this account should be written off entirely and he expressed this opinion to Mr. Warner Brown and to Mr. Weyler. These officials told him that the matter would be taken care of in 1935 by applying to the outstanding balance certain exchange profits which had been made, and which, as far as the witness recalled, amounted to $50,-000 or $60,000, Chinese currency.

Referring to the sizeable short sales which appeared in the trading account which Mr. Raven had with the A.-O.F.C. and similar sales which appeared in the A.-O.F.C's account with itself, in April and May, 1935, shortly before the crash of the Raven concerns, Mr. Waung said that the orders for these short sales had been filled out by Mr. Brown and Mr. Weyler.

The items in question were referred to extensively in the evidence given earlier by Mr. Driscoll and Mr. Haley and more light was shed on them by Mr. Waung. Witness said he had brought the short sales to the attention of Mr. Warner Brown when they appeared for entry into the books.

"I asked Mr. Brown if these sales had been made intentionally. He replied 'yes.' I then remarked that the market appeared to be taking an upward turn. Mr. Brown agreed. I asked, then, why these sales had been made, and Mr. Brown replied that it was by order of the Executive Council.

In previous evidence it was established that this Executive Council had been set up to direct the destinies of all the Raven enterprises and the evidence given yesterday by Mr. Thomas Waung, regarding short sales, related to a statement made by Dr. George Sellett more than three weeks ago, when, in outlining the case for the prosecution, he declared that this Executive Council, at the head of which stood Mr. Raven, had plunged wildly on the stock market in a desperate effort to save the Raven enterprises just before the crash came.

Salaries Not Material

During the course of Mr. Waung's testimony yesterday, Dr. Sellett tried unsuccessfully to have the witness testify to the salaries which Messrs. Raven and Brown had received from the A.-O.F.C.

Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, objected that any such evidence was immaterial.

Dr. Sellett: If they received only nominal salaries, that might indicate one thing as to motive or intent. If, however, they received, let us say, salaries of $2,800 a month, that would indicate something else.

Judge Helmick: The objection by the defence is well taken.

Dr. Sellett: I want the record to show that the Government sought to put in evidence what the salaries were from January 1, 1930, to May 23, 1935, that the defence objected and that the objection was sustained.

Judge Helmick: It seems to me quite immaterial, from the point of view of responsibility, what an officer is paid. His duties and responsibilities are there.

Wants It In Record

Dr. Sellett: I want the record to show the evidence which the Government is seeking to introduce.

Mr. Evans: That's only another way of putting in this evidence, which is precisely what we are objecting to.

Judge Helmick: I cannot see the materiality. The amount of the salaries neither enhances nor diminishes the officers' responsibility. Could they submit as a defence the contention that they were underpaid?

The argument on the point at issue proceeded for several minutes, with the Judge upholding the defence objection.

Dr. Sellett then asked Mr. Waung the number of clients the A.-O.F.C. had when it closed down. The witness replied that there were approximately 450.

The defence is due to get into its stride to-day after submitting a motion to the Court for the dismissal of the charges on the usual ground that the evidence submitted by the prosecution does not constitute a case against the defendants. Both Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown are expected to take the witness-stand in their own defence, apart from any other witnesses

《字林西报》，1936年1月24日，星期五

美亚金融公司与其自身设有账户，列为资产

证人陈述该公司资产负债表中的奇异项目；检方在雷文案中的举证结束；称雷文的薪水无关紧要

出乎意料的是，昨日上午美国驻华法院的庭审出现了一个相当轰动的亮点。在此次庭审中，助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特博士（Dr. George Sellett）结束了对弗兰克·J·雷文先生（Mr. Frank J. Raven）和J·沃纳·布朗先生（Mr. J. Warner Brown）所涉16项盗窃、挪用公款及欺诈指控的检方举证。前美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）总会计师、也是本案最后一位政府证人的托马斯·王（Thomas Waung）先生出庭作证，陈述了美亚金融公司在仍正常运营时其资产负债表中出现的某些项目。

王先生作证称，美亚金融公司在纽约股票和商品方面与其自身设立的往来账户，在1934年底的资产负债表中被列为可收回资产。证人表示，该账户显示借方余额为117,914美元，而仅有30,000美元作为担保。

应予注销

在进一步的证词中，王先生告诉法庭，他认为该账户应予以全额注销，并向沃纳·布朗先生和韦勒先生（Mr. Weyler）表达了这一意见。这些官员告诉他，此事将在1935年通过运用已获得的某些汇兑利润来冲抵未结余额的方式进行处理，据证人回忆，这些利润金额为50,000或60,000元中国货币。

谈及1935年4月和5月，即在雷文旗下企业崩盘前不久，雷文先生与美亚金融公司的交易账户中出现的巨额卖空交易，以及美亚金融公司与其自身账户中出现的类似卖空交易时，王先生表示，这些卖空交易的订单是由布朗先生和韦勒先生填写的。

德里斯科尔先生（Mr. Driscoll）和黑利先生（Mr. Haley）早先提供的证据中曾广泛提及上述项目，而王先生的证词对此作了进一步澄清。证人表示，当这些卖空交易出现并需入账时，他曾提请沃纳·布朗先生注意。

“我问布朗先生，这些卖出是否是有意为之。他回答‘是’。我随后指出，市场似乎正呈现上升趋势。布朗先生表示同意。于是我问，既然如此，为何还要进行这些卖出操作，布朗先生回答说，这是执行委员会的命令。”

在此前的证据中已查明，该执行委员会系为指导所有雷文企业的命运而设立。托马斯·王先生昨日关于卖空交易的证词，与乔治·塞莱特博士三周多前的一份陈述相呼应。当时，塞莱特博士在概述检方案情时宣称，以雷文先生为首的执行委员会，在崩盘来临前的绝望努力中，曾在股票市场进行疯狂投机。

薪水问题无关紧要

在王先生昨日的作证过程中，塞莱特博士试图让证人就雷文先生和布朗先生从美亚金融公司领取的薪水作证，但未获成功。

雷文先生的辩护律师理查德·T·埃文斯先生（Mr. Richard T. Evans）提出异议，认为任何此类证据均无关紧要。

塞莱特博士：如果他们只领取名义上的薪水，这可能表明某种动机或意图。然而，如果他们领取，比如说，每月2,800美元的薪水，那将表明另一种情况。

赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）：辩方的异议成立。

塞莱特博士：我希望记录显示，政府试图提交1930年1月1日至1935年5月23日期间的薪水证据，辩方对此提出反对，且该反对被采纳。

赫尔米克法官：在我看来，从责任的角度来看，官员的薪酬多少是完全无关紧要的。他们的职责和责任是既定的。

要求记入记录

塞莱特博士：我希望记录显示政府试图引入的证据。

埃文斯先生：这只是引入该证据的另一种方式，而这正是我们要反对的。

赫尔米克法官：我看不出其相关性。薪水的数额既不会增加也不会减少官员的责任。他们能否以薪水过低作为抗辩理由呢？

围绕这一争议点的辩论持续了几分钟，法官维持了辩方的异议。

随后，塞莱特博士询问王先生，美亚金融公司在停业时拥有多少客户。证人回答说，大约有450家。

辩方预计今日将进入正式辩护阶段，此前已向法庭提交动议，以通常的理由——即检方提交的证据不足以构成对被告的起诉——要求撤销指控。除其他证人外，预计雷文先生和布朗先生都将亲自出庭为自己辩护。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JANUARY 23, 1936

Revealing Testimony Is
Given By Mr. Hough And
Raven's Own Secretary

Liquidator Discloses In U.S. Court Sorry State Of
Raven Concerns; Miss Hibbard Tells Of Mr.
Raven's Handling Of Haley's Report

CASE FOR PROSECUTION ENDS TO-DAY;
ONLY ONE WITNESS TO BE CALLED

Evidence of considerable importance from the point of view of the prosecution, and of revealing interest as far as the general public is concerned, was tendered yesterday afternoon in the United States Court for China by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the Raven enterprises, and Miss Olive Eleanor Hibbard, formerly private secretary to Mr. Frank J. Raven, at the resumed trial of Mr. Raven, and his confrere Mr. J. Warner Brown, who are charged on 16 counts with theft, embezzlement and fraud arising from the collapse of the Raven enterprises in May of last year.

When the Court, over which Judge Milton J. Helmick presides, adjourned at 4.30 p.m. until 10 a.m. to-day, the defence had finished its cross-examination of Mr. Hough, the last witness to be called yesterday, and Dr. George Sellett, Assistant District Attorney, announced that the Government proposed to call only one more witness. This witness will be called this morning and the case for the defence will then open. Mr. Raven is represented by Attorney Richard T. Evans of Tientsin, while Mr. C. S. Franklin appears for Mr. Brown.

Raven's Secretary Testifies
Efficient-looking, bespectacled, but decidedly pretty, Miss Olive Eleanor Hibbard took the witness-stand for the prosecution and, replying to questions by Dr. Sellett, told the Court that she was an American citizen, 27 years old, and that she had spent most of her life in Shanghai.

Witness said that she had been in the employ of Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the Raven concerns, since the latter closed down in May of last year. Prior to that she had worked for the Raven group for about eight years. At first, she was with the Asia Realty Company, but in June, 1928, she became private secretary to Mr. Frank J. Raven, a position which she continued to hold until the crash.

Dr. Sellett: As private secretary to Mr. Raven, did you have charge of the filing of documents relating to the business of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation?
Miss Hibbard: I did.

Mr. Haley's Report
Witness went on to say that she knew Mr. C. J. Haley, who at Monday's session of the trial testified to having submitted a report to Mr. Raven early in 1934 in which he stated that there were serious conditions with regard to the customers' fully paid-up shares instead of being held by A. Pierce and Company, brokers in San Francisco. Nothing had been done about this report, Mr. Haley told the Court.

Dr. Sellett: Do you recall that Mr. Haley visited Mr. Raven at his office early in 1934, shortly after his arrival in China?
Miss Hibbard: Yes, I remember it quite well.
Dr. Sellett: Where was Mr. Raven's office situated?
Miss Hibbard: At 50 Nanking Road.
Dr. Sellett: Did you hear any of the conversation between Mr. Haley and Mr. Raven?
Miss Hibbard: No.

Identifies Document
Witness then identified Government Exhibit 307, which is the report which Mr. Haley testified having handed to Mr. Raven in the latter's office at about the time stated.
Dr. Sellett: You have seen this document before?
Miss Hibbard: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: When did you first see it?
Miss Hibbard: When I filed it.
Dr. Sellett then drew the witness's attention to an initial "R" on the top right-hand corner of the first page of the document. "Do you recognize that initial?" he queried.
Miss Hibbard: Yes, it is the initial of Mr. Raven.
Dr. Sellett: In his own handwriting?
Miss Hibbard: Yes.
Prosecuting counsel then drew the witness's attention to the notation "February, 1934" appearing next to the initial. "In whose writing is that notation?" he queried.

Her Own Writing
Miss Hibbard: That is my own writing.
Dr. Sellett: Where did you get this document for filing?
Miss Hibbard: From Mr. Raven's desk, from the place where he usually deposited all documents intended for filing.
Dr. Sellett: Now, Miss Hibbard, you say you worked for Mr. Raven for about eight years—was it Mr. Raven's practice to initial documents?
Miss Hibbard: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: What did Mr. Raven's initial on a document usually signify?

What It Signified
Miss Hibbard: It signified that Mr. Raven had given it his attention.
Witness then went on to say that she next saw the document when asked by Mr. Hough to look for it in the files. That was after the Raven concerns had gone into liquidation. She found it in Mr. Raven's "H" file, which was a "miscellaneous folder."
Replying to further questions, Miss Hibbard identified Government Exhibit 238 as a letter dated May 13, 1930 from Mr. Brown to Mr. Raven.
Dr. Sellett: Whose initial is that on the letter?
Miss Hibbard: Mr. Raven's.
Dr. Sellett: And the other initials which appear on it?
Miss Hibbard: Those are the initials of Mr. Kleffel and Mr. Brown.
A single question was put to the witness in cross-examination by Mr. Evans. "Do you recall having had any conversation with Mr. Raven regarding the report submitted by Mr. Haley?" he queried. Miss Hibbard replied that she did not.

Mr. Hough On Stand
The next witness was Mr. Frank L. Hough, who is the Liquidator of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, the American-Oriental Banking Corporation and the Raven Trust Company, and Trustee of the Asia Realty Company, which is undergoing reorganization.
Replying to Dr. Sellett, witness gave his age as 51, nationality American, and said he had been in Shanghai three years. His regular business was manager of the R.C.A. Victor Company of China.
Continuing, Mr. Hough said he had prepared a statement showing the position of affairs of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation as of May 24, 1935, the date on which the Raven concerns failed to reopen. This statement, which witness produced, gave information as to the assets of the A.-O.F.C. at that date, the value of those assets, and particulars of the corporation's liabilities.
In estimating the value of the assets, witness said, he had taken, in cases in which assets had already been realized, the figures at which they had actually been disposed of. Not all the assets had been disposed of as yet, however. The total amount realized from the assets sold, plus the estimated realizable value of the assets still to be disposed of, was Sh. $1,-396,387.14 against liabilities totalling Sh. $7,822,012.93.

Evidence Objected To
At this stage, counsel for the defence objected to the introduction of this evidence, and all evidence on the statements, as irrelevant, since it related to facts ascertained since the closure of the Raven concerns on May 23, 1935. Judge Helmick over-ruled the objection and counsel for the defence noted an exception to all the ensuing testimony.
Dr. Sellett then continued his examination of the witness, asking him what amount of actual cash he expected to realize from the A.-O.F.C.'s assets in the final count.

《字林西报》，1936年1月23日，星期四

霍夫先生与雷文本人的秘书
提供揭露性证词

清算人在美国法庭披露雷文企业令人痛心的状况；希巴德小姐讲述雷文先生对哈利报告的处理方式

控方案件今日终结；仅传唤一名证人

昨日下午，在雷文先生及其同伙J. 华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生的续审中，雷文企业清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生和前雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生私人秘书奥利弗·埃莉诺·希巴德（Olive Eleanor Hibbard）小姐，向驻华美国法庭提供了从控方角度看来相当重要、且令公众颇感兴趣的证据。雷文与布朗被控16项罪名，涉及去年五月雷文企业崩溃引发的盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈行为。

当由米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官主持的法庭于下午4时30分休庭，直至今日上午10时复庭时，辩方已完成对昨日最后一名证人霍夫先生的交叉质询，助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士宣布，政府方面拟再传唤一名证人。该证人将于今早出庭，随后辩方将开始举证。雷文先生由天津律师理查德·T. 埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）代表，而C. S. 富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生则代表布朗先生出庭。

雷文的秘书作证

外表干练、戴着眼镜但确实颇为漂亮的奥利弗·埃莉诺·希巴德小姐作为控方证人出庭。在回答塞莱特博士的提问时，她告诉法庭，她是美国公民，现年27岁，大部分时间在上海度过。

证人表示，自去年五月雷文企业停业以来，她一直受雇于雷文企业清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生。在此之前，她在雷文集团工作了约八年。起初，她任职于亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company），但在1928年6月，她成为弗兰克·J. 雷文先生的私人秘书，并一直担任该职直至企业崩溃。

塞莱特博士：作为雷文先生的私人秘书，您是否负责归档与美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）业务相关的文件？
希巴德小姐：是的。

哈利的报告

证人接着说，她认识C. J. 哈利（C. J. Haley）先生，哈利先生在周一的庭审中作证称，他于1934年初向雷文先生提交了一份报告，指出客户的全额缴付股份存在严重问题，这些股份本应由旧金山经纪人A. 皮尔斯公司（A. Pierce and Company）持有，却未由其持有。哈利先生告诉法庭，这份报告未得到任何处理。

塞莱特博士：您是否记得哈利先生于1934年初抵达中国后不久，曾到办公室拜访雷文先生？
希巴德小姐：是的，我记得很清楚。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生的办公室位于何处？
希巴德小姐：南京路50号。
塞莱特博士：您是否听到哈利先生与雷文先生之间的任何谈话内容？
希巴德小姐：没有。

辨认文件

随后，证人指认了政府展物第307号，即哈利先生作证所称在所述时间左右于雷文先生办公室递交给雷文先生的那份报告。
塞莱特博士：您以前见过这份文件吗？
希巴德小姐：见过。
塞莱特博士：您第一次见到它是什么时候？
希巴德小姐：在我归档的时候。
塞莱特博士随即提请证人注意该文件第一页右上角的一个首字母“R”。“您认出这个首字母吗？”他问道。
希巴德小姐：是的，这是雷文先生的首字母。
塞莱特博士：是他亲笔书写的吗？
希巴德小姐：是的。
控方律师随后提请证人注意出现在该首字母旁边的标注“1934年2月”。“这处标注是谁的字迹？”他问道。

她自己的字迹

希巴德小姐：这是我自己的字迹。
塞莱特博士：您从哪里拿到这份文件进行归档？
希巴德小姐：从雷文先生的办公桌上，从他通常存放所有待归档文件的地方。
塞莱特博士：那么，希巴德小姐，您说您为雷文先生工作了大约八年——雷文先生是否有在文件上签署首字母的习惯？
希巴德小姐：有。
塞莱特博士：雷文先生在文件上签署首字母通常意味着什么？

其含义

希巴德小姐：这意味着雷文先生已审阅过该文件。
证人接着说，她下一次见到这份文件是在霍夫先生要求她在档案中寻找它的时候。那是在雷文企业进入清算程序之后。她在雷文先生的“H”卷宗中找到了它，那是一个“杂项文件夹”。
在回答进一步提问时，希巴德小姐指认政府展物第238号为布朗先生于1930年5月13日写给雷文先生的一封信。
塞莱特博士：信上的那个首字母是谁的？
希巴德小姐：雷文先生的。
塞莱特博士：上面出现的其他首字母呢？
希巴德小姐：那些是克莱费尔（Kleffel）先生和布朗先生的首字母。
在交叉质询中，埃文斯先生向证人提出了一个问题。“您是否记得曾就哈利先生提交的报告与雷文先生进行过任何交谈？”他问道。希巴德小姐回答说她不记得。

霍夫先生出庭

下一位证人是弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生，他是美亚金融公司、美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）和雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的清算人，也是正在重组中的亚洲地产公司的受托人。
在回答塞莱特博士的提问时，证人称其年龄为51岁，国籍为美国，并表示他在上海已三年。他的正式职业是中国 RCA 维克多公司（R.C.A. Victor Company of China）的经理。
霍夫先生继续说道，他编制了一份报表，显示截至1935年5月24日（即雷文企业未能重新开业之日）美亚金融公司的事务状况。证人出示的这份报表提供了该公司当日的资产信息、资产价值以及公司负债详情。
证人表示，在估算资产价值时，对于已经变现的资产，他采用了实际处置的价格。然而，并非所有资产都已处置。已售出资产的变现总额，加上待处置资产的估计可变现价值，共计规元1,396,387.14两，而负债总额为规元7,822,012.93两。

对证据提出异议

在此阶段，辩方律师反对引入此项证据及所有基于该报表的证据，认为其不具相关性，因为它涉及1935年5月23日雷文企业关闭后才查明的事实。赫尔米克法官驳回了这一异议，辩方律师对所有随后的证词记录例外保留。
随后，塞莱特博士继续讯问证人，询问他预计最终能从美亚金融公司的资产中实际变现多少现金。

Dr. Sellett: How much cash did
the A.-O.F.C. have on hand with
banks, excluding the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation, on
the date of the closure, May 23,
1935?
Mr. Hough: About Sh. $10,000;
but this sum, which was in several
banks, was held by those banks
against exchange contracts which
they had with the A.-O.F.C.
Collections Made
In reply to further questions,
Mr. Hough said that, as regards
the A.-C.F.C., he had collected
about Sh. $160,000 and U.S.
$7,400 since liquidation started.
Dr. Sellett: What was the
amount of valid claims against the
A.-O.F.C. on May 24, 1935?
Mr. Hough: About Sh.$3,239,-
641.78.
Dr. Sellett: So that if your
previous figure of Sh. $1,396,-
387.14, given as an estimate of
the total realizable value of A.-
O.F.C. assets, is correct, then you
would have only that sum with
which to discharge valid claims
amounting to Sh. $3,239,641.78?
Mr. Hough: That is correct.
Witness then went on to state
that considerable sums were owing
to the A.-O.F.C. by officers and
employees of the Raven concerns,
including the A.-O.F.C., when the
crash came.
Non-Collectable Accounts
Dr. Sellett: Have you been able
to collect anything on those
accounts?
Mr. Hough: No, nothing.
Dr. Sellett: Mr. Raven was a
debtor through a R. T. Co. ac-
count. Have you collected any-
thing on that?
Mr. Hough: No.
Dr. Sellett: Or anything on the
accounts of Mr. Hill, Mr. Price,
Mr. Driscoll or Mr. Warner
Brown?
Mr. Hough: No.
Prosecuting counsel then asked
the witness whether the figure of
valid claims which he had pre-
viously given included liabilities
in respect of capital stock, namely,
liabilities to shareholders. The
answer was in the negative.
The A.-O.F.C., he continued,
held shares in the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation, the
Raven Trust Company and the
Asia Realty Company.
Shares Valueless
Dr. Sellett: In estimating the
value of the A.-C.F.C's assets, did
you accord any value to these
shares?
Mr. Hough: No.
Witness added that general
creditors of the A.-O.F.C. could
expect a dividend of about 1½
per cent. He hoped that the
general creditors of the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation
would ultimately get about 20 per
cent.
Regarding the position of the
Asia Realty Company, witness
said that there were unsecured
creditors to the approximate
amount of Sh. $2,500,000. The
company owned no free, unencum-
bered property excepting furni-
ture and fixtures. All its real
estate was mortgaged.
Franklin Cross-Examines
Mr. C. S. Franklin then cross-
examined the witness regarding
deposits which the A.-O.F.C. had
with the A.-O.B.C. on May 24,
1935. There was one deposit of
Sh. $13,2558.26, witness said, and
this was worth 20 per cent. to the
A.-O.F.C. as a general creditor of
the bank.
Mr. Franklin: Did the A.-O.F.C.
not also have on deposit with the
bank U.S. $90,000?
Mr. Hough: Not as far as I
am aware.
Mr. Franklin: What was the
amount of Asia Realty shares and
debentures which the A.-O.F.C.
held at the time of the closure?
Mr. Hough: Sh. $174,940.71.
No Real Value Before
Dr. Sellett (re-examining): On
the basis of the knowledge which
you have gained since you took
over as Liquidator, do you con-
sider that the shares of the
A.-O.F.C., A.-O.B.C., Raven Trust
Company and Asia Realty Com-
pany had any real value even
before the closure?
Mr. Hough: No, I do not think
they were worth anything.
This concluded Mr. Hough's evi-
dence and counsel for the defence
moved to strike all of it from the
record as irrelevant. Judge Hel-
mick overruled the motion and an
exception was noted.
Prior to the hearing of the testi-
mony of Miss Hibbard and Mr.
Hough, two of the prosecution's
previous witnesses, Mr. Hermann
Aufwerber, former A.-O.F.C. sales-
man, and Mr. Alfred H. Driscoll,
former A.-O.F.C. secretary, were
recalled by the defence for fur-
ther cross-examination. This was
preceded by the cross-examination
of Mr. C. J. Haley, prosecution
witness of the previous day, which
occupied all of the morning and
part of the afternoon session.
Aufwerber Recalled
The defence questioning of Mr.
Aufwerber related to the A.-O.F.C.
practice with regard to getting
customers to endorse signature
cards.
Replying to Mr. Franklin, Mr.
Aufwerber agreed that he had
never got a signature card from
Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland, one of
the complaining witnesses in the
case.
"From some clients," witness
said, "it was difficult to get signa-
ture cards, especially Chinese
clients.
Mr. Franklin: But you carried
margin accounts for customers
even if they had not completed
signature cards?
Mr. Aufwerber: Yes.
The defence then recalled Mr.
Driscoll and submitted him,
through Mr. Evans, to a lengthy
cross-examination. Witness said
he was aware that in May, 1935
considerable short sales had been
debited on the A.-O.F.C. ledger to
the account known as R. T. Co.
101-I. 1, which was Mr. Raven's
account.
Mr. Evans: How did the short
sales in that account come about?
Mr. Driscoll: The first time I
knew about it was when I receiv-
ed the confirmation slips of the
short sales from the A.-O.F.C.
Mr. Evans: But were you not,
in May, 1935, the person who
would give instructions for such
sales?
Dr. Sellett objected to the ques-
tion since it related to a matter
which had arisen in the trial
through another witness, after Mr.
Driscoll had given his evidence-in-
chief.
Judge Helmick: I don't see that
any harm would be done if the
witness answered the question.
Short Sales Instructions
Mr. Driscoll then answered the
question by saying that instruc-
tion for the short sales would have
had to be given either by Mr.
Raven or himself.
Mr. Evans: Well, when you re-
ceived the confirmation slips from
the A.-O.F.C., what did you do?
Mr. Driscoll: I asked Mr. Raven
about the sales but he said he
hadn't given any instructions.
Mr. Evans: And what did you
do then?
Mr. Driscoll: I approached Mr.
Warner Brown and he simply said
that he would take care of the
matter.
Mr. Evans then asked the wit-
ness whether he recalled a tiffin
conversation with Mr. Raven in
the Spring of 1934. Mr. Driscoll
said he did not recall it, where-
upon Mr. Evans said he might re-
fresh the witness's memory by
stating that Mr. Raven had re-
marked at the time that it was
the worst tiffin he had ever had.
Judge Helmick: This will have
to stop. You cannot ask a question
that way.
Those Cypher Accounts
Revealing testimony was then
given by Mr. Driscoll as to the
motive which prompted the
A.O.F.C. management to inaugur-
ate the practice of cypher ac-
counts for customers. This follow-
ed from a query by Mr. Evans to
the witness as to whether the lat-
ter remembered when the practice
was started.
Mr. Driscoll: It was started
before I came to China. Mr. Price
explained to me that it was in-
augurated because the A.-O.F.C.
expected to have a large number
of Chinese clients, who disliked
the prospect of other people know-
ing about their affairs.
Re-examined by Dr. Sellett, wit-
ness said he had spoken to Mr.
Raven about the short sales in his
account probably 10 days after
they were made. Mr. Raven said
he had not authorized the sales
but did nothing about it.
Who Used Cyphers
Coming then to the question of
the motive for the cipher accounts,
Dr. Sellett asked the witness if it
was not a fact that no substantial
use was made of them other than
by persons who were officers or
employees of the Raven enter-
prise. Mr. Driscoll replied that
that was so. Other than such offi-
cers and employees he knew of
only one account carried under a
cypher number. This was the ac-
count of a Mr. C. P. Yen, another
was run by a Chinese employee
named Kuo. There were about 20
of these cipher accounts all told,
witness added in reply to Mr.
Evans.
Mr. Evans' final question to Mr.
Driscoll was as to whether Mr.
Raven had taken part in negotia-
tions for the merger of the Raven
interests with the interests of Mr.
C. V. Starr. Witness said that Mr.
Raven was a participant.
Morning Proceedings
When the morning session of
the trial opened at 10 o'clock, Mr.
C. S. Franklin launched into a
lengthy cross-examination of C. J.
Haley, former employee of the
A.-O.F.C. and now a resident of
San Francisco, who testified for
the Government on Monday.
Counsel for the defence elicited
the information that when Mr.
Raven engaged Mr. Haley in San
Francisco in 1933 it was because
the A.-O.F.C. desired someone with
"homeside brokerage experience."
