加速办理

德里斯科尔先生：我认为雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）应当从中获得某些利益。我还认为，如果美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）必须就股份价值支付利息，他们便会更迅速地将股份转移至保管账户。

在回答进一步提问时，证人表示，他不记得在执行委员会决定“逐步”将本杰明（Benjamin）的股份转移至保管账户时，美亚金融公司在皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）的保证金头寸状况如何。至于本地知名建筑师L. E. 胡代克（L. E. Hudec）先生拥有的缴足股款股份，他指示将这些股份也转移至皮尔斯公司保管，此事已照办。这些股份的价值约为42,000美元。

在此作证过程中，雷文先生的代理律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生以无关为由提出反对。“我们并不否认这些转移至保管账户的行为确实发生，”他声明道。

证人无可指责

塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）：我提请法庭注意，这完全具有相关性。我的目的是表明，证人的行为始终光明正大且无可指责。

赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）驳回了该异议，塞莱特博士继续沿着同一思路进行讯问。他的下一个问题引出了如下信息：切斯特·M·托宾（Chester M. Tobin）先生拥有的缴足股款股份，是应雷文信托公司的要求转移至保管账户的，该公司曾就此事宜接洽美亚金融公司。

塞莱特博士：那么，是谁发起了雷文信托公司的这一行动？

德里斯科尔先生：是我。

执行委员会的活动

转向执行委员会的活动，控方律师获悉，雷文企业最重要的业务是由该机构处理，而非由各独立公司的董事会处理。

证人称，执行委员会每周召开会议，会议结果未必向董事会报告。只有那些需要董事会采取正式行动的事项才会向他们报告。

随后，塞莱特博士将注意力转向雷文企业的办公设置，指出主要机构——美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）和雷文信托公司——均设在南京路29号的同一栋大楼内，从而在公众心目中倾向于将它们视为一体。

短途步行

“如果您作为雷文信托公司的秘书，想要向美亚金融公司经理J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生递交一封信，您或信差需要走多远？”他问证人。

德里斯科尔先生：15英尺。

塞莱特博士：那去美亚银行呢？

德里斯科尔先生：大约70英尺。

塞莱特博士：那去位于南京路50号的亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）呢？

德里斯科尔先生：大约250英尺。

雷文的薪金

在回答进一步提问时，证人表示，雷文先生从雷文信托公司领取薪金直至1933年底，但此后继续无偿为公司提供服务。他还从美亚金融公司领取薪金，但证人不知具体金额。他也不知道布朗先生作为美亚金融公司副总裁兼经理领取多少薪金。雷文先生主要负责各公司经理的聘任以及其他人员的雇佣。

随后，塞莱特博士将话题转向1935年5月23日雷文企业崩盘前夕的时期，特别提及该时期内雷文执行委员会的会议。

证人称，这些会议每周召开两次，有时三次，旨在审议雷文企业陷入的财务困境并寻找出路。

证人表示，雷文先生出席了所有会议，布朗先生也出席了一些会议，但后者于5月6日前往马尼拉，因此在最后一段开会期间不在场。

意见分歧

关于雷文各公司能否渡过难关，意见存在分歧。执行委员会的一些成员认为它们能够挺过去，但其他人则非常怀疑。

证人继续说道，为了挽救局势，美亚金融公司撤回了其在伦敦和纽约的大部分存款余额，并将其投入美亚银行，因为后者处于最困难的境地。

随后，证人被问及5月23日晚举行的执行委员会最后一次决定性会议，会上做出了关闭机构的决定。此次会议之后，又在纽约花旗银行上海分行经理J. A. 麦凯（J. A. Mackay）先生家中举行了另一次会议。

目的未明

由于法庭在进入这一方面的质询前休庭，此次会议的确切目的未被引出，但当被问及谁出席了该会议时，证人回答说，除麦凯先生外，出席者还有：弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生、美亚金融公司董事H·桑多尔（H. Sandor）先生、美亚金融公司的H. W. 韦勒（H. W. Weyler）先生、美亚银行前经理J·克莱费尔（J. Kleffel）先生、大通银行上海分行经理A. E. 舒马赫（A. E. Schumacher）先生、亚洲人寿保险公司及承保人储蓄银行（Underwriters' Savings Bank）的C. V. 斯塔尔（C. V. Starr）先生、斯旺、卡尔伯特森和弗里茨律师事务所（Swan, Culbertson and Fritz）合伙人J. E. 斯旺（J. E. Swan）先生、万国储蓄会（International Savings Society）的M·斯佩尔曼（M. Speelman）先生，以及德里斯科尔先生。会议从晚上9点持续到凌晨1点。

此时，法庭休庭至今日上午10点。

德里斯科尔先生昨天上午在座无虚席的法庭上当众出庭作证，面对昔日的雇主和同事，他明显表现出紧张和不安的迹象。尽管如此，他以清晰、坚定的声音回答了向他提出的问题。

在回答塞莱特博士时，他说自己30岁，是美国公民，目前与前美亚银行经理J·克莱费尔先生同住于阿默斯特大道（Amherst Avenue）333号。他是一名职业律师，毕业于利兰·斯坦福大学（Leland Stanford），曾在美国执业。目前他是美国在华法院律师公会成员。

始于1932年

1932年9月，他接替詹姆斯·F·普赖斯（James F. Price）先生成为美亚金融公司秘书，并一直担任该职直至雷文企业崩盘。1934年6月，他成为美亚金融公司董事，并于1935年1月1日被加授司库一职，在这两个职位上一直任职至崩盘发生。

在担任美亚金融公司董事、司库和秘书期间，他没有领取薪金，但曾因夜间工作获得过一次奖金。他的薪金来自雷文信托公司和美亚银行。起初他每月领取600美元，但在崩盘发生时，他的月薪为1,000美元。

根据他的证词，雷文先生作为总裁，几乎每天都过问雷文信托公司的事务。

当塞莱特博士开始引入德里斯科尔先生持有的一本活页簿中的页面，其中包含美亚金融公司密码账户的身份信息时，辩护律师提出了强烈反对。

动机待示

塞莱特博士：我将证明被告，特别是雷文先生，进行了大量的纽约交易账户操作，这些账户大多无担保，且经常遭受巨额损失。这将显示被告有实质性的动机去实施被指控的罪行，即利用他人的财产为己所用。

赫尔米克法官驳回了该异议，随后雷文先生的代理律师埃文斯先生表示，他希望明确记录，辩护律师对任何可能与德里斯科尔先生持有的账簿有关的问题均提出反对，并要求对每一个问题都记录在案以示异议。

昨天传唤的唯一另一位新证人是乔治·科克莱特（Georges Coquelet）先生，他是一位比利时特许会计师，此前受雇于美亚金融公司，现就职于哈迪维利耶公司（Hardivilliers and Company）。他表示，他从1932年1月至1933年5月1日期间在美亚金融公司工作。

埃文斯先生提出异议

埃文斯先生指出，这早于针对被告的指控所依据的任何交易发生的时间。对此，塞莱特博士回答说，他希望展示公司的运营方式以及被告与

page_data.en:
it. Judge Helmick overruled the objection and Mr. Evans noted exceptions to all the witness's testimony.
Mr. Coquelet said he had made many reports on the positions of clients, which reports had gone to Mr. J. Warner Brown, manager of the A.-O.F.C.
Three such reports were then introduced in respect of November 18, 1932, one of which showed a list of clients whose collateral did not cover their indebtedness. Another was a list of clients on short margin, while the third was a list of clients with fully paid shares, which, Mr. Coquelet said, was the first of its kind he had ever prepared. He recalled Mr. Brown asking him to make it up for Mr. Raven.
In making this statement originally, the witness said "I think," to which Mr. Evans objected. "If he says: 'That is my recollection,' all right."
Mr. Coquelet: I should improve my English. Excuse me!
The list of clients whose collateral did not cover their debit balances included one, "R. T. Co. Trust Account." The list itself totalled U.S.$364,346.
Judge Helmick: Take the figures of one account,. U.S.$4.291. Does that figure represent the deficiency which would ensue if that person's securities were sold out on that day?
Mr. Coquelet: Yes, but it doesn't show the amount of his holdings, nor does it directly show his debit balance.
Deficiency On Sale
Judge Helmick: Doesn't it practically show his debit balance?
Mr. Coquelet: No, it merely shows that if he were sold out this amount of U.S.$4.291 would be the loss to the A.-O.F.C. on the whole transaction. The same is true with respect to the other names on the list.
Judge Helmick: So that if all the shares were sold out, what would be the loss to the A.-O.F.C. —U.S.$364,346?
Dr. Sellett: Regarding the account, if all the clients on that list were to pay in enough money to bring their accounts up to margin requirements, what would they have to pay in?
Mr. Coquelet: They would have to pay in U.S.$22,581.
Cross-examining the witness, Mr. Franklin, counsel for Mr. J. Warner Brown, asked: "With this huge loss you have testified to, did you consider the A.-O.F.C. was insolvent?"
Mr. Coquelet: I had nothing to do with that.
What Would Be Lost
The second list, Government Exhibit 292, was the subject of much questioning and it was finally established that the A.-O.F.C. would have lost U.S.$364,346 on the date previously referred to if the shares of the clients named on it had been sold out. In other words, their collateral was short by that amount to cover their total debits.
Most of this sum was accounted for by the debits of Mr. C. H. Raven, Mr. E. E. Shamoon, and the Raven Trust Company and the "R.T. Co." as trustees for a number of clients identified only by ciphers.
Mr. Hermann Aufwerber, salesman of the A.-O.F.C. was recalled briefly to testify to an account with a Mr. Richard R. Newman. Mr. Evans objected.
Pledged All They Could
Dr. Sellett: I am getting testimony to show how certain securities got into safekeeping. This has a bearing on how others did not. The defendants hypothecated all the securities they could. It was no mistake or oversight that the shares mentioned in the Government information did not get into safekeeping.
Mr. Evans: We are quite willing to admit that securities were never put into safekeeping without request
Dr. Sellett: I will show that shares did not always go into safekeeping even when requested by clients.
Judge Helmick: It certainly seems that unless requested by a client, shares never went into safekeeping.
Dr. Sellect (to defence counsel): Why won't you admit specifically that Newman's shares went into safekeeping only when Newman requested it?
Mr. Franklin: Our admission covers that.
Judge Helmick: The Court is satisfied that the Newman shares went into safekeeping only at his request.

赫尔米克法官驳回了该异议，埃文斯先生对证人的所有证词均记录例外异议。

科克莱特先生表示，他曾就客户头寸提交过许多报告，这些报告已提交给美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）经理J. 华纳·布朗先生。

随后呈堂了三份关于1932年11月18日的此类报告，其中一份列出了抵押品不足以抵偿其债务的客户名单。另一份是保证金不足的客户名单，而第三份则是全额付清股款的客户名单，科克莱特先生称这是他编制的第一份此类名单。他回忆说，布朗先生曾要求他为雷文先生编制这份名单。

在最初作出这一陈述时，证人说道“我想”，对此埃文斯先生提出反对。“如果他说：‘那是我的记忆’，那就可以。”

科克莱特先生：我应该改进我的英语。请原谅！

抵押品不足以抵偿借方余额的客户名单中包括一个名为“R. T. Co. 信托账户”的账户。该名单总额为364,346美元。

赫尔米克法官：取其中一个账户的数字，4,291美元。这个数字是否代表如果该人的证券在当天被平仓出售将会产生的亏空？

科克莱特先生：是的，但它并未显示其持有量，也未直接显示其借方余额。

出售时的亏空

赫尔米克法官：这实际上不是显示了他的借方余额吗？

科克莱特先生：不，它仅表明，如果他被迫平仓，这4,291美元将是美亚金融公司在整笔交易中的损失。名单上的其他名字也是如此。

赫尔米克法官：那么，如果所有股票都被平仓出售，美亚金融公司的损失是多少——364,346美元？

塞莱特博士：关于该账户，如果名单上的所有客户都存入足够的资金以使其账户达到保证金要求，他们需要存入多少？

科克莱特先生：他们需要存入22,581美元。

在对证人进行交叉询问时，J. 华纳·布朗先生的律师富兰克林先生问道：“鉴于你作证提到的巨大损失，你是否认为美亚金融公司已经资不抵债？”

科克莱特先生：那与我无关。

将会损失什么

第二份名单，即政府证据第292号，受到了大量质询，最终确定，如果名单上所列客户的股票在之前提到的日期被平仓出售，美亚金融公司将损失364,346美元。换句话说，他们的抵押品短缺该金额，无法覆盖其总借记额。

这笔款项的大部分是由C. H. 雷文先生、E. E. 沙蒙先生、雷文信托公司以及作为若干仅以代号标识客户的受托人的“R.T. Co.”的借方余额构成的。

美亚金融公司的推销员赫尔曼·奥夫韦伯先生被短暂传召出庭，就与理查德·R. 纽曼先生的一个账户作证。埃文斯先生提出反对。

质押了他们所能质押的一切

塞莱特博士：我正在获取证词，以显示某些证券是如何进入保管状态的。这与另一些证券为何未进入保管状态有关。被告们将他们所能质押的所有证券都进行了质押。政府起诉书中所提及的股份未进入保管状态，并非错误或疏忽所致。

埃文斯先生：我们完全愿意承认，未经请求，证券绝不会放入保管状态。

塞莱特博士：我将证明，即使客户要求，股份也并不总是进入保管状态。

赫尔米克法官：看来确实如此，除非客户要求，否则股份绝不会进入保管状态。

塞莱克特博士（对辩护律师）：你们为何不具体承认纽曼的股份仅在纽曼要求时才进入保管状态？

富兰克林先生：我们的承认已涵盖这一点。

赫尔米克法官：法庭确信，纽曼的股份仅在其要求下才进入保管状态。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JANUARY 16, 1936 13114

More Evidence By Curtis
At The Raven Trial

Witness Testifies To The Disposal Of Securities
Worth U.S. $1,100,000 To Settle Indebtedness
Of A.-O.F.C. When Crash Came Last Year

Stocks to the approximate value of U.S. $1,100,000 were being held for the American-Oriental Finance Corporation by E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco, on May 23, 1935, the date on which the A.-O.F.C. closed its doors, according to testimony given by Mr. C. C. Curtis, an official of the San Francisco firm, at the continued hearing in the United States Court for China yesterday of the 16 charges of theft, embezzlement and fraud on which Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown are undergoing trial.

When the A.-O.F.C. crashed, all these stocks, which had been pledged by the A.-O.F.C., were sold out by Pierce and Company to cover the A.-O.F.C.'s indebtedness on its margin account, with resultant heavy losses to Shanghai investors, many of whom had paid in full, through the A.-O.F.C., for stocks which the A.-O.F.C. had hypothecated to Pierce and Company.

It is the contention of the prosecution that in pledging stocks belonging to A.-O.F.C. customers who had paid for them in full, Messrs. Raven and Brown, as the responsible heads of the A.-O.F.C., committed acts of embezzlement and theft as charged in the indictment.

At yesterday's session of the trial, Mr. Curtis, continuing his evidence of the day previous, with Dr. George Sellett, assistant District Attorney, examining, told of the opening by the A.-O.F.C. of branch offices in Hongkong and Manila in the spring of 1934. These offices, he said, did business direct with the San Francisco office of E. A. Pierce and Company. When their accounts were short margined, Pierce and Company looked to the head office of the A.-O.F.C. in Shanghai to furnish the required additional margin.

Stocks Liquidated

The witness then went on to say that on May 24, 1935 the A.-O.F.C. cabled Pierce and Company, informing them that the Raven group had gone into voluntary liquidation and requesting the cancellation of all buying orders.

Dr. Sellett: What did E. A. Pierce and Company do?

Mr. Curtis: We proceeded to liquidate the debit balance of the A.-O.F.C. in the usual manner—by selling out their stocks.

The Manila office, witness added, cabled Pierce and Company not to liquidate its business since this was being transferred to another brokerage house. Securities in the accounts of the A.-O.F.C. at Shanghai and Hongkong were liquidated on May 25.

What The A.-O.F.C. Owned

In reply to further questions by Dr. Sellett, Mr. Curtis said that at the close of business on May 23, the A.-O.F.C. was indebted to Pierce and Company in the sum of U.S. $865,567.67 in respect of the Shanghai office, U.S. $73,-892.65 in respect of the Hongkong office, and U.S. $5,640.41 in respect of the Manila office.

By May 31, all the debit balance of the Shanghai office had been liquidated, except for about U.S. $20,000. By August 31, this had been reduced to U.S. $8,000. The A.-O.F.C. had never had a credit balance with Pierce and Company, Mr. Curtis said. The Hongkong office never had a safekeeping account, but the Manila office had put some shares into safekeeping.

Continuing to describe the business relations of Pierce and Company with the A.-O.F.C., Mr. Curtis said that when the account was first opened the A.-O.F.C. furnished margin both in cash and securities. Later, however, it deposited with Pierce and Company two letters of credit, one on the Chase National Bank for U.S. $200,000 and the other on the Belgian bank for U.S. $30,000. Pierce and Company drew against neither, however.

Approached By Brown

Concluding his examination of Mr. Curtis, Dr. Sellett asked him whether he had at any time been approached by Mr. J. Warner Brown, one of the defendants, since his arrival in Shanghai.

"Mr. Brown spoke to me when I got off the boat," witness replied. "Later, he telephoned me and invited me to accompany him to the races. I declined the invitation, telling him that I had come to Shanghai as a government witness in his case and that I would not care to be seen in his company until the trial was over."

In commencing his cross-examination of Mr. Curtis, Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for Mr. J. Warner Brown, revealed that a Mr. Woods, partner in E. A. Pierce and Company, resident in San Francisco, had written a letter to Mr. Brown, advising him that Mr. Curtis was coming to Shanghai and suggesting that the latter would be glad to see him. This letter, which was not read in full, referred to the "unfortunate charges" which had been preferred against the defendants.

Replying to Mr. Franklin, Mr. Curtis said that Mr. Woods had given him a letter to mail to Mr. Brown on the boat, but he (Mr. Curtis) was unaware of the contents. Further questioning elicited the information that Mr. Curtis and Mr. Brown had been well acquainted socially in San Francisco.

Safekeeping Accounts

Mr. Curtis was then cross-examined in regard to the general practice of Pierce and Company in the matter of safekeeping accounts. In the case of individual customers, he said, Pierce and Company had the right to take shares out of safekeeping for margin requirements.

Judge Helmick: That presupposes, of course, that the customer has a margin account and a safe-keeping account?

Mr. Curtis: Naturally, your honour.

But in the case of a brokerage house customer, witness continued, the request safekeeping account was not disturbed, even if the customer became under-margined. In the case of an ordinary safe-keeping account, however, where there was a "long" position, shares could be transferred back and forth between the margin and safekeeping accounts. This practice was in accord with the regulations of the New York Stock Exchange.

The trial will continue at 10 a.m. to-day.

《字林西报》，1936年1月16日，星期四 13114

柯蒂斯提供更多证据
在雷文案审判中

证人作证称处置价值110万美元的证券
以清偿去年崩盘时美亚金融公司的债务

据旧金山E. A. 皮尔斯公司官员C. C. 柯蒂斯先生昨日在中国美国法院继续审理弗兰克·J. 雷文先生和J. 华纳·布朗先生所面临的16项盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈指控时提供的证词，1935年5月23日，即美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）关门之日，旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司为美亚金融公司持有价值约110万美元的股票。

当美亚金融公司崩盘时，所有这些由美亚金融公司质押的股票均被皮尔斯公司平仓出售，以弥补美亚金融公司在保证金账户上的债务，导致上海投资者遭受重大损失，其中许多人已通过美亚金融公司全额支付了那些被美亚金融公司质押给皮尔斯公司的股票款项。

检方主张，雷文先生和布朗先生作为美亚金融公司的负责人，将已全额付款的美亚金融公司客户的股票进行质押，构成了起诉书中指控的挪用公款和盗窃行为。

在昨日的庭审中，柯蒂斯先生继续前一天的证词，助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特博士对其进行主问，他讲述了美亚金融公司于1934年春季在香港和马尼拉开设分支机构的情况。他说，这些办事处直接与E. A. 皮尔斯公司的旧金山办事处开展业务。当它们的账户保证金不足时，皮尔斯公司便向美亚金融公司位于上海的总部寻求提供所需的追加保证金。

股票被清算

证人接着说，1935年5月24日，美亚金融公司向皮尔斯公司发出电报，通知他们雷文集团已进入自愿清算程序，并要求取消所有买入指令。

塞莱特博士：E. A. 皮尔斯公司做了什么？

柯蒂斯先生：我们按常规方式清算了美亚金融公司的借方余额——即平仓出售其股票。

证人补充说，马尼拉办事处致电皮尔斯公司，要求不要清算其业务，因为该业务正转移到另一家经纪行。5月25日，美亚金融公司在上海和香港账户中的证券被清算。

美亚金融公司拥有什么

在回答塞莱特博士的进一步提问时，柯蒂斯先生说，截至5月23日营业结束时，美亚金融公司欠皮尔斯公司的债务为：上海办事处865,567.67美元，香港办事处73,892.65美元，马尼拉办事处5,640.41美元。

到5月31日，上海办事处的所有借方余额均已清算，仅剩约20,000美元。到8月31日，这一数额减少至8,000美元。柯蒂斯先生说，美亚金融公司在皮尔斯公司从未有过贷方余额。香港办事处从未设有保管账户，但马尼拉办事处将一些股份放入了保管状态。

柯蒂斯先生在继续描述皮尔斯公司与美亚金融公司的业务关系时说，账户刚开立时，美亚金融公司以现金和证券形式提供保证金。然而，后来它在皮尔斯公司存入了两份信用证，一份开自大通国家银行，金额为200,000美元，另一份开自比利时银行，金额为30,000美元。不过，皮尔斯公司并未动用这两份信用证。

布朗的接触

塞莱特博士在完成对柯蒂斯先生的主问后，问他自抵达上海以来，是否曾有任何时候被被告之一的J. 华纳·布朗先生接触过。

“我一下船，布朗先生就和我说话了，”证人回答。“后来，他打电话给我，邀请我陪他去赛马场。我拒绝了邀请，告诉他我是作为他案件的政府证人来到上海的，在审判结束之前，我不愿被人看到与他在一起。”

在开始对柯蒂斯先生进行交叉询问时，J. 华纳·布朗先生的律师C. S. 富兰克林先生透露，居住在旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司合伙人伍兹先生曾写信给布朗先生，告知他柯蒂斯先生即将前往上海，并暗示后者会乐意见到他。这封信未全文宣读，其中提到了针对被告提出的“不幸的指控”。

在回答富兰克林先生的提问时，柯蒂斯先生说，伍兹先生在船上给了他一封寄给布朗先生的信，但他（柯蒂斯先生）并不知晓信的内容。进一步的询问得知，柯蒂斯先生和布朗先生在旧金山时私交甚笃。

保管账户

随后，柯蒂斯先生就皮尔斯公司在保管账户方面的一般做法接受了交叉询问。他说，对于个人客户，皮尔斯公司有权出于保证金要求将股份从保管状态中取出。

赫尔米克法官：这当然预设了客户既有保证金账户又有保管账户？

柯蒂斯先生：自然如此，法官大人。

但是，证人继续说道，对于经纪行客户，即使客户保证金不足，指定的保管账户也不会受到干扰。然而，在普通的保管账户情况下，如果存在“多头”头寸，股份可以在保证金账户和保管账户之间来回转移。这种做法符合纽约证券交易所的规定。

审判将于今天上午10点继续进行。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 15, 1936
13076

Curtis Testifies Regarding
A.-O.F.C. Safekeeping

Evidence At Yesterday's Session Of Raven Trial
Shows That Corporation Operated For Several
Years Without Such Customers' Safeguard

Practically the entire length of yesterday's session of the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, President and Vice-President, respectively, of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, on 16 charges of theft, embezzlement and fraud, was devoted by the U.S. Court for China to the hearing of testimony by Mr. C. C. Curtis of the San Francisco office of E. A. Pierce and Company regarding the safekeeping account which the A.-O.F.C. had with his firm.

The session, which began at 10 a.m. and lasted until 4 p.m., with the usual lunch hour intermission, was singularly lacking in interest from the public point of view.

When it terminated, the prosecution had handed in its 285th exhibit in the case, and it was indicated that with the continuance of full-day sessions, except on Saturday and Sunday when the Court does not sit, the trial will not be concluded before January 24, which is Chinese New Year, and may even continue beyond that date.

Mr. Curtis, who was recalled by the prosecution after having given testimony on several previous occasions, told the Court how Mr. J. Warner Brown had visited him in San Francisco in 1930 with a view to studying the business methods of E. A. Pierce and Company in stock market transactions.

Dr. Sellett, Assistant District Attorney, introduced a letter written by Mr. Brown in San Francisco to Mr. Raven in Shanghai and reading, in part, as follows:

Mr. Brown's Letter
"I took up both with Mr. Woods and Mr. Curtis the matter of holding securities in our margin account which have been entirely paid for. This is a matter of importance and where the stock has been fully paid for, it is taken out of the margin account and set aside in safekeeping. We will arrange to do this, as the liability in this respect is considerable in case we should have such shares in our margin account and were borrowing against them."

Evidence then elicited by Dr. Sellett in examining Mr. Curtis showed that the A.-O.F.C. had opened a safekeeping account with E. A. Pierce and Company in June of 1933. Previous to the opening of that account, Mr. Curtis said, there had only been one transaction of a safekeeping character between the two firms and that had taken place in 1930.

No Safekeeping Account
Having thus established the fact that the A.-O.F.C. had operated for several years without having any safekeeping account with E. A. Pierce and Company, and that all the transactions between the two firms both in margin and fully-paid stocks, had been through the medium of the regular or margin account which the A.-O.F.C. had with Pierce and Company, Dr. Sellett then took the witness in detail through the various transactions recorded in the A.-O.F.C.'s safekeeping account with Pierce and Company from the time it was opened in June, 1933 until the end of May, 1935, a few days after the A.-O.F.C. closed its doors.

Photostatic copies of the sheets of the safekeeping account in the ledger of E. A. Pierce and Company were introduced by Dr. Sellett and identified by Mr. Curtis as authentic records. The witness also identified sundry correspondence which had passed between the A.-O.F.C. and Pierce and Company relative to transfers of stocks into and from the safekeeping account as recorded on the ledger sheets. Most of this correspondence bore the signature of Mr. J. Warner Brown in his capacity as manager of the A.-O.F.C.

Dr. Sellett: Do the photostatic copies of the ledger sheets introduced here, and the correspondence relating to the entries therein, reflect all the safekeeping transactions which the A.-O.F.C. had with Pierce and Company between June, 1933 and the end of May, 1935?

Mr. Curtis: They do.

In reply to further questions, witness stated that shares of a value of U.S.$3 or more were accepted by Pierce and Company for hypothecation in the A.-O.F.C.'s margin account as from March 6, 1935.

The Jones Transaction
This point was introduced by the prosecution to show that the Electric Bond and Share stocks lost by a previous witness, Mr. C. R. Jones, were accepted in the margin account, whereas counsel for the defence had tried to show at an earlier session that shares of a value of U.S.$5 or less were not accepted in the margin account by E. A. Pierce and Company.

The only other witness yesterday was Mr. Hermann Aufwerber, who was recalled by the prosecution to testify to A.-O.F.C. dealings with Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland, a witness of the previous day.

Mr. Aufwerber, who was employed by the A.-O.F.C. as a salesman, said he had visited Mr. Kirkland several times in May, 1933 to solicit business. One day, Mr. Kirkland telephoned to him asking him to call. Witness duly called and Mr. Kirkland handed him certain scrip for transmission to E. A. Pierce and Company through the A.-O.F.C.

Wanted Scrip Held
Mr. Kirkland, explained, witness said, that he wanted the scrip held by Pierce and Company as he, Mr. Kirkland, had no facilities for handling it nor for collecting the accruing dividends. There was no reason for Mr. Kirkland to endorse a signature card, since he was neither selling nor buying.

Cross-examined by Mr. C. S. Franklin, who appears for Mr. J. Warner Brown, Mr. Aufwerber said that he got no commission and only bother out of the transaction with Mr. Kirkland. He took the business in the hope that it would lead to further business later on, business that would carry a commission.

The Court will sit again at 10 a.m. to-day.

D.

（批：Jule H.）

《字林西报》，1936年1月15日，星期三
13076

柯蒂斯就美亚金融公司证券保管事宜作证

雷文案昨日庭审证据显示，该公司在数年间未设立此类客户保管账户

美国驻华法院在审理已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）总裁弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和副总裁J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生所涉16项盗窃、挪用公款及欺诈指控时，昨日的庭审几乎全程用于听取旧金山E. A. Pierce公司C. C. 柯蒂斯（C. C. Curtis）先生的证词，内容涉及美亚金融公司在该公司开立的证券保管账户。

庭审于上午10时开始，至下午4时结束，中间按惯例午休。从公众角度来看，此次庭审显得索然无味。

庭审结束时，控方已提交本案第285号证物。据示，除周六和周日法院休庭外，若继续全天开庭，本案在1月24日（即中国新年）之前无法审结，甚至可能延至该日期之后。

柯蒂斯先生此前已数次出庭作证，此次经控方再次传唤，向法庭陈述了J·沃纳·布朗先生曾于1930年前往旧金山拜访他，旨在考察E. A. Pierce公司在股票交易方面的业务运作方式。

助理地区检察官塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）提交了一封布朗先生在旧金山写给上海雷文先生的信件，部分内容如下：

布朗先生的信件
“我已就全额付清的股票在我们保证金账户中的保管问题，分别与伍兹先生（Mr. Woods）和柯蒂斯先生进行了商讨。此事至关重要，凡已全额付清的股票，应从保证金账户中取出，单独列为保管账户。我们将安排此举，因为若此类股票留存在我们的保证金账户中并以此抵押借款，我们将承担巨大的责任。”

随后，塞莱特博士在讯问柯蒂斯先生时获得的证据显示，美亚金融公司于1933年6月在E. A. Pierce公司开立了证券保管账户。柯蒂斯先生称，在该账户开立之前，两家公司之间仅发生过一次具有保管性质的交易，且该交易发生在1930年。

无保管账户

既然已证实美亚金融公司在数年间未在E. A. Pierce公司设立任何证券保管账户，且两家公司之间所有涉及保证金股票和全额付清股票的交易，均通过美亚金融公司在Pierce公司开立的常规或保证金账户进行，塞莱特博士随后详细询问了证人，梳理了自1933年6月账户开立起，直至1935年5月底（即美亚金融公司停业后数日）止，美亚金融公司在Pierce公司证券保管账户中记录的各项交易。

塞莱特博士提交了E. A. Pierce公司分类账中证券保管账户页面的静电复印副本，并由柯蒂斯先生确认为真实记录。证人还辨认了美亚金融公司与Pierce公司之间关于股票转入和转出保管账户（如分类账页所记录）的各种往来信函。这些信函大多由J·沃纳·布朗先生以美亚金融公司经理的身份签署。

塞莱特博士：此处提交的分类账页静电复印副本，以及与之相关的往来信函，是否反映了美亚金融公司与Pierce公司在1933年6月至1935年5月底期间所有的证券保管交易？

柯蒂斯先生：是的。

在回答进一步提问时，证人表示，自1935年3月6日起，Pierce公司接受价值3美元或以上的美亚金融公司保证金账户股票作为抵押。

琼斯交易

控方提出这一点是为了表明，前一位证人C. R. 琼斯（C. R. Jones）先生所损失的电力债券与股票公司（Electric Bond and Share）股票曾被纳入保证金账户，而辩方律师曾在 earlier 庭审中试图证明，E. A. Pierce公司不接受价值5美元或以下的股票进入保证金账户。

昨天的另一位证人是赫尔曼·奥夫韦伯（Hermann Aufwerber）先生，他经控方再次传唤，就美亚金融公司与前一天出庭的证人斯坦利·G·柯克兰（Stanley G. Kirkland）先生之间的交易作证。

奥夫韦伯受雇于美亚金融公司担任推销员，他说自己曾在1933年5月多次拜访柯克兰先生以招揽业务。有一天，柯克兰先生打电话给他，请他过去一趟。证人随即前往，柯克兰先生交给他一些临时股票凭证（scrip），要求通过美亚金融公司转交给E. A. Pierce公司。

要求保管临时股票凭证

证人解释说，柯克兰先生希望将这些临时股票凭证交由Pierce公司保管，因为他本人既无设施处理这些凭证，也无法收取由此产生的股息。柯克兰先生没有理由签署签名卡，因为他既非卖出也非买入。

在代表J·沃纳·布朗先生出庭的C. S. 富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生的交叉盘问下，奥夫韦伯表示，他从与柯克兰先生的这笔交易中未获得任何佣金，只带来了麻烦。他承接这笔业务是希望日后能带来其他能产生佣金的业务。

法院将于今日上午10时再次开庭。

D.

（批注：Jule H.）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JANUARY 14, 1936
130-92

Two Further Witnesses In
Raven Case Testify

American Factory Representative Tells Of Loss Of
Sundry Shares Entrusted To The A.-O.F.C. For
Transmission To E. A. Pierce And Co.

Yesterday afternoon's session of the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown in the U. S. Court for China on 16 charges of theft, embezzlement and fraud saw the conclusion of testimony of the five victims of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation crash who are named in the indictment framed against the two defendants.

The only witness called during the afternoon session was Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland, local factory representative of the American Hardware Corporation, who related to the Court the circumstances under which he came to lose numerous shares of stock which he turned over to the A.-O.F.C. for transmission in safekeeping to E. A. Pierce and Company, New York.

Mr. Kirkland's evidence related to the 15th and 16th charges in the indictment, which allege the embezzlement and theft of 25 Socony-Vacuum shares, 25 I. T. and T. shares, 25 Packard Motor Car shares, 15 General Electric shares, 10 Studebaker Corporation shares and 2 3/8 Radio Corporation of America shares, belonging to Mr. Kirkland and placed in the custody of the A.-O.F.C. for safekeeping.

Knew Them By Sight

In answer to questions by Dr. George Sellett, Assistant U. S. District Attorney, Mr. Kirkland said he was 42 years of age and had resided in Shanghai since 1921. He knew the defendants by sight, but not personally.

In May, 1933, witness went on to relate, Mr. Hermann Aufwerber, a salesman of the A.-O.F.C., called at his office to solicit business and witness turned over to him the shares enumerated in the indictment. He instructed that these shares, which were registered in his name, be sent to E. A. Pierce and Company, New York, and Mr. Aufwerber gave him a receipt for the scrip.

Dr. Sellett (producing an A.-O.F.C. signature card): Did you ever see or sign a card of this type before the A.-O.F.C. closed down on May 23, 1935?
Witness: No.
Dr. Sellett: Why did you give your share certificates to Mr Aufwerber?
Witness: I wanted them sent to New York for my account. They were to be lodged with E. A. Pierce and Company, because I had no facilities for handling the dividends which accrued on them.

Certificates Forwarded

Mr. Kirkland then went on to say that he received a letter from the A.-O.F.C. (produced in Court) informing him that his share certificates had been forwarded to Pierce and Company, New York, by registered parcel post.

Dr. Sellett then produced a letter written by the A.-O.F.C. to Pierce and Company, advising despatch of the certificates. This letter, which was signed by Mr. J. Warner Brown, asked Pierce and Company to credit the A.-O.F.C. account with the shares.

Mr. Kirkland identified numerous statements which he had received from the A.-O.F.C. showing the shares as standing to his credit, also statements showing the dividends earned on them.
Dr. Sellett: Did you collect these dividends from the A.-O.F.C.?
Witness: No. I just left them there to accumulate.

Photostatic Copies

Dr. Sellett then produced photostatic copies of Mr. Kirkland's share certificates, upon which the witness identified the copy of his own signature of endorsement.
Dr. Sellett: Why did you endorse these certificates?
Witness: I endorsed them "in blank" to render them negotiable for transmission to E. A. Pierce and Company.
Dr. Sellett: Were these share certificates your property?
Witness: Absolutely. All the shares which they represented were fully paid for and were absolutely my property.
Dr. Sellett: Did you ever see them again after they had been handed to Mr. Aufwerber?
Witness: No, I never got them back.
Dr. Sellett: Did you ever authorize the A.-O.F.C. of either of the defendants to hypothecate, pledge or sell these shares:
Witness: I never did.

Never Received Value

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever receive from the A.-O.F.C. or either of the defendants the value of the certificates?
Witness: No.
Dr. Sellett: What was the approximate worth of the shares when you turned them over to the A.-O.F.C.?
Witness: About U. S. $2,500.
Mr. C. S. Franklin, who appears for Mr. J. Warner Brown, pointed out that this figure contradicted the figure given in the indictment, which is U. S. $1,007.92.
Dr. Sellett: Yes, the discrepancy is obvious, but I will prove the value at a later stage.
Judge Helmick: It is only necessary to prove that a value of U. S. $30 is involved.

Cross-Examination

Mr. Kirkland was then submitted to a lengthy cross-examination by Mr. Franklin as to what he understood was to happen to his shares when he handed them over to the A.-O.F.C. Witness said that he had chosen the A.-O.F.C. for the business instead of placing it with his bankers, the National City Bank of New York, merely because Mr. Aufwerber had called on him and solicited the business.
Mr. Franklin: But just why did you do it? Was it not because you contemplated trading in the shares?
Witness: No. I happened to know of Pierce and Company and I wanted them placed with that firm as I hadn't the facilities for handling accruing dividends. I travel a lot and am frequently out of town.

Reason For Endorsement

Mr. Franklin: If you did not intend trading in the shares, why did you endorse them and render them negotiable?
Witness: Simply because...

Mr. Franklin then drew the witness's attention to the fact that the receipt which he received from the A.-O.F.C. for the scrip did not mention Pierce and Company, merely stating that the shares had been received for Mr. Kirkland's New York stock account.
Witness: But I received a letter from the A.-O.F.C. enclosing a copy of a letter which they had sent to Pierce and Company when they forwarded the certificates to New York.

Whose Account?

Mr. Franklin: Did you not notice that in that letter which the A.-O.F.C. sent to Pierce and Company it was asked that the shares be credited to the account of the A.-O.F.C. and not to your account?
Witness: I gave it no consideration.
Mr. Franklin then referred to a statement which Mr. Kirkland had received from the Liquidator after the A.O.F.C. had closed down. This statement showed that Mr. Kirkland's shares had been sold on May 27, 1935, three days after the closure.
Mr. Franklin: I take it you did not authorize the sale of your shares?
Witness: I did not.
Mr. Franklin: Now, Mr. Kirkland, the statements sent to you by the A.-O.F.C. show that you were credited by the A.-O.F.C. with interest at the rate of three per cent. on your credit balance. Did that not indicate to you that the A.-O.F.C. was using your funds?

Not A Financier

Witness: It did not. I was not financing the A.-O.F.C. The interest allowed was on the dividends which accrued from my shares and which I did not collect. This had nothing to do with the shares themselves. It was my understanding that the shares were to be taken out of my name and transferred to the A.-O.F.C. so that the A.-O.F.C., through Pierce and Company, could collect the dividends for me.
Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. Raven, asked the witness where he kept the shares before turning them over to the A.-O.F.C.
"In my office safe," witness replied.
Under re-examination by Dr. Sellett, Mr. Kirkland said that when he received periodical statements from the A.-O.F.C., setting forth particulars of the shares which he had handed over to them for transmission to New York, he always understood that the shares were his own absolute property.

Mr. Yates Gives Evidence

At the morning session of the Court, testimony was taken from Mr. Gordon Yates, general shipping agent of the Glen Line, regarding a transaction with the A.-O.F.C. involving 100 Curtiss-Wright shares.
Mr. Yates' evidence was to the effect that he had paid the A.-O.F.C. for the purchase of these 100 shares in full, but had never received them. After the A.-O.F.C. had closed down, he was informed by the Liquidator that the shares had been sold on May 27, 1935. That was three days after the closure.
As in the case of previous witnesses, Mr. Yates declared that he had never authorized the A.-O.F.C. or either of the defendants to pledge, hypothecate or sell his shares or any of them.
The trial proceedings adjourned at 4.15 p.m. yesterday and will be resumed at 10 a.m. to-day. One of the government witnesses expected to be called to-day is Mr. C. J. Haley of San Francisco, who was formerly an official of the A.-O.F.C. Together with Mr. C. C. Curtis of E. A. Pierce and Company, he was brought to Shanghai specially for the purpose of testifying at the trial of Messrs. Raven and Brown.

《字林西报》，1936年1月14日，星期二
130-92

雷文案中又有两名证人作证

美国工厂代表讲述委托美亚金融公司转交E. A. Pierce公司的若干股票遗失经过

昨日午后，在美国驻华法院审理Frank J. Raven先生和J. Warner Brown先生被控盗窃、挪用公款及欺诈等16项罪名的庭审中，起诉书所列针对两名被告的五位美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）倒闭案受害人的证词全部陈述完毕。

下午庭审期间传唤的唯一证人是美国五金公司（American Hardware Corporation）驻沪工厂代表Stanley G. Kirkland先生，他向法庭陈述了他将多只股票交给美亚金融公司，委托其安全转交至纽约E. A. Pierce公司保管，结果导致股票遗失的经过。

Kirkland先生的证词涉及起诉书中的第15和第16项指控，这些指控称属于Kirkland先生并交由美亚金融公司保管的25股美孚真空石油公司（Socony-Vacuum）股票、25股国际电话电报公司（I. T. and T.）股票、25股帕卡德汽车公司（Packard Motor Car）股票、15股通用电气公司（General Electric）股票、10股斯图贝克公司（Studebaker Corporation）股票以及2又3/8股美国无线电公司（Radio Corporation of America）股票被挪用和盗窃。

仅面熟

在回答美国助理地区检察官George Sellett博士的提问时，Kirkland先生表示他今年42岁，自1921年起居住在上海。他对两名被告面熟，但并无私交。

证人接着叙述道，1933年5月，美亚金融公司的推销员Hermann Aufwerber先生来到他的办公室招揽业务，证人便将起诉书中列举的股票交给了他。他指示将这些登记在他名下的股票寄往纽约的E. A. Pierce公司，Aufwerber先生为此出具了一张收据。

Sellett博士（出示一张美亚金融公司的签名卡）：在美亚金融公司于1935年5月23日停业之前，您是否见过或签署过此类卡片？
证人：没有。
Sellett博士：您为何将股票证书交给Aufwerber先生？
证人：我希望将它们寄往纽约存入我的账户。它们将被存管于E. A. Pierce公司，因为我无法处理这些股票所产生的股息。

证书已寄出

Kirkland先生随后表示，他收到美亚金融公司的一封信（已在法庭出示），通知他他的股票证书已通过挂号包裹邮件寄往纽约的Pierce公司。

随后，Sellett博士出示了美亚金融公司写给Pierce公司的一封信，告知证书已发出。这封信由J. Warner Brown先生签署，要求Pierce公司将这些股票记入美亚金融公司的账户贷方。

Kirkland先生辨认了多份他收到的美亚金融公司对账单，显示这些股票记在他的贷方名下，还有显示这些股票所获股息的对账单。
Sellett博士：您是从美亚金融公司收取这些股息的吗？
证人：不。我只是让它们留在那里累积。

静电复印副本

随后，Sellett博士出示了Kirkland先生股票证书的静电复印副本，证人在上面辨认出了他自己背书签名的复印件。
Sellett博士：您为何在这些证书上背书？
证人：我进行了“空白”背书，以便使其可流通，从而转交给E. A. Pierce公司。
Sellett博士：这些股票证书是您的财产吗？
证人：绝对是。它们所代表的所有股份均已全额付清，绝对是我的财产。
Sellett博士：在交给Aufwerber先生之后，您还见过它们吗？
证人：没有，我从未收回它们。
Sellett博士：您是否曾授权美亚金融公司或任何一名被告抵押、质押或出售这些股票？
证人：我从未这样做过。

从未获得对价

Sellett博士：您是否曾从美亚金融公司或任何一名被告那里收到这些证书的价值款项？
证人：没有。
Sellett博士：当您将这些股票交给美亚金融公司时，它们的大致价值是多少？
证人：大约2,500美元。
代表J. Warner Brown先生出庭的C. S. Franklin先生指出，这一数字与起诉书中列明的1,007.92美元不符。
Sellett博士：是的，差异显而易见，但我将在后续阶段证明其价值。
Helmick法官：只需证明涉及的价值超过30美元即可。

交叉质询

随后，Franklin先生对Kirkland先生进行了长时间的交叉质询，询问他在将股票交给美亚金融公司时，认为这些股票会发生什么情况。证人表示，他选择美亚金融公司办理此项业务，而不是交给他的银行——纽约国家城市银行（National City Bank of New York），仅仅是因为Aufwerber先生拜访了他并招揽了这笔业务。
Franklin先生：但您究竟为何这样做？难道不是因为您打算交易这些股票吗？
证人：不是。我碰巧知道Pierce公司，并且希望将它们存放在该公司，因为我无法处理累积的股息。我经常出差，经常不在本市。

背书的原因

Franklin先生：如果您不打算交易这些股票，为何要对其进行背书并使其可流通？
证人： simply because...（原文此处似有缺漏或语意未尽，直译为：仅仅因为……）

随后，Franklin先生提请证人注意，他从美亚金融公司收到的关于该证券的收据并未提及Pierce公司，仅说明已收到用于Kirkland先生纽约股票账户的股票。
证人：但我收到了美亚金融公司的一封信，信中附有一份他们在将证书寄往纽约时发给Pierce公司的信件副本。

谁的账户？

Franklin先生：您没有注意到，在美亚金融公司发给Pierce公司的那封信中，要求将股票记入美亚金融公司的账户，而不是您的账户吗？
证人：我没有考虑这一点。
Franklin先生随后提及Kirkland先生在美亚金融公司停业后从清算人那里收到的一份对账单。该对账单显示，Kirkland先生的股票已于1935年5月27日售出，即停业后的三天。
Franklin先生：我想您并未授权出售您的股票？
证人：我没有。
Franklin先生：那么，Kirkland先生，美亚金融公司发送给您的对账单显示，美亚金融公司按百分之三的利率将利息记入您的贷方余额。这难道没有向您表明美亚金融公司正在使用您的资金吗？

并非金融家

证人：并没有。我并不是在为美亚金融公司提供融资。允许的利息是针对我的股票产生而我未领取的股息。这与股票本身无关。我的理解是，股票将从我的名下取出并转让给美亚金融公司，以便美亚金融公司通过Pierce公司为我收取股息。
Raven先生的辩护律师Richard T. Evans先生询问证人在将股票交给美亚金融公司之前将其存放在何处。
“在我办公室的保险箱里，”证人回答。
在Sellett博士的再次讯问下，Kirkland先生表示，当他收到美亚金融公司定期发出的对账单，详述他交给他们转寄纽约的股票明细时，他一直认为这些股票是他绝对的私有财产。

Yates先生作证

在上午的庭审中，Glen Line轮船公司的总航运代理Gordon Yates先生就涉及100股柯蒂斯-莱特公司（Curtiss-Wright）股票的一笔与美亚金融公司的交易提供了证词。
Yates先生的证词大意是，他已全额支付美亚金融公司以购买这100股股票，但从未收到股票。在美亚金融公司停业后，他被告知清算人，这些股票已于1935年5月27日售出。那是停业后的三天。
与之前的证人一样，Yates先生声明，他从未授权美亚金融公司或任何一名被告质押、抵押或出售他的股票或其中任何部分。
庭审于昨日下午4点15分休庭，将于今日上午10点继续。预计今日传唤的一名政府证人是来自旧金山的C. J. Haley先生，他曾是美亚金融公司的一名官员。他与E. A. Pierce公司的C. C. Curtis先生一同被特意带到上海，目的是在Raven和Brown先生的案件审判中作证。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JANUARY 11, 1936

S.M.P. Officer Testifies
At Continuance Of Raven
Trial In The U.S. Court

Witness Tells How He Intended To Sell His Shares
Which A.-O.F.C. Held, But Raven Crash Killed
Project; Shares Gone And Money With Them

TESTIMONY BY CURTIS SHOWS THAT RAVEN
FIRM PLEDGED FULLY-PAID STOCKS

Court proceedings in the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven
and Mr. J. Warner Brown on charges of theft, embezzlement
and fraud were somewhat enlivened yesterday after the
preceding dull session by the dry humour of Mr. Charles
Robert Jones, an officer of the Shanghai Municipal Police,
who was called by the prosecution to testify to his transac-
tions with the American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

The testimony of Mr. Jones re-
lated to Counts 12, 13 and 14 in the
indictment of the defendants, who
are being tried before Judge Milton
J. Helmick in the United States
Court for China. These counts
charge the defendants with em-
bezzlement of a cheque for
Sh.$549.18, drawn by Mr. Jones on
the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank-
ing Corporation in favour of the
American-Oriental Finance Cor-
poration, embezzlement of the pro-
ceeds of the cheque, and theft of
the cheque itself.

The cheque, according to the
testimony, was given to the A.-
O.F.C. by Mr. Jones in full pay-
ment of 50 shares of Electric Bond
and Share stocks, but Mr. Jones
never received the shares, nor was
the money refunded to him.

Mr. Jones Testifies

Stating that he was a British
subject, 32 years of age, and that
he had been in the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police for six years, Mr.
Jones told the Court, in reply to
questions by Dr. George Sellett,
Assistant District Attorney, that
he was acquainted with both de-
fendants, but that he was better
acquainted with Mr. Brown than
with Mr. Raven.

His dealings with the A.-O.F.C.,
witness went on, commenced in
August, 1931, when he bought 57
shares of stock in the A.-O.F.C.
It was in 1932, however, that he
started dealing in New York stocks
through the A.-O.F.C. He con-
tinued such dealings until the A.-
O.F.C. closed down in May, 1935.

Mr. Jones identified a signature
card of the A.-O.F.C. which he had
signed when he commenced dealing
in New York stocks. It was dated
February 29, 1932. He also iden-
tified his signature on the reverse
side of the card, which was a gen-
eral form of hypothecation.

Dr. Sellett: What were the cir-
cumstances which led you to start
business with the A.-O.F.C.?

Easy Money Waiting

Witness: I started dealing with
them when I received a letter from
the bank saying that there was
easy money to be made.

Dr. Sellett: When you say you
received a letter from the bank,
do you mean you received it from
the A.-O.F.C.?

Witness: To me the bank
(American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration) and the A.-O.F.C. were
one.

Prosecuting counsel then asked
Mr. Jones whether he recalled
what his position was with the
A.-O.F.C. early in March, 1935.
(Continued on Page 5, Col. 1.)

"Only Too Well"

Asked if he could recall what
his first stock transaction had
been, Mr. Jones said he remem-
bered it only too well because he
had lost money on it. It was a
venture in Canadian Pacific Rail-
way shares. He then bought
shares of General Motors in an
effort to recoup his loss. These
were bought at 20, but they
slumped to 7.13. Later, however,
they soared to 30, but he sold out
when they stood at 22.

Fully paid up shares which he
acquired through the A.-O.F.C.,
witness said, were lodged by him
with the A.-O.F.C. as security for
further trading.

Coming to his several dealings
in Electric Bond And Share,
witness told the Court that he
bought them at a rock bottom
price.

"When they rose, I intended
selling them and buying a car
with the proceeds. But the bank
closed and I did not get my car."

Mr. Thomas Waung, accountant
of the A.-O.F.C. was then recalled
by the Assistant District Attorney
and spent some time on the
witness-stand identifying office
documents and accounts relating
to the transactions between the
A.-O.F.C. and the previous wit-
ness.

Shares Under U.S.$5

Under cross-examination by
Mr. Franklin, witness disclosed
the fact that customers of the
A.-O.F.C. had to pay cash for all
shares of stock which were of a
lesser value than U.S. $5.

Mr. Franklin: Why was that?
Witness: Because F. A. Pierce
and Company would make no loans
against such shares. Shares of
less than U.S. $5 had no loan
value.

Dr. Sellett: But Pierce and
Company accepted hypothecation
of such shares?
Witness: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: In other words,
such shares were accepted in the
margin account which the A.-O.-
F.C. had with Pierce and Com-
pany?
Witness: Yes.

Mr. Franklin thereupon drew
the Court's attention to the fact
that the witness had given con-
trary answers to two questions
which were in essence the same.

Ask Mr. Curtis

Mr. Waung: You had better
ask Mr. Curtis to answer these
questions. He is the representative
of Pierce and Company and knows
the position better than I do.

During the course of yesterday's
proceedings, Mr. C. S. Franklin
addressed the Court with a com-
plaint, to the effect that the
defence was being treated unfair-
ly.

"We have been very seriously
handicapped," counsel declared,
"by not having at our disposal
any of the documents which will
prove the defendants' entire in-
nocence. Even witnesses who have
been called for the Government
have been cautioned against an-
swering any questions put by us."

In reply, Dr. Sellett said that
in such a case as the one now
being tried the defence would
would naturally refrain from dis-
cussing the matter with Govern-
ment witnesses, and from question-
ing them.

"Only too well," witness prompt-
ly returned. "I had to my credit
50 fully paid up Electric Bond and
Share stocks. Previously the A.-
O.F.C. had delivered to me 200 of
these shares for which I had paid
in full. That was a few weeks be-
fore the bank closed."

Continuing, the witness said he
had received monthly ledger state-
ments showing his position with
the A.-O.F.C. He then went on to
describe the transaction in the 50
Electric Bond and Share stocks
which he said he had fully paid for
but never received.

Transaction Described

Witness ordered these shares on
February 28, 1935, and in due
course received a notification from
the A.-O.F.C. to the effect that the
shares had been purchased for his
account and asking him to pay
them the cost of same, namely,
U.S.$210.12. That was on March
14, 1935. Thereupon witness drew
a cheque on the Hongkong and
Shanghai Banking Corporation for
the equivalent amount in Shang-
hai dollars. The amount of that
cheque, which he delivered to the
A.-O.F.C., was $549.18 and it in-
cluded an amount of U.S.$2 which
he owed the A.-O.F.C. for the
cost of a cable. He received from
the A.-O.F.C. a receipt for the
cheque.

The cancelled cheque for the
amount in question was produced
by Dr. Sellett and the witness
identified it as the one which he
had delivered to the A.-O.F.C. and
with which his account with the
Hongkong and Shanghai Banking
Corporation had been debited.

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever receive
the 50 Electric Bond and Share
stocks which you paid for with that
cheque?

Did Not Set Shares

Witness: I did not. When I
heard that the A.-O.F.C. had gone
smash I sent them a letter, in-
structing that under no circum-
stances were my 50 shares to be
disposed of in any way.

Dr. Sellett: Did you get the
shares then?

Witness: No. I received a reply
stating that the affairs of the A.-
O.F.C. were being placed in the
hands of a liquidator.

Dr. Sellett: Did you get back the
money which you had paid for the
50 shares?

Witness: I did not.

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever at any
time authorize the A.-O.F.C. or
either of the defendants to pledge
or hypothecate those shares?

Witness: I did not.

Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for
Mr. J. Warner Brown, then rose to
cross-examine Mr. Jones and ques-
tioned the latter in detail as to his
various transactions with the A.-
O.F.C.

《字林西报》，1936年1月11日，星期六

上海公共租界工部局警务处警官作证
在美国法院继续审理雷文案期间

证人讲述其拟出售由美亚金融公司持有的股份，但雷文公司倒闭致使计划落空；股份与钱款均告失踪

柯蒂斯提供的证词显示雷文公司将已缴足股款的股票进行了抵押

在针对弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生提出的盗窃、挪用公款及欺诈指控的审判中，昨日的法庭程序因上海公共租界工部局警务处警官查尔斯·罗伯特·琼斯（Charles Robert Jones）先生的冷幽默而略显活跃，此前一天的庭审较为沉闷。检方传唤琼斯先生出庭，就其与美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的交易作证。

琼斯先生的证词涉及被告起诉书中的第12、13和14项指控，被告正由中国美国法院（United States Court for China）的米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官审理。这些指控指称被告挪用了琼斯先生开具给汇丰银行（Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation）、收款人为美亚金融公司的一张金额为上海银元549.18元的支票，挪用了该支票的收益，并窃取了支票本身。

据证词所述，这张支票是琼斯先生交给美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.），作为全额支付50股电力债券与股票公司（Electric Bond and Share）股票的款项，但琼斯先生从未收到这些股票，钱款也未退还给他。

琼斯先生作证

琼斯先生陈述自己是英国臣民，现年32岁，已在上海公共租界工部局警务处任职六年。他在回答助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士的提问时告诉法庭，他认识两名被告，但与布朗先生比与雷文先生更为熟识。

证人接着说，他与美亚金融公司的交易始于1931年8月，当时他购买了57股该公司的股票。然而，他是从1932年开始通过美亚金融公司交易纽约股票的。此类交易一直持续到1935年5月美亚金融公司停业为止。

琼斯先生辨认了一张美亚金融公司的签名卡，这是他在开始交易纽约股票时签署的，日期为1932年2月29日。他还辨认了卡片背面的自己的签名，那是一份通用的抵押表格。

塞莱特博士：是什么情况促使你开始与美亚金融公司做生意的？

轻松赚钱的机会在等待

证人：当我收到银行来信说可以轻松赚钱时，我就开始与他们打交道了。

塞莱特博士：当你说收到银行的来信时，你是指从美亚金融公司收到的吗？

证人：对我来说，银行（美亚银行公司 American-Oriental Banking Corporation）和美亚金融公司是一回事。

随后，公诉律师询问琼斯先生是否记得1935年3月初他在美亚金融公司的地位如何。（续见第5栏第1栏。）

“再清楚不过了”

当被问及是否记得他的第一笔股票交易是什么时，琼斯先生说他对那笔交易记忆犹新，因为他在那笔交易中亏了钱。那是一次投资加拿大太平洋铁路（Canadian Pacific Railway）股票的交易。随后，为了弥补损失，他购买了通用汽车（General Motors）的股票。这些股票是以20美元的价格买入的，但随后跌至7.13美元。不过后来股价飙升至30美元，但他在股价处于22美元时全部卖出。

证人表示，他通过美亚金融公司获得的已缴足股款的股票，被他存放在美亚金融公司，作为进一步交易的担保。

谈到他在电力债券与股票公司（Electric Bond And Share）的几笔交易时，证人告诉法庭，他是在底价时买入这些股票的。

“当股价上涨时，我打算卖掉它们，用所得款项买一辆汽车。但银行倒闭了，我也没买到车。”

随后，助理地区检察官再次传唤美亚金融公司的会计师黄汤姆斯（Thomas Waung）先生，他在证人席上花了一些时间辨认与前一位证人之间交易相关的办公室文件和账目。

股价低于5美元的股票

在富兰克林（Franklin）先生的盘问下，证人透露，美亚金融公司的客户必须为所有价值低于5美元的股票支付现金。

富兰克林先生：为什么会这样？
证人：因为F. A. 皮尔斯公司（F. A. Pierce and Company）不会以这类股票作为抵押发放贷款。价值低于5美元的股票没有贷款价值。

塞莱特博士：但是皮尔斯公司接受这类股票的抵押？
证人：是的。

塞莱特博士：换句话说，这类股票被计入美亚金融公司在皮尔斯公司开立的保证金账户中？
证人：是的。

富兰克林先生随即提请法庭注意，证人对两个本质相同的问题给出了相互矛盾的回答。

询问柯蒂斯先生

黄先生：你最好请柯蒂斯（Curtis）先生来回答这些问题。他是皮尔斯公司的代表，比我更了解情况。

在昨天的诉讼过程中，C. S. 富兰克林先生向法庭提出投诉，大意是辩方受到了不公平对待。

辩护律师宣称：“我们受到严重阻碍，因为我们无法获取任何能证明被告完全无辜的文件。甚至政府传唤的证人也被警告不要回答我们要提出的问题。”

对此，塞莱特博士回答说，在目前审理的这种案件中，辩方自然会避免与政府证人讨论此事，并避免向他们提问。

“再清楚不过了，”证人立即回答道。“我有50股已缴足股款的电力债券与股票公司股票记在贷方。在此之前，美亚金融公司曾向我交付过200股此类股票，我已全额付款。那是在银行倒闭前几周。”

证人继续说，他收到了显示其在美亚金融公司账户状况的月度分类账对账单。随后，他描述了那50股电力债券与股票公司股票的交易，他说他已全额付款但从未收到股票。

描述交易过程

证人于1935年2月28日订购了这些股票，并在适当时候收到美亚金融公司的通知，称股票已为其账户购入，并要求他支付成本，即210.12美元。那是1935年3月14日。于是，证人向汇丰银行开具了一张等值上海银元的支票。他交给美亚金融公司的这张支票金额为549.18元，其中包括他欠美亚金融公司的2美元电报费。他从美亚金融公司收到了该支票的收据。

塞莱特博士出示了涉案金额的注销支票，证人辨认出这就是他交给美亚金融公司并从其汇丰银行账户中扣款的支票。

塞莱特博士：你是否收到过你用那张支票付款的50股电力债券与股票公司股票？

未获得股票

证人：没有。当我听说美亚金融公司破产时，我给他们写了一封信，指示在任何情况下都不得处置我的那50股股票。

塞莱特博士：那你后来拿到股票了吗？

证人：没有。我收到回复称，美亚金融公司的事务已移交给清算人处理。

塞莱特博士：你收回为这50股股票支付的款项了吗？

证人：没有。

塞莱特博士：你是否曾在任何时候授权美亚金融公司或两名被告中的任何一人抵押或质押那些股票？

证人：没有。

随后，J·沃纳·布朗先生的辩护律师C. S. 富兰克林先生起身对琼斯先生进行盘问，并就其与美亚金融公司的各种交易细节对后者进行了质询。

page_data.en:
No Obstruction Intended
"The Government does not wish to prevent the defence from obtaining any evidence which might be helpful to them. They can question our witnesses on the witness-stand as much as they like. After all, it is obvious that certain witnesses are Government witnesses and I think the usual practice is to stay away from such witnesses in the same way that the prosecution would not presume to get into contact with witnesses whom the defence propose to call."
Judge Helmick: If the defence calls for any specific document, the Government will certainly produce it, but it is unreasonable to expect them to go over a wide, unspecified area in a general hope of something turning up.
Another feature of yesterday's proceedings was a heated altercation between the prosecution and the defence as to whether the A.-O.F.C. carried out all requests by clients for transfer of shares from its general, or margin, account with E. A. Pierce and Company to the safekeeping account or to any other account which clients might specify.
This arose from the morning testimony of Mr. Thomas Waung, A.-O.F.C. accountant, which dealt with the transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Lucien C. M. Basset, French exchange broker, who gave evidence at a previous session, regarding his loss of approximately U.S. $50,000 as a result of transactions with the A.-O.F.C.

Stocks In Margin
Prosecuting counsel elicited from Mr. Yaung the fact that the A.-O.F.C. had both a safekeeping account and a margin account with E. A. Pierce and Company, but that all of Mr. Basset's stocks, for which he had paid the A.-O.F.C. in full, were placed in the margin account.
Under cross-examination by Mr. Franklin, Mr. Waung stated that share were put into the safekeeping account only when customers of the A.-O.F.C. so requested. Counsel than asked the witness to prepare a list of all share transfers to safekeeping, or for registry and delivery to clients, from December 1, 1933 to May 23, 1935, when the A.-O.F.C. closed its doors.
Mr. Waung: There were many requests for such transfers.
Mr. Franklin: Were all such requests fulfilled?
Mr. Waung: Yes.
Mr. Franklin: Up to the very time the A.-O.F.C. closed its doors?
Mr. Waung: Yes.
Mr. Franklin: Was Mr. Basset notified of all changes in his account and of its status at all times?
Mr. Waung: Yes.

Basset Not Informed
Dr. Sellett: Did notices to Mr. Basset inform him that his transactions were in the general, or margin, account, and that his shares had not been fully paid for by the A.-O.F.C.?
Mr. Waung: No.
Dr. Sellett: Was Mr. Basset informed that his shares had been hypothecated to Pierce and Company?
Mr. Waung: No.
Mr. Franklin: Would Mr. Basset have been notified if his shares had been put in the safekeeping account?
Mr. Waung: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: With reference to Mr. Franklin's request that Mr. Waung prepare a list of share transfers, the Government would be glad to comply, if the defendants through their counsel will inform us where requests for such transfers may be found.
Mr. Franklin: Are you suggest-
ing that such requests were not carried out?

Unable To Re-Finance
Dr. Sellett: I will prove that one was not carried out, except slowly, over a period of months, because the A.-O.F.C. was not in a position to do the necessary re-financing.
Mr. C. C. Curtis of E. A. Pierce and Company was then re-called and identified various letters which he had sent to the A.-O.F.C. confirming the purchase of Mr. Basset's stocks. Mr. Franklin subjected the witness to a lengthy cross-examination on the subject of the margin account which the A.-O.F.C. with E. A. Pierce and Company.
Mr. Franklin: If Mr. Basset had requested the A.-O.F.C. to transfer his shares, on May 23, 1935, to the safekeeping account with Pierce and Company, and the request had been transmitted to you, would this have been done?
Witness: It would if the A.-O.F.C. had sufficient margin with us.
Mr. Franklin: Did they on that date—the date on which the A.-O.F.C. closed—have sufficient margin?
Witness: I don't think so.
Dr. Sellett: The Basset shares were at all times pledged to E. A. Pierce and Company?
Witness: Yes.

Leeway Allowed
Dr. Sellett: How much did you usually allow the A.-O.F.C. to be undermargined?
Witness: Usually not more than U.S. $15,000 to U.S. $20,000.
Mr. Waung was again recalled and identified initials on letters received by the A.-O.F.C. from Mr. Curtis. One set he identified as those of Mr. J. Warner Brown.
Mr. Curtis was followed on the witness-stand by Mr. Hermann Aufwerber, Austrian salesman employed by the A.-O.F.C., who had put through the transactions of the corporation with Mr. Basset.
This witness testified that all the orders for stocks which he secured, including those from Mr. Basset, were initialled by Mr. J. Warner Brown before being placed in the locked order box at the A.-O.F.C. offices.
Continuing, the witness related how Mr. Basset had on one occasion asked him if his (Mr. Basset's) shares held by the A.-O.F.C. were safe.

Asked At Office
Witness, as far as he could recollect, inquired of one of the A.-O.F.C. officials, since it was his habit, when a customer made an inquiry, to get the information sought at the office and not assume personal responsibility by answering without reference to his superiors.
"I was told at the office on this occasion," Mr. Aufwerber said, "that Mr. Basset's shares were in the safekeeping account as distinct from the margin account. I do not remember which of the officials gave me this information."
On another occasion, witness said, he had a conversation with Mr. Samuel Sievertz, an official of the A.-O.F.C. who was in charge of the collection of margin. At that time the New York market had taken a drop and he was asked to collect margin. But later Mr. Sievertz told him everything was alright since they could use the Basset account, the A.-O.F.C. being "good enough for a day or two."

Procedure Attacked
"I answered that this was not right and that all fully paid shares, including Mr. Basset's, must be kept separate."
Replying to further questions, witness said that the A.-O.F.C. had employed seven or eight salesmen, foreign and Chinese. He started with the firm at a salary of $150 a month. The second month he got $200. Later on, he worked exclusively on a commission basis and earned on the average over $1,000 per month.
Cross-examined by Mr. Franklin, Mr. Aufwerber said the conversation with Mr. Sievertz to which he had referred took place in October or November, 1934 but he could not remember exactly when. Sievertz went on leave and when he returned to Shanghai, witness said to him: "You have put me in a hell of a mess."
Mr. Franklin: I don't want to hear about that. I want you to tell me when your conversation with Mr. Sievertz took place.
Witness: I don't recollect. It was in October or November. I remember that because it was just after Mr. Sievertz returned.
Mr. Leon Feingold, accountant of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, was then recalled by Dr. Sellett and testified that a cheque drawn by Mr. Basset for U.S. $11,553 in favour of the A.-O.F.C. had been paid in and credited to the account of the latter on December 18, 1923.
Dr. Sellett: From the bank ledger it appears that the cheque was cashed?
Witness: Yes.
Yesterday's session of the Court lasted until 4.15 p.m. and Judge Helmick then ordered an adjournment until 10 a.m. on Monday.
page_data.zh:
无意阻挠
“政府并不希望阻止辩方获取任何可能对他们有帮助的证据。他们可以在证人席上随意盘问我们的证人。毕竟，某些证人是政府方面的证人，这是显而易见的，我认为通常的做法是回避此类证人，正如控方不会 presumptuously（擅自）去接触辩方拟传唤的证人一样。”
赫尔米克法官：如果辩方要求提供任何特定文件，政府肯定会予以出示，但指望他们在广泛且未指定的范围内进行搜寻，以期偶然发现某些东西，这是不合理的。
昨日庭审的另一特点是，控方与辩方就亚美远东公司（A.-O.F.C.）是否执行了客户将所有股份从其与 E. A. Pierce 公司的普通账户或保证金账户转移至保管账户或客户指定的任何其他账户的所有请求，发生了激烈的争执。
这一争议源于亚美远东公司会计师 Thomas Waung 先生上午的证词，其内容涉及亚美远东公司与法国汇兑经纪人 Lucien C. M. Basset 先生之间的交易。Basset 先生曾在之前的庭审中作证，称因与亚美远东公司的交易损失了约 50,000 美元。

保证金股票
控方律师从 Yaung 先生处获悉，亚美远东公司在 E. A. Pierce 公司既设有保管账户，也设有保证金账户，但 Basset 先生已全额付款给亚美远东公司的所有股票，均被放入了保证金账户。
在 Franklin 先生的交叉询问下，Waung 先生表示，只有当亚美远东公司的客户提出请求时，股票才会被放入保管账户。随后，律师要求证人编制一份清单，列出从 1933 年 12 月 1 日至 1935 年 5 月 23 日亚美远东公司停业期间，所有转移至保管账户、或为注册及交付给客户而转移的股票。
Waung 先生：有许多此类转移请求。
Franklin 先生：所有这些请求都得到履行了吗？
Waung 先生：是的。
Franklin 先生：直到亚美远东公司停业的那一刻？
Waung 先生：是的。
Franklin 先生：Basset 先生是否随时获知其账户的所有变更及其状态？
Waung 先生：是的。

未通知 Basset
Sellett 博士：发给 Basset 先生的通知是否告知他，他的交易是在普通账户或保证金账户中进行的，且亚美远东公司并未为其股票全额付款？
Waung 先生：没有。
Sellett 博士：Basset 先生是否得知他的股票已被抵押给 Pierce 公司？
Waung 先生：没有。
Franklin 先生：如果 Basset 先生的股票被放入保管账户，他会收到通知吗？
Waung 先生：会的。
Sellett 博士：关于 Franklin 先生要求 Waung 先生编制股票转移清单一事，如果被告通过其律师告知我们在哪里可以找到此类转移请求，政府乐意配合。
Franklin 先生：您是在暗示这些请求未被执行吗？

无法再融资
Sellett 博士：我将证明有一项请求未被执行，或者说是在数月内缓慢执行的，因为亚美远东公司无力进行必要的再融资。
随后，E. A. Pierce 公司的 C. C. Curtis 先生再次出庭作证，并辨认了他发送给亚美远东公司、确认购买 Basset 先生股票的多封信件。Franklin 先生就亚美远东公司与 E. A. Pierce 公司之间的保证金账户问题，对证人进行了长时间的交叉询问。
Franklin 先生：如果 Basset 先生在 1935 年 5 月 23 日要求亚美远东公司将他的股票转移至 Pierce 公司的保管账户，且该请求已转达给您，这会执行吗？
证人：如果亚美远东公司在我们这里有足够的保证金，就会执行。
Franklin 先生：在那一天——即亚美远东公司停业之日——他们有足够的保证金吗？
证人：我想没有。
Sellett 博士：Basset 的股票是否一直质押给 E. A. Pierce 公司？
证人：是的。

允许的余地
Sellett 博士：你们通常允许亚美远东公司的保证金不足额度是多少？
证人：通常不超过 15,000 至 20,000 美元。
Waung 先生再次被传唤出庭，辨认了亚美远东公司收到的来自 Curtis 先生的信件上的首字母缩写。其中一组他辨认为 J. Warner Brown 先生的首字母。
Curtis 先生之后出庭作证的是 Hermann Aufwerber 先生，他是受雇于亚美远东公司的奥地利籍销售员，负责处理该公司与 Basset 先生之间的交易。
这位证人作证说，他经手的所有股票订单，包括来自 Basset 先生的订单，在放入亚美远东公司办公室的上锁订单箱之前，均由 J. Warner Brown 先生签署首字母。
接着，证人讲述了 Basset 先生曾有一次问他，由亚美远东公司持有的（Basset 先生的）股票是否安全。

在办公室询问
据证人回忆，他向亚美远东公司的一位官员进行了查询，因为他的习惯是，当客户提出询问时，要在办公室获取所需信息，而不是在不请示上级的情况下自行回答从而承担个人责任。
Aufwerber 先生说：“这次我在办公室被告知，Basset 先生的股票是在保管账户中，区别于保证金账户。我不记得是哪位官员告诉我的这个信息。”
证人还说，在另一次场合，他与亚美远东公司负责收取保证金的官员 Samuel Sievertz 先生进行过谈话。当时纽约市场下跌，他被要求去收取保证金。但后来 Sievertz 先生告诉他一切正常，因为他们可以使用 Basset 的账户，亚美远东公司“还能撑一两天”。

程序受到抨击
“我回答说这不对，所有已全额付款的股票，包括 Basset 先生的，必须分开存放。”
在回答进一步的问题时，证人表示亚美远东公司雇佣了七八名销售员，包括外籍和华人。他刚加入该公司时月薪为 150 美元。第二个月他拿到了 200 美元。后来，他完全按佣金制工作，平均每月收入超过 1,000 美元。
在 Franklin 先生的交叉询问下，Aufwerber 先生表示，他提到的与 Sievertz 先生的谈话发生在 1934 年 10 月或 11 月，但他记不清确切时间。Sievertz 去休假了，当他回到上海时，证人对他说：“你让我陷入了一团糟。”
Franklin 先生：我不想听那些。我要你告诉我你与 Sievertz 先生的谈话是什么时候发生的。
证人：我不记得了。是在 10 月或 11 月。我记得是因为那正好是 Sievertz 先生回来之后。
随后，Sellett 博士再次传唤美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）会计师 Leon Feingold 先生出庭作证。他证实，Basset 先生开具的一张金额为 11,553 美元、收款人为亚美远东公司的支票，已于 1923 年 12 月 18 日存入并贷记入后者的账户。
Sellett 博士：从银行分类账来看，这张支票似乎已兑现？
证人：是的。
昨日的庭审持续至下午 4:15，随后赫尔米克法官宣布休庭，直至周一上午 10 点继续。

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JANUARY 9, 1936

Broker Tells Court How
Faith In Mr. Raven Cost
Him Loss Of Large Sum

Testimony Given By Mr. Lucien Basset At Trial Of
Messrs. Raven And Brown Discloses Limitless
Confidence In Former Finance Magnate

VICTIM DID EXTENSIVE BUSINESS WITH THE
A.-O.F.C. BUT NEVER VISITED OFFICE

Evidence showing how a customer of the now defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation lost approximately U.S. $50,000 largely as a result of reposing unlimited confidence in that institution due to the reputation of its President, Mr. Frank J. Raven, was given yesterday in the United States Court for China, when Mr. Lucien Claude Marie Basset, prominent local French exchange broker, testified to his stock transactions with the A.-O.F.C. at the continued hearing of the 16 charges of theft, fraud and embezzlement which have been preferred against Mr. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, who was Vice-President of the A.-O.F.C.

The Court was in recess in the morning and the fourth session in the case commenced at 2 p.m. in a courtroom crowded with prominent representatives of the local community of stock and exchange brokers, who are evincing a lively interest in the proceedings. The entire session was devoted to the examination of Mr. Basset by Dr. George Sellett, Assistant U.S. District Attorney, and cross-examination by Mr. C. S. Franklin and Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for the defendants.

Speaking in halting English with an obvious French accent, Mr. Basset told the Court that he commenced dealing with the A.-O.F.C. in the latter part of 1933 through one of the A.-O.F.C.'s salesmen, a Mr. Aufwerber.

Was A Neighbour

Mr. Aufwerber, he said, was a neighbour of his. The first transaction with the A.-O.F.C. was put through, however, in Mr. Basset's office in the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank Building.

The first step taken was Mr. Basset's signature of the customary "signature card" form which the A.-O.F.C. used for all transactions with clients.

Dr. Sellett drew the witness's attention to the fact that this card, produced in Court, was not signed on the reverse side by Mr. Basset. It was dated November 11, 1933.

"Why did you not sign the card on the reverse side, in the space provided for signature?" Dr. Sellett asked the witness.

Witness: I did not sign on the reverse side because the business which I intended doing with the A.-O.F.C. was to be cash business and not a margin business. The reverse side of the card related to the margin type of transactions.

In reply to further questions by Dr. Sellett, Mr. Basset went on to describe numerous stock transactions which he had with the A.-O.F.C., in which he purchased and sold blocks of stock in the American Telephone and Telegraph Company and the Western Union Telegraph Company. Witness also identified numerous order slips, advices and statements relating to these transactions upon which his signature appeared and which were offered as exhibits by prosecuting counsel.

Memos Received

All orders, witness told the Court, were placed through Mr. Aufwerber. "When I placed an order for stocks I always received from the A.-O.F.C. a debit memo for the cost of the cable to San Francisco. Similar debit notes were sent to me when I gave orders for the sale of stocks or for the cancellation of orders which I had placed."

Dr. Sellett: After you had placed orders, did you always receive from the A.-O.F.C. notifications that the stocks you had ordered had been purchased for your account?

Witness: I did.

Mr. Basset then went on to describe a transaction involving the payment by him to the A.-O.F.C. of U.S. $11,553 by means of a draft drawn by the Shanghai office of the Banque Franco-Chinoise on the Irving Trust Company in New York.

Messrs. Raven and Brown are charged with embezzlement and theft of this draft and with feloniously defrauding Mr. Basset by having falsely pretended and represented to him that the A.-O.F.C. had, on or about December 16, 1933, purchased for him 100 shares of American Telephone and Telegraph stock of the reasonable worth and value of U.S. $11,-553, represented by the aforementioned draft, whereas they had not in fact purchased said shares.

Cheque For $11,553

Witness identified a letter which he had written to the Banque Franco-Chinoise requesting them to issue a comprador order for U.S. $11,553 to pay for the 100 A. T. and T. shares. The bank, however, only issued comprador orders for Chinese currency. Accordingly, they furnished him a cheque for the amount in question on the Irving Trust Company, New York, their correspondents.

"I endorsed this cheque over to the A.-O.F.C.," said Mr. Basset, "and handed it to Mr. Aufwerber, the salesman for the A.-O.F.C., to pay for the 100 A. T. and T. shares.

"Thereafter I received a slip from the A.-O.F.C. notifying me that the 100 shares had been purchased. Likewise in other transactions. Then, periodically, I received statements showing the number of shares which the A.-O.F.C. was holding for my account. I did not keep the notification slips as I thought the statements were sufficient.

"I always checked these statements very carefully. They always correctly reflected my transactions with the A.-O.F.C. They were always correct."

Defence Protests

In giving his testimony, Mr. Basset's answers to the Assistant District Attorney's questions were frequently rephrased by the latter for clearer entry in the record. This procedure brought protests from counsel for the defendants, who asserted that Dr. Sellett was putting words into the mouth of the witness.

These objections were usually overruled by Judge Helmick, who remarked that the witness's meaning was quite obvious and there could be no objection to Dr. Sellett's clearer repetition of the answers.

Mr. Basset then went on to describe a transaction involving a sum of U.S. $28,000 which he had paid by telegraph to the A.-O.F.C. for the credit of the latter's account with E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco.

This remittance was also sent through the Banque Franco-Chinoise. At the time, he had already received notification from the A.-O.F.C. that they had filled an order which he had placed for a further 100 A. T. and T. shares. This remittance was to cover the purchase price of those shares. But the remittance covered more than that amount and the balance was to be placed to his credit for further transactions.

After that, Mr. Basset said, he continued to do business with the A.-O.F.C. for more than a year, buying and selling shares. He described several transactions in January and February, 1934 involving orders for blocks of A. T. and T. and Western Union stock.

Never Visited Offices

Dr. Sellett: During the entire period of these transactions did you ever visit the offices of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation?

Witness replied that he did not.

Dr. Sellett: Did you visit those offices at all before the A.-O.F.C. closed down on May 23, 1935?

Witness: No.

Dr. Sellett: Were you credited by the A.-O.F.C. from time to time with dividends on the New York stocks which you had purchased?

Witness: Yes, I received credit memos.

Dr. Sellett: Who asked you to telegraph the U.S. $28,000 to E. A. Pierce and Company?

Witness: The A.-O.F.C. It was to pay for shares and to establish a credit for me with Pierce and Company. But all my dealings were through the A.-O.F.C.

Mr. Basset then told the Court of another telegraphic transfer which he had made to Pierce and Company through the Banque Franco-Chinoise, for the sum of U.S. $10,000 also in connection with stock purchases through the A.-O.F.C.

Sel: When you transferred the sums to E. A. Pierce Company—the U.S. $28,000 and U.S. $10,000—were you owing money to the A.-O.F.C.?

Owed Them Nothing

The witness looked momentarily nonplussed and then exclaimed:

"I owed them money! I did I owe them any money! They owed me money! They st—ows me money!" Loud laughter from the audience, in which the defendants joined, greeted this reply.

《字林西报》，1936年1月9日，星期四

经纪人向法庭陈述
因信任雷文先生而致巨额损失

在雷文与布朗先生受审期间，吕西安·巴塞特先生的证词披露
其对这位前金融巨头无限的信心

受害者与美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）业务往来频繁
但从未造访其办公室

昨日，在美国驻华法院审理针对雷文先生及美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）副总裁J. 华纳·布朗先生提出的16项盗窃、欺诈和挪用公款指控的续审中，当地著名的法国汇兑经纪人吕西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特（Lucien Claude Marie Basset）先生就其与美亚金融公司的股票交易作证。证据显示，一位现已倒闭的美亚金融公司客户损失了约5万美元，这主要是因为他基于该公司总裁弗兰克·J. 雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生的声誉，对该机构抱有无限信任。

法庭上午休庭，下午2时开始了本案的第四次庭审。法庭内挤满了当地证券和汇兑经纪人社区的知名代表，他们对诉讼程序表现出浓厚的兴趣。整个庭审环节均用于由美国助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士对巴塞特先生进行主问，以及由被告辩护律师C. S. 富兰克林先生和理查德·T. 埃文斯先生进行的交叉询问。

巴塞特先生操着带有明显法国口音的生硬英语告诉法庭，他于1933年下半年通过美亚金融公司的一名销售人员奥夫韦伯（Aufwerber）先生开始与该公司进行交易。

曾是邻居

他说，奥夫韦伯先生是他的邻居。然而，与美亚金融公司的第一笔交易是在汇丰银行大楼内的巴塞特先生办公室完成的。

采取的第一步是巴塞特先生签署了美亚金融公司在与客户进行所有交易时使用的常规“签名卡”表格。

塞莱特博士提请证人注意，当庭出示的这张卡片背面并没有巴塞特先生的签名。该卡片日期为1933年11月11日。

“您为什么不在卡片背面预留的签名处签名？”塞莱特博士问证人。

证人：我没有在背面签名，因为我打算与美亚金融公司做的是现金交易，而不是保证金交易。卡片背面涉及的是保证金类型的交易。

在回答塞莱特博士的进一步提问时，巴塞特先生继续描述了他与美亚金融公司进行的 numerous 股票交易，其中包括买卖美国电话电报公司（American Telephone and Telegraph Company）和西联电报公司（Western Union Telegraph Company）的大宗股票。证人还指认了许多与此类交易相关的订单 slip、通知和对账单，上面有他的签名，这些文件由控方律师作为证据提交。

收到备忘录

证人告诉法庭，所有订单都是通过奥夫韦伯先生下达的。“当我下达股票订单时，我总是收到美亚金融公司发来的借记备忘录，内容是支付给旧金山的电报费。当我下达卖出股票或取消已下订单的指令时，也会收到类似的借记单。”

塞莱特博士：在您下达订单后，您是否总是收到美亚金融公司的通知，告知您所订购的股票已为您账户买入？

证人：是的。

随后，巴塞特先生描述了一笔交易，涉及他通过法中银行（Banque Franco-Chinoise）上海分行开具的一张以纽约欧文信托公司（Irving Trust Company）为付款人的汇票，向美亚金融公司支付11,553美元。

雷文和布朗先生被指控挪用和盗窃这张汇票，并通过虚假声称和表示美亚金融公司已于1933年12月16日左右为他购买了价值11,553美元的100股美国电话电报公司股票（由上述汇票代表），从而重罪欺诈巴塞特先生，而事实上他们并未购买所述股票。

11,553美元的支票

证人指认了他写给法中银行的一封信，请求银行开具一份金额为11,553美元的买办订单（comprador order），用于支付100股美国电话电报公司股票。然而，该银行只开具以中国货币计价的买办订单。因此，他们向他提供了一张由其代理行纽约欧文信托公司支付的相应金额支票。

“我将这张支票背书转让给美亚金融公司，”巴塞特先生说，“并将其交给美亚金融公司的销售人员奥夫韦伯先生，以支付100股美国电话电报公司股票的费用。

“此后，我收到美亚金融公司的一张 slip，通知我那100股股票已买入。其他交易也是如此。然后，我会定期收到对账单，显示美亚金融公司为我账户持有的股票数量。我没有保留那些通知 slip，因为我认为对账单就足够了。

“我总是非常仔细地核对这些对账单。它们总是准确反映我与美亚金融公司的交易。它们总是正确的。”

辩护方抗议

在作证过程中，助理地区检察官经常重新表述巴塞特先生对其问题的回答，以便更清晰地记录在案。这一做法引起了被告辩护律师的抗议，他们声称塞莱特博士是在诱导证人作答。

赫尔米克（Helmick）法官通常驳回了这些异议，他指出证人的意思非常明显，塞莱特博士更清晰地复述答案并无不妥。

随后，巴塞特先生描述了另一笔交易，涉及他通过电汇向美亚金融公司支付28,000美元，存入该公司在旧金山E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company）的账户贷方。

这笔汇款也是通过法中银行发送的。当时，他已经收到美亚金融公司的通知，称他们已执行了他下达的另外100股美国电话电报公司股票的订单。这笔汇款旨在支付这些股票的购买价款。但汇款金额超过了该数额，余额将存入他的账户贷方，用于后续交易。

巴塞特先生说，在那之后，他继续与美亚金融公司做生意一年多，买卖股票。他描述了1934年1月和2月的几笔交易，涉及大宗美国电话电报公司和西联电报公司股票的订单。

从未造访办公室

塞莱特博士：在这些交易的整个期间，您是否曾去过美亚金融公司的办公室？

证人回答说没有。

塞莱特博士：在美亚金融公司于1935年5月23日关闭之前，您是否曾去过那些办公室？

证人：没有。

塞莱特博士：美亚金融公司是否不时将您购买的纽约股票的红利记入您的贷方？

证人：是的，我收到了贷记备忘录。

塞莱特博士：是谁要求您将28,000美元电汇给E. A. 皮尔斯公司的？

证人：美亚金融公司。这是为了支付股票费用，并在皮尔斯公司为我建立信用额度。但我所有的交易都是通过美亚金融公司进行的。

随后，巴塞特先生向法庭讲述了另一次通过法中银行向皮尔斯公司进行的电汇转账，金额为10,000美元，同样与通过美亚金融公司购买股票有关。

塞莱特博士：当您向E. A. 皮尔斯公司转移款项——即28,000美元和10,000美元时——您是否欠美亚金融公司的钱？

不欠他们钱

证人 momentarily 显得困惑，随即惊呼：

“我欠他们钱！我难道欠他们任何钱吗！是他们欠我钱！他们欠——欠我钱！”此回答引得听众哄堂大笑，被告也参与其中。

page_data.en:
When the U.S. $10,000 was telegraphed, witness proceeded, he already had a credit balance with A.-O.F.C. And when the A.-O.F.C. closed down on May 23, 1934 the A.-O.F.C. should have been holding for him, according to the statements which they rendered, 400 shares of A. T. and T. and 100 shares of Western Union stock.

Dr. Sellett then questioned the witness as to the ownership of the first draft for U.S. $11,553 which he had handed over to the A.-O.F.C.

“Did you own that draft?” prosecuting counsel queried.

Witness: Yes, I bought the draft at my bank. It was my property. I endorsed it over and delivered it to the A.-O.F.C.

Dr. Sellett: Did the bank debit your account with the draft?

Witness: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: And the A.-O.F.C. credited your account with the amount of the draft?

Witness: Yes.

Dr. Sellett: Was the draft ever returned to you by the A.-O.F.C.?

Witness: No, I never got it back.

Dr. Sellett: The A.-O.F.C. also credited your account with the draft for U.S. $28,000?

Witness: They did.

Nature Of Transactions

Prosecuting counsel then went on to question Mr. Basset as to what he understood to be the nature of his transactions with the A.-O.F.C.

“I thought,” witness declared, “that the A.-O.F.C. were using my money to buy and pay for the stocks which I ordered.”

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever authorize the A.-O.F.C. or the defendants to hypothecate the stock which you bought to any third party?

Witness: Certainly not.

Mr. Basset then went on to say that on one occasion he had asked Mr. Aufwerber whether the shares he had bought were under his (Mr. Basset’s) cover and in his (Mr. Basset’s) name.

“Mr. Aufwerber told me he had inquired at the office and had found that everything was all right.”

Dr. Sellett: Did this happen while you were still actively engaged in buying and selling stocks through the A.-O.F.C.?

Witness replied that it did and added that not only were all the shares which he ordered paid for by him in full, but, on May 23, 1935, when the A.-O.F.C. closed down he had a cash credit with the A.-O.F.C. of more than U.S. $4,000.

Prosecuting counsel then asked the witness whether he had ever authorized the sale of his shares. The answer was in the negative.

“Now, Mr. Basset,” Dr. Sellett continued, “when you telegraphed the U.S. $28,000 to Pierce and Company, would you have done so had you known that the A.-O.F.C. had not used your previous draft to purchase the 100 A. T. and T. shares which you had ordered?”

Would Not Have Paid

Witness replied that he would never have made the remittance had he known such was the case.

Dr. Sellett: Would you have telegraphed that money if you had known that your shares were hypothecated to E. A. Pierce and Company.

Witness answered that he would certainly not have done so. It was his belief that his draft had been used to pay for the 100 A. T. and T. shares which he ordered. He thought that these shares had been paid for in full by the A.-O.F.C.

The statements which they sent him showed that the shares had been paid for in full.

Dr. Sellett: Have you received the 400 shares of A. T. and T. which the A.-O.F.C. stated it held for you?

Witness: No.

Dr. Sellett: Or the 100 shares of Western Union?

Witness answered that he had not received them, but had been under the impression that the A.-O.F.C. was holding them for him in safekeeping.

Mr. Basset was next asked whether he knew Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown, the defendants in the case. He replied that he had known Mr. Raven for years but had only met Mr. Brown once, when the latter became a member of the Shanghai Club.

In reply to Dr. Sellett’s final question in the examination-in-chief, Mr. Basset said that he had no other transactions with the A.-O.F.C. beyond those to which he had testified and that he had ceased dealing with the A.-O.F.C. some time before that institution closed down — probably three months or more before.

Cross-Examination

Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for Mr. J. Warner Brown, then rose to cross-examine the witness and the crowded court-room leaned forward to catch more clearly the line of defence which it was expected the questioning would disclose.

Counsel commenced by asking Mr. Basset whether all his transactions with the A.-O.F.C. had been effected through the salesman referred to, Mr. Aufwerber. Mr. Basset replied that they had.

Mr. Franklin: Were all your transactions on a telegraphic transfer basis?

Witness: Yes.

Mr. Franklin: Did you ever suggest to Mr. Aufwerber that your shares be placed in safekeeping with the New York correspondent of the Banque Franco-Chinoise, that is, with the Irving Trust Company?

Was A City Father

Witness: No, I never made such a suggestion. I thought the A.-O.F.C. was good enough. Mr. Raven was very well-known here. He was a City Father. The A.-O.F.C. was a flourishing concern (this with a suggestion of sarcasm) and I thought I would like to help it along with some business.

Loud laughter from the audience greeted this reply and when it subsided Mr. Franklin resumed his cross-examination.

“Did you have confidence in the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Raven when you started doing business with them? counsel asked.

Witness: Yes, I did have confidence or I would not have given them my business.

Mr. Franklin then asked the witness whether he had such confidence when the A.-O.F.C. closed down, but Mr. Basset said he refused to answer that question.

The next question to witness was inquiry as to what he understood by the words “held for your account,” which appeared in the statements sent him by the A.-O.F.C.

Witness: I understood that they meant that the A.-O.F.C. owed me the stated number of shares.

Mr. Franklin: It was your understanding that you had an “account” with the A.-O.F.C.?

Witness (emphatically): No, I had no account, but a credit.

Mr. Richard T. Evans, counsel for Mr. J. Warner Brown, then plied the witness with questions. All his dealings in New York stocks, witness declared, had been put through the A.-O.F.C. He had never received any money from the A.-O.F.C. nor had he ever asked them to pay him anything from his credit balance.

Mr. Evans: Did you ever ask the A.-O.F.C. for any share certificates?

Witness: No.

Mr. Evans: Did you ever deal in stocks elsewhere—in London or Paris?

Stick To New York

Witness: We are talking about New York and not about London or Paris.

Judge Helmick: He has made a perfectly good legal objection.

Mr. Evans then asked Mr. Basset whether he had expected that the drafts which he had given the A.-O.F.C. would be sent to New York by the A.-O.F.C. and not deposited by the A.-O.F.C. in an account here

“That is cuisine,” witness replied.

“A domestic affair,” Mr. Evans elucidated.

The Court then adjourned until 10 a.m. to-day.

当那笔一万美元电汇至美国时，证人继续陈述，他在美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）已有贷方余额。而当美亚金融公司于1934年5月23日停业时，根据该公司出具的账单，其本应为他持有400股美国电话电报公司（A. T. and T.）股票和100股西联汇款公司（Western Union）股票。

随后，塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）就证人交给美亚金融公司的第一张面额为11,553美元的汇票的所有权问题向证人提问。

“那张汇票是属于你的吗？”公诉律师问道。

证人：是的，我在我的银行购买了这张汇票。它是我的财产。我背书转让并将其交付给了美亚金融公司。

塞莱特博士：银行是否从你的账户中扣除了该汇票的金额？

证人：是的。

塞莱特博士：而美亚金融公司是否将该汇票的金额记入你账户的贷方？

证人：是的。

塞莱特博士：美亚金融公司是否曾将那张汇票退还给你？

证人：没有，我从未收回过它。

塞莱特博士：美亚金融公司是否也将那张28,000美元的汇票记入了你账户的贷方？

证人：他们确实这样做了。

交易性质

随后，公诉律师继续询问巴塞特先生（Mr. Basset），他对自己与美亚金融公司之间交易的性质作何理解。

“我以为，”证人宣称，“美亚金融公司是在用我的资金购买并支付我所订购的股票。”

塞莱特博士：你是否曾授权美亚金融公司或被告将你购买的股票抵押给任何第三方？

证人：当然没有。

巴塞特先生接着说，有一次他曾问奥夫韦伯先生（Mr. Aufwerber），他所购买的股票是否在他的（巴塞特先生的）名下并由他（巴塞特先生）持有。

“奥夫韦伯先生告诉我，他已在办公室查询过，发现一切正常。”

塞莱特博士：这件事发生在你仍通过美亚金融公司积极买卖股票期间吗？

证人回答说确实如此，并补充说，不仅他订购的所有股票均由他全额付款，而且在1935年5月23日美亚金融公司停业时，他在美亚金融公司还有超过4,000美元的现金贷方余额。

随后，公诉律师询问证人是否曾授权出售他的股票。回答是否定的。

“那么，巴塞特先生，”塞莱特博士继续说道，“当你向皮尔斯公司（Pierce and Company）电汇那28,000美元时，如果你知道美亚金融公司并未使用你之前的汇票去购买你所订购的100股美国电话电报公司股票，你还会这样做吗？”

不会付款

证人回答说，如果他早知道情况如此，他绝不会进行这笔汇款。

塞莱特博士：如果你知道你的股票已被抵押给E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company），你还会电汇那笔钱吗？

证人回答说他肯定不会这样做。他相信他的汇票已被用于支付他所订购的100股美国电话电报公司股票。他认为这些股票已由美亚金融公司全额付清。

他们寄给他的账单显示这些股票已全额付清。

塞莱特博士：你是否收到了美亚金融公司声称为你持有的400股美国电话电报公司股票？

证人：没有。

塞莱特博士：或者是那100股西联汇款公司股票？

证人回答说他并未收到，但他一直以为美亚金融公司正代为保管这些股票。

接下来，有人问巴塞特先生是否认识本案被告雷文先生（Mr. Raven）和布朗先生（Mr. Brown）。他回答说，他认识雷文先生多年，但只见过布朗先生一次，那是后者成为上海总会（Shanghai Club）会员的时候。

在回答主问环节中塞莱特博士的最后一个问题时，巴塞特先生说，除了他已作证的那些交易外，他与美亚金融公司没有其他交易，并且在该机构停业前的一段时间——可能在三个月或更久之前——他就已停止与其进行交易。

交叉质询

J. 华纳·布朗先生（Mr. J. Warner Brown）的辩护律师C. S. 富兰克林先生（Mr. C. S. Franklin）随即起身对证人进行交叉质询，拥挤的法庭向前探身，以便更清楚地听清预计将通过提问揭示的辩护思路。

辩护律师首先询问巴塞特先生，他与美亚金融公司的所有交易是否都是通过那位被称为销售员的奥夫韦伯先生进行的。巴塞特先生回答说确实如此。

富兰克林先生：你所有的交易都是基于电汇转账方式吗？

证人：是的。

富兰克林先生：你是否曾向奥夫韦伯先生建议，将你的股票交由法中工商银行（Banque Franco-Chinoise）的纽约代理行，即欧文信托公司（Irving Trust Company）保管？

曾任市议员

证人：不，我从未提出过这样的建议。我认为美亚金融公司已经足够可靠。雷文先生在这里非常有名。他是一位市议员（City Father）。美亚金融公司是一家兴旺的企业（此处带有讽刺意味），我想通过做一些生意来帮衬一下它。

听众对此回答报以大笑，笑声平息后，富兰克林先生恢复了交叉质询。

“当你开始与他们做生意时，你对美亚金融公司和雷文先生有信心吗？”辩护律师问道。

证人：是的，我有信心，否则我不会把业务交给他们。

富兰克林先生随后问证人，在美亚金融公司停业时他是否仍有这样的信心，但巴塞特先生表示他拒绝回答这个问题。

下一个向证人提出的问题是他如何理解美亚金融公司寄给他的账单上出现的“为你账户持有”（held for your account）一词的含义。

证人：我理解这意味着美亚金融公司欠我所述数量的股票。

富兰克林先生：你的理解是你在美亚金融公司有一个“账户”吗？

证人（强调地）：不，我没有账户，只有贷方余额。

随后，J. 华纳·布朗先生的辩护律师理查德·T. 埃文斯先生（Mr. Richard T. Evans）向证人连珠炮似地提问。证人宣称，他在纽约股票的所有交易都是通过美亚金融公司进行的。他从未从美亚金融公司收到过任何款项，也从未要求他们从其贷方余额中支付任何款项给他。

埃文斯先生：你是否曾向美亚金融公司索要任何股票证书？

证人：没有。

埃文斯先生：你是否曾在其他地方——伦敦或巴黎——进行过股票交易？

坚持谈论纽约

证人：我们谈论的是纽约，而不是伦敦或巴黎。

赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）：他提出了一个完全合法的反对方。

随后，埃文斯先生询问巴塞特先生，他是否预期他交给美亚金融公司的汇票会被美亚金融公司寄往纽约，而不是由美亚金融公司存入此地的某个账户

“那是内部事务（cuisine），”证人回答道。

“家事（A domestic affair），”埃文斯先生解释道。

法庭随后休庭，直至今天上午10点继续开庭。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JANUARY 10, 1936

Government Exhibits Reach
High Mark In Raven Case

171 Documents Put In By Prosecution By Close Of
Session Yesterday; Confirmation Of Basset
Trading Given By Accountants

Documentary evidence comprising 171 exhibits had been put into the record at the close of the U. S. Court for China session yesterday in the trial on criminal charges of Mr. F. J. Raven, president, and Mr. J. Warner Brown, vice-president of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

These exhibits, confirmed by accountant witnesses, pertained largely to the dealings by Mr. Lucien C. M. Basset, prominent exchange broker, who is alleged to have lost U. S. $50,000 in the crash of the "Raven group" in May, 1935.

Mr. G. Choplin, comptroller of the Banque Franco-Chinoise pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, identified records showing the issuance of cheques amounting to $11,553, $28,000, and $10,000 (all in U. S. currency) drawn on Mr. Basset's account between the dates December 16, 1933, and May 31, 1934. The latter two amounts were sent through the Irving Trust Company of New York for the credit of Messrs. E. A. Pierce and Company, and Mr. Basset's name did not appear in the transaction.

Highly detailed evidence continued in the afternoon when Mr. Thomas Waung, chief accountant of the defunct firm, identified these same amounts on the records of the A.-O.F.C., also notifications of dividends which were sent to Mr. Basset and entries in ledgers pertaining to the Basset account.

No objection was made by the defence, represented by Messrs. C. S. Franklin and Richard T. Evans.

On April 30, 1935, witness said, the account of Mr. Basset was credited with 400 shares of American Telephone and Telegraph, 100 shares of Western Union, and $4,136.75 in cash. Mr. Basset never had a debit balance since December 30, 1933, he said.

Sold After Crash

Referring to an entry on May 27, 1935, three days after the bank closed its doors and in the period before the liquidator took over, it was shown that the shares owned by Mr. Basset had been sold.

Dr. Sellett: Did Mr. Basset give an order to sell these stocks at any time?—I do not think so, but I cannot be sure without examining the records.

Mr. Evans: We assume that no such order existed, but I think this is not the proper witness to confirm the fact.

Dr. Sellett said he would withdraw the question until witness had examined the books. He said he wanted confirmation of Mr. Basset's testimony.

Opening again this morning for a full day's session, the prosecution it is believed will recall Mr. C. C. Curtis, officer of Messrs. A. E. Pierce and Company, and Mr. Aufwerber, the salesman who handled Mr. Basset's business.
