《字林西报》，1936年1月10日，星期五

雷文案中政府呈堂证物达到高峰

庭审昨日结束时检方提交171份文件；会计师证实巴塞特的交易情况

在昨天美国在华法院审理已倒闭的美亚金融公司总裁F. J. 雷文先生和副总裁J. 华纳·布朗先生刑事指控案件的庭审结束时，共有171份书证被录入案卷。

这些由会计师证人确认的证物，主要涉及著名外汇经纪人吕西安·C. M. 巴塞特先生（Mr. Lucien C. M. Basset）的交易，据称他在1935年5月“雷文集团”崩盘中损失了50,000美元。

法中工商银行的审计长G. 肖普林先生（Mr. G. Choplin）辨认了记录，显示在1933年12月16日至1934年5月31日期间，从巴塞特先生的账户开出了金额分别为11,553美元、28,000美元和10,000美元（均为美元）的支票。后两笔款项通过纽约欧文信托公司汇出，存入E. A. 皮尔斯公司名下，巴塞特先生的名字未出现在该交易中。

下午继续进行高度详细的举证，已倒闭公司的主计长托马斯·王（Thomas Waung）先生辨认了美亚金融公司记录中的相同金额，以及寄送给巴塞特先生的股息通知和与巴塞特账户相关的分类账条目。

由C. S. 富兰克林先生和理查德·T. 埃文斯先生代表的辩方未提出异议。

证人称，1935年4月30日，巴塞特先生的账户被记入400股美国电话电报公司股票、100股西联汇款公司股票以及4,136.75美元现金。他说，自1933年12月30日以来，巴塞特先生从未有过借方余额。

崩盘后售出

提及1935年5月27日的一条记录，即在银行关门三天后、清算人接管前的期间，记录显示巴塞特先生拥有的股票已被出售。

塞莱特博士：巴塞特先生是否在任何时候下达过出售这些股票的指令？——我不这么认为，但不查阅记录我无法确定。

埃文斯先生：我们假设不存在此类指令，但我认为这位证人不是确认这一事实的合适人选。

塞莱特博士表示，在证人查阅账簿之前，他将撤回该问题。他说他希望确认巴塞特先生的证词。

今天上午重新开庭，进行全天的庭审，据信检方将再次传唤E. A. 皮尔斯公司的职员C. C. 柯蒂斯先生（Mr. C. C. Curtis）以及负责处理巴塞特先生业务的销售员奥夫韦伯先生出庭。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 8, 1936
A.-O.F.C. Business Methods
Described At Raven Trial
Court Hears How Customer Paid For 30 Shares Of
Douglas Aircraft Stock While A.-O.F.C.
Bought Them On 25 Per Cent. Margin

Evidence showing how Major Edward P. Howard, Shanghai representative of the Douglas Aircraft Corporation, had placed an order with the American-Oriental Finance Corporation in July, 1934 for 30 shares of Douglas Aircraft stock; how he had paid for the stock with a draft for U.S. $507.60 drawn on the National City Bank of New York, but never got delivery of the stock, and how the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, in turn, bought the stock from E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco, on a 25 per cent. margin, was given yesterday in the United States Court for China before Judge Milton J. Helmick at the resumed hearing of the 16 charges of theft, embezzlement and fraud on which Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown are standing trial.

The case, still in its initial stages, shows every promise of becoming the most protracted in the Court's history and is likely to stretch out for at least another 10 days or two weeks. With the conclusion of yesterday's session, the prosecution had only called six witnesses, while the number of exhibits had reached an even 50. There are still many witnesses whom the prosecution intends to call.

Major Howard Testifies
Major Edward P. Howard was the first witness called yesterday and his evidence pertained to three of the 16 counts in the indictment. He told the Court that in July, 1934 he gave to the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, through one of its salesmen, a Mr. McTaggert, a verbal order for 30 shares of Douglas Aircraft stock at 16½.

Soon thereafter he received a signature card from the A.-O.F.C. which contained the notation: "Buys Outright." Witness identified the signature on the card as his own. On July 26, he purchased a draft from the Shanghai office of the National City Bank of New York in the sum of U. S. $507.60 and sent this to the A.-O.F.C. in payment of the shares ordered. This draft was payable to the A.-O.F.C. at the head office of the National City Bank in New York.

Continuing, witness said that he received from the A.-O.F.C. a receipt for the draft and after that an advice from the A.-O.F.C. stating that 30 Douglas Aircraft shares had been purchased for his account. From time to time thereafter, he received statements from the A.-O.F.C. showing that they held these shares for his account.

"For Your Account"
Asked by Dr. George Sellett, prosecuting counsel, what he understood by the words "for your account" witness replied that it was his belief that the A.-O.F.C. were holding for him 30 shares of Douglas Aircraft stock.

Dr. Sellett: Did you ever authorize the A.-O.F.C. or any of its officers or employees to hypothecate this stock to a third party?
Witness: No.
Dr. Sellett: Did you at any time authorise the A.-O.F.C. or the defendants to sell the stock?
Witness: No.
Judge Helmick: Did you ever receive the stock which you ordered?
Witness: No.

In cross-examination by Mr. C. S. Franklin, counsel for Mr. J. Warner Brown, Major Howard said he did not know whether Mr. Brown and Mr. Raven were in Shanghai at the time he made this transaction with the A.-O.F.C. Questioned further, he said this had been his first transaction in New York stocks. He was under the impression that they would be registered in his name since he had paid for them in full, but had never inquired whether this had actually been done.

Annual Company Meetings
In reply to Mr. Richard T. Evans, Mr. Raven's attorney, witness said he was aware that the Douglas Aircraft Corporation held annual meetings.

Mr. Evans: Then did it not surprise you—if you were under the impression that the shares were registered in your name—that you never received notices of these meetings?
Witness: I did not give it a thought.

Formal evidence was then given by Mr. W. R. Marchman and Mr. C. G. Yow, employees of the Shanghai branch of the National City Bank of New York, showing that Major Howard had, on July 26, 1934 purchased at their office a draft for U. S. $507.60, in favour of the A.-O.F.C. and payable on demand after 30 days at the head office of the bank in New York.

Mr. Marchman testified that the draft had been duly paid, since no notification to the contrary had been received from the head office of the bank.

Former Employee Testifies
The next witness was Mr. Thomas Waung, 35, who told the Court that he had started working for the A.-O.F.C. in 1930 Prior to that he had been with the Amoy branch of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation.

In the Shanghai office of the A.-O.F.C., from 1930 on, he had been engaged in general office and sales work and latterly in the accounting department. The head of the accounting department, when witness entered it, was Mr. H. T. Chang, but the latter soon left and witness took his place, remaining head of the accounting department until the A.-O.F.C. closed in May of last year.

Continuing, witness said he was familiar with the methods of business of the A.-O.F.C., including their dealings with E. A. Pierce and Company, San Francisco.

A Mr. Rosse was one of the officers of the A.-O.F.C. connected with sales work. They were the initials of Mr. Rosse which appeared on Major Howard's purchase order for 30 Douglas Aircraft shares. This order was also initialled by Mr. K. Hartman, the accountant.

How It Was Done
Describing the office routine in handling customers' orders, witness said the first step was to place an order slip in a locked box to which the cable department had the key. At the end of each day, the box was cleared by the cable department and the orders cabled to E. A. Pierce and Company in San Francisco. The names of the A.-O.F.C.'s customers for whom the shares were being bought did not appear in these cables.

Pierce and Company, witness continued sent cabled advice of the execution of orders. These incoming cables also did not contain the names of the A.-O.F.C.'s customers.

When a cabled advice of orders executed was received from Pierce and Company, the cable department compiled from it a "Business Done Sheet." This was sent in to the accounting department, which in turn sent out notifications to the customers of the A.-O.F.C. advising them that so and so many shares of such and such stock had been purchased for their account.

This procedure, witness went on, was observed in the case of the transaction with Major Howard. The draft which Major Howard used to pay for the shares was deposited by the A.-O.F.C. in a gold dollar account which it had with the American-Oriental Banking Corporation.

Raven, Brown Away
Asked by Dr. Sellett whether Messrs. Raven and Brown were in Shanghai at the time of the transaction with Major Howard, witness replied that both were away. Mr. Raven was in the United States. That was in July, 1934.

Cross-examined by Mr. Franklin, witness said that the A.-O.F.C. bought the 30 Douglas Aircraft shares on July 21, the same day that Major Howard placed the order.

Mr. Franklin: Were those shares in the account of the A.-O.F.C. with Pierce and Company on May 23, 1935, the date when the A.-O.F.C. closed down?
Witness: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: When you say these shares were in the account of the A.-O.F.C. with Pierce and Company, what exactly do you mean by that?
Witness: They were in the margin account which the A.-O.F.C. ran with Pierce and Company.

25 Per Cent. Margin
Dr. Sellett: The margin account was for about 25 per cent., was it not?
Witness: Yes.
Dr. Sellett: In the case of this Howard transaction, then, this means that the A.-O.F.C. did not pay in full for the 30 shares of Douglas Aircraft, but only 25 per cent?
Witness: That is so.

Under further interrogation he went on to indicate that shares for which local customers of the A.-O.F.C. had paid in full went into the margin account with Pierce and Company and that the A.-O.F.C. effected remittances to Pierce and Company by telegraphic transfer only when Pierce and Company sent a call for further margin, that is to say, when the margin fell below 25 per cent.

Mrs. Muriel Aylward Woolly, a British subject formerly in the employ of the A.-O.F.C., was next called to the witness-stand. She said she had been employed by the A.-O.F.C. from July, 1931 until December 31, 1934. Her job was at the information desk and she also had to attend to salesmen's correspondence.

It was in this latter connection,

《字林西报》，1936年1月8日，星期三
雷文案庭审中描述美亚金融公司业务手法
法庭听取客户如何为30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票付款，而美亚金融公司仅以25%保证金购入该股

昨日，在中国美国法院（United States Court for China），米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官主持重启对弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生所涉16项盗窃、挪用公款及欺诈指控的审理。庭上出示了证据，显示道格拉斯飞机公司（Douglas Aircraft Corporation）驻上海代表爱德华·P·霍华德（Edward P. Howard）少校于1934年7月向美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）下达购买30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票的订单；他通过一张开具给纽约花旗银行（National City Bank of New York）的507.60美元汇票支付了股票款项，但从未收到股票交割；而美亚金融公司转而以25%的保证金从旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司（E. A. Pierce and Company）购买了这些股票。

该案仍处于初期阶段，但极有可能成为该法院历史上耗时最长的案件，预计至少还将持续10天至两周。随着昨日庭审结束，控方仅传唤了六名证人，而提交的物证数量已达整整50件。控方仍计划传唤许多其他证人。

霍华德少校作证
爱德华·P·霍华德少校是昨日首位被传唤的证人，其证词涉及起诉书16项罪名中的三项。他告诉法庭，1934年7月，他通过美亚金融公司的一名销售员麦塔格特（McTaggert）先生，口头订购了30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票，价格为16½美元。

不久后，他收到美亚金融公司寄来的一张签名卡，上面注明：“直接买入”（Buys Outright）。证人确认卡上的签名为其本人所签。7月26日，他从纽约花旗银行上海办事处购买了一张金额为507.60美元的汇票，并将其寄给美亚金融公司以支付所订股票的款项。该汇票在纽约花旗银行总行兑付，收款人为美亚金融公司。

证人继续说道，他收到了美亚金融公司出具的汇票收据，随后又收到美亚金融公司的通知，称已为其账户购买了30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票。此后不时收到美亚金融公司的对账单，显示该公司为其账户持有这些股票。

“为您账户”
当公诉人乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士询问他对“为您账户”（for your account）一词的理解时，证人回答说，他认为这意味着美亚金融公司为他持有30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票。

塞莱特博士：您是否曾授权美亚金融公司或其任何高管或员工将这些股票抵押给第三方？
证人：没有。
塞莱特博士：您是否曾在任何时候授权美亚金融公司或被告出售这些股票？
证人：没有。
赫尔米克法官：您是否曾收到您所订购的股票？
证人：没有。

在接受J·沃纳·布朗先生的辩护律师C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生的交叉质询时，霍华德少校表示，他在与美亚金融公司进行这笔交易时，不知道布朗先生和雷文先生是否在上海。经进一步询问，他说这是他第一次交易纽约股票。他的印象是，既然他已经全额付款，股票应该会登记在他的名下，但他从未核实过是否确实如此。

公司年度会议
在回答雷文先生的代理律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生的提问时，证人表示他知道道格拉斯飞机公司会举行年度会议。

埃文斯先生：那么，如果您认为股票是登记在您名下的，您从未收到这些会议的通知，难道不感到惊讶吗？
证人：我根本没想过这件事。

随后，纽约花旗银行上海分行的员工W·R·马奇曼（W. R. Marchman）先生和C·G·尤（C. G. Yow）先生提供了正式证据，证明霍华德少校于1934年7月26日在该行办事处购买了一张金额为507.60美元、收款人为美亚金融公司的汇票，该汇票在30天后见票即付，兑付地点为纽约银行总行。

马奇曼先生作证说，该汇票已得到正常兑付，因为银行总行未收到任何相反的通知。

前雇员作证
下一位证人是35岁的托马斯·王（Thomas Waung，音译）先生。他告诉法庭，他于1930年开始在美亚金融公司工作。在此之前，他曾在美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）厦门分行任职。

自1930年起，他在美亚金融公司上海办事处从事一般办公室和销售工作，后期在会计部工作。证人进入会计部时，该部门负责人是H·T·张（H. T. Chang，音译）先生，但后者很快离职，证人接替了他的职位，一直担任会计部主管，直到美亚金融公司于去年5月关闭。

证人继续说，他熟悉美亚金融公司的业务方法，包括其与旧金山E. A. 皮尔斯公司的交易往来。

罗斯（Rosse，音译）先生是美亚金融公司负责销售工作的高管之一。霍华德少校购买30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票的订单上出现了罗斯先生的姓名首字母缩写。该订单也由会计师K·哈特曼（K. Hartman，音译）先生签署了姓名首字母缩写。

操作方式
在描述处理客户订单的办公室常规流程时，证人表示，第一步是将订单单放入一个带锁的盒子中，电报部持有该盒子的钥匙。每天结束时，电报部会清理盒子，并将订单通过电报发送至旧金山的E. A. 皮尔斯公司。这些电报中并未出现美亚金融公司为其购买股票的客户的姓名。

证人继续说，皮尔斯公司会发送电报通知订单执行情况。这些 incoming 电报同样不包含美亚金融公司客户的姓名。

当收到皮尔斯公司发来的订单执行电报通知后，电报部据此编制一份“已办业务单”（Business Done Sheet）。该单据被送至会计部，会计部随即向美亚金融公司的客户发出通知，告知他们已为其账户购买了某某数量的某某股票。

证人接着说，在与霍华德少校的交易中也遵循了这一程序。霍华德少校用于支付股票款项的汇票被美亚金融公司存入其在美亚银行开设的金元账户中。

雷文、布朗不在场
当塞莱特博士询问在与霍华德少校进行交易时，雷文先生和布朗先生是否在上海时，证人回答说两人都不在。雷文先生当时在美国。那是1934年7月。

在接受富兰克林先生的交叉质询时，证人表示，美亚金融公司在7月21日购买了这30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票，也就是霍华德少校下达订单的同一天。

富兰克林先生：在美亚金融公司于1935年5月23日关闭之日，这些股票是否仍在美亚金融公司与皮尔斯公司的账户中？
证人：是的。
塞莱特博士：当您说这些股票在美亚金融公司与皮尔斯公司的账户中时，您确切的意思是什么？
证人：它们位于美亚金融公司与皮尔斯公司往来的保证金账户中。

25%保证金
塞莱特博士：保证金比例大约是25%，是吗？
证人：是的。
塞莱特博士：那么，在这笔霍华德交易中，这意味着美亚金融公司并没有全额支付这30股道格拉斯飞机公司股票的费用，而只支付了25%？
证人：正是如此。

在进一步的讯问下，他指出，美亚金融公司的本地客户全额付款购买的股票也进入了与皮尔斯公司的保证金账户，而美亚金融公司仅在皮尔斯公司要求追加保证金时，即保证金比例低于25%时，才通过电汇向皮尔斯公司汇款。

接下来出庭作证的是英国籍人士穆里尔·艾尔沃德·伍利（Muriel Aylward Woolly）女士，她曾是美亚金融公司的雇员。她说她于1931年7月至1934年12月31日期间受雇于美亚金融公司。她的职位是在问询处，同时也负责处理销售员的信件往来。

正是在后一方面，

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JANUARY 7, 1936
Make-Up Of Raven Organs
Features Testimony
Records Of Companies Reviewed By China Trade
Act Registrar; Pierce Company Official
Tells Of A.-O.F.C. Relationship

A mass of detailed evidence, purporting to show the composition and control of the "Raven Group" in connection with the defendants, Frank Jay Raven and J. Warner Brown, in their trial on 16 different counts for theft, embezzlement and fraud, featured yesterday's session before Judge Milton J. Helmick of the U.S. Court for China. The principal witness was Miss A. Viola Smith, Registrar for the China Trade Act, while Mr. Carleton Coleman Curtis, an official of Messrs. A. E. Pierce and Company, American stock and commodity brokers, told of the relationship existing between his firm and the A.-O.F.C. since 1930.

Producing the articles of incorporation, Miss Smith testified that the A.-O.F.C. came into existence in July, 1926. Mr. F. J. Raven was president and director, and Mr. J. Warner Brown was vice-president and director. The list of shareholders was also produced against the objection of Mr. Richard T. Evans, for the defence, when Dr. George Sellett, prosecuting, said that he proposed to show that Mr. Raven was the controlling shareholder in the Raven Trust Company and that at all times he was the controlling shareholder in the A.-O.F.C.

The records showed that the Raven Trust Company, or F. J. Raven, held 43,940 shares of "A" stock at the time of the last annual report, and that the amount of common "A" stock issued and paid up amounted to $2,435,800; the "B" stock to $1,876,340; and preferred stock to $15,700.

Interests Of Accused

Protests of irrelevancy by defence counsel were again overruled in the matter of records of the Raven Trust Company by means of which Dr. Sellett said he hoped to show the nature and extent to which accused, as officers of the Raven Trust Company, were financially interested in the A.-O.F.C.

While the A.-O.F.C. came into existence in July, 1926, the Raven Trust Company was incorporated under the China Trade Act on December 3, 1926, with F. J. Raven as president, A. H. Driscoll as secretary and treasurer, and with Messrs. C. H. Raven, J. Kleffel, Hugo Sandor and J. F. Price as directors. According to the annual report for March 14, 1934, the directors and officers were the same. Mr. F. J. Raven became the first president of the R.T.C. on March 14, 1927.

Mr. Franklin questioned Miss Smith:

I want to ask if the name of J. Warner Brown appears as the name of a director, officer or shareholder of the Raven Trust Co. since its inception—I have not searched the records for that point but shall do so if you wish.

Miss Smith later gave the answer "No" to the question!

A.-O.F.C. Account

Mr. Curtis, an official of Messrs. A. E. Pierce and Company, in San Francisco, said that he had handled the account of the A.-O.F.C. for his firm and that it was in the nature of the usual corporation client's relationship.

Objections by defence counsel led to prolonged questioning of witness on documents showing the existence of such relationship between the two parties. The original signature and hypothecation card, allegedly signed by Mr. F. J. Raven, could not be produced inasmuch as the American firm declined to part with it under the circumstances.

Dr. Sellett was upheld by Judge Helmick in his plea that secondary evidence was clearly admissible because the document was without the jurisdiction of the court.

Witness identified Mr. Raven and his handwriting on several documents. He also identified Mr. Brown. He then told of the accounts carried by the A.-O.F.C. which were:—a margin account, a paid-for securities account and a commodities account. Most of the trading, he indicated, had been done on the margin account, whereby 25 per cent. of the value of the stock or securities was allowed. When a customer becomes short in his margin, he is asked to produce more security, he said.

He testified that the paid-for securities account had been opened in 1933 but that comparatively little business had gone through this channel. Paid-for securities, he explained, were required to be put into this account by regulations of the U.S. Stock Exchange without specific request.

Cross-examined, witness said that certain stocks had been put into this account at the specific request of the A.-O.F.C. He said that he had not noticed anything unusual about the A.-O.F.C. account.

《字林西报》，1936年1月7日，星期二
雷文集团构成情况
证词要点
中国贸易法注册官审查的公司记录；皮尔斯公司官员讲述与A.-O.F.C.的关系

昨日，在美国驻华法院米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官主持的庭审中，大量旨在显示“雷文集团”构成及控制情况的详细证据成为焦点，该集团涉及被告弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown），二人因盗窃、挪用公款和欺诈等16项不同罪名受审。主要证人为中国贸易法注册官A·维奥拉·史密斯（A. Viola Smith）小姐，而美国股票及商品经纪人A. E. 皮尔斯公司（Messrs. A. E. Pierce and Company）的官员卡尔顿·科尔曼·柯蒂斯（Carleton Coleman Curtis）先生则讲述了其所在公司与A.-O.F.C.自1930年以来存在的关系。

史密斯小姐出示了公司章程，作证称A.-O.F.C.成立于1926年7月。F. J. 雷文先生任总裁兼董事，J. 沃纳·布朗先生任副总裁兼董事。尽管辩护方律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生提出异议，股东名单仍被呈堂，当时公诉人乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士表示，他拟证明雷文先生是雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的控股股东，且在任何时候都是A.-O.F.C.的控股股东。

记录显示，在上一份年度报告时，雷文信托公司或F. J. 雷文持有43,940股“A”类股票，已发行并缴足的普通“A”类股票金额为2,435,800美元；“B”类股票为1,876,340美元；优先股为15,700美元。

被告的利益关系

辩护律师以无关为由提出的抗议再次被驳回，此次涉及的是雷文信托公司的记录，塞莱特博士称他希望借此显示被告作为雷文信托公司高管在A.-O.F.C.中经济利益的性质和程度。

虽然A.-O.F.C.成立于1926年7月，但雷文信托公司于1926年12月3日根据《中国贸易法》注册成立，F. J. 雷文任总裁，A. H. 德里斯科尔（A. H. Driscoll）任秘书兼财务主管，C. H. 雷文、J·克莱费尔（J. Kleffel）、雨果·桑多尔（Hugo Sandor）和J. F. 普赖斯（J. F. Price）等先生任董事。根据1934年3月14日的年度报告，董事和高管人员相同。F. J. 雷文先生于1927年3月14日成为雷文信托公司（R.T.C.）的首任总裁。

富兰克林先生询问史密斯小姐：

我想问一下，自雷文信托公司成立以来，J. 沃纳·布朗的名字是否作为董事、高管或股东出现——我尚未就此点查阅记录，但如果您希望，我可以去查。

史密斯小姐随后对该问题给出了“否”的回答！

A.-O.F.C. 账户

旧金山A. E. 皮尔斯公司的官员柯蒂斯先生表示，他曾为其公司处理A.-O.F.C.的账户，其性质属于通常的公司客户关系。

辩护律师的异议导致对证人进行了长时间的质询，内容涉及显示双方存在此类关系的文件。据称由F. J. 雷文先生签署的原始签名和抵押卡未能出示，因为在该情况下，这家美国公司拒绝交出该文件。

赫尔米克法官支持了塞莱特博士的主张，即次要证据显然可予采纳，因为该文件不在法院管辖范围内。

证人指认了雷文先生及其在几份文件上的笔迹。他还指认了布朗先生。随后，他讲述了A.-O.F.C.持有的账户，包括：保证金账户、已付证券账户和商品账户。他指出，大部分交易是通过保证金账户进行的，该账户允许按股票或证券价值的25%提供保证金。他说，当客户的保证金不足时，会被要求提供更多担保品。

他作证称，已付证券账户于1933年开立，但通过该渠道进行的业务相对较少。他解释说，根据美国证券交易所的规定，已付证券需存入该账户，无需特别要求。

在交叉询问中，证人表示某些股票是应A.-O.F.C.的特别要求存入该账户的。他说，他未注意到A.-O.F.C.账户有任何异常之处。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JANUARY 4, 1936
13016

Raven Trial Opens With
Ringing Indictment By
Government Prosecutor

Dr. Sellett Says Defendants Conducted Business
Of A.-O.F.C. With Reckless And Criminal
Disregard Of Interests Of Clients

ASSISTANT DISTRICT ATTORNEY OUTLINES
THEFT AND EMBEZZLEMENT CHARGES

A ringing indictment of the manner in which, according to the evidence that the Government proposes to bring forward, the affairs of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation were conducted, was made yesterday in the United States Court for China by Dr. George Sellett, Assistant U.S. District Attorney, in outlining the case for the prosecution at the opening session of the trial of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J. Warner Brown, President and Vice-President of the Corporation, who are indicted on 16 counts of theft and embezzlement involving approximately U.S. $25,000.

Among the highlights of Dr. Sellett's opening speech to the Court, in which Judge Milton J. Helmick presided, were statements to the effect that the defendants had conducted the business of the A.-O.F.C. with reckless and criminal disregard of the interests of their clients by using monies and shares of stock belonging to the latter to bolster up the A.-O.F.C. and its affiliates (the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the Raven Trust Company and the Asia Realty Company); that in turn had utilized the A.-O.F.C. to further their own heavy gambling transactions on the New York stock market; that despite the fact that each of the Raven companies was nominally controlled by a separate board of directors, the companies were in fact operated as one and that the dictator of their policies was Mr. Frank J. Raven.

Crowded Courtroom
Dr. Sellett's address to the Court lasted for an hour and a half and was listened to by a crowded courtroom from which all witnesses, both for the Government and the defence, had been excluded by order of the Judge.

Alongside Dr. Sellett sat Mr. Felthan Watson, U.S. District Attorney for China, but he took no part in the proceedings. Mr. Raven was represented by Attorney Richard T. Evans of Tientsin, while Mr. C. S. Franklin, of the local law firm of Franklin and Harrington, appeared for Mr. Brown.

Court proceedings commenced at 10 a.m. but were delayed by a request from Mr. Evans that the Government be required to set forth in the body of the information the exact statutes under which it is proceeding.

"We want this so that the Government shall be bound by what they say," Mr. Evans pleaded, adding that he would not be satisfied with a formal endorsement upon the back of the information.

Government Not Bound
Dr. Sellett said the Government was of the opinion that it was not bound to set out in the information or to endorse thereon the statutes to which the charges referred, and declared that he would not consent to anything which might be interpreted as an amendment of the information. He proposed that the Court adjourn until 2 p.m. so that the necessary authorities might be consulted. In this suggestion Judge Helmick concurred and the Court adjourned.

When the case was resumed at two o'clock, Dr. Sellett said he had consulted the legal authorities and found beyond any reasonable doubt that the Government was not required under any law or rule of procedure to state the statute or statutes under which an indictment is brought or an information filed. Nor was it required that the title of the statute or statutes should be endorsed upon an indictment or information.

The Assistant District Attorney then quoted copious decisions referring to this matter, showing that any reference, in an indictment or information, to the statute on which such indictment or information is based is "immaterial" and does not form a part of the indictment or information. The same applied in the case of an endorsement of the title of the statute.

Cannot Invalidate
He also showed by quotation that misreference to a statute in an indictment or information does not invalidate them, any indictment or information being "good if it charges an offence under any statute."

Mr. Evans then rose to state that the weight of authority was clearly against his motion, but nevertheless, according to rule, the title of the relevant statute must be embodied in an indictment or information if it were necessary in order to make it "clear and certain." And in this case, counsel contended, reference to statute was necessary.

Judge Helmick, however, sustained Dr. Sellett and over-ruled the motion. Exceptions were noted by Mr. Evans and by Mr. Franklin and it was agreed that during the course of the trial any exception noted by counsel for one of the defendants should automatically be considered as noted for the other defendants as well.

Plead Not Guilty
Pleas of "Not Guilty" were then entered by counsel for the defendants and Dr. Sellett rose to address the Court.

After traversing briefly the 16 counts charging theft and embezzlement against the two defendants, Dr. Sellett launched into an outline of the facts which the Government would seek to prove. The evidence, he said, would be voluminous and complicated. For the sake of clarity and logical development it would

The first section would deal with transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Lucian Claude Marie Bassett. The second involved transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Edward P. Howard. The third involved transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Gordon Yates. The fourth hinged on dealings between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. C. R. Jones. The fifth concerned transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland.

Speaking in measured, incisive tones, the Assistant District Attorney then went on to describe the origin and development of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation. It was started originally, he began, as a holding corporation and in May, 1930, it commenced dealing in New York stocks through the San Francisco office of E. A. Pierce and Company, a New York stock brokerage concern.

Raven Dominating Spirit
"The Government will show," Dr. Sellett continued, "that Mr. Raven, as President, was the moving, dominating spirit in the A.-O.F.C. throughout its existence. He also dominated three other companies — the Raven Trust Company, the American-Oriental Banking Corporation and the Asia Realty Company.

"Mr. Brown was Vice-President and Manager of the corporation. Now an attempt will doubtless be made by the defence to show that Mr. Raven had only the loosest connection with the detailed transactions of the corporation. The Government, however, will prove that this was not at all the case, that Mr. Raven was, in fact, cognizant of everything of importance concerning the corporation and its transactions."

Dr. Sellett went on to relate that in the year 1929 Mr. Raven visited New York and established relations with E. A. Pierce and Company. As a result of this visit, the A.-O.F.C. became a client of E. A. Pierce and Company in stock transactions. A "margin account" was opened by the A.-O.F.C. with E. A. Pierce and Company.

Mr. Raven returned to Shanghai and the A.-O.F.C. commenced soliciting business in shares among the community of Shanghai. The five persons referred to in the indictment were members of a large body of persons who had share dealings with the A.-O.F.C.

Stocks Hypothecated
"These persons," Dr. Sellett declaimed, "thought that they were buying New York stocks through the A.-O.F.C., but in fact the A.-O.F.C. did not buy and pay for the stocks which these persons thought they were buying. All such stocks were at all times hypothecated to E. A. Pierce and Company as security for the indebtedness of the A.-O.F.C. to that company and notwithstanding the fact that these stocks were bought, or supposedly bought, and paid for, through the A.-O.F.C. by customers of the A.-O.F.C. in Shanghai."

Dealing with Mr. Brown's position with the A.-O.F.C., Dr. Sellett said that he had been manager of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation in Tientsin and was brought to Shanghai in 1930 and made Vice-President of the A.-O.F.C. after a preliminary visit to New York to acquaint himself with the stock and share business conducted by E. A. Pierce and Company.

(批：File 3/8 5 JAN. 1936)

《字林西报》，1936年1月4日，星期六
13016

雷文案开庭
政府检察官提出严厉指控

塞莱特博士称被告经营美亚金融公司业务时
对客户利益持鲁莽且犯罪的漠视态度

助理地区检察官概述盗窃和挪用公款指控

根据美国政府拟提出的证据，已倒闭的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation，简称A.-O.F.C.）的事务处理方式受到了严厉指控。昨日，在美国驻华法院审理弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生和J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生案件的开庭会议上，美国助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士在概述控方案情时提出了这一指控。雷文先生和布朗先生分别为该公司总裁和副总裁，他们被指控犯有16项盗窃和挪用公款罪，涉案金额约为25,000美元。

在由米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官主持的法庭上，塞莱特博士在向法庭所作的开场陈述中，重点指出：被告在经营美亚金融公司业务时，对客户利益持鲁莽且犯罪的漠视态度，利用属于客户的资金和股票来支撑美亚金融公司及其关联公司（美亚银行公司、雷文信托公司和亚洲地产公司）；而这些关联公司反过来又利用美亚金融公司为其在纽约股市上的大规模投机交易提供资金；尽管每家雷文旗下的公司在名义上均由独立的董事会控制，但实际上这些公司作为一个整体运作，其政策的独裁者是弗兰克·J·雷文先生。

法庭座无虚席

塞莱特博士向法庭发表的讲话持续了一个半小时，座无虚席的法庭聆听了他的发言。根据法官的命令，所有证人，无论是政府方还是辩护方的证人均被排除在法庭之外。

坐在塞莱特博士旁边的是美国驻华地区检察官费尔坦·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生，但他未参与诉讼程序。雷文先生由天津律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）代表出庭，而布朗先生则由本地富兰克林与哈林顿律师事务所（Franklin and Harrington）的C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生代表出庭。

庭审于上午10时开始，但因埃文斯先生提出要求而推迟，他要求政府在起诉书正文中明确列出其所依据的确切法规。

“我们希望这样，以便政府受其所述内容的约束，”埃文斯先生恳请道，并补充说，他不会对仅在起诉书背面作正式背书感到满意。

政府不受约束

塞莱特博士表示，政府认为其无需在起诉书中列明或在其上背书指控所涉及的法规，并声明他不会同意任何可能被解释为修改起诉书的行为。他建议法庭休庭至下午2时，以便查阅必要的法律依据。赫尔米克法官同意了这一建议，法庭遂休庭。

当案件于两点钟恢复审理时，塞莱特博士表示，他已咨询法律权威人士，并发现毫无疑问，根据任何法律或程序规则，政府无需在提起起诉或提交控告书时说明其所依据的法规。也不要求在起诉书或控告书上背书法规的标题。

随后，这位助理地区检察官引用了大量涉及此事项的判例，表明在起诉书或控告书中提及作为其依据的法规是“无关紧要的”，并不构成起诉书或控告书的一部分。同样的原则也适用于背书法规标题的情况。

不能使其无效

他还通过引文表明，在起诉书或控告书中错误引用法规并不会使其无效，任何起诉书或控告书只要“指控了某项法规下的罪行”即为有效。

埃文斯先生随即起身陈述，虽然权威判例显然不利于他的动议，但根据规则，如果为了使起诉书或控告书“清晰明确”而有必要，相关法规的标题必须包含其中。而在本案中，辩护律师主张，引用法规是必要的。

然而，赫尔米克法官支持塞莱特博士，驳回了该动议。埃文斯先生和富兰克林先生记录了异议，并商定在审判过程中，任何一方被告律师提出的异议应自动视为也为其他被告提出。

 plea 不认罪

随后，被告辩护律师提出了“不认罪”的答辩，塞莱特博士起身向法庭发言。

在简要回顾了针对两名被告的16项盗窃和挪用公款指控后，塞莱特博士开始概述政府试图证明的事实。他说，证据将数量庞大且复杂。为了清晰和逻辑展开起见，这将……

第一部分将处理美亚金融公司与卢西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特（Lucian Claude Marie Bassett）先生之间的交易。第二部分涉及美亚金融公司与爱德华·P·霍华德（Edward P. Howard）先生之间的交易。第三部分涉及美亚金融公司与戈登·耶茨（Gordon Yates）先生之间的交易。第四部分取决于美亚金融公司与C·R·琼斯（C. R. Jones）先生之间的往来。第五部分涉及美亚金融公司与斯坦利·G·柯克兰（Stanley G. Kirkland）先生之间的交易。

助理地区检察官以沉稳、犀利的语调继续描述美亚金融公司的起源和发展。他开始说道，该公司最初是作为一家控股公司成立的，并于1930年5月通过纽约股票经纪公司E. A. Pierce and Company的旧金山办事处开始进行纽约股票交易。

雷文的主导精神

塞莱特博士继续说道：“政府将证明，雷文先生作为总裁，在美亚金融公司存续期间一直是其行动和主导的核心人物。他还主导着另外三家公司——雷文信托公司、美亚银行公司和亚洲地产公司。

“布朗先生是该公司的副总裁兼经理。现在，辩护方无疑会试图表明，雷文先生与公司详细交易之间的联系极为松散。然而，政府将证明事实并非如此，雷文先生实际上知晓有关公司及其交易的所有重要事项。”

塞莱特博士接着叙述道，1929年，雷文先生访问纽约并与E. A. Pierce and Company建立了关系。此次访问的结果是，美亚金融公司成为E. A. Pierce and Company在股票交易方面的客户。美亚金融公司在E. A. Pierce and Company开设了一个“保证金账户”。

雷文先生返回上海，美亚金融公司开始在上海社群中招揽股票业务。起诉书中提到的五人是与美亚金融公司有股票交易往来的众多人员中的一部分。

股票被抵押

塞莱特博士宣称：“这些人以为他们是通过美亚金融公司购买纽约股票，但实际上，美亚金融公司并没有购买和支付这些人以为他们正在购买的股票。所有这些股票在任何时候都被抵押给E. A. Pierce and Company，作为美亚金融公司对该公司债务的担保，尽管这些股票是由美亚金融公司在上海的客户通过该公司购买或据称购买并支付的。”

在谈及布朗先生在美亚金融公司的职位时，塞莱特博士表示，他曾任天津美亚银行的经理，于1930年被带到上海，并在初步访问纽约以熟悉E. A. Pierce and Company经营的股票和股份业务后，被任命为美亚金融公司副总裁。

（批注：档案 3/8 1936年1月5日）

Continuing to describe the alleged methods of business of the A.-O.F.C., Dr. Sellett told the Court that in case of non-cash transactions clients of the A.-O.F.C. paid an average margin of 25 per cent. on the shares which they ordered, hypothecating the shares to the A.-O.F.C. as security for the balance. But the A.-O.F.C. never actually bought the shares ordered by clients. What they did was to, in turn, buy on margin from E. A. Pierce and Company and deposit the shares with that company as security for the balance owing.

Cash Customers Also
This same procedure was observed, Dr. Sellett asserted, in the case of cash customers of the A.-O.F.C. The Government proposed to prove this in the case of the transactions between the A.-O.F.C. and Mr. Lucian Claude Marie Bassett, who paid the A.-O.F.C. cash for the purchase of certain shares which were never in fact purchased, although he was led to believe that they had actually been purchased.

"Mr. Bassett at no time became the owner of the American Telephone and Telegraph and Western Union shares which he paid the A.-O.F.C. cash to purchase for him. The A.-O.F.C. took his money and used it to finance their own business," Dr. Sellett declared.

Asserting that the alleged theft of Mr. Bassett's money by the A.-O.F.C. was deliberate, prosecuting counsel went on to state that evidence would be brought to show that the A.-O.F.C. had sent written reports to Mr. Bassett showing, at various times, that he was the owner of the American Telephone and Telegraph and Western Union shares which he had paid for.

Reposed In Margin A/C
"But when the A.-O.F.C. closed its doors on May 24 last year," Dr. Sellett declared, "it was found that these shares reposed in the margin account which the A.-O.F.C. had with E. A. Pierce and Company—and then not all of them. Pierce and Company held only 377 American Telephone and Telegraph shares for the A.-O.F.C. account all told. In other words, it did not hold sufficient to deliver the number supposedly belonging to Mr. Bassett.

"And when the A.-O.F.C. closed down, Pierce and Company exercised their unquestionable right by selling out all the stocks held on the A.-O.F.C. margin account to satisfy the indebtedness of the A.-O.F.C.

"If, early in May, Mr. Bassett had asked the A.-O.F.C. for the 400 American Telephone and Telegraph shares which he supposed he owned, and if the A.-O.F.C. had answered truthfully, they would have had to tell him that they did not have that many and that they would have to go out and buy them."

Never Became Owners
Continuing, Dr. Sellett said that the purchasers of shares, Mr Bassett, Mr. Howard, Mr. Yates and Mr. Jones, had paid for shares of which they never became the owners. In the case of Mr. Bassett a draft had been given the A.-O.F.C. in payment, and it had been cashed by the A.-O.F.C. It was the Government's contention that the owner of the draft should have become the owner of the shares, but he never did.

In the case of Mr. Kirkland, counsel for the prosecution continued, the victim was induced to part with shares actually registered in his name, with actual scrip.

"Kirkland owed the A.-O.F.C. not a dime and the latter offered to do him a gratuitous service by placing his stocks with Pierce and Company in New York to facilitate dealings in them. But what happened? These shares were dumped by the A.-O.F.C. into its margin account with Pierce and Company. The A.-O.F.C. thus got an additional $1,000 for the financing of its own transactions. And when Pierce and Company sold out the A.-O.F.C. margin stocks, Kirkland's went the way of all the rest."

No Isolated Transaction
"This was not just an isolated transaction. It was the rule," Dr. Sellett asserted. "This is the way the A.-O.F.C. did business. Not in one single instance in which persons fully paid for shares, did the A.-O.F.C. make those persons the owners of such shares."

The Government would show, he went on, that the A.-O.F.C. dealt in shares for three full years before opening a "safe-keeping account" with E. A. Pierce and Company as distinct from the "margin account." Before then, everything was dumped into the margin account. And even when the safe-keeping account had been opened, customers had to exert pressure to get their securities deposited there.

"The A.-O.F.C., of course, had a reason. They wanted to utilize other people's money for their own financial operations. That is why everything went into the margin account. It was with the greatest reluctance that any of the shares of customers of the A.-O.F.C. were deposited in that safe-keeping account."

Heavy Stock Gambling
It was not, however, merely a question of the financial operations of an impersonal corporation. It was a question of the heavy gambling and speculation which the defendants in this case were themselves indulging in New York stocks.

"The Government will bring evidence to show that Mr. Raven was at one time indebted to the A.-O.F.C. in the sum of approximately $200,000 in connection with share transactions, while the indebtedness of Mr. Brown rose as high as $60,000.

"Mr. Brown had, however, found it necessary to show that he was not playing fast and loose with the monies of the A.-O.F.C. It was a simple matter of a book entry. He switched the indebtedness to his wife's name, so that Mrs. Brown and not Mr. Brown appeared as the debtor.

"Mr. Raven had a different device. He made convenient use of the Raven Trust Company. He did not deal in any securities in his own name, but through an account with the Raven Trust Company."

Valueless Security
Dr. Sellett then went on to say that the defendants would try to show that they gave the A.-O.F.C. security for their indebtedness. But this security was of no value to anyone now, he declared.

"The point will also be made that we are accusing officers of the A.-O.F.C. of embezzling money and property belonging to clients, whereas it was the A.-O.F.C., a corporation, which conducted the transactions. The test, however, is whether the defendants dealt with this money and property, which belonged to others, as if they, the defendants, were the owners. The Government will call direct, conclusive evidence to show that they did. They dealt likewise with shares committed to their charge.

"The evidence will show," he declared, "that the Raven Trust Company was controlled by Raven, that practically all of the voting stock was owned by Raven. The American-Oriental Finance Corporation voting stock was practically all owned by the Raven Trust Company, and the American-Oriental Bank and Asia Realty Company voting stock belonged to the Finance Corporation. The evidence will show that these companies in reality were Frank Jay Raven—that Mr. Raven was the dominant figure overshadowing them all.

Conspicuous By Absence
"We do not find his name very often on documents that might incriminate him. His signature, in fact, is conspicuous by its absence. Mr. Brown carried out his orders—carried them out faithfully, but Mr. Brown's story is another case. We will show by at least four important pieces of direct evidence that Raven knew from the very beginning that so-called fully-paid-up shares were being made use of to finance the company's business—that when the Finance Company got possession of shares and scrip that he knew that the common routine procedure was to take it and pledge it to E. A. Pierce and Company.

"In one case, a man with whom they were trying to do business was persuaded to turn over U.S. $76,000 worth of shares and then they took those shares and dumped them into this margin business. Only through someone on the outside interceding did they take them out and put them into a safe-keeping account. Their position was so bad that they had to do this little by little—they could not finance it all at one time because they would need three-quarters of this amount in cash.

No Question Of Mistakes
"There can be no question of mistakes, of slips and errors. It was on more than one occasion that fully paid securities were being held in this way. No one knew better than he (Mr. Raven) what the requirements were for financing the three companies.

"The companies were all linked together. There was no distinction. If one company had money they transferred it to the others. If a gift of Tls. 135,000 each from three companies to one company which was going into the red would cause the public not to lose confidence, it was done. This was the case in April and May, 1935, when they took shares and securities and disposed of them in an effort to save the bank—a fruitless endeavour.

Alleged Guilty Knowledge
"The actual control was not by a board of directors but by a so-called executive council which sat when the board was not in session. Mr. Raven had guilty knowledge of these things at all times.

"I do not think it is necessary to dwell any longer on the facts of the case—the evidence will necessarily be quite voluminous. I will not be able to call any one witness to tell of all of these transactions which are involved as the business of the Finance Company. And when I say 'involved' I say so advisedly, for it is very involved. It may be necessary for the Government to call some witnesses and to then recall them several times so that a clear picture may be given."

Judge Helmick ruled that both the prosecution and the defence might call and recall witnesses at will, and by stipulation of both sides it was entered in the record that both defendants were and had always been American citizens. The hearing was then adjourned until 10 a.m. on Monday.

在继续描述美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.）被指控的经营手法时，塞莱特博士（Dr. Sellett）向法庭陈述，在非现金交易中，美亚金融公司的客户需为其订购的股票支付平均25%的保证金，并将股票抵押给美亚金融公司，作为余款的担保。但美亚金融公司实际上从未购买客户所订购的股票。他们的做法是，转而向E. A. Pierce and Company进行保证金交易购买股票，并将这些股票存入该公司，作为欠付余款的担保。

现金客户亦然
塞莱特博士断言，在美亚金融公司的现金客户案例中，也采用了同样的程序。政府方面拟在美亚金融公司与卢西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特先生（Mr. Lucian Claude Marie Bassett）的交易案中证明这一点。巴塞特先生曾向美亚金融公司支付现金以购买某些股票，尽管他被引导相信这些股票确实已被购买，但实际上它们从未被购入。

“巴塞特先生从未成为他付现金委托美亚金融公司购买的美国电话电报公司（American Telephone and Telegraph）和西联汇款公司（Western Union）股票的所有人。美亚金融公司拿走了他的钱，并将其用于资助其自身的业务，”塞莱特博士宣称。

公诉律师声称美亚金融公司盗窃巴塞特先生的钱财是蓄意为之，并进一步指出，将提出证据表明，美亚金融公司曾向巴塞特先生发送书面报告，在不同时间显示他是其所付款购买的美国电话电报公司和西联汇款公司股票的所有人。

存于保证金账户
“但当美亚金融公司于去年5月24日关门停业时，”塞莱特博士宣称，“人们发现这些股票存放于美亚金融公司在E. A. Pierce and Company开立的保证金账户中——而且甚至并非全部股票。Pierce and Company总共仅为美亚金融公司账户持有377股美国电话电报公司股票。换言之，其持有的数量不足以交付据称属于巴塞特先生的股票数目。

“而当美亚金融公司倒闭时，Pierce and Company行使了其无可争议的权利，出售了美亚金融公司保证金账户中持有的所有股票，以清偿美亚金融公司的债务。

“如果巴塞特先生在5月初向美亚金融公司索要他自以为拥有的400股美国电话电报公司股票，而如果美亚金融公司如实回答，他们就必须告诉他，他们没有那么多股票，并且必须出去购买这些股票。”

从未成为所有人
塞莱特博士继续说道，股票的购买者，即巴塞特先生、霍华德先生（Mr. Howard）、耶茨先生（Mr. Yates）和琼斯先生（Mr. Jones），支付了款项却从未成为这些股票的所有人。在巴塞特先生的案例中，他曾向美亚金融公司开具汇票作为付款，该汇票已被美亚金融公司兑现。政府方面主张，汇票的所有人本应成为股票的所有人，但他从未成为所有人。

公诉律师接着指出，在柯克兰先生（Mr. Kirkland）的案例中，受害者被诱使交出了实际登记在他名下、并有实体股票凭证的股票。

“柯克兰并不欠美亚金融公司一分钱，而后者提出无偿为他提供服务，将他的股票存入纽约的Pierce and Company，以便于交易。但结果如何？这些股票被美亚金融公司扔进了其在Pierce and Company的保证金账户。美亚金融公司因此额外获得了1,000美元，用于资助其自身的交易。而当Pierce and Company抛售美亚金融公司保证金账户中的股票时，柯克兰的股票也随其他股票一同遭殃。”

并非孤立交易
“这不仅仅是一笔孤立的交易。这是常规做法，”塞莱特博士断言。“这就是美亚金融公司的经营方式。在任何人全额支付股票款项的情况下，美亚金融公司没有一次使这些人成为这些股票的所有人。”

他继续说道，政府方面将表明，美亚金融公司在与E. A. Pierce and Company开立区别于“保证金账户”的“保管账户”之前，已从事股票交易整整三年。在此之前，所有东西都被扔进保证金账户。即使后来开立了保管账户，客户也必须施加压力才能将其证券存入该账户。

“当然，美亚金融公司是有原因的。他们希望利用他人的资金进行自身的金融运作。这就是为什么所有东西都进入保证金账户的原因。美亚金融公司客户的任何股票被存入该保管账户都是极不情愿的。”

大规模股票投机
然而，这不仅仅是一个非人格化公司的金融运作问题。本案被告自身在纽约股票市场上沉迷于大规模赌博和投机，这也是一个问题。

“政府将提出证据表明，雷文先生（Mr. Raven）曾因股票交易欠美亚金融公司约20万美元，而布朗先生（Mr. Brown）的欠款高达6万美元。

“然而，布朗先生觉得有必要表明他并未随意挪用美亚金融公司的资金。这只是账面上的一个简单的操作。他将债务转至其妻子名下，因此债务人显示为布朗夫人而非布朗先生。

“雷文先生则使用了不同的手段。他便利地利用了雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）。他不以自己的名义进行任何证券交易，而是通过雷文信托公司的账户进行交易。”

无价值的担保
塞莱特博士随后表示，被告将试图表明他们为自身的债务向美亚金融公司提供了担保。但他宣称，这种担保对现在的任何人来说都没有价值。

“还有一点需要指出，我们指控美亚金融公司的高管侵吞属于客户的资金和财产，而进行交易的是美亚金融公司这一法人实体。然而，检验标准在于被告是否像他们是所有者一样处理这些属于他人的资金和财产。政府将提供直接、确凿的证据表明他们确实如此行事。他们同样处理了交由他们保管的股票。

“证据将表明，”他宣称，“雷文信托公司由雷文控制，几乎所有有表决权的股票均由雷文拥有。美亚东方金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的有表决权股票几乎全部由雷文信托公司拥有，而美亚东方银行（American-Oriental Bank）和亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）的有表决权股票则属于该金融公司。证据将表明，这些公司实际上就是弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）——雷文先生是笼罩在所有公司之上的主导人物。

因缺席而显眼
“我们在可能使其获罪的文件上并不常看到他的名字。事实上，他的签名因缺失而显得格外显眼。布朗先生执行了他的命令——忠实地执行，但布朗先生的说法又是另一回事。我们将通过至少四份重要的直接证据表明，雷文从一开始就知道，所谓的全额付清股票正被用于资助公司业务——当金融公司获得股票和实体凭证时，他知道通常的程序是拿走这些股票并将其质押给E. A. Pierce and Company。

“在一个案例中，一个他们试图与之做生意的人被说服移交了价值76,000美元的美国股票，随后他们将这些股票扔进了这项保证金业务。仅靠外部人士的干预，他们才将这些股票取出并放入保管账户。他们的处境如此糟糕，以至于只能一点一点地这样做——他们无法一次性为全部业务融资，因为他们需要这笔金额的四分之三作为现金。

绝非失误问题
“这不存在失误、疏忽或错误的问题。全额付清的证券以这种方式被持有不止一次。没有人比他（雷文先生）更清楚为这三家公司融资所需的要求。

“这些公司都是相互关联的。没有区别。如果一家公司有钱，他们就将其转移到其他公司。如果从三家公司各向一家即将出现赤字的公司赠送135,000两白银，能防止公众失去信心，他们就会这样做。1935年4月和5月就是这种情况，当时他们处置股票和证券，试图挽救银行——这是一次徒劳的努力。

被指控的明知故犯
“实际控制权不在董事会手中，而在一个所谓的执行委员会手中，该委员会在董事会休会期间召开会议。雷文先生对这些事情始终具有犯罪明知。

“我认为没有必要再详述案件事实——证据必然相当庞杂。我无法传唤任何一位证人来讲述涉及金融公司业务的所有这些交易。当我说‘涉及’时，我是经过深思熟虑的，因为情况非常错综复杂。政府方面可能有必要传唤一些证人，然后多次重新传唤他们，以便呈现清晰的画面。”

赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）裁定，控辩双方均可随意传唤和重新传唤证人，并且经双方约定，记录在案表明两名被告均为且一直是美国公民。随后听证会休庭，直至周一上午10点继续。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, DECEMBER 31, 1935

Raven, Brown Motion For
A Trial By Jury Denied
By U.S. Court For China

Judge Helmick Not Prepared Lightly To Upset The
Established Practice Of The Past 29 Years;
Time Limit Results In Prompt Ruling

DEFENDANTS' COUNSEL URGE EXTENSION
OF 700-YEAR-OLD HUMAN RIGHT

Declaring that because of the limitations of time and
the necessity for a prompt ruling it was impossible for him
to write or even attempt to state a reasoned opinion on the
question, and that he was not disposed lightly to upset what
had been the established and unquestioned policy for the
past 29 years, Judge Milton J. Helmick yesterday afternoon
overruled the motion of Mr. Frank J. Raven and Mr. J.
Warner Brown, President and Vice-President, respectively,
of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, for
a trial by jury on the 16 charges of theft and embezzlement
which are due for hearing in the United States Court for
China on Friday morning.

This decision followed a lengthy
presentation of the pros and cons
by Mr. Richard T. Evans, attorney
for Mr. Raven, Mr. C. S. Franklin,
attorney for Mr. Brown, and Dr.
George Sellett, Assistant U. S.
District Attorney.

Constitutional Right
The burden of Mr. Evans'
argument revolved around the
question as to whether the right
of an American citizen to a jury
trial, as embodied in the Constitu-
tion of the United States, could be
denied in an extraterritorial
jurisdiction where local conditions
did not render a trial by jury
impracticable.

Citing a well-known case in the
United States Court at Yokohama
in the year 1880, many years
before extraterritoriality was
abolished in Japan, Mr. Richards
said that in the case in question
a trial by jury had been denied
to an American citizen charged
with murder solely for the reason
that there was not a sufficient
number of American citizens
then resident in that jurisdiction
from which a jury could have been
drawn.

The situation in Shanghai to-
day, counsel went on to contend,
was vastly different. What was
impossible in Yokohama in 1880
was entirely possible in Shanghai
to-day. There were 3,700 Ameri-
can citizens in Shanghai, of whom
there were 800 men, between the
ages of 21 and 50, eligible as
jurors and, if eligible women
were added, twice that number.

The panel provided for in the
District of Columbia Code, which
governed the procedure of the
U.S. Court for China, counsel
said, was one of 300. It was
obvious, therefore, that there was
no obstacle in this respect to
finding the required number from
which to draw eligible jurors in
Shanghai.

Cogent Reasons Sought
Continuing, Mr. Evans declar-
ed that the Constitution was a
part of the law of the United
States and that it was applicable
outside of the United States,
although not as an over-riding
law. There was no reason for
not applying it here. Whenever
a jury was denied, there must be
cogent reasons for so doing.

"The question is not one of
mere convenience," he went on
to say. "There may be technical
difficulties, but they are not in-
superable. However, the question
is one of the rights of the in-
dividual, which cannot be denied
without due cause. Their right
of the individual is the right to
be tried by men of his own neigh-
bourhood, who live in his own
environment, people who will
judge him by the standards of
conduct of the people in his own
community and not merely ac-
cording to the law—in a word,
the right to trial by a jury of
his peers.

"It is not our submission,"
counsel concluded, "that the de-
fendants in this case must have
a jury trial because of their right
to a fair trial—that issue is not
involved here—but because the
case should be dealt with in ac-
cordance with stated principles."

Mr. Franklin's View
Mr. C. S. Franklin, who fol-
lowed, said there was no ques-
tion but that the Constitution
was a part of the law of the
United States. That being so, it
must be applied within the
jurisdiction of the U.S. Court
for China unless there was a
law preventing its application or
local conditions rendered its ap-
plication impracticable.

"The constitutional provision
for jury trials was inapplicable
in Yokohama in 1880," counsel
said, "solely because there were
too few Americans there in those
early days, the number then being
exceedingly small. It is an
inescapable conclusion that this
was the reason. If this same
reason could be applied to Shang-
hai, it would be inapplicable
here, too. But, as Mr. Evans
has shown, such is not the case."

Replying to counsel for the
defendants, Dr. George Sellett
told the Court that their argu-
ments amounted to this, namely,
that since there had been a
growth of the American popula-
tion in Shanghai since 1880, trial
by jury had become necessary,
notwithstanding the fact that the
law on the subject had not
changed.

The Act Of 1906
"By the Act of Congress, in
1906 which established this
Court," the Assistant District
Attorney declared, "a provision
was made for a better system of
administration of justice in this
jurisdiction than that which had
existed previously. The Legis-
lature supplanted the old system
of Consular Courts, in which
Consuls tried cases with one or
more associates, with an appeal to
the Minister, knowing full well
that up till then there had been
no such thing as trial by jury.
Yet in the Act of 1906 by which
this Court was established no pro-
vision was made for trial by jury.
It seems clear, therefore, that the
Legislature contemplated no such
thing."

On the subject of the practicabil-
ity of trial by jury, Dr. Sellett
said it might be possible to find
12 qualified jurors in Shanghai,
but it was necessary to consider
the jurisdiction of the U. S. Court
for China as a whole. "Could 12
jurors be found in such places as
Amoy, Foochow or Yunnanfu?"
counsel queried. On the question
of practicability, therefore, the
facts were entirely against the de-
fendants. The law on the subject,
on the other hand, was well settled
and established.

700-Year-Old Right
Mr. Evans, in rejoinder, said he
was fully sensible of the difficul-
ties in the way of jury trials
which Dr. Sellett had suggested.
But these were matters of detail
and the question at issue was far
more fundamental than that. Trial
by jury had been regarded as a
right of man for some 700 years.
It was not something of no con-
sequence which could be lightly
swept away. The defendants
should not be denied this right
otherwise than if the Court found
itself prohibited by law from
granting it.

Adding to these remarks, Mr. C.
S. Franklin asserted that the Con-
stitution followed the flag of the
United States even into extra-
territorial jurisdictions where it
was locally applicable. In was
entirely possible to get a jury in
Shanghai and therefore the Con-
stitution, a part of the general law
of the United States, should be
applied here.

Judge Helmick's Decision
In rendering his decision, Judge
Helmick said: "Because of the
limitations of time and the neces-
sity for a prompt ruling on this
motion, it is, of course, impossible
to write, or even attempt to state,
a reasoned opinion on this ques-
tion. If I had been the first judge
of the United States Court for
China, and this argument had been
presented 29 years ago, there
would be no limit of time prevent-
ing me. But, after 29 years of
settled policy, I do not feel that I
should make any ruling lightly, in
off-hand fashion, which would up-
set that settled policy.

"If we have been mistaken all
these years, I think correction
should come from our Courts. It
seems to me that there are plenty
of precedents in this Court which
support the propositions advanced
by the Government. Any judge,
I think, would prefer to divide re-
sponsibility with a jury in a
criminal case, but that is not of
persuasive force in passing on this
question, which is one purely of
law.

"I am sure that although I agree
to a great extent with the views
of the Government, no extempor-
aneous expression will contribute
anything to the law on the subject
or be of much importance. There
has been an established and un-
questioned policy which is not like-
ly to be departed from. I shall
therefore over-rule the motion,

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年12月31日，星期二

拉文（Raven）、布朗（Brown）要求
由陪审团审判的动议被
美国驻华法院驳回

赫尔米克（Helmick）法官不愿轻易推翻
过去29年既定的惯例；
时限导致迅速裁决

被告律师敦促延长
这项拥有700年历史的人权

赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官昨日下午驳回了已解散的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）总裁弗兰克·J·拉文（Frank J. Raven）先生和副总裁J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生的动议，二人就定于周五上午在美国驻华法院听审的16项盗窃和挪用公款指控要求由陪审团进行审判。法官声明，由于时间限制以及需要迅速作出裁决，他不可能撰写甚至尝试陈述关于此问题的推理意见，并且他不愿意轻易推翻过去29年来既定且毋庸置疑的政策。

这一决定是在拉文先生的律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生、布朗先生的律师C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生以及美国助理地区检察官乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士对正反双方观点进行了 lengthy（冗长）陈述之后作出的。

宪法权利

埃文斯先生辩论的重点围绕这样一个问题：在美国宪法中体现的美国公民由陪审团审判的权利，是否可以在当地情况并未使陪审团审判变得不切实际的治外法权管辖区域内被剥夺。

埃文斯先生引用了1880年在横滨美国法院的一个著名案例，那是在日本废除治外法权很多年之前。他说，在该案中，一名被控谋杀的美国公民被拒绝由陪审团审判，唯一的原因是当时该管辖区内居住的美国公民数量不足，无法从中选出陪审团。

律师接着争辩说，如今上海的情况大不相同。1880年在横滨不可能做到的事，在今天上海是完全可能的。上海有3,700名美国公民，其中有800名年龄在21至50岁之间的男性符合担任陪审员的资格，如果加上符合条件的女性，人数将是这一数字的两倍。

律师说，管辖美国驻华法院程序的《哥伦比亚特区法典》规定陪审团候选名单为300人。因此，显而易见的是，在上海从符合条件的人选中找出所需数量的陪审员在这方面没有任何障碍。

寻求有力理由

埃文斯先生继续声明，宪法是美国法律的一部分，虽然它不是至高无上的法律，但也适用于美国境外。在这里没有理由不适用它。每当拒绝由陪审团审判时，必须有充分的理由这样做。

“这不仅仅是一个便利与否的问题，”他接着说，“可能存在技术上的困难，但这些困难并非不可克服。然而，这是一个个人权利的问题，如果没有正当理由，不得予以剥夺。个人的权利是由与其生活在同一环境、同一邻里的同类人来审判的权利，这些人将以其所在社区人们的行为标准而不仅仅是根据法律来评判他——简而言之，就是由同等地位的人组成的陪审团进行审判的权利。

“我们并非主张，”律师总结道，“本案被告因为享有公平审判的权利而必须接受陪审团审判——这里不涉及这个问题——而是因为本案应按照既定原则进行处理。”

富兰克林先生的观点

随后发言的C·S·富兰克林先生说，毫无疑问，宪法是美国法律的一部分。既然如此，除非有法律阻止其适用，或者当地情况使其适用变得不切实际，否则必须在美国驻华法院的管辖范围内适用宪法。

“1880年在横滨，宪法关于陪审团审判的规定不适用，”律师说，“仅仅是因为在那些早期日子里，那里的美国人太少，数量极其微小。这是一个不可避免的结论，即这就是原因。如果同样的理由可以适用于上海，那么它在这里也不适用。但是，正如埃文斯先生所示，事实并非如此。”

在回复被告律师时，乔治·塞莱特博士告诉法庭，他们的论点归结为这一点，即既然自1880年以来上海的美国人口有所增长，尽管有关此事的法律并未改变，但由陪审团审判已成为必要。

1906年法案

“通过1906年建立本法院的国会法案，”助理地区检察官宣称，“为本管辖区建立了比此前存在的更好的司法管理体系。立法机关取代了旧的领事法院体系，在旧体系中，领事与一名或多名协理官审理案件，并可向公使上诉，他们完全清楚直到那时还没有陪审团审判这回事。然而，在建立本法院的1906年法案中，并没有规定由陪审团审判。因此，似乎很清楚，立法机关并未考虑此类事情。”

关于陪审团审判的可行性问题，塞莱特博士说，在上海也许能找到12名合格的陪审员，但有必要考虑美国驻华法院的整体管辖范围。“在厦门、福州或云南府这样的地方能找到12名陪审员吗？”律师问道。因此，就可行性而言，事实完全对被告不利。另一方面，关于此事的法律已经非常明确和确立。

700年的权利

埃文斯先生在反驳中说，他充分意识到塞莱特博士提出的陪审团审判面临的困难。但这些都是细节问题，而争议的问题要根本得多。大约700年来，陪审团审判一直被视为人的权利。这不是可以轻易扫除的无关紧要之事。除非法院发现法律禁止授予此项权利，否则不应剥夺被告的这一权利。

C·S·富兰克林先生补充这些 remarks（言论）时断言，宪法跟随美国国旗，甚至进入其在当地适用的治外法权管辖区域。在上海组成陪审团是完全可能的，因此，作为美国一般法律一部分的宪法应在此适用。

赫尔米克法官的裁决

赫尔米克法官在作出裁决时说：“由于时间的限制以及对此动议迅速作出裁决的必要性，当然不可能撰写，甚至尝试陈述关于此问题的推理意见。如果我是美国驻华法院的第一任法官，并且这一辩论是在29年前提出的，那么就不会有时间限制阻碍我。但是，经过29年既定的政策之后，我觉得我不应该以轻率、随意的方式作出任何会推翻该既定政策的裁决。

“如果这些年来我们都错了，我认为纠正应来自我们的法院。在我看来，本法院有足够的先例支持政府提出的主张。我认为，任何法官在刑事案件中都更愿意与陪审团分担责任，但这对于通过这一纯粹的法律问题没有说服力。

“我确信，虽然我在很大程度上同意政府的观点，但任何即兴的表达都不会对有关此事的法律有所贡献，也不会具有多大重要性。已经存在一项既定且毋庸置疑的政策，不太可能偏离。因此，我将驳回该动议， noting the...”

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, December 28, 1935
191273

Jury Trial Asked
In A.-O.F.C. Cases

16 New Counts Filed
Against Raven And
Brown Today

Shortly after 16 additional counts on criminal charges had been filed against them in the United States Court for China this morning, the Messrs. Frank Jay Raven and John Warner Brown filed a motion for a jury trial.

Their motion, through their attorneys, Mr. Richard T. Evans of Tientsin and the Messrs. Franklin and Harrington of Shanghai, set forth that there are enough Americans here for qualified jurors, that they are innocent of the charges against them, and that they desire a trial by a jury of their peers in accordance with law.

The motion asks that a jury list be made, talesmen drawn and a jury impaneled.

Affidavit Is Filed

In addition to the motion both Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown, Mr. Brown filed an affidavit for a jury trial.

The move for a jury trial created much interest and speculation in local legal circles. During the approximately 30 years' history of the United States Court for China, there have never been any jury trials. It is believed, however, that there are several cases dating far back, including one when Americans had extraterritoriality in Japan, which provide precedents bearing on the issue. There is also a famous decision of the United States Supreme Court that "the constitution does not follow the flag," which referred specifically to the Philippines but might have bearing here, it was suggested.

Only British Use Juries

No local extraterritorial courts excepting that of Great Britain use the jury system.

The sixteen additional counts, charging embezzlement, fraud and theft, were filed by the United States Government against the Messrs. Raven and Brown as president and vice-president respectively of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

Fifteen charges of embezzlement were filed against the Messrs. Raven, Brown and Alfred H. Driscoll, secretary and treasurer of the A.O.F.C., on August 31. Their arrest followed and they were released under bonds of U.S.$10,000 each for the Messrs. Raven and Brown and U.S.$5000 for Mr. Driscoll.

Trial Starts Next Friday

Recently, in connection with hearing on postponement of trial for the second time, it was announced that new counts would be filed, but without requiring additional bail. It was also indicated that the trial now scheduled to begin next Friday would be on the new counts with probable eventual nol-prossing of the old counts.

The 16 new counts do not include Mr. Driscoll, and consequently a sensational development in the trial appeared foreshadowed.

The new counts were filed by United States District Attorney Pelham Watson and his recently appointed Special Assistant, Dr. George Sellett.

Nature Of Counts

The first of the new counts

Brown on or about December 18, 1933, embezzled a draft for U.S.$11,-553 in favor of Mr. Lucian Claude Marie Bassett which was drawn on the Irving Trust Company, New York City, by the Shanghai office of the Banque Franco-Chinoise pour le Commerce et l'Industrie. The second count charges embezzlement of money from Mr. Bassett in the amount of the draft. The third count charges theft of the draft.

The fourth count charges that the Messrs. Raven and Brown did "feloniously and with intent to defraud one Lucian Claude Marie Bassett falsely pretend and represent to him and cause to be falsely pretended and represent to him that the said American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc. U.S.A., had....on or about December 16, 1933, purchased for the said Lucian Claude Marie Bassett 100 shares of stock of the American Telegraph and Telephone Company of the reasonable worth and value of U.S.$11,553," represented by the aforementioned draft, "whereas in truth and fact that said American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc. U.S.A., had not purchased" the aforesaid shares.

More Stock Purchases

The fifth count also charges fraud in the case of Mr. Bassett, and involves the alleged purchase of 500 shares of A. T. & T. and 200 shares of Western Union, and the alleged sale of 200 shares of A. T. & T. and 100 shares of W. U. between December 16, 1933 and May 31, 1934, through E. A. Pierce and Company, New York City, and further, that in consequence of the alleged deals, Mr. Bassett paid to the E. A. Pierce and Company U.S.$10,000 to establish an additional credit balance with the A.-O.F.C. to be used for buying other stock.

The sixth count charges embezzlement of a draft of U.S.$507.60, drawn by the Shanghai office of the National City Bank of New York in favor of the A.-O.F.C. for Mr. Edward P. Howard. The seventh count charges embezzlement of money from Mr. Howard in the amount of the draft. The eighth count charges theft of the draft.

Yates Charges

The ninth count charges embezzlement of a check for Shanghai $1225.97 to the A.-O.F.C. by Mr. Gordon Yates on the Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China. The 10th count charges embezzlement of money from Mr. Yates in the amount of the check. The 11th count charges theft of the check.

The 12th count charges embezzlement of a check for Shanghai $549.18 to the A.-O.F.C. by Mr. C. R. Jones on the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank. The 13th count charges embezzlement of money from Mr. Jones in the amount of the check. The 14th count charges theft of the check.

Kirkland Charges

The 15th count charges embezzlement from Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland of 25 Socony-Vacuum shares (each U.S.$9.87), 25 I. T. and T. shares (each U.S.$12.75), 25 Packard Motor Car Company shares (each U.S.$4.25), 15 General Electric shares (each U.S.-

In a brief hearing this morning in chambers, Judge Milton J. Helmick allowed amendment of Mr. Raven's petition in bankruptcy to include an additional claim of the Asia Life Insurance Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A., for Shanghai $11,050.

191273

美亚金融公司案
要求陪审团审判

今日对雷文和布朗
提起16项新指控

今天上午，在中国美国法院对他们提起16项额外的刑事指控后不久，弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）先生和约翰·沃纳·布朗（John Warner Brown）先生提交了陪审团审判的动议。

他们的律师——天津的理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生以及上海的富兰克林（Franklin）和哈林顿（Harrington）诸位先生——通过该动议陈述称，此处有足够数量的美国人可担任合格陪审员；他们对所受指控无罪；并且希望依法由同等地位的同伴组成陪审团进行审判。

该动议请求编制陪审员名单，抽取候补陪审员，并组建陪审团。

提交宣誓书

除了该动议外，布朗先生还提交了一份要求陪审团审判的宣誓书。（注：原文此处表述略显重复，意指雷文和布朗均提出动议，且布朗额外提交了宣誓书）

要求陪审团审判之举在当地法律界引起了极大关注和猜测。在中国美国法院约30年的历史中，从未有过任何陪审团审判。然而，据信有几个年代久远的案件，包括一个美国人在日本享有治外法权时期的案件，提供了与此问题相关的先例。此外，还有人指出，美国最高法院有一项著名裁决称“宪法不随国旗延伸”，该裁决虽特指菲律宾，但可能与此处情况有关联。

仅英国使用陪审团

除英国法庭外，当地没有任何治外法权法庭使用陪审团制度。

这16项新增指控指控侵吞、欺诈和盗窃，由美国政府针对已解散的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的前总裁雷文先生和前副总裁布朗先生提起。

8月31日，针对雷文先生、布朗先生以及美亚金融公司秘书兼财务主管阿尔弗雷德·H·德里斯科尔（Alfred H. Driscoll）先生，提起了15项侵吞指控。随后他们被捕，并以每人10,000美元（雷文和布朗）及5,000美元（德里斯科尔）的保释金获释。

审判将于下周五开始

最近，在第二次延期审判的听证会上，当局宣布将提起新的指控，但无需增加保释金。同时表示，现定于下周五开始的审判将针对新指控进行，旧指控可能会最终被撤销（nol-prossing）。

这16项新指控不包括德里斯科尔先生，因此审判中似乎预示着一个轰动性的发展。

新指控由美国地区检察官佩勒姆·沃森（Pelham Watson）及其最近任命的特别助理乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士提起。

指控性质

第一项新指控

布朗于1933年12月18日左右，侵吞了一张以吕西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特（Lucian Claude Marie Bassett）先生为收款人、金额为11,553美元的汇票，该汇票由法中实业银行（Banque Franco-Chinoise pour le Commerce et l'Industrie）上海分行开具，付款人为纽约市欧文信托公司（Irving Trust Company）。第二项指控指控从巴塞特先生处侵吞与该汇票金额相等的款项。第三项指控指控盗窃该汇票。

第四项指控指控雷文先生和布朗先生“重罪性地并意图欺诈吕西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特先生，虚假地向他声称并导致向他虚假声称，上述美亚金融公司（联邦股份有限公司，美国）……已于1933年12月16日左右，为上述吕西安·克劳德·玛丽·巴塞特购买了价值合理的100股美国电话电报公司（American Telegraph and Telephone Company）股票，价值11,553美元”，由前述汇票代表，“而事实上，上述美亚金融公司（联邦股份有限公司，美国）并未购买”上述股票。

更多股票购买行为

第五项指控也指控在巴塞特先生一案中存在欺诈行为，涉及据称在1933年12月16日至1934年5月31日期间，通过纽约市的E. A. Pierce and Company公司购买500股美国电话电报公司股票和200股西联汇款公司（Western Union）股票，以及出售200股美国电话电报公司股票和100股西联汇款公司股票的行为；此外，据称由于这些交易，巴塞特先生向E. A. Pierce and Company公司支付了10,000美元，以在美亚金融公司建立额外的信用余额，用于购买其他股票。

第六项指控指控侵吞一张金额为507.60美元的汇票，该汇票由纽约花旗银行（National City Bank of New York）上海分行为爱德华·P·霍华德（Edward P. Howard）先生开具给美亚金融公司。第七项指控指控从霍华德先生处侵吞与该汇票金额相等的款项。第八项指控指控盗窃该汇票。

耶茨相关指控

第九项指控指控戈登·耶茨（Gordon Yates）先生通过印度新金山打马银行（Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China）向美亚金融公司开具的一张金额为上海银1,225.97两的支票被侵吞。第十项指控指控从耶茨先生处侵吞与该支票金额相等的款项。第十一项指控指控盗窃该支票。

第十二项指控指控C. R. 琼斯（C. R. Jones）先生通过汇丰银行（Hongkong and Shanghai Bank）向美亚金融公司开具的一张金额为上海银549.18两的支票被侵吞。第十三项指控指控从琼斯先生处侵吞与该支票金额相等的款项。第十四项指控指控盗窃该支票。

柯克兰相关指控

第十五项指控指控从斯坦利·G·柯克兰（Stanley G. Kirkland）先生处侵吞25股索科尼-真空石油公司（Socony-Vacuum）股票（每股9.87美元）、25股国际电话电报公司（I. T. and T.）股票（每股12.75美元）、25股帕卡德汽车公司（Packard Motor Car Company）股票（每股4.25美元）、15股通用电气公司（General Electric）股票（每股19.87美元）、10股斯图贝克公司（Studebaker Corporation）股票（每股3美元）以及2又3/8股美国无线电公司（Radio Corporation of America）股票（每股7.25美元），所有这些股票均由美亚金融公司保管。

第十六项指控指控盗窃上述股票。

内室听证

在今天上午简短的内室听证会上，米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官允许修改雷文先生的破产申请，以包含亚洲人寿保险公司（Asia Life Insurance Company，联邦股份有限公司，美国）的一项额外债权，金额为上海银11,050两。

关于雷文先生通过破产申请解除所有债务的请求听证会延期举行。

归档
1935年12月8日

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 27, 1935 19244

New Actions
Are Expected
Against Raven

Information Reported
Due For Filing At
U.S. Court

FURTHER DELAYS
NOT ANTICIPATED

Trial Scheduled To
Start Jan. 3 In
Local Court

With the opening of the trial of Messrs. Frank J. Raven, J. Warner Brown and A. H. Criscoll on charges of misappropriation scheduled to commence before Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China on January 3. It is reported that additional information against them will probably be filed with the clerk of courts within the next day or two.

This knowledge was obtained by a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday afternoon from reliable sources. The filing will be done by Dr. George Sellett, especially appointed assistant U.S. District Attorney, more than a month ago to work with the Government in the handling of the case. Dr. Sellett and Mr. Felthan Watson, U. S. District Attorney, have been working hard for the past month preparing this information and it is understood that it is practically ready to be filed.

That such information would be filed was announced on November 29 when the case was set to come up for hearing. A reset was requested at that time on the grounds that more information had been obtained since the arrival of Messrs. Charles Curtis and C. J. Haley from the United States, brought here to appear as witnesses for the prosecution. The reset was granted, and January 3 was the date agreed upon.

It is believed that no further delay will be requested by the prosecution and the Government is prepared to go ahead with its case. This, however, is not certain since THE CHINA PRESS reporter could obtain neither confirmation or denial from the interested authorities. The case was originally scheduled to open on October 29, but was reset to November 29 in order to give Messrs. Curtis and Haley time to arrive from the United States, and reset against for the filing of new information.

In the charges filed last August by Mr. Watson, the three accused are alleged to have disposed of shares and bonds placed in the care of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, of which they were directors, on 15 different counts.

《字林西报》，1935年12月27日，星期五 19244

预计将对雷文
提起新诉讼

据报道将在
美国法院提交
起诉书

预计不会
进一步延期

审判定于1月3日
在地方法院开始

随着弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）、J·沃纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）和A·H·克里斯科尔（A. H. Criscoll）三位先生涉嫌挪用公款案的审判定于1月3日在中国美国法院由米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官主持开庭，据悉，针对他们的补充起诉书很可能在未来一两天内提交给法院书记员。

《字林西报》记者昨天下午从可靠消息来源获悉了这一情况。提交工作将由乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士完成，他于一个多月前被特别任命为美国地区检察官助理，协助政府处理此案。塞莱特博士和美国地区检察官费尔坦·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生在过去一个月里一直在努力准备这份起诉书，据了解，该文件已基本准备好提交。

早在11月29日该案安排听证时，就已宣布将提交此类起诉书。当时以查尔斯·柯蒂斯（Charles Curtis）和C·J·哈利（C. J. Haley）两位先生从美国抵达此处作为控方证人出庭为由，获得了自他们抵达后获取更多证据的机会，因此请求重新安排日期。重新安排获准，商定日期为1月3日。

据信，控方不会要求进一步延期，政府已准备好推进其案件。然而，这并不确定，因为《字林西报》记者未能从相关当局获得确认或否认。该案原定于10月29日开庭，但为了给柯蒂斯和哈利两位先生从美国抵达留出时间，改期至11月29日，后又因提交新证据而再次改期。

在沃森先生去年8月提起的指控中，三名被告被指控在15项不同罪名下，处置了交由他们担任董事的美亚金融公司保管的股票和债券。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 18, 1935
Bitter Accusations Made In
Asia Electric Litigation
Mr. Truman Johnson Charged With Betraying The
Friendship Of The Whittakers In Inducing
Them To Buy Shares In The Company

After a lengthy hearing in the
United States Court for China
yesterday of the case of Edward
G. and Evelyn L. Whittaker
against the Asia Electric Com-
pany, Fed. Inc., U.S.A., in which
the plaintiffs are seeking nullifica-
tion of a contract for the pur-
chase of $51,000 worth of shares
in the defendant corporation on
the ground that they were induc-
ed to buy the shares through
fraudulent misrepresentation,
judgment was reserved and Judge
Milton J. Helmick announced that
he would file a memorandum
thereon within the next day or
two.

Yesterday's hearing was note-
worthy for the bitter accusations
of the plaintiffs against Mr.
Truman Johnson, former pres-
ident of the corporation, and Mr.
Felthan Watson, the U.S. District
Attorney. Mr. Myron L. Weiner
appeared for the Whittakers,
while N. F. Allman represented
the Asia Electric Company.

Mrs. Whittaker testified at
great length concerning the pre-
liminaries which led her husband
and herself to purchase and pay
cash for $51,000 worth of shares
in the corporation. She said they
had been induced to do so by Mr.
Truman Johnson, on the strength
of statements by the latter to the
effect that he himself had made
substantial investments in the
stock of the corporation.

Discovery In August

It was discovered last August,
however, that Mr. Johnson had
not paid for his shares, which had
been issued to him against pro-
missory notes, a procedure which
was clearly irregular under the
provisions of the China Trade
Act which governs the operations
of the corporation.

Mr. Johnson, witness said, had
been a close personal friend of
herself and her husband. In in-
ducing them to invest in the Asia
Electric Company he had fraud-
ulently misrepresented the true
position and betrayed their
friendship.

When she discovered that Mr.
Johnson had bought shares in the
corporation against promissory
notes, Mrs. Whittaker told the
Court, she went to Mr. Felthan
Watson, the District Attorney,
and asked him to take appropri-
ate action.

"Mr. Watson assured me," she
said, "that Mr. Johnson would
not leave town. I filed a com-
plaint, and Mr. Watson said he
would have it served on Mr. John-
son if the latter tried to leave
Shanghai. Mr. Johnson did leave
and Mr. Watson took no action
whatsoever."

Government Failed Her

"I went to my government for
aid," witness declaimed indig-
nantly, "and did not get it. I then
engaged a private attorney to
protect my interests."

Extensive testimony was given
by Mrs. Whittaker and her hus-
band concerning their personal
relations with Mr. Johnson, de-
signed to show that personal
friendship and the confidence
springing therefrom had been
the determining factor in induc-
ing the Whittakers to part with
$51,000 for shares in the Asia
Electric Company.

Counter-evidence to prove that
the Whittakers could have ascer-
tained the true position in regard
to Mr. Johnson's shares had they
tried to do so and that there had
been no attempt to misrepresent
the position of the corporation,
was given by Captain A. R. St.
Louis, the present responsible
officer of the Asia Electric Com-
pany.

At the conclusion of evidence,
Mr. Myron L. Weiner, for the
plaintiffs, told the Court that
fraudulent misrepresentation had
been abundantly proved. When
Mr. Johnson told the plaintiffs
that he owned 10,000 shares in
the Asia Electric Company, he in
fact owned only 3,000 since the
other 7,000, although registered
in his name, were not paid for.
At other times, Mr. Johnson had
represented himself as the owner
of 25,000 and 35,000 shares re-
spectively. In fact, however, these
shares were "paid for" with pro-
missory notes which had not yet
been met.

Corporation Responsible

There was no responsibility in
the plaintiffs, counsel argued, to
attempt to verify Mr. Johnson's
statements. Mr. Johnson was
a responsible officer of the
corporation and the corporation
was liable for his statements. He
therefore asked the Court to
order rescission of the contract
whereby the Whittakers had pur-
chased $51,000 worth of shares
and refund of the $51,000 paid for
them.

In reply, Mr. Allman pointed
out that the balance sheets of the
Asia Electric Company, to which
Mr. Whittaker had access, show-
ed Mr. Johnson as indebted to the
corporation in respect of promis-
sory notes. As one-time secretary
of the corporation, Mr. Whittaker
was, he contended, in a position
to ascertain all the facts.

Because the corporation had
lost money and was not to-day in
a very healthy position, counsel
for the corporation contended,
was not a reason for cancelling
the sales of shares. The Whit-
takers would have to take their
medicine. Mr. Johnson, it was
true, had not paid cash for his
shares, as the Whittakers had
done, but he was still paying up
his instalments, as represented by
the promissory notes, when they
fell due.

Judgment was then reserved.

（批：B. D. 6748 12 12 3:）
（手写签名：Jile JH）

《字林西报》，1935年12月18日，星期三

亚洲电力公司诉讼案中的激烈指控

特鲁曼·约翰逊先生被控背叛惠特克夫妇的友谊，诱使他们购买该公司股票

昨日，在美国驻华法院对爱德华·G·惠特克（Edward G. Whittaker）和伊夫林·L·惠特克（Evelyn L. Whittaker）诉美国联邦注册的亚洲电力公司（Asia Electric Company, Fed. Inc., U.S.A.）一案进行了长时间的聆讯。原告以受欺诈性虚假陈述诱导为由，寻求废除购买被告公司价值51,000美元股票的合同。法庭暂保留判决，米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官宣布将在未来一两天内就此提交备忘录。

昨日的聆讯引人注目之处在于，原告对该公司前总裁特鲁曼·约翰逊（Truman Johnson）先生和美国地区检察官费尔森·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生提出了激烈的指控。迈伦·L·韦纳（Myron L. Weiner）先生代表惠特克夫妇出庭，而N·F·奥尔曼（N. F. Allman）则代表亚洲电力公司。

惠特克夫人就导致其丈夫和她本人购买并以现金支付价值51,000美元该公司股票的前因后果作了长篇证词。她表示，他们是受到特鲁曼·约翰逊先生的诱导才这样做的，依据是后者声称他自己已在该公司股票中进行了大量投资。

八月间的发现

然而，去年八月发现，约翰逊先生并未支付其股票款项，这些股票是凭本票发给他的，这种做法显然违反了管辖该公司运营的《在华贸易法》（China Trade Act）的规定。

证人称，约翰逊先生曾是她和她丈夫的亲密私人朋友。在诱使他们投资亚洲电力公司时，他欺诈性地歪曲了真实情况，背叛了他们的友谊。

惠特克夫人告诉法庭，当她发现约翰逊先生是凭本票购买该公司股票时，她去找了地区检察官费尔森·沃森先生，请他采取适当行动。

她说：“沃森先生向我保证，约翰逊先生不会离开上海。我提交了投诉书，沃森先生说，如果约翰逊先生试图离开上海，他会将传票送达给他。但约翰逊先生确实离开了，而沃森先生未采取任何行动。”

政府未能提供帮助

“我向我的政府寻求帮助，”证人愤慨地陈述道，“但没有得到帮助。随后我聘请了一位私人律师来保护我的利益。”

惠特克夫人及其丈夫就他们与约翰逊先生的私人关系提供了大量证词，旨在表明私人友谊及由此产生的信任是促使惠特克夫妇拿出51,000美元购买亚洲电力公司股票的决定性因素。

亚洲电力公司现任负责人A·R·圣路易斯（A. R. St. Louis）上尉提供了反证，以证明如果惠特克夫妇尝试去查明，他们本可以弄清约翰逊先生持股的真实情况，且并不存在歪曲公司状况的企图。

举证结束后，原告代理人迈伦·L·韦纳先生告诉法庭，欺诈性虚假陈述已得到充分证明。当约翰逊先生告诉原告他拥有亚洲电力公司10,000股股票时，事实上他只拥有3,000股，因为其余7,000股虽然登记在他名下，但并未付款。在其他时候，约翰逊先生曾分别声称自己拥有25,000股和35,000股。然而事实上，这些股票是用尚未兑现的本票“支付”的。

公司应负责任

辩护律师辩称，原告没有责任去核实约翰逊先生的陈述。约翰逊先生是公司的负责官员，公司应对其陈述负责。因此，他请求法庭命令撤销惠特克夫妇购买价值51,000美元股票的合同，并退还已支付的51,000美元。

作为回应，奥尔曼先生指出，惠特克先生有权查阅的亚洲电力公司资产负债表显示，约翰逊先生因本票事宜对公司负有债务。他争辩说，惠特克先生曾任公司秘书，有能力查明所有事实。

公司律师辩称，因为公司亏损且目前财务状况不佳，并不是取消股票销售的理由。惠特克夫妇必须自食其果。诚然，约翰逊先生不像惠特克夫妇那样用现金支付股票款项，但他仍在按期支付由本票代表的分期付款。

随后法庭暂保留判决。

（批：B. D. 6748 12 12 3:）
（手写签名：Jile JH）

12,000 Checks To
A.O.B.C. Depositors
Mailed Out By Hough

The first checks for the
initial 7½ per cent dividend for
depositors and preferred cre-
ditors of the American-Oriental
Banking Corporation were mailed
Saturday morning, Mr. Frank L.
Hough, liquidator of the bank,
told a CHINA PRESS reporter
last night.
Mailings will continue daily,
Mr. Hough stated, until the
entire dividend has been paid.
A second mailing was sent out
yesterday. About 600 checks
were mailed Saturday and ap-
proximately the same number
went out yesterday. Approxi-
mately 600 more will be sent out
today.
Mr. Hough stated about 600
checks were all he could sign in
a day without acquiring a severe
stroke of writer's cramp. To get
that many signed, he said, was
quite a task and kept him well
occupied.
The 7½ per cent dividend is
being paid out of collections
amounting to more than $850,000,
this sum having been collected
by the liquidator since he took
over the affairs of the bank al-
most seven months ago.

霍夫寄出
12,000张支票给
美亚银行储户

美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生昨晚告诉《大美晚报》记者，针对该银行储户和优先债权人的首期7½%股息的第一批支票已于周六上午寄出。

霍夫先生表示，邮寄工作将持续每天进行，直到全部股息支付完毕。第二批邮件已于昨日发出。周六寄出了约600张支票，昨天发出的数量大致相同。今天还将再寄出约600张。

霍夫先生称，一天签署约600张支票是他不至于患上严重书写痉挛的极限。他说，签署这么多支票是一项艰巨的任务，让他忙得不可开交。

这7½%的股息是从总额超过850,000美元的收款中支付的，这笔款项是清算人在近七个月前接管银行事务以来所收集的。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, NOVEMBER 29, 1935

MR. RAVEN ASKS FOR
DEBT DISCHARGE

U.S. Court To Consider
Bankrupt's Petition
On December 28

Discharge from all claims for
debt against him personally is be-
ing sought by Mr. Frank J. Raven,
President of the defunct American-
Oriental Banking Corporation and
affiliates, in a petition which he
has submitted to the United States
Court for China, hearing on which
will take place before Milton J.
Helmick on December 28.

Mr. Raven declares in his peti-
tion, which was filed on his behalf
by Mr. Richard T. Evans, his at-
torney, that he was adjudged a
bankrupt and has now surrendered
all his property and property
rights to the Trustees appointed
in his estate and has fully com-
plied with all the provisions of the
Federal Bankruptcy Act of the
United States and all orders of the
Court relating to his property.

He therefore asks the Court to
give him a full discharge from all
debts provable against his estate
under the Act relating to such
debts, and which may be accepted
in law as dischargeable.

$10,000 Legal Fee

Simultaneously, Mr. Richard T.
Evans has filed with the Court an
affidavit giving details of a $10,000
claim against Mr. Raven for legal
fees, it being stated that Mr.
Evans agreed to represent Mr.
Raven in all legal proceedings for
a single fee of that amount, pay-
able in advance.

This agreement was to be effec-
tive for a period of two years
from July 27, 1935. No part of
the fee, however, has yet been paid,
nor has there been any set-off or
counter-claim filed.

As security for payment of the
fee, the affidavit continues, Mr.
Evans was given a second mort-
gage on the land and home of Mr.
Raven at 55 Hungjao Road. The
deed of mortgage is now in the
hands of Mr. Frank L. Hough,
Trustee of Mr. Raven's estate and
Liquidator of the Raven concerns.

《字林西报》，1935年11月29日，星期五

雷文先生申请
解除债务

美国法院将于
12月28日审议
破产者请愿书

已停业的美亚银行及其关联机构总裁弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生向美国驻华法院提交了一份请愿书，寻求免除针对他个人的所有债务索赔。该请愿书的聆讯将于12月28日由米尔顿·J·赫尔米克主持。

雷文先生在其由其律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生代为提交的请愿书中声明，他已被裁定为破产者，现已将其所有财产和财产权利移交给为其遗产指定的受托人，并完全遵守了美国《联邦破产法》的所有规定以及法庭关于其财产的所有命令。

因此，他请求法庭根据与该等债务相关的法案，免除其遗产下所有可证明的、且在法律上可被视为可免除的债务。

10,000美元律师费

与此同时，理查德·T·埃文斯先生已向法庭提交了一份宣誓书，详细说明了针对雷文先生的一笔10,000美元律师费索赔。宣誓书称，埃文斯先生同意以该笔一次性费用代表雷文先生处理所有法律诉讼，该费用需预付。

该协议自1935年7月27日起生效，为期两年。然而，该笔费用至今未支付任何部分，也未提出任何抵销或反诉。

宣誓书继续称，作为支付该笔费用的担保，埃文斯先生获得了雷文先生位于虹桥路55号的土地和住宅的第二顺位抵押权。该抵押契据目前由雷文先生遗产受托人兼雷文相关机构清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫先生持有。
