THE SHANGHAI TIMES. FRIDAY. OCTOBER 18. 1935
U.S. Court Postpones Raven
Trial To November 29
Vigorous Legal Argument At Hearing Yesterday As
Defence Attorneys Oppose Further Delay In
Case; Affidavits By Three Defendants

A postponement of the trial of
Mr. Frank J. Raven, Mr. J.
Warner Brown and Mr. Alfred H.
Driscoll on charges of embezzle-
ment arising from the alleged con-
version of securities committed for
safekeeping to the American-
Oriental Banking Corporation, now
in process of liquidation was
granted by Judge Milton J. Hel-
mick in the United States Court
for China yesterday at the in-
stance of Mr. Felthan Watson.
U.S. District Attorney, but in the
face of strenuous opposition from
the defence attorneys.

At the conclusion of a session
which lasted all morning, the
Judge ordered that the case,
originally scheduled to open on
October 29, be re-set for hearing
on November 29, or 30 days later.

Mr. Watson's motion, asking for
a continuance for at least one
month, was filed on Wednesday
afternoon. It set forth that the
United States Attorney General
had asked for this continuance by
telegraph on October 15, declaring
that it was absolutely necessary
in order that the Attorney General
might be able to complete arrange-
ments for securing the presence at
the trial of certain witnesses now
residing in the United States and
to obtain certain essential
documentary evidence.

All three defendants were pre-
sent in Court yesterday. Mr.
Raven was represented by Mr.
Richard T. Evans of Tientsin,
while both Mr. C. S. Franklin and
Mr. W. B. Harrington, of the
local law firm of Franklin and
Harrington, appeared for Messrs
Brown and Driscoll.

Investigation In U.S.A.

When the proceedings opened at
10 a.m., the District Attorney rose
to inform the Court that ever since
the filing of the informations
against the accused on August 31,
investigations, conducted through
the Department of Justice, had
been proceeding in various cities
of the United States and that
these had not been completed.

"There has been no negligence
in my office," Mr. Watson said.
"The Court will realize that there
are difficulties in view of the fact
that we are 3,000 miles from head-
quarters. There are four witnesses
to be brought here for the Govern-
ment from the U.S.A., and the
Attorney-General advises that they
cannot get here by October 29, the
date already set for this trial.
Hence my motion for a continu-
ance."

Mr. Evans, speaking for the
defending attorneys, said that they
objected to the motion being dealt
with in the form in which it had
been filed. Legal practice for the
past 200 years, Mr. Evans declar-
ed, required that such a motion
should be supported by an affidavit
showing proper legal cause for a
continuance, regardless of whe-
ther the continuance was sought
by the defence or the Government.
Such an affidavit, counsel con-
tinued, must be such as to satisfy
the Court that the absent witnesses
are material witnesses in the
case, and that the party making
the application for continuance
has not been negligent in produc-
ing his witnesses in due time. The
Court must also be reasonably
satisfied that the witnesses sought
will be present on the date to
which a postponement of the trial
is asked.

"Most Casual Manner"

Asking leave to intervene in the
discussion, Mr. C. S. Franklin de-
clared that the District Attorney
had come into Court in the most
casual manner, without any sub-
stantial support for his motion.
The defendants, he continued, were
entitled to an early and speedy
trial. Their characters and their
whole future were at stake. At
present they were living in Shang-
hai without means and might, if
obliged to remain here indefinitely,
become a charge upon the Am-
erican community.

"Suppose that, when the District
Attorney is finally forced to trial,
it is found that the witnesses in
respect to whom this motion was
filed are immaterial and the
documentary evidence inadmiss-
ible?" counsel queried, associating
himself with Mr. Evans' demand
for a supporting affidavit from the
District Attorney.

Judge Helmick: I would be in
entire agreement with you in the
case of a continuance in the legal
and technical sense. But since the
Court here, unlike the United
States, does not have terms, I am
inclined to treat the District At-
torney's motion as an application
to rest.

Mr. Franklin: What would your
Honour consider a continuance in
the legal and technical sense in
this Court?

Judge Helmick: That is very
hard to say, but there is a dis-
tinct difference between a continu-
ance and a re-setting and I feel
that there is no such thing as a
continuance within this jurisdic-
tion. Therefore, I am inclined to
treat this as an application to re-
set, and to give the Attorney-
General the additional time asked
for. I don't like to do it, but I
think it is necessary."

Motion Not Verified

It then transpired that the Dis-
trict Attorney's motion had not
been verified and, at the sugges-
tion of the Judge, he agreed to
withdraw it and refile it latter,
after verification.

Assuming verification and refil-
ing, Judge Helmick then said he
would treat the motion as an ap-
plication to re-set, a matter in
which the Court was entitled to
exercise its discretion.

Mr. Franklin said he wished the
Court to note two exceptions, first
to the weight attached by the
Court to the Attorney General's
representation, and secondly to
any re-setting as an abuse of the
Court's discretion in view of the
lack of any support for the Dis-
trict Attorney's motion. Mr. Evans
said he wished to be associated
with these two exceptions.

Judge Helmick proceeded to re-
peat his previously-expressed view
of the matter. "I shall treat this
as an application to re-set the
case. The Court realizes that it
must exercise its discretion in a
reasonable manner. The defendants
are entitled to a speedy trial, but
I do not think the application is
unreasonable. It comes from the
Attorney-General of the United
States. He would not wish to
harass the defendants or do them
an injustice. The Court has to be
more indulgent than would be the
case if all the Government wit-
nesses resided in Shanghai or in
China. This is an important case
and should be thoroughly present-
ed on both sides. The Court should
not refuse any reasonable request
which will make possible a com-
plete hearing.

Defendants' Affidavits

Asking that the Court exercise
its discretion against any post-
ponement of the trial, counsel for
the defence presented to the Court
affidavits by each of the defend-
ants. The affidavit of Mr. Raven,
read out by his attorney, declared
that the defendant was not guilty
of the charges preferred against
him and that he desired a speedy
trial; that he was about to file a
petition in voluntary bankruptcy
and, therefore, considered that
such means as he had above the
necessity of his subsistence should
be kept intact for his creditors;
that he was without employment
pending these proceedings; that he
was 60 years of age and under a
great mental strain at the present
time.

Mr. Brown's affidavit, read out
by Mr. W. B. Harrington, stated
that Mr. Brown is now and has
at all times been ready to defend
himself against the charges
brought against him; that he is
not guilty on any of the counts
alleged; that of his own free will
and volition he urged the Court
to allow him to return to its
jurisdiction from Manila after he
had learned of the charge against
him; that he is now in Shanghai
without remunerative occupation
and that to delay or continue the
hearing over a matter of 30 days
or a longer indefinite period will
embarrass him financially and will
in all likelihood render him de-
pendant on others.

The affidavit of Mr. Driscoll,
also read out by Mr. Harrington,
stated that he is now and at all
times has been prepared to defend
himself against the charges; that
he is not guilty on any of the
counts; that he has at no time
made himself a fugitive from
justice, nor encumbered nor in-
terfered with a speedy trial; that
he is without means of earning his
livelihood in Shanghai and has
been without remunerative occupa-
tion since August 23; that to wait
in Shanghai over an indefinite
period of time or for a greater
length of time beyond October 29
will render him destitute.

Apparently unmoved by the
considerations set forth in these
documents, Judge Helmick ordered
that the case be re-set for Novem-
ber 29, intimating that no delay
beyond that date would be per-
mitted.

File
JMS

美国法院将雷文案审判推迟至11月29日
昨日听证会上激烈的法律辩论，辩护律师反对进一步延期；三名被告提交宣誓书

美国驻华法院法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）昨日应美国地区检察官费尔桑·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生的请求，批准推迟弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生、J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）先生和阿尔弗雷德·H·德里斯科尔（Alfred H. Driscoll）先生的审判，尽管此举遭到辩护律师的强烈反对。上述被告被控挪用罪，罪名源于涉嫌将委托给美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation，现正处于清算过程中）保管的证券进行非法转换。

在持续整个上午的庭审结束时，法官命令将原定于10月29日开庭的案件重新排期，定于11月29日，即30天后进行审理。

沃森先生要求至少延期一个月的动议于周三下午提交。动议指出，美国司法部长已于10月15日通过电报要求此次延期，声明这对于司法部长完成安排确保证人出庭至关重要，这些证人目前居住在美国，此外还需获取某些必要的书面证据。

三名被告昨日均出庭。雷文先生由来自天津的理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生代理，而布朗先生和德里斯科尔先生则由本地富兰克林与哈林顿律师事务所（Franklin and Harrington）的C·S·富兰克林（C. S. Franklin）先生和W·B·哈林顿（W. B. Harrington）先生共同代理。

在美国的调查

上午10时程序开始后，地区检察官起身告知法庭，自8月31日对被告提起控告以来，通过司法部在美国各城市进行的调查一直在进行，且尚未完成。

“我办公室没有任何疏忽，”沃森先生说。“法庭会意识到，鉴于我们距离总部有3,000英里，存在诸多困难。政府需要从美国带四名证人到这里，司法部长告知他们无法在10月29日之前赶到，而这一天已是原定审判日期。因此我提出延期动议。”

代表辩护律师发言的埃文斯先生说，他们反对以目前提交的形式处理该动议。埃文斯先生宣称，过去200年的法律实践要求，此类动议必须附有宣誓书，显示延期的正当法律理由，无论延期是由辩方还是政府提出。 counsel 继续说道，此类宣誓书必须足以让法庭确信，缺席的证人是案件中的重要证人，且申请延期的一方在及时提供证人方面没有疏忽。法庭还必须合理地确信，所寻求的证人将在要求推迟审判的日期出庭。

“最为随意的态度”

C·S·富兰克林先生请求介入讨论，他宣称地区检察官以一种最为随意的方式进入法庭，其动议没有任何实质性支持。他接着说，被告有权获得早期且迅速的审判。他们的名誉和整个未来都危在旦夕。目前他们在上海生活，没有经济来源，如果被迫无限期地留在这里，可能会成为美国社区的负担。

“假设当地区检察官最终被迫进行审判时，发现就该动议所涉及的证人并不重要，且书面证据不可采纳，那该怎么办？” counsel 问道，并表示支持埃文斯先生要求地区检察官提供支持性宣誓书的诉求。

赫尔米克法官：如果是法律和严格意义上的延期，我将完全同意你的观点。但是，既然这里的法庭不像美国那样有庭期（terms），我倾向于将地区检察官的动议视为重新排期的申请。

富兰克林先生：阁下认为在本法庭中，法律和严格意义上的延期是指什么？

赫尔米克法官：这很难说，但延期和重新排期之间有明显的区别，我觉得在本司法管辖区内不存在所谓延期的概念。因此，我倾向于将此视为重新排期的申请，并给予司法部长所要求的额外时间。我不喜欢这样做，但我认为这是必要的。”

动议未经核实

随后 выяснилось，地区检察官的动议未经核实，在法官的建议下，他同意撤回该动议，并在核实后重新提交。

假定经过核实并重新提交，赫尔米克法官随后表示，他将把该动议视为重新排期的申请，这是一项法庭有权行使自由裁量权的事项。

富兰克林先生说，他希望法庭记录两项异议，第一是对法庭赋予司法部长陈述的权重表示异议，第二是鉴于地区检察官的动议缺乏任何支持，将任何重新排期视为滥用法庭自由裁量权的行为。埃文斯先生说，他希望附议这两项异议。

赫尔米克法官接着重申了他此前对此事的看法。“我将把这视为重新排期案件的申请。法庭意识到必须以合理的方式行使自由裁量权。被告有权获得迅速审判，但我认为该申请并非不合理。它来自美国司法部长。他不希望骚扰被告或对他们造成不公。如果所有政府证人都居住在上海或中国，法庭本不必如此宽容。这是一个重要案件，双方都应充分陈述。法庭不应拒绝任何能使全面听证成为可能的合理请求。

被告的宣誓书

辩护律师请求法庭行使自由裁量权反对任何审判延期，并向法庭提交了每名被告的宣誓书。由其律师宣读的雷文先生的宣誓书声明，被告对被指控的罪名无罪，并希望迅速审判；他即将提交自愿破产申请，因此认为除维持生计必需之外的资产应保持完整以偿还债权人；在这些诉讼 pending 期间他处于失业状态；他现年60岁，目前承受着巨大的精神压力。

由W·B·哈林顿先生宣读的布朗先生的宣誓书指出，布朗先生现在及一直以来都准备对自己面临的指控进行辩护；他对所有被指控的罪名均无罪；他在得知针对他的指控后，出于自愿主动请求法庭允许他从马尼拉返回本司法管辖区；他目前在上海没有有报酬的职业，将听证会推迟或延期30天或更长的不确定时期将使他在财务上陷入困境，并很可能使他依赖他人。

同样由哈林顿先生宣读的德里斯科尔先生的宣誓书指出，他现在及一直以来都准备对指控进行辩护；他对所有罪名均无罪；他从未让自己成为逃避司法制裁的人，也未阻碍或干扰迅速审判；他在上海没有谋生手段，自8月23日以来一直从事无报酬的工作；在上海等待不确定的时期或超过10月29日更长的时间将使他一贫如洗。

显然未受这些文件中所述考虑因素的影响，赫尔米克法官命令将案件重新排期至11月29日，并暗示不允许超过该日期的任何延误。

归档

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 19, 1935

Secrecy Veils Arrival
Of Raven Witnesses

Names May Be Withheld
Until They Actually
Take The Stand

4 OR 5 EXPECTED
FROM AMERICA

Evans May File Petition
Of Bankruptcy This
Morning

Utmost secrecy is being maintained by U. S. District Attorney Felthan Watson regarding the identities of the four or five witnesses who are to be sent to Shanghai to testify at the trial of Messrs. Frank Jay Raven, J. Warner Brown and A. H. Driscoll, former officials of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation. The trial has been reset for November 29.

Questioned yesterday by a CHINA PRESS reporter as to whether or not he had anything to say concerning the identities of the witness, Mr. Watson said that there was nothing he could say, not even if he wanted to.

It was learned later the identities of the witnesses may not be disclosed until they have actually taken the witness stand. No information is to be released concerning the boat they are to arrive on, and it is likely that every effort will be made to keep their names away from the press.

In the meantime, Mr. Richard T. Evans, attorney for Mr. Raven, is busy in connection with the filing of petition of bankruptcy for his client. This petition is expected to be filed this morning, but there is nothing certain about it, and it may be held over until early next week.

It is believed that, this petition will not contain a list of the personal assets and indebtedness of Mr. Raven but will merely state that cause exists as to why bankruptcy should be granted, and that the list of financial responsibilities and holdings will be prepared and submitted within a time limit set by the court.

Mr. Raven and his co-defendants charged with misappropriation strenuously objected to Judge Milton J. Helmick's consent to delay their trial another month, both through their attorneys and in signed affidavits presented to the court and which stated that all three were in difficult financial circumstances and that a speedy trial was needed.

The three have been charged on 15 counts of misappropriation of stocks and bonds placed in their custody for safe keeping.

《大美晚报》，1935年10月19日，星期六

雷文案证人抵达情况笼罩在秘密之中

姓名可能在实际上庭作证前不予公开

预计4或5人从美国前来

埃文斯可能于今晨提交破产申请

关于将被派往上海在美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）前官员弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）、J·华纳·布朗（J. Warner Brown）和A·H·德里斯科尔（A. H. Driscoll）先生的审判中作证的四五名证人的身份，美国地区检察官费尔桑·沃森严守秘密。审判已重新排期至11月29日。

昨日，《大美晚报》记者询问沃森先生是否就证人身份发表任何评论时，沃森先生表示他无可奉告，即使他想说也不行。

后来得知，证人的身份可能要直到他们实际出庭作证时才会披露。关于他们将乘坐哪艘船抵达的消息不会发布，而且很可能会尽一切努力使他们的名字不被媒体知晓。

与此同时，雷文先生的代理律师理查德·T·埃文斯先生正忙于为其客户提交破产申请。预计该申请将于今晨提交，但这并不确定，可能会推迟到下周初。

据信，该申请不会包含雷文先生的个人资产和债务清单，而仅陈述存在授予破产的理由，财务责任和持有资产清单将在法庭规定的期限内编制并提交。

雷文及其同案被告被控挪用罪，他们通过律师以及向法庭提交的签署宣誓书，强烈反对米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官同意将他们的审判再推迟一个月，宣誓书中指出三人都处于困难的财务状况，需要迅速审判。

三人被控15项挪用罪，罪名涉及挪用交由他们保管的股票和债券。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 19, 1935 11348

Leaves Town

Mr. Truman Johnson, former president of the Asia Electric Company, and head of the Pacific Banking Corporation, who left Shanghai on the Nagasaki Maru yesterday, en route to his home in California.

Johnson Leaves
Shanghai With
Nagasaki Maru

Former Asia Electric
President Will Not
Return To City

Mr. Truman Johnson, whose name figured prominently in the news the past three weeks because of his connection with the court hearings into the affairs of Asia Electric Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A., has departed from Shanghai, it has been learned, and does not plan to return to this city.

He has resigned as president of Asia Electric and departed from this city yesterday. He was also president of the Pacific Banking Corporation. A notice in the window of the latter institution at 210 Szechuen Road, announces that the space is for rent. The bank is moving, a CHINA PRESS reporter was told yesterday, but the informant didn't say where.

Regarding the departure of Mr. Johnson, Captain A. R. St. Louis, managing-director of Asia Electric, stated yesterday that a new president will be elected at the next meeting of the board of directors. At present, Captain St. Louis is in active charge of the organization.

Mr. Johnson was an active force in the founding of the Asia Electric and the Pacific Banking Corporation, the latter being established a year ago. Asia Electric became news when Miss A. Viola Smith, Registrar of the China Trade Act, filed action against the company on the grounds that stock had been sold for promissory notes in direct violation of the Trade Act. She asked revocation of the charter and the appointment of a trustee. Both of these requests were denied by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Court for China be-

fore whom the case was heard. Judge Helmick, however, announced that the court would retain the case and that the defendant company could have 60 days in which to remedy the situation that existed because of the purchase of stock with promissory notes. In this connection, Captain St. Louis stated yesterday that the directors have now passed a resolution in exact accordance with Judge Helmick's resolution, and he expected the trouble would be straightened out in the near future.

Mr. Johnson had planned to leave Shanghai sometime ago but postponed his departure when Miss Smith filed her action. Much of the stock involved in the court affair had been issued to him and his wife. Mr. Johnson was accompanied by his wife and children and are bound for their home in Pasadena, California.

《字林西报》，1935年10月19日，星期六 11348

离沪

亚洲电力公司（Asia Electric Company）前总裁、太平洋银行公司（Pacific Banking Corporation）负责人杜鲁门·约翰逊（Truman Johnson）先生，昨日乘长崎丸号（Nagasaki Maru）离开上海，前往其位于加利福尼亚的家中。

约翰逊乘
长崎丸号
离开上海

前亚洲电力
公司总裁将不
返回本市

据悉，杜鲁门·约翰逊先生已离开上海，并无意返回本市。过去三周，因牵涉美国联邦亚洲电力公司（Asia Electric Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A.）事务的法庭听证会，他的名字频繁见诸报端。

他已辞去亚洲电力公司总裁职务，并于昨日离开本市。他还曾担任太平洋银行公司总裁。昨日，一位《字林西报》记者获悉，该机构位于四川路210号的橱窗内张贴了一则告示，称该处房屋招租。该银行正在搬迁，但消息人士未透露迁往何处。

关于约翰逊先生的离任，亚洲电力公司总经理A. R. 圣路易斯（A. R. St. Louis）上尉昨日表示，将在下一次董事会会议上选举新总裁。目前，圣路易斯上尉正积极主持该机构的工作。

约翰逊先生在创立亚洲电力公司和太平洋银行公司方面发挥了积极作用，后者成立于一年前。当中国贸易法注册官A. 维奥拉·史密斯（A. Viola Smith）小姐以违反《贸易法》直接规定、用本票出售股票为由对公司提起诉讼时，亚洲电力公司成为新闻焦点。她请求撤销公司章程并任命受托人。审理此案的美国在华法院法官米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）驳回了这两项请求。然而，赫尔米克法官宣布，法院将保留此案管辖权，并给予被告公司60天时间，以补救因用本票购买股票而造成的状况。对此，圣路易斯上尉昨日表示，董事会已通过一项完全符合赫尔米克法官决议的决议，他预计这一问题将在不久的将来得到解决。

约翰逊先生此前曾计划于某时离开上海，但在史密斯小姐提起诉讼后推迟了行程。涉及法庭案件的大量股票已发行给他及其妻子。约翰逊先生由其妻儿陪同，正前往他们在加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳（Pasadena）的家。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 16, 1935

NO RECEIVER FOR
ASIA ELECTRIC

Judgment Given in China
Trade Act Case

JUDGE HELMICK FINDS
VIOLATION OF LAW

A period of sixty days in which
to remedy a stock sale violation was
given the Asia Electric Co., Fed. Inc.,
by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the
U.S. Court for China yesterday
afternoon. The application by Miss
A. Viola Smith, China Trade Act
Registrar, for the appointment of a
trustee or receiver to investigate the
company's affairs was dismissed. on
the grounds that the U.S. Govern-
ment was not concerned in the
internal financial affairs of the com-
pany or with any controversy be-
tween shareholders.
Giving judgment, Judge Helmick
said that the proceedings were insti-
tuted by the China Trade Act Re-
gistrar for the revocation of the
certificate of incorporation of the
defendant company, under the provi-
sions of Section 14 of the Act. It
appeared that 4,040 shares of stock
were sold during 1932 and 1934, in
exchange for promissory notes, none
of which had been paid.
It could not be questioned that
promissory notes were "personal pro-
perty," and that stock could be law-
fully issued and paid for by promis-
sory notes, but the Act clearly laid
down that no stock could be paid for
in anything but cash unless a cer-
tificate describing the property for
which it was sold. and stating the
value at which it was to be received,
had been filed with the Secretary of
Commerce or the Registrar, and
providing that either the Secretary
or the Registrar certified that the
value placed on the property was not
more than its fair mortgage value.
No such certificate had ever been
filed, and the Court found a clear
violation of the Act, although the
violation in itself was not harmful to
the corporation or the stockholders.

The Corporation's Condition

The corporation was not in a
prosperous condition, but had dis-
posed of the greater part of its assets
to pay creditors, and was now trying
to build up a business in a compara-
tively small way. The remedy ap-
peared to lie in the enforcement of
immediate payment for the stock if
the purchasers were sufficiently
solvent, or in its cancellation if they
were not. It was not clear how re-
vocation of the company's charter
would especially benefit creditors or
other stockholders, and indeed the
directors, who held a majority of the
stock, did not desire liquidation or
the appointment of a receiver or
trustee.
The government's interest was
served when the illegal stock trans-
action was corrected, and any decree
of liquidation or receivership would
have to be made in a proper suit
brought by interested parties.
"The Court will retain jurisdiction
of this cause," he concluded," and
allow the defendant sixty days within
which to remedy the stock sale
violation before making any final
order. The restraining order here-
tofore entered will be vacated."
***The full text of the judgment will
appear in the "North-China Herald," on
October 23.

《字林西报》，1935年10月16日，星期三

亚洲电力公司
不设接管人

中国贸易法案件
作出判决

法官赫尔米克认定
违法

昨日下午，美国在华法院法官米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克给予美国联邦亚洲电力公司（Asia Electric Co., Fed. Inc.）六十天期限，以补救股票销售违规行为。中国贸易法注册官A. 维奥拉·史密斯（A. Viola Smith）小姐申请任命受托人或接管人以调查公司事务的请求被驳回，理由是美国政府不关心公司的内部财务事务或股东之间的任何争议。

赫尔米克法官在宣判时表示，诉讼程序是由中国贸易法注册官根据该法第14条的规定提起的，旨在撤销被告公司的注册证书。经查，1932年和1934年间，有4,040股股票是以本票交换出售的，且这些本票均未兑付。

毫无疑问，本票属于“个人财产”，股票可以合法发行并以本票支付，但该法明确规定，除非向商务部长或注册官提交一份描述所售财产并声明其接收价值的证书，且由部长或注册官证明该财产的价值不超过其公平抵押价值，否则股票不得以现金以外的任何形式支付。从未提交过此类证书，法院认定这明显违反了该法，尽管这种违规本身并未对公司或股东造成损害。

公司的状况

该公司经营状况不佳，但已处置大部分资产以偿还债权人，目前正试图以相对较小的规模重建业务。补救措施似乎在于：如果购买者有足够的偿付能力，则强制立即支付股票款项；如果没有，则取消股票。目前尚不清楚撤销公司章程如何能特别有利于债权人或其他股东，事实上，持有大多数股票的董事们并不希望清算或任命接管人或受托人。

当非法股票交易得到纠正时，政府的利益即得到维护，任何清算或接管令都必须在利害关系方提起的适当诉讼中作出。

“法院将保留对此案的管辖权，”他总结道，“并在作出任何最终命令之前，给予被告六十天时间来补救股票销售违规行为。此前发布的禁止令将被撤销。”
***判决书全文将于10月23日刊登在《北华捷报》上。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 17, 1935
11327

SUBMISSION TO JUDGMENT BY
MR. F. J. RAVEN

Strongly Denies Allegation of Any Attempt at
Fraud: Voluntary Petition in Bankruptcy

Acting upon the advice of his counsel, Mr. Frank J. Raven submitted to judgment in the U. S. Court for China yesterday, when he appeared in answer to three claims totalling Tls. 405,000 filed against him last July by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corp. and the American-Oriental Finance Corp., and trustee of the Asia Realty Co. Mr. R. T. Evans, who appeared on Mr. Raven's behalf, stated that his client would file almost immediately a petition for voluntary proceedings in bankruptcy.

A large crowd filled the court-room in the U. S. Consulate-General yesterday morning, and an extra number of chairs had to be put in to accommodate the interested spectators. In accordance with Federal Court procedure, a large American flag hung from a flag-pole near the Bench. Dr. George Sellett, who was counsel for the plaintiff and the defence, represented by Mr. R. T. Evans and Mr. Frank Raven, took their seats.

Upon Judge Milton J. Helmick's enquiring as to whether counsel had any objection to the three cases being tried at the same time, Dr. Sellett said that for the purpose of the morning's hearing, both he and Mr. Evans desired that all three cases be called together.

Allegation of Insolvency

Dealing briefly with the bills of complaint, he said that with regard to the bill of complaint filed by Mr. Hough as liquidator of the A.-O.B.C., it was alleged that in January, 1932, following a resolution of the board of directors, the bank paid to the defendant Tls. 135,000 as a honorarium, and this money was actually paid to him on January 19. It was alleged that the bank was insolvent at the time, although the plaintiff did not consider it necessary to prove this. In the case of the suit by the trustee of the Asia Realty Co., it was alleged that the same sum was paid on or about the same date, and for the same reason, although there was no suggestion that the company was insolvent. The Asia Realty, however did not owe Mr. Raven any money at the time. With regard to the A.-O.F.C., there was the same allegation as in the case of the A.-O.B.C.

An answer to the bill of complaint of the A.-O.F.C. only had been filed by the defence, setting out that the Tls. 135,000 had been voluntarily returned to them in the Spring of 1933! At the time the complaint was filed, this had not been known. They were now claiming interest, at the rate of 6 per cent. per annum, on this sum from January 19, 1932 to February 25, 1933.

"The defendant in this case denies that the bank and the finance corporation were insolvent, and denies any allegation of fraud," said Mr. Evans. "The plaintiff's counsel has announced that he proposes to offer no evidence in support of the allegation of insolvency. Notwithstanding this, I have come to the conclusion, after a careful examination of the law and the facts, that the burden of proof is on the defendant, even in the absence of fraud or insolvency, to justify the payment to him of the sums referred to in the complaint, and that in order to establish the correctness of such payments he must prove that the American-Oriental Bank and Asia Realty Co. were respectively indebted to him at the time of the passing of the resolution of January, 1932, and to establish such indebtedness he must prove a contract, express or implied to pay him compensation.

Mr. Evans' Advice

"Inasmuch as the bye-laws of the corporations concerned contain no provision for the remuneration of officers and directors, and as there was no express contract, and as the defendant cannot establish the existence of an implied contract in view of the death of the only independent persons who could now testify to such a contract, namely Messrs. Britton and Fleming, I have advised the defendant to submit to judgment, and he now does so submit.

"I accept full responsibility for this decision, to which I have come after the most painstaking investigation of which I have been capable, and my client in accepting judgment against himself is following my advice. In the case of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation there is a plea of payment and I understand that this is conceded.

"The fact that the amounts received by Mr. Raven in January, 1932, were paid to the Raven Trust Co. to bolster that company is, I am satisfied, irrelevant, and even if the companies concerned had desired to pay the money direct to the Raven Trust Co. it would have been beyond the power of the directors to authorize such a payment."

Allegation of Fraud

Dr. Sellett said that he wished it to be understood that the plaintiff did not waive the allegation of fraud. In the case of the A.-O.B.C., he would have been able to prove that, far from performing services as president without any form of salary, Mr. Raven had been receiving a regular and monthly wage since 1921. With respect to the other two companies, the same would also have been proved, although payments did not begin so far back. He also pointed out that most of the stock of the Raven Trust Co. was held either by the defendant or his family.

Stating that he did not want to enter into an argument, Mr. Evans said that his client wished it to be known that he did not receive any money from the Raven Trust Co., and the money put into it was for the benefit of creditors and preferred stock-holders. A dividend was declared not long afterwards, but Mr. Raven received no part of this.

It was admitted that the defendant had received money from the A.-O.B.C., and for some time from the Asia Realty Co. But Mr. Evans asserted that this was no evidence of fraud, and that his client would strongly fight the criminal charges against him.

His client further wished him to file voluntary proceedings in bankruptcy, and as soon as a date could be fixed by the court, he would do so.

Judge Helmick instructed Dr. Sellett to draw up a decree for the return and restitution of the money, to submit it to Mr. Evans for consideration, and then to bring it before him for signature.

Criminal proceedings against Mr. Raven, instituted by Mr. Feldman Watson, U.S. District Attorney, on charges of fraud will open in the U.S.

《字林西报》，1935年10月17日，星期四
11327

F. J. 雷文先生
服从判决

强烈否认任何欺诈企图指控：自愿申请破产

弗兰克·J. 雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生听从其法律顾问的建议，昨日在美国在华法院服从判决。他出庭回应去年七月由美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corp.）和美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corp.）清算人、以及亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Co.）受托人弗兰克·L. 霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生对他提出的三项总计规平银405,000两的索赔。代表雷文先生出庭的R. T. 埃文斯（R. T. Evans）先生表示，他的当事人将几乎立即提交自愿破产程序申请。

昨日上午，美国总领事馆的法庭内挤满了大量人群，不得不增加额外座位以容纳感兴趣的旁观者。按照联邦法院的程序，法官席附近的一根旗杆上悬挂着一面巨大的美国国旗。原告律师乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士，以及由被告律师R. T. 埃文斯先生和弗兰克·雷文先生代表的辩护方，各自入座。

当米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官询问律师是否反对同时审理这三起案件时，塞莱特博士表示，为了上午的听证目的，他和埃文斯先生都希望将这三起案件合并审理。

资不抵债的指控

在简要处理诉状时，他表示，关于霍夫先生作为美亚银行公司（A.-O.B.C.）清算人提交的诉状，指控称1932年1月，遵循董事会决议，银行向被告支付了规平银135,000两作为酬金，这笔钱实际上于1月19日支付给他。指控称当时银行已资不抵债，尽管原告认为无需证明这一点。在亚洲地产公司受托人提起的诉讼中，指控称在同一日期或大致同一日期，出于相同原因支付了相同金额，尽管没有暗示该公司资不抵债。然而，当时亚洲地产公司并不欠雷文先生任何钱。关于美亚金融公司（A.-O.F.C.），指控与美亚银行公司案相同。

辩护方仅针对美亚金融公司的诉状提交了答辩，指出这规平银135,000两已于1933年春季自愿退还给他们！在提交诉状时，此事尚不为人知。他们现在要求支付从1932年1月19日至1933年2月25日期间该款项的年息6%。

“本案被告否认银行和金融公司资不抵债，并否认任何欺诈指控，”埃文斯先生说。“原告律师已宣布，他打算不提供任何证据来支持资不抵债的指控。尽管如此，经过对法律和事实的仔细审查，我得出的结论是，即使没有欺诈或资不抵债的情况，举证责任仍在被告身上，以证明诉状中提到的支付给他的款项是正当的，并且为了确立此类支付的正确性，他必须证明在1932年1月决议通过时，美亚银行和亚洲地产公司分别对他负有债务，并且为了确立这种债务，他必须证明存在明示或默示的支付补偿合同。

埃文斯先生的建议

“鉴于相关公司的章程中没有关于官员和董事薪酬的规定，且没有明示合同，而且由于唯一能就此种合同作证的独立人士——即布里顿（Britton）和弗莱明（Fleming）先生——已经去世，被告无法确立默示合同的存在，我建议被告服从判决，他现在也照此办理。

“我对这一决定承担全部责任，这是在我所能做到的最艰苦的调查之后得出的，我的客户接受对自己不利的判决是听从了我的建议。在美亚金融公司一案中，有已付款的抗辩，我理解这是被承认的。

“我确信，雷文先生于1932年1月收到的款项被支付给雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Co.）以支撑该公司这一事实，是无关紧要的，即使相关公司希望直接将钱支付给雷文信托公司，这也超出了董事授权此类支付的权力范围。”

欺诈指控

塞莱特博士表示，他希望明确一点，原告并未放弃欺诈指控。在美亚银行公司案中，他本能够证明，雷文先生绝非像无薪总裁那样履行职责，而是自1921年以来一直领取固定的月薪。对于其他两家公司，情况也将得到同样证明，尽管付款开始的时间没那么早。他还指出，雷文信托公司的大部分股票由被告或其家人持有。

埃文斯先生表示他不想陷入争论，他说他的当事人希望让人知道，他没有从雷文信托公司收到任何钱，投入该公司的钱是为了债权人和优先股股东的利益。不久后宣布了股息，但雷文先生未从中获得任何部分。

据承认，被告从美亚银行公司收到了钱，并在一段时间内从亚洲地产公司收到了钱。但埃文斯先生断言，这并非欺诈的证据，他的当事人将坚决反驳针对他的刑事指控。

他的当事人还希望他提交自愿破产程序申请，一旦法院确定日期，他将立即这样做。

赫尔米克法官指示塞莱特博士起草一份退款和 restitution（归还/恢复原状）的法令，提交给埃文斯先生审议，然后呈交给他签署。

由美国地区检察官费尔德曼·沃森（Feldman Watson）先生以欺诈罪指控提起的针对雷文先生的刑事诉讼将在美国……

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, OCTOBER 13, 1935
Frank J. Raven To Appear
In U.S. Court Tuesday
Judge Helmick To Hear Three Civil Suits Filed By
Liquidator Of American-Oriental Bank For The
Recovery Of Tls. 405,000; Crowd Expected

The Courtroom of the United States Court for China is expected to accommodate an unusually large representation of the general public on Tuesday, when Judge Milton J. Helmick mounts the bench to try the first of several civil actions instituted against Mr. Frank J. Raven by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, the Raven Trust Company, and Trustee of the Asia Realty Company. The amounts involved total Tls. 405,-000.

With the arrival in Shanghai of Mr. Richard T. Evans, Mr. Raven's attorney, from Tientsin, the stage has finally been set for the trial of three actions in a series which are likely to be the most sensational in the history of the United States Court for China. Mr. Hough will be represented by Dr. George Sellett.

On October 29, when it is expected that the first civil suits against Mr. Raven will have been disposed of, Mr. Raven is to stand trial on 15 criminal charges of fraud and embezzlement.

In the proceedings which will open at 10 a.m. on Tuesday, Mr. Hough is seeking judgments against Mr. Raven for three sums of Tls. 135,000, voted and paid as honoraria to Mr. Raven in January, 1932, by the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Asia Realty Company.

Corporations Insolvent
It is the contention of Mr. Hough that these sums were voted to and received by Mr. Raven at a time when the three corporations were insolvent; that Mr. Raven knew that the corporations were insolvent; and that he wrongfully accepted the honoraria when no monies whatsoever were due to him for services rendered.

In the case of the Tls. 135,000 received by Mr. Raven from the Asia Realty Company, the Liquidator alleges that for a long period of time prior to January, 1932, Mr. Raven was paid a salary by the Company covering all services rendered and that during the whole of the year 1931 this salary amounted to $2,000 per month. It is not alleged, however, that Mr. Raven received any salary from either the American-Oriental Banking Corporation or the American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

One of the most serious blows ever sustained by American business in Shanghai was delivered when the four Raven corporations closed their doors on May 24 last. The American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company were placed in liquidation, while in the case of the Asia Realty Company Mr. Hough was appointed Trustee to effect a reorganization under the provisions of Section 77-B of the Federal Bankruptcy Act of the United States.

Statements issued from time to time by Mr. Hough, as Liquidator of the first three concerns, have revealed a state of affairs in which book assets have shrunk to amazingly small proportions, indicating tremendous losses to depositors, stockholders and other creditors.

Heavy Losses Indicated
As far as the depositors of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation are concerned, the losses are likely to be exceptionally heavy, notwithstanding a statement by Mr. Raven that there were sufficient assets held by the Bank to pay all depositors in full. This statement was made the day the Bank closed and was accompanied by the remark that Mr. Raven himself had "lost everything" in the crash. Subsequent statements by the Liquidator, however, showed Mr. Raven to be heavily indebted to the Bank for an overdraft and unpaid promissory notes. He was even more heavily indebted to the American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

In respect of all these sums, shown on the books as owing by Mr. Raven, the Liquidator has instituted suits in the United States Court for China. Hearings thereanent will take place after disposal of the criminal actions on October 29.

Mr. Alfred H. Driscoll and Mr. J. Warner Brown, President and Secretary-Treasurer, respectively, of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, are charged

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1935年10月13日
弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）将于周二出庭美国法院
赫尔米克法官将审理美亚银行清算人提起的三起民事诉讼，以追索规平银405,000两；预计旁听者众多

周二，当米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官升庭审理由美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）、雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的清算人兼亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）受托人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生对弗兰克·J·雷文先生提起的一系列民事诉讼中的第一案时，预计美国在华法院的法庭内将有异常众多的公众代表出席。涉案金额总计规平银405,000两。

随着雷文先生的律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）先生从天津抵达上海，这一系列诉讼中可能成为美国在华法院历史上最轰动的三起案件的审判舞台终于搭建完毕。霍夫先生将由乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士代理。

预计在10月29日，针对雷文先生的首批民事诉讼结案后，雷文先生将就15项欺诈和挪用公款的刑事指控受审。

在将于周二上午10点开始的诉讼程序中，霍夫先生寻求法院判决雷文先生支付三笔款项，每笔规平银135,000两。这些款项是美亚银行公司、美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司于1932年1月作为酬金投票决定并支付给雷文先生的。

各公司资不抵债
霍夫先生主张，这三家公司在资不抵债的情况下向雷文先生投票支付并由其收取了上述款项；雷文先生明知这些公司资不抵债；且在未提供任何应得报酬的服务的情况下，他不当接受了这些酬金。

关于雷文先生从亚洲地产公司收取的规平银135,000两一案，清算人指控称，在1932年1月之前的很长一段时间里，该公司一直向雷文先生支付薪水，以涵盖其提供的所有服务，且在1931年全年，该薪水的金额为每月2,000美元。然而，并未指控雷文先生从美亚银行公司或美亚金融公司领取任何薪水。

去年5月24日，四家雷文旗下公司关门停业，这对在上海的美商企业造成了有史以来最沉重的打击之一。美亚银行公司、美亚金融公司和雷文信托公司已进入清算程序，而在亚洲地产公司一案中，霍夫先生被任命为受托人，以便根据美国联邦破产法第77-B条的规定实施重组。

作为前三家机构的清算人，霍夫先生不时发布的声明揭示了一种局面：账面资产已缩减至惊人的微小比例，表明存款人、股东和其他债权人遭受了巨大损失。

显示巨额亏损
就美亚银行公司的存款人而言，尽管雷文先生曾声明银行持有足以全额支付所有存款人的资产，但损失可能会异常沉重。该声明是在银行关闭当天发表的，并附带表示雷文先生本人在此次崩盘中“失去了一切”。然而，清算人随后的声明显示，雷文先生因透支和未付本票而对银行负有巨额债务。他对美亚金融公司的债务甚至更为沉重。

针对账面上显示雷文先生欠付的所有这些款项，清算人已在美国在华法院提起诉讼。相关听证会将在10月29日刑事案件处理完毕后进行。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 12, 1935
Hearings In Action To Revoke
Asia Electric Charter Ended
Allman Asks Whittaker If He Instigated
U. S. Court Action Brought By Miss
Smith, Trade Act Registrar

After an entire day had been consumed in hearing evidence and lawyer's arguments, hearings in the action asking revocation of charter brought against the Asia Electric Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A. by Miss A. Viola Smith, registrar of the China Trade Act, were brought to a close before Judge Milton J. Helmick in the United States Courts for China yesterday afternoon.

Miss Smith, appearing as her own attorney, closed her arguments yesterday afternoon with the plea that the charter of the defendant concern be revoked, and that if the court did not see fit to grant this request, that a trustee be appointed and that he be bound to report to the court from time to time, the state of affairs that he found within the company. Miss Smith, who was admitted to practice in the American Courts here some time ago, and who was handling her first public case, made an excellent public appearance.

She based her claims on grounds that the company had issued shares, accepting promissory notes in payment, in violation of the provisions of the China Trade Act.

"Crusade" Reference Made

Mr. N. F. Allman, appearing for the defendant, argued that there had been no violation of the China Trade Act, inasmuch as the shares had not been issued, had been sold to employees and were being held in escrow pending receipt of full payment. In opening his argument in answer to Miss Smith's plea, he said something about the China Trade Act registrar being a trifle too hasty and just because a couple of banks had closed up was not sufficient reason for her to embark on a crusade.

Asia Electric had done nothing wrong, he pointed out, by issuing stock in escrow for promissory notes, and produced a number of briefs from similar proceedings elsewhere to prove his point. He further argued that the appointment of a trustee would damage the business to a considerable extent and further claimed that business had already been badly hurt by the filing of Miss Smith's action.

The testimony of Captain A. R. St. Louis, vice-president and manager of Asia Electric; Mr. Truman Johnson, president; Mr. J. A. Verner, salesman handling exports for the company, and Mr. E. G. Whittaker, secretary, who resigned recently, was taken during the afternoon. Miss Smith called Messrs. Verner and Whittaker as witnesses for the plaintiff.

Johnson Testifies

At the proceedings in the morning and early afternoon, testimony had been taken from Messrs. Johnson and St. Louis to the effect that Miss Smith's action had caused considerable financial loss to the company. Miss Smith, not exactly sure that her action has caused such losses as described, intimated that the sale of the factory premises last July had been responsible for some losses and called Mr. Verner to the stand. The latter said that it had caused him some loss of business but indicated that he desired to continue his contract with the company.

Mr. Whittaker, however, came in for some heavy cross-examination. He had resigned from the company, it was brought out, following the filing of Miss Smith's action, and the letter of resignation he sent the company mentioned that a reason for his leaving the board of directors was because he had not been informed of the sale of shares for promissory notes. The shares in question were produced in court and a few were found to contain Mr. E. G. Whittaker's signature. Questioned by Mr. Allman, the witness admitted that the signature was his, but declared that he didn't know that the stock was being sold for promissory notes. They had just been given him to sign, he pointed out, and were not in the share book.

Whittaker Questioned

Attorney Allman wanted to know if the witness had read the annual company reports distributed to all directors at the annual meetings, said reports, the attorney brought out, having contained mention of the shares sold for promissory notes. Mr. Whittaker didn't know whether he had read these reports or not. Maybe he had. One was shown to him. He admitted having seen it but said it was so long ago that he didn't have time to go through it all.

Mr. Allman then caused a bit of excited silence in the courtroom when he asked Mr. Whittaker whether or not Miss Smith's action was not instigated by him. The witness turned pink and denied that he had instigated the suit.

"Is it not a fact that you ran to Miss Smith and complained about the company?" the attorney wanted to know.

Mr. Whittaker's voice was hardly audible to the press or anyone else very far away from the witness stand. He said something in way of denial but reporters were not able to mark out his exact words.

Denies Wife's Influence

Mr. Allman wanted to know if Mrs. Whittaker had influenced him in complaining about the company. Mr. Whittaker said no.

Mr. Truman Johnson, president of the concern, gave but little testimony in the afternoon, merely stating under examination that heavy losses had been caused by Miss Smith's action and that the appointment of a trustee was not desirable by either directors or stockholders.

Miss Smith wanted to know if he had sounded out any of the stockholders on the question. Mr. Johnson said he hadn't, but reiterated that the question of a trustee had never come before the directors and the directors represented the majority of shareholders.

《字林西报》，1935年10月12日，星期六
撤销亚洲电力公司执照诉讼的听证会结束
奥尔曼询问惠特克是否煽动了由贸易法案注册官史密斯小姐提起的美国法院诉讼

在经过整整一天听取证据和律师辩论后，昨天下午，在美国在华法院，由中美贸易法案注册官A·维奥拉·史密斯（A. Viola Smith）小姐对美商联邦亚洲电力公司（Asia Electric Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A.）提起的要求撤销其公司章程的诉讼听证会，在米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官面前结束。

史密斯小姐亲自担任自己的律师，于昨天下午结束了她的辩论，请求撤销被告公司的章程；如果法院认为不宜批准此请求，则请求任命一名受托人，并约束其定期向法院报告他在公司内部发现的情况。史密斯小姐不久前获准在此地的美国法院执业，这是她处理的第一起公开案件，她的公开表现非常出色。

她的诉求依据是：该公司发行股票并接受本票作为支付，违反了《中美贸易法案》的规定。

提及“十字军运动”

代表被告出庭的N·F·奥尔曼（N. F. Allman）先生辩称，并未违反《中美贸易法案》，因为股票并未正式发行，而是出售给员工，并在收到全额付款前由第三方托管。在开场回应史密斯小姐的请求时，他表示，《中美贸易法案》注册官有些过于急躁，仅仅因为几家银行倒闭并不足以成为她发起一场“十字军运动”的理由。

他指出，亚洲电力公司将股票托管以换取本票的做法并无不当，并出示了多处类似诉讼的简报以证明其观点。他进一步辩称，任命受托人将在很大程度上损害业务，并声称史密斯小姐提起诉讼已经对业务造成了严重伤害。

下午听取了亚洲电力公司副总裁兼经理A·R·圣路易斯（A. R. St. Louis）上尉、总裁杜鲁门·约翰逊（Truman Johnson）先生、负责公司出口业务的销售员J·A·弗纳（J. A. Verner）先生以及最近辞职的秘书E·G·惠特克（E. G. Whittaker）先生的证词。史密斯小姐传唤弗纳先生和惠特克先生作为原告方证人。

约翰逊作证

在上午和下午早些时候的诉讼程序中，听取了约翰逊先生和圣路易斯先生的证词，大意是史密斯小姐的诉讼给公司造成了相当大的经济损失。史密斯小姐并不完全确定她的诉讼是否造成了所述那样的损失，她暗示去年七月工厂场地的出售造成了一些损失，并传唤弗纳先生出庭。后者表示这导致他的一些业务损失，但表明他希望继续履行与公司的合同。

然而，惠特克先生受到了严厉的交叉盘问。据披露，他在史密斯小姐提起诉讼后从公司辞职，他发给公司的辞职信中提到，他离开董事会的原因是他未获悉以本票出售股票一事。涉案股票在法庭上出示，其中几张被发现带有E·G·惠特克先生的签名。在奥尔曼先生的询问下，证人承认签名是他的，但声称他不知道股票是被用来换取本票的。他指出，这些股票只是拿给他签字，并未登记在股东名册中。

询问惠特克

奥尔曼律师想知道证人是否阅读了在年度会议上分发给所有董事的公司年度报告，律师指出，这些报告中提到了以本票出售的股票。惠特克先生不知道他是否阅读过这些报告。也许读过。有人向他展示了一份。他承认见过，但说那是很久以前的事了，他没有时间通读全文。

随后，当奥尔曼先生询问惠特克先生，史密斯小姐的诉讼是否由他煽动时，法庭内出现了一阵激动的沉默。证人脸色变红，否认他煽动了这起诉讼。

“事实难道不是你跑到史密斯小姐那里投诉公司吗？”律师问道。

惠特克先生的声音对于记者或离证人席较远的任何人来说几乎听不见。他说了一些否认的话，但记者们无法辨认出他的确切措辞。

否认妻子的影响

奥尔曼先生想知道惠特克夫人是否影响了他对公司的投诉。惠特克先生说没有。

该公司总裁杜鲁门·约翰逊先生在下午提供的证词很少，仅在受询时表示，史密斯小姐的诉讼造成了重大损失，且董事和股东都不希望任命受托人。

史密斯小姐想知道他是否就此问题试探过任何股东的意见。约翰逊先生说他没有，但重申受托人问题从未提交董事会讨论，而董事代表了大多数股东。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D REGISTRY
S. B. D.
THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1935

Hough Burns
2 Million In
A. O. Currency

Armed Guard On Hand
As $1, $5, $10 Bills
Go Up In Smoke

BLAZE POPS OFF
BOILER VALVE

"Made An Excellent
"Fire," Liquidator
Declares

Two million dollars worth of banknotes went up in smoke yesterday afternoon and they were not old, worn-out notes at that. In the hands of the wrong people, they would have been worth a considerable pile of money. They were the notes issued by the American-Oriental Bank, and many of them were nice, new and crinkly and had never been used.

Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the bank and other defunct Raven concerns, has nursed the idea of staging a big bonfire for several days and about 3 o'clock yesterday afternoon, put the idea into effect. The banknotes, all nicely bundled in packages of $1,000 each and in denominations of $1, $5, and $10 bills, were loaded into a truck owned by the R.C.A.-Victor Company, which Mr. Hough heads here in China, and proceeded under armed guard to the R.C.A. plant in Yangtsepoo.

Armed Guard On Hand

The armed guard was supplied by the Shanghai Municipal Police and according to Mr. Hough it was quite necessary to have it along. Frankly, he stated, he didn't like the idea of having the truck fall victim to a gang of armed robbers. The banknotes, despite their worthlessness inside the vaults of the bank, might have a definite value to the man on the streets provided he could get his hands on them. They could be presented as claims, claims that might have to be recognised.

The incinerator used was one of the factory boilers, and according to Mr. Hough, it was some fire. A good coal blaze was started and the bundles of banknotes were then shovelled into the fire-box. In fact, the boilers got so hot that steam pressure was forced up and blew off a safety valve. The exact amount of thermal units obtained from the two million dollars worth of banknotes was not recorded but it got so hot around the premises that windows had to be opened in the boiler room. Mr. Hough's comment concerning the fire was terse and directly to the point.

"The banknotes of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation made an excellent fire," he said.

Two Hours Required

The blaze was conducted in the presence of Mr. Hough, Mr. Henry DeVault, the auditor for the liquidation, and the armed guard of the Shanghai Municipal Police. The entire process required about two hours.

With the business of signing checks for depositors with accounts under $50 local currency or the equivalent in foreign currency, still the most important task on the liquidation schedule at present, the business of moving the offices of the liquidator from the American-Oriental Bank premises to the Dollar Building on Canton Road has been delayed several days. It is possible that the business of moving may be completed early next week.

Mr. Hough is still busily engaged in signing checks and the staff has not yet completed making them all out. More than 3,000 are to be mailed out, and are leaving the bank in small lots as fast as they are completed and the envelopes addressed. One batch is being mailed today, which another will find its way to the Post Office on Saturday.

《字林西报》，1935年10月4日，星期五

霍夫·伯恩斯（Hough Burns）
两百万
美亚银行货币

武装警卫在场
随着1美元、5美元、10美元纸币
付之一炬

锅炉阀门
因大火爆裂

清算人宣称
“烧了一场好火”

昨天下午，价值两百万美元的钞票化为灰烬，而且这些并非陈旧破损的废钞。若落入不法之徒手中，它们将是一笔巨款。这些是美亚银行（American-Oriental Bank）发行的钞票，其中许多崭新挺括，从未流通使用。

该银行及其他已倒闭的雷文（Raven）相关企业的清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生筹划举行一场大型篝火焚烧活动已有数日，并于昨天下午3时许付诸实施。这些钞票均被整齐捆扎，每包面值1,000美元，面额包括1美元、5美元和10美元纸币，装入由霍夫先生在中国担任负责人的美国无线电公司-胜利者留声机公司（R.C.A.-Victor Company）所属的一辆卡车中，并在武装护卫下前往杨树浦的无线电公司工厂。

武装警卫在场

武装警卫由上海公共租界工部局警务处提供，据霍夫先生称，此举十分必要。他坦率地表示，他不希望这辆卡车成为武装劫匪团伙的猎物。尽管这些钞票在银行金库内已毫无价值，但若有人能将其弄到手，对街头之人而言或许仍有确切价值。它们可被用作索赔凭证，而这些索赔可能不得不被承认。

所使用的焚化炉是工厂的一台锅炉，据霍夫先生称，火势相当猛烈。先点燃优质的燃煤大火，随后将成捆的钞票铲入炉膛。事实上，锅炉变得如此炽热，以致蒸汽压力骤升，冲开了一个安全阀。从这两百万美元钞票中获得的热能单位确切数值并未记录，但现场周围温度极高，锅炉房的窗户不得不打开。霍夫先生对此番火势的评论简洁而切中要害。

他说：“美亚银行公司的钞票烧了一场好火。”

耗时两小时

焚烧过程在霍夫先生、负责清算审计的亨利·德沃尔特（Henry DeVault）先生以及上海公共租界工部局警务处武装警卫的见证下进行。整个过程耗时约两小时。

目前，清算工作中最重要的任务仍是向账户余额低于50元本地货币或等值外币的储户签发支票，因此，将清算人办公室从美亚银行旧址迁至广东路美元大楼（Dollar Building）的工作已推迟数日。搬迁工作有可能在下周初完成。

霍夫先生仍忙于签发支票，职员们尚未全部开具完毕。需寄出的支票超过3,000张，随着填写完成及信封地址书写完毕，正分批迅速从银行发出。今日寄出一批，另一批将于周六送达邮局。

归档
JWS

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1935
（印：S. D. R. CISTRY No. S. B. D.）

Case Against Asia Electric Company Postponed Again
China Trade Act Registrar Appears In U.S. Court Unprepared To Prove Charges Of Irregularity In Stock Issues; Asks For Continuance

Lack of preparedness of Miss A. Viola Smith, Registrar of the China Trade Act, led yesterday to a postponement of the proceedings instituted in the United States Court for China against the Asia Electric Company, in which the appointment of a trustee for the Company is sought as a preliminary step to the revocation of the Company's charter for alleged infringement of the China Trade Act.

Miss Smith having stated that she was not ready to go into the merits of the case, Judge Milton J. Helmick intimated that he was not prepared to order the appointment of a trustee for the Company unless there were proof of the allegations embodied in the complaint.

The Registrar's complaint against the Company is to the effect that it issued 41,400 shares of stock to Mr. Truman Johnson, President of the Company, to Mr. Johnson's wife, and to several other persons, against promissory notes which have not been paid; that these shares were voted at meetings of the Company, although they had not been paid for; and that dividends were paid upon these shares.

Company Not Prejudiced
When the Court went into session before Judge Milton J. Helmick yesterday morning, N. F. Allman, who appeared for the Asia Electric Company, announced that his clients had filed an answer to the complaint of the Registrar only because they submitted that the filing of this answer did not prejudice the Company's right to file any petitions it might deem necessary.

Miss Smith said that the hearing was called to provide the defendant company an opportunity to show cause why a trustee should not be appointed, and the proceedings should be confined to that aspect of the matter without going into the merits of the case.

Mr. Allman then intimated that he wished to make a demurrer to the complaint on the ground of legal insufficiency. Of the $41,400 worth of shares involved in the case, $20,000 worth had already been paid for, he said, thus leaving an unpaid balance on the promissory notes of approximately $21,400.

Continuing, counsel declared that the China Trade Act provided, in case of shares not sold for cash, only for suits by creditors for the unpaid balance. The United States was clearly not a creditor here, and the complaint was, therefore, bad in substance.

Overruling the demurrer, Judge Helmick said it would be to the best interest of all concerned to have the facts of the case aired.

Miss Smith Not Ready
Miss Smith: I am not ready to go into the merits of the case. I was under the impression that this hearing was merely to enable the defendant company to "show cause." I would, therefore, ask for a postponement for three days.

Mr. Allman: We are prepared to go ahead, but if a postponement is granted, we want a full 20 days, from the date service of the complaint was obtained, in which to file our full answer. The complaint was filed on September 23. We should therefore, be given until October 13.

Judge Helmick (to Miss Smith): Assuming your application for the appointment of a trustee is separated from other parts of the complaint, you should have been prepared to give evidence this morning on the facts alleged. I don't know what on earth you expected to accomplish this morning. Have you no proof whatever to offer in support of your allegations?

Miss Smith repeated that she was not ready to go into the merits of the case, to which Mr. Allman retorted that he either wanted the complaint dismissed or else to be allowed a full 20 days in which to reply, as provided by law.

Denies Any Offence
Counsel said he had ample legal authorities to show that it was no offence under the China Trade Act or any other law to issue shares on the instalment plan, especially where such shares were issued to employees. Almost every corporation follows this practice, Mr. Allman asserted.

Continuing, counsel declared that even if it were held to be irregular to issue shares for other than a cash consideration, the complaint in this case must fail, because the shares had not been actually issued. They were being held by the Company in escrow against full payment.

Judge Helmick asked Mr. Allman if he could have his full reply to the complaint filed by October 10, so that hearing might take place on October 13. Mr. Allman undertook to do this, and the case was ordered continued to October 13.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年10月3日，星期四
（印：S. D. R. CISTRY No. S. B. D.）

起诉亚细亚电力公司案再次延期
《对华贸易法》注册官出庭美国法院，未准备好证明股票发行违规指控；请求延期

由于《对华贸易法》注册官A·维奥拉·史密斯（A. Viola Smith）小姐准备不足，导致昨天在美国驻华法院对亚细亚电力公司（Asia Electric Company）提起的诉讼程序延期。在该案中，原告寻求任命一名公司受托人，作为以涉嫌违反《对华贸易法》为由撤销该公司章程的初步步骤。

鉴于史密斯小姐表示她尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行审理，米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官暗示，除非有证据证明诉状中所载的指控属实，否则他不愿下令任命公司受托人。

注册官对公司的诉状大意如下：公司向该公司总裁杜鲁门·约翰逊（Truman Johnson）先生、约翰逊先生的妻子以及其他几人发行了41,400股股票，以此换取尚未支付的期票；尽管这些股份尚未付款，却在公司会议上参与了投票；并且基于这些股份支付了股息。

公司未受损害
昨天上午，法庭在米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官主持下开庭时，代表亚细亚电力公司出庭的N·F·奥尔曼（N. F. Allman）宣布，其当事人提交对注册官诉状的答辩，仅是因为他们认为提交此答辩并不损害公司提交其认为必要的任何请愿书的权利。

史密斯小姐称，召开听证会是为了给被告公司提供机会，说明为何不应任命受托人，且诉讼程序应局限于该方面，而不深入案件实质问题。

随后，奥尔曼先生暗示，他希望以法律依据不足为由对诉状提出抗辩。他表示，本案涉及的41,400美元股票中，价值20,000美元的部分已经付清，因此期票上未付余额约为21,400美元。

律师继续陈述道，《对华贸易法》规定，对于非现金出售的股份，仅允许债权人就未付余额提起诉讼。在此情况下，美国显然并非债权人，因此该诉状在实质上是不成立的。

赫尔米克法官驳回了该项抗辩，并表示，让本案事实得到公开审查符合所有相关方的最大利益。

史密斯小姐未准备好
史密斯小姐：我尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行审理。我原以为此次听证会仅是为了让被告公司“说明理由”。因此，我请求延期三天。

奥尔曼先生：我们已准备好继续进行，但如果批准延期，我们希望自收到诉状送达之日起，拥有完整的20天时间来提交我们的完整答辩。诉状于9月23日提交。因此，我们应该获准延至10月13日。

赫尔米克法官（对史密斯小姐说）：假设你关于任命受托人的申请与诉状的其他部分分开处理，你本应准备好在今天上午就所指控的事实提供证据。我真不知道你今天上午究竟指望达成什么目的。难道你没有任何证据来支持你的指控吗？

史密斯小姐重申她尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行审理，对此奥尔曼先生反驳称，他要么要求驳回诉状，要么要求按照法律规定给予完整的20天时间进行答复。

否认任何违法行为
律师表示，他有充分的法律依据表明，根据《对华贸易法》或任何其他法律，分期付款发行股份并不构成违法，尤其是当这些股份发行给员工时。奥尔曼先生断言，几乎每家公司都遵循这一做法。

律师继续陈述道，即使认定非现金对价发行股份属于违规行为，本案的诉状也必须败诉，因为这些股份实际上并未发行。它们由公司代为保管（escrow），以待全额付款。

赫尔米克法官询问奥尔曼先生是否能在10月10日前提交对诉状的完整答复，以便在10月13日举行听证会。奥尔曼先生承诺做到这一点，案件遂被命令延期至10月13日。

中国贸易法注册官出庭美国法院
未准备好证明股票发行违规指控；请求延期审理

中国贸易法注册官 A. Viola Smith 女士准备不足，导致昨日在美国驻华法院对亚细亚电力公司（Asia Electric Company）提起的诉讼程序延期。在该案中，原告寻求为公司任命一名受托人，作为以涉嫌违反《中国贸易法》为由撤销该公司章程的初步步骤。

Smith 女士表示她尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行辩论，Milton J. Helmick 法官暗示，除非有证据证明诉状中所载的指控属实，否则他不愿下令为公司任命受托人。

注册官对公司的诉状大意称：公司向该公司总裁 Truman Johnson 先生、Johnson 先生的妻子以及其他几人发行了 41,400 股股票，以此换取尚未兑付的本票；这些股票在未付款的情况下仍在公司会议上参与了投票；并且基于这些股票支付了股息。

公司未受损害

昨日上午，法庭在 Milton J. Helmick 法官主持下开庭时，代表亚细亚电力公司的 N. F. Allman 先生宣布，其当事人之所以提交对注册官诉状的答辩，仅是因为他们认为提交此答辩并不损害公司提交其认为必要的任何请愿书的权利。

Smith 女士称，此次听证会的目的是给予被告公司一个机会，以说明为何不应任命受托人，且诉讼程序应仅限于该方面，而不深入案件的实质问题。

Allman 先生随后暗示，他希望以法律依据不足为由对诉状提出抗辩（demurrer）。他说，本案涉及的价值 41,400 美元的股票中，价值 20,000 美元的部分已经付清，因此本票上未付余额约为 21,400 美元。

律师继续陈述称，《中国贸易法》规定，对于非现金出售的股份，仅允许债权人就未付余额提起诉讼。在此案中，美国显然不是债权人，因此该诉状在实质上是站不住脚的。

Helmick 法官驳回了该抗辩，并表示，将案件事实公之于众符合所有相关方的最大利益。

Smith 女士未做好准备

Smith 女士：我尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行辩论。我原以为此次听证会仅仅是为了让被告公司“说明理由”。因此，我请求延期三天。

Allman 先生：我们已准备好继续进行，但如果批准延期，我们希望从送达诉状之日起获得完整的 20 天时间，以便提交我们的完整答辩。诉状于 9 月 23 日提交。因此，应给予我们直到 10 月 13 日的时间。

Helmick 法官（对 Smith 女士说）：假设你关于任命受托人的申请与诉状的其他部分分开处理，你本应准备好在今天上午就所指控的事实提供证据。我不知道你到底期望今天上午达成什么目的。你没有任何证据来支持你的指控吗？

Smith 女士重申她尚未准备好就案件实质问题进行辩论，Allman 先生对此反驳称，他要么要求驳回诉状，要么要求按照法律规定给予完整的 20 天时间进行答复。

否认任何违法行为

律师表示，他有充足的法律依据表明，分期发行股票并不违反《中国贸易法》或任何其他法律，特别是当这些股票是发给员工时。Allman 先生断言，几乎每家公司都遵循这一做法。

律师继续陈述称，即使认定非现金对价发行股票属于违规行为，本案的诉状也必须败诉，因为这些股票实际上并未发行。它们正由公司托管，以待全额付款。

Helmick 法官询问 Allman 先生是否能在 10 月 10 日前提交对诉状的完整答复，以便在 10 月 13 日举行听证会。Allman 先生承诺这样做，案件被命令延期至 10 月 13 日。

（批：归档 / 手稿）

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

BANKRUPTCY LAW TO BE ENFORCED FROM OCTOBER 1.

The Bankruptcy Law promulgated by the National
Government will be put in force as from October 1.

There is a separate law of six Articles

Lib Pao of September 28 :-

THE KOO TSO HSIEN CASE : THE INTERESTING EVIDENCE OF A WITNESS

Koo Tso Hsien sat wiping the sweat off his brow
with his handkerchief while he listened attentively to the
evidence given by the witnesses.
Chang Ting Kwei (张廷桂) gave the following
evidence :- "On June 13, 1933 Wong King Kwei (王金奎) took
me to the Yachow Hotel. Koo Sz (Koo Tso Hsien) was in a
room. He handed out two pistols and said that he would pay
us each $10,000 as remuneration after the deed had been done.
Later I received $50. After my arrest I wished to reveal
all. King Kiu Ling (an Inspector of the French Police),
who is a relative of Koo Sz, sent one Zee Yu Ming (钱裕民)
to stop us from speaking and threatened that if we spoke we
would be tortured with electricity. Later, when I was being
held in the Detention House, I heard that Koo Sz was making
certain arrangements and that there was some hope for an
appeal. For this reason, I did not speak. I do not know
whether or not Wong Hsing Keo (王兴高) is connected with the
case."

Shuh Pao :-

THE REORGANIZATION OF THE CHINA REALTY COMPANY.

The application for reorganization made by the
China Realty Company, one of the companies of the Raven group,
to the U.S. Court for China is intended for the better
protection of its shareholders.
Four or five years ago, the shares of the
China Realty Company were quoted at double their par value.
A large number of these shares is held by Chinese and it is
to be feared that the holders of shares bought when their
value was very high will sustain a loss after the reorganization
of the company.
Furthermore, many Chinese who desired to register
their property with the U.S. Consulate had made use of the name
of the China Realty Company for this purpose. Will they be
able to regain possession of their property after the
reorganization?

9月28日《立报》：

顾佐贤案：证人有趣的证词

顾佐贤一边用手帕擦拭额头的汗水，一边专心聆听证人提供的证词。

张廷桂提供了以下证词：“1933年6月13日，王金奎带我到雅州酒店。顾氏（顾佐贤）在一个房间里。他拿出两把手枪，并说事成之后会付给我们每人 10,000 美元作为报酬。后来我收到了 50 美元。被捕后，我想揭露一切。顾氏的亲戚、法租界巡捕房的一名督察金乔林（King Kiu Ling，音译）派了一个叫钱裕民（Zee Yu Ming，音译）的人来阻止我们说话，并威胁说如果我们开口就会遭受电刑。后来，当我被关押在拘留所时，我听说顾氏正在做某些安排，上诉有一些希望。因此，我没有说话。我不知道王兴高是否与本案有关。”

《舒报》：

华业地产公司的重组。

雷文集团（Raven group）旗下公司之一的华业地产公司（China Realty Company）向美国驻华法院提出的重组申请，旨在更好地保护其股东。

四五年前，华业地产公司的股票报价为其面值的双倍。大量此类股票由中国人持有，令人担忧的是，那些在股价很高时买入股票的持有人将在公司重组后遭受损失。

此外，许多希望在美国领事馆登记其财产的中国人曾利用华业地产公司的名义为此目的。他们在公司重组后能否重新收回其财产？

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1935
6743
50 7 26
Hough Ready
To Mail Out
Bank Checks
Liquidator Says He Is
Fast Developing
Writer's Cramp
3,200 PEOPLE TO
BE PAID TOMORROW
Offices Will Be Moved
To Suite In Dollar
Building
With only another day to go before mailing starts, every available man and woman in the employ of Mr. Frank Hough, liquidator of the American-Oriental Bank has been busy the past two days making out checks that will be paid to depositors of the institution with under $50 local currency, or the equivalent in foreign currency, on deposit.
Mr. Hough told a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday that he was developing writer's cramp from signing so many checks, but calculated that his wrist would probably hold out long enough to get the job completed. There are more than 3,200 accounts of less than $50 on the books and checks are being made out for most of them.
It is estimated that about one-fourth of the accounts are very small, amounting to a matter of only a few dollars each. A number are the accounts of people who have left town, forgetting all about the few dollars they had left in the American-Oriental Bank. The amount of money to be disbursed will be approximately $42,000, or an average of about $13 per depositor.
These depositors are being paid off in full in accordance with an order issued four days ago by Judge Milton J. Helmick, of the United States Court for China, after receipt of a petition from Mr. Hough asking that he be permitted to pay off the small accounts.
In his petition, the liquidator stated that full payment to the small depositors would immediately do away with a great deal of book work, the cost of which would be about as much as the cost of making the payments. He added that it also would greatly speed up the work of liquidation.
Commencing Monday, the liquidator will start moving his offices to the Dollar Building, Canton Road, where a suite of four offices has been engaged.

《大美晚报》，1935年9月29日，星期日
6743
50 7 26
霍夫准备
寄出银行支票
清算人称他很快
患上了书写痉挛
3,200人将于
明日获付款
办公室将迁至
美元大楼的一套房间
在美亚银行（American-Oriental Bank）清算人 Frank Hough 先生手下工作的所有男女职员，在过去两天里一直忙于开具支票，这些支票将支付给在该机构存款不足 50 元当地货币或等值外币的储户。距离开始邮寄只剩下一天时间。

Hough 先生昨天告诉《大美晚报》记者，由于签署太多支票，他患上了书写痉挛，但他估计他的手腕大概能坚持足够长的时间以完成这项工作。账面上有超过 3,200 个低于 50 美元的账户，大部分账户正在开具支票。

据估计，约四分之一的账户金额非常小，每笔仅几美元。其中一些账户属于那些离开上海的人，他们完全忘记了在美亚银行留下的几美元。待支付的金额约为 42,000 美元，平均每位储户约 13 美元。

根据美国驻华法院 Milton J. Helmick 法官四天前发布的命令，这些储户将获得全额偿付。该命令是在收到 Hough 先生请求允许其清偿小额账户的请愿书后发出的。

在其请愿书中，清算人指出，全额支付小额储户将立即消除大量的簿记工作，其成本几乎与支付款项的成本相当。他补充说，这也将大大加快清算工作的进度。

从星期一开始，清算人将开始将其办公室迁至广东路美元大楼（Dollar Building），那里已租用了一套四间的办公室。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 26. 1935

Judge Helmick Orders
Full Payment Of Small
A.-O. Bank Depositors

Decision Handed Down Yesterday On Petition By
Liquidator Of Defunct Raven Bank Expected
To Reduce Expense Of Liquidation

APPROXIMATE TOTAL OF $42,000, CHINESE
CURRENCY, TO BE PAID OUT IMMEDIATELY

Good news for small depositors in the defunct
American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the first since the
bank went into liquidation on May 24 of this year, is made
possible of announcement by a decision of Judge Milton J.
Helmick, of the U.S. Court for China, authorizing Mr. Frank
L. Hough, the Liquidator, to pay in full all checking, savings
and fixed deposit accounts with the bank which, with
accrued interest thereon, are not in excess of the following
sums:

Shanghai Dollars . . . . . 50
Tientsin Dollars . . . . . 50
U. S. Dollars . . . . . . 20
Yen . . . . . . . . . . . 60
Pounds . . . . . . . . . . 4

Hongkong Dollars . . . . 40
Francs . . . . . . . . . 300

A petition, seeking authority to
make such payments, was submit-
ted by Mr. Hough to the Judge
yesterday afternoon and immedi-
ately granted by the latter.
In this petition, Mr. Hough
stated that the total number of
checking, savings and fixed de-
posit accounts in all currencies
appearing upon the records of the
bank, in the Shanghai and Tientsin
branches, is approximately 8,226
accounts totalling $6,728,559.19. It
is further stated that the number
of such accounts which do not
exceed the amounts specified above
is approximately 3,273, and that
to pay these 3,273 accounts in full
the Liquidator will be required to
disburse approximately $42,000,
Chinese currency.
$625,000 In Hand
Of the monies already collected
for the bank, Mr. Hough's petition
continues, there is now a cash
balance of approximately $625,000,
Shanghai currency, and the
Liquidator believes that before the
liquidation is completed a consider-
ably larger sum will be available
for distribution to the depositors
and creditors of the bank.
The petition then goes on to
state that the work and expense
of liquidation would be consider-
ably reduced if the aforesaid 3,273
accounts are immediately paid in
full; that the cost of such payment
in full is relatively small as com-
pared with the total amount which
will be available for payment to
depositors and creditors of the
bank; and that, although other
depositors and creditors of the
bank do not receive payment in
full, the saving in the expense of
liquidation will, in the opinion of
the Liquidator, approximately off-
set the excess paid to the 3,273
depositors if those depositors are
paid in full.
Finally, the Liquidator asked
that interest on the 3,273 accounts
shall not be paid beyond the date
to which interest has already been
accrued upon the books and records
of the bank, with the proviso that
no depositors who are indebted to
the bank be paid until they have
liquidated their indebtedness to
the bank.
Judge Helmick's order grants
the Liquidator's petition, with the
provisos as stated, and it is ex-
pected that payment of the small
depositors will commence immedi-
ately.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年9月26日，星期四

赫尔米克法官命令
全额支付美亚银行
小额储户存款

昨日就已倒闭的美亚信托公司（Raven Bank）清算人提出的请愿书作出裁决，预计将降低清算费用

立即支付总额约42,000元中国货币

对于已倒闭的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）的小额储户来说，这是一个好消息。这是自今年5月24日该银行进入清算程序以来的第一个好消息。美国在华法院法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）作出裁决，授权清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生全额支付该银行的所有支票账户、储蓄账户和定期存款账户，只要这些账户连同应计利息不超过以下金额：

上海银元 . . . . . 50
天津银元 . . . . . 50
美元 . . . . . . 20
日元 . . . . . . . . . . . 60
英镑 . . . . . . . . . . 4

港元 . . . . . 40
法郎 . . . . . . . . . 300

霍夫先生于昨日下午向法官提交了一份寻求授权进行此类支付的请愿书，并立即获得批准。
在这份请愿书中，霍夫先生指出，根据银行记录，上海和天津分行所有币种的支票账户、储蓄账户和定期存款账户总数约为8,226个，总金额为6,728,559.19美元。请愿书还指出，不超过上述指定金额的此类账户数量约为3,273个，要全额支付这3,273个账户，清算人需支出约42,000元中国货币。
手头有625,000美元
霍夫先生的请愿书接着指出，在已为银行收回的资金中，目前现金余额约为625,000上海银元，清算人相信，在清算完成之前，将有相当大的一笔资金可用于分配给银行的储户和债权人。
请愿书随后指出，如果立即全额支付上述3,273个账户，清算工作和费用将大大减少；与可用于支付给银行储户和债权人的总金额相比，这种全额支付的成本相对较小；而且，虽然银行的其他储户和债权人无法获得全额支付，但清算人认为，节省下来的清算费用大致可以抵消如果向这3,273名储户全额支付而多付的金额。
最后，清算人请求，这3,273个账户的利息只支付到银行账簿和记录中已累积利息的日期为止，并规定任何欠银行债务的储户在清偿其对银行的债务之前不得获得支付。
赫尔米克法官的命令批准了清算人的请愿书，并附有上述规定，预计对小额储户的支付将立即开始。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 20, 1935

Judge Helmick
Delays Chase
Bank Case

Kwei Chow Action May
Be Settled Out
Of Court

Action of Mr. Kuei Chow against
the Chase Bank and Mr. Frank L.
Hough, liquidator of the American-
Oriental Finance Company, for the
recovery of securities worth appro-
ximately $20,000, will in all prob-
ability be settled out of court, it
was learned yesterday.

The action was scheduled to have
been brought before Judge Milton
J. Helmick in the United States
Court for China yesterday morning
but the matter was held over until
next Wednesday pending an ad-
justment between the parties con-
cerned.

Mr. Kuei Chow, in his bill of
complaint, stated that he was a cus-
tomer of the American-Oriental
Finance Company, operating through
them on the New York cotton and
London rubber markets. He de-
clares that on September 13, 1934,
he placed 2,970 shares of Lanchow
Mining Stock, worth approximately
$20,000, with the A.O.F.C. as col-
lateral.

He further maintains that the
stocks are his sole property and that
his account with the A.O.F.C. has
been paid in full. He also stated
that the stocks had never been
pledged with the A.O.F.C.

The American-Oriental Finance
Company, it developed, had pledged
the stock with the Chase Bank as
collateral for a loan of U.S.$16,000,
the complaint stated. Mr. Kuei
Chow is suing for the return of the
stock as well as a temporary in-
junction preventing the Chase Bank
from disposing of it in order to
satisfy their loan.

Mr. Kuei Chow states that he first
learned that his stock had been
hypothecated when he called on Mr.
Hough in July. The liquidator told
him that former officials of the
company had pledged it, adding
that the Chase Bank could sell the
stock at any time it wished to do
so. Mr. Kuei Chow stated that Mr.
A. E. Schumacher, manager of the
Chase Bank, told him the same
thing, hence his bringing the matter
into court.

It is understood that an adjust-
ment outside of court is now pos-
sible, the Chase Bank having sold
other securities which had been
pledged to it to cover the loan, and
the stock owned by Mr. Kuei Chow
is not required. In that event, the
stocks will in all probability be
handed over to Mr. Hough for return
to Mr. Kuei Chow.

《字林西报》，1935年9月20日，星期五

赫尔米克法官
推迟大通银行
案件

桂洲（Kwei Chow）的行动可能
庭外和解

据悉，桂洲先生起诉大通银行及美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Company）清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫先生，要求追回价值约20,000美元的证券一案，极有可能通过庭外方式解决。

该案原定于昨天上午在美国在华法院由米尔顿·J·赫尔米克法官审理，但因等待有关各方进行调整，此事被推迟至下周三。

桂洲先生在诉状中称，他是美亚金融公司的客户，通过该公司在纽约棉花市场和伦敦橡胶市场进行交易。他声称，1934年9月13日，他将价值约20,000美元的2,970股兰州矿业股票（Lanchow Mining Stock）作为抵押品交给美亚金融公司。

他进一步坚持认为，这些股票是他的唯一财产，他在美亚金融公司的账户已全额付清。他还表示，这些股票从未向美亚金融公司质押过。

诉状指出，事实证明，美亚金融公司已将这些股票质押给大通银行，作为16,000美元贷款的抵押品。桂洲先生正在起诉要求归还股票，并申请临时禁令，阻止大通银行为偿还贷款而处置这些股票。

桂洲先生表示，他是在7月拜访霍夫先生时首次得知自己的股票已被抵押。清算人告诉他，公司前官员已将股票质押，并补充说大通银行可以随时出售这些股票。桂洲先生表示，大通银行经理A. E. 舒马赫（A. E. Schumacher）先生也对他说了同样的话，因此他将此事诉诸法庭。

据了解，现在有可能达成庭外和解，因为大通银行已出售其他质押给它的证券以覆盖贷款，因此不需要桂洲先生拥有的股票。在这种情况下，这些股票很可能会移交给霍夫先生，以便退还给桂洲先生。

September 19, 1935. Morning Translation.

Shanghai Morning Post and other local newspapers:

THE CLOSING OF THE AMERICAN-ORIENTAL BANKING CORPORATION

Chinese depositors have sustained heavy losses through the failure of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company. According to an investigation, Chinese deposits in the bank total $2,300,000.

In order to protect the interests of Chinese creditors in these three concerns, the Ministry of Finance of the National Government has appointed lawyer Huang Tsoong Shiung (黃宗勳) to participate, on behalf of Chinese depositors, in the liquidation of the three concerns.

It is learned that the Chinese creditors of the three concerns will hold a meeting in a few days.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

CLOSING OF A PAWNSHOP

On September 18, the Yui Shing Pawnshop (裕興當), Carter Road, went into liquidation.

The pawnshop had a capital of $30,000, but owing to trade depression, the whole amount has been lost. Ling Zung Tse (林慎之) is the Manager of the shop.

Lawyer Chen Ping Sin (陳炳生), acting on behalf of the pawnshop, has issued the following notice:-

"Owing to trade depression, this pawnshop has suspended business. Creditors are hereby notified to call at my office within 14 days bringing proofs of their claims. Debtors should settle their accounts in the same period.

"Pawned articles, the period of redemption of which has not yet expired, must be redeemed at short notice".

Shanghai Morning Post and other local newspapers:

THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE SEPTEMBER 18 INCIDENT

Yesterday was the anniversary of the September 18 Incident.

The local Tangpu held a brief ceremony at 9 a.m. yesterday in observance of the anniversary.

Local Chinese broadcasting stations suspended operations the whole day. Chinese official organizations, public bodies, schools and factories carried on as usual. The national flag was hoisted at half-mast.

JAPANESE MARINES TO HOLD MANOEUVRES THIS MORNING

From 2 a.m. to-day, the Japanese Landing Force will hold manoeuvres at Yangtszepoo and vicinity. The practice will end at daybreak.

THE CHINA PRESS. SUNDAY. SEPTEMBER 15. 1935

Liquidators Of
Raven Interests
Plan To Move

Will Shift Offices To
3rd Floor Of Dollar
Building

OFFERS MADE FOR
BANK PROPERTY

Auditor Is Completing
Asia Realty, Raven
Trust Reports

Cost of liquidating the American-Oriental Bank, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company, the three defunct concerns of the House of Raven, will be considerably reduced commencing the first of October when the offices of Mr. Frank L. Hough, the liquidator are moved to the Dollar Building on Canton Road a CHINA PRESS reporter learned yesterday.

Mr. Hough has engaged a suite of offices of four rooms on the third floor of the building and has taken an option on more space if required. All essential members of the present staff will be retained it is understood, and since most of the work of liquidating has developed into general routine, it is felt that there will be no need for taking up the option on additional space.

Moving To Be Easy Job

The job of moving will not be an exceedingly difficult one since most of the furniture and office equipment owned by the three bankrupt concerns has been sold by private sale, and only bare necessities have been retained. There are still a few typewriters on hand, and an adding machine or two, but for the most part, all the equipment except that which is needed in the actual work of liquidation has been sold.

It is further understood that most of the members of the liquidator's staff, now on the job, will be retained for another month or two since the work of preparing final reports on the positions of the three companies will not be completed before the first part of November.

In the meantime, however, the liquidator is negotiating for the sale of the bank property. Several offers have been received, it is understood, and these are now under consideration.

One Satisfactory Offer Made

One bidding firm, a local real estate concern, has made a satisfactory offer and should it obtain possession of the property, it plans to demolish the present building and erect a large office structure on the site. A large London concern also was reported to have been angling for the property with the idea of remodeling the present building, but it was reported yesterday that this deal had fallen through.

In the meantime, Mr. Henry De-Vault, auditor assisting Mr. Hough with the liquidation, is busy completing his reports on the Asia Realty Company and the Raven Trust Company and it is understood that these will be ready for publication in a few days.

While no definite information has been released concerning these reports, it is understood that they are not exactly favorable. Before being submitted to the press, they will be taken before Judge Milton J. Helmick, of the United States Court for China, and that will probably be done the early part of this week.

For the purpose of safeguarding Chinese financial interests, the Ministry of Finance has appointed Mr. Huang Tsung-hsun, attorney-at-law, to watch the liquidation of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the American Banking Corporation, it was revealed yesterday.

It was estimated that more than 700 Chinese are owed money by the two banks to the amount of about $2,300,000 at the time of their closure, in current deposits and American stocks and shares, it was declared.

雷文（Raven）系产业清算人
计划搬迁

将把办事处迁至
美元大楼（Dollar Building）
三楼

已有人出价
竞购银行房产

审计员正在完成
亚细亚地产公司、雷文信托公司
的报告

据《字林西报》记者昨日获悉，自10月1日起，随着清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生的办事处迁往广东路（Canton Road）的美元大楼，对雷文集团（House of Raven）旗下三家已停业机构——美亚银行（American-Oriental Bank）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）和雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）——的清算成本将大幅降低。

霍夫先生已在该大楼三楼租用了一套四间的办公室，并保留了在需要时增租更多空间的优先权。据悉，现有职员中的核心成员均将留任；鉴于大部分清算工作已转入常规程序，预计无需行使增租空间的优先权。

搬迁工作将很轻松

搬迁工作不会十分困难，因为这三家破产机构拥有的大部分家具和办公设备已通过私下出售方式售出，仅保留了最基本的必需品。目前手头仍剩有几台打字机和一两台加法机，但除清算实际工作所需的设备外，其余设备大多已售出。

另悉，清算人团队的大部分现职成员将继续留任一两个月，因为关于这三家公司状况的最终报告准备工作在11月上旬之前无法完成。

与此同时，清算人正在就银行房产的出售进行谈判。据悉，已收到数份报价，目前正在审议中。

已有一份令人满意的报价

一家本地房地产公司作为竞标方之一，提出了一份令人满意的报价；若其获得该房产，计划拆除现有建筑，并在原址上建造一座大型办公大楼。另有报道称，一家大型伦敦公司也曾有意获取该房产，打算对现有建筑进行改建，但昨日消息称该交易已告吹。

与此同时，协助霍夫先生进行清算工作的审计员亨利·德沃尔特（Henry De-Vault）先生正忙于完成关于亚细亚地产公司（Asia Realty Company）和雷文信托公司的报告，据悉这些报告将在数日内准备就绪以供发布。

虽然尚未发布关于这些报告的确切消息，但据悉报告内容并非完全有利。在提交给新闻界之前，这些报告将呈交美国在华法院法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）审阅，此举预计将于本周初进行。

昨日披露，为保护中国金融利益，财政部已任命律师黄宗勋（Huang Tsung-hsun，音译）先生监督美亚金融公司及美亚银行公司（American Banking Corporation）的清算工作。

据称，在这两家银行关闭时，估计有700多名中国人被拖欠款项，包括活期存款及美国股票和股份，总额约为230万美元。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1935

CHARGES AGAINST
A.-O. OFFICERS

Further Particulars Wanted
of Alleged Conversion

The hearing of charges of embezzlement against Mr. Frank J. Raven, Mr. John Warner Brown, and Mr. Albert Hamilton Driscoll, former officers of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, was set at October 29 by Judge Milton J. Helmick in the U. S. Court for China yesterday afternoon. All the charges, filed by the District Attorney, Mr. Felthan Watson, state that the defendants received stock from clients for safe keeping, and that they converted the stocks placed in their care to their own use.

Declaring that the case is not an ordinary one, Mr. R. T. Evans, attorney for the first defendant, asked for various dates and the manner of the alleged conversion. Mr. W. B. Harrington, who appeared for Mr. Driscoll, also asked for additional information of the alleged conversion, stating that it was of great importance that particulars of the dates of the alleged offence should be given together with the information as to whom the stocks were alleged to have been entrusted. Judge Helmick ruled that further particulars concerning the charges be given five days before the date of trial.

Since Mr. J. Warner Brown had not yet obtained counsel, no similar motion was made in the Court yesterday on his behalf.
