THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1935

Raven And Associates
To Be Tried In U. S.
Court On October 29

Date Of Hearing On Embezzlement Charges Set By
Judge Helmick Yesterday; District Attorney
To Furnish Precise Dates To Defence

COURT ANNOUNCES OCTOBER 15, DATE FOR
COMMENCEMENT OF CIVIL HEARINGS

Mr. Frank J. Raven, Mr. J. Warner Brown and Mr. Alfred H. Driscoll, President, Vice-President and Secretary-Treasurer, respectively, of the defunct American-Oriental Finance Corporation, will be tried on October 29 in the United States Court for China on the 15 charges of embezzlement brought against them by the U.S. District Attorney, it was announced by Judge Milton J. Helmick yesterday. This date was set at the first session of the Court to be held in several weeks, simultaneous announcement being made that hearings in the numerous civil actions brought against Mr. Frank J. Raven by the Liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company, will commence on October 15, two weeks earlier.

The Court gave consideration yesterday to motions filed on behalf of Messrs. Raven and Driscoll, asking that the District Attorney be required to furnish, in addition to information already on file, a Bill of Particulars setting forth the precise dates on which the alleged embezzlement of stocks, held in trust for customers by the A.-O.F.C., took place, and also the precise manner in which the alleged embezzlement was carried out.

Mr. W. B. Harrington, who appeared for Mr. Driscoll, said that according to law the granting of a motion for the furnishing of a Bill of Particulars rested entirely within the Court's discretion. He asked the Court, however, to exercise its discretion in favour of Mr. Driscoll and order the District Attorney to specify his charges in greater detail. Otherwise, he contended, the defence would be seriously embarrassed.

Case Of Mr. Driscoll
"Exact dates of the alleged acts of wrongful conversion should be set out in each of the 15 counts," Mr. Harrington contended. He went on to state that this was particularly important since Mr. Driscoll, who was charged in his capacity as Secretary and Treasurer of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, had in fact ceased to be the Treasurer on January 1, 1935, while some of the allegations of the District Attorney related to subsequent dates.

Appearing for Mr. Frank J. Raven, Attorney Richard T. Evans of Tientsin said he associated himself with Mr. Harrington's remarks, adding that there was no dispute as to the allegation that Mr. Raven was an officer of the A.-O.F.C. at the various times when the alleged wrongful acts were done. Nevertheless, he felt that in fairness to his client the fullest possible information should be furnished to the defence by the District Attorney.

Judge Helmick said he felt that the information which had been filed against the accused was perfectly clear. In the case of Mr. Driscoll, however, he thought there was some justification for the request for further particulars to enable the defence properly to prepare its case.

Dates To Be Given
He asked the District Attorney if he would undertake to furnish the defence with the precise dates asked for five days in advance of the trial. The District Attorney agreed and Messrs. Harrington and Evans expressed themselves as satisfied with this arrangement.

No application for the further particulars was made yesterday by Mr. J. Warner Brown, the third defendant in the embezzlement case. As far as is known, he has not yet engaged counsel to defend him.

The trial of the three officials of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation is expected to prove one of the most sensational in the annals of the United States Court for China. It was the bankruptcy of this concern and its two affiliates — the American-Oriental Banking Corporation and Raven Trust Company—which led to the extensive investigation on which the present charges of embezzlement are based.

In the information filed against the defendants, the charge, consisting of 15 separate counts, alleges that they "wilfully, unlawfully, fraudulently and feloniously embezzled and converted to their own use" various securities entrusted to the American-Oriental Finance Corporation for safe-keeping, the amount involved being in excess of U.S.$62,000.

Arrested August 31
Mr. Raven and Mr. Driscoll were arrested here on August 31 and released the same day on bond after a brief period spent in the Amoy Road Gaol. Bond for Mr. Raven was set by Judge Helmick at U.S.$10,000, while that of Mr. Driscoll was set to U.S.$5,000. Mr. J. Warner Brown was arrested in Manila, where he was engaged in winding up the affairs of the Manila branch of the A.-O.F.C., and brought to Shanghai on Monday in the custody of the captain of the s.s. President Hoover. Meanwhile, a bond for U.S.$10,000 was posted for Mr. Brown with the Department of Justice in Washington and approved here by Judge Helmick, with the result that Mr. Brown was set at liberty on his arrival here.

Civil suits filed against Mr. Raven and some of his relatives since the Liquidator, Mr. Frank L. Hough, took charge of the bankrupt Raven enterprises last June, call for the reimbursement by the defendants of sums totaling approximately Sh.$1,500,000, exclusive of interest. Hearings in these suits is being held in advance of the criminal prosecution, and it is considered likely that some of the evidence given in the former will be made use of in the latter.

Those Honoraria
Among the items for which the Liquidator is seeking judgment against Mr. Frank J. Raven are three sums of Tls. 135,000 each, voted to Mr. Raven and received by him in January, 1932 from the American-Oriental Banking Corporation and the Asia Realty Company as honoraria for services rendered. The Liquidator alleges that these sums were wrongfully received by Mr. Raven at a time when all three concerns voting them were allegedly bankrupt.

Judgment is also asked for U.S. $118,000 stated to be owing by Mr. Raven to the A.-O.F.C. on accounts opened and continued in his name to enable him to buy and sell stocks on the New York Stock Exchange. Other claims represent unpaid promissory notes and unliquidated overdraft balances.

In addition to the bond of U.S. $10,000 which he was required to post in the criminal action which is to be heard on October 29, Mr. Raven is under bond of U.S.$20,-000 not to leave the Republic of China without the express permission of the U.S. Court.

《上海泰晤士报》，1935年9月11日，星期三

雷文及其同伙
将于10月29日在美国
法院受审

赫尔米克法官昨日确定挪用公款指控听证日期；
地区检察官将向辩方提供确切日期

法院宣布10月15日为
民事听证开始日期

法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克昨日宣布，已倒闭的美亚金融公司的总裁、副总裁兼秘书兼司库——弗兰克·J·雷文先生、J·华纳·布朗先生和阿尔弗雷德·H·德里斯科尔（Alfred H. Driscoll）先生——将于10月29日在美国在华法院就美国地区检察官对他们提出的15项挪用公款指控接受审判。该日期定在数周后举行的首次法庭会议上，同时宣布，针对弗兰克·J·雷文先生提起的多起民事诉讼的听证会将于10月15日开始，即提前两周。这些民事诉讼由美亚银行公司、美亚金融公司和雷文信托公司的清算人提起。

法庭昨日审议了代表雷文先生和德里斯科尔先生提交的动议，要求地区检察官除已存档的信息外，还需提供一份详细说明书（Bill of Particulars），列明据称由美亚金融公司代客户保管的股票发生挪用行为的确切日期，以及据称实施挪用行为的具体方式。

代表德里斯科尔先生出庭的W·B·哈林顿先生说，根据法律，是否批准提供详细说明书的动议完全由法庭酌情决定。但他请求法庭行使裁量权，支持德里斯科尔先生，命令地区检察官更详细地明确其指控。他辩称，否则辩方将面临严重困境。

德里斯科尔先生的案件
哈林顿先生辩称：“15项罪名中的每一项都应列出涉嫌非法挪用行为的确切日期。”他接着指出，这一点尤为重要，因为德里斯科尔先生是以美亚金融公司秘书兼司库的身份被起诉的，而事实上他已于1935年1月1日不再担任司库一职，但地区检察官的部分指控涉及此后的日期。

代表弗兰克·J·雷文先生出庭的是来自天津的律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）。他表示赞同哈林顿先生的意见，并补充说，对于雷文先生在涉嫌不法行为发生的各个时期均担任美亚金融公司高管这一指控并无争议。尽管如此，他认为为了公平对待其当事人，地区检察官应向辩方提供尽可能详尽的信息。

赫尔米克法官表示，他认为针对被告所提交的信息已经非常清晰。然而，在德里斯科尔先生的案件中，他认为要求提供更多详情以使辩方能够妥善准备案件是有正当理由的。

将提供日期

他询问地区检察官是否承诺在审判前五日向辩方提供所要求的确切日期。地区检察官表示同意，哈林顿先生和埃文斯先生均表示对该安排感到满意。

挪用公款案的第三被告J·华纳·布朗先生昨天未申请提供进一步详情。据所知，他尚未聘请律师为其辩护。

美亚金融公司这三名高管的审判预计将成为美国在华法院历史上最轰动的案件之一。正是该公司的破产及其两家关联公司——美亚银行公司和雷文信托公司——的破产，导致了广泛的调查，目前的挪用公款指控即基于此次调查。

在对被告提起的起诉书中，包含15项独立罪名的指控称，他们“故意、非法、欺诈且重罪地挪用并转换归己使用”委托给美亚金融公司保管的各种证券，涉案金额超过62,000美元。

8月31日被捕

雷文先生和德里斯科尔先生于8月31日在此被捕，在厦门路监狱（Amoy Road Gaol）短暂停留后，于同日保释释放。赫尔米克法官将雷文先生的保释金定为10,000美元，德里斯科尔先生的保释金定为5,000美元。J·华纳·布朗先生在马尼拉被捕，当时他正在处理美亚金融公司马尼拉分行的收尾事务，并于周一由“胡佛总统号”（President Hoover）轮船船长监护押送至上海。与此同时，布朗先生已向华盛顿司法部缴纳10,000美元保释金，并经赫尔米克法官在此批准，因此布朗先生抵达此处后即获自由。

自清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫先生去年六月接管破产的雷文企业以来，针对雷文先生及其部分亲属提起的民事诉讼要求被告偿还总额约150万上海两（Sh.$1,500,000）的款项，不含利息。这些诉讼的听证会在刑事起诉之前进行，人们认为在前者中提供的一些证据可能会在后者中被使用。

那些酬金

在清算人寻求针对弗兰克·J·雷文先生判决的项目中，包括三笔各为135,000两白银（Tls. 135,000）的款项，这些款项于1932年1月投票决定支付给雷文先生，并由其从美亚银行公司和亚细亚地产公司收取，作为提供服务的花红（honoraria）。清算人指控，雷文先生在收取这些款项时，投票决定支付这三笔款项的三家公司据称均已破产，因此他是非法收取的。

此外，还要求判决雷文先生欠美亚金融公司118,000美元，该款项系以其名义开立并延续的账户所欠，旨在使其能够在纽约证券交易所买卖股票。其他索赔包括未付本票和未结清的透支余额。

除了在被定于10月29日审理的刑事诉讼中需缴纳的10,000美元保释金外，雷文先生还负有20,000美元的保释义务，未经美国在华法院明确许可，不得离开中华民国。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 4, 1935

WATCH KEPT ON MR.
WARNER BROWN

Arrest Warrant Not Served
on Former A.O.F.C. Officer

Nothing further has been heard by
the U.S. Court for China regarding
Mr. J. Warner Brown, vice-president
of the American-Oriental Finance
Corp. in liquidation, who is at pre-
sent in Manila, and against whom,
in company with Messrs. Frank J.
Raven and A. H. Driscoll, fifteen
charges of embezzlement, totalling
U.S.$62,679.51 were filed on Saturday
by the U.S. District Attorney, Mr.
Felthan Watson.

A United Press message yesterday
stated:—
“Permission to return to Shanghai
in custody of the Captain of the ss.
President Hoover is sought by Mr.
J. Warner Brown, former official of
the defunct American-Oriental
Finance Corporation. Mr. Brown to-
day sent a radio message to his
attorney, asking him to request per-
mission of the United States Court
for China in the matter. Mr. Brown,
named as one of the defendants in
embezzlement charges filed with the
court at Shanghai, has not yet been
arrested, although the documents for
his arrest were prepared early yes-
terday.”

Although documents for his arrest
have been drawn up, they have not
been served on Mr. Warner Brown,
but should there be any indication
that he will not carry out his stated
intention of coming up to Shanghai
on the President Hoover, he will be
arrested by the Philippine authorities
and the local court notified. In this
event, it will be necessary for a
Deputy Marshal to proceed to Manila
and accompany him back. Under
American law, he can be held for
ninety days, at the end of which
time, should no Deputy Marshal ar-
rive from Shanghai to take him in
charge, the authorities would have no
recourse but to turn him loose.

Both Mr. Raven and Mr. Driscoll
have been released on bail of U.S.$10,-
000 and U.S.$5,000 respectively. Judge
Milton J. Helmick, when the charges
of embezzlement were filed, fixed
Mr. Warner Brown’s bail at U.S.$10,-
000, but as he has not yet been ar-
rested or the warrant served on him,
he has not put up any money as
security. Further news from the
Philippine authorities is expected
shortly.

《字林西报》，1935年9月4日，星期三

对沃纳·布朗先生（Mr. Warner Brown）进行监视

未向美亚金融公司前高管送达逮捕令

关于正在清算的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corp.）副董事长J. 沃纳·布朗先生（Mr. J. Warner Brown），美国驻华法院目前未收到进一步消息。布朗先生现居马尼拉。上周六，美国地区检察官费尔桑·沃森先生（Mr. Felthan Watson）联合弗兰克·J. 雷文先生（Messrs. Frank J. Raven）和A. H. 德里斯科尔先生（A. H. Driscoll），对其提起十五项挪用公款指控，涉案总金额达62,679.51美元。

合众社昨日消息称：
“已停业的美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）前官员J. 沃纳·布朗先生寻求获准在‘胡佛总统号’轮船（ss. President Hoover）船长的监护下返回上海。布朗先生今日向其律师发送无线电报，请其就此事向美国驻华法院申请许可。布朗先生被列为在上海法院提起的挪用公款指控的被告之一，尽管逮捕他的文件已于昨日清晨备妥，但他尚未被捕。”

虽然逮捕文件已经拟定，但尚未送达沃纳·布朗先生。不过，若有任何迹象表明他不会履行其 stated 乘坐‘胡佛总统号’来沪的意向，菲律宾当局将其逮捕，并通知当地法院。在此情况下，将需由一名副法警前往马尼拉，并陪同其返回。根据美国法律，他可被拘留九十天；若期限届满仍无来自上海的副法警抵达并将其接管，当局除将其释放外别无他法。

雷文先生和德里斯科尔先生已分别以10,000美元和5,000美元保释获释。米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官（Judge Milton J. Helmick）在提出挪用公款指控时，将沃纳·布朗先生的保释金定为10,000美元，但由于他尚未被捕或收到逮捕令，故未缴纳任何保证金。预计不久后将收到来自菲律宾当局的进一步消息。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, SEPTEMBER 5, 1935

J. WARNER BROWN
OF A.-O. FINANCE
CORP. IN CUSTODY

Unable to Arrange for Bail
of 20,000 Pesos

COMING TO SHANGHAI
FOR TRIAL

Manila, Sept. 4.
Mr. J. Warner Brown, vice-president and director of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, who was arrested yesterday afternoon on a warrant issued in the morning spent the rest of the day in the company of his attorney, Mr. George Harvey, searching for bail of 20,000 pesos. Unable to find it up to a late hour, he spent the night in the custody of the secret police, who have arranged for him to go to Shanghai in the Dollar liner President Hoover, which sails this afternoon.
Mr. Brown visited town this morning, in the nominal custody of a detective, to attend to personal business. During the voyage to Shanghai, he will be in the custody of Capt. Anderson, of the President Hoover, who will act as a United States deputy marshal for the purpose.
Mr. Brown cabled to Mr. Cornell S. Franklin, yesterday, asking him to request Judge Milton J. Helmick, of the United States Court for China, to give him permission to travel to Shanghai in the custody of the captain of the President Hoover.
Reuter.

《字林西报》，1935年9月5日，星期四

美亚金融公司的J. 沃纳·布朗
被羁押

无法安排20,000比索保释金

将来沪受审

马尼拉，9月4日电。
美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）副董事长兼董事J. 沃纳·布朗先生于昨日下午依据当日早晨签发的逮捕令被捕，随后余下的时间与其律师乔治·哈维先生（Mr. George Harvey）在一起，试图筹措20,000比索的保释金。直至深夜仍未能找到保释金，他在秘密警察的羁押下度过了一夜。警方已安排他搭乘今日下午启航的美资邮轮‘胡佛总统号’（President Hoover）前往上海。
布朗先生今晨在一名侦探的名义监护下进城处理私人事务。在前往上海的航程中，他将由‘胡佛总统号’船长安德森上尉（Capt. Anderson）监护，后者为此目的担任美国副法警职务。
布朗先生昨日致电康奈尔·S. 富兰克林先生（Mr. Cornell S. Franklin），请其请求美国驻华法院的米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官（Judge Milton J. Helmick），准许他在‘胡佛总统号’船长的监护下前往上海。
路透社。

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年8月31日，星期六    11651
美国法院对
美亚金融公司管理层提起
挪用公款指控    6748
F. J. 雷文、J. W. 布朗和A.H. 德里斯科尔三位先生
被点名；15项指控涉及盗用
价值超过62,754美元的股票

本地两项保释金立即缴付

美国地区检察官费伊桑·沃森（Feithan Watson）今日向美国驻华法院提交起诉书，指控弗兰克·杰伊·雷文（Frank Jay Raven）、约翰·沃纳·布朗（John Warner Brown）和阿尔弗雷德·汉密尔顿·德里斯科尔（Alfred Hamilton Driscoll）三位先生在担任美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）高管期间犯有十五项挪用公款罪。

米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官（Judge Milton J. Helmick）裁定保释金金额为：雷文先生10,000美元，布朗先生10,000美元，德里斯科尔先生5,000美元。

雷文先生和德里斯科尔先生均在中午前响应通知出庭。曾任美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）副董事长兼总经理的朱利叶斯·克莱费尔先生（Mr. Julius Kleffel）偕同克莱费尔夫人出庭，由克莱费尔夫人代表德里斯科尔先生缴纳保释金。

等待裁决

然而，此举需经赫尔米克法官批准。中午过后不久，雷文先生和德里斯科尔先生被带往厦门路监狱用餐，美国法警爱德华·L. 福佩尔（Edward L. Faupel）特别指示，应给予他们最自由的通讯权利。与此同时，克莱费尔夫妇上楼前往赫尔米克法官的寓所，等待其对德里斯科尔保释金的裁决。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 1, 1935
11643

EMBEZZLEMENT CHARGES
OVER A.O.F.C. AFFAIRS

Mr. F. J. Raven and Mr. A. H. Driscoll Held on Bail:
Complaint Laid Against Mr. J. Warner Brown

FIFTEEN COUNTS INVOLVING U.S. $62,679

Alleged Conversion of Stocks Deposited by Clients
for Safe Keeping

FIFTEEN charges of embezzlement, totalling U.S. $62,679.51, were filed yesterday by the District Attorney, Mr. Felthan Watson, in the U.S. Court for China, against Mr. Frank J. Raven, Mr. John Warner Brown, and Mr. Albert Hamilton Driscoll, former officers of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation. It was the first official action of the United States Government in connection with the affairs of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and other organizations, which suspended business on May 24, this year. All the charges state that the defendants received stock from clients for safe keeping, and that they converted the stocks placed in their care to their own use.

Bail for Mr. Raven and Mr. Brown, who is now in Manila, was set by Judge Milton J. Helmick at U.S. $10,000, and that for Mr. Driscoll at U.S. $5,000.

NOTHING TO GO
TO STOCKHOLDERS
OF RAVEN TRUST

7 Per Cent. Available for
Unsecured Creditors

ASSETS AND LIABILITIES
SHOWN BY AUDITOR

The estimated shrinkage in values and the estimated amount that may be realized for the benefit of the creditors is shown in a balance-sheet prepared by Mr. H. S. De Vault, certified public accountant, for Mr. Frank Hough, liquidator of the Raven Trust Co., yesterday. The balance sheet shows the assets and liabilities of the Raven Trust Co. on May 23, this year, the last day the company was open for business. Mr. Hough took over as liquidator for the firm on June 4.

The principal item of assets, namely, investments in stocks, is expected to realize $150,000, or approximately 8½ per cent. of the book values. About 85 per cent. of these investments are in stocks of associated and affiliated companies.

"The statement of the liabilities," said Mr. Hough, "includes all known obligations. It may be that there are some claims which were not on record, but, if so, the amounts are not believed to be material."

The balance sheet shows that there may be realized approximately $300,-000, less the cost of liquidation, which will be available for creditors. This amount is about 7 per cent. of the total unsecured creditors' claims. As indicated by the statement, there will be nothing available for the stockholders.

Mr. De Vault and his staff at present are at work on an analysis of the operations of the Raven Trust Co. from the beginning of its existence, and Mr. Hough stated yesterday that he hopes within a short time to be able to present a full report on all transactions of the company.

The balance-sheet follows:-

Mr. Raven arrived in the U.S. Consulate in response to a telephone call from the U.S. Marshal, Mr. Edward Faupel, shortly before noon. He was unescorted, coming from his home entirely of his own free will. He was taken to the Amoy Road gaol, as a formality, until his bail could be arranged. This was done by his bother, Mr. C. H. Raven, who wrote out a cashier's cheque for U.S. $10,000 on the Chase National Bank. Immediately upon receipt of the cheque, Mr. Faupel instructed the gaol officials to release Mr. Raven.

Mr. Driscoll's bail was put up by Mrs. Julius C. Kleffel, wife of the

[图片：Mr. F. J. Raven]

former vice-president and manager of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation. She posted her home as security. It was necessary first for Judge Helmick to approve the security. In the meantime, Mr. Driscoll also was taken to the gaol, with Mr. Raven. He was released shortly, when Judge Helmick approved the security.

美亚金融公司事务中的
挪用公款指控

F. J. 雷文先生和A. H. 德里斯科尔先生交保获释：
对J. 沃纳·布朗先生提出控告

十五项指控涉及62,679美元

涉嫌转换客户寄存保管的股票

地区检察官费尔桑·沃森先生（Mr. Felthan Watson）昨日在美国驻华法院对美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）前高管弗兰克·J. 雷文先生（Mr. Frank J. Raven）、约翰·沃纳·布朗先生（Mr. John Warner Brown）和阿尔伯特·汉密尔顿·德里斯科尔先生（Mr. Albert Hamilton Driscoll）提起十五项挪用公款指控，总计62,679.51美元。这是美国政府针对今年5月24日停业的美亚金融公司及其他相关机构事务采取的首次官方行动。所有指控均称，被告接收客户股票代为保管，并将置于其照管下的股票挪作私用。

赫尔米克法官（Judge Milton J. Helmick）将现居马尼拉的布朗先生和雷文先生的保释金定为10,000美元，德里斯科尔先生的保释金定为5,000美元。

雷文信托公司股东
一无所获

无担保债权人可获得7%

审计师显示
资产与负债

注册公共会计师H. S. 德沃尔特先生（Mr. H. S. De Vault）昨日为雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Co.）清算人弗兰克·霍夫先生（Mr. Frank Hough）编制了一份资产负债表，其中显示了估值缩水的估计金额以及可为债权人实现的估计金额。该资产负债表显示了雷文信托公司在今年5月23日（即公司营业的最后一天）的资产和负债情况。霍夫先生于6月4日接任该公司清算人。

主要资产项目，即股票投资，预计可实现150,000美元，约占账面价值的8½%。这些投资中约85%为关联公司和附属公司的股票。

霍夫先生表示：“负债表包括所有已知债务。可能存在一些未记录的索赔，但如果存在，相信金额不大。”

资产负债表显示，扣除清算成本后，可供债权人使用的资金约为300,000美元。这笔金额约占无担保债权人索赔总额的7%。正如报表所示，股东将一无所获。

德沃尔特先生及其团队目前正在分析雷文信托公司自成立以来的运营情况，霍夫先生昨日表示，他希望能在短时间内提交一份关于公司所有交易的完整报告。

资产负债表如下：-

雷文先生在接到美国法警爱德华·福佩尔先生（Mr. Edward Faupel）的电话后，于中午前不久抵达美国领事馆。他无人陪同，完全出于自愿从家中前来。作为一种形式，他被带往厦门路监狱，直到安排好保释手续。此举由其兄弟C. H. 雷文先生（Mr. C. H. Raven）完成，他开具了一张大通国家银行（Chase National Bank）的10,000美元本票。福佩尔先生一收到支票，便指示监狱官员释放雷文先生。

德里斯科尔先生的保释金由朱利叶斯·C. 克莱费尔夫人（Mrs. Julius C. Kleffel）缴纳，她是

[图片：F. J. 雷文先生]

美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前副董事长兼总经理的妻子。她以自家房产作为担保。首先需经赫尔米克法官批准该担保。在此期间，德里斯科尔先生也与雷文先生一同被带往监狱。当赫尔米克法官批准担保后，他很快获释。

Mr. Brown Not Served
Mr. Brown, in Manila, according to a United Press despatch, stated yesterday that the charges filed against him had not yet been served and he declined to make any comment on the matter. The Manila branch of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation recently partially paid its creditors, and hopes that all can be paid off if the Manila branch is separated from the other branches of the Corporation. Whether or not it can be is now being decided by the Courts in Manila.
It will be necessary for the U.S. Court to send a marshal to Manila to bring Mr. Brown to Shanghai. Mr. Faupel yesterday morning cabled to Governor Frank Murphy about the developments here, and stated that a man would be sent to Manila formally to serve the warrant upon Mr. Brown.
A United Press message from Manila, yesterday, stated:—"Inasmuch as the Secret Service has not received any request to detain Mr. John Warner Brown, there will probably be no action taken against him during the weekend."
Mr. Raven and Mr. Driscoll will be given a preliminary hearing by the Acting Commissioner, Mr. William T. Collins, next week. The penalty for embezzlement in this case is ten years in the Federal Prison on McNeill's Island, near Seattle, or U.S. $1,000, or both.

[图片：Mr. J. Warner Brown]

Details of Charges
The largest of the fifteen charges is for U.S. $50,000, this stating that on or about November 17, 1934, Mr. L. Bassett brought to the American-Oriental Finance Corporation for safe keeping 400 shares of American Telephone & Telegraph and 100 shares of Western Union Telegraph Co. The charge goes on to state that, from November, 1934, until May 27, this year, the defendants used the shares for their own benefit, and that, when the American-Oriental Finance Corporation suspended business, the defendants were unable to repay Mr. Bassett.
Of the other fourteen charges, six are in four figures, ranging from U.S. $1,041.57 to U.S. $2,808.02. The other eight are all under U.S. $1,000, the smallest being for U.S. $22.75. This is for three shares in the Electric Bond & Share Co., which Mr. L. J. Bergmann placed with the American-Oriental Finance Corporation for safe keeping.
Besides Mr. Bassett and Mr. Bergmann, the people mentioned in the charges as having placed stock with the defendants are Mr. D'Ungern Sternberg, Mr. Edward P. Howard, Mr. O. Bordes, Mr. H. W. Brook, Mrs. John to F. Stevens, jun., Mr. C. R. Jones, Mr. John Cornfield, Mr. M. J. Harris, Mr. William N. and Florence C. Gray, Mr. Stanley G. Kirkland, Mr. Gordon Yates, Mr. John A. Ely, and Mr. H. G. Smith.
With the present charges, the amount of money involved in the case now reaches a total of U.S. $259,041.69 and Sh. $1,121,761.88.

布朗先生未收到传票
据合众社电讯，身在马尼拉的布朗先生昨日表示，针对他的指控文件尚未送达，他拒绝对此事发表评论。美亚金融公司马尼拉分行最近已向债权人部分付款，并希望如果马尼拉分行能与该公司其他分行分离，所有债务均可还清。此事能否实现，目前正由马尼拉法院裁决。
美国法院需派遣法警前往马尼拉，将布朗先生带回上海。福佩尔 (Faupel) 先生昨日上午就此处事态发展向州长弗兰克·墨菲 (Frank Murphy) 发电报，并表示将派人正式前往马尼拉向布朗先生送达逮捕令。
合众社昨日发自马尼拉的消息称：“鉴于特勤局未收到任何拘留约翰·沃纳·布朗 (John Warner Brown) 先生的请求，周末期间可能不会对他采取任何行动。”
雷文 (Raven) 先生和德里斯科尔 (Driscoll) 先生将于下周由代理专员威廉·T·柯林斯 (William T. Collins) 先生进行初步聆讯。本案挪用公款的刑罚为在西雅图附近的麦克尼尔岛 (McNeill's Island) 联邦监狱服刑十年，或罚款 1,000 美元，或两者并罚。

[图片：J. 沃纳·布朗先生]

指控详情
十五项指控中金额最大的一项为 50,000 美元，该项指控称，1934 年 11 月 17 日左右，L. 巴塞特 (L. Bassett) 先生将 400 股美国电话电报公司 (American Telephone & Telegraph) 股票和 100 股西联电报公司 (Western Union Telegraph Co.) 股票交由美亚金融公司保管。指控接着指出，从 1934 年 11 月至今年 5 月 27 日，被告将这些股票用于个人利益，且在美亚金融公司停业时，被告无法偿还巴塞特先生。
在其余十四项指控中，有六项金额为四位数，范围从 1,041.57 美元到 2,808.02 美元不等。另外八项均低于 1,000 美元，最小的一项为 22.75 美元。该项涉及三股电力债券与股票公司 (Electric Bond & Share Co.) 的股票，由 L. J. 伯格曼 (L. J. Bergmann) 先生交由美亚金融公司保管。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, August 24, 1935

Liquidator Sues Raven Family
For U.S. $196,362, Sh.$363,005
On American-Oriental Accounts

Mr., Mrs. Charles, Walter
Raven Named; Court
Serves Papers

Promissory Notes, Overdrafts Listed

A total of U.S.$196,362.18 plus Sh. $363,005.69 is asked from various members of the Raven family in suits filed with the U. S. Court For China today by Mr. Frank L. Hough in his capacity of liquidator for the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, at the Raven Trust Company.

Those named in the suits are Mr. Frank J. Raven, former president of the institutions, who in the largest of the suits is asked for a total of U.S.$128,313.29 on New York stock trading accounts; Mr. Charles H. Raven; Mr. Walter F. Raven; and Mr. Charles H. and Mrs. Lillian S. Raven.

SERVING PAPERS

Service was obtained on Mr. Charles Raven this morning and it was expected that papers would be served in the other suits during the course of the day save in the case of Mr. Raven, who is not at present in Shanghai.

The suits are based on stock trading accounts, unpaid balances of promissory notes, overdrafts and loans. In some instances security in the form of stocks was put up, and the liquidator asks in such instances for sale of the collateral to satisfy judgment.

Two March Loans

Included among the suits are such recent causes for action as two loans as of March 1 of the present year, to Mr. Walter F. Frank J. Raven, five causes of action are cited involved five trading accounts on the New York Stock Exchange handled through the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, these being carried on the books as "R.T. Co. Trustee, No. 191-11," "R. T. C. Trustee, No. 101-A-5," and so on.

On the first account an indebtedness of U.S.$107,213.41 is claimed, on the second U.S.$12,-472.36, on the third U.S.$6434.65, on the fourth U.S.$1248.74, and on the fifth $944.13. On all, judgment is asked for the amounts named with interest on the first three accounts at 6 per cent and on the last two at 8 per cent.

Charles H. Raven Suit

Suit against Mr. Charles H. Raven, likewise on behalf of the Finance Corporation, also has to do with a New York Stock Exchange account, bearing 8 per cent interest, and it is declared there is owing U.S.$52,724.85.

Against this there was pledged as collateral 10,800 shares of Common "A" Bakerite Company stock, 11 Socony-Vacuum Corporation shares, and 940 Common "A" American-Oriental Finance Corporation shares, sale of which is requested of the court for satisfaction of judgment.

A third suit, also against Mr. Charles H. Raven, is based on a Sh.$120,183.90 loan from the Raven Trust on which the unpaid balance is stated to be Sh.$50,183.90 bearing interest at 8 per cent from July 20, 1933.

Raven Trust

Another cause for action in the same suit cites disbursements by the Raven Trust on which Mr. Raven is said to be indebted to the extent of U.S.$1824.04 plus Sh.$861.74.

Suit against Mr. Walter F. Raven is based on a promissory note for U.S.$5000 on which it is alleged no payment has been made so return of the money plus interest at 8 per cent from March 1, 1935, is asked. This money was loaned by the American-Oriental Banking Corporation.

Second Cause

A second cause for action is based on a bank overdraft on which Sh.-$29,887.91 is sought, plus interest at 8 per cent from May 24.

Suit against Mr. Charles H. and Mrs. Lillian S. Raven is based on an American-Oriental Banking Corporation overdraft to these two jointly on which it is alleged Sh. $93,749.64 is due with interest at 8 per cent from May 24.

Against this, a pledge of 13,125 Common "A" shares of Bakerite Company stock stands, and sale of this is asked for satisfaction of judgment.

Promissory Note

Another suit against Mr. Charles H. Raven is based on a promissory note to the American-Oriental Banking Corporation for U.S.$7500, on which nothing has been paid and full repayment is asked with interest at 8 per cent since March 1, 1935.

清算人起诉雷文家族
索赔美亚账户项下
196,362 美元及 363,005 上海两

查尔斯、沃尔特·雷文
先生及夫人被列为被告；
法院送达文书

列出本票及透支款项

弗兰克·L·霍夫 (Frank L. Hough) 先生今日以美亚金融公司及美亚银行公司清算人的身份，向在华美国法院提起诉讼，要求雷文信托公司的雷文家族各成员支付总计 196,362.18 美元外加 363,005.69 上海两。

诉讼中点名的人员包括：上述机构前总裁弗兰克·J·雷文 (Frank J. Raven) 先生，在最大的一起诉讼中，他被要求支付纽约股票交易账户款项共计 128,313.29 美元；查尔斯·H·雷文 (Charles H. Raven) 先生；沃尔特·F·雷文 (Walter F. Raven) 先生；以及查尔斯·H·雷文先生和莉莲·S·雷文 (Lillian S. Raven) 夫人。

送达文书

今晨已向查尔斯·雷文先生完成送达，预计当天内将完成其他诉讼的文书送达，但雷文先生除外，他目前不在上海。

这些诉讼基于股票交易账户、未付本票余额、透支和贷款。在某些情况下，提供了股票作为担保，清算人在此类情况下请求出售抵押品以执行判决。

两笔三月贷款

诉讼中包含近期的起诉理由，例如今年 3 月 1 日向沃尔特·F·雷文和弗兰克·J·雷文提供的两笔贷款。另五项起诉理由涉及通过美亚金融公司处理的五个纽约证券交易所交易账户，这些账户在账簿上列为“R.T. Co. Trustee, No. 191-11”、“R. T. C. Trustee, No. 101-A-5”等。

第一个账户声称欠款 107,213.41 美元，第二个账户 12,472.36 美元，第三个账户 6,434.65 美元，第四个账户 1,248.74 美元，第五个账户 944.13 美元。对所有账户均要求按所列金额作出判决，前三个账户按 6% 计息，后两个账户按 8% 计息。

查尔斯·H·雷文诉讼案

同样代表金融公司对查尔斯·H·雷文先生提起的诉讼，也涉及一个年利率为 8% 的纽约证券交易所账户，据称欠款 52,724.85 美元。

为此质押了 10,800 股贝克莱特公司 (Bakerite Company) 普通股“A”类股票、11 股索科尼-真空公司 (Socony-Vacuum Corporation) 股票和 940 股美亚金融公司普通股“A”类股票作为抵押品，并请求法院出售这些股票以执行判决。

第三起诉讼也是针对查尔斯·H·雷文先生，基于雷文信托的一笔 120,183.90 上海两贷款，据称未付余额为 50,183.90 上海两，自 1933 年 7 月 20 日起按 8% 计息。

雷文信托

同一诉讼中的另一项起诉理由 citing 雷文信托的支出，据称雷文先生因此欠款 1,824.04 美元外加 861.74 上海两。

对沃尔特·F·雷文先生的诉讼基于一张 5,000 美元的本票，据称未支付任何款项，因此要求归还本金及自 1935 年 3 月 1 日起按 8% 计算的利息。这笔钱由美亚银行公司借出。

第二项起诉理由

第二项起诉理由基于银行透支，要求支付 29,887.91 上海两，外加自 5 月 24 日起按 8% 计算的利息。

对查尔斯·H·雷文先生和莉莲·S·雷文夫人的诉讼基于美亚银行公司向这两人共同提供的透支，据称欠款 93,749.64 上海两，自 5 月 24 日起按 8% 计息。

为此质押了 13,125 股贝克莱特公司普通股“A”类股票，并请求出售该股票以执行判决。

本票

另一起针对查尔斯·H·雷文先生的诉讼基于一张向美亚银行公司出具的 7,500 美元本票，据称未支付任何款项，要求全额还款及自 1935 年 3 月 1 日起按 8% 计算的利息。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 1, 1935
Hearing Of Raven Suits Likely
To Be Delayed Until Autumn

Sellett Indicates That
Case May Not Be Set
For Some Months Yet

Hough Not Likely To
Answer Evans Letter

The hearings of the three actions filed with the clerk of the United States Court for China against Mr. Frank J. Raven, formerly head of the defunct concerns that bear his name, will in all probability not be conducted until fall, a CHINA PRESS reporter learned yesterday during a short conversation with Dr. George Sellett, attorney for Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator, of the American-Oriental Bank, American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the Raven Trust Company.

Dr. Sellett was reticent about discussing the probable time when the three cases will be heard, saying that he could not say anything definite as to when the attorneys concerned would present motions to the court to set date of hearing.

In view of the fact that Mr. Richard Evans, attorney for Mr. Raven, has returned to his home in Tientsin for the purpose of attending to other affairs pending before he agreed to defend Mr. Raven and at the same time to study matters pertaining to the three cases, it was reported as being unlikely that any motions to set the date will be made during August.

Liquidating Continues

The three bills of complaint against Mr. Raven ask the recovery of bonus money, aggregating Tls. 405,-000, alleged to have been paid to him by the A.O.B.C., the A.O.F.C., and the Asia Realty Company. Two of the complaints allege that the bonus transactions were wrongful and fraudulent.

In the meantime, the business of liquidating the three defunct concerns and reorganization of the Asia Realty Company, of which Mr. Hough is trustee, has developed into a matter of heavy routine, according to the liquidator.

Regarding the open letter sent to him by Mr. Raven, in which statements alleged to have been made by the liquidator, were attacked, Mr. Hough has had very little to say, and up to the present time has given no indication of intending to answer the epistle. He has informed a CHINA PRESS reporter that he does not at the present time intend to send an open letter to Mr. Raven.

It is understood that the Asia Realty audit is nearing completion, but it could not be learned yesterday as to what time a financial statement concerning this company can be expected. It is known, however, that drastic cuts have been made in overhead by Mr. Hough in an effort to realize some actual cash on the company's income and that the trustee's work in this direction has been somewhat successful.

雷文案件聆讯可能
推迟至秋季

塞莱特表示
案件可能数月内
不会排期

霍夫不太可能
回复埃文斯的信件

《字林西报》记者昨日在与乔治·塞莱特 (George Sellett) 博士简短交谈中获悉，向在华美国法院书记官提交的针对弗兰克·J·雷文先生（以其名字命名的已倒闭机构的前负责人）的三起诉讼，很可能要到秋季才会进行聆讯。塞莱特博士是美亚银行、美亚金融公司和雷文信托公司清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫先生的律师。

塞莱特博士对讨论这三起案件可能的审理时间持谨慎态度，他表示，无法确定相关律师何时会向法院提出动议以设定聆讯日期。

鉴于雷文先生的律师理查德·埃文斯 (Richard Evans) 先生已返回天津家中处理其他待决事务，并在同意为雷文先生辩护的同时研究涉及这三起案件的相关事宜，据报道，8 月份不太可能提出设定日期的动议。

清算工作继续进行

针对雷文先生的三份诉状要求追回奖金，总计 405,000 两，据称由美亚银行公司、美亚金融公司和亚洲置业公司支付给他。其中两份诉状指控奖金交易不当且存在欺诈。

与此同时，据清算人称，清算这三家已倒闭机构以及重组亚洲置业公司（霍夫先生担任其受托人）的业务已发展成繁重的常规工作。

关于雷文先生发给他的公开信，信中攻击了据称由清算人在媒体上发表的言论，霍夫先生几乎未予置评，截至目前也未表现出有意回复这封信的迹象。他告知《字林西报》记者，他目前不打算向雷文先生发送公开信。

据悉，亚洲置业公司的审计工作已接近尾声，但昨日未能获悉何时可以期待看到有关该公司的财务报表。然而，众所周知，霍夫先生大幅削减了 overhead（间接费用/管理费用），以期从公司收入中实现一些实际现金，且受托人在这方面的工作取得了一定成功。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JULY 30, 1935
11295

Raven's Attorney Sends
Letter Of Protest To
Liquidator Of A.-O. Bank

Former Bank Head Reiterates That Failure Of His
Companies Was Due To Tight Money Market
And U.S. Silver Policy

MR. HOUGH CRITICIZED FOR PREJUDICING
REORGANIZATION OF ASIA REALTY CO.

A protest against allegations made publicly from time to time by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company, was made yesterday on behalf of Mr. Frank J. Raven and other officers of the three companies by Attorney Richard T. Evans, of Tientsin, in the form of an open letter addressed to the Liquidator and later released to the Press.

Issue is taken with the Liquidator specifically in regard to statements that the Raven companies were insolvent as far back as the beginning of 1932, when Mr. Raven, received from them honoraria totalling Tls. 405,000; the suggestion that Mr. Raven acted fraudulently in regard to at least one of these honoraria, and that the bankruptcy of the Raven companies was not due to the operation of President Roosevelt's Silver Purchase Act.

Apart from this, it is claimed that Mr. Hough's periodical statements have injured the prospects of reorganization of the Asia Realty Company, of which Mr. Hough is Trustee, while at the same time affecting adversely the work of liquidating the other three companies to the best advantage of the creditors.

Text Of Letter

Mr. Evans' letter, in full, is as follows:—

Frank L. Hough, Esquire,
Liquidator, American-Oriental
Banking Corporation,
29 Nanking Road,
Shanghai.
Dear Sir:
On behalf of Mr. Frank J. Raven and the other officers of the three companies in your charge, I venture respectfully to protest against the allegations which you have freely made in the public press concerning the conduct of the affairs of these companies. You have said that these companies have been insolvent for some time and that Mr. Raven and other officers must have known it. You have implied, even if you have not said it in so many words, that Mr. Raven at least has been guilty of fraud.

If you will take the trouble to look at the detailed statements of accounts of the four companies which were prepared at the end of December, 1934, and will compare the securities which were then listed and which were held by the various companies and ascertain the actual market quotations thereof at that time, you should be satisfied that all of these companies were solvent then. You have said more than once that the shares of stock in the Asia Realty Company are worthless, notwithstanding that this company is not insolvent and is assumed to be in process of reorganization. Such a statement made by you, the person in responsible charge of this company and an officer of the United States Court for China, has carried great weight and has seriously injured the prospect of reorganization. Not only has it injured the prospect of reorganization of this company, but by so doing it has also injured the possibility of the other three companies obtaining the same substantial return from their investment or loans against its securities which they would have obtained had you been more discreet.

U. S. Silver Policy

You have said that the failure of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation had nothing to do with tight money conditions in Shanghai and nothing to do with the silver situation which, admittedly, caused these tight money conditions. A large part of the capital and reserves of the Bank are stated in United States currency and the equivalent is stated in the balance sheet in local currency. About two and a half years ago the equivalent of these items in local currency was about double their value when the Bank closed. As the currency with which the Bank mainly deals is local currency, it was obvious that this meant a considerable shrinkage in the actual surplus of the Bank during this period. This was directly due to the United States monetary policy as the intrinsic value of silver in terms of gold bullion has not changed by more than 25 per cent. At the end of December, 1934, the Bank had capital and reserves in United States money of about one million dollars which at that time was worth approximately three million dollars, Shanghai currency. By the 23rd of May this one million, United States currency, had shrunk to less than two million four hundred thousand dollars, Shanghai currency. It is apparent from the accounts of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation that this Bank had more than two million dollars in actual cash either on hand or in other banks in December 31, 1934, forming over 20 per cent. on the deposits. Considering the money conditions which prevailed in Shanghai during the autumn of 1934 and the gradual worsening of these conditions towards the end of December, I think you will agree if you compare this reserve with the reserve of other banks in proportion to their deposits, that it was a higher percentage of cash as against deposits than was held by most of the banks, even the biggest ones.

That cash reserve became depleted as people began to withdraw their deposits. Many of the deposits in the other three companies which were for fixed terms would, under normal monetary conditions, have been renewed and the experience of these three companies has been over a period of years that something like 7 per cent. of their fixed deposits are renewed on expiration. Due to the very tight money conditions it was practically impossible to borrow during the winter of 1934 and 1935 from any bank in Shanghai even on the best of securities. It is not surprising, therefore, that these depositors required payment and would not renew. These companies, therefore, had to obtain funds as best they could to meet these deposits. Their assets were no less, their liabilities were no greater than they had been previously. They felt justified in applying to the American-Oriental Banking Corporation for accommodation against securities of these affiliates. Now it may be that a bank ought not to lend on the shares of any of its affiliates but that is quite another thing from saying that such lending is fraud and that it means that there is a condition of insolvency.

Responsible Men

The Directors of these companies are representative and responsible business men of Shanghai. It is not likely that they would lend their aid or countenance to the continuation in business of an insolvent concern or to any kind of fraud or misrepresentation.

I appreciate the difficulty and responsibility of your work and you deserve and should receive the co-operation of all concerned. I appreciate that it is your duty to be fearless and outspoken. With respect, I do not think it is your duty to make the comments which you have seen fit to make them in the public press concerning the former officials of these institutions.

I trust that you will give this letter serious consideration and that, in the future, in making statements to the public, if you feel justified in making statements to other than those directly interested, that you confine yourself to statements of strict fact and abstain from comment that is likely to cause injury to innocent people.

Yours very truly,
(Signed) RICHARD T. EVANS.

The letter was handed to press representatives personally by Mr. Frank J. Raven in the office of the Chocolate Shop, on Nanking Road. Mr. Raven's attorney returned to Tientsin on Saturday and is not expected to return to Shanghai until a date has been set for the hearing of the three suits filed against his client in the United States Court.

Contrary to earlier expectations, hearing is not likely to take place until September or October, it was learnt yesterday. The delay is necessary since both Dr. George Sellett, attorney for the Liquidator, and Mr. Richard T. Evans, attorney for Mr. Raven, require additional time in which to prepare their cases.

《字林西报》，1935年7月30日，星期二
11295

雷文（Raven）的律师向
美亚银行清算人递交抗议信

前银行负责人重申，其旗下公司倒闭系因银根紧缩
及美国白银政策所致

霍夫先生因损害亚洲地产公司重组前景而受批评

昨日，天津律师理查德·T·埃文斯（Richard T. Evans）代表弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生及其他三家公司的高级职员，以一封致清算人的公开信形式提出抗议，反对美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）及雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生不时公开发表的指控。该信随后向新闻界发布。

抗议主要针对清算人的以下言论：声称雷文旗下的公司早在1932年初就已资不抵债，当时雷文先生从这些公司收取了总计40.5万两白银的酬金；暗示雷文先生在至少其中一笔酬金问题上存在欺诈行为；以及声称雷文旗下公司的破产并非由于罗斯福总统的《白银收购法案》所致。

此外，信中称霍夫先生的定期声明损害了亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）的重组前景，霍夫先生是该公司的受托人；同时也对另外三家公司的清算工作产生了不利影响，未能使债权人获得最大利益。

信件全文

埃文斯先生的信件全文如下：——

弗兰克·L·霍夫 先生，
清算人，美亚银行，
南京路29号，
上海。

尊敬的先生：

我谨代表弗兰克·J·雷文先生及您负责监管的这三家公司的其他高级职员，冒昧对您就这些公司经营行为在公共报刊上随意发表的指控提出抗议。您曾说这些公司已资不抵债有一段时间，且雷文先生及其他高级职员必然知情。您甚至暗示（即便未明言），雷文先生至少犯有欺诈罪。

若您费心查阅这四家公司于1934年12月底编制的详细账目报表，并对比当时列出的由各公司持有的证券及其当时的实际市场报价，您应能确信这些公司在当时均具有偿债能力。您曾多次表示，尽管亚洲地产公司并未资不抵债，且被认为正处于重组过程中，但其股票毫无价值。身为该公司负责人及美国驻华法院官员的您发表此类言论，分量极重，已严重损害了重组的前景。这不仅损害了该公司的重组前景，而且因此也损害了其他三家公司从其投资或以其证券为抵押的贷款中获得同等实质回报的可能性，若您在言行上更为谨慎，它们本可获得这些回报。

美国白银政策

您曾表示，美亚银行的倒闭与上海的银根紧缩状况无关，也与造成这种银根紧缩的白银局势无关。该银行的大部分资本和准备金以美元列示，并在资产负债表中以当地货币列示等值金额。大约两年半前，这些项目以当地货币计算的等值金额约为银行停业时价值的两倍。由于该银行主要使用的货币是当地货币，显然这意味着在此期间银行的实际盈余大幅缩水。这直接归因于美国的货币政策，因为以金条计价的白银内在价值变化不超过25%。截至1934年12月底，该银行拥有约100万美元的美元资本和准备金，当时约合300万元上海币。到5月23日，这100万美元已缩水至不足240万元上海币。从美亚银行的账目可以明显看出，截至1934年12月31日，该银行手头或在其他银行的实际现金超过200万美元，占存款总额的20%以上。考虑到1934年秋季上海 prevailing 的货币状况以及直到12月底这些状况逐渐恶化，我想如果您将这一准备金与其他银行相对于其存款的准备金进行比较，您会同意，其现金对存款的比例高于大多数银行，即使是最大的银行。

随着人们开始提取存款，这一现金储备逐渐耗尽。在其他三家公司中，许多定期存款在正常的货币条件下本会续存，而这三年来的经验表明，约有7%的定期存款在到期时会续存。由于银根极度紧缩，在1934年和1935年的冬季，实际上不可能从上海的任何银行借到款项，即使提供最好的担保品也不例外。因此，这些储户要求提款而不愿续存也就不足为奇了。因此，这些公司不得不竭尽所能筹集资金以应付这些存款提取。它们的资产并未减少，负债也未比此前增加。它们认为有理由向美亚银行申请以其关联公司的证券为抵押的通融资金。现在，也许银行不应向其任何关联公司的股票提供贷款，但这与说此类贷款是欺诈行为，以及意味着存在资不抵债状况，完全是两回事。

负责任的人士

这些公司的董事都是上海具有代表性且负责任的商界人士。他们不太可能协助或纵容一家资不抵债的企业继续经营，或参与任何形式的欺诈或虚假陈述。

我理解您工作的困难和责任，您值得并应当得到所有相关方的合作。我理解您有无畏和直言不讳的职责。但我 respectfully 认为，在公共报刊上对这些机构的前任官员发表您所认为合适的评论，并非您的职责所在。

我希望您能认真考虑此信，并在将来向公众发表声明时，如果您认为有必要向非直接利害关系人发表声明，请仅限于陈述严格的事实，避免发表可能伤害无辜人士的评论。

您真诚的，
（签名）理查德·T·埃文斯

弗兰克·J·雷文先生在南京路的Chocolate Shop办公室亲自将这封信交给了新闻界代表。雷文先生的律师已于周六返回天津，预计在美国法院审理针对其当事人的三起诉讼的日期确定之前，不会返回上海。

据昨日获悉，与早先的预期相反，听证会可能要等到九月或十月才能举行。延期是必要的，因为清算人的律师乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士和雷文先生的律师理查德·T·埃文斯先生都需要额外的时间来准备他们的案件。

档案
JHS

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JULY 28, 1935

Reflections On Liquidator's
Findings Of A.-O. Bank

Perils That Ever Lurk In Independent Organizations
Existing Outside Bankers' Association;
Essential Safeguards Pointed Out

By ARTHUR & THEODORE SOPHER

Upon the legal aspects of a case sub judice, it would be improper to comment: the matter rests with the U. S. Court and will have to undergo the orderly process of legal administration. But there are other questions, of a fundamental nature, arising from the affairs of the four affiliated companies which bear on the conditions that have made possible such a serious situation, conditions which, if unaltered, would lead, through accumulating momentum, to greater "tragic loadings" than we now witness.

Inherent Unsoundness

In an article entitled "Joint Stock Corporations and Shanghai Crisis" published in these columns on Sunday, June 2, 1935, it is recorded that in the face of the chairman's statement laying blame for the Bank's failure on the U. S. Government's Silver Purchasing Plan, we stressed that the source of its troubles was rather to be found in the direction of unsound investments. A healthy constitution, properly treated, though subjected to the stress and strain of adverse circumstances, could not have met, under equal conditions, with the ugly fate of the A.-O. Bank. Mr. Hough, in his report of the liquidation, bears out our surmise by attributing the failure of the three companies not to bad external conditions, in which the U. S. Silver Policy figures largely, but to the fact that, for several years, the Bank had been unsound and, in his opinion, would have been forced into liquidation under business conditions generally favourable.

A Vital Qualification

Assuming that the President downwards to the lowest office employee were persons of the best of intentions, let us consider what the leaders and principal officers did have to confront in the course of business under conditions lawfully permitted them. A corporation is constituted legally in conformity with the laws of a certain state—one of the forty-eight United States—with whose laws the man on the street is generally unfamiliar—and ignorance of such codes or statutes is no plea for official consideration. The banking entity was not made a member of the Shanghai Bankers' Association—a qualification essential to public safety, and a fact not necessarily widely known.

Under the laws of a particular state, a company may operate in certain ways appropriate to the plan or scheme of the administering personnel. Every step taken by the company, bank, or trust may be duly and legally in accordance with what is "done"—of which the layman is in impenetrable ignorance. This is no fault of the organizers. In principle, company "A" is lawfully permitted to invest in corporation "B" who may invest in "C" and so on ad lib. And, what is more, it is allowable that "A," "B," and "C" be closely related, affiliated or interlocked.

Pyramidal Principle

Further, officer or officers in charge of investments in "A" are permitted to be officers in "B," and again in "C." The principle of strong structures is to build from a broad base and solid foundation and to taper upwards—pyramidal. The opposite of such a principle of development is commonly known as "pyramid-ing," meaning the inverted pyramid where you start from a point and broaden upwards as you go—always top-heavy. Mark you—the law—the particular statute of a certain state—allows it. When the untoward event occurs and the victim gnashes his teeth and is madly abusive or even becomes tragically insane, nothing avails. In demoralizing impotence he beholds the legal machinery tardily roll on.

By these same laws the officers can carry out any scheme and, in effect, dispose of the moneys in any way they desire. Let us suppose that officer in charge of company "A" has opened another company "B" in which he has part or major interest. What judgment, with the best of all intentions and on the most ethical grounds—what judgment short of the divine can decide correctly as to the soundness or not of such investment? It is like the left hand desiring to borrow from the right, and you expect the right hand to be absolutely unbiased in its judgment towards the left. The investor is called upon to divorce his mind from personal interest absolutely and to rule against himself whenever necessary. The natural tendency of self-preservation is bound to distort such judgment, and errors are, therefore, highly probable. Herein lies the worst feature of the operating conditions. And any initial success in "profits" step by step leads on to an increasingly deceptive course, not necessarily due to immoral conduct but per se since the law allows it. Through fortuitous events such an organization may, in practice, come out with flying colours, but in repeated action, over long periods, the chances of meeting with a crack become increasingly likely. In such event, the larger the top-heavy structure, the easier the collapse.

Automatic Protection

As it is far simpler to institute safeguards through active rulings rather than seek processes of developing human nature and judgment, a system, which shall work by routine and afford more or less mechanical protection, is highly desirable.

Before touching upon these constructive measures, emphasis must be laid on the dangers that may arise from independent organizations on whose statements the public relies. They are those competent authorities that issue a business entity's bill of health. Judging from the case in hand, the audits of accounts circulated among the public, instead of being of value in guidance, through the weight of their authority, have preserved public confidence intact, which shows that the real condition of an organization can escape the detection of auditors, and measures in protection of the public and the auditors themselves form a separate channel for improvements in legislation. In this connection, it would be desirable for auditors to take their instructions not from individual concerns but from the government, to whom the company should apply for an audit, the cost of which should be paid to the government as, in the final outturn, the public in its distress looks to the government for aid. The auditor need not, therefore, be concerned over the company's favour or disfavour.

Touching upon safeguards, no bank should be permitted to operate which is not a member of the Shanghai Bankers' Association. There should be complete and thorough inspection of a bank's assets by the Government, as in the case of the life insurance companies. Every bank official should not be permitted to have personal investments and a bank should be utterly divorced from subsidiary companies in which it holds an interest. It should be obligatory on bankers to take oath to that effect.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1935年7月28日

关于清算人对亚细亚-欧美银行（A.-O. Bank）调查结果的思考

独立于银行公会之外的组织所潜藏的危机；
指出必要的保障措施

作者：阿瑟·索珀（Arthur Sopher）与西奥多·索珀（Theodore Sopher）

鉴于案件尚在审理中，对其法律层面发表评论是不妥当的：此事由美国法院管辖，必须经历有序的法律程序。但是，从这四家附属公司的事务中，还产生了一些根本性质的其他问题，这些问题关系到造成如此严重局面的条件；如果这些条件不加以改变，随着势头的积累，将导致比我们要目前所见更为严重的“悲剧性负担”。

固有的不健全

在1935年6月2日（星期日）本刊刊登的题为《股份公司与上海危机》的文章中，曾记载道：面对董事长将银行倒闭归咎于美国政府购银计划的声明，我们强调，其困境的根源更在于不良投资的方向。一个健康的体制，若得到妥善对待，即使遭受逆境的压力和张力，在同等条件下也不至于遭遇亚细亚-欧美银行那样的悲惨命运。霍夫（Hough）先生在清算报告中证实了我们的推测，他将这三家公司的失败归因于该银行多年来一直经营不善，而非归因于恶劣的外部环境（其中美国白银政策占很大比重）；在他看来，即使在总体有利的商业条件下，该银行也会被迫进行清算。

一项至关重要的限定条件

假设从总裁到最底层的办公室职员都怀着最好的意图，让我们考虑一下领导层和主要官员在法律允许的条件下，在业务过程中不得不面对的情况。一家公司是依照某个州——美国四十八个州之一——的法律合法组建的，而普通大众通常不熟悉这些法律，且对这类法典或法规的无知并不能作为请求官方宽恕的理由。该银行实体并未成为上海银行公会的会员——这是关乎公共安全的一项必要资格，而这一事实未必广为人知。

根据特定州的法律，公司可以按照管理人员的计划或方案以某些方式运营。公司、银行或信托所采取的每一步骤，都可能完全且合法地符合其所“做”之事——而外行对此却一无所知。这并非组织者的过错。原则上，法律允许“A”公司投资于“B”公司，后者又可投资于“C”公司，以此类推，随心所欲。而且，更甚者，“A”、“B”和“C”之间可以是紧密相关、附属或相互连锁的，这也是允许的。

金字塔原则

此外，负责“A”公司投资的官员也被允许担任“B”公司乃至“C”公司的官员。稳固结构的原则是从宽阔的基础和坚实的地基开始，向上逐渐变细——即金字塔形。与此发展原则相反的做法通常被称为“金字塔式构建”（pyramid-ing），意指倒置的金字塔，即从一点开始，随着进程向上拓宽——始终头重脚轻。请注意——法律——即某个州的特定法规——是允许这样做的。当不幸事件发生，受害者咬牙切齿、疯狂咒骂，甚至陷入悲剧性的疯狂时，一切都无济于事。他在士气低落的无力感中，目睹法律机器迟缓地运转。

依据同样的法律，官员们可以执行任何计划，并实际上随意处置资金。让我们假设负责“A”公司的官员开设了另一家“B”公司，他在其中拥有部分或大部分利益。凭借最好的意图和最道德的立场——除了神明的判断之外，还有什么判断能正确决定此类投资是否健全？这就像左手想向右手借钱，而你期望右手在对左手的判断上保持绝对公正。投资者被要求将其思想与个人利益彻底分离，并在必要时做出不利于自己的裁决。自我保护的自然倾向必然会扭曲这种判断，因此错误极有可能发生。这正是运营条件中最糟糕的特征。而在“利润”上的任何初步成功，都会一步步引向越来越具有欺骗性的道路，这不一定源于不道德行为，而是因其本身被法律所允许。通过偶然事件，这样的组织在实践中可能会取得辉煌的成功，但在长期的反复操作中，遭遇破裂的可能性越来越大。在这种情况下，头重脚轻的结构越大，倒塌就越容易。

自动保护

由于通过主动裁决来建立保障措施，远比寻求发展人性和判断力的过程简单得多，因此，一个能够通过常规运作并提供或多或少机械化保护的系统是非常可取的。

在探讨这些建设性措施之前，必须强调那些公众依赖其陈述的独立组织可能带来的危险。它们是签发商业实体“健康证明”的主管当局。从本案来看，在公众中流传的账目审计报告，非但未能凭借其权威性起到指导价值，反而维持了公众信心的完好无损，这表明组织的真实状况可能逃过审计员的察觉，而保护公众及审计员自身的措施构成了立法改进的一个独立渠道。在这方面，审计员最好不从个别企业那里接受指令，而是从政府那里接受指令；公司应向政府申请审计，费用支付给政府，因为最终在困境中，公众是向政府寻求援助的。因此，审计员无需担心公司的喜好或厌恶。

谈及保障措施，任何非上海银行公会成员的银行均不得获准运营。政府应对银行资产进行全面彻底的检查，如同对人寿保险公司所做的那样。任何银行官员均不得拥有个人投资，银行应与其持有利益的附属公司彻底脱钩。银行家应有义务就此宣誓。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, JULY 26, 1935
11270
A-O. BANK PRESIDENT'S
ANSWER TO CHARGES

Denies Personal Control in Recent Years: Special
Remuneration Not Asked for or Suggested

HAD NO INTENTION OF LEAVING CHINA

Directors Elected by Stockholders and Exercised
Independent Judgment and Discretion

MR. Frank J. Raven, formerly president of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, the Asia Realty Company, and the Raven Trust Company, late yesterday afternoon, in the United States Court for China, answered the bill of complaint filed by Mr. Frank L. Hough, the liquidator, on June 29.

Mr. Raven denied Mr. Hough's two principal charges, which were that the Bank has been insolvent since December 31, 1931, and that Mr. Raven owes the Bank the sum of Tls. 135,000, which he received in January, 1932, as an honorarium. He stated that at the time the Bank was solvent, and that its shares were quoted then and for some time after on the Shanghai market at twice their par value. He also stated that he repaid the Tls. 135,000 to the Raven Trust Company on February 9, 1933

He stated that the bill of ne exeat served on him was unnecessary, as he had at no time had the intention of leaving China and the jurisdiction of the United States Court.

Following is the gist of Mr. Raven's answers, these being practically identical in each of the three cases—the American-Oriental Bank, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Asia Realty Company:—

Defendant admits that during all of the period of five years last past, the defendant has owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock of the Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A., a corporation, and admits that the said corporation now owns and controls and during all of said period owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock in the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc., U.S.A., a corporation, and admits that the said corporation now owns and controls and during all of said period owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock in the American Oriental Banking Corporation, but defendant denies that during all or any of the period of five years last the defendant has controlled the Bank.

Defendant denies the allegations of Paragraph 5 and alleges that the assets of the Bank on January 12, 1932, were more than twice its liabilities, excluding its capital stock, surpluses and undivided profits and that the cash on hand and in banks on that date was approximately 44 per cent. of all deposits, and that its shares of stock were then and for some time thereafter currently quoted on the Shanghai market at more than twice their par value.

Control Denied

Defendant admits the allegations of Paragraph 6, except that defendant denies that he controlled the Bank on January 12, 1932, for the reason that the directors of the Bank were elected at all material times by the stockholders thereof with the sole object of obtaining men of representative character and ability, and the defendant never at any time voted his own shares or caused the Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A., to vote its shares in the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc. U.S.A., for the purpose of electing or opposing the election of any candidate otherwise than for the purpose aforesaid, and the said directors at all material times exercised their independent judgment and discretion without any control, direct or indirect, of the defendant, and the defendant denies that he was present when the resolution referred to was discussed and passed, though he was present when the meeting referred to commenced. The defendant did not know prior to the meeting of January 12, 1932, that the subject of the payment of T135,000, referred to in Paragraph 6 aforesaid was under consideration, and the defendant neither asked nor suggested that said remuneration be paid to him and he had no knowledge thereof until the resolution referred to was communicated to him after the meeting aforesaid. The defendant paid the said sum of T135,000 to the Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A., as a donation for the purpose of increasing its liquid capital and the defendant did not then or at any time use the said sum of T135,000 or any part thereof for his personal benefit.

Expense Allowances

As to the allegations of Paragraph 7, defendant admits that he received the monthly sums and bonus as stated in said paragraph, but alleges that these were received and receipted for as expense allowance and not as salary, and defendant denies each and every other allegation of the said paragraph. The Bank was organized in the year 1917 and the defendant was the promoter and organizer thereof, but the defendant received no compensation at that time or at any time prior to January 12, 1932, for his services as promoter and organizer. The defendant acted actively and continuously as an officer of the Bank and as organizer of its affairs without any compensation other than payment of Tls. 135,000 above referred to for about 10 years after the organization of the Bank and it was well understood between the defendant and the directors that he would receive compensation for his services as promoter and organizer of the Bank and in respect of his many acts of service in bringing the Bank to prosperity when the circumstances of the Bank would warrant a reasonable payment, and in all the circumstances the payment made was reasonable.

By way of special defence, defendant alleges that any claim which the plaintiff may have by reason of the premises, is barred by the laches of the Bank in that a period of more than three years has elapsed since January 12, 1932, when the plaintiff alleges that said amount was due and repayable by the Defendant to the Bank.

No Intention To Leave

By way of defence to the application for writ of ne exeat issued herein on June 29, 1935, defendant alleges that said writ was issued without notice to him and without a hearing; that the application therefore was made by the plaintiff heedlessly and without any knowledge sufficient to found a belief that the defendant was about to depart quickly from the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court. The defendant had in fact informed the plaintiff that he would not leave the jurisdiction of this Court until the affairs of the Bank, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, the Raven Trust Company, and the Asia Realty Company were in such shape that the liquidator should consider that the defendant could go from China if he wished. The defendant expressly stated to the liquidator that he would not leave the jurisdiction of this Court at this time because his absence might be misinterpreted by some persons. The said writ was at the instance of the plaintiff served on the defendant at 10 minutes before midnight on June 29, 1935, and said service was harsh and oppressive and in violation of the Plaintiff's rights.

Wherefore the defendant prays that the Bill of Complaint herein may be dismissed at the plaintiff's costs, and the writ of ne exeat discharged without prejudice to the plaintiff's right to take such action as he may be advised in respect of any claim for damages in the matter of the alleged wrongful application for the writ of ne exeat.

《字林西报》，1935年7月26日，星期五
11270
美亚银行行长对指控的答复

否认近年来的个人控制：未索取或建议支付特别酬金

无意离开中国

董事由股东选举产生，并行使独立的判断力和裁量权

弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生，前美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）、亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）及雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）总裁，于昨日下午在美国驻华法院，就清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生于6月29日提交的诉状进行了答辩。

雷文先生否认了霍夫先生的两项主要指控，即银行自1931年12月31日起已资不抵债，以及雷文先生欠银行规平银135,000两，该款项是他于1932年1月作为酬金收取的。他表示，当时银行具有偿付能力，其股票在上海市场的报价当时及此后一段时间内均为面值的两倍。他还表示，他已于1933年2月9日将规平银135,000两偿还给雷文信托公司。

他表示，向他送达的禁止出境令（writ of ne exeat）是不必要的，因为他从未有过离开中国及美国法院管辖范围的意图。

以下是雷文先生答辩要点，这三起案件——美亚银行、美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司——的答辩内容基本相同：—

被告承认，在过去五年的整个期间，被告拥有并控制了美国联邦注册公司雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A.）的多数表决权股票，并承认该公司目前拥有并控制，且在上述整个期间内拥有并控制了美国联邦注册公司美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc., U.S.A.）的多数表决权股票，并承认该公司目前拥有并控制，且在上述整个期间内拥有并控制了美亚银行公司（American Oriental Banking Corporation）的多数表决权股票，但被告否认在过去五年中的任何或全部期间内被告控制了该银行。

被告否认第5段的指控，并声称截至1932年1月12日，银行的资产超过其负债的两倍以上（不包括其股本、盈余和未分配利润），且当日的手头现金及银行存款约占所有存款的44%，其股票在当时及此后一段时间内在上海市场的现行报价均超过面值的两倍。

否认控制

被告承认第6段的指控，但被告否认其于1932年1月12日控制了该银行，理由是银行的董事在所有关键时期均由其股东选举产生，唯一目的是选拔具有代表性和才干的人士，且被告从未在任何时候为了选举或反对选举任何候选人以外的目的，亲自投票或其促使美国联邦注册公司雷文信托公司在美国联邦注册公司美亚金融公司中投票，所述董事在所有关键时期均行使独立的判断力和裁量权，不受被告的任何直接或间接控制，被告否认在讨论并通过所指决议时他在场，尽管在所指会议开始时他在场。在1932年1月12日的会议之前，被告不知道上述第6段中提到的支付规平银135,000两的事项正在考虑之中，被告既未要求也未建议向其支付该笔酬金，直到上述会议后将所指决议通知他时，他才得知此事。被告将所述规平银135,000两作为捐赠支付给美国联邦注册公司雷文信托公司，以增加其流动资本，被告当时或任何时候均未将该笔规平银135,000两或其任何部分用于个人利益。

津贴费用

关于第7段的指控，被告承认他收到了该段所述的每月款项和奖金，但声称这些款项是作为费用津贴接收并开具收据的，而非作为薪水，被告否认该段中的每一项其他指控。该银行成立于1917年，被告是其发起人和组织者，但被告在当时或1932年1月12日之前的任何时间，均未因其作为发起人和组织者的服务而获得报酬。在银行成立后的约10年里，被告积极且持续地担任银行高管并组织其事务，除上述提到的规平银135,000两外，未获得任何其他报酬，且被告与董事之间达成明确共识，即当银行状况允许合理支付时，他将因其作为银行发起人和组织者的服务以及在使银行走向繁荣方面的诸多服务行为获得报酬，在所有情况下，所支付的款项是合理的。

作为特别抗辩，被告声称，原告因前述事项可能拥有的任何索赔，均因银行的懈怠（laches）而被禁止，因为自1932年1月12日（原告声称被告当时欠银行该笔款项并应偿还）以来，已超过三年时间。

无意离开

针对1935年6月29日在此签发的禁止出境令申请，被告辩称，该令状是在未通知他且未经听证的情况下签发的；因此，原告的申请是轻率的，且缺乏足以形成被告即将迅速离开本庭管辖范围之信念的必要知识。事实上，被告已告知原告，在银行、美亚金融公司、雷文信托公司和亚洲地产公司的事务达到清算人认为被告可以随意离开中国的程度之前，他不会离开本庭的管辖范围。被告向清算人明确表示，他此时不会离开本庭的管辖范围，因为他的缺席可能会被某些人误解。所述令状应原告请求，于1935年6月29日午夜前10分钟送达被告，该送达方式严厉且具有压迫性，违反了原告的权利。

因此，被告请求驳回本诉状，费用由原告承担，并解除禁止出境令，但不损害原告就所谓错误申请禁止出境令一事所获建议的任何损害赔偿索赔采取行动的權利。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 24, 1935 11262

JUDICIAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
6740
25 / 7 / 35

LEGAL SIDE OF
A.O.B.C. FAILURE
BEING EXAMINED

Many Complications Seen in
Present Position

AMERICAN AUTHORITIES
WATCHING CASE

SPECIAL TO THE "N.-C.D.N."

The "North-China Daily News" understands that the American authorities have under active examination the reports received from the Liquidator regarding the affairs of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation and associated companies. Among this material will be the data which formed the basis of Mr. F. L. Hough's statement to the press on Saturday last.

The work involved in ascertaining the legal position is great. Mr. Hough took pains to point out that the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was not constituted so that its operations would come under the control of the United States banking laws. This does not imply that the Corporation's affairs will not come within the purview of American law as a whole, but it does throw light on the complexities involved. In handling a matter of this kind the responsible authorities have to proceed with great caution if justice has to be done. The machinery of the law has to be very carefully studied, and in particular the conditions prevailing in regard to the trading of American companies in China have to be carefully examined. Precedents are not copious.

Legal Aspect Examined

For all these reasons, although the layman may feel impatient, there is no cause to imagine that the responsible authorities are neglectful of their duties. On the contrary, the Liquidator and Auditor and their respective staffs have been zealously unravelling the affairs of the concerns in liquidation. Similarly, the legal staff of the United States in Shanghai is engaged in a thorough investigation of the lines of action which the circumstances suggest should be taken. It is important to realize that, in a sense, the whole matter is sub judice and the responsible law officers are, therefore, very properly debarred from making preliminary statements until they are fully equipped with knowledge of the most correct method of procedure to be adopted in conformity with American law.

While, therefore, some time may elapse before further developments are made known, the public can rest assured that the officials charged with these important duties are fully alive to the needs of the situation and are assiduously applying their energies accordingly. It is impossible for these officials at this stage to be more specific, for, let it be repeated, the whole of the case is sub judice. They have, moreover, to consider that whatever action is taken it will have to stand the test of judicial review both here and, perhaps, in America.

《字林西报》，1935年7月24日，星期三 11262

司法警察
S. B. 登记处。
6740
35年7月25日

美亚银行倒闭的
法律层面
正在审查中

当前局势中发现
许多复杂情况

美国当局
关注此案

《字林西报》专讯

《字林西报》获悉，美国当局正在积极审查从清算人那里收到的关于美亚银行公司及相关公司事务的报告。在这些材料中，将包括构成霍夫（F. L. Hough）先生上周六向媒体发表声明基础的数据。

查明法律地位所涉及的工作量巨大。霍夫先生特意指出，美亚银行公司的组建方式使其运营不受美国银行法的控制。这并不意味着该公司的业务完全不在美国法律的管辖范围内，但这确实揭示了其中涉及的复杂性。在处理此类事务时，如果要做到公正，主管当局必须非常谨慎。必须仔细研究法律机制，特别是要仔细审查美国公司在中国贸易的相关条件。先例并不多见。

审查法律方面

出于所有这些原因，尽管外行可能会感到不耐烦，但没有理由认为主管当局疏忽职守。相反，清算人和审计师及其各自的工作人员一直在热情地梳理处于清算中的各公司的事务。同样，美国驻上海的法律工作人员正在全面调查根据情况建议应采取的行动路线。重要的是要认识到，从某种意义上说，整个案件尚在审理中（sub judice），因此，主管法律官员非常正当地被禁止在完全掌握符合美国法律的正确程序方法之前发表初步声明。

因此，虽然可能需要一段时间才能公布进一步进展，但公众可以放心，负责这些重要职责的官员充分意识到局势的需求，并正在为此勤勉地投入精力。在此阶段，这些官员不可能更具体地说明，因为需要重申，整个案件尚在审理中。此外，他们还必须考虑到，无论采取何种行动，都必须经受住这里以及可能在美国的司法审查的考验。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 25, 1935

Knotty Points
To The Editor:
Refusal of Mr. Hough's statements appearing in the public press yesterday confirms one's worst fears re the prospect, or rather lack of prospect of creditors recovering anything from the Raven companies. It certainly is not palatable to read of worthless loans, uncollectable loans and loans without security carried as assets in the accounts of the AOBC.
I am sure that all depositors and creditors who stand to lose, would like elucidation on a few knotty points concerning the failure of these companies. Perhaps Mr. Hough despite the fact that he is a very busy man, will spare a few minutes to explain.
Re these "worthless" loans, what is the position of the Bank's auditors who certified the last financial statement before the crash? Can they be held liable in any way for certifying the accounts when the assets are padded with "worthless" items?
Re the several suits filed by Mr. Hough against Mr. F. J. Raven seeking recovery of bonus he collected from his companies, what is the position of the directors of those companies who voted the payments to Mr. Raven? In the several suits against Mr. Raven those bonuses are alleged to be illegal. Are not the directors in an equally vulnerable position for voting and passing such "illegal" payments? Be it remembered that the directors of these companies are all men of standing in this community and if they can be held legally liable in any way for the sorry position of these companies, justice demands that they pay for their negligence and mistakes, if not voluntarily then by due process of law. Or is the law as sympathetic to such directors as it is lenient to a company whose accounts can be padded up ad lib. with worthless assets?
There is a further interesting point in connection with directors. There is at least one director of these companies who is of Chinese nationality. Under Chinese law directors are liable for liquidation in full of a company's debts. Can the aid of Chinese law be invoked in the case of this particular individual? or is he protected by reason of the American registry of these companies?
Yours etc.
FLEECED
Shanghai July 22, 1935.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年7月25日，星期四

棘手问题
致编辑：
霍夫先生（Mr. Hough）拒绝就昨日见诸报端的声明发表评论，这证实了人们最担心的情况，即债权人从雷文（Raven）各公司收回任何款项的前景渺茫，或者说根本无望。读到美亚银行（AOBC）的账目中将毫无价值的贷款、无法收回的贷款以及无担保贷款列为资产，确实令人难以接受。
我相信，所有面临损失的储户和债权人都希望澄清有关这些公司倒闭的几个棘手问题。也许霍夫先生尽管公务繁忙，仍能抽出几分钟时间予以解释。
关于这些“毫无价值”的贷款，在崩溃前认证最后一份财务报表的银行审计师处于何种地位？当资产中掺入“毫无价值”的项目时，他们是否需为认证账目承担任何责任？
关于霍夫先生对F. J. 雷文先生（Mr. F. J. Raven）提起的几起诉讼，旨在追回雷文从其公司收取的奖金，那些投票决定向雷文支付款项的公司董事处于何种地位？在对雷文先生的几起诉讼中，据称这些奖金是非法的。那些投票并通过此类“非法”支付的董事，难道不是处于同样脆弱的境地吗？请记住，这些公司的董事都是本社区中有地位的人士，如果他们因这些公司的糟糕状况而在法律上承担任何责任，正义要求他们为自己的疏忽和错误付出代价，如果不是自愿的话，则通过正当法律程序强制执行。还是说，法律对这些董事的同情，就像它对那些可以随意用毫无价值的资产虚增账目的公司所表现出的宽容一样？
关于董事还有一个有趣的要点。这些公司的董事中至少有一位是中国国籍。根据中国法律，董事对公司债务的清算承担全部责任。在此特定个人的案件中，能否援引中国法律的援助？或者他是否因这些公司在美国注册而受到保护？
此致
敬礼
受欺者（FLEECED）
上海，1935年7月22日。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JULY 27, 1932

Amended Complaint Against
Former A.-O. Bank Head

Liquidator Discloses That Mr. Raven Received
Considerable Salary From Bank Prior To
Getting Tls. 135,000 As Honorarium

An amended Bill of Complaint was filed in the United States Court for China yesterday by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, in the suit entered at the end of June against Mr. Frank J. Raven, President of the Corporation, for recovery of Tls. 135,000 paid to him on January 13, 1932 as an honorarium by the Corporation.

It is shown in the amended Bill that Mr. Raven was in receipt of substantial sums as salary prior to the payment of the honorarium. From June 1, 1928 to December 31, 1929, it is stated, he received from the Corporation a regular monthly salary of $750. During 1930 he received $1,000 per month and at the end of 1930, in addition thereto, a bonus of $1,800. During 1931, Mr. Raven's regular monthly salary was $1,500.

Hence, the Liquidator contends, the Corporation was not obligated to Mr. Raven for any services performed by him. Mr. Raven is therefore obligated, "in equity and good conscience," to immediately repay to the Corporation the sum of Tls. 135,000 received by him.

Knew Bank Was Insolvent

The complaint of the Liquidator is further buttressed by the assertion that, at the time the honorarium was voted and received by Mr. Raven, the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was insolvent and that Mr. Raven knew it to be insolvent.

In addition to the suit for recovery of the Tls. 135,000 paid to Mr. Raven by the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, two further suits for the recovery of similar sums voted to him by the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Asia Realty Company are awaiting trial in the United States Court.

No answer to the complaints has as yet been filed by Mr. Raven. As soon as this is done, it is expected that a date will be set for the hearing of the actions.

《字林西报》，1932年7月27日，星期三

针对前美亚银行行长的
修订起诉状

清算人披露，雷文先生在获得13.5万两酬金之前
已从银行领取可观薪水

已停业的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生（Mr. Frank L. Hough），于昨日在美国驻华法院提交了一份修订后的起诉状。该诉讼于6月底提起，被告为该公司总裁弗兰克·J. 雷文先生（Mr. Frank J. Raven），旨在追回公司于1932年1月13日作为酬金支付给他的13.5万两白银。

修订后的起诉状显示，在支付酬金之前，雷文先生一直领取巨额薪水。诉称，从1928年6月1日至1929年12月31日，他从公司领取每月750美元的固定薪水。1930年间，他每月领取1,000美元，并在1930年底额外获得1,800美元的奖金。1931年期间，雷文先生的固定月薪为1,500美元。

因此，清算人主张，公司并不欠雷文先生任何因其提供服务而产生的债务。因此，雷文先生“基于公平和良知”，有义务立即向公司偿还其收到的13.5万两白银。

明知银行资不抵债

清算人的指控还得到以下断言的支持：即在雷文先生投票决定并接收酬金时，美亚银行公司已资不抵债，且雷文先生对此知情。

除了起诉追回美亚银行公司支付给雷文先生的13.5万两白银外，还有两起旨在追回美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）和亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）投票决定支付给他的类似款项的诉讼，正待美国法院审理。

雷文先生尚未对起诉状作出答辩。预计一旦提交答辩，法院将设定听证日期。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JULY 22, 1935
1123J

THE LIQUIDATION

The Creditors of the American Oriental Banking Corporation will derive small comfort from the statement issued on Saturday by Mr. Frank L. Hough who was appointed Liquidator of that Corporation and its associate concerns on June 3 by order of Judge Milton J. Helmick. The Corporation, on May 24, in announcing its decision to close its doors and apply to the Court for Liquidation, declared that the business depression was responsible for the closure and that, in the opinion of the Directors and Officers,

it would be in the best interest of the depositors to liquidate the bank at this time when it is believed that all depositors in an orderly liquidation will receive 100 per cent. of the deposits.

In the light of the disclosures now made by the Liquidator this statement appears to have been based on excessively optimistic views. Within ten days of his appointment Mr. Hough, on June 13, issued a preliminary review of the state of of the accounts of the American Oriental Banking Corporation, the American Oriental Finance Corporation and the Raven Trust Company as shown by the books on May 23, the last day of business and as compiled by Mr. Henry S. De Vault, the certified public accountant who was appointed to assist the Liquidator on June 5 and took over charge on June 6. That preliminary statement showed that the affairs of the three companies were much interlocked and involved. Its presentation was accompanied by comments which suggested that the Liquidator took a gloomy view of the position. On June 29, it was announced that a writ of ne exeat had been filed in the U. S. Court against Mr. F. J. Raven who was also made the subject of a bill of complaint filed in the same Court by the Liquidator in respect of certain moneys. The Court prescribed a security of U.S. $20,000 to cover the writ of ne exeat; that security was duly furnished by the joint and several guarantee of three American citizens on July 1. Meanwhile Judge Milton J. Helmick was called by judicial duty to Peiping, whence he returned last week. Now the Liquidator has made the further statement which appeared in this journal yesterday.

Briefly that statement, after refuting the notion that the failure could in any way be attributed to the silver policy of the American Government, summarized the position of the three concerns. The American Oriental Banking Corporation was declared to have carried as assets loans to affiliated companies which "were worthless." The condition of the three companies was described as having been "for several years unsound" and Mr. Hough felt that "liquidation would have been forced even if general business conditions were good." Mr. Hough proceeded to add "The Raven Trust Company will have little, if anything, to offer to the creditors" and "The Finance

Corporation presents a problem and very little be available to the creditors." Within the next two months the Liquidator expects to be able to issue Mr. De Vault's analysis of the exact position of the three companies. The work of liquidation is exceedingly complicated. by the peculiar circumstances of the companies' organization and by the prevalent market conditions. It is evident that both the Liquidator and the Auditor are tackling the problem with expedition and zeal. It is re-

grettable to think that their labours, as far as can be judged from these statements, are not likely to bring much material relief to a large number of unfortunate victims of this unhappy disaster.

This is not the time to attempt the formulation of definite conclusions regarding the causes which led to this failure. To begin with the complete statement of figures which will be forthcoming in Mr. De Vault's analysis, is essential to such an endeavour. Then it will be realized that certain proceedings are pending in various courts. It is almost impossible satisfactorily to draw deductions or form opinion on the statements now made without appearing, in some degree, to be prejudicing those proceedings. Mr. Hough's statement deserves, however, the compliment of notice in certain respects. It disposes summarily—and, as this Journal all along has insisted, rightly—of the contention that the silver purchase policy of the United States of America should bear some of the blame for the plight of the Raven companies. Where the blame actually lies it is neither fitting nor possible at this juncture to say. It is obvious, however, that even the most purblind critic of Washington's silver programme cannot find material for his comfort here. Mr. Hough also makes it clear that the American Oriental Banking Corporation has no special American characteristic, beyond its registration, the nationality of its President and the jurisdiction under which its operations come by reason of its extraterritorial status. Here this journal would reiterate the view expressed when this casualty was first reported:

This difficulty should be met in an international spirit. Nationalities are of no account......What may happen to the Utopian Shanghai-lander to-day may quite easily overcome the Laputan Shanghai-lander to-morrow.

Those words were written without knowledge of the facts since brought to light in the course of liquidation. They still remain as deserving of attention, in view of Mr. Hough's remarks. Under the direction of a competent and independent Judge, Mr. Hough and his colleague are carrying out a delicate and difficult task. They have behind them the complete confidence of Shanghai business men and they can be trusted to do their duty, unpleasant or pleasant, in fulfilment of their obligations to the creditors and to the laws of the country which they have sworn to serve.

清算工作

美亚银行公司的债权人从弗兰克·L. 霍夫先生（Mr. Frank L. Hough）周六发表的声明中得到的安慰寥寥无几。霍夫先生于6月3日奉米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官（Judge Milton J. Helmick）之命，被任命为该公司及其关联机构的清算人。该公司在5月24日宣布决定停业并向法院申请清算时声称，商业萧条是导致停业的原因，并且董事和高级管理人员认为，

此时进行银行清算最符合储户的利益，相信在有序清算下，所有储户将获得100%的存款偿付。

鉴于清算人现在披露的情况，该声明似乎基于过度乐观的观点。霍夫先生在受任后十天内，即6月13日，发布了美亚银行公司、美亚金融公司和雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）账户状况的初步审查报告。该报告依据的是5月23日（最后一个营业日）的账簿记录，由注册会计师亨利·S. 德沃尔特先生（Mr. Henry S. De Vault）编制。德沃尔特先生于6月5日被任命协助清算人，并于6月6日接管工作。该初步报告显示，这三家公司的事务相互交织且错综复杂。报告的发布伴随着一些评论，暗示清算人对局势持悲观看法。6月29日，宣布已在美国法院对F. J. 雷文先生发出禁止出境令（writ of ne exeat），同时清算人在同一法院就某些款项问题对雷文先生提起了起诉状。法院规定需提供2万美元保证金以执行禁止出境令；该保证金已于7月1日由三位美国公民提供连带担保 duly furnished。与此同时，米尔顿·J. 赫尔米克法官因司法职责前往北平，并于上周返回。现在，清算人发表了进一步声明，该声明见于本报昨日刊载。

简而言之，该声明在驳斥了将倒闭归咎于美国政府白银政策的说法后，总结了这三家机构的状况。美亚银行公司被指在其资产中列入了对关联公司的贷款，而这些贷款“毫无价值”。这三家公司的状况被描述为“多年来一直不健全”，霍夫先生认为，“即使总体商业状况良好，也不得不进行清算”。霍夫先生接着补充道：“雷文信托公司对债权人几乎没有什么可提供的，即便有也微乎其微”，而“金融公司则是一个难题，可供债权人分配的资产极少”。清算人预计在未来两个月内能够发布德沃尔特先生对这三家公司确切状况的分析。由于公司组织的特殊情况以及普遍的市场条件，清算工作极其复杂。显然，清算人和审计师正以迅速和热忱的态度处理这一问题。令人遗憾的是，从这些声明来看，他们的劳动恐怕无法给这场不幸灾难中的众多不幸受害者带来多少实质性的 relief。

现在并非试图就导致此次倒闭的原因得出明确结论的时候。首先，必须等待德沃尔特先生分析中将提供的完整数据陈述，这对于此类努力至关重要。此外，还需意识到某些诉讼程序正在各级法院进行中。如果不以某种方式显得偏颇从而影响这些诉讼程序，几乎不可能满意地根据目前的声明进行推断或形成意见。然而，霍夫先生的声明在某些方面值得注意。它简洁地——正如本报一贯坚持的那样，正确地——驳斥了这样一种论点，即美国的白银收购政策应对雷文各公司的困境承担部分责任。至于责任究竟何在，在此时既不合宜也不可能说明。然而，显而易见的是，即使是对华盛顿白银计划最视而不见的批评者，也无法从中找到任何自我安慰的依据。霍夫先生还明确指出，除了其注册地、总裁的国籍以及因其治外法权地位而适用的管辖权之外，美亚银行公司并没有特殊的美国特征。在此，本报重申首次报道这一事件时所表达的观点：

应以国际精神来应对这一困难。国籍无关紧要……今天发生在乌托邦式上海人身上的事，明天很可能也会发生在拉普塔式上海人身上。

写下这些话时，我们尚不了解清算过程中揭露的事实。鉴于霍夫先生的言论，这些话仍然值得关注。在一位能干且独立的法官的指导下，霍夫先生及其同事正在执行一项微妙而艰巨的任务。他们背后有着上海商界人士的完全信任，可以信赖他们会履行职责，无论愉快与否，以履行其对债权人的义务以及对其宣誓效忠的国家法律的义务。
