THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JULY 22, 1935

PREVENTION FOR THE
FUTURE

THANKS to Mr. Frank L.
Hough, liquidator for the
Raven enterprises, the public has
been enlightened on their true
state of affairs. Though hopes for
appreciable recovery of funds in-
vested in or deposited with these
institutions are cruelly shattered,
a timely realization of actualities
may help soften the edge of dis-
appointment which would other-
wise grow keener in direct pro-
portion to prolonged anxious wait-
ing on the part of investors and
depositors.

The frank criticism by Mr.
Hough of the mismanagement of
Mr. Raven's companies, as report-
ed in this journal yesterday, is
deserving of official attention both
in Nanking and in Washington.
It is not our intention to constitute
ourselves judge and jury over the
legal battles now being staged in
the United States Court for China,
but sufficient revelation has been
made by Mr. Hough to warrant a
general demand for a much-needed
investigation of enterprises
similar, in nature if not in con-
duct, to the crumbled Raven
edifices. Particularly pertinent is
his pointed comment on the
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration which may be quoted here
to good profit:

I often hear the bank referred to
as an American bank, but it is true
that the bank happened to be esta-
blished by an American, but it was
not in any way affiliated with any
bank in the United States to the ex-
tent that its operations would have
been controlled by United States
Banking laws. Without a doubt,
thousands of people entrusted their
money to the bank with this impres-
sion in mind.

The impression which the ill-
informed public had the misfor-
tune to have created in its collec-
tive mind was undoubtedly the
protection which was presumably
obtainable from the periodic ex-
aminations of the bank by com-
petent American authorities. If
such an impression still persists, it
may be dispelled by Mr. Hough's
observations:

The American-Oriental Bank
could have thrown a United States
bank examiner out of the doors had
they desired, because they were not
operating under any law compelling
them to submit to bank examination.
There was nothing to compel them
to write off worthless loans. If a com-
pany owing the bank money had gone
bankrupt years ago, they could keep
the loan on the books and balance it
against liabilities.

A study of Mr. Hough's state-
ment would seem to indicate that,
though mismanagement may be
primarily responsible for the ruin
of the Raven interests, the failure
of the American government in
providing safeguards for public
institutions incorporated under
American laws but operating in
foreign lands is much to be re-
gretted.

The closure of the Chinese-
American Bank some years ago
and the collapse of the Wing On
Finance (China) Co., last year,
almost on the very eve of its
birth, should have awakened in
official circles a special sense of
responsibility in view of the ex-
istence of extraterritoriality and
consular jurisdiction in China.

The American government
may not feel duty-bound to ex-
amine American banking corpora-
tions conducted in countries whose
governments may exercise the
power of jurisdiction over them
and enforce laws which may as-
sist in the protection of public
welfare. Here in China the Chin-
ese government cannot control
local American banks, and the
American government does not
care to control them. The public,
relying through ignorance upon
American protection, is merely
placing itself at the mercy of
private scruples or their absence
instead.

The present laissez faire
policy has caused incalculable
hardship not only to the Chinese
and Russians but to many Ameri-
cans as well. While it avails lit-
tle to cry over spilt milk, much
may be done to prevent recurren-
ces in other quarters in order to
uphold the good name of the
American community. Surely legal
ingenuity which has seldom been
found wanting in the technical
evasion of legislative enactments
may be readily sought for the
worthy cause of doing justice to
public confidence in America and
American enterprises.

It may be suggested, for
instance, that American public
institutions operating in China
and Hongkong only may be
subjected to periodic examinations
by local American officials. The
investure of authority is a matter
to be left to Washington's decision,
but the principle at issue is beyond
dispute. In the interest of the sound
institutions, a clean bill of health
should be the highest recommenda-
tion to continued confidence.

Should the American govern-
ment be deterred, by political or
juridical considerations, from
pursuing this manifestly urgent
and desirable course, there re-
mains only the choice between
ordering the dissolution of
American institutions over which
the American government ex-
ercises no control and agreeing to
their submission to Chinese juris-
diction. Obviously it would be
neither dignified nor just for
Uncle Sam to permit the use of
American's name in vain.

防患于未然

多亏雷文企业（Raven enterprises）清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生，公众得以了解其事务的真实状况。尽管那些投入或存寄于这些机构的资金有望大幅收回的希望已残酷破灭，但及时认清现实，或许有助于缓和失望之情，否则这种失望会随着投资者和储户焦虑等待时间的延长而愈发尖锐。

正如本报昨日所报道，霍夫先生对雷文先生旗下公司管理不善的坦率批评，值得南京和华盛顿方面的官方关注。我们无意自任法官与陪审团，去裁决目前在中国美国法庭上演的法律争斗，但霍夫先生已披露了足够的事实，足以证明公众普遍要求对那些性质相似（即便运作方式不尽相同）于已崩塌的雷文商业帝国的企业进行亟需的调查。他对美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）的尖锐评论尤为切题，此处引述以飨读者：

“我常听到人们称该行为一家美国银行，但事实是，该行虽由一名美国人创立，却与美国任何银行均无隶属关系，其运营也不受美国银行法的管制。毫无疑问，成千上万的人正是怀着这种印象，才将钱财托付给该银行。”

信息匮乏的公众集体脑海中不幸形成的这种印象，无疑是认为该银行能受到美国主管当局定期检查所提供的保护。如果这种印象仍然存在，霍夫先生的观察可将其消除：

“美亚银行若愿意，本可以将美国银行检查员拒之门外，因为他们并不受任何强制其接受银行检查的法律约束。没有任何力量强迫他们注销不良贷款。如果一家欠银行钱的公司多年前就已破产，他们仍可将该笔贷款保留在账面上，并与负债相抵。”

研究霍夫先生的陈述似乎表明，虽然管理不善可能是导致雷文产业毁灭的主要原因，但美国政府未能对依据美国法律注册却在海外运营的公共机构提供保障，这令人深感遗憾。

几年前中美银行（Chinese-American Bank）的关闭，以及去年永安金融（中国）公司（Wing On Finance (China) Co.）在其成立前夕几乎即刻倒闭，鉴于中国存在治外法权和领事裁判权，本应在官方圈子中唤起一种特殊的责任感。

美国政府可能并不觉得有义务去审查那些在对其拥有管辖权并能执行有助于保护公共福利的法律的国家中经营的美国银行公司。在中国，中国政府无法控制当地的美国银行，而美国政府又无意加以管控。公众因无知而依赖美国的保护，实际上只是将自己置于私人道德良知或其缺失的摆布之下。

目前的放任政策不仅给中国人和俄国人带来了难以估量的苦难，也给许多美国人带来了苦难。虽然为时已晚的懊悔无济于事，但为防止在其他地方重演此类事件，从而维护美国社群的良好声誉，仍可大有作为。诚然，那种在技术性规避立法法令方面鲜有失手的法律巧思，完全可以被用于这一值得追求的事业，即公正对待公众对美国及美国企业的信心。

例如，可以建议，仅对在中国和香港运营的美国公共机构进行由当地美国官员执行的定期检查。授权事宜留待华盛顿决定，但所涉及的原则不容争议。为了健全机构的利益，一份良好的健康证明应是维持信心的最高推荐。

如果美国政府因政治或司法考量而受阻，无法采取这一明显紧迫且可取的方针，那么剩下的选择只有两个：要么下令解散那些美国政府无法控制的美国机构，要么同意它们接受中国司法管辖。显然，让山姆大叔的名义被徒然滥用，既不失体面，也不公正。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, JULY 21, 1935

LIQUIDATOR OF A.O.F.C.
PLEADS A CHECKMATE

Debtors, Willing to Repay, Find Collateral is
Re-hypothecated with Other Banks

VERY LITTLE AVAILABLE FOR CREDITORS

Impossible to Gain Possession of Securities:
Raven Trust Co. Loss Will be “Terrific”

IN an official statement yesterday, Mr. Frank Hough, liquidator
of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the Ameri-
can-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the Raven Trust Co., laid
stress on the fact that very little would be available for creditors
in the finance corporation. Those who owed money to the
American-Oriental Finance Corp. he said, while willing to pay
upon the return of the securities they had as collateral, would
not do so because it is impossible for the liquidator to gain pos-
session of the securities, which have been re-hypothecated with
other banks.

The liquidation of the three Raven
companies is proceeding under great
difficulties Mr. Hough said. The
present condition of business in
Shanghai and in the rest of China is
not the great obstacle to be over-
come. It is the internal conditions
of the three companies and the mis-
management of the affairs for several
years back. Statements have been
made to the press by those who con-
trolled the destinies of the enterprises
to the effect that the frozen assets
when thawed out would be sufficient
to pay the creditors 100 per cent. Why
such a statement should be made by
those who should have been intimate-
ly familiar with the real condition
of the three companies is hard to
understand, unless it was meant to
ease their own position for the time
being in Shanghai.

Take the Bank, for example, he
said. A fairly large percentage of the
loans outstanding, which were carried
as assets, were loans to affiliated com-
panies, which the officials must have
known were worthless. Many loans
have been carried on the books of
the Bank as assets, which, if ordinary
business judgment had been used,
would have been written off several
years ago as uncollectable and worth-
less. Many such loans had no
security backing and of many of those
that had the security was worthless.
To attribute the failure of the three
companies to bad business conditions
or the Roosevelt silver policy was
stretching a point. The condition of
the three companies had been for
several years unsound, Mr. Hough
said, and he feels from what he has
seen that liquidation would have been
forced even if general business condi-
tions were good.

Time and Patience Necessary

The staff employed in the liquida-
tion are working hard to unearth
facts and figures and trace back for
some years various items in an effort
to uncover assets which can be turned
into cash. Such work takes time and
patience. He is conscious of the fact
that the interested creditors and the
public are anxious to know the truth,
but, when it is considered that it has
taken some years for the three com-
panies to work themselves into the
position which caused the officials to
apply for liquidation, it will be
realized that the work of liquidation
will not be finished in a short space

He often heard the Bank referred
to as an American bank. The
Bank happened to be a bank estab-
lished in Shanghai by an American,
but it was not in any way affiliated
with any bank in the United States
to the extent that its operations would
have been controlled by United States
banking laws. Without a doubt,
thousands of people entrusted their
money to the Bank with this impres-
sion in their minds.

The liquidation of the Tientsin
branch of the Bank is progressing
rapidly under Mr. Harry A. Lucker,
assistant to the liquidator. This
branch was much smaller and, from
the branch's balance sheets, was in
better condition than the home office,
with the exception of the Nichols Rug
loan account of $1,000,000. The other
outstanding items are being rapidly
turned into cash. In fact, a remit-
tance was received in Shanghai soon
after Mr. Lucker took charge of
$96,000.

Nothing From Raven Trust

The Raven Trust Company will
have little, if anything, to offer to
the creditors. Considering the amount
of money deposited in the Raven
Trust Company by the public in the
form of fixed trust certificates, the
loss to the creditors will be terrific.
The fact that the other companies had
operated for some time past on over-
drafts in the Bank, amounting to
nearly two million dollars, indicates
that a great deal of the cash put into
the Raven Trust Company and the
Finance Corporation was wasted.

The Finance Corporation presents a
problem and very little will be avail-
able for the creditors. The practice
of re-hypothecating with other banks
and E. A. Pierce & Co. in New York
of customers' securities, even when
wholly owned by the customers, pla-
ced in the Finance Corporation as
collateral against loans or margin ac-
counts, has created a situation that is
extremely bad. Those who owe money
to the Finance Corporation, while
willing to pay upon return of the
securities they have as collateral, will
not do so because it is impossible for
the liquidator to gain possession of
these securities, which have been re-
hypothecated with other banks. In
other words, there is no money in
the Finance Corporation for the
liquidator to use in paying off the
Finance Corporation's obligations to
other banks to free the customers'
securities they hold as collateral.

Mr. Henry S. De Vault, the auditor,
has his organization working in the
three companies which are in liquida-
tion, as well as in the Asia Realty
Company. The complete statement
and analysis of each one of the com-
panies will be given out within the
next two months. These statements
will show the exact condition of the
four companies mentioned.

The following is a condensed sum-
mary, prepared by Mr. De Vault,
of the approximate manner in
which the depositors' and stockhold-
ers' money of the Bank was invested
at the date of the closing of the
Bank:-

LOANS AND OVERDRAFTS
Affiliated and associated
companies .................... $1,888,000.00
Officers ....................... 236,000.00
Automobile companies ....... 2,185,000.00
Rug manufacturing com-
panies ....................... 1,100,000.00
Drug dealers ................. 341,000.00
Theatre companies ............ 125,000.00
Silk merchants ............... 650,000.00
Provision merchants, cold
storage companies, etc. ...... 569,000.00
Sundry merchants ............. 558,000.00
Individuals and various ...... 2,300,000.00
OTHER ITEMS, NETT .......... 1,150,000.00

Total ...................... $11,102,000.00

Out of the above approximate total
of assets of the Bank to be realized,
during the period from the date of
the appointment of the liquidator,
there has been realized only a sum
of $355,655.20.

Mr. Hough feels sure that a review
of these figures will show that busi-
ness conditions locally and the Roose-
velt silver policy have little, if any-
thing, to do with the condition crea-
ted within the three companies due
to the policy of the management.

Liquidation Expenses

Comparing the expense of the
liquidation with the normal pay-roll
of the three companies when they
were operating, it will be seen that
expenses are being held down to a
minimum compatible with the type
of work being done. The following is
a schedule of the monthly expenses
of the three companies, also the pay-
roll of the three companies before
liquidation:

DURING OPERATION
American Oriental Banking
Corp. .................... $18,000.00
American Oriental Finance
Corp. .................... 10,600.00
Raven Trust Company ....... 3,250.00
........................... $31,850.00

DURING LIQUIDATION
American Oriental Banking
Corp. .................... $4,584.00
American Oriental Finance
Corp. .................... 3,850.00
Raven Trust Company ....... 1,275.00
........................... $9,709.00

At the beginning of the liquida-
tor's work, it was necessary to retain
a number of employees of the three
companies in order to facilitate the
work of the auditing and securing
detailed information. As the work
progresses, the liquidator's pay-roll
will diminish.

With regard to the monthly ex-
penses of the three companies dur-
ing liquidation, Mr. Hough further
said that the sum of $9,709 includes
the compensation to Mr. De Vault
and his staff. No compensation has
as yet been arranged for Dr. George
W. Sellett, the liquidator's counsel,
and the amount to be awarded him
for his services will not be fixed by
Judge Helmick until the liquidation
is complete. Similarly, nothing has
yet been said regarding Mr. Hough's
compensation, although a figure
probably will be arrived at by the
Judge when the liquidation is finished,
"should there be anything left," he
concluded.

美亚银行公司清算人
声称陷入僵局

债务人虽愿还款，但发现抵押品已被转抵押给其他银行

债权人可获清偿资产寥寥无几

无法取得证券控制权：雷文信托公司损失将“极为惨重”

美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）及雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Co.）的清算人弗兰克·霍夫（Frank Hough）先生在昨日的一份官方声明中，着重指出美亚金融公司可供偿还债权人的资产微乎其微。他表示，欠美亚金融公司款项的债务人虽然愿意在收回其作为抵押品的证券后还款，但由于清算人无法取得这些证券的控制权——因为它们已被转抵押给其他银行——因此债务人并不实际履行还款义务。

霍夫先生称，这三家雷文系公司的清算工作正面临巨大困难。上海及中国其他地区的商业现状并非需要克服的主要障碍。真正的阻碍在于这三家公司内部的状况以及过去数年来的管理不善。那些掌控企业命运的人士曾向媒体发表声明，称一旦冻结资产解冻，足以向债权人全额支付百分之百的款项。这些本应 intimately 熟悉三家公司真实状况的人士为何会作出如此声明，实在令人费解，除非其目的仅在于暂时缓解他们在上海的处境。

他以银行为例说道。被列为资产的未偿贷款中，有相当大比例是贷给关联公司的，而管理人员必然知道这些公司是毫无价值的。许多贷款被银行记为资产，若运用正常的商业判断，早在几年前就应作为无法收回且毫无价值的项目予以核销。许多此类贷款没有任何担保支持，而在那些有担保的贷款中，许多担保品也毫无价值。将这三家公司的倒闭归咎于恶劣的商业环境或罗斯福总统的白银政策，实属牵强附会。霍夫先生表示，这三家公司的状况多年来一直不健全，根据他所见所闻，即使整体商业环境良好，也不得不进行清算。

需要时间与耐心

参与清算工作的职员正努力挖掘事实与数据，并追溯过去数年的各项账目，以期发现可变现的资产。这项工作耗时且需要耐心。他意识到相关债权人和公众急于了解真相，但考虑到这三家公司花了数年时间才陷入导致管理层申请清算的境地，应当认识到清算工作不可能在短时间内完成。

他经常听到人们将该银行称为一家美国银行。该银行确实是由一名美国人在上海设立的，但其运营并不受美国银行法的控制，因此在任何意义上都未与美国境内的任何银行存在隶属关系。毫无疑问，成千上万的人正是怀着这种印象将资金托付给该银行。

在清算人助理哈里·A·拉克尔（Harry A. Lucker）先生的主持下，该银行天津分行的清算工作进展迅速。除了一笔金额为100万美元的尼科尔斯地毯公司（Nichols Rug）贷款账户外，该分行规模较小，且从其资产负债表来看，状况优于总行。其他未结项目正迅速变现。事实上，在拉克尔先生接手后不久，上海便收到了一笔96,000美元的汇款。

雷文信托公司无款可付

雷文信托公司几乎没有什么资产可以提供给债权人。考虑到公众以固定信托证书形式存入雷文信托公司的资金数额，债权人的损失将极为惨重。其他公司在过去一段时间内依靠在该银行的透支额度运营，金额接近200万美元，这一事实表明，投入雷文信托公司和金融公司的大量现金已被挥霍殆尽。

金融公司呈现出一个难题，可供债权人分配的资产极少。将客户完全拥有的证券作为贷款或保证金账户的抵押品存入金融公司，随后又将这些证券转抵押给其他银行及纽约的E. A. Pierce & Co.，这种做法造成了极其糟糕的局面。欠金融公司款项的债务人虽然愿意在收回其作为抵押品的证券后还款，但由于清算人无法取得这些已被转抵押给其他银行的证券的控制权，他们并不实际还款。换言之，金融公司中没有资金供清算人用来偿还金融公司对其他银行的债务，从而释放其持有的作为抵押品的客户证券。

审计师亨利·S·德沃尔特（Henry S. De Vault）先生已组织团队对正在清算的三家公司以及亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）开展工作。每家公司的完整报表和分析将在未来两个月内公布。这些报表将显示上述四家公司的确切状况。

以下是德沃尔特先生编制的简要汇总，说明了在银行停业之日，存款人和股东的资金大致投资去向：

贷款与透支
关联及附属公司 .................... $1,888,000.00
高级职员 ....................... 236,000.00
汽车公司 ....... 2,185,000.00
地毯制造公
司 ....................... 1,100,000.00
药品经销商 ................. 341,000.00
剧院公司 ............ 125,000.00
丝绸商 ............... 650,000.00
食品商、冷藏
公司等 ...... 569,000.00
各类杂项商人 ............. 558,000.00
个人及其他 ...... 2,300,000.00
其他项目，净额 .......... 1,150,000.00

总计 ...................... $11,102,000.00

在上述银行待变现资产的大约总额中，自清算人任命之日起至目前，仅实现了355,655.20美元。

霍夫先生确信，审查这些数据将表明，本地商业环境和罗斯福白银政策与这三家公司因管理政策而造成的状况几乎没有关系，甚至毫无关系。

清算费用

将清算费用与这三家公司运营期间的正常工资单进行比较，可以看出，费用已被控制在与所从事工作类型相称的最低限度。以下是这三家公司在清算期间的月度费用清单，以及清算前三家公司的工资单：

运营期间
美亚银行公司 .................... $18,000.00
美亚金融公司 .................... 10,600.00
雷文信托公司 ....... 3,250.00
........................... $31,850.00

清算期间
美亚银行公司 .................... $4,584.00
美亚金融公司 .................... 3,850.00
雷文信托公司 ....... 1,275.00
........................... $9,709.00

在清算工作开始时，有必要留用这三家公司的部分员工，以便协助审计工作并获取详细信息。随着工作的推进，清算人的工资支出将会减少。

关于这三家公司在清算期间的月度费用，霍夫先生进一步表示，9,709美元的金额包括德沃尔特先生及其团队的薪酬。尚未就清算人法律顾问乔治·W·塞莱特（George W. Sellett）博士的薪酬作出安排，赫尔米克法官（Judge Helmick）将在清算完成后确定其服务报酬。同样，虽然法官可能在清算结束时确定霍夫先生的薪酬数额，但目前尚未就此进行讨论，“前提是如果还有剩余资产的话”，他总结道。

（右侧页边批注及印章内容）：
S. B. REGISTER
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

S. B. REGI
D 6748
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 13, 1935

Two Years Needed
To Liquidate Bank

A.-O.B.C. Collections
Will Require Time,
Mr. Hough Says

Probably two years or more will
be required for liquidation of the
American-Oriental Banking Cor-
poration, and at the present
time it is quite impossible to say
when an initial payment to deposi-
tors can be made.
These disheartening tidings were
obtained this morning from Mr.
Frank L. Hough, liquidator for the
bank and two other Raven pro-
perties, who intimated that the
more he went into the bank's affairs
the worse they seemed. The gen-
eral public, he feared, still enter-
tains false hopes which facts as now
apparent do not justify.

Makes No Estimate
"It's a mess," he said. "There
is no way that I can make an
estimate as to when the depositors
will get something—I wish I could.
Some of the loans have proved
absolutely hopeless and others will
require a great deal of time for
any appreciable collections."
"The situation has proved a great
surprise. When I came in, with
$6,700,000 in loans outstanding and
not counting obligations from the
other Raven companies which I
immediately counted out of con-
sideration, it seemed reasonable to
assume that a call of these loans
would bring in at least $400,000 or
$500,000 the first month. Ten per
cent the first month would not
have been unreasonable, in fact."

No Short Cuts
"As a matter of actual fact we
got in just $53,000 the first month,
and that gives some idea of the
state of affairs. It is an abnormal
situation within Shanghai's general
abnormal situation."
There seems no way, under the
circumstances, to shorten a some-
what drawn-out liquidation period,
Mr. Hough made clear. On the
other hand, he hopes that the other
companies, especially the Raven
Trust, can be liquidated sooner and
he sees no special obstacle in the
way of this.

D 6748
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1935年7月13日，星期六

清算银行需时两年

霍夫先生称
美亚银行收款
需时日

美亚银行公司（A.-O.B.C.）的清算可能需要两年或更长时间，目前完全无法确定何时能向存款人支付首笔款项。
这些令人沮丧的消息是今晨从该银行及另外两家雷文系产业的清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生处获悉的，他暗示越是深入调查银行事务，情况显得越糟。他担心公众仍抱有事实所不能证明的非分之想。

不作预估

“这是一团乱麻，”他说。“我无法预估存款人何时能拿到钱——我真希望我能。有些贷款已证明绝对无望收回，而其他贷款则需要大量时间才能收回可观的款项。”
“局势 proved 出人意料。当我介入时，未偿贷款达670万美元，这还不包括我立即排除在考虑之外的其他雷文系公司的债务，当时合理假设催收这些贷款在第一个月至少能收回40万或50万美元。事实上，第一个月收回百分之十也并非不合理。”

没有捷径

“事实上，我们第一个月只收回了53,000美元，这让人对事态状况有了些许概念。这是在上海整体异常状况下的一个异常情况。”
霍夫先生明确表示，在这种情况下，似乎没有办法缩短略显漫长的清算期。另一方面，他希望其他公司，特别是雷文信托公司，能更快完成清算，他认为这方面没有特别障碍。

16

S. B. REGI
Date

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JULY 5, 1935

A.-O.B.C. LIQUIDATION
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—Through the courtesy of your columns, I wish to express my views to all depositors in the A.-O.B.C. with the object of uniting in one common cause to recover the largest amount of our deposits.
It seems to me that depositors should be chiefly interested in the collections of the $6,775,435.75 owned by firms in Shanghai, and the $1,299,762.85 owned by firms in Tientsin. Why are such firms allowed to continue business when up to the present time they are paying back so little on their loans. It would be better to foreclose on them and get only 30 per cent. through liquidation of these firms, than allow them to continue business indefinitely and let depositors keep hoping they will repay their loans at some uncertain future date. Thirty per cent. recovery from this total of loans in Shanghai and Tientsin would be $2,700,-000.00 roughly. There is $1,015,-436.71 due from Asia Realty which, we are told by the liquidator, is fully covered by mortgage on the bank building in Shanghai. About $2,000,000.00 can be recovered from other Shanghai and Tientsin assets such as “Advances against bills for collection,” “Bills Purchased,” “Bills Discounted,” “Customers Acceptances,” “Due from Compradore,” “Home office account” “Cash Receivable,” “Investments” and “Accounts Receivable.” All the above, added together, makes a total recovery of $5,700,-000.00, in other words, a sure 80 per cent. return for depositors (deposits in Shanghai and Tientsin total approximately $7,000,000.00). Therefore in the interest of all depositors, why not make sure of 30 per cent. recovery from all large outstanding loans by foreclosure on such firms, instead of waiting two or three years for them to repay 50 per cent. (???) of their loans. During these two or three years of waiting, funds in the bank will surely be reduced by liquidation expenses running into several hundred thousand dollars. If, however, the liquidator guarantees that he will be able to collect more than 30 per cent. of the entire lot of loans by allowing firms to continue business, thereby ensuring 100 per cent. return for depositors during the course of the two or three years waiting, then he would show great wisdom in allowing these firms to carry on—not otherwise.
“WATCHFUL DEPOSITOR.”
Tientsin, July 2, 1935.

S. B. REGI
日期

《字林西报》，1935年7月5日，星期五

亚细亚-东方银行（A.-O.B.C.）清算事宜

编辑先生：
《字林西报》

先生——承蒙贵报提供版面，本人谨向亚细亚-东方银行（A.-O.B.C.）的所有储户表达本人的观点，旨在团结大家为一个共同的目标努力，即追回我们存款的最大数额。

在本人看来，储户应主要关注收回上海各商号所欠的6,775,435.75美元以及天津各商号所欠的1,299,762.85美元。既然这些商号迄今偿还贷款的比例如此之低，为何还允许它们继续营业？最好是对这些商号采取取消赎回权的措施，通过清算这些商号哪怕只收回30%，也胜过让它们无限期地继续营业，让储户一直抱着它们在某个不确定的未来日期偿还贷款的幻想。从上海和天津的贷款总额中收回30%，大致为2,700,000.00美元。据清算人告知，亚细亚地产公司（Asia Realty）欠款1,015,436.71美元，该款项已由上海银行大楼的抵押品充分覆盖。从其他上海和天津的资产中，如“托收票据垫款”、“买入票据”、“贴现票据”、“客户承兑汇票”、“买办欠款”、“总行账户”、“应收现金”、“投资”和“应收账款”等，可收回约2,000,000.00美元。以上各项相加，回收总额为5,700,000.00美元，换言之，储户可确保获得80%的回报（上海和天津的存款总额约为7,000,000.00美元）。因此，为了所有储户的利益，何不对所有大额未偿贷款涉及的商号采取取消赎回权措施，以确保收回30%，而不是等待两三年让它们偿还50%（???）的贷款。在这两三年的等待期间，银行的资金肯定会因高达数十万美元的清算费用而减少。然而，如果清算人保证，通过允许这些商号继续营业，他能够收回全部贷款总额的30%以上，从而确保储户在两三年的等待期内获得100%的回报，那么他允许这些商号继续经营才显示出极大的智慧——否则便不然。

“警惕的储户”
天津，1935年7月2日。

S. B. I. N.Y.
No. D 6748
1935
Date ST 7/1.35

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY

Liquidator Files Two New
Suits Against Mr. Raven

“Wrongful And Fraudulent” Receipt Of A Sum Of
Tls. 135,000 From The Asia Realty Company
Alleged In Complaint

Alleging that his receipt and retention of a sum of Tls. 135,000, voted to him as an honorarium by the Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A., is “wrongful and fraudulent,” Mr. Frank L. Hough, Trustee of the Company, yesterday filed with the United States Court for China a suit against Mr. Frank J. Raven in which repayment of that sum is demanded, plus interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum from January 16, 1932 to the date when repayment is made.

A further suit, instituted in his capacity as Liquidator of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, was filed by Mr. Hough, demanding the return of a similar sum paid by that Corporation to Mr. Raven, also as an honorarium. These two suits, added to the suit previously filed by Mr. Hough as Liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, demanding the return by Mr. Raven of the Tls. 135,000 voted to him as an honorarium by that institution, bring the total claims against the defendant to the sum of Tls. 405,000. Hearing on all three suits will take place when Judge Milton J. Helmick returns from North China.

The Complaint

The complaint in the suit filed by Mr. Hough yesterday as Trustee of the Asia Realty Company reads, in part, as follows:—

“At a meeting of the Board of Directors of the Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A. held at Shanghai, China, on January 13, 1932, at which time defendant was a Director and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the said corporation and controlled said corporation . . . and at which meeting all of the directors, excepting defendant, were present, a resolution in the following words and figures was unanimously adopted:

“Resolved that in view of the long and faithful service performed without salary or other compensation by Frank J. Raven as President, Manager and Promoter of the Asia Realty Company, an honorarium of One Hundred Thirty-five Thousand Taels (Tls. 135,000) be voted to him in recognition of work well and faithfully performed and

“Be it further resolved that the Treasurer be authorized to make this entire payment at once; and to write off from the books of this Company over a period of six (6) years, or fewer, One Hundred Thirty-five Thousand Taels (Tls. 135,000); the amount to be written off in the year 1932 to be Thirty-five Thousand Taels (Tls. 35,000); and the amount to be written off in any one year thereafter to be governed by the net profits accruing to this Company during this period.

And at the next meeting of said Corporation held at Shanghai, China, on February 10, 1932, at which meeting defendant was present, the minutes of the first mentioned meeting of January 13, 1932 were read and approved.

“On January 16, 1932, pursuant to the aforesaid resolution adopted on January 13, 1932, Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A. paid to defendant and defendant received from it the sum of Sh. Tls. 135,000, being equivalent to $188,811.18, Chinese currency.

Monthly Salary

“For a long period of time prior to January 13, 1932 defendant received from and was paid by Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A. a regular monthly salary covering services rendered to said corporation and during the calendar year 1931 the regular monthly salary paid by said corporation to defendant and received by him was Two Thousand Dollars ($2,000), Chinese currency per month, and at the time the aforesaid sum of Sh.Tls.135,000 was received by defendant, Asia Realty Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A. was not indebted or otherwise obligated to defendant and defendant then and there knew that said corporation was not obligated to defendant for any services performed by defendant, and thereupon and by reason of the foregoing defendant was and became obligated in equity and good conscience to immediately repay to the said corporation the sum of Sh. Tls. 135,000.

“Since the payment of the aforesaid sum of Sh. Tls. 135,000 by the said Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A. to defendant, the said sum of Sh. Tls. 135,000 has been due and owing by defendant to the said corporation and although complainant has demanded of defendant payment of said money, defendant has failed and refused to pay the same or any part thereof to the said corporation, and defendant is now indebted to said corporation in the sum of Sh. Tls. 135,000, and defendant’s receipt and retention of the last aforesaid moneys is wrongful and fraudulent in that at the time said moneys were received by defendant all salary and other compensation due him had already been received by him.”

(批：file 11/9)

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. B. I. N.Y.
编号 D 6748
1935年
日期 ST 7/1.35

《字林西报》，七月某日，星期四

清算人对雷文先生提起两项新诉讼

诉状指控其“不当且欺诈性”收取亚细亚地产公司支付的135,000两白银

该公司受托人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生指控弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生收取并保留由美国联邦亚细亚地产公司（Asia Realty Company Federal Inc. U.S.A.）投票授予他的135,000两白银酬金的行为是“不当且欺诈性的”，并于昨日向美国驻华法院对雷文先生提起诉讼，要求偿还该笔款项，并支付自1932年1月16日起至还款日止按年利率6%计算的利息。

霍夫先生以亚细亚-东方金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）清算人的身份又提起了一项诉讼，要求归还该公司作为酬金支付给雷文先生的类似款项。这两项诉讼，加上霍夫先生此前以亚细亚-东方银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）清算人身份提起的、要求雷文先生归还该机构投票授予他的135,000两白银酬金的诉讼，使得针对被告的索赔总额达到405,000两白银。待米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官从华北返回后，将对这三起诉讼进行审理。

诉状内容

霍夫先生昨日以亚细亚地产公司受托人身份提起的诉讼中的诉状部分内容如下：

“1932年1月13日，美国联邦亚细亚地产公司在中华民国上海召开董事会会议，当时被告是该公司的董事兼董事会主席，并控制着该公司……除被告外，所有董事均出席了会议，会议一致通过了以下措辞和数字的决议：

‘决议：鉴于弗兰克·J·雷文作为亚细亚地产公司的总裁、经理和发起人，长期忠诚服务而未领取薪水或其他报酬，特投票授予他十三万五千两（Tls. 135,000）白银作为酬金，以表彰其出色且忠诚的工作；

‘并进一步决议：授权司库立即全额支付此款项；并在六（6）年或更短的时间内，从本公司账目中注销十三万五千两（Tls. 135,000）白银；1932年注销的金额为三万五千两（Tls. 35,000）；此后任何一年注销的金额由本公司在此期间产生的净利润决定。’

随后，该公司于1932年2月10日在中华民国上海召开了下一次会议，被告出席了该次会议，会上宣读并批准了上述1932年1月13日首次会议的会议纪要。

“1932年1月16日，根据1932年1月13日通过的上述决议，美国联邦亚细亚地产公司向被告支付了上海规元135,000两，被告从中收取了该笔款项，折合中国货币188,811.18美元。

月薪

“在1932年1月13日之前很长一段时间内，被告从美国联邦亚细亚地产公司收取并由该公司支付定期月薪，以涵盖其为该公司提供的服务；在1931日历年度，该公司向被告支付并由被告收取的定期月薪为每月中国货币2,000美元（$2,000）；当被告收到上述上海规元135,000两时，美国联邦亚细亚地产公司并不欠被告债务或对被告负有其他义务，被告当时即知该公司不因被告提供的任何服务而对被告负有义务，因此，基于前述原因，被告在衡平法和良知上有义务立即向该公司偿还上海规元135,000两。

“自从美国联邦亚细亚地产公司向被告支付上述上海规元135,000两以来，被告一直欠该公司该笔上海规元135,000两；尽管原告已要求被告支付该笔款项，但被告未能并拒绝向该公司支付该笔款项或其任何部分，被告目前欠该公司上海规元135,000两；被告收取并保留上述最后提及的款项是不当且欺诈性的，因为在被告收取该笔款项时，他已收到了应付给他的所有薪水和其他报酬。”

（批注：归档 11/9）

1112J-
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JULY 4, 1935

TWO MORE SUITS AGAINST MR.
F. J. RAVEN FILED

Return of Honoraria Voted by A.O.F.C. and Asia
Realty Co. Sought by Liquidator

TIENTSIN A.O.B.C. MAY PAY 50 PER CENT.

Bringing the total amount of the claims against Mr. Frank J. Raven to Tls. 405,000, two further bills of complaint, each for Tls. 135,000, were filed with the U. S. Court for China by Mr. Frank Hough, liquidator, on behalf of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation and the Asia Realty Co., yesterday afternoon.

In the case of the Asia Realty Co.'s bill of complaint, it is charged that the defendant's receipt and retention of the money, voted him as a honorarium for "long and faithful services performed without salary or compensation," was "wrongful and fraudulent," inasmuch as for some time prior to the passing of this resolution, Mr. Raven had been receiving a monthly salary of $2,000, which he continued to receive after the resolution was passed and the money given him.

Mr. Raven will not be served with a writ of ne exeat, preventing him from leaving the country, as was done in the case of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, as the one writ will be quite sufficient to hold him within the court's jurisdiction.

The A. O. F. C.'s Claim

The bill of complaint filed by the liquidator of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation is, almost word for word identical with that filed on behalf of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation.

At a meeting held on January 17, 1932, at which all the directors and Mr. Raven, were present, the following resolution was passed:—

Resolved that in view of the long and faithful services performed without salary or other compensation by Frank J. Raven as President, Manager, and Promoter of the American Oriental Finance Corporation, an honorarium of One Hundred and Thirty-five thousand Taels (¥135,000), be voted to him in recognition of work well and faithfully done; and

Be it further resolved that the Treasurer be authorised to make this entire payment to the said Frank J. Raven at once; and to write off from the books of this company over a period of six (6) years, or fewer, One Hundred and Thirty-five thousand Taels (¥135,000), the amount to be written off for any one year thereafter to be governed by the net profits accruing to this company during that period.

As in the case of the Bank, the liquidator alleges that when Mr. Raven received this money, the defendant knew that the corporation was insolvent; an order is requested in the amount of Tls. 135,000, together with interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum from January 10, 1932, to the date when payment shall be made by the defendant.

Asia Realty's Payment of Salary

The bill of complaint filed by the Asia Realty Co., however, differs somewhat, inasmuch as it alleges that although a resolution worded similarly to that of the other two companies was passed, the defendant in this case was in receipt of a monthly salary, on which nothing was due, or owing.

The resolution, which was passed at a meeting of the board of directors, at which the defendant was not present, on January 13, 1932, ran as follows:—

Resolved that in view of the long and faithful services performed without salary or other compensation by Frank J. Raven as President, Manager, and Promoter of the Asia Realty Co., Fed. Inc., U.S.A., an honorarium of One Hundred and Thirty-five thousand Taels (¥135,000), be voted to him in recognition of work well and faithfully done; and

Be it further resolved that the Treasurer be authorised to make this entire payment to the said Frank J. Raven at once; and to write off from the books of this company over a period of six (6) years or fewer, One Hundred and Thirty-five thousand Taels (¥135,000), the amount to be written off in the year 1932 to be Thirty-five thousand Taels (¥35,000), and the amount to be written off in any one year thereafter to be governed by the net profits accruing to this company during that period.

The defendant, continues the bill of complaint, was present at the next meeting of the board of directors, on February 10, 1932, when the minutes of the meeting of January 13 were read and approved. The complaint continues that "for a long period of time next to January 13, 1932" Mr. Raven received and was paid by the Asia Realty Co. a regular monthly salary covering all services rendered to the corporation; during 1931, his regular salary was C.$2,000 per month, and at the time the Tls. 135,000 was paid over the Asia Realty was not indebted to the defendant.

"Wrongful and Fraudulent"

Paragraph 8 of the bill of complaint continues:—

Since the payment of the aforesaid sum of S. Tls. 135,000 by the said Asia Realty Co., Fed. Inc., U.S.A., to defendant, the said sum of Tls. 135,000 has been due and owing by the defendant to the said corporation, and although complainant has demanded of defendant payment of the said moneys defendant, has failed and refused to pay the same, or any part thereof to the said corporation, and defendant is now indebted to the said corporation in the sum of Tls. 135,000 and defendant's receipt and detention of the last aforesaid moneys is wrongful and fraudulent in that at the time said moneys were received by defendant all salary and other compensation due him had already been received by him.

The Court is asked to make an order in the amount of Tls. 135,000, together with interest at the rate of six per cent. per annum from January 16, 1932, to the date when payment shall be made by the defendant. It is alleged defendant knew the company was insolvent at the time.

Court Proceedings Later

Court proceedings by the three companies against Mr. Raven will not take place for another week or so, as Judge M. J. Helmick is still in Tientsin, engaged on a number of cases.

Regarding the Tientsin branch of the bank, Mr. Hough said yesterday that a certain amount of money had been received from that office. If the total amount outstanding could be received, he said, depositors would easily be able to receive fifty cents in the dollar. It was aiming one's hopes rather high, he intimated, however, to expect anything like the full amount owing to be received.

Nothing, he said, could be expected from the liquidation of the American-Oriental Finance Corporation's branch in Hongkong, as that branch came under the jurisdiction of the British Court, which would naturally appoint its own liquidator. A similar state of affairs existed with regard to the company's offices in Manila.

Meanwhile, work is proceeding at a hard pace in the liquidator's office here. To-day is July 4, America's National Holiday, but "it will be just the same as any other Thursday to us," said Mr. Hough, laughingly. Office equipment, such as fans, typewriters, etc., are being sold off individually or in lots, as fast as possible, the appraiser having put a fair second-hand price on them, he said.

1112J-
《字林西报》，1935年7月4日，星期四

针对F. J. 雷文先生又提起两起诉讼

清算人要求返还美亚金融公司与亚洲地产公司投票通过的酬金

天津美亚银行或可支付百分之五十

清算人弗兰克·霍夫（Frank Hough）先生于昨日下午代表美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）和亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Co.），向美国在华法院提交了两份新的诉状，每份索赔金额为规平银135,000两，使得针对弗兰克·J. 雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生的索赔总额达到规平银405,000两。

在亚洲地产公司的诉状中，指控被告收取并保留这笔作为“长期忠诚服务且无薪金或报酬”而投票给予他的酬金的行为是“不当且欺诈性的”，因为在该决议通过前的一段时间内，雷文先生一直每月领取2,000美元的薪水，且在决议通过并发放款项后，他继续领取该薪水。

雷文先生不会像在美亚银行案中那样被送达禁止出境令（writ of ne exeat）以阻止其离境，因为一份禁令已足以将其限制在法院管辖范围内。

美亚金融公司的索赔

美亚金融公司清算人提交的诉状，与代表美亚银行提交的诉状几乎逐字相同。

在1932年1月17日举行的一次会议上，全体董事及雷文先生均出席，会议通过了以下决议：—

决议：鉴于弗兰克·J. 雷文作为美亚金融公司的总裁、经理及发起人，在无薪金或其他补偿的情况下提供了长期且忠诚的服务，特投票授予其规平银十三万五千两（¥135,000）的酬金，以表彰其出色且忠诚的工作；并

进一步决议：授权司库立即向上述弗兰克·J. 雷文全额支付此款项；并在六（6）年或更短的时间内，从本公司账目中注销规平银十三万五千两（¥135,000），此后任何一年注销的金额应根据该期间本公司产生的净利润来确定。

与银行案一样，清算人指控雷文先生在收到这笔钱时，明知该公司已资不抵债；现请求法院下令责令其支付规平银135,000两，并加计自1932年1月10日起至被告付款日止按年利率百分之六计算的利息。

亚洲地产公司的薪金支付情况

然而，亚洲地产公司提交的诉状略有不同，因为它指控虽然通过了一项与其他两家公司措辞类似的决议，但本案被告当时正在领取月薪，且公司并不欠付其任何款项。

该决议于1932年1月13日在董事会会议上通过，被告未出席该次会议，决议内容如下：—

决议：鉴于弗兰克·J. 雷文作为美国联邦注册亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Co., Fed. Inc., U.S.A.）的总裁、经理及发起人，在无薪金或其他补偿的情况下提供了长期且忠诚的服务，特投票授予其规平银十三万五千两（¥135,000）的酬金，以表彰其出色且忠诚的工作；并

进一步决议：授权司库立即向上述弗兰克·J. 雷文全额支付此款项；并在六（6）年或更短的时间内，从本公司账目中注销规平银十三万五千两（¥135,000），其中1932年注销金额为规平银三万五千两（¥35,000），此后任何一年注销的金额应根据该期间本公司产生的净利润来确定。

诉状继续称，被告出席了1932年2月10日举行的下一次董事会会议，会上宣读并批准了1月13日的会议纪要。诉状接着称，“在1932年1月13日之后很长一段时间内”，雷文先生从亚洲地产公司领取并获支付了涵盖其为该公司提供的所有服务的定期月薪；1931年期间，他的固定月薪为大洋2,000元，而在支付规平银135,000两时，亚洲地产公司并不欠被告任何债务。

“不当且欺诈性”

诉状第8段继续写道：—

自上述美国联邦注册亚洲地产公司向被告支付前述规平银135,000两以来，被告即欠上述公司该笔规平银135,000两，尽管原告已要求被告支付该笔款项，但被告未能并拒绝向上述公司支付该款项或其任何部分，被告目前欠上述公司规平银135,000两，被告收取并扣留上述最后提及的款项属于不当且欺诈性行为，因为在被告收取该款项时，其应得的所有薪金及其他补偿均已收讫。

现请求法院下令责令其支付规平银135,000两，并加计自1932年1月16日起至被告付款日止按年利率百分之六计算的利息。指控称被告当时明知公司已资不抵债。

稍后进行法庭程序

这三家公司针对雷文先生的法庭程序还需一周左右才会进行，因为M. J. 赫尔米克（M. J. Helmick）法官仍在天津处理多起案件。

关于该银行的天津分行，霍夫先生昨日表示，已从该办事处收到一定数额的款项。他说，如果能收回全部未偿款项，储户将能轻松获得每美元五十分成的偿付。但他暗示，期望收回类似全额欠款则是希望过高了。

他说，对于美亚金融公司香港分行的清算不能抱有任何期望，因为该分行受英国法院管辖，英国法院自然会任命其自己的清算人。该公司在马尼拉的办事处也存在类似情况。

与此同时，本地清算人办公室的工作正在紧张进行。今天是7月4日，美国的国庆日，但“对我们来说，这和任何一个星期四没什么两样，”霍夫先生笑着说。他说，评估员已对这些办公设备（如风扇、打字机等）给出了公平的二手价格，正尽快单独或批量出售。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 3, 1935    1110-8

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGIST...
No. D 6248
Date 3 / 7 / 35）

2 More Suits
Will Be Filed
Against Raven

Hough To Start New
Actions This Morning
In United States Court

Questioned Honorariums
All Total $405,000

Two more suits will be filed against Mr. F. J. Raven, former president of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, in the United States Court for China this morning.

This is according to a statement made by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the defunct bank, yesterday following a conference with Dr. George Sellett, legal adviser to the liquidator.

The conversations between Mr. Hough and Dr. Sellett occupied most of the afternoon. The session came to an end about 5 p.m., and a few minutes later Mr. Hough stated the two additional suits, contemplated for some time, would definitely be filed.

The actions to be filed this morning will be additional and similar to the one filed against Mr. Raven last Saturday, in which the return of a bonus of Tls. 135,000 granted to the banker in 1932 by the board of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was asked.

In both cases, it is understood, the amounts will be approximately the same, while one of the honorariums in question was that voted Mr. Raven by the board of the Asia Realty Company. The other bonus involved was one granted the financier by the American-Oriental Finance Corporation.

When the business of filing the additional suits has been completed this morning, the total amount requested from Mr. Raven by the liquidator will be approximately Tls. 405,000.

Filing of the two suits today will not involve further writs ne exeat to insure Mr. Raven's presence within the jurisdiction of the court since the first writ, served Saturday shortly before midnight, is deemed adequate to cover the whole situation. Under the terms of the first writ, Mr. Raven was required to post a bond of U.S. $20,-000. This was accomplished late Monday afternoon, four guarantors having been obtained by the ex-banker to sign the bond.

Suits against other leading debtors are now being prepared, Mr. Hough said yesterday, and it is expected that a few of these will be signed this week. In the meantime, the routine work of liquidation is proceeding, slowly perhaps, but making progress. All means possible to turn the bank's assets into cash are being utilized, even to the selling off of the furniture that is not needed by the liquidators.

Overhead costs of liquidation are being reduced as rapidly as possible, the staff constantly dwindling in number as the need for detailed assistance passes.

（批：File 1/9. J）

《大美晚报》，1935年7月3日，星期三    1110-8

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. B. 登记...
编号 D 6248
日期 35/7/3）

又将针对雷文
提起两起诉讼

霍夫今晨将在
美国法院启动
新诉讼

质疑的酬金
总计达405,000美元

今晨将在美国在华法院针对美亚银行前总裁F. J. 雷文先生再提起两起诉讼。

这是已倒闭银行的清算人弗兰克·L. 霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生昨日在与清算人的法律顾问乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士会晤后发表的声明中透露的。

霍夫先生与塞莱特博士的谈话占据了下午的大部分时间。会议于下午5点左右结束，几分钟后，霍夫先生表示，酝酿已久的两起额外诉讼将肯定会被提起。

今晨将提起的诉讼是对上周六针对雷文先生提起的诉讼的补充且性质相似，后者要求归还美亚银行董事会于1932年授予这位银行家的135,000两红利。

据了解，在这两起案件中，金额大致相同，其中一笔受质疑的酬金是由亚洲地产公司董事会投票给予雷文先生的。另一笔涉及的红利是由美亚金融公司授予这位金融家的。

当今晨完成额外诉讼的提交工作后，清算人向雷文先生要求的总金额将达到约规平银405,000两。

今日提交这两起诉讼不涉及发出进一步的禁止出境令以确保雷文先生在法院管辖范围内，因为周六午夜前不久送达的第一份禁令被认为足以覆盖整个情况。根据第一份禁令的条款，雷文先生被要求缴纳20,000美元的保证金。这一要求已于周一傍晚晚些时候完成，这位前银行家找到了四位担保人在保函上签字。

霍夫先生昨日表示，针对其他主要债务人的诉讼目前正在准备中，预计本周将签署其中几份。与此同时，清算的日常工作正在进行，虽然可能缓慢，但正在取得进展。正在利用一切可能的手段将银行资产转化为现金，甚至包括出售清算人不需要的家具。

清算的管理费用正尽可能快地减少，随着对详细协助需求的过去，工作人员数量不断减少。

（批：归档 1/9. J）

BANK PRESIDENT SUED BY
LIQUIDATOR

Mr. F. L. Hough Files Action Against Mr. F. J.
Raven for Return of Tls. 135,000 Honorarium

CHARGES CONCERN WAS INSOLVENT

Writ Preventing Defendant Leaving Jurisdiction
of Court Issued: U.S. $20,000 Bond

DEMANDING the instant return of Tls. 135,000 from Mr. F. J.
Raven, former President of the American-Oriental Banking
Corporation, and holder of similar high positions in the American-
Oriental Finance Corporation, Asia Realty Company, and Raven
Trust Company, a bill of complaint was filed with the U.S. Court

Bank.

"I am suing him," Mr. Hough said yesterday, "to return this
Tls. 135,000 to use for the creditors."

Further, shortly before midnight on Saturday, Mr. Raven was
prevented from leaving this country by a writ of ne exeat also
filed by Mr. Hough, who alleged that Mr. Raven "designs quickly
to depart from the Republic of China and the jurisdiction of this
Court." The writ was endorsed by Judge M. J. Helmick, who
set the security to be submitted by Mr. Raven at U.S. $20,000.
Mr. Raven stated yesterday that he had no intention of leaving.

清算人起诉银行总裁

F. L. 霍夫先生提起诉讼，要求 F. J. 雷文先生归还酬金关平银135,000两

指控该企业资不抵债

签发禁止被告离开法院管辖区域的令状：保证金20,000美元

美国驻沪法院（U.S. Court of China）于周六受理了该银行官方清算人 F. L. 霍夫先生提交的诉状，要求美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）前总裁、并在美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）、亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）及雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）担任类似高职的 F. J. 雷文先生立即归还关平银135,000两。

“我起诉他，”霍夫先生昨日表示，“是为了追回这关平银135,000两，用于偿付债权人。”

此外，在周六午夜前不久，雷文先生被霍夫先生申请的另一份“禁止出境令”（writ of ne exeat）阻止离境。霍夫先生指控雷文先生“企图迅速离开中华民国及本法院的管辖区域”。该令状由赫尔米克法官（Judge M. J. Helmick）签署，并将雷文先生需提交的保证金定为20,000美元。雷文先生昨日声明，他并无意离开。

美亚银行总裁
对保证金命令
感到惊讶

雷文先生称无意离开上海

经法律咨询后
接受酬金

F. J. 雷文先生昨日下午在其虹桥路555号的寓所接待了来访的新闻记者，并在半小时内回答了有关雷文信托公司、美亚金融公司及美亚银行事务的问题。雷文先生表示，他对美国法院签发禁止其离开上海的令状感到惊讶，

nul, as he had never intended to
leave the port. The bond required
by the U.S. Court, he said, will de-
finitely be furnished, probably to-day.
Mr. Raven refused to disclose the
name of his guarantor.
Questioned regarding the honora-
rium of Tls. 135,000 given him by the
American Oriental Bank in January
1932, Mr. Raven said that this amount
had been properly voted, that he ac-
cepted it after taking legal advice,
and that he was convinced that the
concern was solvent at that time, as
well as subsequently. As regards the
amortization of the amount in the
books of the bank over a period of
six years, Mr. Raven said this was
simply a matter of book-keeping and
that he did not see anything strange
in it. He was not an accountant:
the bank's manager was a good ac-
countant, and the bank employed a
good firm of auditors to examine the
books.

Frozen Accounts

When the American Oriental Bank
closed, Mr. Raven hoped and thought
that it would pay 100 per cent., and
he still thinks that it can pay this,
although it may take years. The
bank, he said, in common with many
other banks in Shanghai, had large
frozen accounts; where other banks
can draw on their head offices abroad,
however, the A.O.B.C. cannot, its
head office being in Shanghai.
Should business improve, the frozen
accounts might be liquidated more
rapidly, but should there be no im-
provement, it would take a long time.
As the Raven Trust holds shares in
the American Oriental Finance Cor-
poration, which in turn holds shares
in the A.O. Bank, the accounts of
the first two depend on the last, Mr.
Raven continued.
One more question was asked Mr.
Raven, whether he personally had
owed money to the Raven Trust. He
denied this and said that, on the con-
trary, he had put all he could into
the Trust, as it had "harder sledding"
than the other concerns as it largely
depended on these latter.

Further Actions Impending

Mr. Hough said that at about the
same time the American-Oriental
Banking Corporation passed a resolu-
tion granting Mr. Raven a bonus of
Tls. 135,000, bonuses of similar
amounts were granted to him by
both the American-Oriental Finance
Corporation and the Asia Realty
Company.
Both of the two latter concerns,
the American-Oriental Finance Cor-
poration and the Asia Realty Com-
pany, would be bringing similar pro-
ceedings against Mr. Raven in the
near future, Mr. Hough continued.
Another fact revealed by Mr.
Hough yesterday was that the
American-Oriental Banking Corpora-
tion was originally chartered in
Connecticut as a trading company
under another name. When, how-
ever, the office was opened in Shang-
hai it did banking business.
"The Raven Trust Company is in
a terrible position," Mr. Hough men-
tioned during his interview, "and I
cannot see that there is going to be
anything." Regarding the American
Finance Corporation Mr. Hough
said that there was a lot of money
involved but "whether it belongs to
me," he added, "I do not know."
Everything possible was being done
so that creditors and depositors of the
bank should benefit, Mr. Hough said.
He paid a tribute to the loyal work
of Mr. H. S. de Vault, certified
public accountant under his direction,
and finally he mentioned that there
was still an enormous amount of
work to be done before things were
straightened out.
The order he had asked for in his
bill of complaint Mr. Hough said,
reading from a copy of the bill of
complaint, which he held in his
hands, "that the defendant (Mr.
Raven) pay to complainant the sum
of $188,811.18, which is the value

gether with interest at the rate of six
per cent, from January 13, 1932, to
the date when payment shall be
made."

Court Proceedings Later

Court proceedings, Mr. Hough said,
would be the outcome of his filing
the bill of complaint, but nothing was
likely to take place for the next fort-
night because Judge Helmick, who
made the necessary order for security
on the writ of ne exeat on Saturday,
left for Peiping yesterday afternoon.
Afterwards he is proceeding to
Tientsin, where a number of cases
are to come before him, and it will
probably be a fortnight before he is
back again in Shanghai.

因为他从未打算离开该口岸。他说，美国法院要求的保证金肯定会提供，可能就在今天。雷文先生拒绝透露其担保人的姓名。

当被问及1932年1月美亚银行给予他的关平银135,000两酬金时，雷文先生表示，这笔款项是经过正当表决通过的，他在咨询法律意见后予以接受，并且他确信当时以及随后该企业均具备偿债能力。关于在银行账簿上分六年摊销该笔金额一事，雷文先生称这仅仅是记账问题，他看不出其中有何奇怪之处。他不是会计师：银行的经理是一位优秀的会计师，且银行聘请了一家优秀的审计师事务所来审查账目。

冻结账户

雷文先生说，在美亚银行停业时，他曾希望并认为银行能够百分之百清偿债务，尽管可能需要数年时间，但他至今仍认为能够做到。他说，与上海许多其他银行一样，该银行拥有大量冻结账户；然而，其他银行可以动用其海外总行的资金，而美亚银行公司却不能，因为其总行设在上海。如果业务好转，冻结账户可能会更快地变现，但如果没有任何改善，则将需要很长时间。由于雷文信托公司持有美亚金融公司的股份，而后者又持有美亚银行的股份，因此前两家机构的账目状况取决于最后一家机构，雷文先生继续说道。

记者向雷文先生提出的最后一个问题是，他个人是否欠雷文信托公司的钱。他予以否认，并表示相反，他已尽其所能将资金投入信托公司，因为与其他企业相比，信托公司的处境更为艰难，因为它在很大程度上依赖于这些企业。

即将采取进一步行动

霍夫先生表示，大约在美亚银行公司通过决议授予雷文先生关平银135,000两奖金的同时，美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司也授予了他同等金额的奖金。

霍夫先生接着说，后两家企业，即美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司，将在不久的将来对雷文先生提起类似的诉讼。

霍夫先生昨日披露的另一个事实是，美亚银行公司最初在康涅狄格州注册为一家贸易公司，使用另一个名称。然而，当在上海开设办事处时，它从事的是银行业务。

“雷文信托公司的处境非常糟糕，”霍夫先生在采访中提到，“我看不到会有什么资产。”关于美国金融公司，霍夫先生表示涉及大量资金，但他补充说：“这些资金是否归我（清算），我不知道。”霍夫先生表示，正在尽一切可能使银行的债权人和储户受益。他对在其指导下工作的注册会计师 H. S. 德沃尔特先生（Mr. H. S. de Vault）的忠诚工作给予了赞扬，最后他提到，在事情理顺之前，仍有大量的工作需要完成。

霍夫先生手持一份诉状副本宣读道，他在诉状中要求的命令是：“被告（雷文先生）向原告支付188,811.18美元，该金额相当于关平银135,000两的价值，并支付自1932年1月13日起至付款日止按百分之六利率计算的利息。”

稍后的法庭程序

霍夫先生表示，提交诉状后将进入法庭程序，但在接下来的两周内不太可能发生任何事情，因为周六在禁止出境令上作出必要保证金裁定的赫尔米克法官已于昨日下午前往北平。随后他将前往天津，那里有多起案件等待他审理，预计他要过两周才能回到上海。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, JULY 1, 1935

“NE EXEAT”
The filing of a writ of ne exeat in the U.S. Court and the presentation of a bill of complaint against Mr. E. J. Raven constitute a further stage in the investigation of the affairs of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation under the liquidation proceedings. Developments will be awaited with interest. The immediate cause of the action taken was a desire to ensure the presence of Mr. Raven within the jurisdiction of the U.S. Court while the affairs of his companies were under investigation, for apparently, information of his intention to leave Shanghai for the United States somehow reached Mr. F. L. Hough, the Liquidator. Mr. Raven has now stated that no such intention was entertained by him. However that may be, the proceedings now taken should help to clarify the position, on which, manifestly, there is some difference of opinion. The Liquidator has clearly been able to unravel the accounts with considerable rapidity, judging from the information which he has now made public. Mr. Hough makes no secret of the fact that to this result the services of Mr. H. S. De Vault, an auditor of acknowledged eminence, have greatly contributed.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JULY 2, 1935
11089

Four Prominent Americans
Give Bond For Mr. Raven

Amount Deposited Just Before Dead-Line Fixed
By U.S. Marshal; Signatories Each
Responsible For U.S. $20,000

At 4.55 p.m. yesterday, just five minutes before the dead-line set by the Marshal of the United States Court, a bond was posted with the Court for the sum of U.S.$20,000 as surety for the continued presence here of Mr. Frank J. Raven, president of the defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, who was threatened with incarceration in the event of his failure to find the stipulated surety.

Those signing the bond were Mr. C. H. French, Chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce and Vice-President of Messrs. Andersen, Meyer & Co., Ltd.; Mr. George A. Fitch, General Secretary of the Foreign Y.M.C.A.; the Rev. Charles L. Boynton of the National Christian Council, and Dr. A. M. Dunlap.

The four signatories assumed responsibility, jointly and severally, for the total amount of the bond, which will be forfeited in the event that Mr. Raven should depart from the Republic of China or the jurisdiction of the United States' Court. This means that any one of the signatories may be called upon to pay up the full amount, should Mr. Raven leave.

Final Formalities
Formalities in connection with the posting of the bond were carried out in the office of Mr. Edward L. Faupel, United States Marshal. It took the Marshal a full hour to satisfy himself as to the qualifications of the signatories. When this was done, signatures were appended to the documents and Mr. Raven, who attended throughout the proceedings, walked out of the Court building a free man once more.

In addition to the signatories and Mr. Raven, those who were present included Mr. Felthan Watson, U. S. District Attorney, Dr. George Sellett, legal adviser to the Liquidator of the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, and Mr. Cornell S. Franklin, attorney to Mr. Raven.

Terms Of Order
Mr. Raven was required by an order of the United States Court to furnish bail or security in the sum of U.S.$20,000 following a complaint lodged by Mr. Frank L. Hough, Liquidator of the Raven companies, charging that he had received from the American-Oriental Banking Corporation, in 1932, an honorarium of Tls. 135,000, while the concern was insolvent and unable to meet its liabilities. Repayment of this sum is demanded by the Liquidator.

The complaint was lodged with the Court on Saturday evening and was served on Mr. Raven at his Hungjao Road residence a few minutes before midnight, together with a Court order requiring him to put up bail or security. Over the week-end and until the bond was posted, Mr. Raven was kept under close surveillance by the Marshal of the U. S. Court and his deputy.

Hearing on the complaint will not take place for at least another two weeks, and possibly longer, since Judge Milton J. Helmick is now in North China, holding sessions of the U. S. Court in Peiping and Tientsin.

《字林西报》，1935年7月2日，星期二
11089

四位知名美国人为雷文先生提供担保

保证金在美国法警规定的截止日期前一刻存入；每位签署人承担20,000美元的责任

昨日下午4时55分，就在美国法院法警设定的截止时间前五分钟，向法院提交了一份金额为20,000美元的保释金，作为已倒闭的美亚银行（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）总裁弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生继续留在此地的担保。若他未能找到规定的担保人，将面临监禁。

签署该保释文件的人士包括：美商总会主席、安得森·梅尔公司（Andersen, Meyer & Co., Ltd.）副总裁C. H. 弗伦奇（C. H. French）先生；基督教青年会总干事乔治·A·菲奇（George A. Fitch）先生；全国基督教协进会的查尔斯·L·博因顿（Charles L. Boynton）牧师，以及A. M. 邓拉普（A. M. Dunlap）博士。

这四位签署人对保释金总额承担连带及个别责任。如果雷文先生离开中华民国或美国法院的管辖范围，该笔款项将被没收。这意味着，如果雷文先生离开，任何一位签署人都可能被要求支付全额款项。

最后手续

与提交保释金相关的手续是在美国法警爱德华·L·福佩尔（Edward L. Faupel）先生的办公室办理的。法警花费了整整一个小时来核实签署人的资格。完成这一程序后，各方在文件上签字，全程出席诉讼程序的雷文先生再次以自由之身走出了法院大楼。

除签署人和雷文先生外，在场者还包括美国地区检察官费尔坦·沃森（Felthan Watson）先生、美亚银行清算人的法律顾问乔治·塞莱特（George Sellett）博士，以及雷文先生的律师康奈尔·S·富兰克林（Cornell S. Franklin）先生。

命令条款

根据美国法院的一项命令，雷文先生被要求提供20,000美元的保释金或担保。此前，雷文旗下公司的清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生提出控告，指控雷文在1932年从美亚银行收取了135,000两白银的酬金，而当时该公司已资不抵债，无力偿还债务。清算人要求归还这笔款项。

诉状于周六晚间提交法院，并在午夜前几分钟送达位于虹桥路住所的雷文先生手中，同时附有一份法院命令，要求他提供保释金或担保。在整个周末直至保释金提交期间，雷文一直受到美国法院法警及其副手的严密监视。

针对该诉状的听证会至少在两周后才会举行，甚至可能更久，因为米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官目前正在华北地区，在北平和天津主持美国法院的庭审。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JULY 1, 1935

Raven Placed In U.S.
Court Custody, Must
Post Bond, Stay Here

F. J. Raven Denies Trip Planned,
Says Writ A Complete Surprise

“No Intention Whatsoever Of Leaving,” Head
Of Defunct Bank Tells Reporters; Declares
Nothing Unusual In Payment Of Bonuses

“I never had any intention whatsoever of leaving Shanghai and I was most surprised to be served with the writ restraining my leaving.” Mr. Frank J. Raven, former head of the now-defunct American-Oriental Banking Corporation, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the Raven Trust Company, told press representatives yesterday afternoon at his home at 555 Hungjao Road.

Mr. Raven on Saturday was placed in the custody of the U.S. Court for China by Judge Helmick following a bill of complaint filed by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the three institutions, and must post a bond of U.S.$20,000. The bill of complaint alleges that a bonus of Tls35,000 was paid by the bank to Mr. Raven in 1932 at which time the bank was alleged to be insolvent.

“The honorarium mentioned in the bill of complaint,” Mr. Raven said, “was properly voted and I accepted it with legal advice. It was passed unanimously at a directors’ meeting.”

No Intention Of Leaving
“I have no intention of leaving Shanghai. I have nothing to run away from. I expect to stay here for some time,” the ex-president remarked.

In answering questions, Mr. Raven said that the U.S. $20,000 bond required in Judge Helmick’s writ would probably be posted today. He would not reveal who was arranging the bond and ridiculed rumors that it was being arranged by Mr. C. V. Starr.

Commenting on the closing of the three concerns, Mr. Raven said that he is still of the opinion that all three are solvent. He had stated when the bank closed that he sincerely hoped that the depositors and creditors would be paid in full and he still believed such payment will be possible, though it may take many years. The three companies have millions of dollars in frozen accounts, he remarked.

Others Said In Same Boat
Other banks in Shanghai, Mr. Raven said, are in the same condition that the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was at the time of its failure. Only these banks are able to draw funds from head offices in other cities while the American-Oriental Bank, with its head office in Shanghai, was unable to do so, he continued.

In regard to the payment of the bonus in 1932, Mr. Raven said that the fact that it was to be written off over a period of six years did not in his opinion indicate that the bank was insolvent, as is alleged by the liquidator. Such a procedure of payment, he said, was ordinary and natural.

The accounts of the bank, he continued, were left in the hands of Mr. J. Kieffel, manager, and the auditors, and he had nothing to do with them. “I am not an auditor,” he said. “The accounts of the bank were audited yearly by competent auditors. If they would have found something wrong, such as insolvency, certainly they would have commented upon it.”

Wanted To Help Out
Questioned as to the allegation that he had in 1932, shortly after receiving bonuses from the American-Oriental Bank, the American-Oriental Finance Corporation, and the Asia Realty Company, totalling about Tls. 405,000, transferred the sum to the Raven Trust Company to pay a personal debt which allegedly had suddenly appeared on the books of the Raven Trust Company, Mr. Raven said that he had no personal debts with the Raven Trust Company. “On the contrary,” he remarked, “I constantly put my own funds into the company as loans. When the Raven Trust Company had tough sledding, I tried to help it out.”

In answering a concluding question, Mr. Raven said that the American-Oriental Banking Corporation was organized as an ordinary corporation under the laws of Connecticut but that its charter included the right of carrying on of banking business in addition to ordinary business trading.

Mrs. Raven and three daughters are in Heidelberg, Germany, where the latter are attending school.

《大美晚报》，1935年7月1日，星期一

雷文被置于美国法院监管之下，必须缴纳保释金并留在本地

F. J. 雷文否认计划出行，称传票完全出乎意料

“绝无离开之意”，已倒闭银行行长告诉记者；宣称发放奖金并无不妥

“我从未有过任何离开上海的意图，收到限制我离境的传票令我极为惊讶。”已倒闭的美亚银行、美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）及雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）的前负责人弗兰克·J·雷文先生，昨日下午在其虹桥路555号的寓所中对新闻界代表如是说。

周六，在这三家机构的清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫先生提交诉状后，赫尔米克法官将雷文先生置于驻华美国法院的监管之下，并要求其缴纳20,000美元的保释金。诉状指控该银行在1932年向雷文先生支付了一笔35,000两白银的奖金，而据称当时该银行已资不抵债。

雷文先生说：“诉状中提到的那笔酬金是经过正当表决通过的，我在法律咨询的建议下接受了它。这是在董事会议上全票通过的。”

无意离开

“我无意离开上海。我没有什么可逃避的。我预计会在这里待一段时间，”这位前总裁说道。

在回答提问时，雷文先生说，赫尔米克法官传票中要求的20,000美元保释金可能会在今天缴纳。他不肯透露是谁在安排保释事宜，并对有关由C. V. 史带（C. V. Starr）先生安排保释的谣言嗤之以鼻。

在评论这三家机构关闭一事时，雷文表示他仍然认为这三家机构均有偿付能力。他在银行关闭时曾真诚地希望存款人和债权人能获得全额赔付，他至今仍相信这种赔付是可能的，尽管可能需要多年时间。他指出，这三家公司有数百万美元的资金被冻结在账户中。

其他银行处境相同

雷文先生说，上海的其他银行也处于美亚银行倒闭时的相同状况。只不过这些银行能够从位于其他城市的总行调拨资金，而总部设在上海的美亚银行却无法做到这一点，他继续说道。

关于1932年发放奖金一事，雷文先生说，这笔款项分六年摊销的事实，在他看来并不像清算人所指控的那样表明银行资不抵债。他说，这种支付程序是平常且自然的。

他接着说，银行的账目交由经理J·基费尔（J. Kieffel）先生和审计师处理，与他无关。“我不是审计师，”他说。“银行的账目每年都由合格的审计师进行审计。如果他们发现任何问题，比如资不抵债，他们肯定会对此发表评论。”

意在提供帮助

当被问及一项指控，即他在1932年从美亚银行、美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司（Asia Realty Company）收到总计约405,000两白银的奖金后不久，将这笔钱转入雷文信托公司以偿还一笔据称突然出现在雷文信托公司账面上的个人债务时，雷文先生表示他与雷文信托公司之间不存在个人债务。“相反，”他说，“我经常将自己的资金作为贷款投入公司。当雷文信托公司陷入困境时，我试图帮助它渡过难关。”

在回答最后一个问题时，雷文先生说，美亚银行是根据康涅狄格州法律组建的一家普通公司，但其章程除了允许进行普通商业贸易外，还包括经营银行业务的权利。

雷文夫人和三个女儿目前在德国海德堡，孩子们在那里上学。

归档
1935年7月1日

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JULY 1, 1935

Helmick Issues Writ Re-
quiring Ex-Bank Head
To Remain In China;
Hough Files Complaint

U.S. Trip Was Said Con-
templated; Payment Of
Bonus, Insolvent Bank
Condition Is Alleged

Mr. Frank J. Raven, former pre-
sident, manager, and promoter of
the now-defunct American-Oriental
Banking Corporation, the Raven
Trust Company, and the American-
Oriental Finance Corporation, which
failed on May 24, was placed under
the custody of the U.S. Court for
China and is restrained from leav-
ing Shanghai following the serving
of a writ ne exeat in equity issued
Saturday by Judge Milton J. Hel-
mick of the U.S. Court for China.

Judge Helmick issued the writ
following receipt of a bill of com-
plaint filed with the U.S. Court
Saturday by Mr. Frank L. Hough,
liquidator of all three concerns,
and was served on Mr. Raven
Saturday at 11:50 p.m. by U. S.
Marshal Edward L. Faupel at Mr.
Raven's home, 555 Hungjao Road.
Mr. Raven is required to post a
U.S. $20,000 bond and told a CHINA
PRESS reporter that he expected to
do so today. A bond of $2,500 re-
quired by Mr. Hough has already
been posted.

Mr. Hough's bill of complaint
alleges that the American-Oriental
Banking Corporation was, with the
knowledge of Mr. Raven, insolvent
at the beginning of 1932 and that
on January 13, 1932, the bank
directors authorized the immediate
payment of a bonus of Tls. 135,000
to Mr. Raven, the sum to be writ-
ten off over a period of six years.
Mr. Raven is therefore said indebted
to the bank for Tls. 135,000, and Mr.
Hough desires payment with 6 per
cent per annum interest on $188,-
811.18, the equivalent sum in Chin-
ese dollars.

Mr. Hough yesterday said that he
did not know at present whether
similar action might be taken
against other Raven officials but
that he intended filing two more
bills of complaints against Mr.
Raven within the next few days
for two bonuses of Tls. 135,000 each
received by him from the American-
Oriental Finance Corporation and
the Asia-Realty Company in 1932.

Text Of Writ Given

The text of the writ issued to the
U.S. Marshal by Judge Helmick,
who left yesterday for Peiping, fol-
lows in part:

"Whereas . . . amongst other most
things . . . defendant is greatly
indebted to said complainant and
designs quickly to depart from the
Republic of China and the juris-
diction of this Court, as by oath
made on that behalf appears, which
tends to the great prejudice and
damage of the said complainant
therefore, in order to prevent this
injustice, I hereby command that
you do, without delay, cause the
said F. J. Raven personally
to come before you and give suffi-
cient bail or security in the sum
of U.S. $20,000 that the said F. J.
Raven will not go or attempt to
go into parts beyond the Republic
of China and the jurisdiction of
this Court, without leave of this
Court. And in case the said F. J.
Raven shall refuse to give such
bail or security, then you are to
keep him in your safe custody until
he shall do it of his own accord."

Deadline Today

The original deadline for the post-
ing of Mr. Raven's bond was set for
yesterday but in view of the banks
being closed on Sunday, it has been
set at about 5 p.m. today, Mr.
Faupel, U. S. Marshal, told a CHINA
PRESS reporter last night. If the
bond is not posted, Mr. Raven will
be placed in the Amoy Road Jail.
A U. S. Court official has been post-
ed at Mr. Raven's home on 555
Hungjao Road since the writ was
served.

In a press interview yesterday in
the now-darkened offices of the
American-Oriental Bank of Nanking
Road, Mr. Hough revealed a com-
plete picture of the reasons behind
his bill of complaint.

He stated that Mr. Raven paid
a call to him on Saturday and
voiced his intention of leaving for
the United States via Manila and
that he had advised against it.
"But I thought he might leave," Mr.
Hough said.

Auditors Praised

Continuing, Mr. Hough said that
he has been serving as a liquidator,
with the aid of Mr. Henry De Vault
and his staff of auditors, to whom
he gave high praise, for a month and
had only started to get a complete
picture of the inner workings of the
three defunct corporations. In addi-
tion to the Tls. 135,000 bonus voted
by the bank, Mr. Hough pointed out
that the American-Oriental Fin-
ance Corporation and the Asia
Realty Company also voted identical
bonuses to Mr. Raven within the
same few days, the three bonuses
totalling Tls. 405,000. Shortly after-
wards the balance sheet of the
Raven Trust Company disclosed a
sum of about Tls. 450,000 as an as-
set in the form of a personal debt
due from Mr. Raven. The books
showed that this sum had been paid
within a month or two afterwards,
he said.

"This strikes me as a most
peculiar co-incidence," Mr. Hough
declared. "And within the next few
days I intend to file similar bills of
complaint and applications for writs
ne exeat in regard to the two
bonuses paid Mr. Raven by the
American-Oriental Finance Corpora-
tion and the Asia Realty Company."
Mr. Hough added that the resolu-
tions in regard to the three bonuses
are identical with the exception of
the company names, even includ-
ing the phrase "without compensa-
tion" though he was paid by at
least one of the two other com-
panies.

"The remarkable thing about the
resolution is that it shows that the
bank was insolvent in 1932," Mr.
Hough said. "If the bank was solvent
and desired to vote a bonus, it is
most natural that it would pay the
bonus at once and write it off at
once and not over a period of years.
It is interesting to note that the
bonus resolutions on January 13, 14,
15, or thereabouts in 1932, were un-
animously carried, that is, with the
participation of Mr. Raven as well
as the other officials.

"At first the 1931 Raven Trust
balance sheet appear such that Mr.
Raven did not owe the company
money. Then it appears that on
January 16-17, 1932, Mr. Raven owed
about Tls. 405,000. I believe the
books of the company were reopened
after they were closed to include
this item. Shortly afterwards and
after Mr. Raven had been paid Tls.
405,000 in bonuses, this approximate
Tls. 405,000 debt was paid into the
Raven Trust Company."

Commenting on the general pro-
gress of the liquidation, Mr. Hough
stated that he was just beginning to
get a picture of the three com-
panies and that it would take
months more of laborious auditing
to get into further roots of various
transactions. In regard to the pay-
ment of Raven Trust creditors, Mr.
Hough said: "Frankly, I don't see
that anybody will get anything. . .
It is difficult to say about the finance
corporation, there are so many
ramifications and many millions of
dollars involved. It will take many
months to get a better picture."

Has Big Overdraft

Mr. Hough also revealed that be-
sides the bonuses totalling about
T405,000, Mr. Raven has an over-
draft in the American-Oriental
Bank of about $60,000. "It is true
that Mr. Raven lost every cent of
his overdraft when the bank failed,"
Mr. Hough stated.

Commenting on the bank's me-
thod of making loans, Mr. Hough
said that it appeared as though
the bank never had a loan com-
mittee but that the final say about
loans probably rested in one or two
high officials of the bank. The
branch of the American-Oriental
Bank in Tientsin issued a loan to
the now-defunct Nichols Rug Com-
pany of almost $1,000,000. Despite
the fact that it allegedly seemed
apparent that the company might
fail, this loan was carried for some
time as an asset on the books of
the bank, Mr. Hough said.

Mr. Hough also remarked that
while under the laws of Connecticut
the corporation papers of the in-
stitution entitled it to conduct
banking, it's charter primarily in-
ferred that the corporation was a
trading company. If such a cor-
poration were operating in Con-
necticut, many of the practices
here probably would not have been
permitted to occur, the liquidator
remarked.

Concluding, the liquidator said
that many bank depositors had
been writing him asking about pos-
sibilities of payment. Several mis-
sionaries had been writing in, many
who had large accounts in the
bank, telling pathetic stories of
their circumstances. "I am doing
my best," Mr. Hough said, "only I
wish I had more to show for it. If
I could say that I could pay 60 or
70 per cent, then I would be doing
something. At the present time, at
least I can't say that."

《字林西报》，1935年7月1日，星期一

赫尔米克签发禁令，要求前银行行长留华；霍夫提出申诉

据称曾计划赴美；被指在银行资不抵债情况下支付奖金

已於5月24日倒闭的美亚银行公司（American-Oriental Banking Corporation）、雷文信托公司（Raven Trust Company）及美亚金融公司（American-Oriental Finance Corporation）的前任总裁、经理及发起人弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）先生，现处于美国驻华法院的监管之下。在美国驻华法院法官米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）于周六签发一项衡平法上的禁止出境令（writ ne exeat in equity）并送达后，雷文被限制离开上海。

赫尔米克法官是在收到上述三家机构的清算人弗兰克·L·霍夫（Frank L. Hough）先生于周六向美国驻华法院提交的诉状后，签发了该禁令。该禁令于周六晚上11时50分由美国法警爱德华·L·福佩尔（Edward L. Faupel）在虹桥路555号雷文先生的住所送达给他。雷文先生需缴纳20,000美元保证金，他告诉《字林西报》记者，预计今日将办理此事。霍夫先生要求的2,500美元保证金已经缴纳。

霍夫先生的诉状指控称，美亚银行公司在1932年初即已资不抵债，且雷文先生对此知情；1932年1月13日，银行董事会授权立即向雷文先生支付135,000两白银的奖金，该笔款项将在六年内分期注销。因此，据称雷文欠银行135,000两白银，霍夫先生要求支付相当于188,811.18元中国货币的等额款项，并按年利率6%计息。

霍夫昨日表示，他目前尚不清楚是否会对其他雷文系官员采取类似行动，但他打算在未来几天内就雷文先生于1932年从美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司（Asia-Realty Company）收到的两笔各为135,000两白银的奖金，再对雷文先生提起两项诉讼。

公布禁令文本

赫尔米克法官昨日已启程前往北平，其向美国法警签发的禁令部分文本如下：

“鉴于……除其他重要事项外……被告对上述原告负有巨额债务，并企图迅速离开中华民国及本法院之管辖范围，此点经宣誓证实属实，此举将对上述原告造成极大不利和损害；因此，为防止此种不公，本人特此命令你立即促使上述F. J. 雷文亲自到你面前，并提供金额为20,000美元的充分保释金或担保，以保证上述F. J. 雷文在未获本法院许可的情况下，不会进入或试图进入中华民国及本法院管辖范围以外的地区。若上述F. J. 雷文拒绝提供此类保释金或担保，则你应将其妥善羁押，直至其自愿履行为止。”

今日为最后期限

美国法警福佩尔昨晚告诉《字林西报》记者，雷文先生缴纳保证金的原定截止日期为昨日，但鉴于周日银行停业，截止期限已延至今日下午5时左右。若未缴纳保证金，雷文先生将被关入爱多亚路监狱。自禁令送达以来，一名美国法院官员一直驻守在虹桥路555号雷文先生家中。

昨日，在南京路现已昏暗的美亚银行办公室内接受媒体采访时，霍夫先生全面揭示了他提出诉状背后的原因。

他表示，雷文先生于周六拜访了他，并表示打算经马尼拉前往美国，而他已劝其不要这样做。“但我认为他可能会离开，”霍夫先生说。

称赞审计人员

霍夫先生接着说，他在亨利·德·沃尔特（Henry De Vault）先生及其审计团队的协助下担任清算人已有一个月，他对这些审计人员给予了高度评价，并且才刚刚开始全面了解这三家已倒闭公司的内部运作情况。除了银行投票通过的135,000两奖金外，霍夫先生指出，美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司也在同样的几天内投票通过了给予雷文先生的相同数额奖金，三笔奖金总计405,000两。不久之后，雷文信托公司的资产负债表显示，有一笔约405,000两的资产以雷文先生个人欠款的形式存在。他说，账目显示这笔款项在一两个月后已付清。

“这在我看来是一个非常奇特的巧合，”霍夫先生宣称。“而在未来几天内，我打算就美亚金融公司和亚洲地产公司支付给雷文先生的两笔奖金，提交类似的诉状及禁止出境令申请。”霍夫先生补充说，关于这三笔奖金的决议内容完全相同，除了公司名称不同外，甚至包括“无报酬”这一短语，尽管他至少从另外两家公司中的一家获得了报酬。

“该决议引人注目的地方在于，它表明银行在1932年已资不抵债，”霍夫先生说。“如果银行有偿付能力并希望发放奖金，最自然的做法是立即支付奖金并立即注销，而不是分多年进行。值得注意的是，1932年1月13日、14日、15日或前后的奖金决议均一致通过，也就是说，雷文先生以及其他官员都参与了投票。”

“起初，1931年雷文信托公司的资产负债表显示雷文先生并不欠公司钱。随后显示，在1932年1月16日至17日，雷文先生欠款约405,000两。我相信公司在结账后又重新开账，以便列入该项目。不久之后，在雷文先生收到405,000两奖金后，这笔约405,000两的债务又还入了雷文信托公司。”

在评论清算工作的总体进展时，霍夫先生表示，他才刚刚开始了解这三家公司的情况，还需要数月艰苦的审计工作才能深入查清各种交易的根源。关于雷文信托公司债权人的受偿问题，霍夫先生说：“坦率地说，我看不到任何人能获得任何赔偿……至于金融公司，情况错综复杂，涉及金额达数百万美元，很难做出判断。需要很多个月才能更清楚地了解情况。”

存在大额透支

霍夫先生还透露，除了总计约405,000两的奖金外，雷文先生在美亚银行还有约60,000美元的透支额。“确实，当银行倒闭时，雷文先生损失了他透支的每一分钱，”霍夫先生 stated。

在评论银行的放贷方式时，霍夫先生说，看来银行似乎从未设立过贷款委员会，贷款的最终决定权可能掌握在一两名银行高级官员手中。美亚银行天津分行向现已倒闭的尼科尔斯地毯公司（Nichols Rug Company）发放了近100万美元的贷款。霍夫先生说，尽管该公司显然可能倒闭，但这笔贷款在银行的账目上作为资产列示了一段时间。

霍夫先生还指出，虽然根据康涅狄格州法律，该机构的法人文件赋予其从事银行业务的权利，但其章程主要暗示该公司是一家贸易公司。清算人评论说，如果这样的公司在康涅狄格州运营，这里的许多做法可能不会被允许发生。

最后，这位清算人说，许多银行储户一直写信给他，询问获得赔付的可能性。几位传教士也来信，其中许多人在银行有大额存款，讲述了他们处境的悲惨故事。“我正在尽最大努力，”霍夫先生说，“只是我希望能有更多的成果可展示。如果我能说可以支付60%或70%，那我就算做了一些事情。但目前，我至少不能这么说。”

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, JULY 1, 1935

Text Of Hough's Complaint

The text of the bill of the complaint filed last Saturday by Mr. Frank L. Hough, liquidator of the Raven interests, to Judge Milton J. Helmick of the U. S. Court for China, follows in full:

Your orator, Frank L. Hough, as liquidator of The American-Oriental Banking Corporation brings this bill of complaint against Frank J. Raven, and hereupon your orator complains and says:
1. The aforesaid The American-Oriental Banking Corporation is a corporation organized and existing under and by virtue of the laws of the State of Connecticut, United States of America, and for more than 10 years last past has maintained offices and carried on a banking business in Shanghai, China, and Tientsin, China, and nowhere else, and is subject to the jurisdiction of this Honorable Court.
2. On May 27, 1935, the said The American-Oriental Banking Corporation filed a bill in equity in the above entitled court (In the Matter of the Liquidation of The American-Oriental Banking Corporation, Cause No. 3870, Civil No. 1813) praying for the appointment of a liquidator to take over all of its assets and business for the purpose of liquidating the same, and upon hearing said bill in equity your orator, Frank L. Hough, a citizen of the United States of America residing at Shanghai, China, was by order of this Honorable Court on the 3rd day of June, 1935, appointed liquidator of The American-Oriental Banking Corporation, and your orator, Frank L. Hough, is now the duly appointed, qualified and acting liquidator of said corporation, and the business and affairs of said corporation are now being liquidated by your orator.
3. The defendant is a citizen of the United States of America residing at Shanghai, China, and now is and for more than 10 years last past has been a director and president of the aforesaid The American-Oriental Banking Corporation.
4. During all of the period of 10 years last past defendant has controlled said The American-Oriental Banking Corporation by reason and virtue of the fact that during said period defendant has owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock of Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A. (a corporation), which last named corporation now owns and controls and during all of said period owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock in The American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc. U.S.A. (a corporation), which last named corporation now owns and controls and during all of said period owned and controlled a majority of the voting stock in the said The American-Oriental Banking Corporation.
5. The American-Oriental Banking Corporation is now insolvent in that its liabilities are greater than its assets and at all times between the 31st day of December, 1931, and the present time the said corporation has been insolvent.
6. At a meeting of the board of directors of the said The American-Oriental Banking Corporation held at Shanghai, China, on January 12, 1932, at which time defendant was a director and president of the said corporation and controlled said corporation in the manner aforesaid, and at which meeting all of the directors including defendant were present, a resolution in the following words and figures was unanimously adopted:
"Resolved, that in view of the long and faithful service performed without salary or other compensation by Frank L. Raven as president, manager and promoter of The American-Oriental Banking Corporation, an honorarium of One Hundred Thirty-five Thousand Taels (T135,000.00) be voted to him in recognition of work well and faithfully performed; and
Be It Further Resolved, that the Treasurer be authorized to make this entire payment to said Frank J. Raven at once; and to write off from the books of this company over a period of six (6) years, or fewer, One Hundred Thirty-five Thousand Taels (T135,-000.00); the amount to be written off in the year 1932 to be Thirty-five Thousand Taels (T35,000.00) and the amount to be written off in any one year thereafter to be governed by the net profits accruing to this company during this period."
And pursuant to the aforesaid resolution, on January 13, 1932, The American-Oriental Banking Corporation paid to defendant and defendant received from it the sum of ShT135,000.00, being equivalent to £188,811.18, Chinese currency.
7. At the time the aforesaid sum of Sh.-T135,000.00 was received by defendant, The American-Oriental Banking Corporation was not indebted or otherwise obligated to defendant and defendant then and there knew that said corporation was then and there insolvent and that its assets were insufficient to meet its liabilities and obligations to its depositors and creditors and thereupon and by reason of the foregoing defendant was and became obligated in equity and good conscience to immediately repay to the said corporation the said sum of ShT135,000.00.
8. Since the payment of the aforesaid sum of ShT135,000.00 by the said The American-Oriental Banking Corporation to defendant, the said moneys have been due and owing by defendant to the said corporation and defendant has failed and refused to pay the same or any part thereof to the said corporation, and defendant is now indebted to said corporation in said sum of ShT135,000.00.
Wherefore your orator prays that a decree and order be entered herein—
1. That defendant pay to complainant the sum of £188,811.18, Chinese currency, which is of value equivalent to ShT135,-000.00, together with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum for the 18th day of January, 1932, to the date when payment shall be made by defendant;
2. And that complainant may have such other and further relief in the premises as the circumstances of the case may require and as to this Honorable Court may seem just and proper.
And your orator as in duty bound will ever pray.

豪夫诉状全文

雷文（Raven）利益相关方清算人弗兰克·L·豪夫（Frank L. Hough）先生于上周六向美国驻华法院米尔顿·J·赫尔米克（Milton J. Helmick）法官提交的诉状全文如下：

具状人弗兰克·L·豪夫，作为美亚银行公司（The American-Oriental Banking Corporation）的清算人，针对弗兰克·J·雷文（Frank J. Raven）提起本诉状，兹陈述如下：

1. 上述美亚银行公司系依据美利坚合众国康涅狄格州法律组建并存续的公司，在过去十年以上的时间里，仅在中国上海和中国天津设有办事处并经营银行业务，未在其他地方开展业务，且受本庭管辖。

2. 1935年5月27日，所述美亚银行公司向上述具名法院提交了一份衡平法诉状（案件名称：美亚银行公司清算案，案号3870，民事编号1813），请求任命一名清算人接管其所有资产和业务以进行清算。经审理该衡平法诉状，本庭于1935年6月3日下令任命居住于中国上海的美国公民弗兰克·L·豪夫为美亚银行公司的清算人。具状人弗兰克·L·豪夫现为该公司正式任命、具备资格并在任的清算人，该公司的业务和事务正由具状人进行清算。

3. 被告系居住于中国上海的美国公民，现为且在过去十年以上的时间里一直担任上述美亚银行公司的董事及总裁。

4. 在过去十年的整个期间，被告因拥有并控制雷文信托公司联邦股份公司（Raven Trust Company, Federal Inc. U.S.A.，一家公司）的多数表决权股票而控制了所述美亚银行公司；该最后提及的公司现在拥有并控制，且在整个所述期间一直拥有并控制美亚金融公司联邦股份公司（The American-Oriental Finance Corporation, Federal Inc. U.S.A.，一家公司）的多数表决权股票；而该最后提及的公司现在拥有并控制，且在整个所述期间一直拥有并控制所述美亚银行公司的多数表决权股票。

5. 美亚银行公司目前资不抵债，因其负债大于资产；且在1931年12月31日至目前的任何时间，该公司均处于资不抵债状态。

6. 1932年1月12日，所述美亚银行公司董事会在中国上海召开会议，当时被告为该公司的董事兼总裁，并以如前所述的方式控制该公司，包括被告在内的所有董事均出席了会议。会议一致通过如下决议：
“决议：鉴于弗兰克·L·雷文（Frank L. Raven）作为美亚银行公司的总裁、经理和发起人，长期忠诚服务且未领取薪金或其他报酬，特授予其十三万五千两（T135,000.00）酬金，以表彰其出色且忠诚的工作；
并进一步决议：授权司库立即向所述弗兰克·J·雷文支付全部款项；并在六（6）年或更短的时间内，从本公司账目中注销十三万五千两（T135,000.00）；1932年注销金额为三万五千两（T35,000.00），此后任何一年的注销金额视本公司在此期间产生的净利润而定。”
根据上述决议，美亚银行公司于1932年1月13日向被告支付了上海规元135,000.00两，被告予以收受，该金额相当于中国货币英镑188,811.18镑。

7. 被告收受上述上海规元135,000.00两时，美亚银行公司并不欠被告债务或对其负有其他义务；被告当时明知该公司已资不抵债，其资产不足以偿付对储户和债权人的负债及义务；因此，基于前述理由，被告在衡平法和良知上有义务立即向该公司偿还上述上海规元135,000.00两。

8. 自所述美亚银行公司向被告支付上述上海规元135,000.00两以来，被告一直欠付该公司该笔款项，但被告未能且拒绝向该公司支付该款项或其任何部分，被告目前欠该公司上述上海规元135,000.00两。

为此，具状人恳请颁布判决如下：
1. 判令被告向原告支付中国货币英镑188,811.18镑（价值相当于上海规元135,000.00两），并支付自1932年1月18日起至被告付款之日止按年利率百分之六计算的利息；
2. 判令原告获得本案情况所需且本庭认为公正适当的其他进一步救济。
具状人将依职责永远祈请。
